If a will was not made, inheritance would follow the prevailing law. Your Donee will not be able to act on your behalf to manage the inheritance.
By writing a will, you can ensure that your inheritance will be managed according to your wishes and you would be able to appoint an executor to manage your estate.

questions.title: How do I check if deceased has made a will?
questions.text: Information about what one might do if a loved one passes on and they would like to check if the deceased had made a will can be found at this webpage on My Legacy.

questions.title: How can I edit my Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) form?
questions.text:
You cannot edit your LPA after it’s been submitted and sent to your Donees for acceptance of their appointments.
If you would like to make changes to the LPA application, you will need to cancel your current LPA and draft a new LPA.
If your LPA has already been registered and you would like to make changes, you will need to revoke your registered LPA before making a new one. You may start drafting a new LPA while waiting for the cancellation of your existing LPA. However, the new LPA will only be accepted by OPG for registration after your existing LPA is cancelled. (adhered to copy in link)

questions.title: I haven't registered my Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) but want to download a copy of my LPA draft. How do I do this?
questions.text: You may access and retrieve the electronic copy of your LPA application from Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) - MSF. Login via Singpass and click ‘LPA No.’ on your Overview page.

questions.title: How much do Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) Certificate Issuers charge for their services?
questions.text:
There are three groups of professionals who can act as LPA Certificate Issuers - Medical practitioners accredited by the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), Lawyers* and Psychiatrists.
*This refers to a Singapore solicitor qualified to practice Singapore law in a Singapore law firm.
OPG does not prescribe the CI fees charged as it varies with the complexity of the case. Hence, there is a range of CIs who can offer services to meet the different needs of the Donors. Members of the public are advised to check with the individual CI on his professional charges. More information can be found here.
You may also use this appointment booking listing to search for the listed fees of your preferred CI.

questions.title: How can I find help on using Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO)?
questions.text:
You may view instructional videos and Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) on how to use the various services on OPGO, such as applying for an LPA, accepting an LPA Donee appointment, certifying an LPA, and submitting a Deputy Report. The videos are subtitled and voiced in English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil.
If you need guided assistance, you can seek help from your family first. Alternatively, you may also approach community touchpoints at ServiceSG centres.

questions.title: Does a Donor still need to visit a Certificate Issuer in person?
questions.text:
Yes, the Donor needs to visit a Certificate Issuer in-person to certify the LPA. An LPA is an important legal document.
Visiting a certificate issuer in person helps us to make sure that you:
understand the purpose of the LPA
understand the powers you are granting your Donees
are not under pressure to make the LPA
After your LPA has been certified, the certificate issuer will submit the LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian on your behalf via OPGO.
Do note that your LPA must be submitted to OPG for registration within 6 months from the date of your LPA application. This includes obtaining your Donee's consent to be appointed and your LPA certification.

questions.title: How do I search for a certificate issuer?
questions.text: You may make appointments with a Certificate Issuer (CI) or check a list of CIs through this webpage. Only individuals accredited by the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) can certify your LPA.

questions.title: Can I send my Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) to other individuals or third parties?
questions.text:
After an LPA is registered by OPG, the Donor and his/her Donees can view and send the LPA to individuals or third-party organizations via OPGO.
When sending to third parties, the LPA will be a password protected PDF document with an attachment. The process of viewing and sending the LPA is the same for the Donor and Donee but the Donee will only be able to send the LPA after declaring on OPGO that the Donor had been certified by a doctor to lack mental capacity.
You may refer to the OPGO Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) for step-by-step guidance on how to send the LPA.

questions.title: When and how does my Donee use the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) to make decisions for me and transact with third parties?
questions.text:
A Donee can transact on a Donor’s behalf when the Donor has been certified by a registered medical practitioner to have lost mental capacity to handle his/her own affairs.
When transacting with any third-party agency (e.g., banks, insurance agencies, HDB, CPFB, SLA, etc.), the Donee would need to produce:
your registered LPA (by sharing it via Office of the Public Guardian Online). You may refer to the OPGO Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) for step-by-step guidance on how to send the LPA.
the medical report on your loss of mental capacity
other supporting documents as required by the organisation that the Donee is transacting with.
The type of decision your Donee can make for you depends on the powers you have granted them in your LPA. For example, a Donee with property and affairs powers will be able to transact directly with banks to manage your money.

questions.title: I do not have a smart device / my phone is unable to install the Singpass application, but I would like to make an Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA). How can I proceed?
questions.text:
To enjoy the benefit of making an online Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), we would like to encourage you to approach persons you trust, such as your family members or loved ones, to set up your Singpass app on their spare smart device. Please follow the instructions below to set up your Singpass on the spare device:
If the smart device's Singpass app has an existing Singpass account logged in, click on Settings on the Singpass app and reset the app following the in-app instructions.
Set up the Singpass app with your Singpass Account by entering your Singpass ID and password. For local users with a mobile number registered with Singpass, enter the SMS One-Time Password sent to your mobile number. You may be prompted to perform a face scan enabled by Singpass Face Verification to authenticate your identity.
Follow the in-app instructions to set up your 6-digit app passcode or biometric option.
Reset the Singpass app using Step 1 after you have completed your LPA-related transactions before returning the phone.
If you are unable to obtain a spare smart device, you may submit a hardcopy LPA form instead. Mail in or drop off the completed hardcopy LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) at 3 Bishan Place #03-00, CPF Bishan Building, Singapore 579838. Do note that the acceptance of a hardcopy LPA is subject to OPG's approval.

questions.title: Can I submit a hardcopy Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) application?
questions.text:
All LPA applications should be submitted online. If you're uncomfortable with technology and need help completing your LPA application online, visit a ServiceSG centre or contact the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG).
The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) may accept hardcopy LPA applications if you fall within one of the following exceptional situations:
you or your Donees (including replacement Donee) are unable to complete the application online due to physical disability or other circumstances
the prepare your LPA service on My Legacy and the Office of the Public Guardian (OPGO) is down
you or your Donees (including Replacement Donee) do not have an electronic device to receive SMSes or to create and access the Singpass account
you or your Donees (including Replacement Donee) are not eligible for a Singpass account
If you are unable to obtain a spare smart device, you may submit a hardcopy LPA form instead. Mail in or drop off the completed hardcopy LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) at 3 Bishan Place #03-00, CPF Bishan Building, Singapore 579838.

questions.title: If I appoint my Donees to act jointly on my LPA and one of my Donee passes on, is the remaining Donee the sole decision maker to act on the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)? (I do not have a replacement donee)
questions.text:
If your Donees are appointed to act jointly on your LPA, the Donees must act together and not individually. When any one Donee is no longer able to act, all the Donees in the joint appointment will be terminated.
If there was a replacement Donee appointed in the LPA, the replacement will replace the 2 Donees who were appointed to act jointly. Otherwise, the LPA will no longer be in effect.
You are thus advised to carefully think through the appointment of your Donees as well as indicate a replacement Donee to cover unexpected situations.

questions.title: Does my Donee need to accompany me when I have my Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) certified?
questions.text: There is no requirement for the Donee(s) to be present when the Certificate Issuer (CI) witnesses and certifies on the LPA. However, some CIs may prefer that the Donee(s) are present so that the CI can explain the Donee’s duties to them. Hence, it would be best for Donors to check with the CI beforehand.

questions.title: What if I do not have anyone suitable around me to be my Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS)?
questions.text:
If you’ve appointed or are intending to appoint a Professional Deputy as a Donee in your Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), you can appoint the same person as your NHS. Make sure they are agreeable before you appoint them. You can find more details and the list of Professional Deputies on the Ministry of Social and Family Development website.
Alternatively, speak to an ACP facilitator to document and register your ACP. They’ll be able to guide you in making decisions on your healthcare preferences.
Some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: How to get started on doing an Advance Care Planning (ACP) and how much does it cost?
questions.text:
You can complete your ACP in 2 ways:
1. Complete your ACP digitally through myACP or if you prefer to speak to an ACP facilitator, you can book an appointment with an ACP service provider to discuss your healthcare preferences with an ACP facilitator. You may find an ACP service provider via website: Find an Advance Care Planning service provider - MyLegacy@LifeSG.
Your completed ACP will be updated in the National Health Electronic Record (NEHR) and be assessable to healthcare providers.
There are no fees involved to complete and register your ACP using the myACP online service. However, if you make an appointment with an ACP facilitator, some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Cost may vary, please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: When will my doctors act on the wishes in my Advance Care Planning (ACP)? When will it take into effect?
questions.text:
An ACP is effective only when the individual loses their mental capacity and is unable to make decisions for themselves. In such a scenario, the healthcare team will take into account your preferences, together with their medical assessments, to provide the appropriate treatment and care that is in your best interest.
As long as you have mental capacity, you will be consulted on your healthcare preferences.

questions.title: What are the difference(s) between ACP, Advance Medical Directive (AMD) and Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
AMD and LPA are legal documents, while ACP is not.
AMD is to inform the doctor treating you (in the event you become terminally ill and unconscious) that you do not want any extraordinary life-sustaining treatment to be used to prolong your life.
LPA allows you to appoint one or more trusted persons (Donees) to act on your behalf for personal welfare and/or property and affairs matters should you lose mental capacity to make your own decisions.
ACP is useful because it would serve as a guide for your loved ones and healthcare team to act according to your best interests in the event that you are unable to make decisions or speak for yourself. The ACP will include healthcare preferences such as extent of treatment, pain control options etc. It also allows you to appoint up to 2 Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons (NHS) to speak on your behalf when you cannot speak for yourself.

questions.title: Must my Advance Care Planning (ACP) Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS) be my LPA Donee?
questions.text:
No, you do not have to appoint your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers to be your ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson.
However, you’re encouraged to do so, to reduce conflicting decisions made by your Donee and NHS.
An LPA grants your Donee the legal rights to make decisions for you if you’re unable to do so, but it does not tell your Donee what to do for your Personal Welfare. An ACP helps you to communicate to your Donee what decisions they should make for your personal welfare. This includes decisions such as where you should live, who you should live with, your daily lifestyle and healthcare decisions.
Because of this, appointing your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers as your ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson will help to avoid conflicts amongst your loved ones.

questions.title: How to check the deceased's insurance policy?
questions.text:
Each insurance provider may have their own processes with regards to the release of information related to a deceased policyholder.
You can check with the insurance company on the necessary documentation needed such as a death certificate and proof of your relationship to the deceased, to establish your legitimacy in seeking this information.

questions.title: Can I nominate my family members who are not a Singaporean/ Permanent Resident as my CPF Nominees?
questions.text: CPF members can nominate any person in their nominations, including those who are non-Singaporeans / Permanent Residents.

questions.title: If the deceased passed on without a will and did not make a CPF nomination. Will CPF contact the next-of-kin directly or do we need to appoint an administrator ourselves?
questions.text:
If a member did not make a CPF nomination, upon his/her passing, his/her CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws (for Muslims).
The next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration and approach PTO to proceed with the distribution. PTO will charge an administrative fee for this service. You may read more here.

questions.title: If a person nominates the religion organization under their CPF nomination, will CPF inform the organization?
questions.text:
Nominations are confidential. CPFB will not disclose your nomination details to anyone, including your nominee(s).
This will only be done when you pass away. You are encouraged to keep your nominees informed yourself, should you wish for them to know of the CPF Nomination.

questions.title: How to check the deceased’s CPF nomination?
questions.text: You may refer to this FAQ from CPFB for more details.

questions.title: How do I bring ashes back to Singapore from overseas?
questions.text:
If you wish to bring human ashes back to Singapore, you will have to:
place the ashes in a covered urn or container during travel (choose a non-metallic urn so that they can be x-rayed during security screenings).
make sure that a copy of the death certificate and cremation certificate (both in English) are accompanying the urn during travel. You will need to get an English translation of these documents if they are issued in another language. Translations from private organizations are accepted.
contact the airline to find out whether you can carry the ashes as hand luggage or as checked-in luggage.
There is no requirement for a permit to bring human ashes back to Singapore. However, each country has its own rules about departing with human ashes and there may be additional requirements. Contact the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission for advice.

questions.title: Once someone passes on, can I directly proceed to Mandai crematorium to cremate immediately? Do I need to book with NEA?
questions.text:
For post-death matters related to cremation, you can refer to this webpage on My Legacy.
You do need to apply for a permit to cremate via the NEA ePortal. You should submit only one application.
If you need to make changes or cancel the approved permit, contact the service counter at Mandai Crematorium directly.
To book a cremation slot at Mandia Crematorium, you can:
Visit the Mandai Crematorium Service Counter (during opening hours)
Book online using the NEA ePortal
Your funeral director can help you with this. If you need to make changes to the date or time of the confirmed booking, please do so in person at the Mandai Crematorium Service Counter.

questions.title: If godparents who have no next-of-kin pass on and would like their godchild to manage their post-death matters, how will the godchild be able to apply for cremation and permit for ash scattering?
questions.text:
A person who is not a next-of-kin may still apply for a permit to cremate and act on behalf of the decease if:
a next-of-kin has authorised them to do so
the deceased has appointed them as an executor for their estate
The non‑NOK will need a Letter of Authorisation (LOA) from the deceased’s next‑of‑kin. The LOA template is available at: https://go.gov.sg/loa-nea-adfs.
When submitting the cremation or burial permit application on NEA’s e‑portal, please upload the completed LOA as part of the application. If you encounter issues with the submission and the matter is not resolved within 24 hours, please contact MyLegacy at go.gov.sg/edc for assistance.
You may visit NEA's website for more information on post-death matters related to cremation and ash scattering here for more information.

questions.title: Is burial cost a recurring fee or one time only cost?
questions.text:
The Choa Chu Kang Cemetery Complex is the only cemetery in Singapore open for burials that is managed by the National Environment Agency (NEA). The burial fee as indicated in NEA's website is a once-off payment.
The payment of the burial fee for the grave plot is to be made at the service counters before burial. Foreigners are allowed to be buried in Singapore only if the deceased persons have immediate family members who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents. More information related to burial can be found at NEA's website.

questions.title: How to find the approved funeral services providers/undertakers that handles HIV deceased. Is it a must for the deceased to be buried or cremated within 24 hours?
questions.text: The list of approved funeral services providers that could handle HIV deceased can be found in the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) website. There is no requirement for HIV deceased to be buried or cremated within 24 hours.

questions.title: How can I arrange for relocation of niche from Mandai to Chua Chu Kang ?
questions.text:
To relocate the niche from Mandai Columbarium to Choa Chu Kang Columbarium, the Original Applicant (OA) must make two applications.*
(1) 'Application for Removal of Urn(s) and Surrender Niche Lease' at Mandai Columbarium. This will initiate the process of relocation.
(2) Followed by 'Application of Niche in Government Managed Columbarium' submitted to Choa Chu Kang Columbarium.
*These 2 applications can be made concurrently. You can indicate the date you wish to remove the urn (from Mandai) and install (at Choa Chu Kang) in the respective applications after you have work out these dates with the contractor.
In cases where the OA is unavailable to carry out these transactions personally, they may provide written authorization for a family member or third party to act on their behalf.
If the OA has passed away, the new applicant is required to present proof of the OA's death (such as a death certificate issued by ICA), followed by making a statutory declaration to proceed with the application.
There is no service fee for surrendering the niche lease. However, there are charges for applying for a new niche at Choa Chu Kang Columbarium, as outlined below:
Standard Niche - $500
Family Niche - $900
An additional selection fee of $250 will be imposed if you wish to select a specific niche location. Otherwise, the system will automatically allocate a niche sequentially based on its allocation logic.
Should you have any further feedback or suggestion, please contact NEA via OneService or the myENV mobile applications. Alternatively, you may reach NEA via this Online Feedback Form.

questions.title: What are the operating hours of this e-Service?
questions.text: The e-Resale system is available 24 hours a day, including Sundays and Public Holidays.

questions.title: Is the helpdesk available 24 hours, 7 days a week?
questions.text: For assistance on resale policies and procedures, you can write to us.

questions.title: I am a salesperson submitting application on behalf of my clients (i.e. buyers or sellers). Upon logging in, I encounter an error message "You are not the salesperson of this estate agent". Why should I do?
questions.text:
Please check against the CEA's Public Register to ensure that your name is updated under the correct estate
agent.

questions.title: What is the security feature in protecting the information transmitted through e-Resale system?
questions.text: The e-Resale system protects the information transmitted by using the SSL (Secure Socket Layer).

questions.title: For online payment by credit card, what is the hardware or software required?
questions.text:
For credit card payments, no special hardware or software is required. When the credit card payment option
is invoked, you will be prompted to key in your name, credit card number and the card expiry date.

questions.title: Who can submit the Request for Value?
questions.text:
Only buyers who have been granted an Option to Purchase by the flat owners can submit the request. The
buyers (or their salesperson) must submit to HDB the Request for Value, together with scanned copy of page 1of
the OTP, by the next working day after the Option Date.

questions.title: What is the information required to submit a Request for Value?
questions.text: To submit a Request for Value, you will need to prepare the following information:

questions.title: Can I change the photo after submitting the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application online?
questions.text: Once you have clicked the 'Submit' button for your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application, you will not be able to make further changes to your photo attachment.

questions.title: Can I retrieve and re-submit my ABTC application If there is an error in the information submitted?
questions.text: The e-Service on APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application will prompt you to check that the information that you have keyed in is correct before you submit the application. Once you click the submit button, you will not be able to make any changes to your online application.

questions.title: Can I submit an APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application on behalf of another person?
questions.text: The applicant is required to submit the ABTC application personally as the applicant's Singpass is required.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my ABTC application submitted previously and re-submit a new one?
questions.text: The withdrawal and re-submission of the ABTC application is at your discretion. However, the fee paid for the current application is non-refundable and you will have to make payment for the new application. The new application will be assessed on its own merits by the participating economies.

questions.title: How do I know whether my APEC Business Travel Card application has been submitted successfully?
questions.text: An acknowledgement page will be displayed when your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application is successfully submitted. You are advised to print the acknowledgement page for reference.

questions.title: How do I know which are the economies that I can travel to using my ABTC card?
questions.text:
The economies will be listed on your card according to the following economy codes:
AUS - Australia
BRN - Brunei Darussalam
CHL - Chile
CHN - People's Republic of China
TWN - Chinese Taipei
HKG - Hong Kong, China
IDN - Indonesia
JPN - Japan
KOR - Republic of Korea
MYS - Malaysia
MEX - Mexico
NZL - New Zealand
PNG - Papua New Guinea
PER - Peru
PHL - The Philippines
RUS - Russia
SGP - Singapore
THA - Thailand
VNM - Vietnam
Cardholders can also use the fast-track immigration lanes (currently designated for air-crew) at all international airports in the USA and designated airports in Canada. However, ABTC holders will still be subjected to the existing immigration clearance process applicable to travellers entering the USA and Canada. This is because these two economies are not participating economies of the ABTC Scheme.
Please refer to APEC Business Travel Card for information about arrangements at airports, length of stay permitted, etc.

questions.title: How do I resubmit documents for my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application?
questions.text: You can submit the additional documents for your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application via the online form.

questions.title: How would I know the status of my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application?
questions.text: You will be notified by email if the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application is successful. Alternatively, you can check the status of your application online.

questions.title: What are the required documents when submitting an APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application?
questions.text: Please refer to APEC Business Travel Card for more information. You will need to prepare a digital photograph according to the photo guidelines.

questions.title: What can I do if I am unable to upload my signature for APEC Business Travel Card application?
questions.text: You can submit an enquiry on your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application via the online enquiry form.

questions.title: Why am I not able to access the e-service to apply for the APEC Business Travel Card?
questions.text:
You may wish to check your internet settings on your browser and disable the pop-up blocker before submitting the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application.
You will also not be allowed to submit an ABTC application if your passport is expiring within 9 months. You can submit the ABTC application after you have collected your new passport.

questions.title: Will I be able to obtain the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) if a participating economy rejects my application?
questions.text: You can still obtain the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC), as long as there are other economies that have approved your application. In this case, your card will not bear the economy code of the economies that have rejected your application, and you are not eligible to enjoy the facilities provided by these economies when you travel there. Your entry to that economy will be subjected to their prevailing requirements, which may include having to apply for an entry visa.

questions.title: How do I cancel the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) due to resignation or change of company?
questions.text:
You can contact us via the enquiry form if you wish to cancel the ABTC due to resignation or change of company.
Please note that you are required to apply for a new ABTC if you have joined another company.
topics: APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) / Cancellation of Card

questions.title: What happens if no one is home to receive the registered mail on APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text: Your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) will be delivered to your mailbox, according to current guidelines for delivery of registered mail by SingPost.

questions.title: What if I do not receive my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) after I receive the email notification?
questions.text: You can submit an enquiry on your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application via the online enquiry form.

questions.title: Where can I collect my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text:
If your ABTC application is approved, your card will be mailed to your residential address that is reflected on your Singapore Identity Card.
Please ensure that your address is promptly updated with ICA to avoid delivery issues. If any card reprint is required due to an outdated address, do note that additional fees will apply. Delivery to overseas addresses may take longer.

questions.title: Will I be notified when I can receive my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text: You will be notified by e-mail once your ABTC is ready. The delivery of the ABTC takes about 7 working days, and will take longer for overseas addresses.

questions.title: Who is eligible to apply for an APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) with ICA?
questions.text:
Singapore citizens are eligible to apply for the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) with ICA:
Bona fide business person (i.e. those who represent an economically-active business entity)
Members of professional bodies such as doctors, lawyers and other members of professional bodies
Public officers from Ministries, Government departments, economic agencies and statutory boards who need to travel in their official capacity
All applicants must have a valid Singapore Passport.
You can refer to the ICA website for more information on ABTC application.

questions.title: Can APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) be used when travelling for personal trips?
questions.text: ABTC is strictly for business use only and should not be used for personal trips.

questions.title: Can I still travel with my existing ABTC during the renewal process?
questions.text: You may travel with your existing ABTC provided that there is no change in your passport details.

questions.title: Can I use the APEC lane together with my family members?
questions.text: The APEC lane may only be used by APEC Business Travel Card holders.

questions.title: Do I have to replace my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) if I change my personal particulars?
questions.text: You have to apply for a replacement card under the category of "Change of Singapore Passport". You should first replace your IC to update your personal particulars and obtain a new Singapore passport before you can replace your ABTC.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a new ABTC upon expiry if my passport remains valid after my ABTC expires?
questions.text: The validity of the ABTC is 5 years or up to the validity of the passport, whichever is shorter. Should you require a new ABTC upon the expiry of your existing ABTC, although your passport is still valid, you need to apply for a new ABTC.

questions.title: Do I need to replace my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) if I have renewed or replaced my passport?
questions.text:
You must apply for a new ABTC if you have renewed or replaced your passport. You may do so by applying under the category "Change of Singapore Passport". Please submit an application to replace your ABTC only after you have collected your new passport as you would need to provide the information of your new passport in the ABTC application.
If you replace your passport while your ABTC application is still being processed, please withdraw your ABTC application and submit a new application.
You can contact us via the enquiry form to withdraw your application. Do note that no refund will be given for the withdrawn application.

questions.title: How do I report the loss of my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) card?
questions.text: You are advised to apply for a replacement ABTC at a fee of $50. The replacement card will bear the same date of expiry as the original card.

questions.title: How long can an ABTC holder stay in a participating APEC member economies?
questions.text: An ABTC holder can stay between 60 to 90 days in participating economies. The exact period of stay will be advised by the participating economies’ immigration upon the traveller’s arrival in that economy.

questions.title: What are the fees for the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text:
The relevant fees for the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application are as follows:
Types of Application
Fee
Validity of ABTC
a) New application
S$100
For new ABTC applications submitted: Valid for five years, or up to the validity of the passport, whichever is shorter

v. Loss and change of particulars (as reflected in your passport)
S$100
For ABTC applications submitted: Valid for five years, or up to the validity of the passport, whichever is shorter

questions.title: What documents should I provide for my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application if I have an overseas company registered under Singapore?
questions.text: You can provide either ACRA Business profile or Overseas Business Profile for your APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application if the company is registered in both Singapore and overseas.

questions.title: What is APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text:
The ABTC scheme aims to facilitate movement of business travellers between APEC member economies. Cardholders enjoy the following benefits:
Streamlined processing through designated lanes at the airports and entry points of participating economies.
Without having to make a separate visa application, pre-cleared cardholders will be able to travel to and enter the participating economies for business purposes; and stay up to 60 or 90 days.
Please note that the ABTC is not meant to replace the passport as a travel document. You will still need a valid passport to travel. It remains the right of each economy to determine who may travel to, enter and remain in that economy even after a person has been issued with the ABTC.
You can refer to the ICA Website for more information on ABTC.

questions.title: What is the difference between the interim and the final APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text:
The interim card for APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) will bear fewer economy codes compared to the final card as not all economies would have granted clearance when the interim card is issued. Your entry to the economies (not listed in the interim card) will be subject to their prevailing requirements, which may include the application for an entry visa.
The interim card will also have a different document number from the final card.
The conditions of use of the interim card is no different from the final card i.e.:
Cardholders are required to carry a valid passport that tallies with the passport details listed on the card;
It remains the right of each economy to determine who may travel to, enter and remain in that economy even after a person has been issued with the ABTC. Normal immigration, customs and entry conditions otherwise apply during a visit to a participating economy.

questions.title: What is the validity of the APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text: Currently, each ABTC is valid for 5 years, or up to the validity of the passport, whichever is shorter.

questions.title: What should I do if my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) card is damaged?
questions.text: You are advised to apply for a replacement ABTC at a fee of $50. The replacement card will bear the same date of expiry as the original card.

questions.title: What should I do if my APEC Business Travelling Card (ABTC) is lost in transit?
questions.text: You may replace your lost ABTC at a fee of $50.

questions.title: What should I do with the interim APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) after I have received my final card?
questions.text: You should destroy your interim APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) by cutting it into half and only use the final card for your travel to the participating economies. The interim card is no longer valid once the final card is issued. You may be inconvenienced if you use an outdated card.

questions.title: Who should I contact for enquiries on APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text: You can submit your enquiry on APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) via the online enquiry form.

questions.title: Why must I pay a fee for a new card when a new economy joins the ABTC scheme?
questions.text:
Any changes to the information on the card issued will be treated as a new application, as the application will be subjected to another round of clearance by the participating economies, including the newly-joined one.
If you have not been pre-cleared by the economy concerned (i.e. your card does not bear the name of that foreign economy), your entry to that economy will be subjected to their prevailing requirements, which may include the application for an entry visa. You will also not be able to use the ABTC facilities provided by that economy when you travel there.

questions.title: Will my current ABTC card be affected due to the change in the validity of passport?
questions.text: The validity of the ABTC is 5 years or up to the validity of the passport, whichever is shorter. However, if your Singapore passport number has changed, you need to apply for a new ABTC under the category of 'replacement due to change of particulars'. You should submit an application only after you have collected your new passport.

questions.title: What are the payment modes available for APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application?
questions.text:
All ABTC applications must be made online and be paid for by using:
VISA or MasterCard credit/ debit cards; or
American Express (AMEX) Card; or
Internet banking (DBS/ POSB, OCBC, UOB and Standard Chartered Bank banking account in Singapore); or
PayNow.
Please refer to the ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.

questions.title: What should I do if payment is not successful for my APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) application?
questions.text:
If you are submitting a new application and payment is not successful, please clear the browser cache and re-submit the application via the e-Service.
If you are submitting a renewal application and payment is not successful, you will receive an email with instructions to complete payment.
(Note: ICA e-Service is optimized for Edge, Firefox, Chrome and Safari).

questions.title: What should I do if I am not able to upload my photo image for my ABTC application online?
questions.text:
You should check the details of the error message. Please note the following photo criteria:
jpg, jpeg, heic, heif and png file extension format
Preferred dimension is 400 x 514 pixels
File size is not more than 8MB
The above criteria must be fulfilled for the photo to be accepted in e-Service.
You may refer to the photo guidelines for more information. Do note that your photo image will be checked by ICA according to our requirements after successful upload.
topics: APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) / Technical Enquiries

questions.title: Who is eligible to use the automated lanes and what are the requirements?
questions.text:
All foreign visitors arriving in Singapore, regardless of nationality, can use automated lanes without the need for prior enrolments. You will need to produce the following to use the automated lanes:
The registered passport that is valid for more than 6 months or a valid QR Code generated from the MyICA mobile app
A submitted SG Arrival Card
A valid Singapore visa (if applicable)
You will need to provide a valid email address in your SG Arrival Card submission to receive your Visit Pass (e-Pass) when using the automated lanes. You will not be issued with an arrival immigration endorsement in your passport.

questions.title: Can I request for the inked immigration endorsement?
questions.text: From 11 March 2022, all foreign visitors arriving in Singapore will receive an electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) through email in lieu of inked endorsement stamps on the passport. The e-Pass will contain details of the visit pass granted, including the maximum number of day(s) of stay and the last day of stay allowed in Singapore.

questions.title: How do I know which lanes to use for automated clearance upon arrival at the checkpoints?
questions.text: There will be signages to inform visitors to use the automated lanes for immigration clearance at the passenger hall of the respective checkpoints.

questions.title: Is there a validity period once I am eligible to use the automated lanes?
questions.text: You can use the automated lanes as long your registered passport is valid for more than 6 months and you have a valid visa, if required. Your eligibility for automated clearance will be re-assessed during clearance at the immigration counter when you change to a new passport.

questions.title: Do I need to update my new passport details if the registered passport for BIKES has expired?
questions.text:
For Singapore Passport Holders
You do not need to update your new passport information separately every time you renew your passport.
For Non-Singapore Passport Holders
You will need to update your new passport details with the relevant e-Services:
For Singapore Permanent Residents (via ICA e-Service on REP Renew/Transfer)
For Long-Term Pass holders registered with ICA
Travel Document update for Long-Term Visit Pass holders
Travel Document update for Student's Pass holders
For Holders of a Work Pass (Work Permit, S Pass, Employment Pass or Dependant's Pass) (with Ministry of Manpower (MOM) via MOM website)
The service is free-of-charge.

questions.title: How do I clear through automated gates if I am newly registered with BIKES?
questions.text:
You will use the same passport that you have registered for BIKES at the automated gates for immigration clearance.
You may refer to the ICA website for more information on how to use the registered passport for clearance at the BIKES gates.

questions.title: What is Biometric Identification of Motorbikers (BIKES)?
questions.text:
The Biometric Identification of Motorbikers (BIKES) System uses biometric technology to provide efficient and secure automated immigration clearance for eligible and registered motorcyclists at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints.
You may refer to the ICA website for more information on automated clearance for bikes.

questions.title: Can my child use the automated lanes if he/ she is below 6 years old?
questions.text:
Travellers with children under 6 years of age may use the Special Assistance Lanes (SAL), available at Changi Airport Terminal Halls, Seletar Airport, Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore, Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal, Woodlands Bus Hall, and Tuas Bus Hall for immigration clearance.
Each SAL can accommodate family groups of up to 4 people, allowing the child and their accompanying parents, caretakers, or companions to clear immigration together.

questions.title: Do I need to update my new passport details if the registered passport for automated clearance has expired?
questions.text:
For Singapore Passport Holders
You do not need to update your new passport information separately every time you renew your passport
For Non-Singapore Passport Holders
You will need to update your new passport details with the relevant e-Services:
For Singapore permanent residents (via ICA e-Service on REP Renew/ Transfer)
For Long-Term Pass holders registered with ICA
Travel Document update for Long-Term Visit Pass holders
Travel Document update for Student's Pass holders
Ministry of Manpower (MOM) if you are Employment/ Dependant's Pass holders (via MOM website).
The service is free-of-charge.

questions.title: What is New Clearance Concept (NCC)?
questions.text:
Under the New Clearance Concept (NCC), all travellers will enjoy automated clearance[1], and all Singapore residents and eligible foreign travellers will enjoy immigration clearance without having to present their passport.
There are 2 types of passport-less immigration clearance, to provide travellers with hassle-free and faster clearance:
Token-less clearance at air and sea checkpoints: Singapore residents[2] at both arrival and departure, and all foreign travellers at departure, clear immigration using simply facial and iris biometrics, without the need to present their passport.
QR code clearance at land checkpoints: Travellers use a QR code, instead of presenting their passport, during immigration clearance.[3]
[1] Children below the age of 6 years will not be able to use the automated lanes for immigration clearance.
[2] Singapore residents include Singapore citizens, permanent residents and long-term pass holders.
[3] First-time foreign visitors and those re-entering Singapore using a different passport from the previous trip will need to present their passport for immigration clearance. They will be able to clear immigration using QR code on their subsequent trips.

questions.title: How do I change my child’s race if the other parent has passed away or is uncontactable?
questions.text:
In the case where one parent has passed away, the other parent may submit an application to change the child’s race, with a copy of the other parent's death certificate.
The parent (applicant) who is applying for the race change is required to declare the following:
- The other parent/ legal guardian(s) is no longer alive and has not appointed any legal guardian in respect of the above-listed minor.
In the case where one parent is uncontactable, an Order of Court empowering the other parent to change the child’s race unilaterally will be required.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Change of Particulars

questions.title: How do I change the race of my child to follow mine after my divorce or separation from my husband?
questions.text:
If your child is below 21 years old, the consent of both parents is required before the child's race can be changed.
An application to change the child’s race can be submitted at this link:
https://go.gov.sg/ica-race-dialect
If your child is an IC holder, he/ she will be required to apply for a replacement of IC at ICA. The prevailing fee for replacement of IC will apply.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Change of Particulars

questions.title: How do I apply for a change in race? Is there any fee involved?
questions.text:
You are allowed to change your race twice: once before the age of 21, and once at or after the age of 21.
A Singapore citizen, who is 21 years old and above, may submit an application to change his/ her race. For Singapore citizens below 21 years old, one of their parents will be required to submit the application.
ICA does not charge a fee to effect a change in race. However, in cases where the Singapore citizen is an IC holder, he/ she will need to apply for a replacement of IC at ICA. The prevailing fee for replacement of IC will apply.
You may refer to the ICA website for more information on change of race.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Change of Particulars

questions.title: What are the documents required to remove parent's name on the (digital) birth certificate?
questions.text: You can email the identification documents of both parents and the relevant DNA test results to ICA_RBD@ica.gov.sg.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Change of Particulars

questions.title: Can I convert physical death certificate into digital format?
questions.text: Death certificates issued after 29 May 2022 are in digital format. Death certificates issued before this date remain valid and will not be converted into digital format.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Can I download the digital death certificate from My Legacy after 30 days? If yes, any fee involved?
questions.text: The next of kin may contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Do I need to download the digital death certificate if I have a Confirmation of Death?
questions.text:
The Confirmation of Death is only a temporary document. You should download the digital death certificate at the My Legacy website, following online death certification by the doctor.
To do so, you will need to make use of the following information from the Confirmation of Death: Confirmation of Death Number, Deceased's ID Number and Date of Death.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Do I need to surrender the deceased's NRIC to the police station or ICA for physical invalidation?
questions.text:
There is no longer a need to surrender the deceased’s NRIC for physical invalidation. The deceased’s NRIC will be automatically invalidated in ICA’s system once the death is registered.
To prevent misuse, you may either destroy the invalidated NRIC, or punch a hole in it.
The use of another person’s NRIC is an offence under the National Registration Act, which carries a penalty of a fine not exceeding $10,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years, or both.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: How do I report death that occurred overseas?
questions.text:
If a Singapore citizen or permanent resident had passed on overseas, you should register the death and get a death certificate from the foreign authorities in the country where the person had passed on. You can then report the death to ICA with the foreign death certificate to update ICA's records.
Please refer to the ICA website for more information on Report Death that Occurred Overseas.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Is there a limit on number of people who can download the digital death certificate from My Legacy?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of persons who can download, but there is a 30-day limit from the date of death to download the certificate from the My Legacy website. You should save a copy in your personal device when downloading the certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of times I can download the digital death certificate from My Legacy?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of times you can download the digital death certificate, but there is a 30-day limit from the date of death to download the certificate from the My Legacy website. You should save a copy in your personal device when downloading the certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What can I do if I am unable to apply for the permit to bury/cremate with a Confirmation of Death?
questions.text: You may contact National Environment Agency for assistance if you encounter difficulties using the Confirmation of Death document to apply for the permit to bury or cremate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do if I cannot download the digital certificate with the Confirmation of Death number?
questions.text:
You may contact the certifying doctor/hospital to confirm if the death information has been submitted online and to obtain the Death Certificate Number from him.
You may then use the Death Certificate Number to download the digital certificate from My Legacy.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do if I did not receive information to download the death certificate from the hospital?
questions.text: You must return to or contact the hospital concerned to obtain the required information.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do if I have misplaced the information from the doctor to download the death certificate?
questions.text:
If it is within 30 days from the date of death, you can request the certifying doctor or hospital for the information.
If it is more than 30 days from the date of death, you may email ICA at ICA_DPU_RBD@ica.gov.sg for assistance.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do with the incorrect death certificate after I received the updated certificate?
questions.text: The death certificate issued earlier is no longer valid. If a copy has been stored in your personal device, please delete it and cease using it for any transaction.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What is a Confirmation of Death?
questions.text:
It is a temporary document issued by the doctor in lieu of a death certificate during system downtime, or when the next-of-kin does not have digital access to download the digital certificate.
This document is accepted by NEA and Town Councils for funeral, burial or cremation related applications.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: What should I do if there is incorrect information in the digital death certificate?
questions.text:
If it is within 6 months from the date of death, you may approach the certifying doctor to amend the information. Once notified by the doctor that the information has been corrected, you can download the updated death certificate from the My Legacy website within 30 days from the amendment date.
If it is after 6 months, please email ICA at ICA_DPU_RBD@ica.gov.sg with the details.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Will there still be physical death certificates issued?
questions.text: All deaths certified on and after 29 May 2022 will be issued with a digital (PDF) death certificate. The next-of-kin can download and save a copy from the My Legacy website and print it if required.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Can I change my first component race of my double-barrelled race to facilitate my flat application?
questions.text: HDB will only recognise the records registered with the ICA in the administration of the Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP). Those with a double-barrelled race who wish to make changes to their race must comply with ICA's requirements on such changes. Details on the policy and registration procedures can be found on the ICA Website.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: Can I register my child with double-barrelled race if the sibling was registered with singular race?
questions.text:
All siblings who are below 21 years old from the same set of parents should have the same recorded race. This does not apply to siblings who are 21 years old or above.
The parents may submit an application to change race for the affected child(ren).
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: How much does it cost to register a double-barrelled race for my child?
questions.text: There is no separate charge for registering a double-barrelled race for your child. The fee of S$18 for the issuance of a birth certificate applies.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: Is switching the order of my child’s race from Indian-Malay to Malay-Indian considered a change?
questions.text: This is considered a race change request. The request will also be treated as one count of race change application.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: What is the double-barrelled race option for birth registration?
questions.text:
Since 1 January 2011, ICA has implemented the registration of double-barrelled race options for Singaporean children born to parents of different races. Singaporeans born before 1 January 2011 to parents of different races may request for a change from a singular to double-barrelled race if they fulfill the eligibility criteria.
Declaring or changing one's race is a serious matter that should not be taken lightly. If you are considering doing so, you will need to carefully deliberate the impact and implications of the change.
The general information on the implementation of the double-barrelled race registration are listed for reference. For further queries, you may contact ICA at ICA_RBD@ica.gov.sg
Eligibility
A child born on or after 1 January 2011 to parents of different races will be eligible to register for a double-barrelled race during birth registration.
Important Information to Note
Parents who wish to register a double-barrelled race for their child should take note of the following:
(a) For relevant Government policies, such as the initial assignment to a mother-tongue language class in schools and the HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy, the first component of a double-barrelled race will be used. There will not be any advantage in terms of policy considerations for those who register either a double-barrelled or a singular race.
(b) If both parents are each registered with a double-barrelled race and wish to register a double-barrelled race for their child, the first component race of the child must be taken from the first component race of either parent. For example, if one spouse is Malay-Chinese and the other is Indian-Thai, the first component race for the child can only be Malay or Indian.
(c) All siblings should have the same recorded race.
- Parents will be asked to indicate the race of their first-born child when registering the race of their subsequent children. In cases where their first-born child/children were born before 1 January 2011, parents will be allowed to register a double-barrelled race for their subsequent children so long as parents apply to change the race of their children born before 1 Jan 2011 to a double-barrelled race.
- Once the parents have registered a child with a double-barrelled race on or after 1 January 2011, any subsequent children will have to follow the same race. If the situation requires a change of race, all siblings must change their race together. This would not be necessary for siblings 21 years of age and above. Exceptions may be allowed on a case-by-case basis.
(d) A Singaporean is allowed to change his race twice; once before the age of 21 and once at or after the age of 21.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: Would Singaporean with double-barrelled race enjoy more benefits than those with singular race?
questions.text: Singaporeans who are registered with a double-barrelled race do not enjoy more benefits as compared to those with a singular race. For relevant Government policies, such as the initial assignment to a mother-tongue language class in schools and the HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy, only the first component race of a double-barrelled race will be considered. There will not be any advantage in terms of policy considerations for those who register either a double-barrelled or a singular race.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Double-Barelled Race

questions.title: Can I request for a physical extract?
questions.text: After 27 March 2023, all extracts are issued in digital format. No physical copy will be issued. You may print out the extract and approach the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) for legalisation of the document, if required.

questions.title: How do I check the application status for the extract or search that I had applied for?
questions.text: You may enquire the status of your extract or search application at the e-Service. You will need your application reference number and e-mail address provided during application to access this function.

questions.title: I have received a digital certificate of extract. How do I verify if it is genuine?
questions.text:
Please scan the QR code embedded in the digital certificate of extract to verify it online at ICA website.
Alternatively, you may visit ICA website > Verify Digital Certificate (https://go.gov.sg/ica-verify-ecerts) to verify the digital certificate.

questions.title: Can I travel to Singapore to give birth?
questions.text: A visitor who intends to give birth in Singapore must apply for permission through a local sponsor. You may refer to the ICA website for more information.

questions.title: Can my child follow his maternal or paternal grandparents' race?
questions.text:
Your child can follow your race, your spouse's race or an acceptable mixed race if you and your spouse are of different races.
A child who is a Singapore citizen is also eligible to register a double-barrelled race comprising both parents’ races.

questions.title: How can I correct an error on a birth certificate?
questions.text: You may email us at ICA_RBD@ica.gov.sg with elaboration and supporting documents about the details to be corrected.

questions.title: How do I check my newborn's citizenship status?
questions.text: A child born in Singapore to legally married parents who are both Singapore citizens (or either one is a Singapore citizen) at the time of child's birth, is automatically a Singapore Citizen.

questions.title: How do I find out my child’s race as declared during birth registration?
questions.text: You may log in to Singpass and view your child’s recorded race in MyInfo.

questions.title: How do I register my newborn's birth in Singapore?
questions.text:
Please refer to the ICA website for more information on the registration of birth in Singapore.
Please note that Singapore does not register births that occurred overseas. Parents should register the child's birth and obtain a birth certificate where the child is born.

questions.title: How many days can a foreign newborn baby stay in Singapore?
questions.text:
You will need to obtain a travel document for your child from the respective Embassy or High Commission within 42 days of your child's birth. Details of the regularisation of the immigration status of a foreign child born in Singapore can be found in the advisory note that is issued together with the digital birth certificate.
You may re-download the advisory note at ICA e-Service within 90 days from the date of birth registration.

questions.title: Must the birth be registered in Singapore for a child born overseas to both Singaporean parents?
questions.text: There is no need for the parents to return to Singapore to register the birth. The parents should register the child's birth and obtain the birth certificate from the country/ place where the child is born.

questions.title: What are the race options available for my child if my spouse and I are of different races?
questions.text:
The race of a child can follow that of either parent, or an acceptable mixed race if the child's parents are of different races. A child who is a Singapore citizen is also eligible to have a double-barrelled race comprising both parents’ races. All siblings of the child who are below 21 years old from the same set of parents should have the same race.
Possible examples of child’s race
Example (1): Father: Chinese; Mother: German
1) Chinese (follow father's race)
2) German (follow mother's race)
3) Eurasian (an acceptable mixed race of European and Asian)
4) Chinese-German (follow father-mother's race)
5) German-Chinese (follow mother-father's race)
Example (2): Father: Indian-Chinese; Mother: Malay-German
Note: For double-barrelled race, the child's first component race must be taken from the first component race of either parent.
1) Indian (follow father's first component race)
2) Malay (follow mother's first component race)
3) Indian-Chinese (follow father's race)
4) Malay-German (follow mother's race)
5) Indian-Malay (combination of father's and mother's first component race)
6) Malay-Indian (combination of mother's and father's first component race)
7) Indian-German (combination of father's first component race and mother's second component race)
8) Malay-Chinese (combination of mother's first component race and father's second component race)

questions.title: Can I name my stillborn child?
questions.text: If you wish to name your stillborn child, you may submit an application for a commemorative birth certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I request for a digital stillbirth certificate if the stillbirth occurred before 29 May 2022?
questions.text: Digital stillbirth certificates will only be issued for stillbirths that are certified by a doctor on and after 29 May 2022.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: Do I need to download the digital stillbirth certificate if I have a Confirmation of Stillbirth?
questions.text:
The Confirmation of Stillbirth is a temporary document. Parents should download the digital stillbirth certificate from My Legacy website after 24 hours, following the stillbirth certification by the doctor.
To do so, you will need the following information from the Confirmation of Stillbirth: Confirmation of Stillbirth Number, Mother’s ID Number and Date of Stillbirth.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do if I am unable to apply for a permit to bury/cremate with a Confirmation of Stillbirth?
questions.text: You may contact National Environment Agency (NEA) for assistance if you encounter difficulties applying for the Permit to Bury/ Cremate with the Confirmation of Stillbirth document.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do if I cannot download digital certificate with the Confirmation of Stillbirth Number?
questions.text:
You may contact the certifying doctor/ hospital to confirm if the stillbirth information has been submitted online and to obtain the Stillbirth Certificate Number from the doctor/hospital.
Thereafter, you can use the Stillbirth Certificate Number to download the digital certificate from My Legacy.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: What do I do with the incorrect stillbirth certificate after I have received the updated copy?
questions.text: The stillbirth certificate issued earlier is no longer valid. If a copy has been stored in your personal device, please delete it and stop using it for any transaction.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: What is a Confirmation of Stillbirth?
questions.text:
It is a temporary document issued by the doctor in lieu of a stillbirth certificate for parents during system downtime, or when the parents do not have digital access to download the digital certificate.
This document is accepted by NEA and Town Councils for funeral, burial or cremation-related applications.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: What should I do if there is incorrect information on the digital stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
If it is within 6 months from the date of stillbirth, you may approach the certifying doctor to amend the information. Once notified by the doctor that the information has been corrected, parents can download the updated stillbirth certificate from the My Legacy website within 30 days from the amendment date.
If it is after 6 months, please email ICA at ICA_DPU_RBD@ica.gov.sg with the details.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Stillbirth Registration Process

questions.title: How do I know if the QR code or URL on the digital certificate is genuine?
questions.text:
You are strongly advised to check the URL in the address bar at the browser.
You may also visit ICA website > Verify Digital Certificate (https://go.gov.sg/ica-verify-ecerts) to verify the digital certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Verification of Digital Certificate

questions.title: Am I required to undergo quarantine?
questions.text: There are quarantine requirements for Yellow Fever. Please refer to the Entering Singapore for full details and entry requirements.

questions.title: What are the immigration requirements to enter Singapore?
questions.text: You may refer to the Entering Singapore page for full details and entry requirements.

questions.title: Do I need to be vaccinated to travel to Singapore?
questions.text:
Vaccination requirements for Yellow Fever are still in place if you have visited Yellow Fever high risk countries.
You can refer to the Entering Singapore page for full details on entry and vaccination requirements.

questions.title: How do we truck the shipment out of FTZ if it is trucked in for export but has been cancelled?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Can photocopied cargo permits be used to clear our shipments?
questions.text:
Traders or drivers may enjoy paperless cargo clearance if you have successfully submitted your vehicle information and the corresponding Cargo Clearance Permit (CCP) numbers for your journey via the ICA e-Service or MyICA Mobile App (under 'Submit cargo clearance').
You are also encouraged to submit supporting documents such as the Master Airway Bill and invoices via TradeNet during permit declaration. If the submission is successful, you are not required to present physical supporting documents at the counter.
Drivers and traders may still use photocopies of approved permits, together with supporting documents to clear their cargoes at the checkpoint. However, you are strongly encouraged to adopt the paperless clearance process.

questions.title: How can I get the list of exchange rates for the purpose of declaring permits?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: How can I make GST payment for my postal articles?
questions.text: For queries pertaining to postal articles, please visit the Singapore Customs website or SingPost website.

questions.title: How do I know whether my cargo is among the Controlled/Restricted items?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: How do I move my cargo from one Free Trade Zone to another?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What are the dutiable items?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What are the procedures to claim the overpaid GST?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What are the supporting commercial documents required for cargo clearance?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What should I do if my cargo clearance permit has expired?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Why has my original shipper's seal been replaced with a green seal bearing "Singapore Customs"?
questions.text:
The original shipper's seal was broken by ICA officer at the checkpoint for inspection of the container and its contents.
After inspection of a container, ICA reseals it with a Customs green seal to safeguard the integrity of the container. Every Customs green seal carries a serial number.
You may refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information on the seal types.

questions.title: Can I break the seal and unstuff my container if it has been affixed with a Customs Red seal?
questions.text: You may refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Can I bring my pet dog, cat or any live animal into Singapore?
questions.text: Please visit the National Parks Board website for more information.

questions.title: Can I perform bulk breaking inside the Free Trade Zone if I have a Class 2 DG container?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Do I need to pay GST if my supplier sends me some trade samples which are not meant for sale?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: How do I clear my imported goods container from the Free Trade Zone?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: How do I clear the Class 2 DG container from the Free Trade Zone?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What are the procedures if I intend to import a consignment of wines for personal consumption?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: What are the procedures if I intend to import medicines into Singapore for my personal consumption?
questions.text: Please visit the Health Science Authority website for more information on importation of medicine.

questions.title: Where can I locate the HS code to declare in the permit if I wish to import a shipment?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Are physical permits or documents required for cargo clearance after I made a SGAC-Cargo submission?
questions.text:
If you have successfully submitted your vehicle information and the corresponding Cargo Clearance Permit (CCP) numbers for your journey via the MyICA Mobile App (under ‘Submit cargo clearance’) or the ICA e-Service, you are not required to present physical CCP(s) for cargo clearance. ICA officers will be able to retrieve the permit information tagged to your vehicle license plate number.
For the relevant export/ transhipment permits, you are required to stop and declare to officers at the checkpoint that you are carrying such permits.
You are also strongly encouraged to upload supporting documents such as commercial invoice, Bill of Lading/ Air WayBill, packing list, and Competent Authority (CA)'s license/ approval, together with the permit application via TradeNet before proceeding to the checkpoints. If you have successfully submitted your supporting documents electronically via TradeNet, you are not required to present physical supporting documents at our counter, thus enabling a paperless clearance process.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: Are we still required to keep physical cargo clearance permits in case of system downtime or issues?
questions.text:
Users will be informed of both scheduled and ad-hoc downtime via the MyICA Mobile App or the ICA e-Service.
Please be informed that submissions made before the downtime would have been stored in ICA's cargo clearance system. Drivers can proceed to the checkpoints without the need to make a new submission. Users who need to make a new submission or amend an earlier submission during system downtime can continue to do so via the MyICA Mobile App (under cargo clearance) or ICA e-Service. A QR code will be generated for each successful submission or amendment. Drivers will need to present the QR code at the checkpoints and no physical copies of cargo clearance permits are required for cargo clearance.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: How do we verify that the cargo permits have been cleared under the new paperless clearance system?
questions.text:
All cargo clearance information will be captured in ICA's systems based on the cargo clearance permit(s) tagged to the vehicle license plate number submitted via the MyICA Mobile App (under cargo clearance) or the ICA e-Service.
Since 6 Jan 2023, traders can view the clearance information via Customs Permit Clearance Enquiry Service (PCES) on the Networked Trade Platform. With the PCES, traders will be required to key in the permit number and a Unique Entity Number (UEN) of the trader or any party involved in the shipment to perform the query. Traders may refer to Singapore Customs Circular No: 02/2023 for more information.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: Is the SGAC-Cargo module applicable to both containerised and conventional cargoes?
questions.text: The SGAC-Cargo module applies to conventional cargoes only. There is no change to the current clearance of containerised cargoes, which has been paperless since 1997.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: What do I do if I need to replace the vehicle for a trip that has been submitted in SGAC-Cargo?
questions.text: Upon every successful submission, you will receive an application reference number. You should use this application reference number to retrieve your submitted details, and change or update the vehicle number accordingly.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: What if system fails to retrieve my permit and vehicle details despite the SGAC-Cargo submission?
questions.text: This may happen when companies or drivers submit an incorrect vehicle number via the MyICA Mobile App (under ‘Submit cargo clearance’) or the ICA e-Service. For instance, if the actual vehicle number is V1234D but V1235D was submitted instead, ICA would not be able to retrieve the permit using V1234D. The driver would be requested to show a screenshot or PDF copy of the submission details on their mobile device to the ICA officer for verification. If further verification is required, the driver would be directed to the secondary office. Hence, it is important to ensure that the correct vehicle number is submitted to minimise such inconveniences.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: What should I do if I have omitted some permits or wish to amend my SGAC-Cargo submission?
questions.text:
Upon every successful submission, you will receive an application reference number. You should use this application reference number to retrieve your submitted details and furnish other permit numbers, or make the necessary amendments required for the trip.
To view/ edit your SGAC Cargo submission via the MyICA mobile app, you may click on the cargo clearance icon and select the relevant submission. Alternatively, you may click on the cargo clearance icon, followed by the search icon located at the top right-hand corner of the page, and enter the application reference number or vehicle number.
To view/ edit your SGAC Cargo submission via the ICA website e-Service, please click on “e-Services and Forms” > “Cargo clearance” > “Apply for paperless clearance for conventional cargo” > “Manage Submission” and enter the application reference number or vehicle number.
It is important to ensure that all the permit numbers required for the trip are correctly submitted prior to making the trip, as no further updates to the SGAC Cargo submission can be made thereafter.
topics: Cargo Clearance / Paperless Clearance for Conventional Cargo

questions.title: How do I cancel my Immigration Exemption Order (IEO)?
questions.text: You will have to inform your embassy to liaise with MFA on your IEO cancellation.

questions.title: What documents do I need to produce to apply for Immigration Exemption Order (IEO)?
questions.text: You will need to work with your respective embassies to liaise with MFA on the requirements for an Immigration Exemption Order (IEO) application.

questions.title: What is Immigration Exemption Order (IEO)?
