As the Early Childhood and Development Agency (ECDA) serves as the regulatory and developmental authority for all ECDCs in Singapore, an application for a Student's Pass may only be submitted for a foreign child enrolling in an ECDA-licensed childcare centre.

questions.title: Why is my Student's Pass validity issued less than what I have applied for?
questions.text: The Student's Pass issued is subjected to prevailing guidelines.

questions.title: Will a Student's Pass Holder be issued a Long-Term Pass automatically upon course completion?
questions.text:
Upon course completion, students will have to cancel their Student's Pass (STP) and surrender any physical STP card that was issued to them for cancellation to ICA. Upon cancellation of their STP, they may be granted a short-term visit pass to stay in Singapore (up to 89 days).
If you are studying in an Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) and wish to have a longer period of stay to look for jobs upon completion of your course, you may apply for a 1-year (non-renewable) Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP).
You may refer to LTVP for Graduate from IHL Seeking Employment in Singapore for more details.

questions.title: Will I be issued a visit pass along with my Student's Pass In-Principle Approval (IPA)?
questions.text: The visit pass is not issued with your Student's Pass In-Principle Approval (IPA). The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officer will issue you with a visit pass if you are eligible for entry into Singapore. After you enter Singapore, you must complete formalities for your Student's Pass before the expiry of your visit pass in order to commence your studies in Singapore. Please ensure that you have a valid immigration pass throughout the whole duration of your stay in Singapore at all times.

questions.title: Will I be penalised if I do not renew my Student's Pass before expiry?
questions.text: If you do not renew your Student's Pass and are not on any valid pass, you will have overstayed in Singapore. Overstaying is an immigration offence. If you overstay, you may be subjected to a composition fine or prosecution in court.

questions.title: Will I receive a refund if I withdraw my Student's Pass application?
questions.text: Please note that the processing fee is non-refundable.

questions.title: Will my Student's Pass be cancelled if I departed Singapore for 3 months?
questions.text: Your Student's Pass (STP) will not be cancelled if you are still studying in your Education Institution. However, if you are no longer studying in your Education Institution, you are required to cancel your STP and surrender any physical STP card that was issued to you upon cancellation of the STP.

questions.title: How do I collect my Student's Pass as a polytechnic or university student?
questions.text:
Off-site enrolment at your Institute of Higher Learning
In collaboration with the Institute of Higher Learning, ICA conducts offsite enrolment on an ad-hoc basis for the enrolment and issuance of Student's passes.
The institution will advise the applicant on the date, time and venue for the offsite enrolment. After the applicant has arrived in Singapore, he/ she is required to report for offsite enrolment as scheduled for the enrolment and issuance of a Student's pass.
Without Off-site enrolment
If you are not scheduled for offsite enrolment by your school, please make an appointment via ICA e-Service for the Student's Pass enrolment and collection. On your appointment date, you may report to ICA Services Centre with the necessary documents as stated in the IPA letter for the enrolment and collection of your Student's Pass.

questions.title: Must my medical examination be done in Singapore in order to be issued a Student's Pass?
questions.text: If you are a new applicant and not in Singapore, the medical examination can either be done in your home country/ place or in Singapore by a qualified doctor. However, the medical examination required for subsequent renewal of the Student's Pass must be done in Singapore. The doctor must record and certify the results of the medical examination in the designated medical report form. The medical report should not be issued more than 3 months from the submission date of your application or renewal. If a medical report was submitted to ICA or MOM not more than 2 years from your submission date, there is no need to re-submit a fresh medical report. (The above requirement is not applicable to applicants who are below 15 years old.)

questions.title: What are the documents that I need to produce for the issuance of my Student's Pass?
questions.text: You will need to furnish the documents stated in your IPA letter, to be issued your Student's Pass.

questions.title: Can I return the replacement pass and use my old card if I found my lost valid Student's Pass card?
questions.text:
You should use your new Student's Pass (STP) issued to you. The lost card is invalidated once you are issued with a replacement STP at ICA.
You should return the invalidated/ expired/ cancelled card to ICA via one of the following ways:
Send by post;
Return to checkpoint officers when departing Singapore; or
Return to ICA Services Centre.
topics: Student's Pass (STP) / Loss of Valid Student's Pass Card

questions.title: Do I have to pay a higher replacement fee if my Student's Pass card has been stolen?
questions.text: Each case will be assessed on its individual merits. Where a decision has been made not to impose a higher replacement fee, you will still have to pay $60 to have your pass replaced, which is levied to recover the processing and issuance cost for the Student's Pass.
topics: Student's Pass (STP) / Loss of Valid Student's Pass Card

questions.title: What are the fees for replacement of Student's pass card due to damage or change of particulars?
questions.text: The fee for the issuance of a new Student's Pass (STP) due to damage or change of particulars will remain at $60 (applicable to physical STP cards and digital STPs). The replacement fee of $60 is levied to recover the cost of processing your application and issuing the new STP.
topics: Student's Pass (STP) / Loss of Valid Student's Pass Card

questions.title: What must I do if I lose my valid Student's Pass card?
questions.text:
Under Regulation 8(5)(c) of the Immigration Regulations, you are required to report the loss of your Student's Pass (STP) card to ICA within 7 days of knowledge of the loss and apply for a replacement Student's Pass.
You may refer to report loss of STP card for more information on the relevant procedures.
topics: Student's Pass (STP) / Loss of Valid Student's Pass Card

questions.title: Am I required to print my receipt as a proof during my completion of formalities for Student's Pass?
questions.text: It is not necessary for you to print if you have a screenshot of the receipt in your mobile phone.

questions.title: Can I seek a refund for the Student's Pass issuance fee?
questions.text: If your application is withdrawn after you have paid the issuance fee, we will process the refund of the issuance fee. The process takes approximately 4 weeks and the amount will be credited to the payee’s account for payment via credit card.

questions.title: Can the Student's Pass processing fees be refunded if my application is not successful?
questions.text: The processing fee is non-refundable regardless of the outcome of the application.

questions.title: How do I make payment for the Student's Pass processing or issuance fees?
questions.text:
Either the foreign student, local sponsor or any member of public can make the necessary payment when the Student's Pass (STP) application status is reflected as “Pending Processing Fee” or “IPA-Pending Issuance Fee”.
Prospective students of Institute of Higher Learning can log in to the e-Service at https://eservices.ica.gov.sg/solar/index.xhtml to make the necessary payment for the STP application.
Prospective students of other education institutions or schools can make payment after logging in to the e-Service at https://eservices.ica.gov.sg/esvclandingpage/solarplus.
Payments must be made via the e-Service using eNets, Credit/ Debit, Internet banking or PayNow. Please refer to ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.

questions.title: When do I make payment for my Student's Pass?
questions.text:
The payment milestones for Student's Pass (STP) are as follows:
A) Payment for STP Processing Fees
You will need to pay the processing fee during the application stage. The e-Service for STP will prompt you that the application is "Pending Processing Fee".
B) Payment for STP Issuance and/ or Visa Fees
If your application is successful, you will need to make payment for the issuance and/ or visa fees. You can arrange to make the necessary payment once the status reflected in the relevant e-Service for Student's Pass is "IPA (Pending Issuance Fee)".
Prospective students of Institute of Higher Learning can make the necessary payment for the STP application at the e-Service.
Prospective students of other education institutions or schools can make the necessary payment for the STP application after selecting the school type and logging in to this e-Service.
The available payment modes in the e-Service are eNets; Credit/ Debit Cards; Internet banking or PayNow.
Please refer to ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.

questions.title: Can I extend my short-term visit pass if the course duration is longer than my current visit pass?
questions.text:
You should sign up for a course that can be completed within the validity of the short-term visit pass granted at the checkpoint.
If the duration of your course is expected to be longer than the duration of your visit pass, you may have to apply for a Student's Pass.
Any extension of visit pass for the said purpose will be considered on its own merits and subjected to approval.

questions.title: Can I extend my stay to take up another short course upon completion of a short course in Singapore?
questions.text:
Any extension of stay (including one for the purpose of attending short courses) will be considered on its own merits.
If you intend to take up more than 1 short course, you are advised to ensure that these courses can be completed within the validity of your short-term visit pass.
You should apply for a Student’s Pass if you intend to take up longer courses.

questions.title: Do I need a Student’s Pass if my course involves occupational training or industrial attachment?
questions.text: You are required to apply for a training pass at the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) if the course involves hands-on practical occupational training and/or industrial attachment, has interaction with walk-in customers, and/or is conducted at premises that are also the places of business, e.g. hair salons and beauty salons. You may refer to Ministry of Manpower (MOM) for more information.

questions.title: Is my entry to Singapore guaranteed if I produce my school's placement letter at the checkpoint?
questions.text:
A school's placement letter does not guarantee your entry into Singapore. The grant of entry will be determined by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority officers at the Singapore checkpoints.
Like other visitors, you will need to satisfy the entry requirements before you can be considered for entry into Singapore.

questions.title: What are the types of courses that I can attend without applying for a Student's Pass?
questions.text:
You are exempted from applying for a Student's Pass to take up a short course provided that:
• It is conducted and completed within the validity of the initial visit pass granted at the Singapore checkpoint or 30 days, whichever is shorter;
• It is a complete and stand-alone module on its own; and
• It does not involve hands-on practical occupational training and/or industrial attachment, which has interaction with walk-in customers, or is not conducted at premises that are also the places of business, e.g. hair salons and beauty salons.

questions.title: As a school representative, can I amend the group size while retaining the group appointment slot?
questions.text: You can make changes to the list of students: reduce or increase the number in the group. (As long as this is done at least 2 days in advance and the group size must not fall below the minimum number.)

questions.title: As a school representative, can I change a group appointment for the school booked by a colleague?
questions.text: You will be allowed to change and view the booking details if you are an authorised school representative of the school.

questions.title: Can I change my appointment for my Student's Pass within the day?
questions.text: You can make changes to your appointment at least 1 day in advance. If you have made a group appointment, changes in appointment need to be at least 2 days in advance.

questions.title: Can I proceed directly to the counters since I have a prior appointment for my Student’s Pass?
questions.text: To ensure those who have made an appointment using ICA e-Service are served on their pre-booked timings, you are required to obtain a queue number ticket at the registration kiosk.

questions.title: How can I complete formalities for Student's Pass if there are no appointment slots left?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: How do I make a group appointment for a group of 15 students?
questions.text: You can book 2 consecutive timeslots for a group of 10 students & another 5 students. (As long as each group size does not fall below the minimum number.)

questions.title: How do I retrieve the school code for group appointment on completion of Student's Pass formalities?
questions.text: You can obtain your school code from the first 6 alphanumeric characters of the STP application number.

questions.title: What if I am late for my appointment for my Student’s Pass?
questions.text: A longer waiting time is expected if you are late for your appointment as those who are on time for their appointments will be prioritised. You are advised to be punctual for your appointment to allow us to serve you promptly.

questions.title: What should I do if I cannot turn up for my appointment for my Student's Pass?
questions.text:
If you are unable to turn up for the scheduled appointment, you may make another appointment at ICA e-Service after your appointment date has lapsed.
Should you miss 2 appointments, you will not be allowed to make further appointment bookings and must complete formalities as a walk-in customer. You should expect a longer waiting time as a walk-in customer, since priority is given to customers with appointments.

questions.title: What should I do when I arrive at the appointment time for my Student’s Pass?
questions.text: You are required to obtain a queue ticket by scanning the bar code on the approval letter at the registration kiosk at the ICA Services Centre. The queue ticket will show your queue number and the designated counter serving you.

questions.title: Can I apply for a visa upon arrival at the checkpoint?
questions.text: The application for a Singapore visa must be submitted and approved prior to arrival in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I enter Tuas Checkpoint by foot or bicycle?
questions.text: Tuas Checkpoint is designated as a vehicular checkpoint, hence entry by foot or bicycle is not allowed.

questions.title: Can I walk out of Tuas Checkpoint to the bus stop nearby to catch the public transport?
questions.text: Tuas Checkpoint is designated as a vehicular checkpoint. Travellers arriving at the checkpoint by a specific mode of transport are expected to leave with that mode of transport after clearance.

questions.title: Can National Service (NS) registrants or NS liable citizens renew the passport at the checkpoints?
questions.text: National Service (NS) registrants or NS liable male citizens should renew their passports before leaving the country.

questions.title: Do I need to clear immigration on arrival if I have an onward connecting flight from Changi Airport?
questions.text:
Visitors who have arrived at Singapore Changi Airport and have been issued with their onward boarding passes for connecting flights out of Changi Airport can remain in the transit area of the airport without seeking immigration clearance, unless directed to do so by the authorities in Changi Airport. For more information on flights connections, please visit the Changi Airport Group website.
If unsure, visitors connecting through Singapore should consult their airline on whether they need to go through immigration, or if they can remain in the transit area to connect to their next flight.

questions.title: Why must a motorcyclist remove his helmet before the ICA officer?
questions.text: Removing the helmet helps to facilitate a proper face-to-face check by the ICA officer. To speed up the clearance process, motorcyclists are advised to remove their helmets when they are next in line. This will cut down the time spent on clearance.

questions.title: What will happen if I overstay in Singapore?
questions.text:
Overstaying is an offence under the Immigration Act. Depending on the number of days you have overstayed, you will be subjected to a composition fine or prosecution in court.
You can submit your application for a Short-Term Visit Pass (STVP) extension via ICA e-Service for ICA's assessment.

questions.title: Do I have to pay GST/ duty if I return to Singapore with unopened bottle(s) of liquor from Singapore?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Where can I process my GST refund?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Can I bring in my goods from overseas to Singapore for repair?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Can I bring in unconsumed cigarettes that I bought prior to arrival in Singapore?
questions.text: Please refer to Singapore Customs FAQs for more information.

questions.title: Can I buy pets and plants and bring them into Singapore?
questions.text: Please visit the National Parks Board website for more information.

questions.title: Can I drive a foreign-registered vehicle into Singapore?
questions.text:
You may refer to Driving In and Out of Singapore and Land Transport Authority for matters relating to driving of foreign vehicles in Singapore e.g. application or extension of vehicle entry permit.
Please also refer to autopass card page for more information.

questions.title: Can I obtain a copy of my travel history?
questions.text: We regret to inform that we are unable to provide travel records of individuals, as information gathered during the immigration clearance process is strictly meant for ICA to carry out its function as an immigration authority.

questions.title: Can Long-Term Pass Holders still travel with a passport which is expiring in 6 months' time or less?
questions.text:
Generally, as long as long-term passes (i.e. Student's Pass, Long Term Visit Pass, Work Permit, Employment Pass and Dependant’s Pass, etc.) are valid, the pass holders are able to use their current valid passport upon seeking arrival and departure immigration clearance at the Singapore checkpoints.
However, they are advised to be mindful of the immigration requirements of any country they wish to depart from, visit or return to when travelling on a passport that is less than 6 months valid before embarking on their journey. Where applicable, they should also check with the airline to ensure that they are allowed to board the plane as airlines have the prerogative to issue boarding passes to their passengers.
As Singapore’s border measures and entry requirements will evolve as the global situation changes, please visit the CDC website and ICA website for the latest updates on travel and health control measures.
It is important for a long-term pass holder to renew his/ her foreign passport if it is expiring. Ensuring that a passport remains valid will allow ICA to determine his/ her foreign citizenship.
For all matters relating to foreign passport, please approach the respective Embassy/ Consulate/ Overseas Mission in Singapore.
Once a new passport is obtained, a long-term pass holder will need to update his/ her new passport details with the relevant issuing authority accordingly.
ICA-issued Long Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holders are required to update his/ her new passport details with ICA accordingly once he/ she has been issued with a new passport.

questions.title: Can tourists visiting Singapore bring in medicines for personal consumption?
questions.text: Please visit the Health Sciences Authority website for more information.

questions.title: Do I need to bring down all my belongings for security checks if I am entering Singapore via bus?
questions.text: All arriving bus passengers are required to bring down their belongings and luggage from the bus for x-ray screening and security checks at the bus hall. However, exceptions may be made for travellers who are physically impaired or handicapped. In such cases, checks will be conducted on board the bus.

questions.title: How do I obtain the departure endorsement to prove that I left Singapore?
questions.text: ICA no longer issues departure endorsements. You may use proxy documents, such as boarding passes as indicators of your exit record.

questions.title: What items are considered prohibited items?
questions.text: You may refer to the ICA website for more information about the prohibited items.

questions.title: Why are there no endorsements on my passport when I enter or depart Singapore?
questions.text:
ICA has ceased the issuance of departure immigration endorsements (i.e. stamps of departure dates on travel documents) to all foreign travellers departing Singapore from 22 Apr 2019, as part of ongoing efforts to streamline procedures at the checkpoints and facilitate more efficient departure immigration clearance.
From 11 March 2022, all foreign visitors arriving in Singapore will receive an electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) through email in lieu of inked endorsement stamps on the passport. The e-Pass will contain details of the visit pass granted, including the maximum number of day(s) of stay and the last day of stay allowed in Singapore.

questions.title: Why is ICA removing the departure endorsement?
questions.text: The removal of the departure endorsement is part of ICA's on-going efforts to streamline procedures at the checkpoints to facilitate faster and more efficient immigration clearance.

questions.title: Will I encounter issues at my next destination if there is no departure endorsement from Singapore?
questions.text: The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) has notified foreign authorities that departure endorsements will not be given to foreign visitors. You may visit the ICA website for more information.

questions.title: Will immigration clearance be accorded if my visit pass expires?
questions.text:
Travellers will be accorded immigration clearance so long as the visit pass remains valid at the point of departure.
Please note that overstaying is an offence under the Immigration Act.
If your visit pass has expired and you have overstayed, you may be subject to a composition fine or prosecution in court.

questions.title: Can I apply for visa if my passport is less than 6 months?
questions.text: You will not be able to apply for visa if your passport has less than 6 months' validity. You will require a passport that is valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival in Singapore as part of the entry requirements.

questions.title: How do I cancel my visa?
questions.text: For further queries regarding visa application, you may contact us via the enquiry form.

questions.title: How do I check on the visa application status?
questions.text: The processing time of a visa application is within 3 working days (excluding the day of submission). However, some applications may take a longer time to process. You may use the ICA e-Service to enquire your application status. Do note that you will require the visa reference number and applicant's travel document number.

questions.title: How do I submit Form 14A and V39A during online visa application?
questions.text: For visa application submitted via the e-Service, hardcopies of Form 14A and V39A are not required unless ICA requests for the documents.

questions.title: Must I declare my antecedents in Form 14A and how detailed should my declarations be?
questions.text:
Every visa application is considered on its own merits. You must declare your antecedent(s) truthfully and all information furnished in the visa application must be complete, accurate and verifiable.
Should you have further queries regarding visa application, you can contact us via the enquiry form.

questions.title: What are the documents required to apply for a visa?
questions.text: Please refer to the countries or places as listed on ICA website to find out the documents required to submit visa application.

questions.title: What are the photograph requirements for a visa application?
questions.text:
You are required to submit a digital photograph for your visa application via our e-Service.
The photograph should be a recent passport-sized colour photograph taken within the last 3 months and must be taken against a white background with a matt or semi-matt finish.
The photograph must also show the full face of the applicant without headgear (headgear worn in accordance with religious or racial customs is acceptable but must not hide the facial features).
The online photograph submitted must be of JPEG format, with a file size not more than 60 Kbytes and dimension of 400 x 514 pixels.
Failure to meet the requirements listed above can result in a delay or rejection of your visa application.

questions.title: What if I am unable to provide the requested document by ICA?
questions.text: Additional supporting documents may be requested on a case-by-case basis. You are required to upload an explanatory letter if the supporting documents cannot be furnished.

questions.title: What should I select if my passport is issued at an overseas mission instead of a Country/Place?
questions.text: If your passport is issued at the overseas mission, the location of the overseas mission will be the country/ place of issue in the visa application.

questions.title: Where do I find the visa application reference number?
questions.text:
The visa application reference number is generated on the acknowledgement page when a visa is successfully submitted.
You may contact us via the enquiry form for the retrieval of the visa reference number by indicating the applicant’s name and passport number in your email.

questions.title: Who are ICA's strategic partners?
questions.text: ICA’s strategic partners are institutions such as healthcare service providers, travel agencies, SingPost, etc., with good proven records and are granted strategic partner accounts. With the accounts, they can submit visa applications online on behalf of their customers. You may check with the respective institutions for more information regarding submission of visa application for their customers.

questions.title: Who can be the local contact for visa applications?
questions.text: The local contact must be either a Singapore citizen or a Singapore permanent resident who is at least 21 years old with a Singpass account. If you are applying for an entry visa for business visit, the local contact must be acting on behalf of the Singapore registered business entity.

questions.title: How do I appeal against my visa rejection?
questions.text:
You can submit an appeal via the enquiry form within 1 month from the date of visa rejection.
Please include the following documents in your email for us to process your appeal:
A copy of applicant's passport biodata page;
A letter (signed by the local contact) to request ICA to reconsider applicant's visa rejection and reason for reconsideration;
Any other supporting documents
The local contact’s NRIC date of issue for the facilitation of the appeal.
The processing time for appeal is generally 14 working days, depending on its complexity. Each appeal is assessed and considered on its own merits.
Local contacts are advised to monitor the status of the visa appeal online via the Enquire Application Status function.

questions.title: Why is my visa application rejected?
questions.text: ICA does not disclose the reason of rejection due to confidentiality of information. We seek your understanding on this matter.

questions.title: Is my entry to Singapore guaranteed with a valid visa?
What is Visa Free Transit Facility (VFTF) and who is eligible for VFTF?
questions.text:
The 96-hour Visa Free Transit Facility (VFTF) may be available to nationals of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)[1], Georgia, India, Turkmenistan and Ukraine; as well as selected[2] Nationals of the People's Republic of China (PRC) who are not holding ordinary, diplomatic, public affairs or service PRC passports.
Transit travellers who satisfy the criteria for VFTF will have to meet the prevailing entry requirements before they are allowed entry into Singapore. Assessment for entry is determined by the ICA officers at the point of entry. Extension of stay for transit travellers under VFTF is strictly not allowed.
Please refer to the ICA websites for more information on the following:
Visa Free Transit Facility
Check if You Need an Entry Visa
[1] CIS refers to: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan.
[2] These include holders of the PRC Travel Document, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) Document of Identity (DOI) and Macau SAR Travel Permit. Holder of ordinary, diplomatic, public affairs and service PRC passports are excluded.

questions.title: Do I need a visa if I want to transit in Singapore?
questions.text:
If you arrived at Singapore Changi Airport and were issued with the onward boarding passes for connecting flights out of Changi Airport, you may remain within the Changi Airport transit area until time for flight departure.
You can also remain in the transit area if you can obtain the onward boarding passes from any of the Transfer Lounges within the transit area.
However, if you are not issued with the onward boarding passes for connecting flights out of Changi Airport; or unable to obtain the onward boarding passes from any of the Transfer Lounges within the transit area, you are advised to exit the transit area as soon as possible.
We wish to highlight that most passengers who are arriving on a Low Cost Carrier (LCC) or connecting to a LCC are required to seek immigration clearance and obtain your onward boarding passes in the respective Departure Check-in Hall.
If you are required to seek immigration clearance before obtaining your onward boarding passes at the Departure Check-in Hall, you will have to satisfy the prevailing entry requirements, which include possessing an entry visa, where applicable.
All passengers are strongly advised to liaise with the relevant airlines before embarking on your journey. For more information on flights connection and transit facilities/ services, please visit the Changi Airport Group's website.

questions.title: Do I need a visa to enter Singapore?
questions.text:
You will require a visa to travel and seek entry into Singapore if you hold a travel document issued by one of the countries or places as listed on the ICA website.
If you are unable to find your country/ place and the passport types in the list, please forward a clear scanned copy of the passport/travel document's front cover and particulars page (i.e. showing holder's full name, nationality, passport number and its date of issue/expiry) to ICA for assessment.
If in doubt, you may contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a visa if I am entering Singapore to join as a ship crew member?
questions.text:
You are required to apply for a visa prior to your arrival in Singapore if you are from a visa-required country/ place even for the purpose to sign on/ sign off from the vessel in Singapore.
The visa application should be submitted through your shipping agents who will act as your local contact.
If in doubt, you may contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: Does a Singapore passport holder need a visa to travel to another country?
questions.text:
As visa requirements can change at short notice, you are advised to check with the relevant foreign embassies to ensure that you have the most updated visa information. Please note that visa requirements may also differ for holders of Singapore Temporary Travel Document.
You can refer to the MFA website for more information on the entry requirement(s) of the country you are travelling to.

questions.title: How do I check if the visa is genuine?
questions.text: You may check your visa using the 'Enquire Application Status' via the ICA e-Service. You will need to enter the visa reference number and the applicant's travel document number to retrieve the e-Visa.

questions.title: How many visa applications can the local contact/ sponsor apply?
questions.text: There is no restriction to the number of visa applications that a local contact/ sponsor can apply. However, every visa application is assessed and considered on its own merits.

questions.title: Is there a waiting time to apply visa for the same person after rejection?
questions.text: There is no waiting time if you would like to re-apply a visa for the same applicant.

questions.title: Is there any age limit on the visa applicant for visa application?
questions.text: There is no age limit on the visa applicant for visa application.

questions.title: Is visa reference number and e-visa number the same?
questions.text:
The visa reference number and e-visa number are different.
Visa reference number begins with VSCXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, while e-visa number begins with either AXXXXXXXX or KXXXXXXXX.

questions.title: Should I book the flight tickets before getting the outcome of the visa application?
questions.text: Visa applicants are not required to buy a flight ticket before applying for an entry visa. Applicants who choose to buy a flight ticket will have to bear the risk of loss if the visa application outcome is unsuccessful or if the approved visa duration falls outside of the applicant’s intended date of travel. The visa processing fee of S$30/- is also non-refundable regardless of the outcome of the visa application.

questions.title: What are the responsibilities of a Local Contact if a visa applicant breached the law in Singapore?
questions.text: The Local Contact may be called upon for interview to assist in investigation if the foreigner is found to have breached the law in Singapore.

questions.title: What does 'country/place of origin' in Form 14A means?
questions.text: 'Country/place of origin' in Form 14A refers to your country/ place of nationality/citizenship.

questions.title: What is e-Visa?
questions.text: e-Visa is an electronic visa that can be retrieved online and printed by the local contact or authorised visa agent/ strategic partner, without making a trip to the ICA Services Centre or Singapore Overseas Missions to collect the visa.

questions.title: What is Form 14A?
questions.text: Form 14A is a hardcopy application form for entry visa.

questions.title: What is Form V39A?
questions.text: Form V39A is a Letter of Introduction (LOI) for Singapore visa application. The form is required on a case-by-case basis to support visa applications.

questions.title: What is the difference between a business visa and a social visa?
questions.text: A business visa is an application submitted by a company for business purpose whereas a social visa is an application submitted by an individual/ family for social purpose.

questions.title: What is the difference between applying for an entry visa as an Individual User or Business User?
questions.text: You can apply for visa as Individual User if you are applying for individuals/ families for the purpose of social visit. A Singapore registered business entity applying for visa applicants for the purpose of business visit should apply for visa as Business User. In addition, the local contact who submits the visa application must be either a Singapore citizen or a Singapore permanent resident who is at least 21 years old with a Singpass account.

questions.title: What is the difference between visa and visit pass?
questions.text:
A valid Singapore visa is not an immigration pass. A valid entry visa is a pre-entry requirement that you must apply for before travelling to seek entry into Singapore if you hold a travel document issued by one of the following countries/places listed on the ICA website.
Possessing a valid visa does not guarantee entry into Singapore. You will have to satisfy the basic entry requirements (https://www.ica.gov.sg/enter-transit-depart/entering-singapore) before being considered for entry into Singapore.
The grant of a visit pass is determined by the ICA officers at the point of entry. The period of stay granted is shown on the visit pass endorsement given on the passport or the electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) issued to you through email. You can visit the e-Pass portal or use the Visit Pass Validity Tool to check the expiry of your e-Pass or visit pass. Please note that the period of stay is not tied to the validity of your entry visa.
You may refer to ICA website for more information should you need to extend your visit pass.

questions.title: Where can I find the draft visa application I saved earlier?
questions.text:
You can find your draft visa application by logging into the e-Service. You will need to click on the hyperlink of the name of the visa applicant to edit or delete an existing draft application.
Please note that the draft will be deleted automatically after 14 days from the last date it was saved.

questions.title: Where is the remark column for visa application?
questions.text: You can find the remark column under the 'Additional Information to support this application’ field.

questions.title: Who are the authorised visa agents?
questions.text: You are advised to liaise directly with the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission for information of their authorised visa agents, if any. For locations of the Singapore overseas missions, please visit the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' website under "Overseas Missions".

questions.title: Who can I contact for Singapore visa-related matters?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form for Singapore visa-related matters.

questions.title: Who do I approach for enquiry on group visa application?
questions.text: You may wish to check directly with the travel agent that handled your group visa application.

questions.title: Who do I contact if I encounter problems during the submission of visa application?
questions.text: If you encounter any problems with the e-Service, please contact us via the enquiry form with a screenshot of the error message.

questions.title: Why is visa imposed?
questions.text:
The imposition of visas is part of ICA's multi-pronged approach in ensuring that Singapore remains a safe and secure place for our citizens, foreign visitors and investors.
You can refer to the ICA website for visa requirements to enter Singapore.

questions.title: Am I able to retrieve the receipt for the payment I made for a visa application?
questions.text:
After successful payment, the payment receipt will appear in a pop-up window. Kindly disable your pop-up blocker in order to view the payment receipt.
Alternatively, you may contact us via the enquiry form to request for the receipt of your visa application.

questions.title: Can my application fees be refunded due to a rejected application or change of travel plans?
questions.text: The visa processing fee of S$30 is non-refundable.

questions.title: How do I make payment for a visa application?
questions.text:
A S$30 non-refundable processing fee will be collected at the time of submission for each application. The fee is payable online using a Visa or MasterCard credit/debit card, American Express (AMEX) card or Paynow.
Please refer to the ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.

questions.title: What is the processing time for visa application?
questions.text:
The processing time is within 3 working days, excluding the day of submission. Some applications may take longer to process, especially during peak periods.
You can use the Enquire Application Status function to check on the progress of your application.

questions.title: Can the validity of the e-Visa be amended?
questions.text: There is no amendment to the visa validity. A new visa application will have to be submitted if the visa validity period does not cover the entry date that the visa applicant wished to enter Singapore.

questions.title: Does the validity period of visa includes the date of expiry?
questions.text: The visa validity period is inclusive of the date of expiry.

questions.title: How can I extend my Visa?
questions.text: There is strictly no extension of visa validity or change of visa type. You can submit a fresh application via our e-Service upon the expiry or upon utilisation of your current visa. However, please note that each visa application is assessed on its own merits.

questions.title: How can I request for a longer validity of my visa?
questions.text:
Each visa application, including the duration of the visa granted, is considered on its own merits and subject to approval. You may wish to indicate the reason for requiring a visa with longer validity in the "Additional Information" field, for ICA's consideration. Please note that you may be required to submit supporting documents for our consideration.
You will be notified on the validity of the visa granted if your visa application is approved.

questions.title: How do I check my visa validity?
questions.text:
The visa validity is indicated on the e-Visa. You can retrieve your e-Visa using the Enquire Application Status function and key in your Visa Reference Number and Travel Document Number.
If you do not have a visa application reference number, you may contact us via the enquiry form and indicate the applicant's name and passport number for the retrieval of visa application reference number.

questions.title: There is a spelling mistake in my visa application. Can the visa application information be amended after the application has been submitted or approved?
questions.text:
You must ensure that the correct information is submitted at the point of your visa application via the e-Service. Amendment of information is not allowed after successful submission of the visa application to ensure data integrity.
You can disregard the outcome of the previous application submitted and proceed to submit a new visa application with the correct details.
Please note that the processing fee of S$30/- collected at the time of submission is non-refundable.
Lastly, please quote the reference number of the previous application and indicate the reasons for the resubmission on your new application under the 'Additional Information to support this SAVE application/Remarks' field in SAVE and check the application details carefully before submission to avoid any unnecessary delays.

questions.title: What does the “Visa Issue Date” on the e-Visa means?
questions.text: It means that the e-Visa is valid for use from the issue date as indicated.

questions.title: What is the validity period of a Singapore Visa?
questions.text:
Each visa application, including the duration of the visa granted, is considered on its own merits and subject to approval.
Applicants who are applying for a visa via our e-Service are advised to submit the application about 30 days prior to the intended arrival into Singapore so that the visa validity will be sufficient for the visit.

questions.title: How do I register the birth of my foreign child, who is born to foreigner parents, in Singapore?
questions.text:
All parents are required to register their child’s birth via LifeSG. All births in Singapore must be registered within 42 days from the date of birth. Failing to do so is an offence under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act. You could be liable for a fine and/or imprisonment upon conviction.
If the child is not a Singapore citizen, parents will need to obtain a travel document for the child from the respective Embassy or High Commission within 42 days of the child's birth. Details of the regularisation of the immigration status of a foreign child born in Singapore can be found in the advisory note that is issued together with the digital birth certificate. Parents must ensure that the child has a valid immigration pass to remain in Singapore beyond the 42nd day from the child’s birth by applying for the appropriate immigration pass at ICA.
topics: Visitor to Deliver a Child In Singapore

questions.title: How do I appeal a rejected Personalised Employment Pass application?
questions.text:
You can submit an appeal online within 3 months from the date of rejection.
It will take at least 8 weeks to review your appeal. If you don’t appeal within 3 months, you’ll need to reapply for the pass.
topics: Work passes and permits / Personalised Employment Pass

questions.title: Should I submit my PEP application, or should my employer?
questions.text:
If you’re currently an Employment Pass (EP) holder, you should submit your Personalised Employment Pass (PEP) application, and not your employer.
The PEP is non-renewable and does not restrict you to any one company, so you should decide whether to apply for it, and not your employer.
topics: Work passes and permits / Personalised Employment Pass

questions.title: Can I apply for an S Pass while I am on a visit pass?
questions.text:
Yes, you can apply for an S Pass while you are on a visit pass in Singapore.
However, your visit pass will not be extended while you await the outcome of your application. You will have to return to your home country/region when it expires.
We will inform your employer of the outcome accordingly.
topics: Work passes and permits / S Pass

questions.title: I am a foreign spouse holding on to a LTVP/LTVP+ issued by ICA. What happens if my prospective employer applies for a work pass for me?
questions.text: If the work pass (EP, S Pass or Work Permit) application gets approved, your LTVP/LTVP+ will be automatically cancelled once your new work pass gets issued.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: I am holding an EP, S Pass or Work Permit. What happens to my work pass if I marry a Singaporean or Permanent Resident and get a Long-Term Visit Pass from ICA?
questions.text:
Your existing work pass will be cancelled once your LTVP/LTVP+ card is issued by ICA.
To continue working for your current employer, you should request for a Pre-approved Letter of Consent (PLOC) while applying online for your LTVP with ICA.
If you are eligible, the PLOC will be emailed to your LTVP sponsor’s email address (that is registered with ICA) 1 day after you have received your LTVP card. If you are not eligible, your employer can still separately apply for a Letter of Consent (LOC) for you. The processing time is about one week.
If you forgot to request for a PLOC while applying for an LTVP with ICA, you can contact us 2 days after you have received your LTVP card.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: Why does the advertising requirement apply only to companies applying for EPs and S Passes, and not Work Permits?
questions.text:
There are already other safeguards, such as source restrictions, levies and dependency ratio ceilings, that apply to the hiring of Work Permit holders.
The job advertising requirement was extended to S Pass applications to promote greater awareness of vacancies in mid-skilled jobs among local jobseekers, and also require employers to make greater efforts to consider local candidates.

questions.title: What are the PWM wage requirements for part-time employees who are paid on a monthly basis?
questions.text:
For retail and food services PWMs, and Occupational PWs, you can refer to the respective pages for the applicable PWM hourly wage for part-time work.
For the other Sectoral PWMs,

questions.title: If I'm not eligible for re-employment, can I still get Employment Assistance Payment (EAP)?
questions.text:
No, your employer is not obligated to offer you re-employment or an Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) if you are not eligible. Check if you are eligible for re-employment.
However, your employer should inform you at least 3 months before retirement so you have time to look for a new job. Employers are also encouraged to help employees who aren't eligible for re-employment, such as services like career coaching.

questions.title: Is the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) taxable or subject to CPF contributions?
questions.text: No, the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP) isn't considered income, and is not taxable or liable for CPF contributions.

questions.title: Are my employees required to sign off on itemised pay slips?
questions.text:
No. However, it is in your interest that your employees acknowledge the itemised pay slips issued to them.
This ensures that both employers and employees understand the salary components. This will help prevent employment disputes.

questions.title: Some of my Work Permit holders are unable to remember their bank account details. How do I pay salaries electronically?
questions.text:
From 14 July, you can also pay salaries using Corporate Paynow by indicating their FIN.
Find out more at DBS website.

questions.title: Why do I need to pay CPF and tax for my workers who are on light duty medical leave?
questions.text:
When an employee is on light duty, they are required to report to work unless they are excused by their employer.
As an employer, you must pay their normal wages, which are not reimbursed by the work injury insurer. As these are the actual wages paid by the employer, both employer and employee have to contribute CPF under the CPF Act.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: Why are the screening questions mandatory during application?
questions.text: Screening questions serve as a mean for employers to better assess the suitability of a jobseeker beyond what is normally provided in an application.

questions.title: Which web browsers are supported?
questions.text: Opera 19, Internet Explorer 10, Chrome 33, Firefox 14, Safari 5 or later versions are supported. Please ensure that your browser is updated for a better experience in navigating MySkillsFuture.

questions.title: Which web browsers on my mobile devices are supported?
questions.text: Mobile Safari 9, Chrome 51, Firefox 48 or later versions are supported. Please ensure that your mobile browser is updated for a better experience in navigating MySkillsFuture.

questions.title: Can I access MySkillsFuture on my mobile device?
questions.text: Yes, it is a mobile-friendly website designed for easy reading and navigation.

questions.title: I wish to choose and pre-buy a family niche. Can you provide guidance how to do so?
questions.text: The government-managed columbaria at Choa Chu Kang and Mandai are not for advance sale. Applicants will need to provide a death certificate of the deceased at the point of payment.

questions.title: Many Singapore Residents, especially the elderly, do not receive any payout for their bills, due to the deductible. Why must there be a deductible?
questions.text:
The deductible filters out smaller bills that can be adequately covered via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, bills where protection is most critical. This keeps premiums affordable for all policyholders. By avoiding first-dollar coverage, the deductible also encourages prudent use of healthcare.
The deductible can be covered by MediSave. The Government provides MediSave top-ups for the lower-income and elderly Singaporeans through schemes such as Workfare, GST Voucher scheme, and Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation Packages. For those who are unable to afford their healthcare bills after subsidies and MediSave, MediFund assistance is available at public hospitals.
From 1 April 2025, the inpatient deductible will be increased. MediSave withdrawal limits will be raised to help Singaporeans offset the increase in deductible, while the Ward C deductible increase will be phased in gradually. Please refer to the press release for more details.
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Does MediShield Life cover hospice care?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life covers the Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS) at inpatient hospices and community hospitals. Please refer to the latest limits here
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Can I submit the MediShield Life claim directly to the Central Provident Fund Board after I have settled the bill at the medical institution?
questions.text:
All MediShield Life claims must be e-filed by medical institutions to ensure accountability and efficiency in claims processing, due to the high volume of claims involved. The Central Provident Fund Board does not accept claims submitted by patients.
The medical institution will seek your authorisation to submit your claim for you. If a payout is due, it will be made directly to the medical institution to offset your bill.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will the claim details on the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements be changed if the hospital adjusts my bill size?
questions.text: Yes, the online statements will take into account any adjustments made to the hospital bills, if the hospital has informed the Central Provident Fund Board about the change before the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What are the claim details that can be viewed from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
Claim details will be reflected on the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements whenever there is a MediSave deduction and/ or MediShield Life payout.
You will also be able to view the claim details for MediShield Life claims, even if the claimable amounts are below the deductible.
If you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), you will be able to view the claim details for claims under the MediShield Life component of your IP on the ’Summary of Healthcare Payment’ page. IPs comprise two components – the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund Board, and the additional private insurance component administered by private IP insurers. You will have to contact your private insurer if you want to find out more about the total claim computation under your IP.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Why am I unable to view claim details of my hospitalisation from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
Claim details displayed online are accurate as at the date of enquiry. They will be reflected only after the medical institution submits your claim and the MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
Please note that the medical institution can only submit your claim after the medical bill has been finalised. Claim details of your hospitalisation will only be available after your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claim is processed.
You can check the status of your MediShield Life claim via 'My Activities' after you log onto "my cpf Online Services" with your SingPass.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be informed of how much I have claimed to date from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text: You will be able to view the total amount that you have claimed for the current policy year, as at the date of enquiry.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How can I apply? (CHAS)
questions.text:
You can apply for CHAS via the online application by using this link.
Alternatively, you can also pick up a CHAS application form at any Community Centre or Club (CC), Community Development Council (CDC), Public Hospital or Polyclinic or download the application form by using this link . Please send the completed and signed application form to Privy Box No. 920231, Singapore 929292.
If anyone in your household is not a Singapore Citizen, please also include copies of their foreign identification documents (e.g. work permit/long term visit pass).
If your application is successful, all eligible members of your household will receive an individual CHAS card in their name. The card indicates the subsidy tier you qualify for (CHAS Blue or Orange or Green) and is valid for two years. Simply present the card at a CHAS GP or dental clinic when seeking treatment. PG and MG cardholders can use their PG or MG card at any CHAS clinic to obtain CHAS subsidies. You will receive an itemised bill for your treatment.
If this is your first visit to a CHAS GP, please also present your NRIC upon registration (or birth certificate for cardholders under 15 years old).
By using your CHAS or Pioneer Generation or Merdeka Generation card at a CHAS clinic, you consent to allow your doctor/dentist to disclose your personal information to the Ministry of Health (including its authorised agents).

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement policyholder. Do I have to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, you have been auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. You can choose to opt out from CareShield Life by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme.
Those who were not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life.
The Government will provide participation incentives of up to $2,500 ($250/year) to Singapore Citizens who join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. Additional participation incentives of $1,500 ($150/year) will also be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens who join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
To encourage more Singapore Citizens to join CareShield Life, those who join and are covered between 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024 will receive participation incentives of up to $1,875 ($187.50/year). Additional participation incentives of $1,125 ($112.50/year) will be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens.
The Government will also provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I am born in 1979 or earlier and develop severe disability, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. have developed severe disability), you will not be eligible to join CareShield Life.
If you are insured under ElderShield and have not made a claim yet, you may wish to claim from ElderShield instead. Depending on the plan you have, ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts of $300 per month for up to 60 months (under ElderShield 300 plan), or $400 per month for up to 72 months (under ElderShield 400 plan).
If you have received all your ElderShield payouts, you may wish to tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes (such as the Home Caregiving Grant, ElderFund) for assistance. You may also approach the Medical Social Workers at the health institution you are seeking medical treatment from or your nearest Social Service Office (SSO). For more information on MediFund or ComCare, please visit https://www.moh.gov.sg/cost-financing/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medifund or http://www.msf.gov.sg/comcare.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield insured. If I am eligible for ElderShield claims, should I claim from ElderShield or join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. have developed severe disability), and is an ElderShield insured, you should apply to claim under ElderShield so that you can receive your monthly claim payouts in a timely manner.
You will not be eligible for CareShield Life if you have developed severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I have to pay extra premiums if I join CareShield Life with pre-existing medical conditions?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and have pre-existing medical conditions, you can choose to join CareShield Life if you do not develop severe disability. You will not need to pay additional premiums for pre-existing medical conditions.
You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is universal coverage not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier?
questions.text:
Universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier as this is a diverse group - some may have previously opted out of ElderShield, or decided not to upgrade to ElderShield. Others could have bought Supplements or insurance plans. Those born in 1979 or earlier would also likely face higher entry premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payment over. The prevalence of those who already have severe disability in the older cohorts is also much higher, which would make it harder to cover everyone while still keeping premiums affordable. Hence, universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier.
Those who are born in 1979 or earlier and who already have severe disability will not be able to join CareShield Life. The Government will help them through other ways e.g. Government subsidies and other Government schemes such as the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund. They can also tap on ElderFund and their MediSave savings.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund, ComCare can also provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Should I opt out of ElderShield if I would like to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
There is no need to opt out of ElderShield. Your existing ElderShield cover will be upgraded to CareShield Life and the premiums paid for ElderShield will be taken into account.
Simply access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service using your Singpass and we will notify you on the outcome of your upgrade.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will ElderShield 300/400 insureds receive subsidies or an incentive as well since there were no incentives in 2002/2007 when ElderShield 300 and 400 were introduced respectively?
questions.text: CareShield Life premium subsidies and incentives will be extended to Singaporeans (including those on ElderShield 300/400 today) if they join CareShield Life, as these are intended to support the increased benefits under CareShield Life and ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I have opted out from ElderShield. Can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have severe disability.
If you wish to join CareShield Life, you may access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service and log in using your Singpass to complete the application. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. You will be informed if a disability assessment is required.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ESH300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I currently have severe disability but subsequently recover, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you have recovered from your severe disability, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You may be required to go for a disability assessment to determine your eligibility.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I was previously claiming from ElderShield, but have recovered from my severe disability, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you previously claimed from ElderShield but have since recovered, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You may have to go for a disability assessment.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I receive any premium subsidies as an ElderShield 300/400 insured if I upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are an ElderShield insured, you can receive CareShield Life premium subsidies if you upgrade to CareShield Life. CareShield Life is a new scheme, and these subsidies will ensure that the premiums remain affordable even as the new scheme offers better protection and benefits.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I am currently on ElderShield 300/400 and choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, can I opt out or downgrade back to ElderShield 300/400 subsequently?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, you will be automatically enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021, if you are currently covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and do not develop severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can opt out of CareShield Life by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme and you will automatically be placed back onto your ElderShield 400 scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are an ElderShield insured in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to consider your decision. If you choose to opt out, you will be given a full premium refund and automatically be placed back onto your original ElderShield 300/400 scheme.
You will not be able to opt out from the scheme after the applicable opt-out/free-look periods.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Should I upgrade to/join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government encourages Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier without severe disability to consider joining CareShield Life for basic lifetime financial protection for long-term care. CareShield Life provides monthly cash payout in the event of severe disability, for as long as you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government also provides support to help make premiums affordable.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Will I get higher subsidies if I am of an older age since my CareShield Life premiums will be higher?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier, you will receive means-tested subsidies of up to 30% on your base premiums for CareShield Life. Given that premiums increase with age, the annual subsidies for older Singaporeans will also be higher to offset the higher annual premiums.
The Government will also be providing participation incentives of between $500 ($50/year) and $2500 ($250/year) to encourage those born in 1979 or earlier to join the scheme by 31 December 2023. The incentive amount is tiered by age, and older Singaporeans will receive higher incentives. Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens will receive additional participation incentives of $1,500 ($150/year), with the total participation incentives coming up to $4,000 ($400/year). The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
To encourage more Singapore Citizens to join CareShield Life, those who join and are covered between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 will receive participation incentives of up to $1,875 ($187.50/year). Additional participation incentives of $1,125 ($112.50/year) will be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens.
Those who need more assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and the participation incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I opt out from the CareShield Life scheme after joining (e.g. if I cannot afford the premiums)?
questions.text:
To make joining CareShield Life more convenient, you have been auto-enrolled from 1 December 2021, if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can choose to opt out by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to consider your decision.
The Government will provide participation incentives of up to $2,500 ($250/year) to all Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who join CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. Additional participation incentives of $1,500 ($150/year) will also be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens who join CareShield Life by 31 December 2023. The participation incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset premiums payable for each year.
To encourage more Singapore Citizens to join CareShield Life, those who join and are covered between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 will receive participation incentives of up to $1,875 ($187.50/year). Additional participation incentives of $1,125 ($112.50) will be provided to Merdeka and Pioneer Generation citizens.
The Government will also provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties. For this reason, after the applicable free-look periods, you will not be able to opt out from the scheme.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
If you are a foreigner who become a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident from 1 October 2020 onwards, are born in 1979 or earlier and do not develop severe disability, CareShield Life will be mandatory for you.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: If I have finished claiming my ElderShield 300/400 payouts, can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can choose to join CareShield Life but you may be required to undergo a disability assessment. You will not be eligible to join CareShield Life if you are unable to do three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
However, you can tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes such as Home Caregiving Grant and ElderFund, and MediSave Care to complement your personal savings and family support, in meeting your long-term care needs. Government assistance schemes such as the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund can also help defray the cost of consumables and assistive devices.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: The current ElderShield scheme has a maximum entry age of 64 years old. Can I join CareShield Life if I am older?
questions.text:
There is no maximum entry age for CareShield Life.
However, as premiums increase with age, you are advised to use the Premium Checker using your Singpass to check your personalised premium payable before applying to join CareShield Life.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier and did not qualify to join ElderShield previously. Am I eligible to join CareShield Life now?
questions.text: You can choose to join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have severe disability. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. You will be informed if a disability assessment is required.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Can I join both CareShield Life and ElderShield to get double the protection?
questions.text:
You will not be able to be on both CareShield Life and ElderShield.
However, upgrading to CareShield Life will not affect your ElderShield Supplement plan if you already have one. If you are currently covered under ElderShield, you can upgrade to CareShield Life for higher and lifetime payouts. Your ElderShield coverage will be terminated upon joining CareShield Life. For more coverage, you can also purchase Supplement plans from private insurers.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier, and am not enrolled in ElderShield. Am I eligible for CareShield Life?
questions.text: You can join CareShield Life if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not develop severe disability.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: What will happen to my current ElderShield and Supplement plans after CareShield Life is launched?
questions.text:
The launch of CareShield life will not affect your existing ElderShield and supplement plans.
However, you are encouraged to consider upgrading your ElderShield to CareShield Life if you do not have severe disability. If you choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, the ElderShield premiums that you have paid will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower CareShield Life premiums.
The Supplements will also work with CareShield Life cover and do not need to be terminated.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Do I need to back pay premiums from age 30 to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
ElderShield premiums that ElderShield insureds have paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums. Insureds do not need to back pay for CareShield Life coverage starting from 30; they will only be paying for coverage going forward.
However, CareShield Life's annual premiums for older insureds will still be higher than those of younger insureds, as they have less years to spread their premium payment over.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: Why is the Government auto-enrolling ElderShield 400 insureds who are born between 1970 to 1979 to CareShield Life?
questions.text: It was to make it more convenient for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to join CareShield Life. If you were auto-enrolled and do not wish to join the scheme, you can opt out by accessing the Opt-out of CareShield Life e-Service and log in using Singpass to complete the application by 31 December 2023.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: How do the CareShield Life premiums and monthly payouts compare against Supplements and other private long-term care insurance plans?
questions.text:
Supplement premiums are not directly comparable as there are inherent differences in the product design of CareShield Life, Supplements and other private long-term care products:
• Currently, there are no Supplement plans with increasing payouts, although there are Supplement plans that have a higher payout quantum and no cap on payout duration, similar to CareShield Life.
• Supplements generally have premium schedules designed to keep annual premiums lower e.g. some of them allow premiums to be paid up to age 80, 100 or over the insured’s lifetime while CareShield Life only requires premiums to be paid up to age 67. Some Supplements offer additional benefits, such as death benefit, lump sum benefit upon claim or payouts upon not being able to perform at least two out of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), which CareShield Life does not provide.
As part of CareShield Life, the Government will be providing several premium support measures for those born in 1979 or earlier, including means-tested premium subsidies, participation incentives, and Additional Premium Support for those who are unable to pay their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies. No one will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.
