Email: wecare-sg@greateasternlife.com
Hotline: 1800-248-2888
You can check your CareShield Life/ElderShield supplement plan by following these steps:
a. Visit the CPF website.
b. Log in using your Singpass.
c. Hover over "my cpf" and click on "Healthcare" under "My dashboards".
d. Click on “Long-term care insurance” on the anchor links or scroll down to the “Long-term care insurance” section.
If you are covered under a Supplement plan, this section will show the insurer of your Supplement plan (i.e. Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). Do contact your insurer to find out which Supplement plan you are covered under.
If you do not have any Supplement plan, this section will not reflect any information.

questions.title: How do I check the types of supplementary plans which I have purchased for myself or dependants?
questions.text: If you wish to find out about the number or types of supplementary plans which you have purchased, please contact your insurer(s) directly.

questions.title: Can the Supplements work with both CareShield Life and ElderShield?
questions.text: Specific Supplements might work with either ElderShield, CareShield Life, or both schemes. Please approach your insurer or financial advisor for more information on the specific Supplement product.

questions.title: Should I join CareShield Life if I already have an existing ElderShield & ElderShield Supplement plan that provides similar coverage, e.g. lifetime payouts?
questions.text:
Existing insureds’ Supplement plans will not be affected, even if you join CareShield Life. You will continue to pay the same premiums for your Supplements and enjoy the same benefits for as long as you are covered. You will also be able to make claims under both CareShield Life and your Supplement plan.
You may wish to refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support, and also speak to your financial advisor on whether you should upgrade to CareShield Life.

questions.title: Will the Supplement premiums that I have already paid, be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Supplement products are strictly run by the private insurers and the premiums that have already been paid for Supplements will not be taken into account when you upgrade to CareShield Life. These Supplement policies will stay in-force as long as you continue to contribute premiums and do not terminate their coverage.
Nonetheless, ElderShield premiums that ElderShield insureds have paid will be taken into account when computing their CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: If my Supplements overlap with CareShield Life, will insurers provide a refund if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Your Supplement policies will stay in-force as long as you contribute premiums and do not terminate their coverage. Your existing Supplement policies will not be adversely affected because of CareShield Life. You will also be able to make a claim under both CareShield Life and your Supplement.
You may wish to speak with your financial advisor for further advice.

questions.title: There are so many private disability insurance products. Where can I seek advice on which to buy?
questions.text:
If you are covered under CareShield Life/ElderShield, you may consider whether the benefits of the current CareShield Life/ElderShield scheme suits your long-term care preferences. If you wish to have additional coverage or benefits on top of the CareShield Life/ElderShield scheme, you may consider purchasing a Supplement plan.
You may refer here for a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). You may also wish to speak to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers who can share more about their Supplement plans with you.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. If I buy private insurance products/Supplements similar to CareShield Life, can I be exempted from universal coverage?
questions.text: CareShield Life will be universal for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later. Private insurance can still play a complementary role by providing additional benefits above and beyond such basic coverage.

questions.title: What happens if I stop paying for my Supplements if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: Supplement plans will lapse if you stop paying premiums. Please refer to your specific Supplement policy documents or consult your insurer for more information.

questions.title: May I upgrade CareShield Life to get better coverage?
questions.text: CareShield Life is intended to provide basic financial protection for long-term care needs, together with other long-term care financing sources, such as Government subsidies and assistance schemes, community support, personal savings, family support and Government-funded safety nets. If you wish to have additional coverage on top of what CareShield Life provides, you may wish to discuss with your financial advisor on a supplement plan that private insurers offer.

questions.title: Can I purchase CareShield Life Supplement(s) if I have pre-existing illnesses?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are products by private insurers who set the underwriting decisions based on commercial and actuarial considerations.
You may refer here for a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). You may also wish to speak to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers who can share more about their Supplement plans with you.

questions.title: Will ElderShield insurers continue selling Supplements?
questions.text: The ElderShield insurers will continue administering Supplements that complement the current ElderShield schemes.

questions.title: Will the Government be allowing more insurers to sell Supplements for CareShield Life/ElderShield?
questions.text: The Government will review the CareShield Life/ElderShield Supplement market and assess the entry of new insurers into the Supplement market, if there is interest from other insurers.

questions.title: Can I claim from both CareShield Life/ElderShield and my private personal insurance?
questions.text: You may submit claims for CareShield Life or ElderShield with Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), and your Supplement plan with private insurers. You may check with your private insurers on the claims process and payouts for Supplement plan.

questions.title: I have Supplements for CareShield Life/ElderShield. How do I make claim in this case?
questions.text:
To submit CareShield Life/ElderShield Supplements claims, you may approach your respective private insurer for details and advice:
• Singlife (Hotline no: 6827-9933)
• Great Eastern (Hotline no: 1800-248-2888)
• Income Insurance (Hotline no: 6332-1133)

questions.title: What happens after I submit my application?
questions.text:
Our staff will review the information you have submitted, identify the most suitable scheme to apply for and assist you further.
We may contact you for further information, but please attend your appointment as scheduled regardless of whether you hear from us or not - unless specifically told not to.
topics: What happens after I submit my application?

questions.title: What is a Fund?
questions.text:
A parent organisation (which is either a company limited by guarantee, society or a trust) may set up a fund for a specific purpose (e.g. welfare fund). The fund does not have a separate legal entity status as it falls under the umbrella of the parent organisation. Funds are governed by their specific Rules & Regulations.
Members do not enjoy separate legal identity status and are thus exposed to liability issues.
topics: Registering as a Charity in Singapore

questions.title: How to submit a charity registration for an organisation (incorporated as a CLG/ Society)?
questions.text:
One of the personnel from the organisation can submit an online application by logging in to the Charity Portal using his/her Singpass which has been linked to the Corppass account.
***Please ensure that the Corppass Admin has granted the authorised Corppass user, the necesssary access rights to the Charity Portal on the Corppass website.
topics: Registering as a Charity in Singapore

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a Munitions of War permit if I intend to check-in my sporting weapon and ammunitions in my checked baggage for my flight to or from Singapore?
questions.text:
If you wish to carry weapons and ammunitions to or from Singapore in checked baggage, you should seek authorisation from the Police Licensing and Regulatory Department of the Singapore Police Force. You may refer to the Singapore Police Force website for more information.
You should also notify your airline at the time of ticket purchase or prior to arrival at the airport of your intention to carry weapons or ammunitions in your checked baggage.

questions.title: How often do I have to pay this fee?
questions.text: You will need to pay the fee for medical evaluation every time you submit an application for Medical Assessment.
topics: Aviation Safety / Medical Assessment for Flight Crew and ATC

questions.title: How do I convert my foreign professional pilot licence to a Singapore one?
questions.text:
You will need to submit the application and supporting documents online in CAPELS.
In general, to convert your foreign professional pilot licence, you must meet the following requirements:
Be at least 18 years old for CPL (or 21 years old for ATPL) and below 65 years old.
Demonstrate the need to hold a Singapore licence such as obtaining a formal letter from a Singapore air operator or approved aviation organisation indicating prospective employment in a flying capacity.
Hold a valid foreign professional pilot licence, relevant Medical Assessment and valid Radiotelephony Licence
Produce the appropriate theoretical knowledge examination results (e.g. CPL or ATPL level) completed with the foreign licensing authority.
Meet the flying experience requirements stipulated in Chapter 11 of the Singapore Air Safety Publication (SASP) Part 2.
As part of the conversion process, you will be required to complete certain examinations, English language assessment and flight test(s). More detailed information can be found in Chapter 11 of the Singapore Air Safety Publication (SASP) Part 2.

questions.title: When should I make payment for the course?
questions.text: You will receive your Course Placement Letter with payment instructions about 8 weeks before the course starts. Please ensure that payment has been made by due date to secure your spot.
topics: Singapore Aviation Academy / Course Applications / Payment

questions.title: What are the browser compatibility requirements for accessing myTax Portal?
questions.text:
Check the browser compatibility for your device. If you encounter any problems, you may wish to use alternative browsers. If you continue to encounter page errors, please provide the following details:
Date and time when you encountered problems
Browser type and version number (e.g. Apple Safari 9.0, etc.)
Operating system you are using (e.g. Windows Vista, Macintosh OS X El Capitan etc.
Name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP) (e.g. Starhub, Singtel, etc.)
Error messages or the screenshot of the errors encountered (if any)
topics: Individual Income Tax / e-Filing system help

questions.title: I hold a work permit to work as a confinement nanny in Singapore. How do I file tax?
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: What should I do if my employer is not under AIS and I need to submit my Income Tax Return?
questions.text:
If your employer is not participating in the AIS, your employer should have prepared and provided you with the Form IR8A by 1 Mar. Otherwise, you may approach your employer for a copy of your Form IR8A. You should enter the details during your tax filing as per the information in your Form IR8A.The IR8A form contains information of your remuneration of the preceding year, you should enter the details during your tax filing according to it.
You are not required to submit your Form IR8A or other supporting documents unless specifically stated at the acknowledgement page.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: My employer is in AIS but I have mistakenly submitted my employment income and deductions to IRAS when filing my Income Tax Return. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you have submitted the income information via e-Filing, you may re-file once. Re-filing must be done by 18 Apr.
If you are unable to re-file by 18 Apr, please file an amendment upon receiving your Tax Bill for the current Year of Assessment. You may file the amendment via the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal within 30 days from the date of your tax bill.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: I was employed under 2 employers during the year. However, only 1 employer is in the AIS. How should I file my Income Tax Return?
questions.text: You have to manually include the employment income and deductions made through your salary (e.g. CDAC or Mendaki) for the employer that is not participating in the AIS when filing your Income Tax Return.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: I have forgotten to report my income earned in previous years. What should I do?
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: What if I have overlooked to claim for eligible reliefs (e.g. Qualifying Child Relief) in the previous years?
questions.text:
For assessments raised in 2022 and subsequent years, you have up to 4 years from the end of that relevant year to inform us of your claims. For example, if the assessment was raised in 2022, you have up till 31 Dec 2026 (i.e. 2022 + 4 years) to inform us of your claim.
To claim for eligible reliefs in the preceding years, you may file an amendment using the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Making changes after filing/receiving tax bill

questions.title: My employer has sent my employment income details to IRAS. Do I still have to file my tax return?
questions.text:
Although your employer has sent your employment income details to IRAS, you are still required to file your Income Tax Return unless you have received our notification letter or SMS that you are on the No-Filing Service (NFS).
If you received the NFS letter or SMS, you do not need to file an Income Tax Return.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Late filing or non-filing of Individual Income Tax Returns (Form B1/B/P/M)

questions.title: The tax consultant handles expatriates’ employment income information. Can this information be excluded from the electronic submission?
questions.text:
Employers must submit the employment income information of all employees, including expatriates and directors who receive director's fees, unless the director is a non-resident director who received only director's fees.
Employers should authorise their tax consultants via Corppass to submit the employment income information of expatriates.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Join the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income

questions.title: Can we submit hardcopy IR8A if we are already in the scheme?
questions.text: No. AIS participating organisations must submit all employees' employment income information electronically.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Join the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income

questions.title: How do I join the AIS if I am a foreign entity (without tax reference number)?
questions.text:
Write in via myTax Mail (Category: Submission of Employment Income Records, Subject: Submission Matters) with the following:
Documentations to prove the foreign entity's establishment in Singapore, such as:
• CPF Board’s employer confirmation letter
• ACRA BIZ File document
• Certificate of registration/ incorporation in the respective country
Date of Incorporation
Country of Incorporation
Upon approval of your request, IRAS will issue an ASGD number for your future AIS registration and transactions.
If you encounter issues on logging in myTax Mail, please click online chat for assistance.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Join the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income

questions.title: How do I segregate the contributions to Yayasan Mendaki Fund and the Mosque Building Fund?
questions.text: You can refer to MUIS (Majlis Ugama Islam, Singapura) for information on segregation.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Must I report the actual donations made or the tax-deductible donations in the submission for the employee?
questions.text: You should report only the actual donation amount deducted from your employee’s salary. The reported donations must qualify for tax deduction, e.g. Yayasan Mendaki Fund/Community Chest of Singapore/SINDA/CDAC/ECF.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Should I include employees who worked for a short period and left the organisation?
questions.text: You should include all employees who had worked in the organisation regardless the length of employment.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Must I submit fees that are paid to individuals who are not employees of the organisation?
questions.text: Payments made to individuals who are not employees should be excluded in the submission. These individuals should report their fees in their personal income tax reporting.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Do I have to submit the income information of foreign employees whose income is below $22,000 and tax clearance is not required?
questions.text: You are required to include these foreign employees' employment income information in the submission.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Can I use the work permit number for foreign employees for the submission as it is currently captured in the payroll software?
questions.text: Please update your records with their Foreign Identification Number (FIN) before submitting to IRAS. All foreign employees have a FIN issued by Ministry of Manpower (MOM) or Immigration and Checkpoint Authority (ICA).
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: How do I declare exempt income?
questions.text: You can declare the exempt income under "Remission / Overseas Posting / Exempt Income" and select the most appropriate exemption reason on the Form IR8A.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: How do I declare the Appendix 8A if an employee has more than 1 place of residence?
questions.text: Please prepare separate Appendix 8A records for each place of residence. If you are submitting online, you need to prepare Appendix 8A and corresponding Form IR8A for each place of residence.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Can I declare the stock option gains in a foreign currency?
questions.text:
You need to report the foreign stock option gains in Singapore currency for Form IR8A and Appendix 8B.
Actual exchange rates
For the conversion, you should use the actual exchange rate as of the date the employee exercised the stock option.
In-house exchange rates
If you do not have the exchange rate on the date of exercise, you may use your organisation's in-house exchange rate for conversion purpose.
Published exchange rates
If your organisation does not have any in-house exchange rate, you may use the exchange rates published by local banks, locally circulated newspapers and reputable news agencies.
You may use any of the sources of exchange rates listed above. Ensure that you:
Uses the same source for all employees
Apply the same source for all years
Communicates to all employees the source of exchange rate that will be used for the purpose of foreign currency conversion in reporting their stock option gains to IRAS
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: My business is a partnership which paid salaries to partners. Do I report these salaries?
questions.text:
You need to submit employment income information via AIS if the partners are engaged under an employment contract with the partnership (i.e. partners who generally do not assume the liabilities of the business and do not have a share in the profit/loss of the partnership). These partners are considered as employees of the partnership, even though they have the title of 'partner'.
You do not need to submit the remuneration of partners who are self-employed via the AIS. The precedent partner of the partnership should allocate the income of these partners who have a share in the profit/loss of the partnership and receive remuneration (salary, bonus, CPF, and other benefits) in Form P. The partners should then report their allocated share of profit/loss and remuneration (salary, bonus, CPF, and other benefits) from the partnership in the 'Trade, Business, Profession, or Vocation' section and 'Partnership' sub-section of their personal Income Tax Return.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: Will other authorised staff or third party be able to see my submitted records at myTax Portal?
questions.text:
Details of the records submitted via payroll software (API) will not be displayed at myTax Portal. Only the submission date and time will be shown.
For records submitted via the Submit Employment Income Records digital service at myTax Portal, only authorised staff or third party can view the details.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: What should I do with the fields in myTax Portal under Submit Employment Income Records (online application) that do not accept decimals?
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: What should I do if I encounter a page error in myTax Portal during submission?
questions.text:
Only employees or third party authorised as an "Approver" via Corppass for the "Submission of Employment Income Records" digital service can submit employment income information to IRAS via myTax Portal.
You can get the company's Corppass Admin to authorise yourself, an employee or a third party as an "Approver" via the Corppass system. For details on the steps, refer to User Guide to complete the authorisation (PDF, 759KB).
If you are the "Approver" and still encounter the page error, email the following details to ais@iras.gov.sg
Date and time you encountered the problem
Operating system that you are using (e.g. Microsoft Windows 11, macOS 15 Sequoia)
Internet browser and version number (e.g. Microsoft Edge version 139.0.3405.111, Google Chrome version 139.0.7258.128)
Error message or screenshot of the error encountered (if available)
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: Are the payroll software of AIS payroll software vendors approved by IRAS?
questions.text: No, AIS payroll software vendors are not endorsed by IRAS. Being listed as an AIS payroll software vendor only means that AIS submissions made through their software can be accepted by IRAS’ system.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: Are there any requirements for API integration?
questions.text:
Yes, our API endpoints have to be triggered from a Server-to-Server connection. Your server/ software/ application must be able to:
Support the following protocols: HTTP/2, TLS 1.2/1.3, and
Trigger HTTP/GET and HTTP/POST requests.
A Callback URL is also required to redirect users to the payroll software after Corppass login and consent. The Callback URL must use a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN), and meet all of the following requirements:
Must be able to accept parameters,
Must not contain IP address, port number, Hash (#) or Wildcard (*) characters, and
Must not be the same URL for sandbox and production environments.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Technical file format/specifications

questions.title: Must the files be encrypted as a security feature?
questions.text: No, IRAS’ applications use Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) technology, which is an industry-standard protocol for secure, web-based communications and transactions. SSL creates a secure communication channel between the server and the consumer’s browser. SSL provides message privacy by encrypting all information exchanged between the web server and the consumer’s browser.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Technical file format/specifications

questions.title: Which flexible benefit is taxable, which is not?
questions.text:
Generally, all gains and profits derived by an employee due to his employment are taxable. Benefits are "gains and profits" and are taxable unless exempted or given an administrative concession.
An employer offering the flexible benefits scheme would have to make a distinction between taxable and non-taxable benefits. The employer has to keep track of the taxable items so that the taxable benefits are reported in the Form IR8A

questions.title: I am staying somewhere else and decided to let my parents stay in my property instead. Will I be eligible for the owner-occupier tax rates?
questions.text: The owner entered in the Valuation List must reside in the residential property for the property to qualify for the owner-occupier tax rates. Residential properties which are not occupied by the owner will not be eligible for this concession and the property will be taxed at the non-owner-occupier residential tax rates.

questions.title: I have stopped renting out my propety. Why is it still taxed at the non-owner-occupier residential tax rates?
questions.text:
When the lease on your property ends and you have moved back into your home, you have to reapply for the owner-occupier tax rates for your property using ‘Apply/Withdraw for Owner-Occupier Tax Rates’ digital service.
If there is an existing lease on your property and you are planning to reside in your property after the lease has been pre-terminated, you can apply for the owner-occupier tax rates via our ‘Apply/Withdraw for Owner-Occupier Tax Rates’ digital service with supporting documents to show that the lease has been pre-terminated.
The following are some examples of supporting documents that you can provide to show that the lease has been pre-terminated:
1) Tenancy Termination Agreement (e.g. tenant departure slip etc.)
2) HDB termination letter
3) Message between tenant/ agent and owner (e.g. Email/ Instant Messaging)
4) Electricity bill showing the utility account/ utility bill opening
5) SP services’ email showing the date of account opening
6) Approval for commencement of renovation (e.g. Renovation contract)
7) Any bills/ correspondences showing that you have moved into the property (e.g. mover’s invoice etc.)
#You may wish to note that the list of supporting documents is not exhaustive and we will consider your application as long as you are able to show that the lease on your property has been pre-terminated.

questions.title: How do I know if my residential property is taxed at the owner-occupier tax rates or non-onwer-occupier residential tax rates?
questions.text:
From your property tax notice and bill, the tax rate applied on the property is indicated in brackets as [Owner-Occupier Tax Rates] or [Non-owner-occupier Residential Tax Rates] under the “AV and Tax Rates” Column.
Alternatively, you can log in to mytax.iras.gov.sg with your Singpass > Property > View Property Summary.

questions.title: Who qualifies for owner-occupier tax rates?
questions.text: You (as an individual or a married couple) must own and reside in the residential property to qualify for owner-occupier tax rates. If you are a married couple that owns 2 homes, the concession can only be applied to 1 home. Please note that even if a married couple were to occupy two homes, the owner-occupier tax rates can only apply to one of the homes. This is regardless of whether it is owned jointly or separately by the spouses.

questions.title: How does IRAS calculate my annual property tax payable?
questions.text:
Annual property tax is calculated by multiplying the Annual Value (AV) of the property with the Property Tax Rates that apply to you.
For example, if the AV of your property is $30,000 and your tax rate is 10%, you would pay $30,000 x 10% = $3,000 in property taxes.

questions.title: How does IRAS determine the Annual Value (AV) of my residential property?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) is the estimated gross annual rent of the property if it were to be rented out, excluding furniture, furnishings and maintenance fees. It is determined based on estimated market rentals of similar or comparable residential properties and not on the actual rental income received.
The way the AV is determined is the same regardless of whether the property is owner-occupied, vacant or rented out.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen born in 1979 or earlier. How much CareShield Life participation incentives am I eligible for if I join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024?
questions.text:
The Total Participation Incentives you are eligible for will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset the annual premium payable in that year.
For Singapore Citizens who join and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2023:
You will still be eligible for Participation Incentives of up to $4,000 even if you have previously opted out, as long as you are a Singapore Citizen who joins and are covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2023.
For Singapore Citizens who join and are covered under CareShield Life between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024:
You may also access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass for information on your personalised premiums and premium support, which includes the participation incentives you are eligible for.
These Participation Incentives will not apply if you join and are covered under CareShield Life after 31 December 2024. Therefore, you are encouraged to apply to join CareShield Life early if you are planning to do so.
topics: CareShield Life / Joining CareShield Life for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier

questions.title: How do I apply for a birth extract if I lost my birth certificate?
questions.text: You may refer to the ICA website for more information on the application, processing time and download of a birth extract.

questions.title: Are there document photocopying or printing services in ICA Services Centre?
questions.text: There are no photocopying or printing services in ICA Services Centre. Please have your documents ready before visiting ICA Services Centre.

questions.title: Are there photo-taking services in ICA Services Centre?
questions.text: There are no photo-taking services at ICA Services Centre.

questions.title: Can I use a photocopy of my IC?
questions.text: You may wish to consult the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) at 6377-3131 or use the PDPC Feedback and Query Form as the advisory guidelines on the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) for NRIC and other national identification numbers are under the purview of the PDPC.

questions.title: Can I visit ICA Services Centre?
questions.text: You may refer to Visiting ICA Services Centre for further information.

questions.title: Do I need to print out a copy of the appointment details before reporting to ICA Services Centre?
questions.text: There is no need to print out a copy of your appointment details before reporting to ICA Services Centre.

questions.title: Do I need to translate my documents that are not in English?
questions.text:
You will need to provide original documents and official translations (for documents in languages other than English) for your application for immigration facilities.
ICA accepts:
Translations provided by the embassy of the country/ place that issued the document
Translations produced by a notary public in Singapore or the country/ place that issued the document
Privately created translations attested by the embassy of the country/ place that issued the document, or notarised by a notary public in Singapore or the country/ place that issued the document.
ICA does not endorse any private translation companies or entities. Insufficient documentation may result in non-acceptance of your application. You may be required to provide additional documents to support your application.

questions.title: Do we need to affix a stamp for mail-in applications?
questions.text: A postage stamp is required if you are sending your application form by post.

questions.title: How can I access or log in to ICA e-Services?
questions.text: You can refer to the ICA website for the list of e-Services.

questions.title: How can I check the validity of a foreign passport?
questions.text: For all matters relating to foreign passport, please approach the respective country's Embassy/ Consulate/ Overseas Mission in Singapore.

questions.title: How do I access digitalPORT@SG?
questions.text: You may visit the ICA website for more information on crew clearance and related matters.

questions.title: How do I contact ICA?
questions.text:
ICA HQ
You may refer to the ICA website for more information on ICA's contact details.
ICA Checkpoints
You may visit the ICA website for the details of our checkpoints.
Alternatively, you may send in your enquiries or feedback via the ICA online feedback form for further assistance.

questions.title: How do I renew foreign passport?
questions.text: For all matters relating to foreign passport and/or documents, please approach the respective country's Embassy/ Consulate/ Overseas Mission in Singapore.

questions.title: How do I report or provide information against immigration offenders and related activities?
questions.text:
You may send your feedback or report on potential immigration offenders and related activities (illegal immigrant, overstayer, suspected marriage of convenience or sham marriage etc.) through ICA online form.
Please note that all identities and information provided to ICA are used only for our assessment or investigation purposes; and will be treated with the strictest confidence. Information gathered during our assessment or investigation is meant only for ICA to carry out our function as an immigration and checkpoints authority. We are unable to disclose any investigation findings or outcome of the case.

questions.title: How do I transfer the remains of my loved one back to Singapore?
questions.text:
If death had occurred overseas, it should be registered with the relevant foreign authorities where the death occurred.
You will require a permit from the National Environment Agency to transfer human remains from overseas to Singapore for cremation or burial.
If the deceased was a Singapore citizen or Singapore permanent resident, the deceased’s next of kin will then need to report the death to the Registry of Births and Deaths in Singapore. A proxy can also report the death with a letter of authorisation and identification document of the deceased’s next of kin.

questions.title: How do I verify the validity of Identity Card (IC) or Immigration Pass?
questions.text:
You may verify the validity of your Identity Card or Immigration Pass using the following links:
Verify Validity of Identity Card
Verify Validity of Immigration Pass

questions.title: What is a Foreign Identification Number (FIN) or FIN card?
questions.text: A Foreign Identification Number (FIN) is a unique 9-character alphanumeric serial code assigned to foreigners with Long-Term immigration passes in Singapore (e.g. Student's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass, Employment Pass, Work Permit, etc.) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or the Ministry of Manpower (MOM). This FIN is not replicated.

questions.title: What is a Statutory Declaration?
questions.text: A Statutory Declaration is a written statement of facts which is signed by the person making the statement; and solemnly declared to be true before a court, a judicial officer or a Commissioner for Oaths. A Statutory Declaration in Singapore must be in the prescribed form set out in the First Schedule of the Oaths and Declarations Act (Cap 211).

questions.title: What is an In-Principle Approval (IPA) and how can I retrieve my IPA?
questions.text:
An In-Principle Approval (IPA) is issued to an applicant while pending completion of formalities for the following immigration facilities:
Singapore Citizenship
Permanent Residence
Long-Term Visit Pass
Student's Pass
For prospective students of Institute of Higher Learning
For prospective students of other education institutions or schools
You may retrieve your IPA letter (if applicable) from the respective e-Services.

questions.text: You can refer to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website for more information.

questions.title: What is the definition of Singapore resident?
questions.text: A Singapore resident refers to a Singapore citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: What is the difference between Identity Card (IC) Number and Foreign Identification Number (FIN)?
questions.text:
National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) number is a unique 9-character alpha-numeric identification number, with prefix 'S' or 'T', issued to Singapore citizens and Permanent Residents above the age of 15.
A Foreign Identification Number (FIN) is a unique 9-character alpha-numeric identification number, with prefix 'F', 'G' or 'M' assigned to foreigners with Long-Term immigration passes in Singapore (e.g. Student's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass, Employment Pass, Work Permit, etc.) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

questions.text: You may read more about ICA's organisational structure at the ICA website.

Passport

questions.title: What is UIN? What is the difference between a UIN and FIN?
questions.text:
Unique Identification Number (UIN) is issued by Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) to Singapore citizens and Singapore permanent residents only.
Foreign Identification Number (FIN) is issued to foreigners with Long-Term immigration passes in Singapore (e.g. Student's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass, Work Pass, Work Permit etc.) by the ICA or the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

questions.title: What should I do if I lost my foreign passport in Singapore?
questions.text: You can refer to the ICA website for more information on loss of foreign passport in Singapore.

questions.title: What should I do if I suspect the call claiming to be from ICA to be a scam?
questions.text:
If you have reason to believe that the call is a scam, you are advised to take the following precautions:
Ignore such calls and the caller’s instructions
Do not provide personal information such as your name, identification number, passport details, contact details, or banking and credit card details
Report to Police if you suspect any fraudulent act or wrongdoing.
ICA takes a serious view of such scam calls as it undermines public trust in ICA. Members of the public can seek scam-related advice by calling the anti-scam centre at 1800-722-6688 or go to scamshield.gov.sg.

questions.title: What should I do if the e-Service hangs when I am entering my particulars into the system?
questions.text: You can refresh the system and resubmit the application. If you suspect that your application has been submitted, please check the application status online via the e-Service's Status Enquiry by keying in verifying fields when prompted or enquire here.

questions.title: Where can I download ICA's forms?
questions.text: You can find ICA's e-Services at https://www.ica.gov.sg/eservicesandforms and downloadable forms at https://www.ica.gov.sg/eservicesandforms/all-forms.

questions.title: Where can I park my vehicle at ICA?
questions.text:
There is no public parking at the ICA Services Centre. Those who wish to drive may park their vehicles at alternative public carparks located along North Bridge Road, Crawford Lane and French Road.
ICA Services Centre is easily accessible by public transportation services such as MRT and buses. You are strongly encouraged to make use of public transport to visit ICA Services Centre.

questions.title: Who should I report to if my passport information has been used by other people?
questions.text:
If you are a victim of cybercrime, you can make a police report online or at any Neighbourhood Police Centre (NPC).
Should you wish to provide information pertaining to any cybercrime activities, you may submit the information on the IWitness Portal at the SPF website.

questions.title: Will engaging a commercial entity increase my chance to obtain immigration facilities in Singapore?
questions.text:
Every application is assessed and determined on its own merits.
It has come to ICA's attention that there are commercial entities or consultants who claim to have a high success rate in helping applicants to obtain long-term immigration facilities, for example Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and Long-Term passes. ICA does not support or endorse the services offered by these commercial entities/ consultants. Applicants who choose to engage these commercial entities/ consultants for such services are advised to exercise caution, especially if it involves the sharing of personal information.
ICA shall not be responsible or held accountable in any way for any loss that you may suffer arising from your engagement of services provided by these commercial entities/ consultants.

questions.title: What is the photo requirement for ICA applications?
questions.text: Please refer to our photo guidelines for more information.

questions.title: How do I cancel or withdraw the submitted SG Arrival Card (SGAC) if I have cancelled or rescheduled my trip due to change in plans?
questions.text:
You do not need to withdraw or void the submission if you are cancelling your trip.
If you are planning for a new trip to Singapore, you are required to submit a new SG Arrival Card.
If you are using MyICA mobile app, you can delete your record by selecting the record that you wish to delete in 'Group Submission'. Please note that the 'delete' function in the mobile application is meant for travellers to clear their records:
i) after their trip is completed, or
ii) before the submission of their trip information.
Records that are deleted would not result in the retraction of records that have been submitted to ICA.
topics: SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass)
SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) / General

questions.title: I have submitted my SG Arrival Card (SGAC) with health declaration. How can I retrieve my submitted SGAC with health declaration if I did not print the acknowledgement?
questions.text:
Upon successful submission of the SG Arrival Card (SGAC), an acknowledgement email, which contains information on your arrival declarations will be sent to the email address provided in your SGAC submission. Foreign visitors will be able to find the Disembarkation/ Embarkation (DE) number in the acknowledgement email.
Travellers who had submitted the SGAC at ICA e-Service will be able to download a PDF copy of their declarations after submission.
Please be informed that the acknowledgement email would suffice. You can refer to the email spam/ junk folder if you are unable to find the acknowledgement email in your email inbox.
Upon arrival in Singapore, please show the acknowledgement email on your mobile device or a printout copy to the ICA officers.
topics: SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass)
SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) / General

questions.title: My trip to Singapore is cancelled. How do I withdraw the submitted SG Arrival Card (Individual/ Group) for the cancelled trip?
questions.text:
You do not need to withdraw or void the SGAC submission if you are cancelling your trip.
If you are planning for a new trip to Singapore, you are required to submit a new SG Arrival Card.
If you are using MyICA mobile app, you can delete your record by selecting the record that you wish to delete in 'Group Submission'. Please note that the 'delete' function in the mobile application is meant for travellers to clear their records:
i) after their trip is completed, or
ii) before the submission of their trip information.
Records that are deleted would not result in the retraction of records that have been submitted to ICA.
topics: SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass)
SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) / General

questions.title: How do I update my mobile number or handphone number to retrieve my Digital Student's Pass (STP) if I have changed my number?
questions.text:
Singpass holders can login to the FileSG website and view their digital Student's Pass (STP) without OTP authentication.
STP holders who do not have a Singpass account can update their mobile number or handphone number via the e-Service.

questions.title: Can Immigration Exemption Order (IEO) holders study in Singapore?
questions.text: If you hold a valid Immigration Exemption Order (IEO), you are not required to obtain a Student's Pass to pursue full-time studies in an approved institution in Singapore.

questions.title: I am holding a valid Dependant's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass or Immigration Exemption Order (DP/ LTVP/ IEO) and studying full-time in a Private Education Institution (PEI). Can I continue my existing course with the PEI if I no longer hold a valid DP/LTVP/IEO?
questions.text:
Foreigners who are holding a valid Dependant's Pass, Long-Term Visit Pass or Immigration Exemption Order and are enrolled in full-time courses at EduTrust-certified Private Education Institutions (PEIs) may apply for a Student's Pass to complete their course with the PEI when their existing passes expire. A Student's Pass will not be issued to foreigners enrolled in PEIs that are not EduTrust-certified.
For more information on Private Education-related matters, please visit the SWDA website.

questions.title: Can I bring seafood (fish, prawn etc.), fruits and/or vegetables into Singapore?
questions.text: Please visit the Singapore Food Agency website for more information.

questions.title: Do I have to retrieve or download and print the approved e-Visa to travel to Singapore?
questions.text:
You are strongly encouraged to print and bring along your e-Visa to avoid any inconvenience as the airlines and immigration authorities of your country of embarkation are likely to ask for the e-Visa for verification.
You can retrieve your valid e-Visa via the 'Enquire Application Status' function at the ICA e-Service with the visa application reference number and applicant's travel document number.

questions.title: What is the difference between Multiple Journey Visa (MJV) and Single Journey Visa (SJV)?
questions.text:
A Multiple Journey Visa (MJV) has no limit on the number of times you can use the visa so long as it is within the validity period of the issued visa. A single journey visa (SJV) allows you to use the visa once.
Please note that possessing a valid visa does not guarantee entry into Singapore. You will have to satisfy the basic entry requirements before you can be considered for entry into Singapore.

questions.title: Can birth registration be done by a proxy on behalf of the parents with a letter of authorisation?
questions.text:
Only parents are eligible to use LifeSG to register the birth of their newborn.
If the parents are unable to register the child’s birth on LifeSG please email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg for assistance.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I change my child’s particulars after I have submitted the birth registration via LifeSG?
questions.text:
No changes are allowed once the birth registration is submitted.
If you wish to alter your child’s name after the birth has been registered, please refer to ICA website (Alteration of Child's Name on Birth Certificate) for more information on the application procedure and relevant fees.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I convert current physical copy of birth certificate into digital format?
questions.text: Birth certificates issued after 29 May 2022 are in digital format. Birth certificates issued before this date remain valid and will not be converted into digital format.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I download the digital birth certificate of my child after 90 days? If yes, any fee involved?
questions.text: Parents may contact ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg for assistance on the download of your child's digital birth certificate after 90 days.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I register my child’s birth over the counter at the ICA Services Centre instead of using LifeSG?
questions.text: From 29 May 2022, all parents are required to register their child’s birth via LifeSG’s birth registration service. You may refer to the ICA website for more information on birth registration and to download the digital birth certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Can I still register my child’s birth at the hospital registration counter?
questions.text: Maternity hospitals have ceased their birth registration services since 29 May 2022.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Do I need to translate foreign-issued documents into English for the purpose of birth registration?
questions.text: As with current procedures for submission of documents to ICA, you will need to provide official translation for documents in languages other than English.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: How do I obtain the digital birth certificate if ICA’s e-Service is not working?
questions.text:
Parents are advised to access ICA e-Service when the system resumes.
If there is an urgency, parents may email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg for assistance.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: How do I register my child’s birth if LifeSG is down for maintenance?
questions.text: As parents have 42 days to complete the birth registration, you may access LifeSG when the system resumes.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: How do I register the birth if my child is not born in the hospital?
questions.text:
If your child is not born in the hospital, the birth of the child must be registered at ICA Services Centre.
Before this, parents must email the following documents to ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg:
- Proof of child's birth
- Proof of pre-natal checks
- Pre-natal appointment card/booklet
- Pregnancy ultrasound scan
- Parents' identification documents
- Marriage certificate (if any)
We will notify parents via email within 3 working days to report to ICA Services Centre in person for the birth registration.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: I am a Singaporean and my child is born overseas. Can I register my child's birth via LifeSG?
questions.text:
ICA does not register birth of a child who is born overseas. You should register the child's birth and obtain the birth certificate from the foreign authorities in the country/ place where the child was born.
You may refer to the ICA website for more information on citizenship application for your child.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: I had earlier registered my child’s birth at ICA. Will I be issued with a digital birth certificate?
questions.text: Digital birth certificates will be issued only for births that are registered from 29 May 2022.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: What if I am not notified of my child’s birth registration after 3 working days from submission?
questions.text: You may email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg with your details.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: What if I lose the digital birth certificate of my child? Can I re-download the certificate?
questions.text: Parents can access ICA e-Service to download the digital birth certificate again within the 90-day period (from date of registration).
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: What should I do if I cannot register my child's birth via LifeSG?
questions.text:
If you have difficulty using LifeSG, you may visit the ServiceSG Centres for assistance to register your child's birth via LifeSG.
The ServiceSG Centres can also assist you to apply for a Singpass account if you do not have one, or to download and save your child's digital birth certificate in your personal device.
Alternatively, you may email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg for assistance.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: Will there still be physical birth certificates issued?
questions.text: All birth certificates issued on and after 29 May 2022 will be in digital (PDF) format. When downloading the certificates from the ICA website, parents can save a copy and print if required.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Birth Registration Process

questions.title: [ABS] I want an immediate booking slot but the earliest is only x days away. [Applicable for both scenarios: (i) Individual had already self-booked appointment and want to reschedule to earlier date, or (ii) Individual has not booked any appointment yet]
questions.text: Appointment booking system will show all the available slots. The first slot you see is the earliest available slot for the selected location/mode.
topics: Appointment Booking (ABS) / Booking Process - Careers Connect

questions.title: I am insured under CareShield Life/ElderShield. However, I have not developed severe disability. Can I apply for Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)?
questions.text:
If you have not developed severe disability but require some assistance with at least three out of six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), you may apply for Home Caregiving Grant (moderate disability scheme) should you meet the following non-disability eligibility criteria:
a. Singapore Citizen.
Permanent Resident can qualify if either a parent, child or spouse is a Singapore Citizen.
b. Not in a residential long-term care institution (e.g. nursing home).
c. Lives in Singapore.
d. Means-tested.
Household monthly income per person is $2,800 or less; or annual value of property for household without income is $13,000 or less.
To apply, you should visit a General Practitioner or arrange with your care provider to obtain a Functional Assessment Report and submit an application to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

questions.title: How do I view the full copy of my registered Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
After your LPA has been registered, you and your Donees can retrieve it at any time by logging in to the Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) with your Singpass.
If you would like to keep a printed copy of the LPA for personal reference, you can print the PDF after downloading it from OPGO. However, the printed copy will be watermarked and cannot be used for transactions.
Please follow the steps below to view the full LPA:
Open the LPA with Adobe Acrobat Reader DC.
Click on the paper clip icon located on the left panel. This opens up a tab called ‘Attachments’.
Double click the attachment named LPA Form_Certified_XXXXX.pdf to view your full LPA.
Please ensure that your device’s default setting is opening the PDF via Adobe instead of web browser.

questions.title: I am a salesperson submitting an application on behalf of my clients (i.e. buyers or sellers). Do I need to log on using my own personal Singpass or using the buyers’/ sellers' Singpass?
questions.text: As a salesperson, you should log in using your own NRIC number and Singpass.

questions.text:
The person who is doing the submission via the e-Resale system will have to log in using his/her own NRIC

(i) At the (Online Submission of Resale Applications and Request for Value) page of the e-Resale system,
choose 'Submit Resale Application'.
(ii) Log in using your NRIC number and Singpass.
(iii)
Provide all the information requested in the application form.

Personal particulars of the buyers/ sellers and the resale flat transaction details in the Option to Purchase
