questions.title: Does ICA disclose my personal data submitted in applications?
questions.text:
Personal data submitted for application purposes will be shared with relevant government agencies to screen, assess and review the applications. This is necessary as part of immigration control and national security. Safeguards are in place to limit and protect the information shared.
ICA will not share your personal data with non-Government entities, except where such entities have been authorised to carry out specific Government services.
ICA will never sell your personal data.

questions.title: What are the purposes for data collection and processing at ICA’s Services Centre?
questions.text:
Personal data is collected and processed at our Services Centre to fulfil ICA’s statutory functions of national registration and immigration administration. They include—
1. National Registration (e.g. registration/re-registration of NRIC, change of address, etc.)
2. Passport application
3. Registration of birth and death
4. Application for immigration facilities –
Singapore Citizenship
Permanent Residence
Long-Term Visit Pass
Student’s Pass
5. Others – Application for:
Entry visa
APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)
Singapore-United States of America Trusted Traveller Programme
Extension of Visit Pass

questions.title: What happens to my personal data if I withdraw my application e.g. an application for Singapore Citizenship?
questions.text:
Upon withdrawal of application*, ICA will stop processing your personal data for the purpose of the application, including not disclosing your personal data to other relevant government agencies for further assessment of your application. However, as the right to data erasure does not apply under Singapore’s data protection law, please note that ICA is not required to delete your data from our systems. For other purposes authorised or mandated by law, we may still process your personal data for those purposes.
*where applicable

questions.title: Why does ICA require comprehensive information from me in applications?
questions.text:
National security and interests are of top priority when ICA executes our statutory functions. Under the National Registration Act/Regulations, ICA regulates the registration of persons in Singapore for the issuance of identity cards and its related purposes. There is a need for sufficient information to be collected to ensure a high degree of accuracy of our national registry records and correct identification of individuals. This contributes to the effective administration of benefits and programmes by other government agencies and the maintenance of law and order in Singapore.
Similarly, the Singapore passport is an official document to be used as evidence of identity and citizenship by Singapore citizens when travelling internationally. It also affords protection to the bearer by enabling the bearer to secure assistance from Singapore consular officials abroad. With the international recognition and privileges of the Singapore passport, collection of personal data during passport application is essential to ensure and verify that the Singapore passport is issued to the right individuals and minimise the abuse of the passport.
For individuals seeking to apply for an immigration facility in Singapore e.g. Singapore Citizenship, Permanent Residence or Long-Term Visit Pass, ICA needs to collect detailed information from applicants, their sponsor, and family members in accordance with our immigration policies. Information collection, rigorous assessment and checks are essential to protect national interests and security, to prevent any systemic abuses or the entry of undesirable persons and ensure that only deserving applicants are granted long-term stay facilities in Singapore.

questions.title: What is SG Arrival Card or SGAC?
questions.text:
SG Arrival Card, also known as SGAC, is the electronic version of the paper Disembarkation/Embarkation (DE) card that every foreign visitor must present for immigration clearance. A DE number is provided to foreign visitors after SGAC submission.
The submission of the SG Arrival Card is one of the basic entry requirements to visit Singapore. The use of the SG Arrival Card e-Service is free of charge. Please also note that the SG Arrival Card is not a visa.
topics: SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass)
SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) / General

questions.title: My elderly mother is staying in a nursing home and has rented out her property to pay for her own expenses. Can IRAS reinistate the owner-occupier tax rates on her property?
questions.text: As your mother has rented out her property, the owner-occupier tax rates are not applicable, and the property tax is payable based on the residential tax rate. While we appreciate that she has reasons for not staying in her property, we regret that we are unable to accede to her request to reinstate the owner-occupier tax rates to the property.

questions.title: If I own and occupy more than one residential property concurrently, what will be the tax rates applied?
questions.text: The owner-occupier tax rates are only granted to one property owned and occupied by you. For subsequent properties, you will be taxed at non-owner-occupier residential tax rates even if you are occupying it as your second home.

questions.title: My property is not rented out. How does IRAS estimate its rental value in order to arrive at the Annual Value (AV)?
questions.text: IRAS would analyse the rents of comparable or similar properties that have been rented out and make adjustments to the values to account for differences in location, size, conditions and other physical attributes.

questions.title: The actual rent for my property is $2,500 per month. However, IRAS has informed that the Annual Value (AV) is $3,000 per month. How does IRAS determine the AV?
questions.text: The AV could be higher or lower than the actual rental as the AV reflects the market rent at the time IRAS reviews the AV, whereas the actual rental could have been fixed earlier.

questions.title: Why is IRAS using rental value instead of sale prices to determine the Annual Value (AV) of properties?
questions.text:
IRAS uses the annual market rent of comparable properties to determine the AV instead of transacted sale prices because:
There are generally more rental transactions than sales transactions. A higher number of transactions gives a more accurate picture of market activity.
The movements in sale prices are more volatile than rentals prices. Hence, using rental transactions to derive the AV helps to keep property tax more stable for property owners. Other countries like Hong Kong and Malaysia also adopt the same practice of using market rents to determine the AV.
Using historical purchase price to determine AV would be inequitable towards newer owners. This is because the prices of similar and comparable properties can change over time. For instance, newer owners may have a higher AV than those who bought properties in the past if properties prices increase over time.

questions.title: Can I object to the Annual Value (AV) of my property?
questions.text: You can object to the AV and/or its effective date within 30 days from the date of the Valuation Notice . If you do not receive the Valuation Notice, you can also object to the AV at any time in the year if you can show that the market values have dropped to below the AV. You cannot, however, object to the tax rates.

questions.title: I purchased an HDB flat for owner occupation and granted the sellers a rent-free extension of stay for 3 months after the resale completion date. Can IRAS make an exception to apply the owner-occupier tax rates (OOTR) on my flat during the 3-month extension of stay period?
questions.text: No. OOTR is a concession given only if the owner is residing in the flat. As you are not residing in the flat during the extension of stay period, OOTR will not be applicable. Whether rent is involved for the extension period is not a relevant consideration for the OOTR concession.

questions.title: Sellers of HDB flats may arrange with the buyers for a temporary extension of stay in the flat for up to 3 months after the resale completion. During the extension of stay, is the seller or buyer responsible to pay the property tax?
questions.text: Once the flat is transferred to the buyer, the buyer is responsible to pay any outstanding property tax. The extension of stay is a private arrangement between the seller and the buyer, and the parties may wish to liaise separately on payment matters. IRAS does not arbitrate on this matter. Please note the concessionary owner-occupier tax rates will not be applicable during the period when the seller continues to reside in the flat after the resale transaction has been completed. The lower tax rates would only apply from the date the new owner moves in to reside in the flat.

questions.title: I purchased an HDB flat and allowed the previous owner to extend his stay for 3 months after the transfer of the flat. I understand that the previous owner has paid the property tax in full based on the owner-occupier tax rates. Why was I notified now to pay an additional property tax?
questions.text: The lower owner-occupier tax rates is a concession granted only if the owner is residing in the flat. The owner-occupier tax rates will not be applied on the flat for the extension of stay period because you are not residing in the flat. During the extension of stay period, the higher residential tax rates would apply, which would result in additional property tax payable.

questions.title: Are new property owners responsible for paying all outstanding property tax on the property?
questions.text:
Once IRAS is notified of the property transfer, all property tax related correspondence including property tax bills will be sent to you as the new owner.
As the property owner, you will be liable for all property tax on the property. Hence it is important that you, through your lawyer, enquire if there are any outstanding or future property tax liabilities, and make provisions for the seller to reimburse you for the property tax amount that is to be borne by him.

questions.title: My co-owner and I own 50% of the shares of the property respectively. Can IRAS split the property tax amount and send separate bills to each of us instead?
questions.text:
The property tax bill will be issued to the owner who is listed first in the Notice of Transfer filed by the seller's lawyer. The payment arrangement on the property tax payable is a private matter to be settled among the property owners. We are unable
to issue separate bills.

questions.title: My husband and I are co-owners of a property. Why do we see two amounts when we log in to myTax Portal? Are both owners required to pay?
questions.text:
Property tax is a tax levied on property ownership. The payment arrangement on the property tax payable is a private matter to be settled among the property owners. If one of the owners has made payment, the co-owner is not required to make another payment for the same property.
Both owners will be able to view the same amount in myTax Portal as it is tied to the same property.

questions.title: I reside in property (A) while my wife resides in property (B). Are the owner-occupier tax rates allowed to be applied on both properties?
questions.text: Under the Property Tax Act, when 2 owners are married to each other, you can only apply the owner-occupier tax rates to 1 owner-occupied home, regardless of whether it is owned jointly or separately by both of you.

questions.title: I relocated overseas for work purpose. Can the owner-occupier tax rates (OOTR) still apply on my residential property which is my default residence in Singapore?
questions.text: If you (the property owner) reside outside of Singapore temporarily for official or business purposes, OOTR can still be applied so long as your residential property is maintained as your home and is not rented out.

questions.title: Will the 2024 increase in Annual Value (AV) impact my eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The disbursement of social support schemes (e.g. CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, MediShield Life Premium Subsidies) will not be affected by the revision of Annual Values (AVs) in 2024 as AVs as of 2023 will be used to determine scheme eligibility in 2024. The Government will continue to review our social support schemes to ensure that Singaporeans in need of support receive it.
topics: CareShield Life / CareShield Life Premiums and Government Support

questions.title: Where do I obtain my Student's Pass application number which is required for SOLAR or SOLAR+?
questions.text: You may approach your educational institution/ school to obtain your Student's Pass application number in order to access the SOLAR or SOLAR+ e-Service.

questions.title: Under the Healthier SG Chronic Tier, can I receive subsidies for chronic medications that are not found on the Healthier SG Medication List?
questions.text:
Yes, CHAS, Merdeka Generation (MG) and Pioneer Generation (PG) cardholders can still receive dollar-based subsidies between $28 and $135 per visit, subjected to their eligible annual cap (based on their CHAS/MG/PG card status).
Healthier SG benefits and subsidies are available/accessible at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic.

questions.title: Will private entities such as banks or insurance companies accept the digital certificates? How can one verify the digital birth certificate or digital death certificate?
questions.text: Digital birth or death certificates will be the default form issued from 29 May 2022. Private entities should use the QR code embedded on the digital certificate to verify the digital certificate online at the ICA website.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Verification of Digital Certificate

questions.title: How should I stamp a Novation Agreement or an Assignment of Lease to a new Landlord instead of to a new Tenant?
questions.text:
For an assignment of lease to a new landlord, stamp duty is chargeable on the consideration, if any, at the BSD rates. If there is no consideration paid, stamp duty is not applicable.
If you are unsure whether your agreement is subject to stamp duty, please submit your document for our assessment through the e-Stamping Portal by following these steps:
1. Go to myTax Portal and click on "Stamp Duty".
2. Log in as an Individual User or Business User.
3. Click on “Requests” in the top navigation bar.
4. Select “Apply for Assessment/Appeal”.
Upon successful submission, you will receive a case reference number, and you will be notified once the review is completed.

questions.title: I am a single Singapore Citizen and currently own a condominium unit. If I buy a resale HDB flat, do I have to pay Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)?
questions.text:
For Singapore Citizens purchasing an HDB flat (including a resale flat) or a New EC, ABSD is remitted. More information is available under "Acquisition of HDB Flats and New Executive Condominium (EC) Units".
1. Remission is granted automatically upon HDB's approval of the acquisition.
2. Remission is not applicable for Resale EC.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I intend to sell my current private property (of which I am the sole owner) and buy another private property under my sole name. If the buyer exercises the option to purchase, is there a grace period before I can purchase another residential property without incurring Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)?
questions.text:
If a contract or an agreement to purchase the property has been signed, that property is considered to be acquired by the buyer and sold by the seller.
Hence, if a Singapore Citizen purchases a residential property after the contract or agreement for sale of his/her current property is executed, and he/she does not own any other residential property, ABSD is not payable.
For non-Singapore Citizens, they will be considered as purchasing their first property, and the relevant ABSD rate is applicable.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: How do I log in to the e-Stamping portal as a Business User?
questions.text:
To access the e-Stamping Portal as a Business User, you must first be authorised under Corppass for a "Corporate" Role.
Once authorised under Corppass, please follow these steps to register for an e-Stamping Account:
1. Log in to myTax Portal under Stamp Duty as a Business User.
2. Click on "Account" > select "Register a New Account".
3. An Assigned ID will be generated instantly upon successful registration (Assigned ID typically starts with AXXXXXXXXY - X refers to numeric, Y refers to alphabet).
4. Reauthorize the relevant individuals or yourself under Corppass for e-Stamping services using the Assigned ID (AXXXXXXXXY) generated.
Refer to the guide for Account Registration for more information. If you need assistance in adding/amending authorized roles for e-stamping services in Corppass, please contact Corppass at 6335 3530.

questions.title: I had earlier stamped my tenancy agreement and need to make amendments. How do I amend the lease start date?
questions.text:
To amend the lease start date of the tenancy period, please provide a copy of the Tenancy Agreement for our review by following these steps:
1. Log in to myTax Portal under "Stamp Duty".
2. Click on "Inbox" and select "Compose Mail".
3. Input the Document Reference No. before proceeding with your request for amendment.
You do not need to submit a new stamping or revise the stamping record done previously if the lease period has not commenced, and you bring forward or defer the lease without changes in lease term and gross rent.

questions.title: I am a foreigner, and my spouse is a US Citizen. Is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable if we were to purchase a residential property?
questions.text:
ABSD remission under the Free Trade Agreement will apply if the individual is a citizen of the United States of America (US). He/She will receive the same Stamp Duty treatment as Singapore Citizens.
Therefore, if an individual who is a US citizen jointly purchases a residential property with his/her spouse, the ABSD Spouses Remission may be applicable. ABSD will be remitted if all conditions are met, and they do not own any other residential property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I had stamped on a 2-year tenancy agreement. However, the tenancy period was changed to 1 year instead. Can I get a stamp duty refund?
questions.text:
Stamping is required if a new agreement was executed to effect the change.
However, if you had cancelled the previous agreement, no refund can be allowed if the instrument has been made use of.
An instrument is considered 'made use of' if any of the parties to the instrument has enforced his/her rights under the instrument or has in any way acted on the terms of the instrument.
Examples of this include when payment has been made, a deposit has been forfeited, compensation has been obtained, possession of the property has been taken, or the lease term has commenced.

questions.title: If I had extended the tenancy period, do I need to stamp on the extension? And how is the stamp duty computed?
questions.text:
Stamp Duty is a tax on documents (physical or electronic), and there is no stamp duty liability if no documents are executed.
If there is a document executed to extend the lease, stamp duty is payable based on the extended lease period. The lease duty rate is 0.4%.
You can stamp the document at myTaxPortal, click on "Stamp Duty" and under "Stamping" > "Lease/Tenancy" > select "Variation of Lease" under the Nature of Transaction.

questions.title: What services does AIC provide?
questions.text:
The following are the available services under AIC:
Care at Home such as Medical Escort and Transport, Meals On Wheels, Enahanced Home Personal Care, Home Nursing, Home Medical, and Home Therapy.
Care at Centre such as Active Ageing Centre, Day Care, Community Rehabilitation.
Stay-In Care such as Nursing Homes, Sheltered Homes, Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care.
Respite for Caregivers such as Nursing Home Respite
Mental Health Services such as Psychiatric Rehabilitation and Re-integration, Mental Health GP Partnership/ Polyclinic
Please click here for more information on Care Services and Programmes under AIC.
topics: General information on Agency for Integrated Care

questions.title: What is Advance Care Planning (ACP)?
questions.text:
Advance Care Planning (ACP) is a series of conversations to let your family and doctors know how you want to be cared for in the event that you become unable to make decisions for yourself.
ACP allows you to make these decisions ahead of time, discuss the values that underlie these decisions, write down your wishes and communicate them with family members.
You may click here for more information on ACP.
topics: Caregiving Information and Services / Support for Seniors and Caregivers

questions.title: Who can I speak to on Advance Care Planning (ACP)?
questions.text:
You can call 1800-650-6060 or click here if you have any enquiries on Advance Care Planning (ACP).
You can also speak to your healthcare provider to find out more about ACP.
topics: Caregiving Information and Services / Support for Seniors and Caregivers

questions.title: What is Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)?
questions.text:
The Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) is an assistance scheme set up in 2002 for a small group of seniors. They were not eligible for ElderShield at the time, because they were too old or had pre-existing disabilities.
The monthly payout can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses.
Please click here for more information on IDAPE.

questions.title: How can apply for Dementia Day Care?
questions.text:
To apply for Dementia Day Care service, you may approach your loved ones' doctor at the hospital/ polyclinic/ private clinic where they are currently receiving treatment at, to assist with the application for the aforementioned services.
Please click here for more information on the Dementia Day Care service.

questions.title: How to be a Silver Generation Ambassador (SGA)?
topics: General information on Agency for Integrated Care
General information on Agency for Integrated Care / Silver Generation Office

questions.title: What is the training provided to be a Silver Generation Office (SGA)?
questions.text:
Silver Generation Office provides volunteers with…
· Informative training sessions, including role playing to improve engagement skills
· Strong support and guidance
· Various learning and volunteer development opportunities
Please click here for more information about Silver Generation Ambassador.
topics: General information on Agency for Integrated Care
General information on Agency for Integrated Care / Silver Generation Office

questions.title: If senior is in a nursing home, can I still apply for Home Caregiving Grant Scheme (HCG)?
questions.text:
The Home Caregiving Grant is intended to support lower- to middle-income households to care for their disabled loved ones in the community, to support ageing in place and delay institutional care.
Seniors, who are being taken care of in Nursing Homes will thus, not be eligible for this grant. Nonetheless, they may be eligible for means-tested Government subsidies for their nursing home fees and will not be eligible for this Home Caregiving Grant.
Please click here for more information about Home Caregiving Grant.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)

questions.title: What are the eligibility criteria for Home Caregiving Scheme (HCG)?
questions.text:
How to qualify
There are a few criteria your loved one will need to meet to qualify for HCG.
Criteria
Description
Care recipient's nationality
He/ she must be a:
Singapore Citizen
OR
PR (with a parent, child or spouse who is a living Singapore Citizen).
Care recipient's residence
He/ she must:
Be living in Singapore.
Not be living in a residential long-term care institution.
Care recipient's household income
He/ she must meet the means-test criteria for HCG:
Household monthly income per person must be $4,800 or less.
Find out how to update your household details for means-testing
OR
Annual value (AV) of property under $21,000 if there is no household income.
Care recipient's needs
He/ she must:
Permanently requires some assistance with at least three of the six activities of daily living. The six activities are:
Undergo disability assessment.
This must be done by a General Practitioner (GP) or an approved healthcare professional using a Functional Assessment Report (FAR).
Find out how to book an appointment to do the FAR.
You will need to pay the assessment fee, if any. The cost may vary so do check with your healthcare professional.
For care recipients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Intellectual Disability (ID)
His/ her needs will be determined by a Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)-approved assessor using a Client Assessment Form (CAF).
If he/ she lacks mental capacity
Find out more about applying on behalf of someone who lacks capacity.
For those currently applying for severe disability schemes
You do not need to complete the FAR if you are currently applying for:
IDAPE
ElderFund
ElderShield
CareShield Life
MediSave Care
The severe disability assessment done by the MOH-accredited severe disability assessor is enough to assess your level of disability for HCG. This way, you do not need to pay 2 separate assessment fees.
Please click here for more information about Home Caregiving Grant.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)

questions.title: Silver Support Scheme
questions.text:
The Silver Support Scheme provides additional support for elderly Singaporeans who had low incomes through life and who now have little or no family support. There is no need to apply for Silver Support.
You may call the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board at 1800 227 1188 or click here for more information on the scheme.

questions.title: Who is suitable for nursing home placement?
questions.text:
Nursing homes offer long-term care for care recipients who need help with their day-to-day or nursing care needs. This is a residential care service, meaning that the care recipient will move into the nursing home and be cared for there.
Who is this service for
The care recipient:
Has a physical or mental disability due to illness
Is unable to move around and/or do his/ her daily living activities without help or supervision as a result
Cannot be cared for at home, even after you have tried all other options such as day care centres or home care services
Please click here for more information about Nursing Homes.

questions.title: What is Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Services (IHPCS)?
questions.text:
Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS) provides medical and emotional support for patients with serious illnesses who can no longer be cared for at home. The goal is to improve their quality of life by relieving pain and discomfort, and support both the patient and their caregivers.
This is for patients with a serious illness with:
Prognosis of less than 3 months AND
Require specialised care that cannot be provided at home, at a centre or in a nursing home
Prognosis of 12 months or less AND
Require time-limited care of up to 28 calendar days for severe symptoms that cannot be managed in the community
Please click here for more information on IHPCS.

questions.title: What is the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
The Silver Support Scheme provides additional support for elderly Singaporeans who had low incomes through life and who now have little or no family support. There is no need to apply for Silver Support.
Please click here or call 1800 227 1188 for more information on the Silver Support Scheme.

questions.title: How to apply and what are the costs to attend Active Ageing Centre?
questions.text:
How to apply
You may drop by an AAC in your neighbourhood to sign up.
Cost
Activities at AACs are largely free. There may be a fee for selected activities or outings.
To find an AAC near you, search this map using a postal code,
Please click here for more information on Active Ageing Centre.
topics: Centre-Based Care Services / Active Ageing Centre

questions.title: How to find an AAC near me?
questions.text: To find an AAC near you, click here using your postal code.
topics: Centre-Based Care Services / Active Ageing Centre

questions.title: What are the service provided at Active Ageing Centres (AAC)?
questions.text:
Services/ activities at AACs may include:
Active ageing programmes: Fun activities like karaoke, arts and crafts, cooking and exercises to keep the mind and body active.
Befriending and buddying: Home visits and phone calls for vulnerable seniors.
Information and referrals: Get help with understanding and applying for useful eldercare-related schemes, grants or support.
Social connector: AAC staff/ volunteers provide social and lifestyle interventions to support seniors in adhering to their health plan recommendations.
Community screening(s): Seniors can measure vital signs in adherence to their health plan.
Volunteer opportunities: Seniors who wish to give back can volunteer at the AAC.
Emergency alert response: AAC staff at selected centres respond to emergency alerts from seniors in distress.
To find an AAC near you, search this map using a postal code, address or your device’s current location.
Please click here for more information on Active Ageing Centres (AAC).
topics: Centre-Based Care Services / Active Ageing Centre

questions.title: What is an Active Ageing Centre (AAC)?
questions.text:
Active Ageing Centres (AACs) provide a range of activities for seniors to be active and connected. These centres provide opportunities for seniors to stay physically and mentally active explore interests and meet other seniors. Seniors who wish to give back to the community can also choose to volunteer at AACs.
Besides AACs, there are also centres called Active Ageing Centres (Care). These centres offer the same services as AACs, and additionally provide care services such as day care and community rehabilitation.
This is for:
Seniors aged 60 and above
Singapore Citizen or PR regardless of housing and income
topics: Centre-Based Care Services / Active Ageing Centre

questions.title: What is MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is a long-term care scheme that allows Singaporeans and PRs who are severely disabled to make monthly cash withdrawals from their own and their spouse’s MediSave Accounts.
The withdrawals can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses.
Click here to read more information about MediSave Care.

questions.title: Who should I inform if the patient passed away?
questions.text: You may email a copy of the patient's death certificate to apply@aic.sg for our records.

questions.title: How much does ACP cost?
questions.text:
You can check the cost with the ACP provider directly.
Please visit the ACP Directory for their contact details.
topics: Caregiving Information and Services / Support for Seniors and Caregivers

questions.title: How can I apply for Home Nursing services?
questions.text:
For subsidised Home Nursing service, you need to get a referral from a hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with you or your loved ones’ condition and needs, or alternatively, visit an AIC Link near you.
Cost of service starts from $80 per visit before means-testing subsidy. If you require financial assistance for the service, please speak to your service provider or the Medical Social Worker in the hospital or polyclinic.
For more information on caregiving support, please click here to access the Care Services Recommender on the Support Go Where webpage.

questions.title: Who can apply for a Voluntary Visit Limit?
questions.text: Any Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident can apply for a Voluntary Visit Limit.

questions.title: I do not have SingPass account. What should I do?
questions.text: Please visit www.singpass.gov.sg to register for a SingPass account.

questions.title: Does the applicant have to be a Singapore Citizen to be eligible for ComCare assistance?
questions.text: Yes, the applicant must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident (where at least one immediate family member of the same household is a Singapore Citizen) to be eligible for ComCare Assistance. Find out more about ComCare here.

questions.title: Can I apply for ComCare assistance if I have refunded my SIRS payout?
questions.text:
Low-income households that are unable to afford their basic living expenses can approach MSF’s Social Service Offices (SSOs) to apply for ComCare.
If you need financial assistance, you may email Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg, call the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000, or approach the nearest Social Service Office.

questions.title: How much assistance will the needy elderly receive under ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA) and Silver Support?
questions.text:
Long Term Assistance, or LTA recipients aged 65 and above will receive a standard Silver Support payout of $360 per quarter, equivalent to $120 per month.
They will continue to receive their LTA assistance.

questions.title: Since Long Term Assistance (LTA) clients will also qualify for Silver Support, will they receive too much government assistance?
questions.text:
* Unlike Long Term Assistance (LTA) which is a discretionary financial assistance scheme, Silver Support is primarily intended to temper inequalities through life by providing a modest yet meaningful cash supplement to the bottom 20-30% of elderly Singaporeans. LTA recipients aged 65 and above would form part of this target group of Silver Support recipients.
* Nonetheless, in implementing the Silver Support payout for LTA recipients, we have taken into account that their basic living expenses are already covered under LTA.
* Hence, eligible LTA recipients will thus receive an income supplement of $360 per quarter (i.e. $120 per month) through Silver Support.

questions.title: As a parent, how can I plan for my special needs child’s future after I am no longer around?
questions.text:
You can nominate your children with special needs to receive financial support by either visiting or telephoning the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) to apply for a Special Needs Saving Scheme (SNSS) Account. Having an SNSS account will allow parents to nominate their loved one with special needs to receive regular pay-outs upon their death.

questions.text:

questions.title: How do I apply for a civil divorce?
questions.text:
For Civil Divorces
To get a divorce, you need to file for divorce with the Family Justice Courts and comply with the legal requirements for divorce. The law on divorce for civil marriages in Singapore is governed by the Women’s Charter.
For more info you may refer to the Family Justice Courts (FJC)’s [Divorce in Singapore: The Essentials e-brochure].
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Divorce Support

questions.title: If my foreign spouse does not apply for Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) after marriage, will he/she be able to reside in Singapore
questions.text: If you and your non-resident spouse intend to reside in Singapore for the long term, your spouse must hold either a valid immigration pass, such as the Long-Term Visit Pass,or a work pass.
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Long-term Visit Pass (LTVP) for Transnational couples

questions.title: What is the processing time for Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA) and Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
The PMLA will be processed within one month.
For LTVP applications, for couples who have submitted a PMLA, the processing time is up to six weeks; for couples who did not go through the PMLA, the processing time is up to six months, as these couples did not submit their information to ICA through the PMLA earlier.
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA)
Support for Marriages and Divorces / Long-term Visit Pass (LTVP) for Transnational couples

questions.title: Can I submit another Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA) if I receive an unsuccessful outcome?
questions.text: You are strongly advised not to submit a fresh PMLA unless there is a change in circumstances from your previous PMLA submission. You may refer to ICA website ([https://www.ica.gov.sg/reside/pre-marriage-long-term-visit-pass-assessment] for more information on PMLA.
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA)

questions.title: If I do not go through the Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA), can I still get married?
questions.text:
Yes, your prospective spouse and you can still get married. However, being married to a Singapore Citizen does not guarantee a non-resident spouse the right to entry or long-term stay in Singapore. If you and your non-resident spouse intend to reside in Singapore for the long term, your spouse must hold either a valid immigration pass or work pass.
Hence, you are encouraged to submit the PMLA before marriage to assess your prospective spouse’s eligibility for Long-Term Visit Pass. This helps your prospective spouse and you to better plan for your future.
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA)

questions.title: I’ve gone through the Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA) and received the Letter of LTVP Eligibility (LLE). Does that mean I’ll definitely be granted LTVP later?
questions.text:
Persons issued with the LLE will generally be eligible for an LTVP if they apply within the LLE validity period of 1 year and if their circumstances remain unchanged. That said, each application for LTVP is still considered on its own merits. The LLE does not constitute the approval of an LTVP as the PMLA only gives an indication of the non-resident’s eligibility for LTVP based on the information submitted for the PMLA by both parties.
In a small number of cases, the outcomes of the PMLA and LTVP applications may differ if the couple’s circumstances change between their PMLA and LTVP applications. Couples should ensure that the information submitted in the PMLA is correct, for a more accurate assessment of their eligibility for LTVP.
topics: Support for Marriages and Divorces / Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA)

questions.title: Are director’s fees claimable under the Government-Paid Leave Schemes?
questions.text: With effect from 1st January 2021, director’s fees will not be claimable under the Government-Paid Leave Schemes, as this is in line with the Child Development Co-Savings Act and Employment Act where director’s fees are not considered part of gross rate of pay.

questions.title: If I receive my gross rate of pay in a foreign currency, how does MSF calculate the reimbursement to my employer for the paid leave provided?
questions.text:
The gross rate of pay paid in foreign currency will be converted to Singapore Dollar (SGD) when the reimbursement to the employer is calculated.
The conversion will be based on the MAS exchange rate at the point when the salary was paid by the employer (i.e. payment date reflected in the payslip).
topics: Government-Paid Leave Schemes / Claims submission/ Entitlement

questions.title: Once I have started to draft my LPA, is there a deadline for the LPA to be submitted to OPG?
questions.text: You must submit your LPA to OPG for registration within 6 months from the date of creation of your LPA. This means that you must obtain your Donee’s consent to be appointed and have your LPA certified by a certificate issuer within this period. Your draft LPA will be removed from OPGO after 6 months from creation, and you will need to redraft your LPA.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Information on LPA

questions.title: Does a Donor still need to visit a Certificate Issuer in person?
questions.text: Yes, the Donor needs to visit a Certificate Issuer in-person to certify the LPA. In-person attendance before the Certificate Issuer remains a safeguard in ensuring that the Donor understands the purpose of the LPA and the scope of the authority conferred on Donee(s), there is no fraud or undue pressure used to induce the Donor to make the LPA, and there is nothing else that will prevent the LPA from being created.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Information on LPA

questions.title: Can a Donor still submit an LPA in hardcopy after the launch of OPGO?
questions.text:
All LPAs must be made and submitted via [OPGO]. Applicants may log in to OPGO via Singpass to do so.
Hardcopy LPAs certified after the system is launched on 14 Nov 2022 may be accepted under the following exceptional circumstances:
a. The Donor/Donee/Replacement Donee is unable to use OPGO due to his/her physical disability or other circumstances;
b. The online system is unavailable;
c. The Donor does not have an electronic device to receive messages via SMS to create and access his Singpass account/ National Digital Identity (NDI); or
d. The Donor/Donee/Replacement Donee is not eligible for a Singpass account/NDI
The list of circumstances can be found on the 2022 version of the hardcopy LPA form, found on [OPG website].
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Information on LPA

questions.title: As a professional Donee, how do I know if the Donor has lost mental capacity and what must I do thereafter?
questions.text: As a professional Donee, you must keep in regular contact with the Donor and be updated on his personal welfare and financial matters. In this way, you will know if the Donor has lost mental capacity. You will need to have a medical report stating that the Donor has lost mental capacity before you can exercise your powers under the LPA to make decisions on his behalf.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Professional Deputies and Donees

questions.title: How quickly will an application to the foreign Central Authority be processed?
questions.text: The time taken to process applications is dependent on the procedures of the Contracting State’s Central Authority. The Singapore Central Authority will liaise regularly with the relevant Contracting State’s Central Authority to ensure that the application has been received. The Singapore Central Authority may also request the Contracting State's Central Authority to keep the Singapore Central Authority updated on the progress of the application.
topics: MSF General Enquiry / Singapore Central Authority

questions.title: What is the cost of an outgoing application?
questions.text: Most Central Authorities in the foreign jurisdictions do not charge for any work that they do. However, some countries may require an applicant to pay all or part of the cost of legal representation. The applicant should also be prepared to pay costs such as travel expenses for his or her child's return and/or if the applicant is required to be present during the proceedings in the foreign country.
topics: MSF General Enquiry / Singapore Central Authority

questions.title: What can the Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds be used on?
questions.text:
The funds in the PSEA can be used by your child and their sibling(s) for post-secondary education at the locally based ITE, polytechnics and universities.
For more information on how to use the PSEA, you may wish to visit the MOE website.
topics: Baby Bonus (BB) / Annual Closure Exercise of Baby Bonus CDA on 12th Year

questions.title: Who is a Vulnerable Adult?
questions.text:
The Vulnerable Adults Act (VAA) defines a Vulnerable Adult (VA) as any individual who meets all of the following criteria:
a. Is 18 years of age or older; and
b. Has mental or physical infirmity, disability or incapacity; and, because of it,
c. Is unable to protect himself/herself from abuse, neglect or self-neglect.
You can find more information [here].
topics: Protection from domestic violence / Vulnerable Adult Abuse

questions.title: How can I update my passport information with ICA?
questions.text:
You may update your passport information with ICA by clicking on your residence status or pass type:
Permanent Residence
Long-Term Visit Pass
Student's Pass
For work pass or employment pass holders, please approach Ministry Of Manpower to update your passport information.

questions.title: How can I apply for or renew APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)?
questions.text: All APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC) applications must be submitted online at the e-Service. The card will be mailed by registered post to the applicant when it is ready.

questions.title: Do I submit the income information of taxable employees only?
questions.text: You are required to prepare and submit the employment income information for all employees listed here regardless of the income amount, and even if the employee’s income falls below the taxable income threshold of $22,000.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Employees to be Included in AIS Submission

questions.title: How do I apply for death extract without the date of death?
questions.text: You may apply for a search of the death record in the register by providing the period of search. You may refer to the ICA website for more information to apply for death extract and the relevant fees or charges for death extract.

questions.title: What is a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
An LPA is a legal document and a deed*, which allows a person who is at least 21 years of age ('Donor'), to voluntarily appoint one or more persons ('Donee(s)') to make decisions and act on his/her behalf if he/she loses mental capacity one day. A Donee can be appointed to act in the two broad areas of personal welfare and/or property & affairs matters. The LPA also gives the authority to the Donee to sign deeds on the Donor's behalf.
*Examples of deeds include:
An instrument used to appoint another individual to act on your behalf
An instrument used to transfer an interest in immovable property (in the case of an LPA, Donee(s) may be able to do so on behalf of the Donor if they are granted property & affairs powers as defined in the LPA)
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Information on LPA

questions.title: Can I still collect my passport at SingPost if I missed my appointment?
questions.text: You may still collect your passport at the same SingPost outlet, up to 3 days after your appointment date. Alternatively, please make another appointment to collect your passport 1 week after the missed appointment. For example, if your appointment is on a Monday, you will have up to Thursday to collect your passport at the same location. You can only book another appointment to collect your passport after the following Monday.

questions.title: Can I travel if my passport is valid for less than 6 months?
questions.text: Generally, a passport is only acceptable for travel if it has a validity period of at least 6 months.

questions.title: Can I travel with my current passport while my new passport application is still being processed?
questions.text: You may travel using your current passport if it has a validity period of at least 6 months and is not damaged. The current passport will be invalidated only upon issuance of the new passport.

questions.title: During the passport application, I had selected Singapore as my collection centre. How do I change the collection venue to an overseas mission subsequently?
questions.text: Please contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: How can I apply for a new passport?
questions.text:
Please apply for a Singapore passport for yourself (or your child) via our e-Service. You will be notified of the outcome by email.
You may refer to ICA website on apply for passport for more information.

questions.title: How do I check the status of my passport application or retrieve the application reference number?
questions.text: You can check the status of your online passport application or retrieve your application reference number at MyICA. Once logged in, please refer to the 'Applications' section, which displays your current application(s) and status, including the reference number.

questions.title: I am currently overseas and require a new passport. How should I apply for it?
questions.text:
Please submit your Singapore passport application online at the ICA e-Service and select the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission closest to you for the collection venue.
Alternatively, please proceed to the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission to apply in person.

questions.title: I have booked an appointment to collect my passport. Can I change my existing appointment?
questions.text: You may make changes at least 3 working days before your existing appointment. Log in to ICA e-Service to change your existing appointment.

questions.title: My child's passport can only be collected at ICA whereas I can only make an appointment to collect my passport at SingPost. Can I arrange to collect both passports at ICA?
questions.text: 'Group appointments' can only be made for passport collection with the same eligibility. You will need to make appointments separately for the collection.

questions.title: Should I update the photo in the current passport if my/ my child's facial appearance has changed?
questions.text: Regardless of age, you should apply for a new passport with an updated photo if your facial appearance has changed significantly. This will help to facilitate immigration clearance and avoid any misunderstanding over the identity of the passport holder at any checkpoint. The prevailing application fee for a new passport applies.

questions.title: What are the documents required for passport collection?
questions.text:
Please bring along the following documents:
For yourself –
• Physical or digital IC
• Current passport (if valid at the point of application)
For your child (aged below 16 at the point of application) –
• Child's original or digital birth certificate
• Physical or digital IC of the parent who consented to the child's passport application
• Child's current passport (if valid at the point of application)
If the consenting parent is unable to accompany the child for the collection, another person may do so on his/ her behalf with the following additional documents (for collection at ICA Services Centre only):
• Signed authorisation letter by consenting parent, which includes names and IC numbers of both parties as well as name and birth certification number of child
• IC of the authorised person

questions.title: What should I do if I need to travel urgently but I do not have a valid passport?
questions.text:
Singapore citizens who require your passport urgently may approach our service ambassadors at Level 1, ICA Services Centre during our operating hours. Please bring along the following documents:
For yourself –
• Physical or digital IC
• Current passport (if valid at the point of passport application)
• Evidence of urgent travel need (hotel reservations, flight tickets, travel itinerary etc)
• Recent passport-sized photo (taken within 3 months).
For your child (aged below 16) –
• Child's original or digital birth certificate
• Physical or digital IC of the parent who consented to the child's passport application
• Child's current passport (if valid at the point of passport application)
• Evidence of urgent travel need (hotel reservations, flight tickets, travel itinerary etc)
• Recent passport-sized photo (taken within 3 months)
Your request will be assessed accordingly by ICA and the waiting time is expected to be 3 hours or longer.

questions.title: What should I do if my passport is damaged?
questions.text:
Please report to ICA immediately via our e-Service for damaged passport.
If you are overseas, you may visit the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission with the damaged passport to make a damage report.

questions.title: How can I generate a QR code for immigration clearance at land checkpoints?
questions.text:
Travellers can create a profile and generate a QR code through the MyICA mobile app, using Singpass or passport information.
Once the profile is created and QR code is generated, this QR code is valid for multiple trips. Please refer to the video guides for:
car
motorcycle
bus
on how to generate the QR Code from MyICA mobile app.
topics: QR Code Clearance / Before your trip

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of profiles in a group QR code?
questions.text:
For travellers who selected "Car" as the vehicle type, the group QR code will allow up to 10 profiles.
For travellers who selected "Motorcycle" as the vehicle type, the group QR code will allow up to 2 profiles.
For travellers who selected "Lorry" or “Bus” as the vehicle type, the group QR code will allow up to 4 profiles.
Travellers are free to create and customise multiple groups of QR codes, depending on their travel needs.
topics: QR Code Clearance / Before your trip

questions.title: What happens if I submit wrong information for myself or my travel companion(s) during profile creation and have generated the QR code?
questions.text:
It is crucial for travellers to verify and confirm the accuracy of the details included in the QR code. Failure to do so may lead to inconvenience when they undergo immigration clearance at Singapore Land checkpoints.
If you need to correct any inaccuracies in the information you have provided, you may edit the details through navigating to the 'edit' option under your profile.
topics: QR Code Clearance / Before your trip

questions.title: When should I create my QR code?
questions.text: For a smooth journey, travellers are advised to generate their individual or group QR code before their arrival at Singapore land checkpoints.
topics: QR Code Clearance / Before your trip

questions.title: Can I access and view all group QR code(s) that contain my profile via MyICA mobile app on my personal device?
questions.text:
You can access the group QR code(s) which you have created via MyICA mobile app on your personal device by navigating to the "Group QR code" listing.
If you had previously shared your passport details and were added into a group QR code generated by your travel companion, the group QR code will only be visible via MyICA mobile app on the personal device of your travel companion.
For privacy, the essential data of other travellers in the group QR code such as NRIC/FIN, Malaysian ID number, and passport number, will be masked.
topics: QR Code Clearance / Before your trip

questions.title: Do I still need to bring my passport when I travel to Malaysia given that I can use QR code for immigration clearance now?
questions.text:
The QR code can only be used for immigration clearance at Singapore land checkpoints via car, motorcycle, lorry and bus.
Travellers are reminded to bring their passports when travelling overseas, as it remains the official travel document for identification during overseas travel.

questions.title: Can I approach ICA to view, delete or edit my profile information on another individual's MyICA mobile app?
questions.text:
You can arrange with the individual(s) who had previously created your profile via MyICA mobile app on his/ her mobile device to edit or delete your profile information.
ICA does not have access to any individual's MyICA mobile app to view, delete or edit a profile.

questions.title: Can I use the same group QR code for immigration clearance if not all travellers included in the group QR code are travelling?
questions.text:
You cannot use the group QR code for immigration clearance if not all travellers included in the group QR code are travelling.
It is important that all travellers, who had their profiles in the group QR code, travel together in the same vehicle when using the group QR code for immigration clearance.
To ensure a seamless and smooth travel experience, please generate a new group QR code that includes only the profiles of travellers who are travelling in the same vehicle for the trip.
Tip: You can create different group QR codes for different group travels and named the groups for differentiation (e.g. Family, Friends, and Colleagues).

questions.title: Is the QR code secure?
questions.text:
The QR code generated from the MyICA mobile app is designed with security measures to protect personal information and prevent unauthorised access. It is encrypted to safeguard personal data, which can only be retrieved and decrypted by authorised ICA systems.
For added privacy, once a profile is created, the essential data of other travellers in the group QR code such as NRIC/ FIN, Malaysian ID number and passport number, will be masked.
If travellers have concerns about sharing their personal details, they can self-scan their individual QR code or present their passport for immigration clearance.

questions.title: What are the benefits in using the QR code for immigration clearance at Singapore land checkpoints?
questions.text:
The QR code clearance streamlines the immigration clearance process and reduces the overall waiting time for both individual and group travellers who are travelling by car, motorcycle, lorry, or bus.
It is also convenient as the created profile(s) and generated QR code can be saved for future trips. Travellers need not re-enter their details for subsequent trips, unless there are changes to their passport details (e.g., Passport Number, Date of Expiry) or the travel group.

questions.title: What happens if I do not download MyICA mobile app and/or are unable to generate the QR code?
questions.text:
If you have not downloaded the MyICA mobile app and/or are unable to generate the QR code, you can still present your passport at the immigration lanes.
We highly recommend all travellers to download the MyICA mobile app and use the QR code for faster and more convenient immigration clearance.

questions.title: What should I do if my generated QR code(s) in MyICA mobile app is expiring?
questions.text:
If the passport(s) of your saved profile(s) tagged to the QR code remain valid, the QR code validity will be automatically extended when you generate the QR code via the MyICA mobile app.
If the passport(s) of your saved profile(s) tagged to the QR code have expired or is expiring, you may update the profile(s) with the new passport number and new passport expiry date in MyICA mobile app before generating a new QR code.

questions.title: Can I view the profile information of other profiles via the MyICA mobile app on my personal device?
questions.text:
You can view the profile information of other travellers, such as their full name, date of birth, nationality and date of passport expiry, if the profiles were created via the MyICA mobile app using your personal device.
It is necessary to display these information so that the correct profile can be easily identified for editing and/or for selection to generate the group QR code.

questions.title: Which mobile app can I use to generate the QR code for immigration clearance?
questions.text: The QR code is generated via the MyICA mobile app, which can be downloaded for free from both App Store (iOS) and Google Play (Android).

questions.title: Who is eligible to use the QR code for immigration clearance?
questions.text:
All travellers (Singapore citizens, Permanent Residents, Long-Term Pass Holders, and foreign visitors), regardless of age, with the exception of first-time foreign visitors and those re-entering Singapore using a different passport from their last visit to Singapore, can enjoy passport-less clearance by presenting QR code generated via the MyICA mobile app, at Singapore land checkpoints via car, motorcycle, lorry and bus.
Travellers using passports that have not been used for entry into Singapore before, will have to present their passports for immigration clearance. Thereafter, travellers will be eligible to use the QR code for immigration clearance in their subsequent trips.
To use the QR code at the automated immigration lanes, travellers need to ensure that their biometrics identifiers have been enrolled with ICA or MOM. Please refer to ICA website for more information.

questions.title: Why is QR code introduced for immigration clearance?
questions.text:
Travellers arriving and departing via Singapore land checkpoints by car, motorcycle, lorry or bus can use QR codes in lieu of passports for faster and more convenient immigration clearance.
Instead of using passports at the immigration lanes, travellers will only need to scan the QR code, which they have generated via the MyICA mobile app prior to arriving at the checkpoint, for immigration clearance.

questions.title: Will the passport images of other travelling companions be saved in the MyICA mobile app or mobile device which was used to generate the group QR code?
questions.text: The "Scan Passport" function from the MyICA mobile app will only use Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to capture the relevant information from the Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ) of the passport. Images of the passport biodata page will not be saved in the MyICA mobile app or personal mobile device during this process.

questions.title: Can I update the members in the group QR code for different trips?
questions.text: The MyICA mobile app can store multiple group QR codes with different group members. You can edit the members in a group by adding or removing the member's profile and regenerating the QR code even in offline mode (i.e. without mobile data). You also have the option to customise group names (e.g., 'Family', or 'Friends') to fit your travel requirements.

questions.title: If someone scans a QR code that does not bear his/ her particulars, will he/ she be allowed to enter or exit Singapore?
questions.text: While QR code clearance brings convenience and reduces travelling time for travellers in vehicles, security is not compromised as ICA will still perform the necessary checks, including biometric verification after the QR code is scanned.

questions.title: What happens if I do not have mobile data to access the QR Code in the MyICA mobile app?
questions.text:
The QR code generation works in offline mode.
You can still create and retrieve the QR code for self-scanning at the immigration counters, even if you do not have mobile data.
For a smooth journey, you are advised to generate your individual or group QR code before your arrival at Singapore land checkpoints.

questions.title: Can I submit the SG Arrival Card for multiple trips under 'Group Submission'?
questions.text: The 'Group Submission' is meant for a group of persons who are travelling to Singapore together for one trip.
topics: SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass)
SG Arrival Card (SGAC) and Electronic Visit Pass (e-Pass) / General

questions.title: Must I submit Form V39A (Letter of Introduction/ LOI) if my company issues a letter with similar content?
questions.text: Your local contact can submit a letter of support issued by his/ her company in lieu of Form V39A (Letter of Introduction/ LOI) on the condition that all necessary information (such as the local contact’s NRIC details) are included as per V39A. Your local contact must be a Singapore citizen or permanent resident aged 21 years and above.

questions.title: What is ‘MyTransaction’ in MyICA? How can I access 'MyTransaction'?
questions.text: 'MyTransaction' is available from the 'MyICA' dropdown list at the top right corner of the window after users log in to MyICA using their Singpass. 'MyTransaction' in MyICA allows you to view information on immigration facilities requested or sponsored by you. This includes:

questions.title: How can I obtain more information on ICA products and services?
questions.text: You can refer to the ICA Website and ICA FAQs for more information on ICA products and services.

questions.title: How do I make changes (e.g. changes to appointed Donee) to my registered LPA?
questions.text:
To make changes to your appointed Donee (including adding, removing or changing a Donee) for a registered LPA, you will need to revoke your existing LPA and make a new one.
Before revoking your LPA, you must inform all your Donees in writing about your decision. You can notify them either by:
delivering a written notice in person
post
email
To revoke your existing LPA, log in to Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) using your Singpass, to submit your notice of revocation.
Select Revoke LPA under your registered LPA.
Review and acknowledge the information provided.
Complete the required declarations.
Make payment.
Submit your notice of revocation.
If you are unable to access OPGO, submit your completed hardcopy revocation form to the Office of the Public Guardian by post, or via FormSG at https://go.gov.sg/opg-enquiry.
The Public Guardian may require you to provide further information or documents before revoking your registered LPA.
You may start drafting a new LPA while waiting for the cancellation of your existing LPA. However, the new LPA will only be accepted by OPG for registration after your existing LPA is cancelled. (adhered to copy in link)
Before submitting your new LPA for registration, you will need to have it certified by a Certificate Issuer.

questions.title: If the licensees had any contraventions with any healthcare financing schemes, what are the enforcement actions under the HCSA that can be imposed on the licensees to protect patient safety and welfare ?
questions.text:
Any contravention of healthcare financing schemes established by written law (e.g., MediShield Life Scheme Act) can be taken into account by MOH at licence renewal or if errant management decided to apply for a new licence.
In addition, regulatory action may be taken against the licensee if public interest so requires.
The regulatory actions range from censuring the licensee in writing, to paying a financial penalty (a sum of not more than $10,000 for each contravention).

questions.title: The majority of the offences in the HCSA are offences of strict liability. Does this mean that licensees would automatically be guilty of an offence, even though the breach or non-compliance with the law could be completely unintentional or merely technical?
questions.text: Investigations will be carried out when licensees breach the requirements in HCSA, including determining if reasonable care has been exercised by licensees before any enforcement action is meted out.

questions.title: As a patient, is there a list of non-compliant service providers that I can refer to when considering a medical procedure/service?
questions.text:
For the purposes of public interest, we will be publishing information on licensees who have had their licence suspended or revoked.
Information will be available on the MOH web

questions.title: How will MOH know when these service providers are not complying with new regulatory standards?
questions.text:
MOH will conduct inspections and audits on service providers to check on their compliance to these standards during licence renewal and on an ad-hoc basis.
Frequency of such inspections will be determined using a risk-based approach, depending on the nature of the service and the provider’s compliance record.
MOH will also conduct investigations on whether a licensee is compliant with HCSA requirements if there are complaints received.

questions.title: Now that the framework has shifted to service-based licensing, how would inspections be carried out moving forward? Will inspections for various services provided within the same premises be conducted separately at separate times?
questions.text: Inspection processes will be streamlined to reduce administrative burden on licensees.

questions.title: How does a Code of Practice differ from guidance if both do not have regulatory teeth?
questions.text:
The licensee must comply with any Code of Practice as stated under section 38.
Any contravention or failure to comply with the Code of Practice can result in regulatory action being taken against a licensee.
Non-compliance with any Code of Practice issued will be taken into account at licence renewal or licence application.

questions.title: As an authorised officer can enter the premises at any time, will the power of entry/inspection or search affect patient management?
questions.text:
MOH will exercise its inspection and enforcement powers judiciously and in a manner that is least disruptive to the care of patients.
It is important for MOH to investigate and stop continuing offences which may result in serious patient harm.

questions.title: How will MOH decide when to bring a criminal charge or regulatory action?
questions.text:
MOH will look into all relevant facts of a case and the applicable provision(s) to determine the most appropriate course of action to take against an errant licensee.
MOH will also consider the governance structure of the licensee and investigate the lines of accountability to key personnel such as the licensee, governing body, the Principal Officer and the Clinical Governance Officer, where relevant.

questions.title: Under the new healthcare regulatory framework, what are the penalties for unlicensed healthcare service providers?
questions.text: The penalties include criminal sanctions such as jail terms and/or a fine.

questions.title: If members of the public have any further queries on Section 31A or B of the HCSA, who can they write to?
questions.text: If members of the public have any further queries, they may write in to HCSA_Enquiries@moh.gov.sg.

questions.title: Is advertising of educational talks/ workshops/ lectures on psychological interventions for mental conditions to members of the public considered as a healthcare advertisement? If yes, are these advertisements subject to the requirements under Section 31A and B of the HCSA?
questions.text:
Yes, advertising of educational talks/ workshops/ lectures on psychological interventions for mental conditions to members of public by HCSA licensees and non-HCSA licensees is considered as healthcare advertisement.
As such, these advertisements would need to adhere to the requirements under Section 31A and B of the HCSA.
However, if the educational talks/ workshops/ lectures and the publication of related information are restricted to only medical professionals (and not members of public), it is not considered a healthcare advertisement. As such, the requirements under Section 31A and B of the HCSA would not apply. For example, a workshop on psychological interventions conducted for medical professionals by IMH.

questions.title: Do the requirements under Section 31B of the HCSA apply to all clinical psychologists who wish to use the protected title, “Dr” in advertisements regardless of whether they practise at licensed (e.g., IMH and SGH) or non-licensed healthcare service providers (e.g. private psychological service providers/ clinics)?
questions.text:
Yes, the requirements under Section 31B of the HCSA apply to all clinical psychologists who wish to use the protected title, “Dr” in advertisements regardless of whether they practice at licensed (e.g., IMH and SGH) or nonlicensed healthcare service providers (e.g., private psychological service providers).
This is because a clinical psychologist is not a “specified person” (i.e. not a registered healthcare professional) as defined under Section 31B of the HCSA.

questions.title: Should clinical psychologists become registered healthcare professionals in future (i.e., they are included under Second Schedule of the AHPA), would they still need to comply with Section 31A and B of the HCSA?
questions.text:
Should clinical psychologists become registered healthcare professionals in future (i.e., they are included under Second Schedule of the AHPA), they would be regulated by the Allied Health Professions Council and would need to adhere to their Code of Conduct.
The requirements under Section 31B of the HCSA – “Restrictions on use of protected title” would no longer apply to them.
However, advertisements by private psychology service provider would still need to adhere to the requirements under Section 31A of the HCSA as their services are not licensed under HCSA.

questions.title: What is the difference between ‘healthcare service providers’ and ‘healthcare professionals’? Please elaborate
questions.text:
Healthcare service providers are business entities that provide healthcare services, while healthcare professionals are healthcare-trained persons who are employed or engaged by healthcare service providers to deliver healthcare services.
Under HCSA, healthcare service can be classified into:
Licensable healthcare services (e.g., acute hospital service, outpatient medical/ dental service and radiological service); and
Non-licensable healthcare service (e.g., chiropractic service, TCM service, private psychological service and private physiotherapy service).
To provide a licensable healthcare service, a healthcare service provider must be granted the relevant service license under HCSA. To provide a non-licensable healthcare service, a HCSA licence is not required.
Healthcare professionals can be classified into:
Registered healthcare professionals (e.g., Medical Practitioners, Nurses, Physiotherapists, Radiographers and Speech Therapists who are required to be registered under the respective legislative acts that govern them and hold valid practising certificates (PCs) before they can practise); and
Non-registered healthcare professionals (e.g., clinical psychologists, podiatrists, chiropractors and ayurvedic medicine practitioners). Nonregistered healthcare professionals are self-regulated. As such, they need not be registered and does not need to hold valid PCs in order to practise.
Licensed healthcare service providers usually employ both registered and nonregistered healthcare professionals to deliver its services. For example, an acute hospital service provider may employ medical practitioners (registered under Medical Registration Act 1997), nurses (registered under Nurses and Midwives Act 1999), physiotherapists (registered under Second Schedule of the Allied Health Practitioners Act 2011 (AHPA)), clinical psychologists (currently self-regulated and not listed under Second Schedule of AHPA), audiologists (currently self-regulated and not listed under Second Schedule of AHPA), etc.
Non-licensed healthcare service providers (e.g., private physiotherapy/ speech therapy/ psychology/ audiology service providers; and chiropractic/ osteopathic/ ayurvedic medicine service provider) may or may not employ registered healthcare professionals to deliver its services.

questions.title: What are the enforcement actions that can be taken against a person who contravene Section 31A or B of the HCSA?
questions.text:
Depending on the facts and circumstances of the case, a person who contravenes Section 31A or B of the HCSA may be:
a) issued a stern / conditional warning;
b) issued a composition of up to $10,000; or
c) prosecuted in Court.
If the person is prosecuted in Court, he/ she shall be liable on conviction to a fine of up to $20,000 and/ or to imprisonment for a term of up to 12 months. In the case of a continuing offence, to a further fine of up to $1,000 for every day or part of a day during which the offence continues after conviction.

questions.title: Are non-registered healthcare professionals who wish to use the title “Dr” on their business cards required to state their doctorate / PhD qualifications and include the relevant disclaimers?
questions.text:
If the business cards are used to promote a healthcare service, these business cards would be considered as healthcare service advertising, and the requirements under the advertising controls must then be complied with (e.g., on mandatory disclosure of qualifications).
For example, if the business card set out the healthcare services that a nonregistered healthcare professional provides e.g. osteopath services, it would be considered as an advertisement of a healthcare service. Hence, the following requirements apply:
state the educational qualifications whenever the title “Dr” is used; and
include a disclaimer that the educational qualification is not a medical or dental qualification
However, if the information in the business cards is unrelated to healthcare services, the requirements of mandatory disclosure of qualifications and disclaimer would not apply.
For example, if the business card contained information such as the name of the business entity, its address and website, the name of the non-registered healthcare professional, qualifications, email address and associations of which the non-registered healthcare professional is a member, it would not be an advertisement of a healthcare service and is not subject to the requirements set out above.

questions.title: Can overseas-trained or retired doctors and dentists who are not registered in Singapore use the title “Dr” in healthcare service advertising?
questions.text:
Overseas-trained or retired doctors/dentists who are not registered in Singapore and do not hold a valid practising certificate, must comply with the following when using the title “Dr” in their healthcare service advertising:
state their qualifications, and
include a disclaimer that he/ she is not holding a valid practising certificate issued by the relevant local healthcare professional board.
Examples as follows:
Example 1: Overseas-trained dentist who is not registered with SDC: Dr ABC, BDS (NUS, Singapore), does not hold a valid practising certificate under the Dental Registration Act 1999
Example 2: Registered retired doctor in Singapore with no valid practising certificate Dr XYZ, MBBS (Singapore), does not hold a valid practising certificate under the Medical Registration Act 1997
This advertising control would apply when any of these doctors/dentists are featured in advertisements of healthcare services

questions.title: Which group of healthcare professionals are allowed to use the title “Dr” in healthcare service advertising without needing to specify their qualifications?
questions.text:
Only registered healthcare professionals who hold a valid practising certificate are allowed to use the title “Dr” in healthcare service advertising without needing to specify their qualifications or including a disclaimer that their qualification is not a medical or dental qualification.
Registered healthcare professionals include:
an allied health professional who is registered under the Allied Health Professions Act
a dentist or an oral health therapist who is registered under the Dental Registration Act
a medical practitioner who is registered under the Medical Registration Act
a nurse or midwife who is registered, or an enrolled nurse who is enrolled, under the Nurses and Midwives Act
an optometrist or optician who is registered under the Optometrists and Opticians Act
a pharmacist who is registered under the Pharmacists Registration Act o a traditional Chinese medicine practitioner who is registered under the Traditional Chinese Medicine Practitioners Act.
Healthcare professionals who do not come under the above list, including chiropractors or osteopaths, are required to state their qualifications and a disclaimer that their educational qualification is not a medical or dental qualification, when using the title “Dr” in healthcare service advertising.
