If your application is approved, an ABTC will be issued 4 months after the date of your application. If this ABTC does not have all foreign APEC economies’ approvals, we will issue the final card to you 9 months after your application, excluding any pending approvals.
Please note that foreign APEC economies are unlikely to process your application beyond the 9-month mark.

questions.title: Does ICA legalise or authenticate birth or death certificates?
questions.text: ICA does not provide document legalisation and authentication services. For the legalisation or authentication of documents, you may wish to approach the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL). For details on the processes and procedures, please visit https://legalisation.sal.sg.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Verification of Digital Certificate

questions.title: Will I still be able to use my Active Wallet?
questions.text:
As we have discontinued the Active Wallet feature, you will no longer be able to make Active Wallet purchases at participating merchants or earn ActiveSG credits with MyCash spend.
ActiveSG credits from the old ActiveSG app have been migrated to MyActiveSG+ and can be used at https://activesg.gov.sg. Any unused MyCash should have been refunded to your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account by 31 August 2024.

questions.title: Can I change my address at a neighbourhood police post/centre or at ICA Services Centre?
questions.text:
This service is no longer available at the police posts and ICA Services Centre. Please visit ICA e-service to change your address.
If you encounter any technical issues for change of address online, please contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: Can I defer the collection of my IC?
questions.text: ICs which are not collected within 3 months of the collection notification are destroyed. After the IC is destroyed, and you will be required to replace the IC and a replacement fee of $60 applies.

questions.title: Can I register/ replace my IC when I am residing overseas?
questions.text:
Please only register/replace your IC if you are planning to return to Singapore within the next 6 months as you will need to collect your IC in person.
However, if you have lost your IC, you must report the loss via our e-Service using your SingPass immediately to prevent any misuse. You may submit your application to replace your IC when you next return to Singapore.

questions.title: Can I still collect my IC at SingPost if I missed my appointment?
questions.text:
You may still collect your IC at the same SingPost outlet, up to 3 days after your appointment date. Alternatively, please make another appointment to collect your IC 1 week after the missed appointment.
For example, if your appointment is on a Monday, you will have up to Thursday to collect your IC at the same location. You can only book another appointment to collect your IC after the following Monday.

questions.title: How do I replace a lost IC?
questions.text: You must report the loss via our e-Service immediately to prevent any misuse and apply for a replacement within 14 days from the report. If you are currently overseas, you may replace your IC on your next return to Singapore.

questions.title: How do I report a potential misuse of my address?
questions.text: You can submit a report on the misuse of your address.

questions.title: I am unable to book an appointment for the biometrics registration for my 15-year-old child. What should I do?
questions.text: IC registrants who have passed their 16th birthday will no longer be able to make an appointment for the biometrics enrolment. They are required to report in-person at ICA Services Centre. Please expect a waiting time of at least two (2) hours.

questions.title: I have booked an appointment to collect my IC. Can I change my existing appointment?
questions.text: You may make changes at least 3 working days before your existing appointment. Please go to ICA e-Service to change your existing appointment.

questions.title: What can I expect after I submit the application for IC registration for my 15 year-old child?
questions.text:
Your child will be required to complete his/ her biometrics enrolment.
If your child attends a government or government-aided school, biometrics enrolment will be done at schools on a designated day.
If your child does not attend a government or government-aided school, or had missed their school biometrics registration day, please make an appointment for biometrics enrolment via ICA e-Service at the ICA Services Centre after the IC application is submitted (Select “Passport & NRIC" > "IC Registration – Biometrics Enrolment").

questions.title: What are the documents required for IC collection?
questions.text: You must bring along your current physical IC for verification and invalidation unless you are collecting a replacement for a lost IC.

questions.title: What is the expected processing time for an IC application?
questions.text: The expected processing time for IC application is 7 working days. If you also applied for a passport within the same application, the combined processing time for both documents is 3 weeks.

questions.title: What should I do if I am unable to verify my address PIN on the e-Service?
questions.text: You can submit an enquiry for assistance. Please attach an image of your PIN mailer for us to better assist you.

questions.title: What should I do if I have not received my PIN mailer or address sticker?
questions.text: If you have not received your PIN or address sticker after 7 days (for local addresses), please request another PIN or sticker via the e-service under 'Enquire Application Status'. After you request a new PIN, the original PIN will no longer be valid. For overseas addresses, the delivery time may be longer.

questions.title: When do I need to report a change of address on my IC?
questions.text:
IC holders are required to report a change of address within 28 days of moving to the new address.
If you encounter any technical issues for change of address online, please contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: Why is my clinic no longer a Healthier SG Clinic?
questions.text:
This could be due to various reasons, such as, your clinic has ceased operations, changed ownership, or is no longer participating in the Healthier SG scheme. This means that you will not be able to enjoy Healthier SG benefits at this clinic anymore.
You are encouraged to continue your Healthier SG journey by enrolling to a new preferred Healthier SG clinic via HealthHub. If you need assistance with enrolment, you may approach a nearby Healthier SG Enrolment Station, a participating clinic at https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg. For further queries you may also contact the MOH Hotline at 6325 9220.

questions.title: How do I know that the death has been registered if I do not need to register the death? How do I obtain a death certificate?
questions.text:
After the doctor certifies the death online, you can visit the My Legacy website to download the digital death certificate.
To access and download the digital death certificate, you will require the following information from the certifying doctor or hospital:
• Death certificate number (or Confirmation of Death document number)
• Deceased’s Identification Document number
• Deceased’s date of death
You may refer to ICA's website for more information.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Death Registration Process

questions.title: Are Student's Pass applicants eligible to make an appointment?
questions.text:
You are eligible to make an appointment at ICA e-Service if your Student's Pass (STP) application has been approved-in-principle.
To book an appointment, you will need to have the FIN no. and e-Appointment ID stated in your IPA letter. Your e-Appointment ID is the last 3 digits of the Application ID, which can be found on top left-hand corner on Page 1 of the IPA letter. Please refer to the diagram below. questions.title: Will all flats for sale be listed on the portal?
questions.text:
During the application period of a Build-To-Order (BTO) or Sale of Balance Flats exercise, or when there is an open booking of flats, all flats on offer will be displayed on the portal. After the application period has ended, only those who have applied for the flats can view the relevant information.
In addition, information on the BTO flat supply in the next launch is available on the portal.
Find out more about HDB’s different modes of sale and subscribe to HDB e-Alerts service to be notified of a launch.
topics: Flat Listing / Buy a flat from HDB

questions.title: How can I buy a flat listed on the portal?
questions.text: All home buyers must first obtain an HFE letter. With a valid HFE letter, you can then apply for a flat online via the HDB Flat Portal during the application period of the sales launch. Subscribe to HDB e-Alerts service to be notified of a launch.
topics: Flat Listing / Buy a flat from HDB

questions.title: How does the loan listing service help flat buyers?
questions.text: The loan listing service facilitates buyers in comparing the housing loans offered by the financial institutions (FIs) and HDB, and to understand the different terms for taking up a housing loan from the FIs and HDB.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Housing loan options

questions.title: Why are there different terms, e.g. loan-to-value limit, cash payment condition, maximum loan amount, etc. in taking up a housing loan from the financial institutions and HDB?
questions.text: FIs, which are commercial entities, provide housing loans in accordance to conditions and guidelines stipulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. On the other hand, HDB, as the public housing authority, provides housing loans to help Singaporeans, including those with lower incomes, buy their own home. Given the different nature of FIs and the HDB, it is understandable why housing loans from the FIs and HDB have different financing terms.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Housing loan options

questions.title: Why is there a need for 3 different calculators in the portal?
questions.text:
The calculators serve different purposes for home seekers and flat sellers.
Home seekers may:
Calculate their housing budget before embarking on house hunting.
Create a payment plan to work out the finances required to buy a particular flat. If cash payment is required, this will be highlighted.
Flat sellers may calculate the sale proceeds from the sale of their flat.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Financial calculators

questions.title: Do I need to have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter to use the financial calculators?
questions.text:
If you do not have a valid HFE letter, you can still use the financial calculators to work out your budget by keying in on your own the estimated CPF housing grants. You can still receive housing loan estimates from HDB and the participating FIs.
However, having an HFE letter will provide more certainty in your use of the financial calculators. You can then login to the HDB Flat Portal using Singpass. Upon logging in, the details of your eligibility for new and resale flat purchase, CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan in your HFE letter will be automatically populated into the financial calculators, to help you work out your budget and finances.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Financial calculators

questions.title: How is the estimated housing loan amount from the FIs derived?
questions.text: With your consent, the details which you have provided to the calculator are sent to our partner FI, which computes the loan amount for our display at the calculator.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Financial calculators

questions.title: How is the estimated housing loan amount from the financial institutions derived?
questions.text: With your consent, your details which you have provided to the calculator are sent to our partner FI which computes the loan amount for our display at the calculator.
topics: Loan Listing And Financial Calculators / Financial calculators

questions.title: What is My Flat Dashboard?
Do I need Singpass to login to My Flat Dashboard?
questions.text:
Yes. You will need to have a Singpass to login to My Flat Dashboard.
If you do not have a Singpass or need to reset your password, please apply via Singpass online request service.

questions.title: Where do I find more information on the use of My Flat Dashboard?
questions.text: Please click on Get Help for more information.

questions.title: What is the HFE letter?
questions.text:
The HFE letter provides flat buyers with a holistic understanding of their housing and financing options and help them plan their budget before they embark on their home buying journey. It informs flat buyers upfront of their eligibility to purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amounts of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan they are eligible for. Second-timers will also be informed on the resale levy/ premium payable for the purchase of another subsidised flat from HDB.
You must have a valid HFE letter when you apply to buy a flat from HDB. To buy a resale flat on the open market, you must have a valid HFE letter before you obtain an Option to Purchase (OTP) from a flat seller, and when you submit your resale application to HDB.
Find out more about the details of the HFE letter.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

questions.title: Where do I find more information on how to apply for an HFE letter?
questions.text: Please click on Get Help for more information.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

questions.title: How do I apply for a flat from HDB?
questions.text:
All home buyers must first obtain an HFE letter, which will be valid for 9 months from the date of issue. With a valid HFE letter, you can then apply for a flat online at the HDB Flat Portal during the application period of a Build-To-Order (BTO) or Sales of Balance Flats (SBF) exercise, or open booking of flats. An administrative fee of $10 per application is payable by credit card (MasterCard/Visa) or scanning the QR code using any supporting mobile payment apps.
Find out more about the buying procedures for new flats on the HDB InfoWEB.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / New flat application

questions.title: Where can I view the status of my new flat application?
questions.text: The HDB Flat Portal provides a step-by-step guide on your flat buying journey. Please login to the HDB Flat Portal > My Flat Dashboard to view the status of your flat application and follow the steps for your flat buying journey.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / New flat application

questions.title: Where do I find more information on buying a new flat from HDB through the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: Please click on Get Help for more information.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / New flat application

questions.title: Where can I view the status of my resale application?
questions.text: The HDB Flat Portal provides a step-by-step guide on your flat transaction journey. Please log in to the My Flat Dashboard to view the status of your resale application and complete the steps of your journey.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / Resale flat application

questions.title: What is a complete resale application?
questions.text:
A resale application is complete when HDB receives a resale application form from both the flat sellers and buyers.
Flat sellers and buyers must submit their respective portion of the resale application, together with the necessary documents, within 7 calendar days of each other. Otherwise, incomplete application will lapse and there will be no refund for the administrative fee paid. Both parties will then have to restart the application process.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / Resale flat application

questions.title: Where do I find more information on buying and selling an HDB resale flat?
questions.text: You can find more information on the procedures of buying and selling resale flats on the HDB InfoWEB.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / Resale flat application

questions.title: Where can I find more information on resale application submission through the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: Please click on Get Help for more information.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / Resale flat application

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have problems in using the portal?
questions.text: For feedback or enquiries, you can write to us.

questions.title: I want an immediate booking slot but the earliest is only x days away. - e2i/CMPs [Applicable for both scenarios: (i) Individual had already self-booked appointment and want to reschedule to earlier date, or (ii) Individual has not booked any appointment yet]
questions.text: Appointment booking system will show all the available slots. The first slot you see is the earliest available slot for the selected location/mode.

questions.title: What do I need to bring for ticket collection?
questions.text:
Successful applicants must present
(1) the unique QR code included in their notification email; and
(2) the applicant's physical/digital NRIC to redeem their tickets. Please note that the QR code is valid for one-time use only and should not be shared with others to avoid any issues during the redemption process.

questions.title: What do I have to bring for the personnel checks before entry into the Padang?
questions.text: Do bring your physical tickets for entry and avoid carrying bulky items such as large bags and large umbrellas. This will help expedite security checks and ensure a smooth entry for all attendees. Please refer to the NDP website (https://www.ndp.gov.sg)’s Admissions Advisory under Resources.

questions.title: Which are the five locations of the Heartland Celebration sites?
questions.text:
There will be five main Heartland Celebration sites island-wide and the celebrations at these sites will begin at 4.00pm.
Central Singapore District: Open field beside Bishan Junction 8
North East District: Open Field next to One Punggol
North West District: Open field next to FutsalArena @ Yishun
South East District: Open field beside Wisma Geylang Serai
South West District: Bukit Gombak ActiveSG Stadium

questions.title: The Copyright (Collective Management Organisations) Regulations 2023 were published on 31 October 2023. When do these regulations take effect?
questions.text: The regulations take effect on 1 May 2024.

questions.title: Who are considered as immediate family members under the Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA)?
questions.text: Immediate family members are the child’s grandparents, or any other siblings below 21 years old who meet the following criteria: (1) Live at the same address as the applicant, (2) Not working, or have any source of income (3) Singaporean, PR or Foreigners with valid passes (e.g. LTVP, LTVP+, Student Pass, Employment Pass, Dependent Pass, Work Permit, other passes of duration more than or equal to 2 years, etc.).

questions.title: How will I be notified about my Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA) application outcome?
questions.text: You will receive an SMS notification asking you to log in to the SupportGoWhere portal to access your application outcome details. You may also receive emails regarding your application status.

questions.title: What is the minimum Student Care Centre attendance requirement for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA)?
questions.text: A subsidised student shall be required to attain an attendance rate of at least 50% in each calendar month, except for the calendar months of June and December where the attendance rate shall be at least 30%.

questions.title: I am a Singaporean and I have remarried a foreigner. My child is a Singapore Citizen. Does my child fulfil the citizenship criteria?
questions.text: Yes. If the child is a Singapore citizen, his/her parents’ citizenship need not be further assessed.

questions.title: What if I am unable to retrieve certain supporting documents due to them being lost or not kept properly?
questions.text: Please explain why the documents are lost or cannot be retrieved. Upon submission of the deputy report, the case officer will review the report and will contact you should they require further assistance.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Filing of Deputy Report in OPGO

questions.title: How can I register my dialect with ICA?
questions.text:
ICA ascribes to a child the dialect of the father upon the child’s birth, in our national registration database. All individuals can subsequently change his or her dialect registered with the Government via a written declaration to ICA. This means that an individual can have a different registered dialect from his/ her father, or even both parents.
Individuals are allowed to register the language or dialect that they speak, or dialect by lineage. This has been a longstanding practice since the 1970s, and is also specified in our law, i.e. the National Registration Regulations.
Individuals can check their registered dialect via their Singpass, which is the authoritative source of the latest registered dialect information.

questions.title: I am an owner of an HDB and have inherited a private property. Is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable on the inherited property?
questions.text:
Stamp duty is not payable on the transfer of property through an assent to the beneficiaries in accordance to the Will, Intestate Succession Act, or Muslim Law of Inheritance. Therefore, Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) is not applicable to the inherited property.
However, the inherited residential property will be included in the property count when determining the ABSD rate for any subsequent residential property purchase.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is stamp duty payable for the renewal of a tenancy agreement if there is no change in rental fees?
questions.text:
Yes, stamp duty is applicable for the renewal of a tenancy agreement even if there are no changes in the rental fees. Stamp duty is a tax imposed on documents related to immovable properties, stocks, and shares, so stamping is required when the document for the renewal of the tenancy agreement is executed.
You can stamp the tenancy agreement by following these steps:
1. Log in to myTax Portal and navigate to "Stamp Duty".
2. Click on "Stamping" on the top navigation bar.
3. Select "Lease & Tenancy".

questions.title: Is stamping required and is stamp duty payable if an incoming tenant assumes the remaining lease period from the outgoing tenant?
questions.text:
Stamping is not required, and stamp duty is not payable if there is a Novation agreement, provided that:
1. The incoming tenant takes over the remaining lease period from the outgoing tenant, with no change in the lease terms and monthly rent.
2. There is no consideration paid between the parties.

questions.title: What is the difference between a Novation Agreement and a Lease/Tenancy Agreement?
questions.text:
A Novation Agreement is a contract between parties that transfers the rights and obligations of one party under an existing contract to a third party, effectively replacing one party with another.
In a Novation Agreement, typically three parties are involved: the original contracting parties (the outgoing party and the remaining party) and the new party (incoming party) who assumes the rights and obligations of the outgoing party.
A Lease Agreement, also known as a rental agreement or tenancy agreement, is a contract between a landlord and a tenant outlining the terms and conditions of renting a property.
In a Lease Agreement, usually two parties are involved: the landlord (property owner) and the tenant (person or entity renting the property).

questions.title: I am a US Citizen who is also a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR). If I am to purchase a residential property, is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable at SPR rate or Foreigner rate?
questions.text:
As a US Citizen, you will receive the same Stamp Duty treatment as Singapore Citizens under the Free Trade Agreement ABSD Remission.
For the purchase of a residential property, ABSD may be payable. However, the ABSD will be computed at the rate applicable to Singapore Citizens rather than the rate for SPRs.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Do food stall owners need to pay stamp duty?
questions.text:
License agreements are commonly used for the leasing out of a food stall in a food court, coffee shop, or hawker center.
License agreements are not subject to stamp duty.
However, lease duty at 0.4% would be payable if your license agreement meets either of the following criteria:
1. Acts as a lease, or
2. Is in connection to such a lease.
If you are unsure if your agreement is a license of a lease/tenancy, you may wish to seek independent legal advice or submit the document for adjudication. Please note that adjudication fees apply for the latter.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen and had purchased an HDB flat with my fiance/fiancee who is an SPR. Is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable?
questions.text:
ABSD is fully remitted under the Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission if any of the joint acquirers/purchasers is a Singapore Citizen.
1. Remission is granted automatically upon approval of the acquisition by HDB.
2. Remission is not applicable for Resale EC.
Therefore, ABSD is not payable for the joint purchase of your HDB flat.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am 55 years old and own a resale HDB. If I would like to buy a new private condo, can I get an Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) refund if I sell my HDB flat?
questions.text:
Single Singapore Citizens aged 55 years and above may be eligible for a refund under the ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen (SC) Seniors Remission, provided all remission conditions are met.
One of the eligibility conditions for ABSD refund is that the value of the second residential property is less than the value of the first residential property sold.
Do ensure that all conditions are met before applying for a refund under this remission.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I sign a tenancy agreement with a landlord for room rental, do I need to pay for stamp duty?
questions.text:
Stamp duty is a tax on documents (physical or electronic) relating to immovable properties, stocks, and shares.
Therefore, if a tenancy agreement is executed for room rental, stamping will be required for the relevant document, and lease duty is payable.
Lease duty is computed based on the contractual rent or market rent, whichever is higher, at a rate of 0.4%.

questions.title: Do I need to pay any stamp duty if my husband transfers his share of property to me due to our divorce? If I am to sell the property subsequently, will I incur Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD)?
questions.text:
Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD), Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD), and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) are not payable on the transfer of property resulting from matrimonial proceedings if the remission conditions are met.
If you intend to sell the property subsequently, SSD is not payable if the property is sold after the holding period.

questions.title: How do I calculate the holding period for Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD)?
questions.text:
For SSD purposes, the holding period is generally calculated from the date of purchase/acquisition to the date of sale/disposal.
Date of Property Purchase/Acquisition
Minimum Holding Period
Between 14 Jan 2011 and 10 Mar 2017 (all inclusive)
4 Years
Between 11 Mar 2017 and 3 Jul 2025 (all inclusive)
3 years
On and after 4 Jul 2025
4 Years
Please refer to the IRAS website for more information on calculating the holding period for SSD under different circumstances.

questions.title: I own a company and had purchased an HDB shophouse under the company's name. If I am to de-register my company and transfer the shophouse to myself, will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable?
questions.text:
HDB shops with living quarters or shophouses with a portion permitted for residential use are considered residential properties.
Therefore, ABSD may be payable on the transfer of the HDB shophouse, depending on your profile in terms of residency status (whether you are a Singaporean citizen, permanent resident, or foreigner) and the number of residential properties owned at the point of transfer.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: What happens to the value of my Savings Bonds when market interest rates change?
questions.text:
Once a Savings Bond is issued, changes in the interest rate environment will have no effect on the bond’s value. Unlike conventional bonds whose values fluctuate with interest rate movements, Savings Bonds are always redeemable at the amount originally invested with no capital losses.
Future interest rate levels could turn out to be higher (or lower) than the interest rates you receive from your Savings Bond holdings. You have the option to redeem your Savings Bond for the original invested capital with no penalty, and apply for new Savings Bond issues with higher interest rates, if you find that the latter is more attractive. Before you do this, you should consider whether a new Savings Bond with lower initial interest payments outweighs the stepped-up coupons you will be receiving on an existing Savings Bond that you may have held for some years.
topics: Singapore Savings Bonds / Introduction and Product Features

questions.title: How are Savings Bonds different from conventional SGS bonds?
questions.text:
Conventional SGS bonds can be traded on SGX. The prices of conventional SGS bonds can also change depending on market interest rates movements. This means that if you sell your conventional SGS before maturity, you may receive more or less than your invested capital. In contrast, Savings Bonds are not tradable, so you cannot sell them on SGX. You can, however, choose to redeem them from the Government in any month, and receive all your invested capital back.
Savings Bonds have a lower minimum investment amount and unit size of $500 compared to $1,000 for conventional SGS. Individuals can hold up to $200,000 of Savings Bonds at any point, but there are no investment limits on conventional SGS.
topics: Singapore Savings Bonds / Introduction and Product Features

questions.title: Can I use Central Provident Fund (CPF) funds to buy Savings Bonds?
questions.text: No, CPF funds cannot be used to invest in Savings Bonds.
topics: Singapore Savings Bonds / Applying for Savings Bonds

questions.title: Are returns from Savings Bonds taxable?
questions.text: No. The interest which you earn from the purchase of Savings Bonds is tax-exempted and does not have to be included in the chargeable income for your tax return.
topics: Singapore Savings Bonds / Applying for Savings Bonds

questions.title: What is the legal tender limit for notes/coins? Can a vendor or customer use quantities above the legal tender limit to make payment/return as change?
questions.text:
There is no legal tender limit for notes. However, for coins, there is a limit of 20 coins per denomination for each transaction (see Section 13(3) of the Currency Act 1967 ).
A vendor is only obliged to accept payments up to this legal tender limit and can reject any payment exceeding the limit. This is to reduce inconvenience to vendors and their waiting customers should a customer wish to offer a large quantity of coins for payment.
However, if both parties agree before entering into a transaction, a vendor and customer may still use quantities of coins above the legal tender limit.

questions.title: How do I cancel my enrollment?
questions.text: You can send your programme cancellation request and specify reason for the cancellation to the respective Course Manager.

questions.title: How do i apply for a Singpass account?
questions.text:
If you do not have a Singpass account, you can either: (i) register online at https://www.singpass.gov.sg/home/ui/register/instructions for your account here. (ii) set up for the account in any one of the ServiceSG Centres (https://www.psd.gov.sg/servicesg/)
Note: Ensure the address on your NRIC or FIN is correct. To update/change address, go to https://www.ica.gov.sg/documents/ic/update_residential_address
Contact Singpass Helpdesk here if you have any other enquiries pertaining to Singpass account creation.

questions.title: Why is the government combining various agencies' Sender IDs into a single gov.sg Sender ID?
questions.text: Using a single gov.sg SMS Sender ID will make it easier for the public to identify authentic government SMSes. From 1 July 2024 onwards, the public can be sure that all SMSes from the gov.sg Sender ID have been sent from a Singapore Government agency, ministry, statutory board, or service.

questions.title: I am in the midst of filling up the resale application form and realised that I do not have some of the information required (e.g. spouse’s NRIC). What can I do?
questions.text:
There is an option to allow you to save the application as a draft (Save as Draft). You may then complete the
application later for submission.

questions.title: How do I apply for an HFE letter?
questions.text:
There are two steps to the HFE letter application, which must be completed within 30 calendar days of each other.
Step 1: Check Preliminary HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE)
Please login to the HDB Flat Portal using your Singpass to retrieve your personal particulars from Myinfo and declare information including household income and ownership of private property. Based on the information provided, you will receive an instant preliminary overview of your household’s eligibility to purchase a flat, receive CPF housing grants and take up an HDB housing loan.
Step 2: Apply for HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) Letter
All applicants and occupiers (where applicable) will need to login to the HDB Flat Portal using their Singpass to retrieve their personal particulars from Myinfo and fill up the application. They will be guided to upload the supporting documents, where required. The processing time is up to a month, after HDB receives the completed application and all required documents. The HFE letter will be valid for 9 months from the date of issue.
Find out more about the income guidelines and documents required for an HFE letter application.
topics: My Flat Dashboard / HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

questions.title: When can I list my flat for sale on the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: You must first register an Intent to Sell to get a preliminary assessment of your eligibility to sell your flat, before you can list your flat for sale on the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: How can I list my flat?
questions.text:
After registering an Intent to Sell, you can list your flat for sale on the HDB Flat Portal by clicking on Create listing at the Seller Overview page under My Profile.
Information such as your address, flat type, floor area, and remaining lease, are automatically filled in. You will need to provide the following to create a listing:
Photographs of your flat (up to 10).
Your intended listing price.
A description of your flat.
Whether you require Temporary Extension of Stay and/ or Enhanced Contra Facility.
You may also appoint your salesperson to create and manage the flat listing on your behalf.
Please refer to our user guide and instructional video for more details on navigating the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: Does HDB verify the authenticity of the resale flat listings and information provided?
questions.text:
The flat listings are authentic as they are created by eligible flat sellers who have a valid Intent to Sell or by their appointed salespersons.
In each flat listing:
HDB provides information on the flat type, floor area, storey range, upgrading status, remaining lease, unit floor plan (as built), eligibility under the ethnic and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) quotas, and recent transacted prices.
Flat sellers or their appointed salespersons provide the photographs, flat description, listing price, and state if they would require Temporary Extension of Stay and/ or Enhanced Contra Facility. Flat sellers and their appointed salespersons are responsible for the accuracy of the information provided. Should there be any feedback on inaccuracies, HDB will look into the matter and take the necessary actions, including but not limited to removing the listing and restricting the future use of the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: Can I appoint a salesperson to help manage my listing account?
questions.text:
If you have a valid Intent to Sell and decided to engage the services of salesperson, you may appoint a CEA-registered salesperson as your Managing Salesperson to help you:
Create and edit your flat listing.
Update listing price of your flat.
Upload photos of your flat.
Communicate with potential flat buyers or their salespersons (if any).
Schedule flat viewing appointments.
After appointing a Managing Salesperson, you may also appoint up to 5 Co-managing Salespersons to help you add listing descriptions and schedule flat viewing appointments.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: Will I be contacted by a salesperson appointed by a potential flat buyer?
questions.text: Flat buyers with a valid HDB Flat Eligibility letter may appoint salespersons to manage their purchase on their behalf. Hence, you may be contacted by a salesperson appointed by a potential flat buyer on the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: How long will my listing be allowed on the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text:
Your listing can remain on the HDB Flat Portal as long as you have a valid Intent to Sell, until you grant an Option to Purchase (OTP) to a buyer. As granting an OTP has committed you to selling the flat to a specific buyer and not to others, unless the OTP has lapsed without the buyer exercising it, please deactivate your flat listing.
HDB will automatically deactivate your listing after we have receive a Request for Value or resale application for your flat. Your listing will be removed after the sale of your flat is completed or your Intent to Sell has expired, whichever is earlier.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: Do I have to pay to list my flat on the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: You do not have to pay to list your flat for sale on the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: What should I do if I receive unsolicited offer of help or services?
questions.text: You may write to us with details of the incident, such as the name and contact number of the person who contacted you, as well as screenshots of the text or email messages received. We will look into the matter and take the necessary actions, including but not limited to barring the errant user from using the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: What should I do if my listing is reported for inappropriate content?
questions.text: Your flat listing may be reported for violations of our guidelines on appropriate and accurate contents. This could include but is not limited to discriminatory language, offensive imagery, or misleading information. To re-publish your flat listing on the HDB Flat Portal, please edit the listing to comply with our Terms & Conditions and submit it for our review.
topics: Flat Listing / Selling a flat on open market

questions.title: Can I contact the flat sellers directly?
questions.text: Yes, if you have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility letter. To view flat sellers’ and/ or their appointed salespersons’ contact details, simply click on Contact seller or Contact salesperson on the flat listing.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Can I request a viewing appointment for a flat I am interested in?
questions.text: Yes, if you have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility letter. Log in to the HDB Flat Portal to see available viewing appointment slots (indicated by a green circle) on the calendar within a flat listing. To request a viewing appointment, click on your preferred date and time with an available viewing appointment slot, and click Book appointment.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: What can I do if there are no viewing appointment slots available?
questions.text: You may contact the sellers or their salesperson directly to check their availability for a flat viewing appointment.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Can I appoint a salesperson to help me manage my flat search?
questions.text:
Yes, if you have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility letter. You may appoint a CEA-registered salesperson to help you:
Save and edit your search profile.
Add/ remove and compare favourited flats.
Edit notification frequency.
Communicate with flat sellers or their salespersons.
Manage viewing appointments.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: How can I use the My favourite listings function to help me source for a suitable flat?
questions.text: The My favourite listings function allows you to save new and resale flats you wish to consider at the Buyer Overview page under My Profile. You can then compare your favourited flats holistically, including their attributes and preliminary payment plans.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Why do buyers need a valid HDB Flat Eligibility letter before they can access certain features, such as viewing sellers’ contact details, booking viewing appointments, and appointing salespersons?
questions.text: This is to ensure that flat sellers are only put into contact with eligible flat buyers with an intent to purchase a flat.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Are there duplicate listings on the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: No, only one listing can be created for a flat.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Is there a fee to use features for buyers on the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: You do not have to pay to browse and compare flats, or use the contact seller and viewing appointment features on the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: What should I do if I spot inappropriate content in a flat listing?
questions.text: Please notify us of the listing by clicking on Report listing on the flat listing. We will investigate your feedback and take the necessary actions, including but not limited to removing the listing.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: Where can I find more information on using the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: You may refer to our user guide and instructional video for more details on navigating the HDB Flat Portal.
topics: Flat Listing / Buying a resale flat

questions.title: What is the objective of the HDB Flat Portal?
questions.text: The HDB Flat Portal provides objective and holistic information on the available HDB flats and housing loan packages. It facilitates comparison and evaluation of the various options by home seekers according to their budget and needs.

questions.title: Am I eligible to apply for Singapore citizenship under the Aged Parent scheme?
questions.text: You are eligible to apply for Singapore citizenship if you are a PR and an Aged Parent of a Singapore citizen. For more information, you may refer to the Becoming a Singapore Citizen page on the ICA website.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Am I required to attend an interview for the Singapore citizenship application?
questions.text: As part of our enhanced Singapore citizenship application process, there is no longer a need to book an appointment for the interview. We will liaise with you through email should we need additional information.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Am I required to submit testimonials from my previous employers or from the current employment?
questions.text: Testimonials from the company is not a mandatory document. Nevertheless, you may submit it as a supplementary document.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can a Permanent Resident (PR) still apply for Singapore citizenship with an expired passport?
questions.text: Interested applicant is required to have a valid Permanent Residency (PR) status to be eligible for Singapore citizenship. After the application is submitted, applicant may provide the latest travel document information by requesting for a transfer of REP online via MyICA.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore citizenship after completing my National Service (NS)?
questions.text: You may log into ICA e-Service with your Singpass to apply for Singapore citizenship after completing full-time NS with both the Certificate of Service and Service Transcript.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore citizenship if I am not proficient in English?
questions.text: Only persons granted Singapore citizenship under Art 123 (1) of part X of the constitution are required to have elementary knowledge of one of the following languages, namely, Malay, English, Mandarin and Tamil.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore citizenship if I was granted PR under the sponsorship of my spouse?
questions.text: If you are gainfully employed and have satisfied the residential requirement, you can apply for Singapore citizenship on your own merits. Otherwise, you can apply for citizenship under your spouse's sponsorship provided your spouse is a Singapore citizen or is applying for Singapore citizenship.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore citizenship together as a family if my child's PR application is pending?
questions.text: Your child may apply Singapore citizenship and Permanent Resident (PR) concurrently under your/ your spouse sponsorship and we will process them accordingly. One facility will not affect the other. However, each facility will be processed according to the prevailing guidelines.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I omit parents and siblings’ details for my citizenship application as they reside overseas?
questions.text: There should be completeness in your application for Singapore citizenship. Hence, the information and details of your parents and siblings are required for the assessment of your citizenship application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I proceed with the Singapore citizenship registration if I am in the midst of divorce procedure?
questions.text:
If your Singapore citizenship application was approved under the sponsorship of your spouse, you are unable to proceed with your Singapore citizenship registration. Do not renounce your foreign citizenship.
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
Please login to ICA e-Service with your Singpass, select "upload additional documents" and upload the latest documents reflecting your change in marital status (in PDF format) within the citizenship application e-Service for review. Please note that withholding information on your marital status at the time of registration could affect your Singapore citizenship status.
When uploading documents via ICA e-Service, please use a desktop or laptop. Please do not include numbers and special characters in the file names.
Application submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
Please contact us via the enquiry form and upload the latest documents reflecting your change in marital status.
Please ensure the uploaded documents are in PDF format and do not include numbers and special characters in the file names.

questions.title: Can I produce other documents in replacement of the required document for my citizenship application?
questions.text: The alternative documents should be issued by the same authority and have the same information as the required documents.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I sponsor my siblings for Singapore citizenship after I become a Singapore citizen?
questions.text: You can only sponsor your spouse, parents or children for Singapore citizenship.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I sponsor my step-child for citizenship?
questions.text: You are unable to sponsor your step-child for citizenship as there is no legal nexus between you and your step-child.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I travel once I register as a Singapore citizen?
questions.text: You must apply for a Singapore passport for your travel after you become a Singapore citizen.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can I travel overseas after I have submitted an application for Singapore citizenship?
questions.text: You may travel overseas on your existing foreign passport while the application is being processed. For PRs, you are required to ensure you have a valid REP that covers your period overseas before you embark on your trip.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can my sponsor cancel my Singapore citizenship application?
questions.text: If your sponsor wishes to cancel the citizenship application, he/ she may log in to ICA e-Service and click on "withdraw application". Please note that the application fees paid is non-refundable.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Can my spouse apply for Singapore citizenship if I am a Singapore PR?
questions.text: If your spouse is a Singapore PR and presently working, he/ she can apply for citizenship on his/her own merits. If you are applying for citizenship, you may also sponsor your Singapore PR spouse for his/ her citizenship at the same time.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Do I have to submit original documents for citizenship application?
questions.text: You will need to provide a copy of your original documents and official translations (for documents in languages other than English) online.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Do I need to inform ICA if I change job after I submitted the citizenship application?
questions.text:
For Singpass users, please log in to the [ICA e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/esmain) and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
For Non-Singpass users, please [log in the e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/eslogin) with your submitted application Reference ID and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Do I need to renew my REP if my REP is expiring and my citizenship application has been approved?
questions.text: If you need to travel out of Singapore, please log in to ICA e-Service to renew your REP before you leave Singapore. You are required to have a valid REP before you leave.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Does my child need to be a Permanent Resident (PR) before applying for Singapore citizenship?
questions.text:
Your child may apply Singapore Citizenship without the need to be a Permanent Resident under your sponsorship if he/ she is unmarried and below 21 years old.
However, your child must be a PR before applying for Singapore Citizenship if he is applying under his/ her own merits.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I add additional documents or update changes to documents to a pending citizenship application?
questions.text:
For Singpass users, please log in to the [ICA e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/esmain) and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
For Non-Singpass users, please [log in the e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/eslogin) with your submitted application Reference ID and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
If the document(s) you wish to submit is not listed under ‘Update Information’, please [contact us via the enquiry form](https://go.gov.sg/ica-sc-enquiry) and upload the latest documents reflecting the changes.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I apply for Singapore citizenship?
questions.text:
You can submit a citizenship application online via ICA e-Service.
Please refer to Becoming a Singapore citizen for more information.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I apply Singapore citizenship for my child who is born overseas?
questions.text: If either parent is a Singapore citizen, he/ she can submit citizenship application for the child at ICA e-Service using his/ her Singpass. The child must possess a foreign birth certificate issued by the respective authority in the country of birth before the application can be submitted. Parents are encouraged to submit the application before the child turns one-year-old to facilitate the processing of your child's application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I complete the field on foreign identification number for citizenship application?
questions.text: If you are a national/ citizen from a country/ place that issues a foreign identification card, you are required to fill in the number. If not, fill in NA.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I fill in Company Strength in the Singapore Citizenship application form?
questions.text: Company Strength refers to the total number of staff in the company you are working with. You may provide an estimated number for this field if you do not have the information.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What information is required for 'Annual Turnover' field at the employment section in the application form?
questions.text: You would need to check with the company to obtain the information. If the information is not available, you may indicate an estimated amount or tick the 'Not applicable/ Not sure' checkbox.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I retrieve the form which I had filled in as a sponsor for Singapore citizenship application?
questions.text: For applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024, please download a copy of your submitted application from ICA e-Service within 7 days upon application submission.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I travel if I renounced my foreign citizenship but have not register Singapore citizenship?
questions.text: You must complete your citizenship registration before you can apply for a Singapore passport to travel. You can change your appointment at ICA e-Service for citizenship registration.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How do I update my new information for my citizenship application?
questions.text:
For Singpass users, please log in to the [ICA e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/esmain) and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
For Non-Singpass users, please [log in the e-Service](https://go.gov.sg/eslogin) with your submitted application Reference ID and select 'Update information' within your case summary page to provide the update.
If the particulars you wish to amend is not available under ‘Update Information’, you may submit your request via the enquiry form (https://go.gov.sg/ica-sc-enquiry) and upload the latest documents reflecting the changes.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How soon can I register for my Singapore citizenship after my citizenship application is approved?
questions.text: You will be given an appointment date about 1 month from the date of the approval letter to renounce your foreign citizenship and to register for Singapore citizenship. For more information, please refer to the Singapore Citizenship roadmap at ICA website.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: How will ICA contact me if my citizenship application require additional documents?
questions.text: You will receive a notification to log in to ICA e-Service to check and submit the information required.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: Is my overseas-born child eligible for Singapore citizenship by descent if I am a citizen by descent
questions.text: ICA will make an assessment of your child's eligibility for Singapore citizenship by descent on receipt of your child's application. You are encouraged to apply for Singapore citizenship for your child within a year of his/ her birth. If your child has been assessed to be ineligible for Singapore citizenship by descent, your child will be considered for Singapore citizen by registration before providing an outcome.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What can I do if I do not have the requested information when submitting the citizenship application?
questions.text:
For mandatory fields, please indicate 'NA' if you do not have the requested information.
For documents, such as birth certificates, where the system prompts you to upload the actual or extract copy of the document, please ensure you obtain the relevant documents. The alternative documents should be issued by the same authority and have the same information as the documents it replaced.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What can I do if I need help to complete the fields/upload documents to the citizenship application?
questions.text:
You may refer to the video for more information.
For further clarification, you may contact us via the enquiry form with a screenshot of the issue encountered should you face any system error.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What does 'number of staff under supervision' in the citizenship application form refers to?
questions.text: The 'Number of staff under supervision' refers to the staff that is under your supervision. You may indicate an estimated number if you do not have the information.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What does it mean if my Singapore citizenship application is pending?
questions.text: This means that your application is being processed or there may be outstanding instructions. Please visit ICA e-Service to check for any instructions and status update.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What is the application fee for Singapore citizenship application?
questions.text: You can refer to ICA Website on Becoming a Singapore citizen and select 'Fees' for more information.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What is the next step after my Singapore citizenship application is approved?
questions.text: You may refer to the Singapore Citizenship Roadmap at ICA website for more information on what is required at each stage of the citizenship application. The main applicant/ sponsor may log in to view the final instructions.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What is the processing time for Singapore citizenship applications?
questions.text:
All applications for Singapore citizenship are carefully considered and reviewed by ICA. Generally, applications will be processed within 12 months, provided all the required documents are submitted. Depending on the complexity of the case, some applications may take longer to process.
You will be informed of the outcome via email. Meanwhile, you or your sponsor may check the status of your Singapore citizenship application online through ICA e-Service.
There is no need to contact ICA during this time.
New or repeated applications, for the same person(s), will not be accepted while the current application is still in process.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What is the residential requirement of Singapore PR to be considered for citizenship?
questions.text: A Singapore PR can be away from Singapore for 50% of the qualifying residential period, subject to a maximum absence of one year, whichever is shorter, in order to be considered for Singapore citizenship.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Citizenship

questions.title: What is the SG Journey website?
questions.text: The Singapore Citizenship Journey (SCJ) website is for successful applicants to get to know Singapore better. If you need help with the SCJ, please call 1800 222 5008 during office hours or email admin@sgjourney.gov.sg.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass

questions.title: Why is my Singapore citizenship application pending still after 12 months?
questions.text:
All applications for Singapore citizenship are carefully considered and reviewed by ICA. Generally, applications will be processed within 12 months, provided all the required documents are submitted. Depending on the complexity of the case, some applications may take longer to process.
You will be informed of the outcome via email. Meanwhile, you or your sponsor may check the status of your Singapore citizenship application online through ICA e-Service.
New or repeated applications, for the same person(s), will not be accepted while the current application is still in process.

questions.title: Will I automatically become a Singapore citizen after completion of National Service (NS)?

questions.title: Will my child be considered a Singapore citizen if he is born after I become a Singapore citizen?

questions.title: Will my Singapore citizenship application be affected if I accept an overseas job?
questions.text: You will not be eligible for Singapore citizenship as only economic contributions in Singapore will be considered. Also, a Singapore PR can only be away from Singapore for 50% of the qualifying residential period, subject to a maximum absence of one year, whichever is shorter. However, absence due to official business, overseas posting by a Singapore employer may be treated as residence for purpose of citizenship application on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Can a Singapore citizen be a permanent resident of another country?

If there was no sponsor, the main applicant must submit the appeal. If the original application was submitted without Singpass, you must submit the appeal using the same email address.
You can submit the appeal via the Appeal for Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long-Term Visit Pass e-Service.

questions.title: What can I do if my Singapore citizenship application is unsuccessful?
questions.text:
All applications for Singapore citizenship are carefully considered and reviewed by ICA. Factors such as the applicant's family ties to Singaporeans, economic contributions, length of residency in Singapore, ability to contribute to and integrate into Singapore, and commitment to sink roots in Singapore are considered, among other factors.
If there are additional or updated information or documents since your last application, you may consider submitting a fresh application online through ICA e-Service.
Please note that the outcome of the application will remain the same if there are no changes to your circumstances, and if the same information or documents are submitted.

questions.text:
A Singapore citizen below the age of 21, who is also holding a foreign passport, may apply for a Right of Entry (ROE). This ROE facilitates the citizen's immigration clearance using the foreign passport when entering or leaving Singapore through the Singapore immigration checkpoints.

questions.title: Will I lose my Singapore citizenship if I live overseas?
questions.text:
Under Article 135(1)(b) and 135(1)(c) of the Singapore Constitution, a Singapore citizen who has been away from Singapore for a continuous period of 10 years or more without a valid Singapore passport may be deprived of his Singapore citizenship.
You are advised to have a valid Singapore travel document if you wish to remain outside of Singapore for more than 10 years.

questions.title: Am I allowed to renounce my citizenship when my son has not served National Service?
questions.text:
Under Article 128 of the Singapore Constitution, a citizen of Singapore can only renounce his/ her Singapore citizenship if he/she:
a) Is aged 21 and above;
b) Is of sound mind; and
c) Is also or is about to become a citizen of another country.
The Government may withhold the renunciation of Singapore citizenship by a male citizen if he is subjected to the Enlistment Act (Cap. 93) unless he has:
a) discharged his liability for full-time service under section 12 of that Act;
b) rendered at least 3 years of operationally ready national service under section 13 of that Act in lieu of such full-time service; or
c) complied with such conditions as may be determined by the Government
You may refer to Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship for more information.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters /  Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship

questions.title: Can a minor hold on to more than one citizenship in Singapore?
questions.text: A minor is allowed to hold multiple nationalities/ citizenships until the age of 21 years old.

questions.title: Can I continue to be a dual citizen on reaching age 18?
questions.text: You can continue to retain your Singapore citizenship as a dual citizen until the age of 21. You will then be required to show proof of renunciation of your foreign citizenship(s) if you wish to retain Singapore citizenship.

questions.title: Can I renounce my Singapore citizenship before obtaining another country citizenship?
questions.text:
Under Article 128 of the Singapore Constitution, a citizen of Singapore can only renounce his/ her Singapore citizenship if he/ she:
a) Is aged 21 and above;
b) Is of sound mind; and
c) Is also or is about to become a citizen of another country.
As such you may only renounce Singapore citizenship if you have documents to show that you are about to become the citizen of another country.
Please note that the Government may withhold the renunciation of Singapore citizenship by a male citizen if he is subjected to the Enlistment Act (Cap. 93) unless he has:
a) discharged his liability for full-time service under section 12 of that Act;
b) rendered at least 3 years of operationally ready national service under section 13 of that Act in lieu of such full-time service; or
c) complied with such conditions as may be determined by the Government
You may refer to Renunciation of Singapore citizenship for more information.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters /  Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship

questions.title: Does Singapore allow a citizen to keep dual citizenship?
questions.text: Please note that the Singapore government does not allow its adult citizens to hold dual citizenship. Thus, once you have attained the citizenship of another country, you are to renounce your Singapore citizenship as soon as possible.

questions.text:
Under Article 128 of the Singapore Constitution, a citizen of Singapore can only renounce his/ her Singapore citizenship if he/ she:
a) Is aged 21 and above;
b) Is of sound mind; and
c) Is also or is about to become a citizen of another country.
The Government may withhold the renunciation of Singapore citizenship by a male citizen if he is subjected to the Enlistment Act (Cap. 93) unless he has

questions.title: How do I withdraw my renunciation application for Singapore citizenship?
questions.text:
Please note that once your declaration of renunciation is registered, you will cease to be a citizen of Singapore and cannot withdraw the renunciation. There is also no provision for reinstatement once a renunciation is effected. If you have not received confirmation of your renunciation application, you may write in to ica_irr_review@ica.gov.sg to request to withdraw the application with your reasons. There will not be a refund of the fee. As Singapore does not allow dual citizenship you will also need to explain your plan of divesting yourself of your foreign citizenship.
Note: If your renunciation has already been processed, your request to withdraw will not be successful.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters /  Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship

questions.title: I have renounced Singapore citizenship but would like to change my decision. How do I do so?
questions.text: At the time of renunciation of Singapore citizenship you have acknowledged that once your declaration of renunciation is registered, you ceased to be a citizen of Singapore and there is no provision for reinstatement. A person who has renounced Singapore citizenship is no longer a Singapore citizen.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters /  Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship

questions.title: What documents do I need to prepare for renunciation of my Singapore citizenship?
questions.text:
You will be required to submit Certified True Copies of the following documents:
Foreign citizenship certificate
Valid foreign passport (if obtained)
Deed poll or change of name certificate or Religious/ Baptism certificate or Marriage certificate, if there has been a change to your name.
You will also need to submit the following Mandatory Forms:
Statutory Declaration of Renunciation Form
Advisory Note on Renunciation Implication Form
MINDEF Advisory Note (for male applicants only)
You will also be required to return the following documents to ICA:
Original Singapore Identity Card (IC)
Valid Singapore Passport
Singapore Citizenship Certificate (if applicable)
You may refer to Renunciation of Singapore citizenship for more information.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters /  Renunciation of Singapore Citizenship

questions.title: What happens if I renounce my Singapore citizenship?

questions.title: Can I extend my online draft application for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass before it expires?

questions.title: Can I save the application for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass as draft and complete the application at another time?
questions.text:
There are two parts to the application. You are given a total of 14-days (i.e. 7-days for the first part and 7-days for the second part) from the date you start the draft to complete and submit the application.
For the first part of the application, you are required to complete the two sections ('Fill in Particulars' and 'Upload Documents') within seven days from the date you start the draft.
For the second part of the application, you are required to complete the remaining sections 'Review & Declare', make payment and submit your application within the next seven days.
You may save your application as a draft and continue later for submission within the stipulated time indicated in the e-Service.
The draft will be retrieved when you login to the ICA e-Service once you start the application.
