questions.title: I am not able to provide the required document(s) for the Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application. Can I provide other documents in place of them?
questions.text:
The alternative documents should be issued by the same authority and have the same information as the required documents.
If you do not have any alternative documents, you may upload an explanatory letter stating your reason.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Is the application fee for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass refundable?
questions.text: The fee is non-refundable once you have submitted the application and completed the payment regardless of the outcome.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Must I make payment immediately upon submission of the Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application?
questions.text:
Only applications with successful payment made will be considered submitted and processed.
Do note that applications, along with the uploaded documents, which are not submitted within the stipulated window will be removed from the system. If you are unable to make payment before the draft application expires, you will need to start a new application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What are the available payment modes for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application?
questions.text:
Payment can be made using:
Visa card
MasterCard Credit/ Debit Card; or
American Express (AMEX) card; or
Internet banking (DBS/ POSB, OCBC, UOB and Standard Chartered Bank banking account in Singapore); or
PayNow
Please refer to ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What are the documents required to apply for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text: You may view the list of documents required for your Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application once you have keyed in the necessary applicant information and selected the product(s) which you are applying for at ICA e-Service.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What are the fees involved for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application(s)?
questions.text:
You can refer to ICA Website on the respective products for more information on the fees involved:
Singapore Citizenship
Permanent Residence
Long-term Visit Pass
You would also be informed of the processing fee before you start your application at ICA e-Service.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What can I do if I cannot change my address details in the application form for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text:
The address on the application is your registered address with ICA.
Should you wish to update your address, you can do so via the following steps:
1. Report the new address via ICA e-Service
2. Receive a unique PIN by mail at the new address.
3. Enter the PIN via the same e-Service as a way to verify the new address.
4. Receive a sticker bearing the new address by mail.
5. Affix the sticker to the back of the IC according to the instructions provided.
*Note: For LTVP holders, no stickers would be provided.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What can I do if I have not received any response on my extension request for clarification?
questions.text:
All clarifications must be submitted to ICA within the deadline given. You may continue to provide information relevant to the request for clarifications while your request for an extension is pending, as long as the deadline has not lapsed.
If the deadline has lapsed, you will not be able to respond until there is an outcome to your extension request.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What can I do if the person I am applying for does not have a valid email address?
questions.text:
If the person that you are applying for does not have a valid email address, you may wish to seek his/her consent to provide a trusted person's email address or alternatively, for all communications to come through your email address instead.
This email address will be used to convey instructions and updates.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What can the alternative sponsor do?
questions.text: An alternative sponsor is someone identified by ICA as another potential sponsor for the application(s). The nomination of the 'alternative sponsor' will allow ICA to exercise its options to optimise the outcomes when processing the application(s), without the need to seek further consent from you.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What happens if I did not submit my response to the clarification request for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application by the expiry date?
questions.text:
For applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024
Your application for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass will be assessed on prevailing information if you do not submit a response before the expiry date.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What is the processing time for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application?
questions.text:
For applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024
All applications are carefully considered and reviewed by ICA. Generally, if you are applying for a single product, the processing time for:
*Singapore citizenship applications may take up to 12 months to process;
*Singapore Permanent Residence applications may take up to 6 months to process; &
*Long-Term Visit Pass applications may take up to 6 weeks to process.
You will be informed of the outcome via email. Meanwhile, you or your sponsor may check the status of your application online at MyICA or via ICA e-Service.
New or repeated applications, for the same person(s), will not be accepted while the current application is still in process.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What should I do if I encounter an error when I upload photo image for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application?
questions.text:
You are advised to view the details of the error message. Please note that the following photo criteria:
image file is in jpg, jpeg, heic, heif and png file extension format
preferred dimension is 400 x 514 pixels
file size is not more than 8MB
The above criteria must be fulfilled for the photo to be accepted in ICA e-Service.
You may refer to the ICA photo guidelines for more information. Do note that your photo image will be checked by ICA according to our requirements after successful upload.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: What should I do if I want to make edits to my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application details before submitting my declaration?
questions.text:
If you are the main applicant or sponsor, you can click on the 'Edit' button to make the necessary changes to your application.
If someone is applying on your behalf, you will need to inform the main applicant or sponsor to make the necessary edits to your application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Where can I view details of my submitted application for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text:
For applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024
You may download a copy of your submitted application at ICA e-Service within seven days from the date of submission.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Who can edit the details of the Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application if an alternative sponsor is nominated?
questions.text:
For applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024
Any edits to the Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application will need to be completed by the original sponsor. The alternative sponsor will not be able to make edits to the application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Why am I unable submit my response to the clarification request for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application?
questions.text: All clarifications must be submitted to ICA within the deadline given. You are not able to submit a response after the clarification deadline.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Why am I unable to amend my name or surname/ family name in the application form for Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text: For NRIC holder, you will need to update your details via e-Service to make amendments to your name or surname/ family name before proceeding with your application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Why am I unable to upload documents when applying through my mobile phone?
questions.text: Please check your mobile browser application permissions on your phone and ensure that it is allowed to access files and photos on your phone.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Would I be granted more than one product if I applied for more than one?
questions.text: We will only grant you the product (i.e. Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence or Long-Term Visit Pass) that we have assessed you to be eligible for.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / General

questions.title: Can I change my appointment for Completion of Formalities (COF)?
questions.text: You may change your appointment at ICA e-Service if you are unavailable for the scheduled appointment.

questions.title: Can I complete my formalities without making an appointment?
questions.text: The completion of formalities is strictly by appointment only. If you are unavailable for your scheduled appointment, you may change your appointment at ICA e-Service within the validity of your In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter.

questions.title: What should I do if I cannot complete formalities for my Singapore citizenship, Permanent Residence and/or Long-Term Visit Pass application within the period stated in my IPA letter?
questions.text:
For applications submitted on and after 26 June 2024, you may request for an extension to complete your formalities via ICA e-Service. On your e-Service dashboard, you may click on 'View Details' then click on 'Proceed to Complete Formalities'. Submit your extension request by clicking on 'Request for Extension'. Please note that extension requests are subject to ICA's consideration.
For applications submitted before 26 June 2024, the sponsor or applicant may submit request to extend the validity of the IPA letter via the following:
- Singapore citizenship
- Permanent Residence
- Long-Term Visit Pass
Please note that extension requests are subject to ICA's consideration.

questions.title: Will I be served if I am late on my appointment day for completion of formalities?
questions.text: Arriving late for your appointment may result in longer waiting times as priority will be given to applicants who are on time for their appointment. We strongly encourage you to arrive on time to allow us to serve you promptly.

questions.title: Must I be physically present in Singapore while my LTVP application is being processed?
questions.text: There is no need for the applicant to be physically present in Singapore while the application is being processed. However, please note that you and/or your sponsor may be required to attend an interview or submit additional documents during the processing of LTVP.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: How do I amend or update the information submitted for my LTVP application?
questions.text:
The Local Sponsor may wish to log in to the e-Service via MyICA and select 'Update information'' within your case summary page to provide the update.
If you are unable to update the details, please provide the amended or updated information for your LTVP application using this enquiry form.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: How do I withdraw a LTVP application after submission?
questions.text: The sponsor or main applicant can log in to the e-Service to withdraw the LTVP application that is under processing.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: How do I extend my stay if my current LTVP is expiring and my LTVP renewal is still pending?
questions.text:
If the renewal of your Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) application is in process and your current LTVP is expiring, you will receive an email notification on the auto-conversion of your LTVP to a Short-Term Visit Pass (STVP).
If you did not receive any notification from ICA during the renewal application process, you may cancel your LTVP by submitting the Cancellation of Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) form.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: I am a foreign spouse who is widowed or has divorced a Singapore Citizen or Singapore PR. How can I renew my LTVP?
questions.text: If you are unable to submit your LTVP renewal application due to unique circumstances, you can submit a request for further assistance.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: What is the processing time for an LTVP?
questions.text:
The LTVP applications will generally be processed within 6 weeks*, provided all the required documents are submitted and in order. Some applications may take longer to process. We seek your patience as all applications for LTVP are carefully considered and reviewed by ICA.
*For spouse of Singapore citizen who did not submit a Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA), the LTVP application will take up to 6 months to be processed.
You will be informed of the outcome via email. Meanwhile, you or your local sponsor may check the status of your LTVP application through the e-Service.
Please note that new or repeated applications, for the same person(s), will not be accepted while the current application is still in process.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: When can I renew my Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: Please submit your Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) renewal application at least 3 months before the expiry of your current LTVP. The validity of the renewed LTVP will be from the date of issuance (upon payment of the issuance fee). The remaining validity from the current LTVP will not be carried forward to the renewed LTVP.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: How can I contact ICA for LTVP matters?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form for queries on LTVP matters.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: How do I cancel an LTVP/ LTVP+?
questions.text:
You may cancel your LTVP by submitting the Cancellation of Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) form.
The cancellation of a LTVP must be consensual. Both the LTVP holder and sponsor may be required to be physically present for the cancellation.
Notwithstanding the above, a LTVP may also be cancelled at ICA's discretion in accordance with the Immigration Regulations.
The LTVP holder will be issued a short-term visit pass for him/her to make arrangements to leave Singapore upon the LTVP cancellation.

questions.title: What should I do with the Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) if the LTVP holder had passed away?
questions.text: The sponsor of the LTVP may cancel your LTVP by submitting the Cancellation of Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) form.

questions.title: Can I proceed to the counters direct since I have an appointment for Completion of LTVP formalities?
questions.text: You are required to obtain a queue ticket at the registration kiosks at the ICA Services Centre. The queue ticket will show your queue number and the designated counter(s) that will be serving you. Please bring along your passport and all required document(s) as stated on your LTVP In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter.

questions.title: How can I be exempted from visiting ICA Services Centre for completion of formalities for LTVP issuance?
questions.text:
Successful LTVP applicants who have enrolled their biometrics with ICA previously may be exempted from visiting ICA Services Centre to complete the formalities for the LTVP issuance.
ICA will inform eligible applicants of the exemption and issue them with a digital LTVP.

questions.title: How can I book an e-Appointment for Completion of Long-Term Visit Pass formalities?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
You can book your appointment for Long-Term Visit Pass completion of formalities via the e-Service.
(Select ‘Completion of Long-Term Visit Pass Formalities’)
Applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
You will receive an appointment slot to report to ICA Services Centre for your completion of formalities. You can check your appointment date and time at the ICA e-Service. You may change your appointment if you are unavailable for the scheduled appointment.

questions.title: What do I do if I am unavailable for my Completion of Long-Term Visit Pass formalities appointment?
questions.text: You may make another appointment at ICA e-Service before the expiry of your LTVP in-principle approval.

questions.title: What documents do I need to bring for Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) completion of formalities?
questions.text: Successful Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) applicants can refer to the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter on the documents requirement for LTVP completion of formalities.

questions.title: Are there any differences in the digital LTVP from FileSG, MyICA, MyICA Mobile and the Singpass app?
questions.text: The digital LTVPs found on FileSG, MyICA, MyICA Mobile and the Singpass app are official documents that are issued to legitimise a person's stay in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I receive and manage the digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) on behalf of my family members?
questions.text:
Only the sponsor of LTVP holders who are below 15 years old will receive a copy of the LTVP in his/ her own FileSG account. This copy is only issued to sponsors who are Singpass holders.
Family members, who are not sponsors of LTVP holders below the age of 15, can still retrieve the digital LTVP via non-Singpass login on the FileSG website - by logging in with the credentials of the LTVP holder and by satisfying Two-Factor Authentication with the One-Time-Password that will be sent to the mobile number provided in the LTVP application.

questions.title: Can I request for a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) physical card after 27 Feb 2023?
questions.text: ICA has ceased the issuance of Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) physical cards from 27 Feb 2023. LTVP will henceforth be issued in digital format only.

questions.title: Do I need a Singpass account to retrieve my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
LTVP holders can still view, download and print their digital LTVP on the FileSG website, without a Singpass account.
However, we strongly encourage LTVP holders to register for Singpass, if eligible, for easier retrival of the digital LTVP from FileSG.

questions.title: How can I retrieve my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
The LTVP holder will receive an email from FileSG with instructions on downloading the digital LTVP.
If the LTVP holder does not have a Singpass account, he/ she should apply for it via the Singpass website to facilitate his/ her transactions with government agencies in Singapore. The digital pass can be viewed on his/ her Singpass App after 3 working days.
For first-time registrants, please register for a Singpass account from the third working day after your LTVP is issued.

questions.title: How can one verify the authenticity of the digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
The digital LTVP can be verified in two ways:
(1) by using the 'Scan QR Code' function on FileSG website, against the QR code found on the digital LTVP, or
(2) by uploading the digital LTVP in OA format onto the FileSG website

questions.title: How do I retrieve my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) on FileSG?
questions.text:
For users with a Singpass account:
Login to the FileSG website with your Singpass account
Confirm your contact details if you are logging in for the first time
Upon successful login, you can view and download files you have been issued, by different government agencies through FileSG
For users without a Singpass account:
You will need to enter the transaction ID onto the FileSG website, for the file you are trying to retrieve. The transaction ID can be found in the email sent to you, after completion of formalities at ICA.
Input the required personal particulars and complete authentication with the One-Time-Password (OTP) sent to the mobile number provided in your LTVP application.
Upon successful authentication, you can view and download the LTVP that is associated with the transaction ID provided at the start of this process.

questions.title: How do I update my mobile number or handphone number to retrieve my Digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) if I have changed my number?
questions.text:
Singpass holders can login to the FileSG website and view their digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) without One-Time Password (OTP) authentication.
LTVP holders who are not unable to retrieve the digital LTVP may submit a request for assistance.

questions.title: How do I view the digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) after downloading it to my device?
questions.text: The digital LTVP is available for download in two file formats: PDF and OpenAttestation (OA). The PDF version can be downloaded and viewed directly on your personal electronic device (e.g., smartphone, personal computer). The OA version is not meant to be readable but to be shared with a requesting party. The party requesting for the digital LTVP in OA format will have to upload the shared OA file onto FileSG's website, to view the digital LTVP.

questions.title: How long do I need to wait before the digital LTVP is shown in my Singpass app?
questions.text: Please allow 3 working days for the newly issued digital LTVP to be displayed in your Singpass app.

questions.title: What are the platforms that I can use to retrieve my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: Your digital LTVP can be viewed, downloaded and printed from the FileSG website, ICA's website (MyICA) and ICA's mobile app (MyICA Mobile). Singpass holders can also view their digital LTVP on the Singpass app.

questions.title: What if I do not have the transaction ID to retrieve my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
The transaction ID can be found in the email sent to you, after completion of formalities at ICA.
Singpass holders can login to the FileSG website and view their digital LTVP without the transaction ID.
LTVP holders who are not eligible to register a Singpass account can contact us via the enquiry form to request for the email to be resent, or to update ICA with their new email address.

questions.title: What is FileSG?
questions.text: FileSG is a file issuance and storage web service that simplifies file transactions between individuals and the Singapore Government. From 27 Feb 2023, ICA will issue LTVP/ STP digitally via the FileSG platform. LTVP and STP holders can expect an email from FileSG, after the completion of formalities at ICA (if required), that will provide more information on the retrieval of their digital LTVP/STP.

questions.title: What is OpenAttestation (OA) and when do I download my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) as OA?
questions.text: OpenAttestation (OA) is an encrypted file format that provides assurance that the document is authentic. The digital LTVP in OA format can only be viewed after it is uploaded at the FileSG website. Download it only when you are required to submit your digital pass in OA format.

questions.title: What is the recommended platform to retrieve and use my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text:
LTVP holders can use any platform that best suits their situation and needs for the retrieval of the digital LTVP.
As an example, for on-the-spot transactions that require the digital LTVP be shown to a person or entity whom the LTVP holder is transacting with, the LTVP holder can choose to show the digital LTVP on the Singpass app if that is more convenient.
If LTVP holders need to submit a copy of their LTVP, they can do so by downloading the digital LTVP from the FileSG website.

questions.title: What should I do if I did not receive the email on retrieving my digital Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text:
The Long-Term Visit Pass holder should receive the email within 30 minutes after issuance of the Pass. Please do the following to ensure that you can receive the email:
Check the spam or junk folder of your email account
Ensure that your email inbox folder is not full
Ensure that you have an active internet connection on your device
If you are unable to locate the email after performing the above checks, please contact us via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: What should I do if there is an error in my particulars on my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: You can contact us via the enquiry form with a copy of your digital LTVP and a copy of your passport showing your particulars, for assistance.

questions.title: Why am I unable to register for Singpass immediately after my LTVP application is approved?
questions.text:
Please visit the Singpass website for the eligibility requirements and the instructional guide to register for a Singpass account.
For first-time registrants, please register for a Singpass account from the third working day after your LTVP is issued.

questions.title: Why do I see expired digital Long-Term Visit Passes issued to me previously, in my FileSG account?
questions.text: Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holders will have access to expired copies of the digital LTVP to complete any transactions that require proof of the LTVP(s) that they were previously issued with. These expired LTVP(s) may be removed over time, at ICA's discretion.

questions.title: Will I be issued a physical Long-Term Visit Pass card if I complete formalities from 27 Feb 2023?
questions.text: ICA has ceased the issuance of physical Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) cards and has only issued digital LTVPs since 27 Feb 2023. After the completion of formalities at ICA (if required), you will receive an email from FileSG, which will provide you with more information on retrieving your digital LTVP. Those who are exempted from completion of formalities at ICA will receive the email after their application is approved. Singpass holders can also view their digital LTVP on the Singpass app.

questions.title: Will the digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) be recognised and accepted everywhere?
questions.text: The digital LTVP is equivalent to the physical LTVP cards that were issued before 27 February 2023.

questions.title: Will the multiple journey visa be shown on my digital LTVP upon the relevant fees payment?
questions.text: The Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holder is issued a multiple journey visa that is tied to the validity of the digital LTVP. The multiple journey visa is not reflected on the digital LTVP on the Singpass app.

questions.title: Will unauthorised personnel have access to the data on my digital Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: Singpass authentication or Two-Factor Authentication is always required to access your digital LTVP. LTVP holders should ensure that their digital LTVP is shared only when necessary, and to trusted parties.

questions.title: Am I eligible to work with my extended LTVP validity?
questions.text: After the extension of your LTVP validity, please contact Ministry of Manpower to extend your Letter of Consent to work.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: What are the responsibilities and role of a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) sponsor?
questions.text:
As the sponsor, you must ensure that the LTVP holder complies to the following during his/ her stay in Singapore under your sponsorship:
a) Complies with the provisions of the Immigration Act and any regulations in Singapore during his/ her stay in Singapore.
b) His/ her purpose of stay in Singapore is solely for social visit only.
c) He/ she shall not indulge in any activities which are inconsistent with the purpose of the visit pass (long-term or short-term) which was issued to him/ her.
d) He/ she shall not engage in any form of employment paid or unpaid, or in any business profession or occupation, or in any activity which, the opinion of the Controller of Immigration is detrimental to the security, reputation and well-being of Singapore.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: What is the difference between a Dependant's Pass (DP) and a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: Dependant's Pass (DP) is issued to dependants of eligible work pass holders by Ministry of Manpower; whilst Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) is generally issued to dependants of eligible Singapore citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents by ICA.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / LTVP/LTVP+

questions.title: Why are foreigners required to obtain a Visit Pass?
questions.text: The purpose of a Visit Pass is to regulate the stay of foreigners in Singapore. It will be granted at the checkpoint to a foreigner who wishes to enter Singapore for social or business purposes or as a tourist.

questions.title: How do I report the loss of a physical Long-Term Visit Pass card?
questions.text:
With effect from 27 Feb 2023, ICA has ceased the issuance of Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) physical cards.
For replacement of LTVP due to loss/ damage, there is no need to report to ICA as no physical LTVP card will be issued for the replacement.
You may use the digital LTVP in your Singpass app for verification of your status.
Only pass holders who are unable to apply for Singpass (e.g. LTVP holders under 15 years old), may report to ICA Services Centre to seek a digital replacement of their lost/ damaged LTVP card.

questions.title: Will LTVP holders receive an email confirmation after submitting the request to change or update passport particulars?

questions.title: I am a LTVP/ LTVP+ holder. How can I apply for a Letter of Consent (LOC)?
questions.text: You can apply for a Letter of Consent (LOC) to work in Singapore if you are a LTVP or LTVP+ holder who is the spouse or unmarried child of a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident. Please refer to MOM for further information.

questions.title: Who is eligible for LTVP+?
questions.text:
Foreign spouses of Singapore Citizens may be eligible for LTVP+ if the foreign spouse has at least 1 child who is a Singapore Citizen from the marriage; or is pregnant.
Other consideration factors may include the marriage duration, ability of the sponsor to financially support the family, and good conduct of both the sponsor and the applicant. In general, applicants may be considered more favourably for LTVP+ if they have been married for at least 3 years.
An LTVP+ provides the holder with a greater certainty of stay and a longer period of residency in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I apply Singapore PR for my spouse or children if they do not have a valid passport?
questions.text:
You will not be able to apply Singapore PR for your spouse or children if they do not have a valid passport or a passport with validity of at least 6 months at the point of application.
Do note that it is a pre-requisite to have a travel document with at least 6 months validity at the point of submission of the application. Otherwise, the application will be rejected.

questions.title: Can I apply for PR if my passport is expiring?
questions.text: As part of the requirements to apply for Singapore Permanent Residence, your passport will need to be valid for at least 6 months. If you do not have a valid passport or have a passport with validity of less than 6 months at the point of application, the application will be rejected.

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) for my parent(s) without a birth certificate?

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) if my residential address is not within Singapore?

questions.title: Can I apply Singapore Permanent Residence for my spouse without producing the marriage certificate?

questions.title: Can I include my dependant(s) in my Singapore PR application after I have submitted it?

questions.title: Can I submit my Singapore PR application without the testimonials from my previous employer?

questions.title: Can my child attend school if his/ her Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) application is pending?
questions.text:

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a work pass if I am a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) seeking employment?
questions.text: As a Singapore PR, you do not need a work pass to work in Singapore. questions.title: How many times can I apply for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR)?
questions.text:
While there is no limit to the number of times you may apply for PR, you should only do so when there is a substantial change in your circumstances from your last application. Each application would have been carefully reviewed before a decision is made.
If you would still like to be considered for PR, please submit a new application online through ICA e-Service. Please note that fees paid are not refundable.
Please refer to ICA website for more information on the eligibility criteria for PR application.

questions.title: How may I amend my particulars which was wrongly keyed in when applying for Singapore PR?

questions.title: Is there an age limit for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) applications/ applicants?

questions.title: Was my Singapore PR application submitted successfully if I did not get to the payment page?

questions.title: What is my National Service Liability as a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR)?
questions.text:

questions.title: What is the processing time for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) applications?
questions.text:
Generally, Singapore PR applications take about 6 months to process, provided all the required documents are submitted. Depending on the complexity of the case, some applications may take more than 6 months to process.
The main applicant/ sponsor will be informed of the outcome via email/ post. Meanwhile, your sponsor may check the status of your PR application online through ICA e-Service. New or repeated applications, for the same person(s), will not be accepted while the current application is still in process.

questions.title: What should I choose for the education level for my child's PR application if my child is studying in an international school?
questions.text: You should choose a standard that is of an equivalent level (e.g. Grade 1-6 in international school will be equivalent to primary education without a Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE)/ Primary School Proficiency Examination (PSPE) certificate; Kindergarten and Infant/ Child Care will be equivalent to Preschool).

questions.title: What should I do if I did not receive the outcome of my PR application by post?

questions.title: What should I do if my Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) application is unsuccessful?
questions.text:
All appeals for Singapore Citizenship, Permanent Residence, and Long-Term Visit Pass are carefully considered by ICA. We consider factors such as the applicant's family ties to Singapore Citizens, economic contributions, length of residency in Singapore, ability to contribute to and integrate into Singapore, and commitment to sinking roots.
If you have new or updated information or documents since your last unsuccessful appeal, you can submit a new appeal online via the Appeal for Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long-Term Visit Pass e-Service. You must submit the appeal within 12 months from the date in your application rejection letter.
The outcome of the appeal will remain the same if there are no changes to your circumstances and you submit the same information or documents.

Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Permanent Residence (PR)

questions.title: When can my child submit his/her Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) application as a student?
questions.text:
Foreign students studying in Singapore on a valid immigration pass may submit a Singapore PR application online under the Foreign Student Scheme (FSS) if they have resided in Singapore for more than 2 years at the point of application and have passed at least one national exam or are in the Integrated Programme.
You may refer to the Step-by-Step Guide for more information on application submission.

questions.title: Can I use the Singapore PR In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter to return to Singapore?
questions.text: The possession of a PR IPA letter does not guarantee entry into Singapore. Entry into Singapore is subject to the prevailing entry requirements and the assessment by ICA officers at the checkpoints. You may refer to ICA website for more information about entry requirements.

questions.title: Is my child required to produce his/ her health declaration for the completion of PR formalities?

questions.title: What documents should I bring for the completion of Permanent Residence (PR) formalities?

Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:

Application submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
Please login to ICA e-Service to view the instructions on the completion of formalities.

questions.title: What happens to my current work pass after my Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) application is approved?
questions.text:
If you are holding an Employment Pass (EP), your pass would be cancelled once you have been granted Singapore PR status (i.e. after completion of your PR formalities).
If you have family member(s) who are holding on to Dependant's Pass(es) or Long-Term Visit Pass(es) issued by MOM, do note that their passes will not be auto-cancelled. If they wish to continue residing in Singapore, you will need to apply for an appropriate immigration pass for them. To avoid overstaying, please approach your employer or appointed employment agent to cancel the Dependant's Pass(es) or Long-Term Visit Pass(es) before they expire.

questions.title: What is the purpose of EP152 form?
questions.text: The purpose of the EP152 is for the applicants to confirm they are still working in the same company as declared in their application forms.

questions.title: What should I do if I cannot complete PR formalities within the period stated in my IPA letter?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
The sponsor or applicant may submit a request to extend the validity of the IPA letter via the enquiry form. Please note that extension requests are subject to ICA's consideration.
Applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
The main applicant or sponsor may request for an extension to complete your formalities via ICA e-Service. On your e-Service dashboard, you may click on 'View Details' then click on 'Proceed to Complete Formalities'. Submit your extension request by clicking on 'Request for Extension'. Please note that extension requests are subject to ICA's consideration.

questions.title: What should I do if my employer refuses to sign the EP152 when my PR application has been approved?
questions.text:
If your employer refuses to sign the EP152, ICA is prepared to accept other forms of documentary evidence to verify your employment status:-
Valid work pass (S Pass/ Employment Pass), and
Latest 6 months payslips, and
Letter of employment or Annex A (i.e. Employer's information) dated within 2 weeks from the appointment date with ICA.

questions.title: When can I collect my Identity Card after completion of formalities for Singapore PR application?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
You can make an appointment for IC collection 1 week after the completion of your Singapore PR formalities. The collection of Identity Card is by appointment and the time slot is subject to availability.
Application submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
You can make an appointment for IC collection 1 week after the completion of your Singapore PR formalities. The 'Date of Issue' will be required to make the appointment. You can retrieve the 'Date of Issue' from ICA e-Service after you complete the PR formalities.
Your IC must be collected within 3 months after you complete your Singapore PR formalities.

questions.title: Why do I need to book an appointment online for the completion of Singapore PR formalities?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
You are required to make an appointment for your completion of PR formalities before heading down to ICA Services Centre, so that you will be served promptly if you arrive on-time.
If you arrive without an appointment, ICA may not be able to serve you when our appointments are full.
Applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
Applicants who are required to complete your formalities at ICA Services Centre will be assigned an appointment slot. You can check your appointment date and time on the ICA e-Service.
Should you wish to change your appointment slot, you may do so at the online appointment system.

questions.title: Can PRs still travel with a passport which is expiring in 6 months' time or less?
questions.text:
Generally, as long as a Permanent Resident (PR)’s Re-Entry Permit (REP) remains valid, he/ she is able to use his/ her current valid passport for immigration clearance at the Singapore checkpoints.
A valid REP is necessary to facilitate a Singapore PR’s travel. It will also enable him/ her to retain his/ her PR status while away from Singapore and return as a PR. A PR who remains outside Singapore without a valid REP will lose his/ her PR status.
However, they are advised to be mindful of the immigration requirements of any country they wish to depart from, visit or return to when travelling on a passport with less than 6 months' validity before embarking on their journey. Where applicable, they should also check with the airline to ensure that they are allowed to board the plane as airlines have the prerogative to issue boarding passes to their passengers.
As Singapore’s border measures and entry requirements will evolve as the global situation changes, please visit the MOH website and ICA website for the latest updates on travel and health control measures.
It is important for a Singapore PR to renew his/ her foreign passport if it is expiring. Ensuring that a passport remains valid will allow ICA to determine his/ her foreign citizenship.
For all matters relating to foreign passport, please approach the respective Embassy/ Consulate/ Overseas Mission in Singapore.
Once a new passport is obtained, PRs will need to transfer their valid REPs to their new passports online via the e-Service using their Singpass. Parents of minor PRs, who are Singapore citizen/ PR, may log in to the e-Service with their Singpass.
There is no fee for the transfer of REP. Upon successful transfer, PRs can print their new REPs for reference and travel needs.
For more information on transfer of REP, please visit the ICA’s website.

questions.title: Do Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs) need to serve National Service (NS)?
questions.text:
Under the Enlistment Act 1970, all male Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs) will be scheduled for enlistment upon reaching the age of 18 years. PRs granted under the Professionals/Technical Personnel and Skilled Workers (PTS) Scheme are administratively exempted from National Service (NS).
Male applicants who are granted Singapore PR status as a Foreign Student or under their parents' sponsorship are required to register for NS upon reaching 16½ years old and will be scheduled for enlistment at the earliest opportunity upon reaching 18 years old.
MINDEF allows students to attain educational qualifications up to the 'A' Levels certificate, the polytechnic diploma or an equivalent before they are required to serve NS. They will be enlisted at the earliest opportunity when they have finished such courses, or after turning 18, whichever is later. MINDEF does not grant deferment for university studies, regardless of whether such studies have begun.
Males who are granted Singapore PR, and who were previously SCs or Singapore PRs, are liable to be called up for NS regardless of the scheme under which their Singapore PR status was granted.
For more information on NS liability, please contact:
Central Manpower Base
Email: contact@ns.gov.sg
Contact no: 1800-3676767 (local) or +65 65676767 (overseas)

If the original application was submitted without Singpass, you must submit the appeal using the same email address.
You can submit the appeal via the Appeal for Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long-Term Visit Pass e-Service.

questions.text:
Singapore PR refers to the residency status which allows the person to reside in Singapore permanently. Permanent Residents require a Re-Entry Permit (REP) if they wish to travel out and return to Singapore as a Singapore PR.

questions.text:

questions.title: Who can apply for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) under the Global Investor Programme (GIP)?
questions.text:
Investors who are interested to start a business or invest in Singapore may apply for Singapore PR under the Global Investor Programme (GIP) in Singapore for themselves and their immediate family member(s). They may be eligible to apply if they:
Invest at least S$10 million in a new business entity or expansion of an existing business operation in Singapore; or
Invest S$25 million in a GIP-select fund that invests in Singapore-based companies; or
Establish a Singapore-based Single-Family Office with Assets-Under-Management (AUM) of at least S$200 million.
For more details, please refer to Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) website. You may also contact EDB at:-
Address: 250 North Bridge Road, #28-00 Raffles City Tower, Singapore 179101
Tel: 68326832
Website: http://www.edb.gov.sg

Parents, parents-in-law and children above 21 years old will not be eligible to be sponsored by you under your GIP application. Instead, they can apply for a 5-year Long-Term Visit Pass which is renewable and tied to the validity of your Re-Entry Permit.

questions.title: How do I renounce my Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) status?
questions.text:
Advisory on renunciation of PR
If the main applicant intends to renounce the permanent residence status, all the dependants who obtained the permanent residence status under the sponsorship are also required to renounce together within the same application.
NS-liable Permanent Residents (PRs) are expected to serve National Service (NS).
Renouncing or losing one's PR status without serving or completing full-time NS will have a serious adverse impact on applications to work or study in Singapore, or for any long-term immigration facilities in Singapore, whether now or in the future. Renouncing or losing one’s PR status without serving or completing full-time NS will also adversely affect your family members’ applications for long-term immigration facilities, their ability to sponsor such facilities, their renewal of Re-Entry Permits, or their applications for Singapore citizenship.
If you still wish to proceed with the renunciation of your PR, you may submit the application online.
Please refer to ICA website for further information on the documents required to renounce PR.
Should you decide to renounce your PR status, you are also advised to liaise with your employer and the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) on your CPF matters. You can contact CPFB for further information and assistance.

Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:

questions.title: When can I collect my citizenship certificate after registration?
questions.text: As a new citizen, you are required to attend the citizenship ceremony at the respective Group Representation Constituencies (GRCs) to collect your Singapore citizenship certificate. The ceremony would usually take place in approximately 3 to 6 months after your date of registration. Once the date of ceremony is firmed up, you or your sponsor will receive an email informing the detailed information concerning the ceremony.

questions.title: Can I request to reschedule my citizenship ceremony?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form on the request to reschedule your citizenship ceremony.

questions.title: How do I collect my Singapore citizenship certificate?
questions.text: You will be required to attend the citizenship ceremony to collect your original Singapore citizenship certificate. More details of the citizenship ceremony would be sent to you via email once the details are finalised.

questions.title: How do I know when my citizenship ceremony will be held?
questions.text: Typically, the citizenship ceremony will be held 3 to 6 months after you have registered as a Singapore citizen. You will be provided with further details via email closer to the date of the citizenship ceremony.

questions.title: At what age is a minor eligible for the oath taking?
questions.text: A minor who obtained Singapore citizenship by descent or registration is required to take their Oath of Allegiance, Renunciation, Allegiance and Loyalty (ORAL) when they reach the age of 21 years old and before they turn 22 years old in order to retain the Singapore citizenship.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters / Oath-Taking for Minors

questions.title: Can I renew my Singapore passport if I am in the midst of renouncing my foreign citizenship?
questions.text:
Under the Singapore Constitution, minors who are Singapore citizens by descent or registration must take the Oath of Renunciation, Allegiance and Loyalty (ORAL) upon attaining 21 years of age and before attaining 22 years of age. Minor is required to take the ORAL on or after 21st birthday date and no later than 22nd birthday.
Once the minor has completed his/ her oath taking formalities, he/ she may apply for Singapore passport. Nonetheless, should the minor require to extend the validity of his/ her Singapore Passport before taking the Oath, and in need to travel, he/ she may apply for a new passport with a validity 1 day before his/ her 22nd birthday. The passport can only be extended to its full 10-year after the minor has taken the ORAL.
You may contact us via the enquiry form if you require further clarifications on passport renewal.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters / Oath-Taking for Minors

questions.title: Do I need to book an appointment date for the oath-taking?

Please ensure you have the required documents to complete your Oath of Renunciation, Allegiance and Loyalty (ORAL).

questions.title: For my overseas born child, what happens to his/her Singapore citizenship on turning 21?
questions.text:
The Constitution of The Republic of Singapore states that minors who acquired Singapore citizenship by descent or registration must take the Oath of Renunciation, Allegiance and Loyalty (ORAL) within 12 months of attaining the age of 21 years to remain as a Singapore citizen.
They are required to divest themselves of any foreign citizenship before they can take the ORAL. Those who fail to take the ORAL will lose their Singapore citizenship on attaining the age of 22 years, with no assurance of their immigration facilities in Singapore.
ICA will send letters reminding minors of their ORAL only after they attain the age of 21 years. For minors residing overseas, they may take the ORAL at the nearest Singapore Mission, or with the prior permission of the Registrar, take the ORAL before any notary public or person authorised to administer oaths. Persons taking the ORAL should present the following documents for processing:
a) Certificate of Singapore citizenship (original);
b) Singapore National Registration Identification Card / Singapore International Passport (original);
c) Documentary evidence of having divested oneself of any foreign citizenship(s) (original and photocopy).
You may check with the relevant foreign authority on the renunciation procedures for your foreign citizenship.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters / Oath-Taking for Minors

questions.title: How many person(s) is/are allowed in the oath-taking room?
questions.text: Only the person taking the Oath of Renunciation Allegiance and Loyalty will need to be present in the Oath-Taking room.

questions.title: What attire should I wear for the oath-taking?
questions.text: As taking the Oath of Renunciation, Allegiance and Loyalty (ORAL) is a solemn occasion, you are required to be suitably attired. There should strictly be no casual wear such as T-shirts, shorts, slippers, mini skirts and jeans for oath-taking.

questions.title: Can I change the location of my/ my child's citizenship registration to Singapore embassy overseas?
questions.text: All adults and children age 15 and above are required to register for Singapore citizenship in person at ICA Services Centre. Children aged below 15 born overseas to Singapore citizen parents may request for collection of the Singapore citizenship certificate at a Singapore mission overseas.

questions.title: Can I provide my cancelled foreign passport as a proof of my foreign citizenship renunciation?
questions.text: The cancelled foreign passport is not a proof that a person has renounced their foreign citizenship. An official letter indicating cancellation of citizenship is required as proof of renunciation.

questions.title: Can we proceed to register Singapore citizenship for the other family members without the main applicant?
questions.text: You will not be able to register for Singapore citizenship without the main applicant as you are required to register as a family unit.

questions.title: Do I need to complete my foreign citizenship renunciation before Singapore citizenship registration or citizenship completion of formalities?
questions.text: Successful Singapore citizenship applicants above 21 years old are required to renounce their foreign citizenship with the respective foreign authorities with the approval letter issued by ICA. After receiving the foreign renunciation document, they may proceed to ICA Services Centre to complete the Singapore citizenship registration formalities.

questions.title: Do I need to sell my overseas properties after I have become a Singapore citizen?
questions.text: We wish to clarify that ICA's role is mainly to process and grant Singapore citizenship status to eligible applicants. You are advised to seek clarification from the relevant foreign authorities regarding your overseas properties.

questions.title: How can I obtain the final notification letter?
questions.text: Please be informed that there will be no hardcopy letters mailed to your residential address. You may download and print the PDF final notification letter from ICA e-Service.

questions.title: How do I renounce my foreign citizenship in order to register for Singapore citizenship?
questions.text: Please approach the foreign embassy of your foreign nationality/citizenship to enquire on the procedures for renunciation.

questions.title: How do I retrieve the date I was granted Singapore Citizenship?
questions.text: The date on your Singapore citizenship certificate reflects the date you were granted Singapore Citizenship.

questions.title: How do I submit my foreign renunciation documents?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
Please login to ICA e-Service with your Singpass, select "upload additional documents" within the e-Service for citizenship application to upload a copy of your foreign citizenship renunciation letter.
Applications submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
You may log in to ICA e-Service to upload a copy of your foreign citizenship renunciation letter.
If you face difficulties in uploading the documents, you may contact us via the enquiry form with a copy of your foreign renunciation letter for assistance.

questions.title: What am I required to submit for the final renunciation documents?
questions.text:
An official letter from the foreign authority indicating that you have ceased/ renounced your foreign citizenship or are no longer considered a citizen of that country are examples of acceptable final renunciation documents.
You may contact us via the enquiry form for further clarifications.

questions.title: What documents do I need to bring on my appointment for Singapore citizenship registration?
questions.text:
Applications submitted before 26 June 2024:
The details and documents required for the citizenship registration will be stated in the notification letter. You can log in to MyICA using the sponsor or main applicant's Singpass to retrieve and download the notification letter.
Application submitted on or after 26 June 2024:
Please log in to ICA e-Service using the sponsor or main applicant's Singpass to view the final instructions on completing your citizenship registration.

questions.title: What should I do if I have difficulties to renounce my foreign citizenship?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form with documentary proof issued by the foreign embassy for our consideration if it is acceptable for the Singapore citizenship registration.

questions.title: What should I do with my foreign passports after I complete the Singapore citizenship registration?
questions.text: You may approach the foreign embassy to surrender the foreign passport(s).

questions.title: Who is required to be present during my child's Singapore citizenship registration?
questions.text: Children aged 14 years old and below need not attend the citizenship registration at ICA Services Centre. Their citizenship registration will be completed in absentia by their sponsoring parent on the appointment date. Children aged 15 years and above are required to be present accompanied by the main sponsor.

questions.title: Who should I contact regarding my renunciation of foreign nationality?
questions.text: You may approach the Embassy of your foreign nationality/ citizenship to enquire on the procedures for renunciation.

questions.title: Will my children become Singapore citizens automatically If I am registered as a Singapore citizen?
questions.text: Your children will not automatically be granted Singapore citizenship. If your children are below 21 years of age, you can sponsor their citizenship application if you meet the eligibility criteria.

questions.title: What is the e-Service for Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text:
The e-Service for REP allows Singapore permanent residents (PR) in Singapore or overseas, to apply online for a REP or transfer the remaining validity of their REP from an old passport to a new passport. You can also do the following services:
Allow a Singapore citizen (SC) or PR to submit applications for REP renewal for his/ her spouse and children below 21 years of age
Allow PR to apply for transfer of REP for self
Allow SC or PR to apply for transfer of REPs for child below 21 years of age
Check REP application status
Enquire REP details and,
Reprint REP
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Who can I contact on technical or payment matters for Re-Entry Permit (REP) renewal application?
questions.text: Please do a screenshot of the error together with the problems encountered and submit to ICA via the enquiry form for assistance.

questions.title: Who can I contact to check on the outcome of my REP renewal application?
questions.text: You will receive the outcome of your REP renewal application via your declared email to us. You may also check the outcome using our e-Service under 'Enquire Application Status'. We seek your understanding that some applications may take a longer time to process.

questions.title: Would my spouse’s PR be cancelled if I convert to a Singapore Citizen from a Permanent Resident?
questions.text: Your spouse will remain a PR under your sponsorship if you become a Singapore citizen.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: How do I apply for a Certificate of Identity?
questions.text:
For application of Certificate of Identity, you are required to complete and submit the Certificate of Identity Form at ICA Services Centre in person.
You may walk in to the ICA Services Centre during our operating hours.
Please approach the Information Counter at Level 1 to obtain a queue ticket from our service ambassador.

questions.title: How long does it take to apply for a Certificate of Identity?
questions.text: The general processing time for a Certificate of Identity (COI) application is within 3 working days (excluding the day of submission). However, some applications may take longer to process. Please refer to ICA website for more information.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Certificate of Identity

questions.title: What is a Certificate of Identity (COI)?
questions.text: A Certificate of Identity (COI), is a travel document issued to Singapore permanent residents who are stateless to facilitate their travels abroad.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Certificate of Identity

questions.title: Why is my Re-Entry Permit (REP) application withdrawn?
questions.text:
Your online REP application has been withdrawn due to one of the following reasons:
1) You did not respond to our document request within the stipulated time, or
2) You did not make payment within 14 days from the date of the approval of your application.
If you are outside Singapore without a valid REP, you have to apply for an REP within 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP to retain your PR status.
The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis. If you had applied for a new REP within the 180-day period, you will remain a PR until there is an outcome to your REP application. If your REP application is unsuccessful, you will lose your PR status the day after the REP application outcome is sent to you.
You will also lose your PR status automatically if you do not apply for a new REP within this 180-day period.
If your REP application is withdrawn and is within the 180-day period, you may wish to submit a fresh REP application for our consideration.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Are my children eligible to use automated lanes after I renewed the Re-Entry Permit (REP) online?
questions.text:
Children between 6 - 15 years old
Children between 6 - 15 years of age who have not registered for Identity Cards but are holding machine-readable passports may choose to register their fingerprints with ICA to use the automated lanes. Your child can approach the manned immigration counters at our checkpoints to enrol his/her thumbprints when departing or entering Singapore. The officer will advise you on the enrolment procedure.
Children aged 15 and above
Children aged 15 and above who are Singapore PRs and have registered for their blue Identity Cards while holding onto machine-readable passports are eligible to use the automated lanes.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) become another country's PR?
questions.text: There is no restriction of Singapore PR taking up permanent residency of another country.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I access the e-Service to reprint my Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text: You can access the "Download REP/EP and Enquire REP Validity" function on the e-Service to reprint your Re-Entry Permit (REP). There is no charge for the reprint of an REP.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I change my permanent residency sponsor?
questions.text:
You cannot directly change the sponsor for your existing permanent residency.
To change sponsors, you must first renounce your current permanent residency and submit a new application under your new sponsor.
ICA will assess the new application based on current eligibility criteria. All applications are subject to approval.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I enter as a PR if my Re-Entry Permit is tagged to my old passport instead of my new passport?
questions.text: You may enter as a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) if your Re-Entry Permit (REP) is still valid. You will need to use your Singpass to access the ICA e-Service and transfer the remaining validity of your valid REP from the old to the new passport. Otherwise, you may be inconvenienced each time you travel in and out of Singapore.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: I am a Permanent Resident (PR) whose Re-Entry Permit (REP) has expired. Can I enter Singapore?
questions.text:
You will remain a PR during the prescribed period of 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP. You may be allowed entry into Singapore, subject to prevailing entry and public health requirements.
You are advised to apply for a new REP within this 180-day period to avoid losing your PR status, subject to approval on a case-by-case basis.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Do I need to carry my Entry/ Re-Entry Permit when travelling?
questions.text: You may wish to check the entry requirements of the country/ place you intend to visit on the documents required to facilitate your travel.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Do I need to re-register my IC if I am applying for Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text: You need not re-register your blue identity card when you renew your REP.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Does the Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) status expires?
questions.text:
The Singapore PR status will not expire. However, a valid Re-Entry Permit (REP) is needed each time a Singapore PR travels abroad. The REP allows you to retain your Singapore PR status while you are outside of Singapore.
If you are outside Singapore without a valid REP, you have to apply for an REP within 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP to retain your PR status.
The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis. If you had applied for a new REP within the 180-day period, you will remain a PR until there is an outcome to your REP application. If your REP application is unsuccessful, you will lose your PR status the day after the REP application outcome is sent to you.
You will also lose your PR status automatically if you do not apply for a new REP within this 180-day period.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: How can I obtain a letter to state that I am no longer a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR)?
questions.text:
Eligible* applicants can submit an online request for a verification letter.
Please note:
(i) You are not required to obtain a verification letter for the closure of CPF account/ withdrawal of CPF funds.
(ii) For existing PRs, a verification letter will only be issued on a case-by-case basis. You may produce your Entry Permit and/or valid REP to verify your Singapore PR status.
*If you have already lost your PR status by remaining outside Singapore without a valid Re-Entry Permit (REP), or previously renounced PR status.
You may surrender your cancelled Singapore Blue NRIC to an ICA Officer at ICA Services Centre if you are in Singapore, or a diplomatic/ consular officer at the Singapore Overseas Mission nearest to you if you are overseas.
Alternatively, you may send the identity card to us by registered mail. If you choose to do so, please send the mail to:
IC unit, Level 2
ICA Services Centre
2 Crawford Street,
Singapore 207218

questions.text:
You will have lost your PR status if your REP application is unsuccessful.
You will need to submit a new application for PR to be considered for PR again.

questions.title: How do I get back my Permanent Residence (PR) status if I had previously renounced PR?
questions.text: There is no provision to reinstate the PR status of those who have renounced their status voluntarily. If you are interested to become a Singapore PR again, you may submit a fresh application to us for consideration if you meet the prevailing application criteria for PR.

questions.title: How do I obtain a letter for verification of Permanent Residence (PR) issue date?
questions.text: You can access the “Download Verification Letter” function on the e-Service to download your Verification Letter. There is no charge for the reprint of a Verification Letter.

questions.title: Is it possible to change my Permanent Residence (PR) status to a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)?
questions.text: You will need to renounce your PR status before you submit a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) application for ICA's consideration. You may refer to the ICA website on the eligibility to apply for a LTVP.

questions.title: May I have a confirmation of my Singapore Permanent Residence status in Chinese?

questions.title: My Re-Entry Permit (REP) was renewed for one year only. Can I request for a longer duration of Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text: All REP renewal applications are being carefully assessed, taking into consideration all relevant factors, before a decision is made. If there are fresh facts and circumstances to support your request for a longer REP validity, you may furnish them to us for consideration at your next REP renewal.

questions.title: What happens if I lose my passport which is tied to the valid Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text: If you lose your passport in Singapore or overseas, you must report the loss of your passport to your Embassy/High Commission immediately and apply for a new passport. After you have obtained a new passport, you can use the 'transfer function' at the e-Service to transfer the remaining validity of your existing REP to the new passport. Upon successful transfer, you will be able to print your REP which will reflect your new passport details.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What is an Entry Permit (EP) and a Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text:
The EP allows PRs to enter Singapore once, and to remain in Singapore. It is issued when PR status is first granted.
The REP is issued for a fixed validity period, upon application, for PRs to re-enter Singapore if they travel abroad.
Having a valid REP whilst abroad is an indication by the PR that he/she intends to return to Singapore. PRs are required to display a commitment to continue contributing to Singapore, in order to be issued an REP.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What is my Permanent Residence (PR) cessation date?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form on your enquiry.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What is required to maintain Permanent Residence (PR) status?
questions.text:
A valid Re-Entry Permit (REP) is needed each time a Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) travels abroad. The REP allows a Singapore PR to retain his/ her PR status while he/ she is outside Singapore. If the Singapore PR leaves Singapore or remains overseas without a valid REP, he/ she will lose his/ her Singapore PR status.
If you are physically outside Singapore without a valid REP, you have a prescribed period of 180 days to apply for an REP to retain your PR status. The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis. If you had applied for a new REP within the prescribed period, you will remain a PR until ICA has decided on the outcome of the application.
You will automatically lose PR status if you do not apply for a new REP within this 180-day period, on the day after the last day of the prescribed period. You will also lose PR status the day after the REP application rejection, even if you had submitted the REP application within the prescribed period.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What is the validity period of a Re-Entry Permit (REP)?
questions.text: All REPs are issued up to a maximum validity of 5 years.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What should I do if I lose my Entry Permit?
questions.text: The Entry Permit (EP) is available for printing via ICA e-Service. You may print a copy of your EP using the ICA e-Service.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What should I do if my application to renew Re-Entry Permit (REP) is pending still and my REP is expiring?
questions.text: You may enquire the outcome of your REP application with Singpass login.

questions.title: What will happen if my Re-Entry Permit (REP) is expiring and my passport has not been renewed?
questions.text:
If your passport is expiring and you are in Singapore, you can continue to reside in Singapore as a permanent resident (PR). It is advisable for you to obtain a new passport as soon as possible and thereafter apply to renew your re-entry permit (REP) or transfer your valid REP online. Please note that a passport must have at least 3 months validity in order to make an REP application online via the e-Service. You may submit your REP application after you have received your new passport.
If you are outside Singapore and your passport and re-entry permit (REP) is expiring, it is advisable for you to obtain a new passport and thereafter apply to renew REP online as soon as possible. Please note that a passport must have at least 3 months validity in order to make an REP application online via the e-Service. If your REP has expired, you have to apply for an REP within 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP to retain your PR status. The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: When will the validity of my newly issued Re-Entry Permit (REP) commence from?
questions.text: Your new REP validity period will commence from the date of issue.
