questions.title: Who can I contact to enquire on Re-Entry Permit (REP) matters?
questions.text: You may contact us via the enquiry form for assistance. You may also refer to ICA FAQs for more information.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Will an expired passport affect my Permanent Residence (PR) status?
questions.text:
If you are in Singapore and your passport has expired, you can continue to reside in Singapore as a permanent resident (PR), but you will not be able to travel. Hence, it is advisable for you to obtain a new passport and thereafter apply to renew your re-entry permit (REP) as soon as possible or transfer your valid REP online. Please note that a passport must have at least 3 months validity in order to make an REP application online via the e-Service. If you are outside Singapore without a valid REP, you have to apply for an REP within 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP to retain your PR status.
The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis. If you had applied for a new REP within the 180-day period, you will remain a PR until there is an outcome to your REP application. If your REP application is unsuccessful, you will lose your PR status the day after the REP application outcome is sent to you.
You will also lose your PR status automatically if you do not apply for a new REP within this 180-day period.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Will I have a REP endorsement in my passport if I apply for or transfer my REP online?
questions.text: With online applications and submissions, ICA has ceased to issue REP endorsements. If you have successfully applied for, or transferred your REP using the e-Service, you can proceed to print a copy of the REP for your reference and travel needs.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Will my Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) status be removed if I resign from my current job?
questions.text: Your existing Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) status will not be affected by your resignation. However, ICA takes into consideration the circumstances of each Singapore PR when deciding on the renewal of the Re-Entry Permit (REP), and these circumstances may include whether the Singapore PR is gainfully employed and still contributing to Singapore.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Will my Permanent Residence (PR) status be revoked if I am sentenced to prison?
questions.text:
Foreigners, including Singapore Permanent Residents, who break the law or engage in undesirable conduct may have their permanent residency revoked and be prohibited from re-entry into Singapore.
If you are sentenced to prison, ICA will review your permanent residency. We consider various factors, including the nature and severity of the offence, your family roots in Singapore, and your contributions to Singapore. We will contact you directly regarding the review.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I apply a Re-Entry Permit (REP) on behalf of my spouse and children?
questions.text: Singapore citizens or permanent residents who are Singpass holders can use the e-Service to submit REP applications on behalf of their spouse and children below 21 years of age.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Can I complete the Re-Entry Permit (REP) formalities online if I am overseas?
questions.text:
If you have successfully applied for a REP online whilst overseas, you may complete the entire REP renewal formalities online, which include payment for the REP using your credit/debit/Amex card, or Internet banking (DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB and Standard Chartered Bank banking account in Singapore) and printing the REP.
There may be instances where you would be required to return to Singapore to complete formalities for your REP at the ICA Services Centre depending on the circumstances of your case.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: How can I renew my Re-Entry Permit (REP) if my REP has expired and I am in Singapore?
questions.text: Please log in to the e-Service to apply for an REP. You are advised to obtain a new REP or to renew your expiring REP in a timely manner before travelling out of Singapore.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Can I renew my REP if my spouse, who has sponsored me for PR, has passed on?
questions.text: You may submit an application for the renewal of your Re-Entry Permit (REP) via ICA e-Service within 3 months from the expiry of your current REP. Please declare your marital status as "widow" in the application. As your spouse had passed away, your renewal of REP will be assessed on your own merits.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Can I use the e-Service to apply for a REP while I am overseas?
questions.text:
You can login to the e-Service using your Singpass to renew or transfer your Re-Entry Permit (REP).
If you are overseas and do not have a Singpass, you may apply for your REP at the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Do I need to submit any supporting documents if I am applying online for an REP?
questions.text: For REP renewal, you are not required to submit supporting documents unless you have received a letter or email from ICA requesting for such documents to be submitted to support your application.

questions.title: How can I renew my Re-Entry Permit (REP) if I am residing/working overseas?
questions.text:
Applicants with a valid Singpass account can submit your applications for REP facilities using ICA e-Service while overseas.
If you do not have a Singpass account, you can submit your application through our Singapore Missions overseas. Please note that overseas application must be submitted at least two months before the expiry of the current REP.

questions.title: How do I apply for or renew my Re-Entry Permit (REP)?

All Singapore permanent residents can login to the e-Service using your Singpass for Re-Entry Permit (REP) renewal or REP transfer.
If you are overseas and do not have a Singpass, you may apply for your REP at the nearest Singapore Overseas Mission.

questions.title: How do I know my Re-Entry Permit (REP) application has been approved if I submitted online?

questions.title: What do I need to prepare for the renewal of my Re-Entry Permit (REP) application?
questions.text:
You should have the following before using the e-Service:
A Singpass account
A valid travel document
Name and address of your current employer (if any); and
Visa or MasterCard Credit/ Debit Card; American Express (AMEX) card; Internet banking (DBS/ POSB, OCBC, UOB and Standard Chartered Bank banking account in Singapore), or PayNow.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: What should I do if I am unable to make payment for my Re-Entry Permit (REP) online?
questions.text:
You can check the validity of your Credit/ Debit/ AMEX card or Internet Banking account with the respective issuing authority or you can try using another payment mode:
VISA card; or
MasterCard Credit/ Debit card;
American Express (AMEX) card;
Internet banking (DBS/ POSB, OCBC, UOB and Standard Chartered Bank banking account in Singapore); or
PayNow.
You can retrieve your approved REP record from the "Check Application Status" function in e-Service to pay the fee within 14 days from the date of approval of the REP.
Please refer to ICA website for more information on payment-related enquiries.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: When will I be able to renew my Re-Entry Permit (REP) before the expiry date?
questions.text:
You can renew your Re-Entry Permit (REP) using ICA e-Service with your Singpass within 3 months of its expiry date.
If you need to renew your REP earlier due to personal circumstances, please submit your application at ICA in person, together with the supporting documents/ reasons for early REP renewal.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I apply for Re-Entry Permit (REP) transfer on behalf of my spouse?
questions.text: A Singapore citizen or PR sponsor cannot perform the transfer of REP for his/ her sponsored spouse. The PR spouse will have to personally log in to ICA e-Service with his/ her Singpass to declare and transfer his/ her REP.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: Can I apply or transfer my Re-Entry Permit at ICA Services Centre without making an appointment?
questions.text:
ICA does not accept applications for Re-Entry Permit (REP) over the counter. If your REP has expired, you may use the e-Service to apply for REP.
If you have a valid REP, you must renew it using the e-Service within 3 months of its expiry date.
For transfer of REP, it must be submitted using the e-Service as well.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Can I transfer my existing REP to my new passport with the new nationality/ citizenship acquired?
questions.text:
If you have acquired a new nationality, you will have to update the details of your new nationality/ citizenship in your Identity Card (IC) using ICA e-Service before submitting a REP application. Thereafter, you can book an appointment to collect your IC.
To submit a REP application with the new nationality, you are required to bring your supporting documents in person to ICA Services Centre.
Please approach the information counter at Level 1 during operating hours to obtain a queue ticket from our service ambassador.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Can I transfer my REP between two different passports as I am a PR with dual citizenship?
questions.text:
If you have dual nationalities, you are not allowed to transfer your Re-Entry Permit (REP) from one country's travel document to that of another country.
You will need to apply for separate REPs, each for the respective country's travel documents you are currently holding, if you intend to use them for travelling.
For first-time application, you are required to come down to ICA Services Centre in person, together with your blue NRIC and travel documents. A $10 fee is payable for every year, or part thereof, of each REP issued.
All subsequent REP renewal applications can be submitted online using the e-Service.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Apply for/ Renew/ Transfer Re-Entry Permit (REP)

questions.title: Do I have to pay a fee for Re-Entry Permit (REP) transfer?
questions.text:
You can access the e-Service and perform a REP transfer from your old passport to new passport so long as your REP is still valid and you have a Singpass account. Upon successful transfer, you can print your new REP for your reference and travel needs.
There is no fee payable for transfer of REP. This service is free of charge. However, please double check your passport numbers when updating using the transfer function to avoid inconvenience at the borders during immigration clearance.

Applicants without a Singpass account can submit an application for transfer of REP at Singapore Missions overseas.

questions.title: How much cash or CBNI can I bring in to or out of Singapore?

questions.text: A travel document is an identity document (i.e. passport, document of identity) authorised by a government or international treaty organisation to facilitate the movement of individuals across borders.

questions.title: Can I amend or re-submit my extension of short-term visit pass application if I have submitted the wrong information?

questions.title: Who can file for a divorce in Singapore?
questions.text:
To be eligible to apply for a divorce in Singapore, you or your spouse must be a Singaporean citizen or have been living in Singapore for the past 3 years. You should have been married for at least 3 years from the date of registration of the marriage.
If you were married under civil law, you should apply for a divorce in the Family Courts.
If you were married under Syariah Law, you should file for divorce in Syariah Courts.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/understand-requirements-getting-divorce#divorce-eligibility and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How do I file for a divorce in Singapore in the Family Justice Courts?
questions.text:
If you are represented by a lawyer, your lawyer will file the divorce application on your behalf.
If you are representing yourself, and you and your spouse agree on the divorce (i.e. the terms of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage) and the ancillary matters, you can choose to file the divorce application using the Divorce eService. The Divorce eService can be accessed at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/divorce-eservice.
If you are representing yourself, and you and your spouse agree on the divorce (i.e. the terms of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage), but not the ancillary matters, you may choose to file the divorce application on the simplified track. You can read more about filing the divorce application on the simplified track at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/how-to-file-matrimonial-application-divorce-simplified-track.
If you and your spouse are unable to reach an agreement on the divorce (i.e. the terms of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage), the application will be filed on the normal track. You can read more about filing the application on the normal track at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-matrimonial-application-divorce-normal-track.
You will need to prepare the necessary documents and go down to any one of the SG Court Service Bureaus to file the documents.
For more information on the divorce process and the documents to be prepared, you may refer to the FJC’s brochure at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/docs/default-source/family-docs/divorce_guide_english.pdf.
The SG Courts Service Bureaus are located at the following locations, and you may go to either one to file the documents for your matters, regardless of which court your case is being heard in:

questions.title: What are the grounds for divorce in Singapore?
questions.text:
Parties will be granted a divorce only if the court finds that the marriage has irretrievably broken down. If you intend to file the divorce application, you must show the court that you are relying on one or more of these facts to prove that your marriage has broken down irretrievably:
adultery
unreasonable behavior
desertion for at least 2 years
3 years' separation with spouse's consent
4 years' separation
mutual agreement
You may wish to read more about this at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/understand-requirements-getting-divorce

questions.title: What is considered "unreasonable behavior" in a divorce case?
questions.text:
Unreasonable behaviour refers to the behaviour by one spouse that makes it unreasonable to expect the other spouse to continue living together.
Each case depends on its own facts. It would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.
You may wish to read more about this at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/understand-requirements-getting-divorce and https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/judgments/FJC-case-highlights/CaseHighlightSubjectAreas/divorce---facts.

questions.title: In a divorce, what is child custody and how will it be determined?
questions.text:
To have custody of the child means that that person will have authority in making major decisions regarding the child. Some of these decisions include matters concerning education, religion and healthcare.
In deciding the custody, the Court will place paramount consideration on the welfare of the child.
The child's welfare should be understood broadly. It is not only measured in terms of money or material comfort, but also in terms of the child's moral, religious and physical well-being along with his/her ties of affection. Where necessary, the judge may ask for social service reports or counselling sessions to assess the child's and parents' state and the type of custody order suited for them.
Sole Custody means that one parent will be the sole decision-maker for major decisions concerning the child.
Joint Custody means that both parents are the decision makers for major decisions concerning the child. Hence, both parents should communicate with one another and reach a consensus when making decisions.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: In a divorce, how is care and control determined?
questions.text:
In determining care and control, the court’s paramount consideration will be the welfare of the child.
The parent with care and control will live with the child and make decisions on the child’s day-to-day life. The other parent not given care and control may be granted access to the child.
You may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/judgments/FJC-case-highlights and search "care and control" to find out more.

questions.title: What are the options for child maintenance after divorce?
questions.text:
Some examples of child maintenance orders include:
Fixed periodic payments e.g., every month
One time lump-sum payment
Reimbursement of expenses, either in full or in part.
Direct payment of expenses to a service provider (such as a childcare centre)
In determining the quantum for child maintenance, the Women's Charter provides that the Court can consider factors such as the financial needs of the child, the respective parents' ability to provide and the standard of living enjoyed by the child.
Ultimately, each case depends on its own facts. It would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: How is spousal maintenance determined?
questions.text:
In determining the quantum for maintenance, the Women's Charter provides that the Court can consider factors such as the income of each party, the length of the marriage and the standard of living the family had prior to the divorce.
Some examples of spousal maintenance orders include:
A nominal sum
Fixed periodic payments, e.g., every month
One-time lump-sum payment
Ultimately, each case depends on its own facts, and it would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: What happens to our HDB flat after divorce?
questions.text:
Some possibilities include:
Termination of the Agreement for Lease with HDB
Surrendering the flat back to HDB
Selling or transferring the share to one spouse
Selling the flat in the open market
You may wish to contact HDB on your options regarding the flat and possible accommodation before, during and after your divorce.
Ultimately, each case depends on its own facts, and it would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: How are assets divided in a divorce?
questions.text:
If you reach an agreement with your spouse on how the assets are to be divided, the agreed terms can be presented to the Family Court for the court's approval and consideration.
If an agreement cannot be reached, the court will determine how the matrimonial assets should be divided. The Women’s Charter provides that the court can consider factors such as the contribution of the parties.
Ultimately, each case depends on its own facts, and it would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.
You may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/judgments/FJC-case-highlights/CaseHighlightSubjectAreas/ancillary-matters-upon-dissolution-of-marriage-under-part-x-women-s-charter for more information.

questions.title: Who bears the costs of divorce proceedings?
questions.text: The costs can be borne by one party, shared between both parties, or each party bears their own costs.

questions.title: Is counselling available during the divorce process?
questions.text:
Couples with at least one child below 21 years of age are required to attend counselling after they file for divorce. The counselling sessions will be conducted by a Court Family Specialist from the Family Justice Courts.
The counselling sessions seek to assist parties with co-parenting of their children. The children may be invited to attend the counselling sessions, where appropriate.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: Where can I get legal advice for my divorce?
questions.text:
The courts are not able to provide legal advice. Legal advice is when you are provided specific information about your legal matter and guidance on the legal options available to you.
Refer to the following to find out about the legal resources, legal assistance schemes and programmes you can apply for.
Engage a lawyer
The Legal Service Regulatory Authority (LSRA) offers an online directory of the names, addresses and other useful information of all practising lawyers in Singapore. You can also Find a Lawyer based on the area of law provided by the Law Society.
You may also approach any of the following organisations for legal advice:
Legal Aid Bureau.
Legal advice service (People's Association).
Pro Bono SG

questions.title: What if I need help with the court process in a divorce?
questions.text:
Your rights in a family case
You have the right to obtain legal advice, seek legal assistance or engage a lawyer to represent you in court at your court proceedings for a family case.
You may wish to find out:
(If you are representing yourself in court) Your rights and responsibilities.
What is a family case.
The courts are not able to provide legal advice. Legal advice is when you are provided with specific information about your legal matter and guidance on the legal options available to you.
Refer to the following to find out about the legal resources, legal assistance schemes and programmes you can apply for.
Engage a lawyer
The Legal Service Regulatory Authority (LSRA) offers an online directory of the names, addresses and other useful information of all practising lawyers in Singapore. You can also Find a Lawyer based on the area of law provided by the Law Society.
If you are in need of a lawyer but unable to afford one, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/legal-help-support/family-case to understand about the legal assistance schemes relevant to your case.

questions.title: What is the Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme?
questions.text:
From 1 July 2024, all couples with at least one child below 21 years of age will be required to complete the Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme (CPP) before filing for divorce.
Under the CPP, parents receive support from counsellors to help them make informed decisions that prioritises the well-being of their children, such as working out co-parenting arrangements arising from a divorce.
You can find out more about the CPP here: https://familyassist.msf.gov.sg/content/proceeding-with-divorce/divorce-proceedings/mandatory-co-parenting-programme-cpp/cpp-in-english/

questions.title: How long do I have to be separated before filing for divorce?
questions.text:
If you rely on the fact of separation, you will need to be separated for a period of 3 years (if your spouse consents to the divorce), or 4 years (if there is no consent to the divorce).
If you rely on desertion, you will need to show that your spouse has deserted you for a continuous period of 2 years before filing for divorce.
However, if you are filing for divorce under adultery, unreasonable behavior or mutual agreement, there is no period of separation required before you can file for divorce.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: What evidence is required for proving adultery in a divorce?
questions.text:
You can file for a divorce based on the fact of adultery if your spouse has cheated on you by having sexual relations with someone who is not you, and you find it intolerable to live with your spouse.
Evidence of the act (or intention of) including videos, photographs, SMS/email exchanges, reports from a private investigator can be produced to prove adultery.
Ultimately, each case depends on its own facts, and it would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the best course of action in your circumstances.

questions.title: Can I file for divorce under Muslim Law in Singapore?
questions.text: Yes, the divorce will be filed with the Syariah Court. Please visit https://www.syariahcourt.gov.sg/ for more information.

questions.title: What is meant by 'Desertion' when I use it to prove that my marriage has irretrievably broken down?
questions.text:
Desertion refers to your spouse leaving you against your wishes and completely rejecting the marital relationship for at least 2 years.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: Can I rely on separation to file for divorce if my spouse and I are still living in the same house?
questions.text: Yes, separation can be relied on if you and your spouse maintain separate households and no longer perform spousal duties.

questions.title: What is the process for a simplified divorce?
questions.text: You can read more on the court process for a simplified divorce at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-matrimonial-application-divorce-simplified-track

questions.title: How is 'access' to the child/children determined?
questions.text:
The parent without care and control of the child (i.e., the parent that does not live with the child) may be granted access to the child.
Parents can discuss and agree on the amount of time that the child spends with the access parent. Access periods can be managed in terms of weekdays, weekends, school holidays, religious occasions, public holidays, and birthdays.
If parents are unable to come to an agreement, the court will decide on the access that should be granted. In making the access order, the court’s paramount consideration will be the welfare of the child.
It would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.

questions.title: What are Ancillary Matters in a divorce?
questions.text:
Ancillary Matters are issues such as children’s care arrangements (custody, care and control and access), maintenance for spouse and/or children, division of matrimonial assets, and costs of the proceedings.
For more information, you may refer to Divorce in Singapore: the essentials (PDF, 519 KB).

questions.title: How long do I have to be married before I can file for divorce?
questions.text:
You must have been married for at least 3 years from the date of registration of the marriage unless it can be proven that you have suffered exceptional hardship, or your spouse has been exceptionally unreasonable and cruel.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/understand-requirements-getting-divorce.

questions.title: What if I cannot afford a lawyer for my divorce but need legal representation?
questions.text: If you need a lawyer to represent you but you cannot afford one, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/legal-help-support/family-case to understand about the legal assistance schemes relevant to you.

questions.title: Should I file my divorce on the normal track or the simplified track?
questions.text:
If you and your spouse are able to agree on the divorce (i.e. the reasons for the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage), the divorce application should be filed on the simplified track. This applies even if you do not have an agreement on the Ancillary Matters.
If you and your spouse are unable to agree on the divorce (i.e. the reasons for the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage), the divorce application should be filed on the normal track.
Ancillary Matters are issues such as children’s care arrangements (custody, care and control and access), maintenance for spouse and/or children, division of matrimonial assets, and costs of the proceedings.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/divorce.

questions.title: Must I engage a lawyer for my divorce application?
questions.text:
There is no legal requirement that a lawyer must represent you in your divorce application. However, depending on the complexity of your case, you may choose to engage one if you need independent legal advice on the merits of your case.
You may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/divorce for more information, or https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/legal-help-support if you require legal help or support.

questions.title: What should I do if I receive a matrimonial application for divorce from my spouse?
questions.text:
If you have been served with a matrimonial application for divorce, it means that your spouse has started divorce proceedings against you.
For more information on how you can respond to a divorce application, please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/respond-matrimonial-application-divorce-normal-track.

questions.title: How do I apply to change the court date for my divorce case?
questions.text:
If you are representing yourself in a divorce matter heard in the FJC, you can apply to change your hearing date in one of the following ways:
Via eLitigation any of the SG Courts Service Bureau
Via email to fjc_family_registry@judiciary.gov.sg
In writing to the FJC Registry
You should seek the consent of the other party or parties to the matter before adjourning or vacating a hearing. If the other party or parties consent to your request, you will have to attach a letter to your request stating that all parties have consented to your request to adjourn or vacate the hearing.
If the consent of one or more of the other parties is not obtained, the letter should state the reasons for the other parties' objections or explain why their consent could not be obtained.
The court will notify you of the outcome of your application to adjourn or vacate the hearing. If your application is accepted, a new hearing date will be scheduled. If your application is not accepted or if you do not receive a response on the outcome of your application, you must attend court on the date as originally scheduled.

questions.title: How do I request a Certified True Copy of the Divorce Order?
questions.text:
Authentic Court Orders
If your Court Order was issued after 2013, you may be able to retrieve an Authentic Court Order (ACO) from https://courtorders.gov.sg/ . An Authentic Court Order (ACO) is an official, digitally verifiable court document issued by the Singapore Courts. Accessible via www.courtorders.gov.sg, it replaces the need to request, pay for, and collect physical Certified True Copies (CTCs).
If your Court Order HAS a QR code on it:
Scan or Visit: Scan the QR code printed on your document, or go straight to www.courtorders.gov.sg. No login is required.
Verify: Enter the Access Code shown on your document. If prompted, additionally type in the Case Number (without any alphabets).
Download & Share: Instantly view, download, share, or print out the verified digital PDF.
If You Have Misplaced Your Court Order, or Your Court Order DOES NOT have a QR Code
Log In: Go to www.courtorders.gov.sg and log in securely using your Singpass.
Enter Details: Input your Case Number and Document / Court Order Number. Our system will need to ensure that you are a legitimate party in the case.
Request & Retrieve: Submit the details to generate and retrieve your digital authentic court order version for free. The request may take some time to be processed, so please return to check the status regularly.
Certified True Copies
If the above does not work for you, or if you somehow still required a physical Certified True Copy, you can file a "Request for Certified True Copy" via eLitigation.
If you are not represented by a lawyer, visit any one of the Singapore Courts Service Bureaus to file in person. You will need to explain the intended use of the copies in your request, which is subject to the approval of the Registrar. The certified true copy/plain copy will be sent to you electronically. Please note that documents to be submitted to court that contain any NRIC / passport numbers should show the last four characters of the NRIC / passport numbers. Upon submitting/filing the request, the Court will follow up with you on the outcome and further instructions.

questions.title: What is the procedure to apply for a Final Judgment?
questions.text:
If you are the Applicant, you can apply for / extract your Final Judgment through eLitigation at the Singapore Courts Service Bureau.
If you are the Respondent, you must first apply for the Court's permission to apply for your Final Judgment. Apply by summons, with a supporting affidavit explaining why you, and not the Plaintiff, have to apply for the Final Judgment. You may do so through eLitigation at the Singapore Courts Service Bureau.
Note that application for the Final Judgment can only be done after all ancillary matters have been concluded, or 3 months after Interim Judgment is granted, whichever comes later. The application for Final Judgment must also be done within 1 year of Interim Judgment or within 3 months of the Ancillary Order, failing which, a Summons to extend time has to be filed first.

questions.title: How do I check the status/information of my divorce case?
questions.text:

Alternatively, if you are self-represented, you may visit https://services.judiciary.gov.sg/ and login to the Litigant Portal to view some basic information and the documents related to your case.
If you do not have the divorce case number, please email to FJC_FAMILY_REGISTRY@judiciary.gov.sg for assistance on case search.
Depending on your search result(s), you will need to pay either $10 or $20 per year, depending on whether your search is in the Family Courts or the Family Division of High Court. Payment can be made by internet banking / bank transfer or PayNow. In this respect, please note that the Family Justice Courts are only able to conduct this search if the divorce proceedings were commenced in Singapore.

questions.title: If a couple residing in Singapore now has filed for Divorce in another country, how do they make the divorce valid in Singapore? Is it necessary to go through the entire divorce process in Singapore?
questions.text:
If the Divorce Proceedings have already been concluded in the Court of another country, there is no need to validate the Divorce Documents in Singapore.
However, a Certified True Copy of the Divorce Certificate may be required for various applications in Singapore.

questions.title: Is the consent of both parties necessary for divorce proceedings to be carried out?
questions.text:
The consent of both parties is not required for the divorce to proceed.
If you choose to ignore the divorce filed against you, the court may conclude the case without your input and/or presence in court. The orders made will still be binding on both parties.
If you wish to contest the divorce proceedings, you must file a Notice of Contest and Reply. You may also file a cross-application. For more information on how you can respond to a divorce application, please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/respond-matrimonial-application-divorce-normal-track.

questions.title: When can a party who has been involved in a divorce proceeding get married again?
questions.text:
An individual who has gone through a divorce can only get married after the Final Judgment has been issued.
The Final Judgment can be extracted when all the Ancillary Matters (if applicable) have been resolved, or 3 months after the Interim Judgment has been granted, whichever is later.

questions.title: What is the legal procedure regarding amendment of Access and Custody issues?
questions.text:
You may consider applying to change a court order on access and custody if there is a material change in circumstances of either party or of their children (a “variation application”). All court orders can only be amended or changed by another order of court.
If your divorce case was commenced on or after 15 October 2024, the variation application should be filed as a summons (not an originating application).
If your divorce case was commenced before 15 October 2024, the variation application should be filed as an originating application (not as a summons).
If the order you are seeking to change/amend was made more than 1 year ago, the variation application will need to be personally served on any person affected by the order (such as your ex-spouse).
For more information on how you can vary a court order, please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/going-to-court-matrimonial-application-divorce/going-to-court-for-ancillary-matters/varying-a-court-order
You should seek independent legal advice if you need further help and/or require advice on the merits of your case.

questions.title: What can be done if the other party does not abide by the Court Order made regarding Ancillary matters? (E.g. Refusal to sign HDB Transfer)
questions.text:
If you wish to enforce the court order, you will need to make the application by way of summons, supported by an affidavit. Upon filing of the application, the court will deal with the matter in accordance with the law.
It would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case.

questions.title: Can a father, who has custody of his child, apply for maintenance from the child's mother?
questions.text: Yes. Whoever has care and control of the child can apply for maintenance. Under the law, both parents are responsible for maintaining their child regardless of the gender of the parent.

questions.title: How do I amend or vary an Order of Court?
questions.text:
If you wish to vary the court order made in a divorce case, you will need to make the application by way of summons, supported by an affidavit. Upon filing of the application, the court will deal with the matter in accordance with the law.
It would be best to seek independent legal advice if you require advice on the merits of your case. For more information on variation, do visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/going-to-court-matrimonial-application-divorce/going-to-court-for-ancillary-matters/varying-a-court-order.

questions.title: Is it possible to check if another individual has been divorced before?
questions.text: No. Information regarding divorce cases is confidential, and only related parties are able to check on their cases.

questions.title: Can employment agencies update their client company's particulars in EP eService?
questions.text: No, the employing company will have to update the particulars themselves or write to Work Pass Division to have the particulars updated.
topics: Work passes and permits / Employment Pass

questions.title: How to calculate the duty and GST payable if I do not have receipts and invoices of my items?
questions.text: Our officers will assess the condition of the goods before computing the duty and GST payable. If the goods are valued in foreign currency, our officers will convert the value into Singapore dollars based on the exchange rates listed on our Customs website prior to the computation of tax payable.
topics: Valuation, Duties, Taxes & Fees / Establishing Customs Values for Imports

questions.title: I have duplicate permits. Can I cancel the duplicated permit since it is unutilised?
questions.text:
You may cancel an approved Customs permit within the permit's validity period if the permit has not been utilised for cargo clearance.
If your duplicate permit is a payment permit (with GF or G7 condition), please note that application for cancellation must be submitted before 23:59:59 hours of the same day of approval.
If the payment cannot be cancelled, you are required to submit a refund application instead.
topics: Import Procedures / Permit Amendments and Cancellation

questions.title: Can I use photocopies or fax copies of the Cargo Clearance Permits (CCPs) for clearance of non-containerised cargoes?
questions.text: If the Cargo Clearance Permits (CCPs) are required to be produced for clearance of non-containerised cargoes, photocopies or fax copies of approved CCPs may be used.

questions.title: Can I bring plant products into Singapore?
questions.text: The importation of plants, cut flowers and foliage is under the purview of the National Parks Board (NParks). You may refer to their website, or submit an enquiry to NParks through their online feedback form so that they can further advise you on the rules and regulations.

questions.title: When should I apply for refund from IRAS instead of Customs?
questions.text: Please refer to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website for more information.
topics: Valuation, Duties, Taxes & Fees / Refund of Duties & GST

questions.title: How do I collect parcels ordered via the internet which are sent through postal services to Singapore? Do I have to pay taxes for them?
questions.text: Goods imported by post or Speedpost services are processed and managed by SingPost. The collection procedures for postal parcels is dependent on the type of goods and CIF value of the goods. You may refer to here for more information on postal parcels.
topics: Import Procedures / Importing by Postal or Courier Service

questions.title: Whom should I contact to report smuggling activities and/or evasion of duty or Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
questions.text: To report smuggling activities and/or evasion of duty and/or Goods and Services Tax (GST), please fill in the online feedback form here.

questions.title: Where can I locate Singapore Customs' revenue statistics?
questions.text: You may refer to the statistics on our website here.

questions.title: The courier service provider informed me that my parcel is with Singapore Customs. Can Customs update me on the status of my parcel and collection procedures?
questions.text:
We recommend that you contact the courier service company that is handling your parcel for more information on the status of your courier parcel and/or reasons for delay of clearance or shipping. Singapore Customs is unable to advise you as the shipment and clearance process will be handled by your courier service providers. The tracking number provided to you is also not required by Singapore Customs during the permit declaration of the goods in the parcel.
You may wish to note that certain categories of goods are subject to additional documentary requirements and/or the payment of duty and/or GST, namely:
Dutiable goods;
Controlled goods;
Prohibited goods; and/or
Goods of a total CIF value exceeding S$400 and does not have an invoice attached to it at the time of arrival.
Should your courier parcel contain any of the above types of goods, you may wish to liaise with your courier service provider handling the clearance of your courier parcel on your behalf to advise you on its clearance requirements and applicable service fees.
For more information on importation by Postal or Courier Service, please click here.
topics: Import Procedures / Importing by Postal or Courier Service

questions.title: What is the Importer UEN to be declared for importing goods by individuals who made purchases from overseas?
questions.text:
You may declare using the Miscellaneous Unique Entity Number (UEN), 99999990000C, in the permit application for individuals importing or exporting goods (including goods subject to control of Competent Authorities (CAs)) for non-commercial purposes only.
For more information on the correct usage of the generic UEN in permit applications, please refer to Customs Circular No. 11/2014.

questions.title: Are there any Customs regulations to bring goods out of Singapore?
questions.text: Some goods may be subject to export control. Please check with the relevant�Competent Authorities�on their requirements.

questions.title: I will be transiting through Singapore to bring the ashes of my deceased relative located overseas to another country. What are the procedures involved?
questions.text: You are not required to produce documentation if you are not clearing through Singapore’s immigration counter before your next flight as you will only be in transit and will not be bringing the ashes into Singapore.
topics: Transfer of Remains for Cremation or Burial

questions.title: My client wants to import currency notes and coins, which are legal tender, by air. What should I do?
questions.text:
In general, no permit is required for the importation of currency notes and coins.
However, if the importation of currency notes and coins are of substantial quantities (eg. importation of used currencies by money - changing or remittance businesses), then an In-Non Payment (GTR) permit has to be declared prior to the importation.
If the currency notes and coins are collector's pieces, investment articles or items of numismatic value, GST would be payable on the import, via an In-Payment (GST) permit.
The importer and/or the Declaring Agent are also required to check with the relevant agencies and departments (e.g. Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) of the Singapore Police Force) on their requirements prior to the importation.

questions.title: How can the shipper perform a currency exchange conversion to make an export permit application?
questions.text: For currency conversion, please refer to the exchange rate and currency convertor.

questions.title: What does this rejection 'PLS CHECK ORIGIN CRITERION DETAIL 1' meant?
questions.text: Please refer to this handbook and see Annex A for information on the exact details allowed in each line of the field for the different certificate types. Table A.1 specifies the origin criterion(a) to be declared under the "Certificate Item Description", "Origin Criterion" or "Origin Criterion Percentage" field in a CO application, based on the CO scheme and origin criterion(a) satisfied by the goods.

questions.title: Can I pay stamp duty using GIRO?
questions.text:
You may visit IRAS website for more information on GIRO application for payment of Stamp Duty.
However, GIRO is not available for the following:
1. Payment of Conveyance Duty – Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD), Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) & Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD)
2. Payment of Lease Duty that exceeds $5000.

questions.title: If the target company holds a long-term lease on a property but does not own any properties, which option should be chosen in the "Company Type" section of the stamping form?
questions.text:
A long-term lease recorded as a Non-Current Asset in the company's books is considered as having an immovable property.
Hence, "Private Company with Property in Singapore" should be chosen on the stamping form.

questions.title: How do I apply for and check the validity of an Immigration Exemption Order (IEO)?
questions.text: You will need to work with your respective embassies to liaise with MFA on the requirements for an Immigration Exemption Order (IEO) application.

questions.title: Where can I find the Stamp Duties Act?
questions.text: You may wish to view the soft copy of the Stamp Duties Act from Singapore Statutes Website.

questions.title: Do I have to include Goods and Services Tax (GST) when I compute stamp duty?
questions.text: The GST should be excluded when computing stamp duty.

questions.title: If the consideration paid is denoted in foreign currencies, which currency should I use for computation purposes?
questions.text: Computation is based on the Singapore Dollars equivalent of the foreign currencies as at the date of the agreement. You may choose to use the exchange rate from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

questions.title: Is exemption of stamp duty applicable for foreign embassy?
questions.text: Please apply directly to Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) for the exemption of stamp duty for foreign embassy.

questions.title: I have lost or misplaced my citizenship certificate. How do I obtain a replacement copy of my citizenship certificate?
questions.text:
Please come in person to ICA Services Centre between 8.00 am to 4.30 pm, Mondays to Fridays (except Public Holidays), together with the following documents:
one passport-sized colour photograph
your NRIC/Singapore Passport or Birth Certificate (for children below the age of 15 yrs old)
replacement fee of $20
An appointment will be given to you to collect the certificate on a later date.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters / Loss of Citizenship Certificate

questions.title: How do motorcyclists use the QR code at the BIKES lane?
questions.text:
You can scan the QR code at the QR code reader located at the kiosk for immigration clearance. You may refer to QR code for immigration clearance at Woodlands and Tuas Checkpoints for more information.
Travellers are reminded to bring their passport when travelling overseas as it remains the official travel document for identification for overseas travel.

questions.title: With the rollout of QR code clearance, can I continue to use my passport at the BIKES lane?
questions.text: You may continue to use your passport at the BIKES lane for immigration clearance at Singapore land checkpoints.

questions.title: Why do I encounter error/ issue with the QR code during clearance at Singapore land checkpoints?
questions.text:
This issue may arise if travellers have entered incorrect passport information during the profile setup process.
We recommend travellers to verify the accuracy of their profile information in the MyICA mobile app. If the QR code is not working, ICA will request the travellers to present their passports instead for immigration clearance.

questions.title: What can I show to my employer/school that I have been quarantined?
questions.text: If you have received a Quarantine Order from MOH, you may show the QO to your employer/school.

questions.title: If I am under Isolation Order (IO), do I have to pay for medical assessment, treatment and isolation for mpox?
questions.text: Costs related to medical assessment and treatment for mpox will be borne by the Government of Singapore.

questions.title: Can I book two consecutive sessions?
questions.text: You are encouraged to book ONE session (60 mins) per day. This is to ensure that all patrons have equal chance to use the courts.
topics: ActiveSG / ActiveSG Sport Halls and Courts

questions.title: What are the operating hours of the General Office?
questions.text: The General Office is open from 7.00am to 6.00pm, Mondays to Fridays. We are closed on weekends and public holidays.

questions.title: How are my CPF contributions allocated to my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
Your CPF contributions are allocated to three CPF accounts: Ordinary Account (OA), Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA) and MediSave Account (MA).
When you are younger, more of your CPF contributions are allocated to your OA to support your home purchase. As you grow older, more CPF contributions are allocated to your SA or RA and MA to meet growing retirement and healthcare needs respectively. You can view the CPF allocation rates (PDF, 0.1 MB) for details.
When you move to the next age group, the change in allocation rates is applied from the first day of the month after your birthday. This is because on your birthday, you are considered to have just turned the relevant age and remain in your current age group for that month. From the following month onwards, you will move into the next age group and the new allocation rates will apply.
Example:
If you turn 35 years old on 13 January 2026,
Your allocation rates for January 2026 will be based on the “35 years and below” age group; and
Your allocation rates for February 2026 will be based on the “Above 35 to 45 years” age group.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I pay my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
As an employee, you need not do anything as your employer is required to pay the employer’s and employee’s share of CPF contributions to CPF Board on a monthly basis. Your employer will deduct the employee’s share of CPF contributions from your wages.
You may refer to the table below to find out if you and/or your employer need to pay CPF contributions based on your total wages per month.
Total wages per monthCPF contribution by employerCPF contribution by employee
Up to $50NoNo
Above $50 to $500YesNo
Above $500Yes
Yes
You can use the CPF contribution calculator to check if your CPF contributions are correctly paid by your employer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What should I do if my employer did not pay my CPF contributions on time?
questions.text:
You should approach your employer for an explanation and ask when your employer will be making the payment.
If your employer does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you can lodge a report with CPF Board for our investigation and to recover any outstanding CPF contributions from your employer.
In cases where the company is in financial difficulty, CPF arrears may not always be recoverable despite our enforcement efforts.
You may find out more on your rights and employer’s obligations under the CPF Act and the Employment Act.
If you face difficulty servicing your Housing Development Board (HDB) loans, you may contact HDB to explore possible alternative housing repayment options. In the event that you wish to look for alternative employment, you may approach Workforce Singapore for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Will I lose out on interest on my CPF contributions when my employer pays my CPF contributions late?
questions.text: No, you will not lose out on any CPF interest if your employer pays late. When CPF Board recovers the CPF arrears from your employer, the interest will be credited to your CPF account as though the contributions were paid on time.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I lodge a report for non-payment or underpayment of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
For discrepancies in CPF contributions:
If you suspect your employer did not pay your CPF contributions correctly (e.g. did not contribute the CPF contributions on time, paid a lower amount or did not contribute at all), you may use the CPF calculator to verify the CPF contribution rates applicable to you. Please note that certain types of payments do not attract CPF contributions. You may refer to the types of payments to employees to find out more.
If there are discrepancies, you should approach your employer immediately, while the documentary evidence is fresh. Your employer is expected to rectify the errors without delay.
If your employer does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you can lodge a report for the outstanding CPF contributions, with CPF Board. Please enclose all available supporting documents to support your claim (e.g. pay slips and employment contract). Claims made without any supporting documents would require a longer time to investigate.
Please note the likelihood of recovery for any non/underpayment of CPF contributions beyond one year is low as the parties’ recollection of the facts or availability of evidence may diminish over time.
For discrepancies in CPF contributions and employment-related claims:
If you have any salary and dismissal related claims, you should try to resolve the dispute amicably with your employer first. If your employer does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you should file your claims with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM).
The Board will compute the CPF contributions based on the amount of wages due and payable once TADM has concluded your claims.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens to my outstanding CPF contributions if my employer is made a bankrupt, or is under liquidation or winding up?
questions.text:
When your employer becomes bankrupt or enters liquidation, the High Court, company’s shareholders or creditors (depending on the company’s situation) will appoint an Official Assignee (for bankruptcy) or Official Receiver/Liquidator (for company liquidation) to investigate into the individual/company's conduct and assets. CPF Board will file claims for your outstanding CPF contributions with the appointed official on your behalf.
Any proceeds realised by the Official Assignee or Official Receiver/Liquidator will be paid in the order* of priority as accorded by the law. The bankruptcy, liquidation or winding up process will take time, and could take years to complete for complex cases. If you wish to know more about the bankruptcy, liquidation or winding up process, you can visit Ministry of Law – Insolvency Office website.
Whilst employers are obligated to pay CPF contributions, owed contributions may not be recoverable despite CPF Board's enforcement actions when employers face insolvency. You can contact the Official Assignee or Official Receiver/Liquidator directly to find out the status of the bankruptcy, liquidation or winding up process.
We would like to take this opportunity to advise employees that if your employer is in financial difficulties, while CPF Board will continue to take enforcement actions, employees should be mentally prepared that the CPF owed may not be recoverable. In such situation, to avoid adding to the amounts owed, employees may wish to assess their situation carefully and consider approaching Workforce Singapore for job switch assistance.
*Costs and expenses incurred by the Official Assignee or Official Receiver/Liquidator, costs of applicant for the bankruptcy or winding up order, salary (including allowance or reimbursement), retrenchment benefits or ex gratia payments under employment contracts, amounts due in respect of workmen’s compensation under the Work Injury Compensation Act must be paid before it can be paid to employee’s CPF.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: If I am concurrently employed by more than one employer, can I choose to contribute CPF for one of my employments only?
questions.text:
If you are concurrently employed by more than one employer, all your employers must pay CPF contributions based on the wages payable to you. This is because the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling is applicable on a “per employment” basis.
However, if your total OW from your employers exceed the current OW ceiling, you may apply to limit your share of contributions. There will be no change to the employer’s share of CPF contributions. All your employers will have to pay the employer's share of CPF contributions on the OW at the prevailing rate, subject to the OW ceiling. As contributions are payable monthly, the approval cannot be backdated and it will only take effect once CPF Board’s approval has been granted.
You can submit an online application (via Singpass) to limit your share of CPF contributions.

b) Your employee’s share of CPF contributions paid by employer A =$6,000 (current OW ceiling) * 20% = $1,200
c) The amount of employee’s share of CPF contributions you want employer A to contribute on your OW =
$1,200

b) Your employee’s share of CPF contributions paid by employer B =$2,000 * 20% = $400
c) The amount of employee’s share of CPF contributions you want employer B to contribute on your OW =$0
Example 2:
For month of June 2023
Using the same OW ceiling of $6,000 as example.
Employee’s share of CPF contributions based on current OW ceiling =$1,200

b) Your employee’s share of CPF contributions paid by employer A =$6,000 (current OW ceiling) * 20% = $1,200

Note: The value in (c) should not exceed (b) for the respective employer, and the sum of (c) across all employers must be equal to the maximum CPF payable on OW (i.e. prevailing OW ceiling x employee’s share of contribution rate applicable to you)
Please also take note that whenever there are change(s) to the circumstances which may affect your CPF contributions on your OW, such as, but not limited to:
changes to current OW ceiling
your total combined OW falls below the current OW ceiling
changes to employment status (e.g. new or left employment, no longer concurrently employed by 2 or more employers)

Please see below Example 3 for better illustration of circumstance change(s).

($6,300 * 20% = $1,260) - $$1,220 (Employee's share under Employer A)
= $40
In the event of any circumstance change(s) (i.e. the above example illustrate change to OW ceiling), the employee (applicant) has to revised the apportionments by using the applicable rates and inform all affected employers of the new revised apportionments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I apply for refund on my share of CPF contributions that was paid above the CPF wage ceiling(s)?
questions.text: You will need to apply online for refund of CPF contributions paid above the CPF Wage Ceiling(s).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What should I do if my employer overpaid my CPF contributions to CPF Board and did not refund my share to me?
questions.text: Your employer should refund your share of CPF contributions before applying to the Board for a refund of the excess CPF contributions paid in error. If you did not receive the refund, you can write to us and we will contact your employer on the refund.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What documents must I provide when I lodge a report regarding CPF non/under-payment?
questions.text:
You should provide documents such as your monthly pay slips or employment contract for CPF Board to determine the CPF contributions due to you.
To minimise potential disputes between you and your employer, the contract must include key employment terms (KETs) and essential clauses, such as hours of work and job scope. For further information on employment contract and KETs, please refer to the Ministry of Manpower website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I report invalid CPF contributions from employers whom I did not work for?
questions.text:
You can lodge a report with CPF Board by clicking this link if you have received invalid CPF contributions from employers whom you never worked for.
For more information on the risks of receiving unknown CPF contributions, please refer to our educational resource: Phantom workers and the risk of unknown CPF contributions. You may also lodge a report with the Ministry of Manpower directly using the link provided within the article.
Alternatively, if you have worked for the employer before and the employer continued to pay CPF contributions for you after you left employment, please seek clarification with the employer first.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Who is exempted from receiving CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Employees should receive CPF contributions from their employers. However, the following employees are exempted from receiving CPF contributions:
Students who fulfil exemption criteria. Find out more about Who you need to pay CPF contributions for (PDF, 0.2MB) under the header “Students”.
Foreigners. Persons who are not Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
Employees of the United Nations (UN) Organisation, or any agency, institution or related organisation of the UN Organisation that is located in Singapore. Please refer to the UN System Chart (PDF, 0.08 MB) for the list of organisations that are within the United Nations System.
Employees of any of the following entities, which is part of the World Bank Group (a specialised agency of the United Nations Organisation), that is located in Singapore:
i. International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes; or
ii. Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency
Employees of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, who is assigned to work for the International Energy Agency Regional Cooperation Centre that is located in Singapore.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have just obtained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. Do I need to contribute CPF?
questions.text:
Yes, CPF contributions are payable from the day you obtained your Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status.
In the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, you and your employer will contribute to CPF at graduated rates to help you adjust to the lower take-home pay. However, you and your employer have the option to apply jointly to CPF Board to contribute at higher rates.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I determine the year of my Singapore Permanent Resident status for the purpose of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The year of Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status determines your CPF contribution rates as an SPR.
The first year rate applies from the day you obtain your SPR status. This refers to the date indicated on your entry permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority of Singapore (ICA). It ends on the last day of the month of your first anniversary of SPR conversion.
The second and third year rates apply from the month following the anniversary of your conversion to an SPR.
