questions.title: I have just converted from a Singapore Permanent Resident to a Singapore Citizen. When should I apply the CPF contribution rates applicable to Singapore Citizens?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution rates for a Singapore Citizen will apply from the date you have converted to a Singapore Citizen.
For Ordinary Wages (OW), your employer will need to pro-rate your OW and apply the appropriate rates to determine your CPF contributions. Your employer can write to us for assistance on the computation if the OW for the month exceeds the OW ceiling or if the pro-rated wages are below $750.
For Additional Wages (AW), your employer will need to apply the applicable contribution rate depending on when the AW is payable to you.
Example:
Assuming you are in your second year of Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status and become a Singapore Citizen on 15 June 2020:
For OW
The second year SPR rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period 1 June to 14 June 2020.
The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period of 15 June to 30 June 2020.
For AW
The second year SPR rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 1 June and 14 June 2020.
The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 15 June and 30 June 2020.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the minimum age to qualify for CPF contributions?
questions.text: As an employee, you are required to pay CPF contributions as long as you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, and are employed in Singapore under a contract of service.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable when I am on leave?
questions.text:
When you are on leave, you may still receive wages which attract CPF contributions. Some examples of wages that are given when employees are on leave are as follows:
Paid Annual Leave
Paid Sick/Hospitalisation Leave
Paid Maternity/Paternity/Shared Parental/Childcare leave
You can find out more about your leave entitlements on the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on the National Service (NS) make-up pay when I am away from work for NS training?
questions.text:
Your employer should continue to pay CPF contributions on the total wages payable to you, as if you are not away for the NS training. The basic salary and fixed allowance components of your wages, as well as the variable allowances (e.g. overtime pay and allowances) typically paid to you on a monthly basis, as shown in payslips, would attract CPF contributions. These CPF contribution obligations remain the employer's responsibility whether the employer is registered with the DIRECT* scheme, and are not eligible for reimbursement from the Ministry of Defence.
Example
Tim earns a basic salary of $2,000 and an average overtime pay of $800 every month. He went on NS training for one week in July.
Tim’s employer will have to pay CPF contributions on his typical total monthly wage of $2,800. The employee’s share of CPF contributions will also be based on the total wages of $2,800, and Tim’s employer is entitled to recover this from Tim’s wages.
*DIRECT stands for “Direct Reimbursement to Employers of Claims for NS Training”. NSmen whose employers are registered with the DIRECT scheme will continue receiving wages from their employers, who are then reimbursed by MINDEF.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I am working in Singapore for an overseas employer?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are required on wages payable to any Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident employee working in Singapore, even if the contract is signed overseas.
Employed directly by an overseas employer
You should research your prospective employer to ensure that it has legitimate business presence in Singapore and whether it is registered with Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). You should also communicate your CPF rights clearly to the overseas employer before the start of your employment to avoid subsequent disputes. If your CPF contributions are not paid on time or discrepancies are found, please approach your employer for clarification immediately while documentary evidence is fresh. If your employer does not provide you with a satisfactory explanation, you can lodge a report with CPF Board.
Do note that enforcement actions would not be effective against an overseas employer with no presence in Singapore and is not registered with ACRA. CPF Board may not be able to assist you in such claims. You may wish to exercise caution when seeking employment with such employer.
Employed through an Employer of Record (EOR) to work for an overseas entity
You may consider working for an overseas entity through an EOR. An EOR serves as the employer, taking on employment-related roles such as paying salaries for its employees, withholding taxes, paying employment-related benefits, while its employees perform work for its client, e.g. an overseas company.
When you’re employed through an EOR to work for an overseas entity, the EOR is your employer and will be responsible for paying your CPF contributions. Do read through your employment contract with the EOR to ensure your rights are protected.
While it may be easier to take enforcement actions against an EOR located in Singapore compared to an overseas entity, you should still exercise caution when seeking employment with an EOR. The recovery of any unpaid CPF contributions depends on the EOR’s financial ability to pay up the arrears. Do check with the EOR early if any discrepancies are found in your CPF contributions, while documentary evidence is fresh and before your CPF arrears accumulate.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: I work for an overseas employer outside Singapore and have to return to Singapore for personal reasons during the COVID-19 period. Are CPF contributions payable while I work remotely in Singapore?
questions.text:
If you are returning to Singapore for personal reasons and will be working remotely in Singapore for your overseas employer during the Stay Home Notice (SHN) period or unable to return overseas after your personal trip due to COVID-19 travel restrictions, CPF contributions are not payable until 30 June 2021 since this is a temporary work arrangement due to COVID-19 restrictions. However, similar to other employees who are working in Singapore, CPF contributions are payable on wages given to employees who are working remotely in Singapore from 1 July 2021 onwards.
If you choose to continue working remotely in Singapore not due to COVID-19 travel restrictions, and your employer agrees with this work arrangement, CPF contributions are payable on your wages as they are given in respect of your employment in Singapore.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable during my overseas training?
questions.text: CPF contributions are payable during overseas training if you are employed in Singapore but are required to go overseas for the training period.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How much CPF contributions should I receive?
questions.text: Use our CPF contribution calculator to calculate the amount of CPF contributions you should receive from your employer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the Additional Wage (AW) ceiling?
questions.text:
The Additional Wage (AW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of AW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar year for all employees. It is applied on a per employee, per employer, per calendar year basis.
The AW ceiling is computed as follows:
$102,000 - Total Ordinary Wage subject to CPF for the year
You can also compute the amount of AW that is CPF payable using the Additional Wage ceiling Calculator.
Find out more about AW and the AW ceiling.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable by the holding company or the subsidiary company if I am seconded from the former to latter?
questions.text: The employer who had entered into an employment contract with you is required to pay the CPF contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: I received a notification informing me that my CPF contributions have been credited. What is this notification about?
questions.text:
The CPF Contribution Alert is a notification service to inform CPF members (Singapore Citizens and 3rd year onwards Singapore Permanent Residents) when their monthly CPF contributions are credited. For example, you will be notified when your CPF contributions for the month of September 2022 have been credited any day between 1 September 2022 to 31 October 2022.
CPF members can receive the notification via
their registered email address; or
push notification via CPF Mobile app. CPF members will need to enable personalised notifications within the mobile app’s settings to start receiving the alert.
With the CPF Contribution Alert, you can conveniently verify the wages declared and CPF contributions paid by your employer against your pay slip.
If there are any discrepancies or if you have any clarifications, please approach your supervisor or company’s HR immediately so that any error can be rectified early while documentary evidence is fresh. If CPF contributions were paid in error, your employer will need to submit an adjustment or refund request immediately, and no later than one year from the payment date.
Find out more information on the CPF Contribution Alert.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I receive the CPF Contribution Alert via CPF Mobile app?
questions.text: You can enable personalised notifications at CPF Mobile app Settings page.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I view my CPF contributions details in the CPF Contribution Alert email?
questions.text:
If you have downloaded the latest version of the CPF Mobile app, you will be directed to the CPF Mobile app upon clicking the link.
If you have not downloaded the latest version of the CPF Mobile app, or you are viewing on a desktop or laptop, you will be directed to your web browser to view the details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I check whether my CPF contributions are correct?
questions.text: You can use our CPF contribution calculator to check if your CPF contributions are correct by keying in the wages indicated in your payslip. The Employment Act requires your employer to provide you with an itemised payslip.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What should I do if my employer has overpaid my CPF contributions?
questions.text: If your employer has overpaid your CPF contributions, please inform your employer immediately to rectify the errors early while documentary evidence is fresh. Your employer can apply online, for a refund or adjustment of the overpaid CPF contributions immediately and no later than one year from the payment date.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How was the employee's share of CPF contributions indicated on my CPF Contribution Alert being derived?
questions.text:
Your employee’s share of CPF contributions on the CPF Contribution Alert is derived by applying the applicable CPF contribution rate to the total CPF contributions made by your employer.
The computation is performed on a per transaction basis, and is not aggregated if your employer had made multiple CPF contributions for you in a particular month. It also does not take into account if you had applied to limit your employee’s share of contribution on Ordinary Wages for multiple employments. As the employee’s share of CPF contributions indicated on the CPF Contribution Alert are meant to be indicative, please use our CPF contribution calculator to determine the exact breakdown of your employee's share of CPF contributions based on your total wages per month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is it important for my employer to declare accurate wages for me to CPF Board?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are computed based on your wages. It is therefore important that your employer declares accurate wage information to CPF Board so that the correct amount of CPF contribution can be verified.
It is an offence under the CPF Act to knowingly provide false information to CPF Board. If convicted, a first offender may be fined up to $5,000 or jailed for up to 6 months, or both.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: The wages declared are correct, but I did not receive the correct amount of wages. What should I do?
questions.text: If your employer did not pay you the correct amount of wages, you can lodge a report through MOM Workright.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why are my wages reflected as $0 on my CPF Contribution Alert?
questions.text:
Your wages are reflected as $0 as your employer has either declared it as $0 or omitted to declare your wages.
You should approach your supervisor or company HR for an explanation. The discrepancy could be due to an administrative error, and your employer should rectify it as soon as possible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I stop receiving the CPF Contribution Alert via CPF Mobile app?
questions.text: You can disable personalised notifications at CPF Mobile app Settings page.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Where can I find the application forms pertaining to self-employed matters?
questions.text: You can find the list of application forms applicable to the Self-Employed Scheme at CPF website > Tools and services > Forms and e-applications > Growing Your Savings > Self-employment contributions.

questions.title: Do I need to register myself as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You do not need to register your self-employed status with CPF Board.
You will be considered a self-employed person if you:
Declare your net trade income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS);
Declare your net trade income to CPF Board*; or
Make MediSave contributions under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) Scheme.
*for Work Year 2022 (WY2022) and earlier

questions.title: How long does it take to process applications relating to the Self-Employed Scheme?
questions.text:
The applications relating to the Self-Employed Scheme will generally be processed within the service standards as stated in the table below. We strive to process all submitted applications within the service standard and will let you know if more time is needed.
ServiceNormal Processing Time
Manage your MediSave payable
Online: 12 working days
Manual: 15 working days
Refund of CPF/MediSave contributions by self-employed person
Online: 12 working days
Manual: 15 working days
This includes time needed to liaise with other parties or seek clarification on your refund application.
Make full payment for your MediSave payables
Payment via PayNow / OCBC Digital: Will generally be processed almost instantly.

questions.title: I am registered with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) as a partner for my business. Am I considered a self-employed person or an employee of the partnership?
questions.text: For more information on Partnerships, please visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website.

questions.title: I am a Board Member/ Director. Am I considered a self-employed person, and do I have to contribute to my CPF?
questions.text:
It depends on the nature of your relationship with the company, and the nature of the moneys received.
If you’re engaged as a Board Member or Director under a contract of employment (or Contract of Service) with the company, you’ll have to contribute to your CPF as an employee.
If you’re engaged in a business, profession or vocation of providing services as a Board Member or Director to companies, you’ll have to contribute to your MediSave as a self-employed person (SEP).
Please visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website for the differences in treatment between employees and SEPs.

questions.title: How do I deregister my self-employed status with CPF Board if I am no longer self-employed?
questions.text:
You do not need to deregister your self-employed status with CPF Board.
You will only need to make MediSave contributions if you earn an annual Net Trade Income (NTI) of more than $6,000. Your MediSave payable will be computed based on your age and NTI declared.
If you are no longer in self-employment, please note that you will still need to settle any outstanding MediSave payable, as it is compulsory under the CPF Act to contribute to your MediSave Account for the years that you were self-employed.

questions.title: What is the period for income declaration to IRAS?
questions.text:
If you receive a notification (via letter/form/SMS) to file tax from IRAS, or you meet the requirement to file tax (i.e. NTI above $6,000 and/or Total Income above $22,000), please complete and submit the tax return to IRAS directly. The income tax filing period is from 1 March to 18 April annually.
If you do not receive a notification from IRAS or do not meet the requirement to file tax, you can declare your self-employed net trade income (NTI) to IRAS via myTax Portal which will be available from 1 March to 31 October annually for taxpayers to e-File tax returns.
Once IRAS has assessed your income for the year, your assessed NTI will be transmitted to the Board. You can check your updated NTI records by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard with your Singpass.

questions.title: What if my net trade income for the year is zero or negative?
questions.text:
If your net trade income (NTI) is zero or negative for the year, you do not need to make any MediSave contribution for the year.
You will still be required to pay your outstanding MediSave payable for the years you were self-employed.

questions.title: What are the benefits of contributing to MediSave by GIRO?
questions.text:
GIRO lets you contribute to your MediSave Account through monthly instalments. Contributing to MediSave by GIRO provides:
Convenience - Automatic monthly deductions from your bank account to help you stay on track with your MediSave obligations without the risk of missing payments.
Hassle-free licence application and renewal – Your regular contributions ensure you meet MediSave requirements, making licence application and renewal processes smoother.
You can request an instalment plan for your MediSave contributions via the Manage your MediSave payable form.

questions.title: How can I check whether I have any MediSave payable as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You can check your MediSave payable by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
You can apply for your Singpass online if you do not have one.

questions.title: Can I apply for a licence/renew my licence if I have outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Licensing authorities will only process your licence application/renewal if you have an active GIRO arrangement with the Board to settle your MediSave payable via monthly instalments or have fully settled your MediSave payable.
To make your MediSave contributions via monthly instalments, you can request an instalment plan via the Manage your MediSave payable form. You will be cleared for licence application/renewal two working days after the first successful GIRO deduction. GIRO deductions take place on the 25th of each month (or next working day if the 25th is a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). Please allow two working days after the GIRO deduction for the amount to be credited to your MediSave account before proceeding with your licence application/renewal.
To make your MediSave contributions in full, please use the Manage your MediSave payable form to make your contributions via Paynow. The transaction will be processed almost instantly and you will be cleared for licence application/renewal thereafter.
To check your outstanding MediSave payable or your eligibility for licence application/renewal, you may log in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
Refer to this guide for step-by-step instructions on retrieving information on your eligibility for licence application/ renewal.

questions.title: If I do not earn any net trade income for the year, can I renew my licence?
questions.text: You do not need to earn net trade income in order to renew your license. To renew your licence, you will need to have an active GIRO arrangement with the Board to settle any MediSave payable, or have already fully settled your MediSave payable.

questions.title: If I do not intend to renew my licence, do I need to settle my outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text: You’re required to pay your outstanding MediSave payable even if you do not intend to renew your licence.

questions.title: What benefits do self-employed persons enjoy from making MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
When you contribute to MediSave, you enjoy:
Up to 6% interest per annum on your MediSave savings
Self-employed tax relief on your MediSave or CPF contributions, if eligible.
Use of MediSave to pay for medical expenses and healthcare insurance
Hassle-free licence application and renewal
You may also qualify for Workfare Income Supplement scheme for lower-income workers.

questions.title: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave even though I already have enough savings for my healthcare needs?
questions.text: With rising healthcare costs, it is important to have enough savings for your healthcare needs. Contributing regularly to MediSave will help you build up your savings over your working life. These savings can help you meet your own as well as your loved ones’ hospitalisation expenses under unforeseen circumstances.

questions.title: Why do I still need to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though I have already bought insurance for myself?
questions.text:
All working Singapore residents are required to contribute to their MediSave as a form of savings for their own and their loved ones’ healthcare needs.
Many Singaporeans have bought private hospital insurance plans in the form of Integrated Shield Plans, or IPs. IPs comprise of two parts – MediShield Life (MSL) which is a universal basic health insurance plan, and additional private insurance coverage. MediSave can be used to pay the premiums for both MSL and private insurance, up to the current withdrawal limit.
Hence, private medical insurance serves to complement rather than replace your MediSave savings.

questions.title: What are the conditions for applying to limit my MediSave payable as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
You can apply to limit your MediSave payable if your total income from employment (excluding Additional Wages) or platform work for the year exceeds the maximum total annual income.
Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.
Please refer to the table below for the total income from employment (excluding Additional Wages) or platform work that qualifies you to limit your MediSave contributions as a self-employed person.
Year
Maximum Total Annual Income
(excluding Additional Wages)
2022
$72,000
2023
$73,200
2024
$81,600
2025
$88,800
2026 onwards
$96,000
Income earned from platform work in 2025 will only be taken into consideration for applications to limit MediSave payable by self-employed persons made from 1 January 2026 onwards.
If you are a platform worker concurrently working as an employee, you can refer to this FAQ on refunding your share of excess CPF contributions (if any).
To limit your MediSave payable as a self-employed person, you may write to us and we will assess your request.

questions.title: Do I have to pay my MediSave payable when I am no longer self-employed?
questions.text: You’re still required to settle any outstanding MediSave payable, as it is compulsory under the CPF Act to contribute to your MediSave Account for the years that you were self-employed.

questions.title: How can I check if I am eligible for licence application or renewal?
questions.text:
It depends on whether you are a self-employed person or a non-self-employed person.
For self-employed persons
You can check if you are eligible for licence application or renewal by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass. You can apply for your Singpass online if you do not have one.
Your licensing agency, real estate company or financial institution may request for a copy of your MediSave payable statement. To retrieve your MediSave payable statement, click the PDF function icon at the top right of the MediSave payable statement after logging into Singpass.
Refer to this guide for step-by-step instructions on retrieving your MediSave payable statement.
For non-self-employed persons
You can check if you are eligible for licence application by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass through ‘Check your status’ under Hassle-Free licence application/ renewal. You can apply for your Singpass online if you do not have one.
You will be able to view a message indicating your licence application eligibility. Your licensing agency, real estate company or financial institution may request for a screenshot of the message to facilitate your application.
Refer to this guide for step-by-step instructions on retrieving information on your eligibility for licence application.

questions.title: I do not have outstanding MediSave payable as a self-employed person. Can I make MediSave contributions to offset my future payables?
questions.text:
You may make MediSave contributions to offset your future payables, up to the prevailing CPF Annual Limit, via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
The total CPF contributions (voluntary and mandatory CPF contributions) made for the calendar year should not exceed the prevailing CPF Annual Limit. Any contributions made in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.
You can enjoy tax relief on your MediSave contributions, if eligible.

questions.title: What is the cut-off date for self-employed MediSave contributions to be eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
To be eligible for tax relief for the year, MediSave contributions made by self-employed persons must be credited to their CPF accounts by the last calendar day of the year.
MediSave contributions amounts made during the year will be automatically transmitted to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for tax relief in the following year.
Please refer to this FAQ for more information on the tax eligibility of your contributions.
For more details on tax deductions, please visit the IRAS website or call the Individual Income Tax / Property Tax Helpline at 1800-356-8300.

questions.title: When is the deadline to make my MediSave contributions?
questions.text: Your MediSave contributions are due 30 days from the date of issuance of the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board.

questions.title: Why does CPF Board take self-employed persons to court for not contributing to their MediSave?
questions.text:
Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required under the CPF Act to contribute to their MediSave. This ensures that SEPs have enough MediSave savings for their healthcare needs, especially during old age when they have stopped working. SEPs without enough MediSave savings and MediShield Life cover may need to tap on other sources of funds such as their family members’ MediSave savings should they be hospitalised.
The CPF Board will continue to be flexible towards those with genuine financial difficulties. SEPs can request instalment plans to settle the outstanding amounts over a reasonable period. The CPF Board will only take recalcitrant defaulters to court as the last resort.

questions.title: What is the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme?
questions.text: The Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme is a tripartite co-contribution scheme initiated by the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the taxi industry, and supported by the Ministry of Manpower and CPF Board. DAS aims to enhance the welfare of all taxi principal hirers.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: Who is eligible for the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme?
questions.text:
Under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, all taxi principal hirers who make regular contributions1 to their MediSave Account are eligible to receive co-contributions from participating taxi operators. Only contributions that can be used to offset MediSave payable are eligible for DAS co-contributions.
If you have outstanding MediSave payable, you may be eligible for DAS co-contributions from participating taxi operators if you make full payment or be on a monthly GIRO instalment plan of at least $20 for your MediSave payable.
If you do not have outstanding MediSave payable, you may be eligible for DAS co-contributions from participating taxi operators if you pre-pay your future MediSave payable by contributing at least $20 to your MediSave Account monthly.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: How do I register for the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme?
questions.text:
No registration is required for the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme.
Taxi principal hirers who contribute1 at least $20 monthly to their MediSave Account will be eligible to receive2 a co-contribution of $20 monthly from participating taxi operators.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
2 Eligibility for co-contribution is subject to terms and conditions determined by your taxi operator.

questions.title: Will I receive Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions if I make a lump sum payment?
questions.text:
You will receive Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions of $20 monthly if you have contributed1 at least $240 into your MediSave Account in the past 12 months.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.

questions.title: Can taxi principal hirers who are not liable to make a MediSave contribution qualify for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution from their taxi operators?
questions.text:
Taxi principal hirers who do not have outstanding MediSave payable can still receive Drive and Save co-contributions if they make contributions to pre-pay their future MediSave payable1:
A contribution of at least $20 to their MediSave Account monthly, or
A lump sum MediSave contribution of at least $240 in the past 12 months.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions to pre-pay their MediSave payable as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: How does each taxi operator know the Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution amount?
questions.text:
CPF Board will inform participating taxi operators of taxi principal hirers who qualify1 for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions monthly. The amount of contribution made by hirers will not be revealed.
Please note that eligibility for co-contribution is subject to terms and conditions determined by taxi operators.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: How do I terminate my GIRO arrangement as a self-employed person?
questions.text: You may submit an online application Terminate GIRO for MediSave contributions using your Singpass if you wish to terminate your GIRO arrangement as a self-employed person.

questions.title: How do I request an instalment plan for my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
You can request an instalment plan to make your MediSave contributions in monthly instalments via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
If you have an existing instalment plan and wish to lower your existing monthly instalment amount, you can submit a request via the same form.
Please note that your request is subject to the Board’s approval. You may be required to provide additional information or supporting documents, if necessary.

questions.title: What is the status of my request to make self-employed MediSave contributions via monthly instalments?
questions.text:
We will keep you informed about the status of your request to make self-employed MediSave contributions via monthly instalments, once it has been processed.
Please note our normal processing time:
· Requests made via online appeal: generally 12 working days
· Manual transactions: generally 15 working days
You can check the status of your request by clicking on this link.
You can view your approved GIRO instalment plan details on the Self-employment dashboard. To access my cpf Digital Services – Self-employment dashboard, please log in to the CPF website using your Singpass.

questions.title: How do I change my bank account for GIRO instalments for my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
The quickest and easiest way to change your bank account for GIRO instalments for your MediSave contributions is to apply online! If your bank account is with these participating banks, please complete the Set up GIRO for MediSave contributions using your Singpass – Your application will be approved immediately, with no forms or paperwork needed. You will be re-directed to the bank's ibanking portal to complete the application. You can check the status of your online application through my cpf digital services - Activities with your Singpass.
If you would like to use an account from other banks, please download and submit the "Apply for GIRO for MediSave Contributions" (PDF, 0.2MB) to the Board.
Deduction will be made from the existing bank account until the new GIRO arrangement takes effect.

questions.title: As a self-employed person, how will I benefit from participating in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
Through making smaller and more regular MediSave contributions as and when you receive a service fee, Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) makes saving for your healthcare needs through your MediSave Account (MA) easier. MediSave savings can be used to pay for your out-of-pocket healthcare expenses and MediShield Life premiums.
As a self-employed person (SEP), there are many issues that require your attention. CAYE is an easy and hassle-free way to help free up more of your time. For your convenience, your CAYE contributions are automatically deposited into your MA whenever you get paid. This would also be helpful for SEPs whose income may be seasonal. CAYE can also help grow your money as you can start to earn an interest of up to 6% per annum on your MediSave savings earlier.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: As a self-employed person, how will the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme affect me?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) helps you save for your healthcare needs through smaller and more regular MediSave contributions each time you receive a payment. There is no change to your MediSave contributions payable as it would still be based on your actual Net Trade Income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What if I am in financial hardship and is unable to set aside monies for MediSave via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme?
questions.text: We understand that some self-employed persons (SEPs) may be facing financial difficulties and may not be able to cope with Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). Thus, if you do not have outstanding MediSave payable or are contributing via GIRO instalments, you may set your CAYE contribution rate to 0%. This means that you’ll receive your service payment in full, and CAYE contribution will not be deducted from your service payment. Please write to us if you wish to apply for a 0% CAYE contribution rate. CPF Board will assess your eligibility and inform you of the outcome in writing.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Who must participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
SEPs who are individual freelancers or sole proprietors and were awarded jobs with Government agencies will automatically be enrolled into CAYE.
Private companies are also encouraged to voluntarily onboard CAYE to help the SEPs who they have contracted with, save for their healthcare and retirement needs in an easier manner.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: As a self-employed person who provides services to Government agencies, how will I be enrolled into Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: You’ll be automatically enrolled into Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) when you receive a service payment from a Government agency you have provided services to as a self-employed person (SEP). You’ll receive a notification from CPF Board when you receive your first payment via CAYE. Subsequently, you’ll also receive a notification each time you receive a payment via CAYE.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I have already contributed up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). Why am I still required to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, you’re still required to make MediSave contributions even if you have met the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). This is the same for employees.
The MediSave amount above the BHS will be transferred to your CPF Special Account (SA)* or Retirement Account (RA). The BHS cap and overflow arrangement are intentionally planned to avoid over savings in MediSave and to supplement your retirement savings. These overflows which end up in your SA or RA can be withdrawn according to the withdrawal guidelines. If you’ve met the Full Retirement Sum in your SA or RA, the savings in excess of the BHS will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA). Savings in the OA can be used for other purposes such as housing repayment.
*The SA will be closed for members aged 55 and above from early 2025. Read more via this link.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I have contributed up to the maximum mandatory contributions for the year. Do I still have to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text:
If you’ve made Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions up to the maximum MediSave payable for the year, your applicable CAYE contribution rate will be 0%. This means that you will receive your service fee in full, and CAYE contribution will no longer be deducted from your service fee.
However, you’ll still be required to make good your outstanding MediSave payable (if any) via lump-sum payment(s) or GIRO instalment plan.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Will self-employed persons who provide services to the private sector be mandated to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: The Government, as a service buyer, has piloted Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) since 1 January 2020. There are currently no plans to extend CAYE into the private sector. Nonetheless, companies in the private sector are encouraged to voluntarily adopt CAYE.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What if I prefer making MediSave contributions through the current payment modes (e.g. GIRO)?
questions.text:
The small and regular MediSave contributions made through Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) help self-employed persons (SEPs) to reduce the MediSave contributions payable in the following year (after SEPs declare their Net Trade Income and have their MediSave payable computed).
If you’ve made your MediSave contributions in full or are on GIRO instalment plan, you’ll be allowed to set your CAYE contribution rate to 0% and receive your service fee in full.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do I estimate my annual revenue and expenses for the year?
questions.text: You can estimate your annual revenue and expenses for the current year based on the actual revenue and expenses you earned last year. You can adjust your estimated annual revenue and expenses whenever you foresee any changes in revenue (e.g. increase in number of jobs in the current year) or expenses (e.g. increase in business cost, including the cost to engage other to assist in your jobs).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do I adjust my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate?
questions.text: If there are changes to your estimated revenue or expenses for the year, you may update and re-compute your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass, under Contribute As You Earn > Update contribution rate. Generally, your updated CAYE contribution rate will apply to payments made from the next day.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: When should I adjust my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate?
questions.text: You can adjust your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate by updating your estimated revenue or expense whenever you foresee any changes in revenue (e.g. increase in number of jobs in the current year) or expenses (e.g. increase in business cost, including the cost to engage other to assist in your jobs).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I have adjusted my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate. When will the updated rate take effect?
questions.text: Generally, your updated Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate will apply to service fees paid from the next day.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why are different Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rates applied to different service fees?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rates may change when you (i) update your CAYE contribution rate or (ii) are no longer required to make CAYE contributions. Generally, the updated CAYE contribution rate will apply to service fees paid from the next day.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Who do I contact for further details on my Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee payment amount?
questions.text:
To view your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and other payment details, you may log in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass, under Contribute As You Earn > Show all payments. You can also contact us through these channels.
For more details on the net service fee, please contact the company or agency you have contracted with directly. If there are any non-payment, short payment or late payment of service fees, you may wish to take up the dispute directly with your buyer and seek mediation through the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) or other industry facilitated mediation services.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How does the company I contracted with know my Net Trade Income information and/or Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate?
questions.text: The company which you have contracted with will not have access to your Net Trade Income information. CPF Board will only inform the company of the amount that they would have to deduct from your service fee and transmit to your MediSave Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What should I do if the company I contracted with did not pay my service fees?
questions.text: For any disputes on non-payment, short payment or late payment of service fees, you may wish to take up the dispute directly with the company or agency you have contracted with and seek mediation through the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) or other industry facilitated mediation services.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do I know if the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution amount and net service fee payment amount are made correctly?
questions.text:
You can check your payment records by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass, under Contribute As You Earn > Show all payments.
If you’ve previously informed CPF Board of your contact details, you’ll also receive a notification whenever a contribution to your MediSave Account has been made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). If you wish to update your contact details, you can do so via logging on to my cpf digital services using your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if the MediSave contributions I made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) are higher than my MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
If you have outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, your excess CAYE contributions will be used to offset those payables1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to you. You can also choose to retain the excess CAYE contributions in your MediSave Account (MA).
Example:
Based on his estimated income of $22,000 for 2023, Sam contributed $2,200 via CAYE. In the following year, he declared that he earned a lower Net Trade Income of $19,000 for 2023. As such, Sam’s MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $1,900. Hence, he has excess CAYE contributions of $300 for the year. Sam also has an outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022 which would be offset by the excess CAYE contributions, leaving a final excess amount of $200. This amount will be refunded to him2. He can also choose to keep this $200 in his MA.
This example is illustrated within the table below:
Estimated 2023 NTI
$22,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,200
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$19,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$1,900
Outstanding MediSave payable for 2022
$100
Amount Sam will receive as a refund
$200
(i.e. $2,200 - $1,900 - $100)
1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Please write to us if you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
2Sam may also choose not to use his CAYE contributions to offset his outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022. In this case, he will be refunded $300 instead.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if the MediSave contributions I made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) are lower than my MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
If your total CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable for the latest year, you will be required to top up the remaining amount. You’ll be notified accordingly, and you can choose to make payment via a lump-sum payment(s) or sign up for monthly GIRO instalments.
Example:
Based on his estimated income of $21,000 for 2023, Sam contributed $2,100 via CAYE. In the following year, he declared that he earned a higher NTI of $30,000 for 2023. As such, Sam’s MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $3,000. Sam will have to top up the shortfall of $900.
This example is illustrated within the table below:

$21,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,100
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$30,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$3,000

(i.e. $3,000 - $2,100)
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why do I still have outstanding MediSave payable when I am already on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions is an estimate of your MediSave payable for the year and may be lower or higher than your MediSave payable for the year. If your CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable for the year, you’ll be required to top up the shortfall. You’ll also be required to make MediSave contributions for any outstanding MediSave payable incurred in previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I choose to retain my excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: Yes, you can choose to retain your excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in your MediSave Account. You may apply to do so by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I use my excess Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions to offset my outstanding MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions in excess of your MediSave payable for the year will be automatically used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, if any1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to your bank account.
You can also choose to boost your healthcare savings by retaining the excess CAYE contributions in your MediSave Account to earn up to 6% interest per annum, and to offset future MediSave payable. To do so, please apply via the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Please write to us if you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I renew my licence if I have been making Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: You can renew your licence so long as you have no outstanding MediSave payable or are on a monthly GIRO instalment plan.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why do I need to make other payment arrangements in order to renew my licence when I am already on Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Your Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions are only based on an estimate of your MediSave payable for the current year. To renew your licence, you will need to pay your MediSave payable incurred in previous years via lump-sum payment(s) or monthly GIRO instalments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Where can I find guides on how to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) transactions?
questions.text: If you need assistance on how to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) transactions, you can refer to the CAYE step-by-step guide, or you can write to us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How will the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme affect my income declaration to IRAS for tax purposes?
questions.text: There will be no change to Self-Employed Person (SEP)’s declaration of income for tax purposes. SEPs should continue to declare his annual income earned up to 31st December of the preceding year in the Income Tax Return for the current Year of Assessment (YA). For example, the SEP needs to declare his gross income for services provided between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024 in Income Tax Return for YA2025, even if it is invoiced only in January 2025. This is regardless of when the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions for the said services are made.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why is PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) the default mode of bank payments moving forward?
questions.text: PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) aligns with the government's drive for digital transformation and the Smart Nation initiative, as it promotes the adoption of digital payment. It also provides citizens a more secured mode of payment as they do not need to provide their bank account details to receive their service fee payments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: When will I need to be registered for PayNow to continue receiving my net service fee payments without delay?
questions.text: PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) will be the default payment mode from early June 2024. Please ensure that you are registered for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) so that you receive your service fee payments promptly.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What should I know about topping up my retirement savings?
questions.text:
Here are the 3 things you need to know about topping up your retirement savings. Tax relief is subject to terms and conditions.
.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why should I top up my retirement savings?
questions.text:
There are several reasons why you should consider topping up your retirement savings:
1. Higher monthly payouts in retirement
By topping up your Special Account (SA) (if you are below 55) or Retirement Account (RA) (if you are 55 or above), you are growing your retirement savings and will enjoy higher monthly payouts when you retire.
2. Risk-free interest rates* of up to 6% per annum
By topping up your SA or RA, you can earn risk-free interest rates* of up to 6% per annum on your savings.
For instance, if you save $100 a month for 15 years on your own, you would have saved $18,000. On the other hand, if you top up $100 a month to your SA or RA for the same amount of time, you would have saved over $24,000*. If you continue to top up for another 10 years, your savings would grow even more, reaching over $50,000* with compound interest.
3. Enjoy tax relief and matching grant for cash top-ups
By topping up with cash, you can also benefit from:
Tax relief of up to $16,000. Terms and conditions apply.
Matching dollar-for-dollar grant from the Government if you are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme. Terms and conditions apply.
*Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How will the top-ups to my retirement savings be used?
questions.text:
Top-ups to your Special or Retirement Account will form part of your retirement sum. If you are on CPF LIFE, top-ups will increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts. If you are not on CPF LIFE, top-ups will allow you to receive higher payouts or receive payouts for a longer time.
As such, top-up monies cannot be withdrawn as a lump sum, withdrawn from your Retirement Account savings using property, or transferred to your loved ones.
Additionally, top-up monies cannot be used for other CPF schemes, such as withdrawal for immediate retirement needs, withdrawal on exemption from setting aside a retirement sum, and other CPF schemes for education, investment, insurance, housing etc.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I top up using cash or CPF transfers?
questions.text:
Yes, you can top up your retirement savings using cash or by making CPF transfers. Please take note that CPF transfers do not qualify for tax relief or matching grant from the government under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
If you wish to increase your own or your loved ones' retirement savings, you can find out more here:
Who you can make top-ups to
Who you can receive top-ups from
How much you can top up via cash
How much you can top up via CPF transfer
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Who can I make top-ups to?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups
You can make cash top-ups to any Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. Find out the amount of cash top-ups you can make to a recipient.
CPF transfers
You can only make CPF transfers to yourself or your loved ones. CPF transfers can only be made to a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. Find out the amount of CPF transfers you can make to yourself or your loved ones.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Who can I receive top-ups from?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups
You can receive cash top-ups from anyone, including yourself, your family, employers, platform operators or any member of the community.
CPF transfers
You can receive CPF transfers only from yourself or your loved ones.
You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident to receive a top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Who are considered my loved ones?
questions.text:
For CPF transfers and cash top-ups to Special/ Retirement Account, “loved ones” refers to your parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, spouse and siblings*.
Find out why CPF transfer to your children and extended family members (e.g. uncle/ aunts/ cousins) are not allowed.
For first-time CPF transfers: You are required to submit supporting documents. Check required document via this link.

* Includes step-family and adoptive family members in these categories
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum or maximum age for making or receiving top-ups?
questions.text:
There is no maximum age for making or receiving top-ups.
However, you will need to be at least 16 years old to be a giver of cash top-ups.
You can make cash top-ups to a child who is not yet 16 years old, and you can find out how to do so here.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I still receive top-ups if I have started my monthly retirement payouts?
questions.text:
Yes, you can receive top-ups as long as you have not reached the current Enhanced Retirement Sum.
Find out how much top-ups you can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When will the top-ups received in my CPF Special/Retirement Account start to earn interest?
questions.text:
If you receive a cash top-up this month, it will start earning interest in the next month.
For CPF transfers of your existing CPF savings from your account to yourself or your loved ones, the transferred savings will start earning interest in the receiving account from the month of transfer. However, if the transferred savings are fresh injections (e.g. working contributions credited in the current month), it will start earning interest in the receiving account from the next month.
Illustration: $1000 is transferred in January from Ordinary Account (OA) to Special or Retirement Account (SA/RA) of the recipient (self or loved ones).
(A) If the $1,000 is existing OA savings (e.g. giver did not have new working contributions in January), it will start earning SA/RA interest in the recipient's SA/RA from January.
(B) If the $1,000 is January working contributions from OA savings, it will start earning SA/RA interest in the recipient's SA/RA from February.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to transfer my CPF savings to my children?
questions.text:
Your CPF savings are meant to support your retirement needs. Your children would be able to accumulate savings in their working years. Hence, it is more important to prioritise your own retirement savings and ensure that you have sufficient funds to support your retirement needs.
Find out how you can use cash to top up your child's CPF account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to do a CPF transfer to my extended family members (e.g. uncles/aunts/cousins)?
questions.text: The CPF system is meant to provide for and safeguard your individual retirement adequacy. Hence we must be careful when considering allowing CPF transfers to extended family members, beyond immediate family members such as your parents, spouse and siblings. Meanwhile, you can consider using cash to top up to your extended family member's CPF account instead.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: If I wish to make both a CPF transfer and a cash top-up to myself / my loved one, which should I do first?
questions.text:
If you wish to enjoy tax relief on your cash top-up to help you or your loved one up to the Full Retirement Sum, please make the cash top-up first, before the CPF transfer. If you prefer using your CPF savings over cash, please make the CPF transfer first.
You may wish to take note that only cash top-ups to self and loved ones within the Full Retirement Sum can enjoy tax relief. Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When is the best time to top up to grow my savings?
questions.text:
You should top up as early as possible to maximise the growth of your CPF savings through the power of compound interest.
Additionally, you can earn more interest if you top up earlier in the year. For example, if you top up in January each year instead of in December, you can earn up to 20%* more interest on your top-ups in 10 years.
* Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies and extra interest of up to 2% per annum on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances, with $8,000 annual top-up and $0 starting balance.
Do top up early in the year to ensure that your top-ups are processed before the year end as the normal processing time may take longer in December if there is a surge in applications.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my top-up limits?
questions.text:
You can check your top-up limit in your Retirement Dashboard.
Find out how the top up limit is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the maximum amount of top-ups I can receive?
questions.text:
The maximum amount of top-ups you can receive depends on your age and your CPF savings. You can easily check your top-up limit in the “Top-ups” section of your Retirement Dashboard.
If you are below 55, you can refer to the “Maximum amount you can top up using cash” to reach the Current Full Retirement Sum.
If you are 55 or above, you can refer to the “Maximum amount you can top up using cash” to reach the Current Enhanced Retirement Sum.
Here is a breakdown of how the maximum top-up amount is calculated:
Age GroupCalculation Method
Below age 55Current Full Retirement Sum – Special Account (SA) savings – Amount withdrawn from SA for investments1
Age 55 and aboveCurrent Enhanced Retirement Sum – Retirement Account (RA) savings2 - RA savings used for CPF LIFE premiums
1Net SA savings withdrawn under CPF Investment Scheme for investments that have not been completely disposed of.
2 Excludes, generally, interest earned and includes retirement withdrawals.
You can refer to these examples on how the maximum top-up amount is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not able to top up my Special/Retirement Account beyond the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) (below 55) or Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) (55 or above)?
questions.text:
The CPF system is designed to cater to the basic retirement needs of the broad majority of Singaporeans.
If you are below 55, you can top up your Special Account up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) to build up your retirement savings. If you wish to save beyond the FRS, you can choose to tap on the Supplementary Retirement Scheme, where contributions are also eligible for tax relief.
If you are 55 or above, retirement becomes a higher priority. As such, members have the option to voluntarily top up beyond the FRS up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) for higher payouts. This could help the middle-income group better meet their retirement needs.
Find out more about what the retirement sums are.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I transfer to myself or my loved ones?

You can easily check the maximum amount of CPF savings you can transfer in your Retirement Dashboard.
If you would like to learn more about how the amount shown on your Retirement Dashboard is computed, please refer to the table below.

If you have set aside the BRS and own a property bought using CPF savings, the P+I can be considered towards meeting the FRS for making CPF transfers to your parents and/or grandparents. The property you own must have remaining lease that can last you to at least 95 years old. If you have pledged your property for purposes of setting aside part of your retirement sum or to withdraw your retirement savings, the amount secured by the property can be considered towards meeting the FRS for this CPF transfer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of top-ups I can make or receive in a year?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of top-ups you can make or receive as long as the recipient can still receive top-ups.
It is important to note that once you make a top-up, it cannot be reversed. Therefore, we advise you to review that you have sufficient cash or CPF savings for other expenses before making the top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Am I eligible for tax reliefs when I make a cash top-up to my/my loved ones' retirement savings?
questions.text:
You can enjoy tax relief if you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident and make cash top-ups* within the current year’s Full Retirement Sum for yourself, your loved ones, employees or platform workers.
Find out more about the amount of tax relief you can enjoy.
Find out more on the conditions to qualify for tax relief.
*From 1 January 2025, givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $2,000 per year) under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will no longer receive tax relief. Find out more on how this works.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much tax relief can I enjoy when I make cash top-ups?
questions.text:
You can view the estimated tax relief when making top-up via the Cash Top-ups and CPF Transfers for Retirement Form.
You can enjoy tax relief on cash top-ups made each calendar year, up to:
$8,000 when you or your employer/ platform operator tops up your own Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA); and
Another $8,000 when you top up your loved ones' SA/RA.
This means you can receive up to $16,000 in tax relief per year by topping up both your own account and those of your loved ones.
Here are some important things to note:
NotesElaboration
Tax relief up to Full Retirement Sum (FRS) onlyTax relief is only granted up to the current year's FRS.
Giver enjoys tax reliefTax relief is enjoyed by the giver of the cash top-ups, not the recipient.
Tax deduction for employers/ platform operatorsEmployers/ platform operators may also claim tax deductions on cash top-ups made separately.
Shared cap with MediSave top-upsThe $8,000 tax relief cap on cash top-ups to your own SA/RA is shared with cash top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA). This shared cap also applies to the $8,000 cap on tax relief for top-ups to loved ones' SA/RA.
From 1 January 2025, cash top-ups that qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) (up to $2,000 matching per year) will no longer enjoy tax relief. Find out more.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why is there a combined tax relief cap for top-ups to the Special Account/Retirement Account and MediSave Account from 1 January 2022?
questions.text:
The combined tax relief for cash top-ups to the Special/Retirement Account and MediSave Account (MA) was introduced for greater consistency across CPF schemes. This allows members to better understand and take action to benefit from these schemes.
The tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups made before 1 January 2022 had differed1 for top-ups to retirement savings and top-ups to MA. With this change2, the tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups made on or after 1 January 2022 across both schemes have been aligned.
1Before 1 January 2022, the tax relief eligibility conditions for cash top-ups differed between both scheme in terms of (i) tax beneficiary [giver for Retirement Sum Topping-Up (RSTU); recipient for Voluntary Contribution to MediSave Account (VCMA)]; and (ii) tax relief cap for top-ups to self/loved ones (capped at $7k/$7k for RSTU, tax relief cap for VCMA depended on both the Basic Healthcare Sum and the amount of mandatory CPF contributions for the year).
2The changes related to cash top-ups to MA do not apply to MA contributions made as a self-employed person (SEP). If you would like to make MA contributions as a SEP, visit the Self-Employed Scheme page for more information on topping up your MA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When should I submit my top-up application if I want to be eligible for tax relief in the next assessment year?
questions.text:
Your online top-up application and payment will need to reach us by 31 December of the year.
It is important to note that the tax relief is granted based on the calendar year in which the top-up is made, regardless of the actual date of submission.
We would also encourage you to top up earlier in the year. Find out why you should top up as early as possible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What actions do I need to take to file and claim tax relief for my cash top-up?
questions.text:
You do not need to file or claim tax relief for your cash top-up as we will automatically inform Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) if you have instructed to claim tax relief in your top-up application and are eligible.
Please note that only givers who make cash top-ups are eligible for tax relief. If you make cash top-ups to your loved ones, the tax relief does not apply to your receipients. Find out the conditions to enjoy tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the personal income tax relief cap and why is there a cap on this relief for cash top-ups made?
questions.text:
The personal income tax relief cap sets a limit on the total amount of tax relief you can claim.
Even though each relief serves a good purpose, some individuals may end up with a significantly reduced taxable income when multiple reliefs are combined. Therefore, tax relief on cash top-ups is also subjected to the personal income tax relief cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I find out if I have reached the personal income tax relief cap?
questions.text: You can use the tax calculator on Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website to find out if you have reached your personal income tax relief cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why is there no tax relief for top-ups made to my children or non-immediate family?
questions.text:
Tax relief is an incentive given to encourage members to build up retirement savings for themselves or their immediate family members, particularly older Singaporeans who may have less retirement savings.
Your children have more time to accumulate savings in their working years for their own retirement needs. Hence, there is no tax relief for top-ups made to your children or non-immediate family members.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why are CPF transfers not eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are tax-deductible. Therefore, when they are transferred from one CPF account to another, they will not enjoy tax benefits.
Consider topping up using cash to enjoy tax relief while boosting your retirement payouts. Find out the conditions to enjoy tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is the fastest way to make a cash top-up?
questions.text: The fastest way to make a cash top-up would be via PayNow QR or OCBC Digital (for applications via CPF Mobile app or online form). Your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I apply for internet or mobile banking?
questions.text:
Applying for internet or mobile banking is easy and convenient. To get started, you can refer to the digital banking resources compiled by Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA). This list provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply for internet or mobile banking with various banks in Singapore.
You can also visit any SG Digital community hub to enjoy one-on-one guidance from IMDA’s digital ambassadors, who would be happy to assist you in setting up your internet or mobile banking account and answer any questions you may have.

questions.title: How can I make cash top-ups to my child's CPF retirement savings?
questions.text:
To make cash top-ups to your child's CPF retirement savings (regardless his or her age), simply:
1. Indicate your identification number as the giver of the cash top-up in the application
2. Indicate your child's identification number as the recipient
3. Select the relationship as "Others"
Do note that givers of cash top-ups need to be at least 16 years old and cash top-ups to children will not qualify for tax relief. Find out more about the types of cash top-ups which can enjoy tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am making a top-up to myself from overseas. How can I set up a Singpass account if I do not have a mobile phone number registered in Singapore?
questions.text: If you wish to set up a Singpass account for your top-up application but do not have a mobile phone number registered in Singapore, you may contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: My child is below 16 years old. How do I transfer his Ordinary Account savings to his Special Account on his behalf?
questions.text: If your child is below 16 years old and wishes to transfer his Ordinary Account savings to his Special Account, you can complete this application on his behalf.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What is PayNow QR?
questions.text:
PayNow QR is a convenient and faster way for you to make payments by scanning a QR code using your mobile banking app. It is also secure as it adopts the same high security standards adopted by the Singapore banking industry for fund transfers such as FAST and GIRO.
You can use PayNow QR if you have accounts with any of the following banks in Singapore: Citibank Singapore Limited, DBS Bank/POSB, HSBC, Maybank, OCBC Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, United Overseas Bank, Bank of China, and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What are the benefits of making top-ups via the PayNow QR?
questions.text:
Making top-ups via PayNow QR is hassle-free.
All you need to do is scan the QR code provided at the end of your online application, and the required details such as payment amount and transaction type will be automatically included. You do not have to manually enter any details, so you can complete the payment quickly and conveniently.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

1. Submit an online application via the CPF website

It is important to make payment as soon as possible, as the QR code will expire at the end of the day of application. If the QR code expires, you will need to submit a new application and make payment using the new QR code generated at the end of the application.
