questions.title: What is the priority of the Home Protection Scheme deduction if I am also using my CPF savings to pay my monthly housing instalments?
questions.text:
If you are also using your CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalments, the payment of HPS premium takes priority. This is to ensure that you remain financially protected by HPS for your outstanding housing loan.
During the premium grace period, your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings will be reserved for the HPS premium payment. This means that you will not be able to use your OA savings for any payments, including the monthly housing instalments, until your HPS premium is paid.
We recommend that you make alternative arrangements with your mortgagee on the shortfall in your monthly housing instalments during this period.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not pay the annual premium?
questions.text:
If you do not pay the annual premium for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS), your coverage will lapse and you will no longer be protected by HPS. This means that in the unfortunate event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability, you will not be able to make a claim under HPS.
You will need to reapply for an HPS cover if you wish to be covered under HPS in future. However, please note that your eligibility for the new HPS cover will be subject to approval and you being in good health at the time of application.
It is important to ensure that your HPS premiums are paid on time to avoid any lapse in coverage.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I check the premium payable to renew my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) charges a level premium rate (i.e. same amount annually throughout the policy term). This means that you pay the same annual premium throughout 90% of your HPS coverage period. You can find the premium amount on your HPS certificate, which was sent to you when the HPS cover was first issued to you.
Your HPS premium is deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account every year during your policy anniversary month. You can also check the premium payable by viewing the previous premium deductions online using your Singpass or from the Yearly Statement of Account.
To find out more on how long you need to pay your HPS premium, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Where can I check and view my Home Protection Scheme premium deduction?
questions.text: You can check and view the Home Protection Scheme premium deduction from your CPF Ordinary Account online using your Singpass. The deduction will also be shown in your Yearly Statement of Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I reserve monies in my CPF Ordinary Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: The monies in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), including your incoming CPF contributions, will automatically be reserved up to a period of two months for the full Home Protection Scheme premium amount, when you do not have sufficient funds in your OA at the time of HPS cover renewal.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I use the monies in my CPF Special Account to pay the annual renewal premium for my Home Protection Scheme cover if I do not have sufficient savings in my CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme premiums can only be paid from the savings in your CPF Ordinary Account, and not from your CPF Special Account (SA) savings. The SA savings are meant for retirement needs as they may be the only source of funds that members can turn to for financing their living expenses in old age.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the Home Protection Scheme premium not refundable if I did not make a claim?
questions.text: Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums paid for past policy years are not refundable. This is because you have received insurance protection during the period of cover and would have been eligible to receive the HPS benefits in the event of a claim.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why does the status of my Home Protection Scheme cover show “pending renewal” in the Home ownership dashboard when I have sufficient monies in my CPF Ordinary Account for the premium?
questions.text:
The deduction of premiums for the renewal of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers takes place on a weekly basis.
If your HPS cover renewal date falls between the weekly deduction runs, the status of your HPS cover will show as "pending renewal" in the Home ownership dashboard. Once the premium has been successfully deducted, the status of your HPS cover will change to "Active".
In the event that you do not have enough Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the premium, we will inform you to top-up the premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why are only certain individuals allowed to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium using their CPF Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums are consumptive in nature, which means that when your family member (who is your spouse, parent, child, or sibling) uses their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to help with your HPS premium payment, they will have less CPF savings for their retirement.
This is why only certain family members, who are co-owners of the flat, are allowed to use their CPF OA savings to pay your HPS premium. By doing so, they can help to secure the family home while limiting the impact on their retirement savings.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I make a top up for my spouse/parent/child/sibling's outstanding Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text:
If you co-own the flat with your spouse/parent/child/sibling, you can authorise us to use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay the insured’s premium shortfall. You can do this online by logging in with your Singpass.
Once the application is approved by the Board, the premium will be deducted from the available balance in the insured’s CPF OA first, followed by your CPF OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can my family member authorise the Board to deduct my Home Protection Scheme premium from their CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: Your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) who co-owns the flat with you can authorise us to use their CPF Ordinary Account savings online using their Singpass to pay for your Home Protection Scheme premium.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I use more than one of my family members' CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay my Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall?
questions.text:
If you have a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium shortfall, you can only use the CPF Ordinary Account savings of one family member (spouse, parent, child, or sibling), who is a co-owner, to pay the premium at any given time.
If you need help with subsequent HPS renewal premiums, you can approach another family member who is also a co-owner for assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is the priority of Home Protection Scheme deduction if my family member has authorised the Board to deduct my premium from their CPF Ordinary Account?
questions.text: The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium will first be deducted from the available balance in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) followed by your family member's OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Which CPF account would the premium be refunded to if my family member has used their CPF savings to pay for my Home Protection Scheme premium?
questions.text: If your family member (that is your spouse, parent, child or sibling) has used their CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for your Home Protection Scheme premium, any premium refund will be paid into your OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I terminate my standing instruction to use my CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay for my co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premiums?
questions.text: Please write to us if you wish to revoke your standing instruction to use your CPF Ordinary Account savings to pay your co-owner's Home Protection Scheme premium shortfall.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Home Protection Scheme exemption application?
questions.text:
You can contact your insurer to confirm if they have submitted the Home Protection Scheme exemption application to the Board. You may ask them to provide you with the application number (i.e. FormSG ID number).
Once your insurer(s) have submitted your application to the Board, you will receive notification of the outcome generally within five working days from the date it was submitted. Your insurer(s) will also be notified of the outcome.
However, if you haven't received any notification after this period and have confirmed that your insurer has submitted the application, you may write to us to check on the status of your application.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I apply to be exempted from Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are using CPF for your monthly housing instalments, you can apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) provided your private insurance coverage is enough to cover your outstanding housing loan against death, terminal illness and total permanent disability until the end of your loan term or age 65, whichever is earlier.
Here is what you need to do:
Contact your private insurance provider to submit your application to be exempted from HPS.
Submit supporting documents to your insurer that show details of your current* housing loan, such as the commencement date, balance loan amount, balance term of loan and mortgage rate. You can find this information on your housing loan statement.
*Within six months of the submission date of your exemption application.
We will only accept applications submitted by insurers. Once we receive your application and necessary documents from your insurers, we will assess your eligibility for exemption from HPS and inform you of the outcome generally within five working days.
If you are successful in the exemption application, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will receive a full premium refund credited to your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), provided that the exemption application is received by the Board within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When can I apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
The period which you can start applying to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) will differ depending on the following:
If you are a new home owner
You can only apply to be exempted from HPS after you have obtained legal ownership of your Housing Development Board (HDB) flat and the housing loan for the property has been disbursed.
If you have refinanced your housing loan
You can apply for HPS exemption only after the refinancing is completed and the housing loan has been disbursed by the new mortgagee.
If you have not previously used your CPF savings for your current HDB flat
If you have not previously used your CPF savings for your HDB flat at the time of purchase or for your monthly housing instalment, please fill up this application form to start using your CPF savings for your HDB flat.
Please note that you must apply for HPS before applying for exemption to avoid any delay in commencing the use of your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for your monthly housing instalments.
If your exemption application is approved, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will receive a full premium refund credited to your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), provided that the exemption application is received by the Board within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I be granted an exemption from the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption can only be granted if the applicant has appropriate, in-force private insurance policies that are sufficient to cover the outstanding housing loan (till end of the loan term) in the event of the applicant's death, terminal illness or total permanent disability, or age 65, whichever is earlier.
The types of life insurance policies (both traditional and investment-linked) that are acceptable for HPS exemption are:
Whole Life
Term Life
Endowments
Life Riders (must be attached to a basic policy), and
Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA) / Decreasing Term Rider
The types of policies that are NOT acceptable for HPS exemption are:
Policies that are assigned or pledged as collateral
Policies under Section 73 of the Conveyancing Law And Property Act (Cap 61) or under irrevocable nomination/trust arrangement
Policies with loans attached
Non-life insurance policies, such as business insurance policies, legacy insurance policies, health insurance policies or general insurance policies (e.g. personal accidental, fire or home contents policies)
Policies that are priced in foreign currencies
Policies from insurance companies that are not licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and;
Group policies that are not portable
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am currently insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), how much premium refund will I get if my application to be exempted from HPS is approved?
questions.text: If you are successful in the exemption application, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will get a full premium refund into your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) provided that the exemption application is received (by the Board) within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme for my new flat with the private insurance policy that was previously used for my old flat?
questions.text:
You can use the private insurance policy to apply for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption for your new flat if you meet the following conditions:
The remaining policy sum assured and policy term are enough to cover your current outstanding housing loan, and
The policy covers you in the event of death, terminal illness and total permanent disability up to the full term of loan or age 65, whichever is earlier.
To apply for HPS exemption, you will need to approach the insurer(s) of your private insurance policies and have them submit your application to us. Please note that we will only accept applications that are submitted through insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme exemption if I refinance or restructure my housing loan?
questions.text: If you have recently refinanced or restructured your housing loan, or if you have obtained a new housing loan for part-share/transfer of ownership of the flat, it is essential to review your private insurance policy(s) to ensure that the policy(s) remains sufficient to cover the newly refinanced or restructured loan. If the current policy(s) you have used for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption doesn't offer sufficient coverage for your newly refinanced or restructured loan, you will need to approach your insurer(s) to purchase additional policy(s) or apply for HPS.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme exemption if my private insurance policy used for the exemption is discontinued or altered?
questions.text:
If you have been exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) using a private insurance policy, the exemption will no longer be valid once your insurer informs us that the policy has been discontinued or altered.
In such cases, we will automatically issue an HPS cover to you based on the declared percentage you are exempted for, subject to your eligibility for an HPS cover.
Once the HPS cover is issued, you will receive an HPS certificate, containing the details of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I apply to be partially exempted from the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You cannot be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and insured under HPS at the same time. However, you may apply to be 50% exempted from HPS while your co-owner applies for a 50% HPS share of cover.
The total share of coverage for all co-owners must add up to at least 100% of the outstanding housing loan.
You are encouraged to be insured under your private insurance based on your share of responsibility to service your housing loan. This will ensure that you have sufficient coverage to settle your share of outstanding housing loan in the event of a claim.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is the minimal mortgage rate that I need to purchase for my private Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance policy if I wish to be exempted from Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If you wish to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme, the mortgage rate of your Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA) policy must be equal to or higher than the assumed mortgage rate of your housing loan. The assumed mortgage rate depends on whether you are taking an HDB loan or a bank loan.
Housing Development Board (HDB) Loan
If you are taking an HDB loan under the concessionary rate, a mortgage rate of 3% is assumed.
If you are taking an HDB loan under the market rate, a mortgage rate of 4% is assumed.
These mortgage rates are assumed after taking into consideration the historical rates and other factors such as the rising interest rate environment. This is a prudent approach, to ensure that members are adequately covered for their outstanding housing loan over the entire loan tenor.
Bank Loan
If you are taking a bank loan, a mortgage rate of 4% is assumed, after taking into consideration the historical rates and other factors such as the rising interest rate environment. This is a prudent approach, to ensure that members are adequately covered for their outstanding housing loan over the entire loan tenor.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the types of insurance policies that are not accepted for exemption from Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
The following are examples of the types of policies that are not accepted for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) exemption purposes:
Policies that are assigned or pledged as collateral
Policies under section 73 of the Conveyancing Law And Property Act (Cap. 61) or under any irrevocable nomination/trust arrangement
Policies with loans attached
Non-life insurance policies, such as business insurance policies, legacy insurance policies, health insurance policies or general insurance policies (e.g. personal accidental, fire or home contents policies)
Policies that are priced in foreign currencies
Policies from insurance companies that are not licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and
Group policies that are not portable.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I apply for Home Protection Scheme exemption (HPS) using multiple private insurance policies from different insurers?
questions.text:
If you have multiple private insurance policies from different insurers and wish to apply for Home Protection Scheme exemption (HPS), you can use the HPS exemption calculator or approach your insurer to determine if one or more of your policies is needed to cover your outstanding housing loan. If one policy is sufficient, you can apply for HPS exemption using a single application.
However, if you require multiple policies from different insurers to cover your outstanding housing loan, you will need to submit an application for each insurer. Here is how you can go about it:
Approach the respective insurers to submit your applications concurrently. Please submit one application for each insurer.
Attach the relevant supporting documents which show your current* housing loan details i.e. loan commencement date, balance loan amount, balance term of loan and the mortgage rate. These can generally be found on your housing loan statement.
*Within six months from the date of application for exemption is submitted.
Once we receive your application(s) and the necessary documents from your insurers declared in your application forms, we will assess your eligibility for exemption from HPS and inform you of the outcome generally within five working days. Please note that your application would be rejected if we fail to receive all your applications from your insurers within seven calendar days from the date of receipt of the first application submitted by one of your insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am already exempted from Home Protection Scheme (HPS) with my private insurance policy, can I apply for HPS again?
questions.text:
If you are already exempted from Home Protection Scheme (HPS) with your private insurance policy, you may still apply to be covered under HPS anytime.
To apply for an HPS cover, please submit the application online, using your Singpass.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I did not apply to use my CPF savings when buying my HDB flat, can I apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme and use my CPF savings for monthly housing instalments now?
questions.text:
Since this is the first time that you are using your CPF savings for your HDB flat, we will need you to provide further information and documents related to your housing loan, such as details of your financier and outstanding housing loan amount.
Please note that before applying for exemption, you need to apply for Home Protection Scheme first. This is to avoid any delay in commencing the use of your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for your monthly housing instalments.
You will need to submit an application to use your CPF savings for monthly housing instalment and apply for an HPS cover. Thereafter, you may approach your insurer(s) of your private insurance policies to submit your application to be exempted from HPS.
If your HPS exemption application is successful, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will get a full premium refund into your OA provided that the exemption application is received (by the Board) within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
Find out more: What can I do if I do not want to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the common reasons for unsuccessful Home Protection Scheme exemption application?
questions.text:
Your exemption may be rejected for the following reasons:
Your share of the exemption and your co-owners’ share of the exemption/Home Protection Scheme coverage adds up to less than 100%.
You have applied for exemption using private insurance policies from multiple insurers, however we did not receive all your applications from your insurers within seven calendar days from the date of receipt of the first application submitted by one of your insurers.
Your property address provided by your insurer(s) does not tally with our records.
We do not have your housing records as you have not previously used your CPF savings for your HDB flat at the time of purchase or for your monthly housing instalments.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When do I need to apply to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You need to apply to adjust your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover if:
Your loan repayment period or loan amount has increased for your housing loan taken with HDB or a bank: If you have extended the repayment period or taken out a larger loan, it is crucial to review your HPS cover. This ensures that you are adequately protected and that your share of the HPS cover is sufficient to pay your share of the outstanding loan in case of a claim.
Your share of responsibility in repaying the housing loan has changed: If there is a change in your share of responsibility for repaying the loan, it is necessary to adjust your HPS cover accordingly. This ensures that your coverage accurately reflects your current financial obligations.
You have taken a bank loan and have used cash to make a partial repayment of the housing loan: This ensures that your HPS cover is adjusted to align with your outstanding housing loan.
Please submit your application online using your Singpass to adjust your HPS cover. Your HPS cover would be adjusted based on the latest loan details as at application date. No backdated adjustments will be made.
If your HPS cover requires adjustment, the HPS premium will also be adjusted accordingly and we will issue you a new HPS cover.
Specifically, if you are increasing your HPS coverage due to an increase in loan repayment period, loan amount, or your share of cover, a new health declaration is required. If you are not eligible for the additional coverage, you may continue to be insured under the cover that was previously extended to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What can I do if I do not want to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are using CPF for your monthly housing instalments, you can apply to be exempted from the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) if your private insurance policy can adequately cover your outstanding housing loan up to the full term of loan or age 65, whichever is earlier, in the event of death, terminal illness or total permanent disability.
Here is what you need to do:
Contact your private insurance provider to submit your application to be exempted from HPS.
Submit supporting documents to your insurer that show details of your current* housing loan, such as the commencement date, balance loan amount, balance term of loan and mortgage rate. You can find this information on your housing loan statement.
*Within six months of the submission date of your exemption application.
We will only accept applications submitted by insurers. Once we receive the application and necessary documents, we will assess your eligibility for exemption from HPS and inform you of the outcome generally within five working days.
If you are successful in the exemption application, your existing HPS cover will be terminated. You will receive a full premium refund credited to your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), provided that the exemption application is received by the Board within one month from the issuance of the HPS cover. Otherwise, a pro-rated refund will be credited to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I have refinanced my housing loan?
questions.text:
If you have refinanced your housing loan, e.g. from a Housing Development Board (HDB) loan to a bank loan or a change in mortgagee, you do not need to apply to adjust your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. We will automatically adjust your HPS cover if your loan quantum and/or repayment period has reduced. A new HPS cover will be issued to you based on the latest loan details and the premium for the new cover will be deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account.
If your loan quantum and/or repayment period has increased, we will write to you to inform you to apply to adjust your cover. Please note that any increase in your HPS coverage is subject to approval and you being in good health.
If there are no changes to your loan quantum and/or repayment period, no adjustment to your HPS cover is required. We will update our records to reflect your new mortgagee.
Find out more:
What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme exemption if I have refinanced my housing loan?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I make a partial repayment of my loan?
questions.text:
We will automatically adjust your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover accordingly if:
You made a partial repayment towards your HDB loan, regardless of whether you used cash or CPF savings to do so, or
You made a partial repayment towards your bank loan, using CPF savings.
However, if you have taken a bank loan and have used cash for the partial repayment, please submit your application online using your Singpass to adjust your HPS cover, after your bank has recognised the partial repayment. We will then write to your bank to obtain your latest loan details. Your HPS cover would be adjusted based on the latest loan detail as at application date. No backdated adjustments will be made. It is important to promptly inform us of any partial repayment made in cash, so that your HPS cover can be promptly adjusted. Otherwise, you may end up being over-insured or under-insured, which would not be to your benefit.
Once the adjustment is made, your existing HPS cover will end, and any unused premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account (OA). You will be issued a new HPS cover based on the latest loan details after partial repayment. The premium for the new cover will be deducted from your OA.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to inform the Board to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover if I make a partial repayment of my loan?
questions.text:
It depends on the type of loan that you took to purchase your flat.
For Housing & Development Board (HDB) Loan
You do not need to inform us of the partial repayment of your housing loan, regardless of whether you are using cash or CPF savings for the partial repayment.
Your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be automatically adjusted when we are notified accordingly by HDB. Your existing HPS cover will end and any unused premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account. A new HPS cover will be issued to you based on the latest loan details after partial repayment. The premium for the new cover will be deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account.
For Bank Loan
If you are using cash to make a partial repayment of your housing loan, please submit your application online using your Singpass to adjust your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. We will then write to your bank to obtain your latest loan details. Your HPS cover would be adjusted based on the latest loan detail as at application date. No backdated adjustments will be made. It is important to promptly inform us of any partial repayment made in cash, so that your HPS cover can be promptly adjusted. Otherwise, you may end up being over-insured or under-insured, which would not be to your benefit.
If you are using your CPF savings to make a partial repayment of your housing loan, you do not need to inform us of the partial repayment. We will adjust your HPS cover automatically.
Upon adjustment, your existing HPS cover will end and any unused premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account. A new HPS cover will be issued to you based on the latest loan details after partial repayment. The premium for the new cover will be deducted from your CPF Ordinary Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is the premium for my new Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover higher than my old HPS cover even though I have made a partial repayment of my loan?
questions.text:
Your Home Protection Scheme premium is higher than before because you had extended your repayment period to a longer tenure, after you made the partial repayment of your loan.
Find out more:
How is the Home Protection Scheme premium calculated?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I include new co-owners for my Housing & Development Board (HDB) flat and how do they apply to be insured under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You would first need to contact or visit the Housing Development Board (HDB) Branch Office managing your flat to include your new co-owners.
After your new co-owners have obtained legal ownership of the flat, they may apply for a Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. The process to apply for an HPS cover differs, depending on the type of loan that they are taking.
For Housing & Development Board (HDB) Loan
Your co-owners may apply for an HPS cover when applying to withdraw their CPF savings for the monthly housing instalments via HDB.
For Bank Loan
Your co-owners may apply for an HPS cover online using their Singpass. This can be done at the same time when they are applying to withdraw their CPF savings for the monthly housing instalments.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why does my Home Protection Scheme cover end when I have fully redeemed my housing loan?
questions.text: You will not need insurance protection if there is no outstanding housing loan. Thus, we will terminate your Home Protection Scheme cover and any pro-rated premium refund (if any) will be credited to your CPF Ordinary Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I sell my flat, fully repay my loan or buy a new flat?
questions.text:
Your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be affected depending on whether you:
Sell your flat
We will terminate your HPS cover if you sell flat.
Fully repay your loan
This also depends on whether you are fully repaying your:
Housing Development Board (HDB) Loan
Your HPS cover will be automatically terminated when we are notified by HDB that you have fully repaid your loan, regardless of whether you are using CPF savings or cash. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account.
Bank Loan
If you are using your CPF savings to fully repay your loan, your HPS cover will be automatically terminated when we are notified by the bank that you have fully repaid your loan. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account. However, if you are using cash to fully repay your loan, write to us to inform us of the full repayment. We will write to your bank to obtain your loan repayment details before terminating your HPS cover. Upon termination of your HPS cover, any unused premium will be refunded to your CPF Ordinary Account. Your HPS cover will not be terminated if you do not inform us that you have fully repaid your loan in cash.
Buy a new flat
We will terminate your HPS cover for the old flat if you buy a new flat. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account. You will need to apply for an HPS cover for your new flat. The HPS cover for your new flat is subject to your health condition. As such, you will need to declare and fully disclose all information regarding your health in your application.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to inform the Board to terminate my Home Protection Scheme cover if I have fully repaid my loan?
questions.text:
It depends on the type of loan that you took to purchase your flat.
For Housing & Development Board (HDB) Loan
You do not need to inform us of the full repayment of your housing loan, regardless of whether you are using CPF savings or cash. Your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be automatically terminated when we are notified by HDB that you have fully repaid your loan. The unused premium, if any, will be refunded to your CPF Ordinary Account.
For Bank Loan
If you are using cash to fully repay your bank loan, please write to us to inform us of the full repayment. We will write to your bank to obtain your loan repayment details before terminating your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. Upon termination of your HPS cover, the unused premium, if any, will be refunded to your CPF Ordinary Account. Your HPS cover will not be terminated if you do not inform us that you have fully repaid your loan in cash.
If you are using your CPF savings to fully repay your loan, you do not need to inform us of the full repayment. Your HPS cover will be automatically terminated and the unused premium, if any, will be refunded to your CPF Ordinary Account.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I terminate my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You can terminate your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover online using your Singpass.
Ensure that the below requirements are met, otherwise, your application will be rejected.
Should your co-owner(s) (if applicable) continue with HPS coverage, their total HPS share of cover must add up to at least 100% of the outstanding housing loan after the termination of your HPS cover.
You must not have an active arrangement to use CPF monies for the monthly instalment payments of your housing loan. You may check whether you have an ongoing monthly housing deduction arrangement for your housing loan via your Home ownership dashboard. If you have an active arrangement to use CPF monies for the monthly instalment of your housing loan, please stop your CPF monthly housing deduction arrangement before submitting your application to terminate your HPS cover. Learn more about how to stop your monthly deduction for your housing loan.
After being notified that your CPF monthly housing deduction arrangement has been stopped successfully (generally within three to five working days after application), you may submit your application to terminate your HPS cover. Alternatively, three to five working days after application, you may check your Home ownership dashboard to verify that your monthly housing deduction arrangement has been stopped successfully before applying to terminate your HPS cover.
Find out more:
What happens after I have terminated my HPS cover?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What happens to my Home Protection Scheme cover when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency?
questions.text: When you have renounced your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency, your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will cease upon the sale of your HDB flat or at the end of the current HPS policy year, whichever is earlier. There will be no further renewal of your HPS cover, even if you are in the process of selling your HDB flat, as the scheme is only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What happens after I have terminated my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
You will get a full premium refund to your Ordinary Account (OA) if the termination application is received within one month from the issuance of your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover. Otherwise, any unused premium will be refunded back to your OA upon the termination of your HPS cover.
The monthly servicing of your housing loan instalments via CPF savings (if any) will cease upon the termination of your HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the Home Protection Scheme claim criteria?
questions.text:
A Home Protection Scheme (HPS) claim can be made when a member passes away or is certified by an accredited doctor to be suffering from terminal illness or total permanent disability.
Terminal illness refers to an illness that is likely to result in the death of the member within 12 months.
Total permanent disability means that (i) you are unable to take part in any employment permanently, or (ii) you have experienced the total permanent loss of physical function of any of the following:
Both eyes
Two limbs, or
One eye and one limb
To determine eligibility for HPS benefits, a detailed medical report has to be obtained from your doctor. If your doctor is not accredited, we may arrange for you to be examined by one of CPF Board’s appointed doctors.
To qualify for a claim under total permanent disability, you need to also have stopped physical employment.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Who will receive the claim benefits under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
When a claim is made under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), the benefits will be paid to the Housing & Development Board or the mortgagee directly, to settle the outstanding housing loan, up to the insured sum.
If the claim is admitted under death ground, the HPS claim benefits will be paid in a lump sum.
If the claim is admitted under medical ground, the member’s housing instalments (based on the share of HPS cover) may be paid by HPS for up to two years before a review of the member’s eligibility to claim the remaining insured sum in full is carried out.
If the HPS sum assured is more than the outstanding loan, the excess amount will be paid to the insured member’s CPF Ordinary Account.
You may find out more on what happens to the CPF savings for deceased members.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the claim exclusions for the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) provides coverage for CPF members in the event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.
However, there are certain exclusions to the coverage. If any of the following events occur within the first year of the policy, claim benefits will not be payable:
The member committed self-inflicted injury or suicide
The member committed a criminal offence punishable by death
The claim arose from the member’s own intentional criminal act
Additionally, HPS benefits will not be payable if:
The member was not in good health before the start of HPS cover
The member provided false or misleading information
The claim arose from wars or any warlike operations or participation in any riot
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the restrictions imposed on the sale of my flat after I have claimed the Home Protection Scheme benefits?
questions.text: There are no restrictions and you can sell your flat after claiming the benefits under the Home Protection Scheme.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to refund the sale proceeds to my CPF accounts if I sell my flat after claiming the benefits under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: Yes, if you sell your flat, you will need to make a refund to your CPF accounts. The refund amount and how it is handled may vary depending on your age and other factors, as detailed in the answer to How much do I need to refund to my CPF account when selling/transferring my property?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I claim the Home Protection Scheme benefits?
questions.text:
A Home Protection Scheme (HPS) claim may be made when a member passes away or suffers from terminal illness or total permanent disability.
If member passes away
If an outstanding housing loan was insured by the deceased under the HPS, we will automatically assess the deceased’s claim eligibility once CPF Board is notified of the member’s death by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
CPF Board will inform the co-owner(s) or the next-of-kin of the outcome and whether additional information is required.
If member suffers from terminal illness or total permanent disability
For member’s convenience, CPF Board has developed a one-stop application form to apply for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) benefits and withdraw CPF savings, if applicable.
To do so, you will need to:
Submit an online application after logging in via Singpass. The application form will allow you to concurrently apply for both DPS benefits and withdrawal of your CPF savings if applicable.
Download the Medical Assessment Report that is provided upon submission of the online application and have it completed by an accredited doctor. The medical institution must submit the completed Medical Assessment Report to CPF Board within 90 days of your application. Otherwise, your application will be cancelled.
If you are claiming HPS benefits, you must inform your employer to submit your employment information to CPF Board for claim assessment purposes. A FormSG link will be provided to you upon submission of the online application for your employer to complete. Corppass login is required.
After CPF Board receives the completed Medical Assessment Report and employment information (for HPS claim, if required), you will receive an email or SMS notification that the application is in progress. CPF Board will notify you of the outcome of your withdrawal application and HPS claim, while Great Eastern Life will notify you separately of your DPS claim outcome.
If the Medical Assessment Report is to be completed by a doctor from an overseas medical institution, please write to us for assistance.
If you are mailing your documents from overseas, all documents (except for original documents) must be witnessed/certified as true copies by an official of a Singapore Overseas Mission with their official seal/stamp duly affixed.
Alternatively, if you are residing in a country which is part of the Apostille Convention.
Your documents must first be witnessed and certified true by a Notary Public.
Thereafter, the notarised documents must be certified by the designated Competent Authority of your country via the issuance of an apostille certificate.
When the claim is approved, the HPS claim benefits will be paid directly to the mortgagee. to settle the outstanding housing loan, up to the insured sum.
To apply for withdrawal due to Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) only, please write to us for assistance. If you are claiming DPS benefits only, you may submit an application directly to Great Eastern Life.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my co-owner and I are both insured under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) for 75% each, what will happen after my co-owner has claimed the HPS benefits?
questions.text:
Upon approval of your co-owner’s claim, we will pay the sum assured based on his/her 75% share of the HPS cover. After that, your HPS cover will be adjusted to match the remaining 25% of the outstanding housing loan and your premium will be adjusted accordingly.
This means that you will still be covered by the HPS for your share of the loan, and your premiums will be adjusted accordingly.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: My family member has passed on. How do I check if they were covered under the Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If your family member was covered under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), his/her coverage status will be made available for viewing by his/her CPF nominee(s) on the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard.
Alternatively, you may write to us by selecting “Home ownership” as the Subject and “Protecting against losing your home” as the Category to find out more.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I need to inform the Board to terminate the housing monthly instalment from my CPF account if my housing loan is fully paid by the Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text: You do not need to do anything. If your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) sum assured has fully paid off your outstanding home loan, CPF Board will work with your mortgage provider to stop deducting money from the CPF accounts of all the joint-owner(s).
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How do I check the status of my Home Protection Scheme claim application on terminal illness or total permanent disability?
questions.text: To check the status of your Home Protection Scheme claim application on terminal illness or total permanent disability, you can login to CPF website, click on ‘my CPF’, followed by ‘Activities’.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Do I have to submit employment information for Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text: Yes, for claims under Home Protection Scheme, you are required to inform your employer to fill in this form as we require your employment information. The employment information will allow CPFB to accurately determine your claim event date and amount of claim benefits. Your employer would require a Corppass to login.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How can I claim Home Protection Scheme benefits under medical grounds on behalf of my next-of-kin who lacks mental capacity?
questions.text:
As an appointed donee / deputy for your next-of-kin, you can claim his insurance benefits and withdraw CPF savings due to Reduced Life Expectancy by completing this form and submitting the required documents as listed in the form. The form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings.
Upon receipt of the completed form and supporting document(s), CPF Board and Great Eastern Life (for DPS) will review the application and follow up with you.
If you are not the appointed donee/deputy, you can write to us for further assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I choose to switch to Annual Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) if I am currently insured under the Single Premium HPS?
questions.text: If you are currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS), you cannot choose to switch to the Annual Premium HPS. The Annual Premium HPS is only applicable to those who joined HPS on or after 1 March 2001.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). How can I extend my HPS cover until age 65?
questions.text:
Your Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will only insure you up to age 55 or 60. If your original housing loan is still outstanding by then, we will extend your HPS cover to age 65 by issuing you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover when your Single Premium HPS cover expires.
However, if you had restructured your housing loan and had been previously rejected by CPF Board for an increase to your HPS cover period or sum assured arising from the changes to your housing loan, you will not be eligible for the additional AP cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme (HPS). Do I have to pay additional premiums when my HPS cover is extended to age 65?
questions.text: If you are insured under the Single Premium Home Protection Scheme and wish to extend your coverage to age 65, you will need to pay additional premiums. This premium will be paid annually.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if there are changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If your loan repayment period or loan amount has reduced, your Single Premium (SP) Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will be terminated. We will issue you an Annual Premium (AP) HPS cover based on your new outstanding housing loan. Any surrender value of your SP HPS cover will be paid to your CPF Ordinary Account.
However, if the changes to your housing loan result in an increase in your HPS cover, such as an increase in cover period or sum assured, obtaining an additional AP cover will be subject to you being in good health. If you are not eligible for the additional cover, you will remain insured under your SP cover.
Do I need to inform the Board to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover if I make a partial repayment of my loan?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What will happen to my Single Premium Home Protection Scheme cover if I change my share of cover but there are no changes to my outstanding housing loan?
questions.text:
If you have changed your share of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover without making any changes to your outstanding housing loan, you will remain covered under the Single Premium (SP) HPS.
Once the adjustment is approved, your SP HPS cover will be adjusted accordingly to the new percentage declared. However, please note that any increase in your HPS coverage is subject to approval and you being in good health.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Is there a maximum amount that I can save in my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You can save up to the prevailing Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in your MediSave Account (MA) if you have not turned age 65. It is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.
From 1 January 2026, the BHS is $79,000 for all CPF members aged 65 years and below. The BHS applicable to you will be adjusted yearly to keep pace with rising healthcare consumption until you turn age 65. For example, if you are aged 65 years old in 2026, your applicable BHS will be fixed at $79,000 for the rest of your life. questions.title: If I work after age 65, do I still need to contribute to my MediSave Account?
questions.text: As long as you continue to work, you will need to contribute to your MediSave Account (MA). These contributions will accumulate up to the Basic Healthcare Sum and help cover your medical expenses during retirement.

questions.title: How is the Basic Healthcare Sum determined?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum is an estimate of your likely medical expenses from age 65 onwards. It is determined based on past trends in MediSave usage among the elderly and is intended to cover your own basic subsidised healthcare expenses, as well as health and long-term care insurance premiums during old age.

questions.title: Why is the Basic Healthcare Sum adjusted yearly?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted annually for cohorts below age 65 to ensure it remains relevant and keeps pace with rising healthcare consumption, especially with increasing healthcare costs and expansions in MediSave usage.
For each cohort, the BHS is fixed from age 65 onwards and remains the same for the rest of their lives. This helps members save adequately for their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age, while providing certainty on the amount they need to set aside in their MediSave Account.

questions.title: As an employee, how much do I contribute to my MediSave Account (MA)?
questions.text: A portion of your monthly CPF contributions is allocated to your MediSave Account depending on your age group. You can refer to the CPF contribution and allocation rates.

questions.title: I am a government pensioner receiving lifelong medical benefits. Is the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) applicable to me?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) for government pensioners differs from that of other CPF members in the same cohort, depending on the coverage of their Post-Retirement Medical Benefits Schemes.
The BHS does not apply to government pensioners under the Fixed Amount on Ward Charges Scheme (FAW). All working contributions allocated to their MediSave Account (MA) and any MediSave top-ups will be transferred to their other CPF accounts.
Pensioners under the Co-payment on Ward Charges Scheme (CPW) have a lower BHS than other CPF members in their cohort. Once this BHS is reached, any working contributions allocated to their MA and any MediSave top-ups will be transferred to their other CPF accounts.
Pensioners under the Comprehensive Co-Payment Scheme (CCS) and MediSave-cum-Subsidised Outpatient (MSO) Scheme will have the same BHS as other CPF members in their cohort.
Dependants of pensioners will also have the same BHS as other CPF members in their cohort. They can refer to the FAQ ‘What is the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn 65 years old?’ to find out their applicable BHS.

questions.title: What happens if I do not have the Basic Healthcare Sum when I turn age 65?
questions.text: The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MediSave Account (MA) to cover your basic subsidised healthcare expenses in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. If your balance is less than the cohort BHS at age 65, you are not required to top up your MA. However, if you wish to build up your healthcare savings, you can choose to top up your MA with cash. You can do so via this form to make cash top-ups to your own or your loved ones’ MA.

questions.title: What is the Basic Healthcare Sum?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MediSave Account (MA) to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.
For CPF members below age 65, the BHS is adjusted annually to keep pace with rising healthcare consumption. This ensures that the BHS remains relevant when each cohort reaches retirement age.
Once CPF members reach age 65, their BHS is fixed and will remain unchanged for the rest of their lives.
For CPF members below age 65 in 2026
The prevailing BHS is $79,000 , and will be adjusted yearly.
For CPF members who turn age 65 in 2026
The cohort BHS is $79,000 and will remain fixed thereafter.
