questions.title: What is MediSave?
questions.text:
MediSave is a national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement.
Saving for future medical expenses is important, as the need for medical care and hospitalisation increases significantly as one grows older. It is important that you spend your MediSave savings prudently.
MediSave can be used for hospitalisation and day surgery expenses. MediSave can also be used to pay for certain costly outpatient treatments like dialysis, cancer drugs and radiotherapy, as well as treatment for a number of chronic diseases like diabetes and hypertension. Those with severe disability can also tap on MediSave Care for their long-term care needs. You can refer to the MOH website for the uses of MediSave and the withdrawal limits.
Additionally, MediSave can also be used to pay the premiums of approved medical insurance schemes like MediShield Life. If you want additional coverage for your bills in private hospitals, or A and B1 ward types in public hospitals, you can use your MediSave to help pay for an Integrated Shield Plan from an approved private insurer. These plans are integrated with MediShield Life to provide additional medical coverage on top of MediShield Life.
MediSave can also be used to pay the premiums of approved long-term insurance schemes like CareShield Life and ElderShield. For those under CareShield Life who would like additional coverage, you may also use your MediSave to help pay for Supplements from approved private insurers. You can refer to the CareShield Life for more information.

questions.title: What is not covered under the MediSave scheme?
questions.text: MediSave generally does not cover optional and cosmetic treatments, accident and emergency (A&E) fees and non-medical treatments such as ambulance transport. Please approach the medical institution to find out whether your treatment can be covered under MediSave.

questions.title: Are there additional charges for using my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text: CPF Board does not impose any administrative fee for using MediSave.

questions.title: What happens to my MediSave if I do not use it?
questions.text:
Any unused MediSave savings will remain in your MediSave Account and grow with interest.
Learn more about CPF interest rates.

questions.title: What is the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)?
questions.text:
When you seek medical treatment at a Medical Institution (MI) participating in the MediSave scheme, the MI staff will inform you if your MediSave can be used for the treatment as well as the amount you may use.
If you intend to use MediSave for your treatment, you will need to complete the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) provided by the MI staff, and authorise them to submit the claim on your behalf.
There are two types of MCAF available:
1. MCAF (Single Institution)
To authorise a specific Medical Institution (MI) to submit MediSave claim(s) for your own and/or your family member(s) medical expenses that can tap on MediSave. If you have ongoing outpatient treatments at the MI, you can provide authorisation for a specific visit, a specific time period, or a standing authorisation until you revoke it.
2. MCAF (Multiple Institutions)
To authorise all Public Healthcare Institutions (PHI) from now on to submit MediSave claims for your own medical expenses that can tap on MediSave. This means that if you have authorised via MCAF (Multiple Institutions) at one PHI – for example, a hospital, and subsequently visited another PHI such as a polyclinic, the polyclinic need not seek your consent again to claim the medical expenses on your behalf from your MediSave. The authorisation will remain valid until you revoke it.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my siblings' insurance premiums for schemes such as MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans or ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement?
questions.text: Yes. Since 1 June 2019, members may use their MediSave to pay for their siblings' insurance premiums.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my siblings' medical expenses?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your siblings' medical expenses, as long as they are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents (SC/PR). You would have to provide proof to the medical institutions that your siblings are SC/PR (e.g. NRICs).

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the remainder of my medical bill that is not covered under my pensioner benefits?
questions.text:
You can use your own or your immediate family members' (i.e. spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings) MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill that is not covered under your pensioner benefits, up to the MediSave withdrawal limits. The expenses incurred must be for medical treatments approved under the MediSave scheme.
If you would like to use your MediSave to pay the remainder of your medical bill, please inform the Medical Institution (MI). You will be required to complete the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), which authorises the MI to use your MediSave to pay the bill. Please note that any amount above the MediSave withdrawal limits would need to be paid in cash.

questions.title: Why am I receiving digital notifications instead of the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement to inform me of a deduction from my MediSave?
questions.text:
As part of our commitment to protect members against fraudulent deductions and to reduce environmental footprint, we have transitioned to digital notifications to inform you of your MediSave deduction for medical expenses. You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
These digital notifications will ensure that you are informed of any deductions made from your MediSave in a timely manner. If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive both digital notification and a hardcopy MediSave transaction statement?
questions.text: You will not be receiving hardcopies of your MediSave transaction statement once you receive notifications digitally. This will aid us in our pursuit to reduce the use of paper.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement instead?
questions.text:
Notification through hardcopy statements will result in a delay in informing you of deductions made from your MediSave account. It will also contribute to the usage of paper, which is not environmentally friendly.
We encourage members to join us in our efforts to go digital and reduce our environmental footprint, while enjoying the convenience of timely notifications.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my overseas medical treatment if I am living overseas for the long term?
questions.text:
As MediSave is primarily meant for medical treatment in Singapore, it does not cover overseas medical expenses for those residing overseas for the long term. This is a common feature of national healthcare systems in many countries.
If you are residing overseas for the long term, please consider obtaining medical coverage to meet your overseas healthcare needs.

questions.title: I have directed a medical institution to submit a claim on my behalf. However, I would like to make an amendment to that claim. What should I do?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution that submitted the claim on your behalf for assistance.

questions.title: I do not have a Singpass account. How will I be notified of my MediSave deduction?
questions.text:
You will be notified of your MediSave deduction digitally via your contact details maintained with CPF Board.
We strongly encourage you to update your contact details with us using Singpass to obtain timely notification of your MediSave deduction.
Having a Singpass account provides added convenience and security when accessing Singapore government services. You can register a Singpass account by following the instructions on the Singpass website.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for hearing aids?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used for the purchase of hearing aids. This is because MediSave is primarily designed to help Singaporeans offset costly hospitalisations, day surgeries and selected outpatient treatments.
However, you may apply for the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF) which provides subsidies to eligible seniors for a range of assistive devices, including hearing aids. You can call the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at 1800 650 6060* or visit AIC website for more details.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: Can I withdraw my MediSave in cash?
questions.text:
MediSave is primarily designed to help Singaporeans save up during their working years for their healthcare needs in old age. Generally, MediSave cannot be withdrawn in cash and are instead paid directly to MediSave-accredited medical institutions for approved medical treatments.
However, under MediSave Care, Singaporeans with severe disability aged 30 and above may withdraw up to $200 per month in cash from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave account(s). This is because long-term care needs vary significantly across such individuals, and cash withdrawals will provide patients and their caregivers the flexibility to decide on their desired care arrangements and long-term care services. You may refer to AIC’s website and our FAQ for more details on MediSave Care.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will continue to review their financing policies to ensure that care remains affordable for our citizens, while MediSave balances are not depleted prematurely.

questions.title: Why are MediSave withdrawal limits imposed?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to pay for a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills like chemotherapy and dialysis.
To ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account for their basic healthcare needs in old age, MediSave withdrawal limits have been carefully set to strike a balance between the affordability of current treatments and future healthcare needs. These limits, after taking into account Government subsidies and applicable MediShield Life payouts, are generally adequate to cover most of the charges incurred at subsidised inpatient wards and outpatient treatments.
The Ministry of Health reviews the MediSave withdrawal limits from time to time to ensure that they remain relevant to healthcare costs and Singaporeans’ needs.

questions.title: What is the healthcare hotline?
questions.text:
For healthcare-related enquires, you may call us at 1800 222 3399* / 65 6222 3399 (overseas) from Mondays to Fridays, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8, excluding public holidays). Alternatively, you can also write to us.
* Airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: What is the MediSave Grant for Newborns?
questions.text:
The MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) is a MediSave grant to help parents defray their child’s healthcare expenses, such as MediShield Life premiums, recommended childhood vaccinations, hospitalisation, and approved outpatient treatments.
All Singapore Citizen newborns born on or after 26 August 2012 are eligible. Those born on or after 26 August 2012, but before 1 January 2015 are eligible for a grant of $3,000. Those born on or after 1 January 2015, but before 1 April 2025 are eligible for the MGN of $4,000. Those born on or after 1 April 2025 are eligible for the MGN of $5,000.
A CPF MediSave account will be opened for each newborn, and the grant will be credited automatically to your newborn's MediSave account within a week from the registration of birth1, or from the date when Singapore Citizenship was granted2.
For more information on the MediSave Grant for Newborns, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.
1 If your child is a Singapore Citizen at birth.
2 If your child is a Singapore Citizen by registration

questions.title: Why was I notified of my MediSave deduction via a different notification mode before and after 12 June 2023?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous effort to enhance our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These changes were made to ensure alignment with other types of notifications that our members receive from us.
With effect from 12 June 2023, we have started notifying members of their MediSave deductions for medical expenses via email or SMS using their contact details maintained with CPF Board. You may verify that the notification is legitimate by checking that that the sender’s email address ends with @e.cpf.gov.sg, and the SMS sender ID is 'gov.sg'. The SMS will also begin with "Central Provident Fund Board".
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
We encourage you to keep your contact details updated so that you can receive timely notifications. You may update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes take effect.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for my own or an approved dependant's day surgery bills?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave:
Up to $830 per day for ward charges; and
Between $240 and $5,290 for your surgical procedures, depending on the type of procedures performed.
You can use up to the same withdrawal limit for each approved dependant. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: I am going for a day surgery. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for the removal of my wisdom tooth?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave savings to pay for the removal of your wisdom tooth incurred at a participating private dental clinic under the MediSave Scheme, provided that it is a surgical procedure. The day surgery limits are:
1) Day surgeryUp to a maximum of $830 per day for daily hospital charges, including investigations, medicines and doctor's attendance fees.
2) OperationA fixed limit for operations ranging from $240 to $5,290 depending on the type of operations performed.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my dental implant?
questions.text:
You can use MediSave to pay for your dental implant insertion or removal as long as it is a surgical procedure.
For a dental surgery with insertion or removal of dental implants, you can use MediSave to pay for your dental implants, up to the following limits:
Insertion of Dental Implants
Number of implant(s) inserted x $1,120 Operation limit of Table 2C
Removal of Dental Implants
Number of implant(s) removed x $490 Operation limit of Table 1C
For example, if you have to insert two dental implants, you can use up to $2,240 (2 x $1,120) for payment of your dental implants.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my colonoscopy screening?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for colonoscopy screening at all public healthcare institutions and approved private hospitals and medical institutions, provided you are aged 50 years old and above and it is a day surgery procedure. The day surgery limits are:
1) Day Surgery
Up to a maximum of $830 per day for daily hospital charges, including investigations, medicines and doctor's attendance fees.
2) Operation
A fixed operation limit of either $1,120 or $1,390, depending on the type of operations performed.

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment in a hospital. How do I know if I can use my MediSave in that hospital?
questions.text:
Please refer to this list of medical institutions or day surgery centres participating in the MediSave scheme.
To use your MediSave, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: What types of hospital charges can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text: You can use your MediSave for your hospitalisation, surgery, and rehabilitation charges.

questions.title: What happens if my employer or insurer is paying part of my hospital expenses?
questions.text:
If you have given the hospital a Letter of Guarantee or Hospitalisation Identity Card at admission, the hospital will send the bill to your employer or insurer. Your employer or insurer will then work out the part of the bill to be paid by you. They will then ask you to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) if you wish to pay the amount from your MediSave Account (MA).
When your employer or insurer returns the MCAF to the hospital, the hospital will arrange to deduct the amount from your MA.
Some hospitals may request that you sign the MCAF at admission especially if your employer or insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses.

questions.title: If I am hospitalised, how much MediSave can I use to pay for my hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
For daily hospital charges1, you can use up to $1,130 per day from MediSave for the first two days of inpatient stays, and $400 per day thereafter.
If you had undergone a surgery, you can use your MediSave to cover part of, or the whole surgery cost. The amount of MediSave you can use depends on the complexity of your surgery, as listed in the Table of Surgical Procedures. You may refer to the MOH website for more information on withdrawal limits for MediSave.
It is useful to note that you are considered hospitalised if you have been admitted for at least eight hours. This requirement does not apply to day surgeries.
1 Includes eligible Mobile Inpatient Care @ Home stays

questions.title: I do not have enough MediSave to pay for my hospitalisation expenses. Are there other ways to pay for it?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses, you may consider tapping on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
It is important to note that while you can tap on your immediate family members' MediSave, the amount you can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis. If you still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after using up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.
For more information, please speak to the staff at the hospital's Business Office.
You should use your MediSave prudently to provide for your own and your approved dependant's hospitalisation needs. This is because you may require more medical care in your old age.

questions.title: What if my hospital bill is more than what my MediSave can cover?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sufficient to cover bills incurred in B2 or C ward types in a public hospital. This restriction is necessary to prevent premature depletion of your MediSave, as your MediSave savings are to last through your lifetime. This is particularly important as elderly people may require more hospital stays and medical care than younger ones. If there is any part of the hospital bill that MediSave is unable to cover, you will need to pay in cash.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for overseas treatment/hospitalisation?
questions.text:
Use of MediSave for Overseas Treatment - Elective
Patients who are Singaporeans (SC) or Permanent Residents (PR) may use their own or their immediate family member's MediSave for overseas elective treatments at accredited hospitals, subject to the applicable MediSave withdrawal limits. Immediate family members include spouses, children, parents, siblings and/or grandchildren.
To use MediSave for overseas treatment, patients must obtain a referral from MediSave-accredited healthcare provider, Health Management International (HMI). They can contact HMI directly to check if HMI has affiliated hospital(s) in the country where they wish to receive treatment. Please visit the HMI website or call HMI at 6322 6333 for more information.
Use of MediSave for Overseas Treatment - Medical Emergency/Treatment not Available in Singapore
MediSave is primarily meant to help Singaporeans and Permanent Residents pay for their major inpatient hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient expenses locally. When travelling overseas, CPF members should consider purchasing travel insurance to protect against the risk of incurring unforeseen medical expenses.
Requests to use MediSave for overseas emergency treatments will be considered on a case-by-case basis if the following conditions are first fulfilled:
The patient must be a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) of Singapore (Please note that the patient may appeal to use his/her or their immediate family members' MediSave to pay for their own overseas hospitalisations. Immediate family members include member’s spouse, children, parents, siblings and/or grandparents.); and
The use of MediSave is only limited to inpatient admission that exceeds a minimum of eight hours or day surgery, which has been assessed to be a medical emergency by our Medical Advisors. It cannot be used for outpatient treatments.
If the above conditions are fufilled, please submit your request along with the following supporting documents through the Ministry of Health (MOH) feedback form:
Original copy (Certified true copy by Hospital is accepted) of the patient's medical records - Discharge summary, operation notes (if any) or clinical notes showing the history, diagnosis and treatment plan for the patient.
Original copy (Certified true copy by Hospital is accepted) of the final hospital bill for the patient.
Passport information - showing passport holder and the entry/departure of the foreign country.
Completed Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), to authorise the use of MediSave upon an approval. You may find a copy of the MCAF on the MOH website.
NRIC – Front and back copy belonging to patient and MediSave payer (if applicable).
The above documents must be in English, or be officially translated into English.
Should your request be approved by MOH, CPF Board will process the MediSave deduction and pay the money to the MediSave payer’s bank account as maintained in CPF Board’s records. The MediSave payer may confirm or update his/her bank account via my cpf digital services – Account settings.

questions.title: My approved dependant is a foreigner, while I am a Singapore Permanent Resident. He/She has incurred medical expenses in Singapore. Can I use my MediSave to pay for his/her bills?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant's medical bills, if it is a MediSave-approved treatment incurred at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my step/adopted children's hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
If your step children are under your custody, they are considered your approved dependants, and you can use your MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses.
To use your MediSave for your adopted children, you need to submit legal documentary proof of your relationship to the hospital. If the legal process of adoption is still underway, you should submit the following documents to the hospital:
a. A lawyer's letter stating that the legal adoption is underway, and
b. The birth certificate within one year of your child's date of birth.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for the medical treatments received by dependants other than my approved dependants (spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings)?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help you save for your personal or approved dependant's healthcare expenses incurred in any of the participating medical institutions (MIs) under the MediSave Scheme.
You can apply to use your MediSave for a dependant who is not your approved dependant, if the dependant is receiving treatment in a public healthcare institution or voluntary welfare organisation in Singapore. Please approach the medical institution's Business Office for more details on the eligibility criteria and the application process. Such applications will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for optional/cosmetic treatments like liposuction, orthodontics treatment or laser surgery to correct short-sightedness?
questions.text: Generally, MediSave cannot be used for optional/cosmetic treatments. Please check with your attending doctor if the cost of your treatment can be covered by your MediSave.

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I still use my MediSave?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave to pay for your own or your approved dependants' healthcare expenses even if you have declared bankruptcy. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Can MediSave be used for a deceased member's last hospitalisation bill?
questions.text:
The deceased member's MediSave can be used fully, without being subjected to the existing MediSave withdrawal limits to pay the last medical bill, if the member has passed away during his hospitalisation.
If the deceased member had not signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) before his death, his spouse, parent or child aged 21 and above, or Donee/Deputy appointed under the Mental Capacity Act, has to quickly sign the MCAF on behalf of the deceased member to authorise the hospital to submit a claim, before the deceased's CPF funds including MediSave, is disbursed to his nominees or the Public Trustee Office.
If the deceased member does not have a spouse, parent or child aged 21 and above, or Donee/Deputy, a next of kin (NOK) who has been taking care of the deceased can inform the hospital of his intention to sign the MCAF on behalf of the deceased member. The hospital will then seek approval from MOH on behalf of the NOK, before the NOK signs the MCAF.
If more than one MediSave Account (MA) holders had authorised the use of their MediSave to pay the medical bill of the deceased member before his demise and one of the MA belongs to the deceased, the protocol on the use of MediSave from the various accounts are as follows:
The deceased member's MediSave will be used first to pay off the last medical bill without being subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits.
If the deceased member's MediSave is not sufficient to pay the last medical bill, the MediSave from the other account holder(s) can then be used, provided that the MediSave withdrawn from the deceased member's account does not exceed the MediSave withdrawal limits.
Example whereby the MediSave withdrawal limit has been reached
Patient passes away with a final hospitalisation bill of $5,000, after staying in the hospital for five days without surgical treatment.
Patient's MediSave Balance = $4,000
$4,000 can be paid from the patient's MediSave and the remainder of $1,000 must be paid by cash. The patient's spouse, child, parent, grandchild or sibling's MediSave cannot be used as the maximum MediSave Withdrawal Limit of $2,300 has been reached.
Example whereby the MediSave withdrawal limit has not been reached
Patient passes away with a final hospitalisation bill of $5,000, after staying in the hospital for five days without surgical treatment.
Patient's MediSave Balance = $1,500
$1,500 can be paid from the patient's MediSave and a further $800 can be paid from the MediSave of the patient's spouse, child, parent, grandchild or sibling, up to the maximum MediSave Withdrawal Limit of $2,300. The remaining $2,700 of the bill needs to be settled with cash.

questions.title: What outpatient treatments can be paid using MediSave and what are the withdrawal limits?
questions.text: Please refer to the MOH website for the list of outpatient treatments that can be paid using MediSave and their corresponding withdrawal limits.

questions.title: I visited a clinic for an outpatient treatment that can be paid by my MediSave. How do I go about utilising my MediSave?
questions.text:
To use your MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
1. Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your approved dependant, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
2. The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass. This is not needed if the clinic can check on your behalf.
3. You and the patient (if applicable) must sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your MediSave to pay for the outpatient medical treatment bill.
4. If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my approved dependant's renal dialysis?
questions.text:
You may use your MediSave to pay for approved dependent’s renal dialysis treatment costs, up to a limit of $450 per month per patient.
Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
To use your MediSave to pay for your approved dependant’s renal dialysis treatment costs, please complete a Medical Claims Authorisation Form at dialysis centres.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for Traditional Chinese Medicine?
questions.text: If you are aged 60 and above, you may withdraw up to $400 per year from your own, or your spouse’s MediSave Account under the Flexi-MediSave scheme to pay for acupuncture treatment for lower back pain and neck pain at specialist outpatient clinics in public hospitals.

questions.title: How are claim limits for MediShield Life and MediSave determined when more than one cancer drug is used in the treatment?
questions.text:
Patients who need more than one cancer drug treatment on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) in a month may claim up to the higher of the MediShield Life, MediSave and Integrated Shield Plan (IPs) claim limits applicable for the individual treatments.
For example, if a patient uses both Treatments X (MediShield Life claim limit of $2,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) and Y (MediShield Life claim limit of $1,000 & MediSave withdrawal limit of $600) in a month, the patient may claim no more than $2,000 from MediShield Life and withdraw no more than $600 from MediSave in that month.
Please consult your doctor if you wish to clarify the claim limit that will apply for your treatment.

questions.title: What if I need a treatment which is not on the Cancer Drug List (CDL), or is on the CDL but unsubsidised, and I cannot afford the treatment without insurance?
questions.text:
We encourage you to discuss with your doctor if there are suitable alternative treatments on the Cancer Drug List (CDL) that are subsidised and covered by insurance. However, if switching treatments is not feasible, there is support to help you if you face difficulty affording your treatment.
If you are a subsidised patient, you can approach a Medical Social Worker (MSW) in your public healthcare institution (PHI) for financial assistance such as MediFund. If you are a private patient, you can approach your doctor to refer you to a PHI for subsidised care. The PHI’s medical team will review your treatment plan and provide financial counselling (e.g., eligibility for subsidies) before you decide whether to transfer.
To help existing patients during this transition, MOH will provide additional financial support for all PHI patients without an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), and who had started treatments that are unsubsidised or not on the CDL before 1 September 2022. Insurers, on their part, will continue their current coverage until 30 September 2023 for patients with IP that are being renewed between 1 April 2023 and 30 September 2023, and who are on a course of cancer drug treatment as of 31 March 2023.

questions.title: What is outpatient Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave allows members aged 60 years old and above to use their MediSave or their spouse's MediSave (if the spouse is also aged 60 and above), up to $400 a year, for outpatient medical treatments at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Please note that the $400 is applied on a per patient basis, regardless whether you are using your MediSave or your spouse's MediSave.

questions.title: I am aged 65 years old, and I would like to use my Flexi-MediSave to pay for my father's outpatient medical treatment cost at a polyclinic. Can I do so?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave can only be used for your own or your spouse's outpatient medical treatment expenses.

questions.title: My child is paying for my chronic disease treatment under the MediSave500/700 scheme. Can I also tap on my spouse's Flexi-MediSave to pay for the co-payment?
questions.text:
If both you and your spouse are aged 60 years old or above, you can use your spouse's Flexi-MediSave for the 15% co-payment.
Also, if you have reached the withdrawal limit for chronic disease treatment, you can tap on your own or your spouse's Flexi-MediSave to continue reducing the cash payment, provided that you have not reached the $400 withdrawal limit.

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of times I can use Flexi-MediSave for my outpatient treatments in a year?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of Flexi-MediSave claims you may make in a year. However, you can only use up to $400 in a calendar year.

questions.title: Is there a minimum bill amount before I can use Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text: There is no minimum bill amount before Flexi-MediSave can be used. However, as smaller amounts of cash payment are generally affordable, patients may wish to conserve the use of their Flexi-MediSave for larger outpatient bills, e.g. above $20 - $30.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave for some outpatient medical treatments this year, and would like to know how much more I can use under Flexi-MediSave. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can check how much more you can use under Flexi-MediSave through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' from the menu bar or scroll down to the 'Utilisation of healthcare benefits' section for 'Additional benefits for the elderly (Flexi-MediSave)'
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select 'Healthcare' from the menu bar for 'Flexi-MediSave'

questions.title: I visited a clinic for an outpatient medical treatment that can be paid by my Flexi-MediSave. How do I go about using my Flexi-MediSave?
questions.text:
To use your Flexi-MediSave for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your spouse, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport.
The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services, with your Singpass.
You and the patient (if applicable) will need to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your Flexi-MediSave to pay for the outpatient medical treatment bill.
If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic already has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: What can I use Flexi-MediSave for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used for outpatient medical treatments (i.e. visits that do not involve a hospital stay or day surgery) received at polyclinics, public hospital Specialist Outpatient Clinics and general practitioner clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave can cover consultation fees, select restorative dental procedures, tests and drugs, and other services such as physiotherapy, if ordered by your doctor for diagnosis or treatment of your medical condition.
Please refer to this FAQ for medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for.

questions.title: Are there any medical expenses that Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave aims to help elderly patients reduce their cash payment, with the focus on outpatient medical treatment.
It cannot be used for treatments that are for non-medical purposes, such as those for cosmetic or lifestyle purposes (e.g. hair loss, slimming, and erectile dysfunction). It also cannot be used to pay for items from the retail pharmacies, such as skincare products. Non-medical charges such as administrative fees are also not covered.
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for admissions to the Accident and Emergency department and cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.

questions.title: If I have used up other MediSave limits - for example, for scans or for cancer drug treatment, can I use Flexi-MediSave to pay?
questions.text:
If you are already using MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment but have reached your withdrawal limit, you can use Flexi-MediSave to further lower your cash payment, provided that treatment was sought at a polyclinic, public specialist outpatient clinic or general practitioner clinic participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).
Flexi-MediSave cannot be used for cancer drug treatments using cancer drugs that are not on the Cancer Drug List.
However, as Flexi-MediSave covers a much wider range of outpatient treatments than other limits, you may want to save the use of your Flexi-MediSave for treatments that are not already covered by MediSave so as to lower your total cash payments.

questions.title: I intend to seek treatment at a general practitioner (GP) clinic at my void deck. How do I know if I can use my Flexi-MediSave there?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave can be used at:
Polyclinics,
Specialist Outpatient Clinics in the public hospitals and national specialty centres, and
Medical general practitioner (GP) clinics participating in the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) scheme.
The list of participating CHAS medical GP clinics can be found at the following websites:
CHAS
Ministry of Health

questions.title: Is Flexi-MediSave applicable only to the Pioneer Generation or all elderly?
questions.text: Flexi-MediSave applies to all elderly aged 60 and above.

questions.title: Why is Flexi-MediSave only applicable to elderly members aged 60 years old and above?
questions.text:
MediSave is meant to help Singaporeans pay for their more costly medical expenses, especially after retirement. Older Singaporeans usually incur more healthcare expenses as outpatient medical treatments tends to be more expensive for them, while having lower or no income if they have retired. The Flexi-MediSave scheme helps them by allowing them to use MediSave more flexibly to reduce their out-of-pocket expenses for outpatient medical care.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will regularly review Flexi-MediSave and other financing policies to ensure that outpatient care remains affordable for all Singaporeans.

questions.title: What vaccinations can MediSave be used for?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for the following vaccinations received at any of the approved medical institutions in Singapore. Please refer to the list of approved medical institutions that provide these vaccinations.
For a list of MediSave-approved clinics under the MediSave500/700 scheme, please visit the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) webpage.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use to pay for approved vaccinations for myself?
questions.text:
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. The same yearly withdrawal limit applies for approved chronic disease treatments and health screening.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for outpatient treatment of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
You can use MediSave for outpatient treatments of the chronic diseases listed below.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) regularly reviews the list of conditions covered under the Chronic Disease Management Programme, to ensure that they continue to meet the needs of Singaporeans.
For more information, please visit the Ministry of Health website.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use for my outpatient treatments of chronic diseases?
questions.text:
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to fully pay for my chronic diseases treatment?
questions.text: You only need to co-pay 15% of the bill for your chronic diseases treatment in cash before using MediSave to pay the rest, except for treatments received at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic. You may find out more about Healthier SG and search for a clinic near you to enrol into one. This is to help you conserve some of your MediSave savings for future healthcare needs.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave for some outpatient treatments of my chronic disease this year, and would like to know how much more I can use. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can check how much more MediSave you can use for outpatient treatments of your chronic disease through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" from the menu bar or scroll down to the "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" section for "Treatments for chronic illnesses (MediSave500/700)"
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select "My Healthcare" from the menu bar for "Outpatient Treatment"

questions.title: I want to pay for my outpatient treatment for chronic disease using MediSave. How can I do so?
questions.text:
To use your MediSave for your outpatient medical treatment cost:
1. Inform the clinic that you wish to use MediSave to pay for your outpatient medical treatment. The staff will require your NRIC/Passport. If you are paying for your approved dependant, please also produce his/her NRIC/Passport. Approved dependants refer to spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. Please note that your grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
2. The clinic may require information on how much MediSave is available for payment of the outpatient treatment. You will be able to obtain this information by logging in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services, with your Singpass.
3. You and the patient (if applicable) will need to sign a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to allow the clinic to use your MediSave to pay for the outpatient treatment bill.
4. If your employer or insurer is also paying for your outpatient treatment, please bring along your Letter of Guarantee or Employer Identity Pass (i.e. if your clinic already has an existing arrangement with your employer or insurer).

questions.title: How was the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit sized?
questions.text: The MediSave withdrawal limits are generally sized to cover subsidised bills, so that the healthcare costs remain affordable.

questions.title: I have signed up for an approved chronic disease treatment package or an approved vaccination package with my healthcare provider. May I use my MediSave to pay for the package?
questions.text: You may use your MediSave for approved treatments under the MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit. Your healthcare provider will be able to help you to submit a MediSave claim for each treatment of the package. Please contact your healthcare provider for assistance.

questions.title: How do I know if I am eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 under MediSave500/700?
questions.text:
The withdrawal limit under the MediSave500/700 is determined based on the complexity of your chronic condition(s).
You will be eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 per year, if you were treated for two or more conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), or one CDMP condition with complications within a year.
You can check if you are eligible for the higher withdrawal limit of $700 through:
a. my cpf digital services
• Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass
• Select "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" from the menu bar or scroll down to the "Utilisation of healthcare benefits" section for "Treatments for chronic illnesses (MediSave500/700)"
• Check if the "Total withdrawal limit" is $700
b. CPF Mobile app
• Download CPF Mobile app
• Log in using your Singpass
• Select "My Healthcare" from the menu bar and check if the limit is $700 under "Outpatient Treatment"

questions.title: I was diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year. How does this affect my MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit?
questions.text: If you are diagnosed with a complex chronic condition in the middle of the year, your MediSave 500/700 withdrawal limit will automatically be increased from $500 to $700, and the new limit will apply for the entire year.

questions.title: I am a patient with a complex chronic condition. Will I enjoy the higher withdrawal limit of $700 under MediSave500/700 even after my condition improves?
questions.text: The MediSave500/700 withdrawal limit is a yearly limit. This means that you will continue to be able to withdraw up to $700 in the new year if you have had visits for two or more conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), or one CDMP condition with complications in that year.

questions.title: If I have used $500 from my MediSave account for my treatment under MediSave500, can I still withdraw from my family members' MediSave accounts to pay for my treatment?
questions.text: From 1 January 2021, each patient is eligible to withdraw up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for non-complex chronic patients) for their own treatment, regardless of how many MediSave accounts are being withdrawn from.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for my mammogram screening?
questions.text:
If you are aged 50 years old or above, you can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave or your immediate family members' MediSave for your mammogram screening.
Your immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. To use your grandchildren's or siblings' MediSave, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

questions.title: I am concerned of the state of my health, and would like to go for some health screenings. Can I use my MediSave for them?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for your own or your approved dependants' outpatient scans or health screenings at the participating medical institutions. Approved dependants refer to your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. Please note that your grandchildren and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
The use of MediSave for mammograms are for female patients aged 50 years or above. This is in line with recommendations from the Screening Test Review Committee from The Academy of Medicine Singapore.
You may also use MediSave for colonoscopy if you are 50 years old or above, according to the withdrawal limits in the image above.

questions.title: I intend to send my newborn child for health screenings. Which of the health screenings for newborns can be covered by my MediSave?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for the following health screenings for your newborn:
Hearing test
G6P deficiency screening
Metabolic screening
Thyroid function test
You can use up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for patients with non-complex chronic conditions) yearly per patient from your MediSave for your newborn's health screenings.

questions.title: What is the MediSave Maternity Package?
questions.text: The MediSave Maternity Package is a package that allows MediSave to be used to pay expenses incurred during delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses such as consultations, ultrasounds, tests, medications etc.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for my maternity expenses?
questions.text:
MediSave can be used to pay for the delivery and pre-delivery medical expenses.
Pre-delivery expenses have to be claimed under the MediSave Maternity Package. However, post-natal consultation fees cannot be claimed under MediSave.

questions.title: How much MediSave can I use for my maternity expenses?
questions.text:
Under the MediSave Maternity Package, you can use your MediSave for pre-delivery medical expenses, delivery expenses and daily hospital charges.
Each MediSave Maternity Package has a different MediSave withdrawal limit, depending on the delivery procedure (e.g. caesarean or vaginal delivery). If you do not wish to claim for pre-delivery expenses, you can still use your MediSave savings for the delivery procedure and daily hospital charges. Each delivery procedure has a different withdrawal limit.
You may refer to the details on the withdrawal limits for maternity expenses (PDF, 0.1MB).

questions.title: Am I able to use my MediSave for pre-delivery medical expenses before my delivery?
questions.text:
You can only use MediSave for pre-delivery expenses after you have delivered.
You will have to present the bills incurred for pre-delivery medical care to the hospital where you delivered. The hospital will submit these bills, together with the bill for the delivery expenses, for MediSave withdrawal under the MediSave Maternity Package on your behalf.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave for the cost of terminating my pregnancy?
questions.text:
The use of MediSave for termination of pregnancy (TOP) is subject to the MediSave Maternity Package guidelines. This includes a $900 withdrawal limit for your pre-delivery expenses. In addition, if the procedure was conducted in a day surgery setting, you may claim an additional $830 per day for Daily Hospital Charges.
Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving the treatment from to check the specific value of MediSave that can be used. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you on the MediSave usage towards your specific treatment(s) and the expected expenses.

questions.title: I have used my MediSave to pay for my medical expenses. Can my employer or insurer reimburse me in cash?
questions.text: Your employer or insurer cannot reimburse you in cash for the portion of your medical expenses paid using your MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the respective amount must be credited back to your MediSave Account and/or MediShield Life.

questions.title: I have just obtained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. When is the start date of my MediShield Life cover?
questions.text: Your MediShield Life cover will commence on the date that Immigration Checkpoints Authority (ICA) grants you your Permanent Residency status.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life. No application is required.
You will receive a cover issuance or renewal notification about one month before the start or renewal of your MediShield Life cover. The notification will inform you of your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies. If you have children under 21 years old, you will receive their MediShield Life notifications.

questions.title: Why does my child not have a MediShield Life cover to claim for the hospitalisation bills incurred before he passed away?
questions.text:
We are sorry to hear of your child's demise. The MediShield Life claims can be submitted by the medical institution and will be processed if your child was a Singaporean/Singapore Permanent Resident.
Please contact us at 1800-222-3399 or write to us with your child's details.

questions.title: How much can I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life has features such as claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. As such, the amount you can claim from MediShield Life for your bill can only be finalised after the Board processes the completed claim information submitted by the medical institution.
In the meantime, you can use the MediSave and MediShield Life claims calculator to estimate the maximum amount you can withdraw from your MediSave and / or claim from MediShield Life.

questions.title: I intend to visit a clinic/hospital. How do I know if I can use MediShield Life coverage in that clinic/hospital?
questions.text:
You can refer to this list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life.
To make a claim, please inform the staff handling your hospital admission or outpatient treatment that you wish to do so. The staff will submit your claim for you after your authorisation.

questions.title: I wish to check the amount claimed from my MediShield Life coverage for my recent hospitalisation. How can I do so?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediShield Life claims (with transaction dates within the last 15 months from the date of enquiry) at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
1. Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
2. Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims'
3. Select and view the details of your recent healthcare payments and claims. To view more claims, click on 'View past 15 months'.
4. Click on 'View details' under MediShield Life to view the claim details.

questions.title: For those with serious pre-existing conditions, why do they have to pay Additional Premiums for MediShield Life?
questions.text: Those with serious pre-existing conditions pay a higher MediShield Life premium as a reflection of the higher risks they pose to the pool and to fund part of their coverage. The Government will support most of the cost of extending MediShield Life coverage to all Singapore Residents.

questions.title: Can I change my address to receive MediShield Life letters to one not registered under ICA/OSCARS as I am concerned of missing letters or others opening my letters?
questions.text:
MediShield Life letters are sent to your residential address registered with the Immigration Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS). It is an offence for another person to wilfully open letters not addressed to them or to intentionally prevent letters from reaching the recipient under the Postal Services Act.
As part of our efforts to facilitate timelier and up-to-date notifications, you will start to receive MediShield Life notifications digitally in place of hardcopy letters from end 2021.
To receive timely notifications on MediShield Life matters, update your contact information with the following steps:
1. On the CPF homepage (cpf.gov.sg), click “Login” to log on to my cpf digital services with Singpass
2. Click the dropdown button from the top right panel and select "Account settings"
3. Select “Update” to update your contact information. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes take effect.
You can also log in to Healthcare dashboard to check your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: What are the exclusions under the MediShield Life Scheme?
questions.text:
The following treatment items, procedures, conditions, activities are not covered by MediShield Life and cannot be claimed (Applicable for admissions or treatments received on or after 1 March 2021):
Ambulance fees
Cosmetic surgery
Dental work (except due to accidental injuries)
Vaccination
Infertility, sub-fertility, assisted conception or any contraceptive operation, including their related complications (other than surgical procedures associated with freezing of any embryo, egg or ovarian tissue in cases of potential iatrogenic infertility)
Sex change operations, including their related complications
Maternity charges (including Caesarean operations) or abortions, including their related complications, except treatments for serious complications related to pregnancy and childbirth
Treatment of injuries arising from the insured's criminal act
Treatment of injuries arising directly or indirectly from nuclear fallout, war and related risk
Treatment of injuries arising from direct participation in civil commotion, riot or strike
Expenses incurred after the 7th calendar day from being certified to be medically fit for discharge from inpatient treatment and assessed to have a feasible discharge option by a medical practitioner
Surgical interventions, including related complications, for the following rare congenital conditions which are severe and fatal by nature: Trisomy 13, Bilateral Renal Agenesis, Bart's Hydrops and Anencephaly
Optional items which are outside the scope of medical treatment
Overseas medical treatment
Private nursing charges
Purchase of kidney dialysis machines, iron-lung and other special appliances
Treatment which has received reimbursement from Workmen's Compensation and other forms of insurance coverage

questions.title: When will my MediShield Life coverage cease?
questions.text:
Your MediShield Life cover will be terminated when you pass away or renounce your Singapore citizenship/Permanent Residency. Premiums for the unused period will be refunded to the premium payer’s MediSave Account.
The payer may view the refunded premium (if any) at Transaction history statement under “Contributions / Government Cash Grant / Government Top-up".

questions.text:
The deductible is the fixed amount payable by the insured each policy year before any payout from MediShield Life. The deductible is payable only once every policy year. questions.title: Who manages MediShield Life?
questions.text: MediShield Life is administered by the Central Provident Fund Board on behalf of the Ministry of Health.

questions.title: Will checks be conducted for new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
For new Singapore Residents who are covered under MediShield Life, we will have a range of checks, including reviewing medical records after they are covered. They are required to declare their health status upon receipt of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter from the Immigration Checkpoint Authority of Singapore (ICA).
If they are identified to have serious pre-existing medical conditions, they will be subjected to 30% Additional Premiums for 10 years. Those who make false health declarations will be guilty of an offence under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and will be liable to pay penalties.
