topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What are education loan arrears? Are there any penalties for non-payment of monthly instalments?
questions.text: Education loan arrears refer to the amount of monthly loan repayments that have not been paid on time. Arrears will form part of the total outstanding loan, which includes the principal amount and accrued interest, that is repayable to the CPF lender’s Ordinary Account. There are no penalties charged for any missed payments.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why do I still receive notifications from CPF Board regarding my education loan arrears even though I have made repayment via PayNow?
questions.text:
You will receive notifications if there are arrears on your education loan due to missed payments for past and current months. Notifications are sent in two situations:
If you are not on GIRO or your GIRO application is still being processed, any payments made will be used to offset your current month’s payment before offsetting arrears. If the payment is insufficient to cover the total outstanding arrears, you will receive a notification for payment of the outstanding arrears.
If you are on GIRO and there are insufficient funds in your bank account to repay your current month’s instalment, the notification will nudge you to pay for your current month’s instalment and arrears (if any).
All payments received will be used to offset the outstanding education loan and there are no penalties charged for any missed payments.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the crediting sequence for my education loan repayments if I pay via PayNow?
questions.text:
If you are not under any GIRO arrangement or your GIRO application is still being processed, any payment made will be used to offset the outstanding education loan in the following order:
Current month instalment
Arrears (if any)
Partial/ Full lump sum repayment
If you have an active GIRO arrangement, we will deduct the current month’s instalment from your bank account. If you would like to make additional payments towards the arrears, the cash payments will be used to pay the outstanding education loan in the following order:
Arrears (if any)
Partial/ Full lump sum repayment
As long as your GIRO is active, the Board will attempt to deduct the current month’s instalment from your bank account. If the deduction failed due to insufficient funds in your account, we will notify you of the missed payment. You may proceed to make the necessary payments via PayNow only after receiving our notification.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: I am currently studying and have not graduated from the institution. I would like to make a full or partial repayment on my education loan. What do I need to do?
questions.text:
Students (borrowers) may make a full or partial repayment of the education loan before graduation.
The member (lender) must first revoke the use of their CPF savings for the student’s education by completing the "Revoke the use of CPF savings for education" form. In the form, the member must select the option "The student is making an early repayment of the education loan while still studying at the Approved Educational Institution".
Once the revocation is processed, the member will receive an email notification regarding the application status. If the student wishes to make a full or partial repayment prior to graduation, they may check with the member for the repayment details on their 'Activities' page.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Your monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme will be stated in the repayment notification sent to you. Generally, the monthly instalment rate will enable you to fully repay your education loan within six years.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the minimum monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The minimum monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme is $100. The instalment rate stated in the repayment notification will be $100 if this rate is expected to enable you to fully repay the loan within six years. You are encouraged to fully repay the loan within six years to reduce the interest incurred for the loan.
If you have a bigger outstanding loan amount, a higher monthly instalment rate will be stated, to enable you to repay within a period of six years.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I reduce the monthly instalment for my CPF Education Loan stated in my repayment notification?
questions.text:
Reducing the monthly instalment amount will mean a longer repayment period thus incurring more interest on the loan.
Under the Terms & Conditions of the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the loan must be fully repaid within 12 years, which starts one year after you graduate or leave the course of study. Any outstanding balance has to be paid in full before the end of the 12th year. Hence, if you repay at a lower monthly instalment, not only do you incur additional interest due to the prolonged repayment period, you may have to make a lump sum repayment of your outstanding loan at the end of the 12th year.
If you would like to reduce the monthly instalment (subject to a minimum repayment of $100), you may submit your application online through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I increase the monthly instalment for my Education Loan repayment?
questions.text:
You are encouraged to increase the monthly instalment for your education loan repayment if you are financially able to do so. This will enable you to fully repay the loan within a shorter period and hence minimise the interest you have to pay.
If you would like to increase the monthly instalment, you may submit your application online through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I change my monthly instalment for my education loan repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Students (borrowers) may submit an application online to change the monthly instalment payable through "Manage education loan repayments" using their Singpass.
The minimum monthly instalment is $100. Students are encouraged to increase their monthly instalment as this will enable them to fully repay the education loan within a shorter period and hence minimise the accrued interest payable to the member.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there any tool available that can help me project the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may use the online CPF education loan repayment calculator to estimate your monthly instalment rate payable.
You may also check your latest outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there any tool available that can help me project the repayment period under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may use the online CPF education loan repayment calculator to estimate how long it would take to repay your education loan.
You may also check your latest outstanding loan amount by logging in to your Education dashboard with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: When will the change in my monthly instalment rate be effective under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
The effective date for the new monthly instalment rate depends on how you make your payments.
1. Repayment by GIRO: If you pay through GIRO, you will need to submit a request to change the instalment rate before the 15th of the month for it to take effect in the current month. It usually takes one working day to process the request. For example, if the 15th of the month falls on a Sunday, please submit the request by the 12th of the month (Thursday) if you want the new rate to be effective for the current month. Otherwise, the change will only be effective in the following month.
2. Repayment using other payment modes: If you use other payment modes, please change the instalment rate before the end of the month. Generally, it will take one working day to process the request.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my request to change monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: You may check the status of your request to change the monthly instalment rate under the CPF Education Loan Scheme at CPF website by logging in to "Activities" using your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use another person's bank account to repay my CPF education loan?
questions.text: You may authorise the monthly deductions from your own or another person's bank account for the loan repayments under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Please submit a GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" with your Singpass. You will be re-directed to the bank’s ibanking portal to complete the application.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use different bank accounts to repay my education loans for two different courses?
questions.text: Only one bank account may be maintained for repayments under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. If you submit a GIRO form for repayment using a new account, deductions for all the courses that you are repaying will be made from the new account. Please submit a GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" with your Singpass.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Would I receive any acknowledgement after submitting my GIRO application form for the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Generally, you will receive an acknowledgement notification within two weeks upon receipt of your GIRO application form. The notification will indicate the start date of deduction and the monthly instalment rate.
Generally, GIRO applications will be processed within 4 working days for e-application and 21 working days for hardcopy application. Upon receipt of your bank's approval of your GIRO application, we will send a notification to inform you on the approval, together with the start date of the deduction and the monthly instalment rate.
In the meantime, please repay your education loan through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications".
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my GIRO application for repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Your Direct Debit Authorisation / GIRO application for your repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme will be sent to your bank and will generally be processed within 21 working days. We will notify you of the status and effective date of the Direct Debit / GIRO arrangement upon approval.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What is the deduction date if I'm repaying my education loan by GIRO?
questions.text: The GIRO deduction date for repayments under the scheme is on the 20th of every month. If 20th of the month falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, the deduction will be made on the next working day.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I change the bank account for my repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Students (borrowers) will need to submit a new GIRO application through "Set up GIRO for education loan repayments" using Singpass to change the bank account for their repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Students will be re-directed to the bank’s ibanking portal to complete the application. Deductions will continue to be made from the existing bank account until the new account has been verified by the receiving bank.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I terminate my GIRO arrangement for my education loan repayment?
questions.text: You may approach your respective bank directly to terminate the GIRO arrangement for your education loan repayment. Please note that all requests should be submitted and approved before the 15th of each month for the termination to take effect for the current month. Upon termination, all Standing Instruction(s) for repayments will cease. You will need to submit a new GIRO application through "Forms and e-applications" if you want to repay using GIRO in future.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to repay the monies withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: CPF savings cannot be used for repayment of amounts withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan scheme.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why CPF savings cannot be used to repay an outstanding education loan?
questions.text: CPF savings are primarily meant for a member's retirement needs. Allowing the use of CPF savings to repay an outstanding education loan would cause a premature drawdown of your own CPF savings.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Under what circumstances can I apply to defer the repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
Upon notification of the repayment start date for your CPF education loan, you may apply to defer the repayment through "Manage Education Loan Repayments" if you meet any of the following conditions:
Currently studying full-time either locally or overseas; or
Serving full-time National Service; or
Currently unemployed.
Defer repayment or lower monthly instalment rate due to financial difficulties
If you are experiencing financial difficulties repaying your education loan, you may submit a request to either defer your repayment or repay at a lower monthly instalment rate for up to one year. You may submit the request through ‘Write to us’ with the following information:
Reason for deferment or repayment through a lower monthly instalment rate;
Declare that you have sought the CPF lender’s consent to defer the repayment or repay at a lower monthly instalment rate;
Indicate the full name and NRIC of the lender and the loan that you want to defer or repay at a lower instalment rate.
Impact of deferring a repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
Please note that the maximum 12-year repayment period will be reduced by the period of deferment granted. For example, if you have 12 years for repayment and has successfully applied to defer the repayment for two years, the remaining maximum repayment period is 10 years after the deferment has ended.
The monthly repayment amount may also be increased when the deferment period has ended so as to enable you to fully repay the outstanding loan within the remaining repayment period.
As interest on the outstanding loan amount will continue to accrue during the deferment period, you are encouraged to start repayment as soon as you have the ability to do so. You can approach us to end the deferment earlier and to start repayment any time.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply to defer the repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may submit an application online to defer your education loan repayment through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
You must read the Terms & Conditions and declare that you have obtained consent from the CPF lender(s) whose Ordinary Account savings were used, in the online form.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What are the conditions that I have to meet before I can apply to waive the education loan repayment?
questions.text:
You may apply to waive the repayment of the education loan with your Singpass, if you have met the following conditions:
1. You are aged 55 and above; and
2. You have set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in the Retirement Account. The FRS can be set aside fully with cash, or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property pledge.
You can approach us to check whether you are able to waive the repayment if you are withdrawing some of your CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy Scheme.
Please refer to this FAQ for more information on how the Retirement Sum is set aside at age 55. For more information on property pledging, you may refer to this FAQ.
If you have used your CPF savings for your own education and have met the waiver conditions, the Board will waive the repayment when you apply for withdrawal of your CPF savings. If you do not wish to withdraw your CPF savings but wish to waive the repayment of your CPF savings for your own education, you can apply to do so if you meet the waiver conditions.
If you have used your CPF savings for your child / spouse / sibling / relative's education, you will need to meet the waiver conditions to apply to waive the repayment.
You should only apply to waive repayment if you have no intention of continuing the use of your CPF savings for the student’s current course of study. Hence, if the student is still in the midst of study, you have to first revoke the use of CPF savings for future payments for the student's current course before applying to waive repayment. Alternatively, you may submit your application to waive repayment after the student has completed his/her studies.
Please note that the waiver will include the total CPF savings withdrawn and the interest that would have otherwise been earned had the savings not been withdrawn under the scheme. It does not include the amount that has already been repaid by the student and the amount used for the student's current course of study (if applicable). The waiver application once approved, is irrevocable.
If you do not meet the waiver conditions and the student is facing financial difficulties, he or she may apply to defer the loan repayment.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: If I choose not to waive the repayment, what will happen to the repayments made to my CPF Ordinary Account under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: Under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, the repayments will be credited to your CPF Ordinary Account and form part of your CPF savings which you can withdraw if you are eligible to do so under the current CPF withdrawal rules.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can the repayment of the CPF Education Loan and interest be waived, especially during economic downturns?
questions.text:
CPF is primarily for members' retirement needs. Hence, while you can take a loan from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) for your own or immediate family's tertiary education, the principal amount withdrawn has to be repaid to your OA, with the interest that you would otherwise have earned had the monies been left in your OA. This restores your CPF savings so that your retirement security is not worse off compared to not having taken the education loan. Retirement security remains important, if not more so, during economic downturns.
A waiver of the repayment is only allowed if you have already met your retirement needs, i.e. you are 55 years old and above and have set aside the Full Retirement Sum in your Retirement Account.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply to waive the repayment under the CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text:
You may submit an application online to waive the education loan repayment through "Manage education loan repayments" under "Forms and e-applications" using your Singpass.
For more information on the waiver of education loan repayment and the conditions to meet in order to waive the repayment, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text:
Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) holders can use their PSEA funds for full or partial lump sum repayment of their own education loan taken under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Repayments will be credited to the members’ (lenders’) CPF Ordinary Accounts (OAs).
Students (borrowers) may log in to the Ministry of Education’s Student Finance System (SFS) using their Singpass to check their available PSEA balance and submit their application to use PSEA funds for repayment. Account holders will receive an email informing them of their application outcome 30 to 60 days after submitting the form.
For more information on the usage of PSEA, please refer to the PSEA website.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my sibling's Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text: You can only use your own Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay your education loan.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum amount for using Post-Secondary Education Account savings to repay my outstanding education loan?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount set for using Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay loans taken under the CPF Education Loan Scheme.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I use my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings to repay multiple education loans?
questions.text: To repay more than one loan under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, please indicate details of the loan (institution name) in the order of repayment priority in the Loan Repayment Application Form. Withdrawal of Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) savings for loan repayment will be made in the order specified in the application form.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I invest under the CPF Investment Scheme if I am bankrupt?
questions.text:
If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you will not be able to use your CPF savings for investment. If you had previously used your CPF savings to invest, you can continue to hold your investments but you will not be allowed to make new investments. However, if you had previously used your CPF savings to invest in a regular premium insurance policy prior to your bankruptcy, you may continue to use your CPF savings to pay for your regular insurance premium subject to the Board's terms and conditions.
When you subsequently liquidate your investments, the sales proceeds will be credited into your CPF Investment Account or Special Account. If your Special Account is closed, the proceeds will be credited to your Retirement Account up to Full Retirement Sum, and any excess balance will be credited to your Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: If I am an undischarged bankrupt member, how do I sell my shares, property funds, bonds or Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) that I have purchased under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) before I became a bankrupt?
questions.text:
If you have a trading account with a stockbroking firm that has been frozen due to your bankruptcy, you will have to reactivate your trading account to sell your investments. If you no longer have a trading account, you will need to open a new trading account with a stockbroking firm (PDF, 0.1MB) before you can sell your investments.
However, it is at the stockbroking firm's discretion whether they will allow an undischarged bankrupt to reactivate/open a trading account. To assist the stockbroking firm to consider your request favourably, you may wish to provide them with your latest CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) Statement from your agent bank which lists the investment holdings that you intend to sell.
You do not need to seek the CPF Board or Official Assignee's approval to sell the shares held in your CPF Investment Account.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt member, can I sell my Singtel (ST) shares?
questions.text:
You can sell your discounted Singtel (ST) shares through SingPost even though you are a bankrupt member. You would need to bring your identity card or passport personally to any SingPost office to sell your shares. If you are unable to go to any SingPost office personally, you may authorise someone to sell the shares for you. The authorised person must bring along both his and your identity cards. Your signature on the original post office application form is also required. You can refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (PDF, 0.8MB) on selling the shares through the post office for more information.
If you have a trading account with a broking firm, you may sell your discounted ST shares through your stockbroker if your stockbroker is willing to do it for you. If you do not have any existing trading account, you can also open one with any of the Singapore Exchange (SGX) broking firms (PDF, 50KB). However, if you intend to trade through the internet, please check with your stockbroker before selling as broking firms generally do not allow internet trading for discounted ST shares.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I use the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments that I have withdrawn to settle my judgement debts?
questions.text: Once your CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account are withdrawn, they will no longer be protected from claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee. Please liaise with the Official Assignee on using your withdrawn CPFIS investments to settle your debts.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Can I invest after I am discharged from bankruptcy?
questions.text: After your discharge from bankruptcy, you can continue to invest your CPF savings if you are at least 18 years old, subject to the investment thresholds and limits set by the Board.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Can I continue to use my CPF savings for my existing private property housing loan if I am going to be made a bankrupt?
questions.text: Yes, if you own a private property and have earlier used your CPF savings to pay for the property before being declared bankrupt, you can continue to use your CPF to service your housing loan.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt and am planning to sell my property. How much do I need to refund to my CPF account?
questions.text:
When you sell your property, you must refund the CPF principal amount (P) you withdrew and the accrued interest (I) to your CPF account. If you are age 55 or above and have pledged your property to set aside your retirement sum, you must also refund the pledged amount.
IMPORTANT NOTE:
However, please note that your required CPF refund is less than your P+I if you:
were age 55 or older before 1 January 2013; and
have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) before 1 January 2013.
This is because having set aside your FRS before 1 January 2013, you are not required by law to refund the CPF you have used to pay for your property prior to 2013. If you have continued to use your CPF from 1 January 2013, only the principal amount used from 1 January 2013 and the accrued interest need to be refunded when you sell your property.
If you are below 55
The CPF housing refund goes to your Ordinary Account (OA). You can then use these OA savings to participate in other CPF schemes or purchase another property.
If you are over 55 years old
Your housing refund will first be used to set aside your Full Retirement Sum in your Retirement Account. Any remaining balance will stay in your OA for you to manage as needed.
You can find out more about your required housing refund in the “What happens if” section on your Home ownership dashboard.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can my CPF savings be used to pay for my children's tertiary education?
questions.text: You may use your CPF savings for your children's tertiary education under the CPF Education Loan scheme as long as you have the available withdrawal limit.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: As a bankrupt, can I use my CPF savings for my own tertiary education?
questions.text: You may continue to use your CPF savings for your own tertiary education if your application has been approved before your bankruptcy.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I withdraw my CPF savings?
questions.text:
If you are a bankrupt, you can withdraw some of your CPF savings if you meet any of the following grounds for withdrawals:
a) You have reached age 55.
b) You have a reduced life expectancy due to a medical condition, as certified by an accredited doctor. Severe medical conditions that cause you to be permanently unfit for work or to lack mental capacity permanently can also be considered.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am an undischarged bankrupt. Can I still choose to withdraw my Retirement Account savings using my property?
questions.text:
Whether you can withdraw your Retirement Account (RA) savings using your property depends on whether you own an HDB or private property.
For HDB property owners
You can choose to set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of property (up to half your FRS) and cash, and withdraw part of your RA savings down to your Basic Retirement Sum (BRS*) if your HDB property can last you until 95.
For private property owners
You can choose to set aside your FRS with a mixture of property (up to half your FRS) and cash, and withdraw part of your RA savings down to your BRS* if your private property can last you until 95 and the expected housing refund is enough to restore your Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
However, if you have not used your CPF savings for your property, or the expected housing refund is not enough to restore your FRS, you will not be able to withdraw your RA savings. This is because no additional charge can be created on your property. If you need more information, you can approach the Official Assignee.
It is important to note that the amount of RA savings you can withdraw excludes, generally, interest earned, government grants received and top-ups to your retirement savings. It also depends on your RA balance at the point of withdrawal. For example, if you are on CPF LIFE and have started your monthly payouts, any new inflows received in your RA will be used to increase your CPF LIFE premium to provide you with higher monthly payouts, and you will not be allowed to withdraw them in a lump sum.
* Excluding, generally, interest earned, government grants and top-ups made under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme.

questions.title: What should I do if I have obtained a divorce court order overseas?
questions.text:
For foreign divorce court orders, please note that the court order will only have effect in Singapore if it is recognised in Singapore either through legislation in Singapore or by Singapore Courts (which would require an application to the Singapore Courts). The Board will not be bound by orders made by foreign courts.
You may seek the advice of a law firm in Singapore on the issue of the enforcement of a foreign Order of Court in Singapore. You can obtain a list of law firms from the Law Society of Singapore’s website.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Why does the CPF Board need me to provide identification documents of the parties stated in the court orders?
questions.text: As the Board identifies CPF members by their CPF account numbers, we would not be able to verify the parties’ identities based on the passport number or driving license number or any other identities which are not their CPF account numbers, that was indicated in the court order. As such, we would require documents that can allow us to link to the identification numbers of the parties stated in the court orders. Alternatively, the parties may amend the court orders to reflect the parties’ Singapore NRIC number.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Why do I get error messages when I submit my court order?
questions.text:
If you experience any error messages when you submit your court order, please check that your attachment meets the following conditions:
The attachment is in pdf format only.
Attachment size is 5MB or less.
No special characters in the name of the attachment.
If you still encounter issue in your submission, please try again later and if the issue persists, please send us a screenshot of the error message via Write to us.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: If I do not need to submit my court order, does my conveyancing lawyer need to submit any documents to CPF Board?
questions.text:
Yes, your conveyancing lawyer will need to submit the relevant applications at our Housing Business Partner Portal, even if full refunds are to be made to the outgoing owner’s CPF account based on your court order.
If you own an HDB flat, please confirm your eligibility with HDB before proceeding with the housing transaction.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Which court orders are required to be submitted to the CPF Board for the purpose of division of CPF assets in a divorce?
questions.text:
Please submit the court order to the Board if the CPF-related orders pertain to the following:
1. Transfer of property with zero or partial CPF refunds to the outgoing owner; or
2. Division of other (i.e. non-property) CPF-related matrimonial assets such as transfer of CPF savings from Member A to Member B or payment (charging) of Member A’s CPF savings to Member B; or
3. Division of property (with full, partial or zero CPF refunds) and other (i.e. non-property) CPF assets.
Please refer to Annex B (PDF, 396KB) for examples of court orders that are required to be submitted to the CPF Board.
You may also wish to know the types of court orders not required to be submitted to CPF Board.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Which court orders are not required to be submitted to CPF Board for the purpose of division of CPF assets in a divorce?
questions.text:
You do not need to submit your court order to CPF Board if:
1. Your court order only involves dividing a property where the outgoing owner will receive a full CPF refund. This applies to these property transactions (non-exhaustive):
Transfer
Sale
Part-share sale
Surrender
Removal of occupier's name
Cancellation of purchase
2. The property will remain solely owned by its current owner (no change in ownership).
This streamlined process allows you to complete your housing transactions faster without waiting for CPF Board's response. Please refer to Annex A (PDF, 256KB) for examples of court orders that are not required to be submitted to the CPF Board.
The Board will not be replying to court orders that need not be submitted to us. This will enable us to focus our efforts on serving members with complex court orders that require CPF Board’s review. Affected parties may refer to our FAQs for information on housing refund rules and property matters.
Please note that the above process does not change the conveyancing requirements. For conveyancing transactions involving properties with CPF savings embedded, please continue to submit the relevant applications (e.g. Notice of Refund, Application form for use of CPF savings under the CPF Housing Schemes) via our Housing Business Partner Portal. See applications to be submitted for conveyancing transactions.
Separately, you may also wish to know the types of court orders required to be submitted to CPF Board.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How long will CPF Board take to give effect to the court order?
questions.text:
Upon receipt of your court order, the Board will generally take two to three weeks to give effect to the court order. As court orders differ in complexity, the CPF Board will need to review the relevant orders and will keep the lawyers and parties informed on the progress of the matter.
We will upload the replies to you and your ex-spouse via your registered email address in our record or Mailbox for members. An SMS will be sent to the Mailbox recipient's mobile number in our record. For law firms and the Legal Aid Bureau, we will reply via their registered email address.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.text:

For Business Partners and Legal Aid Bureau (LAB):

topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Is my ex-spouse entitled to have a share of my CPF savings upon our divorce?
questions.text: While CPF savings may be considered as matrimonial assets and a share may be given to your ex-spouse, there is nothing in the laws that give your ex-spouse an automatic entitlement. It is up to the Court to decide whether your ex-spouse is entitled to any part of your CPF savings, taking into account the matters set out in section 112 of the Women's Charter / section 52(3)(d) of the Administration of Muslim Law Act. For more information, please visit the Family Justice Courts’ website or Syariah Court’s website.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: How can I ensure that my court order for a transfer order or charging order meets CPF legislations?
questions.text:
Your court order must contain the following information:
Legal provision of your ex-spouse’s entitlement for the CPF savings
The CPF Account that the transfer of CPF savings will be made from
The amount of CPF savings to be transferred (the “Ordered Amount”). If the amount cannot be determined yet, the court order should state which party will be notifying the CPF Board of this information
Triggering event upon which the CPF Board should transfer the Ordered Amount
In the absence of the above information, the CPF Board may not be able to comply with the provisions of the court order.
It is important to note that the use of CPF assets must be for the purpose of a division of matrimonial assets, and not for settling maintenance or personal claims or debts.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What are your obligations after the court order is granted, before and following the transfer or payment of CPF savings to your ex-spouse in a divorce?
questions.text:
You are obliged to comply with the court order and shall not withdraw or transfer or attempt to withdraw or transfer any amount that your ex-spouse is entitled to under the court order.
In the event of a transfer or payment of CPF savings upon the making of housing refunds pursuant to a disposal of the property, loans or grants taken by you which are repayable or refundable to the Government must be repaid or refunded first before the transfer or payment of CPF savings can take place. Grants include housing grants from the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).
Keep in mind that transferring or paying CPF savings to your ex-spouse might impact your participation in CPF schemes. If necessary, consider making alternative financial arrangements.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Should I do a transfer or charging order for my CPF savings?
questions.text:
The choice between a transfer order and a charging order depends on your specific circumstances and intentions.
Transfer Order (i.e. transfer from your CPF account to your ex-spouse’s CPF account) – only applicable for ex-spouse who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
This allows your ex-spouse immediate access to their entitlement of your CPF monies.
The transfer can be from any of your CPF accounts*.
Charging Order (i.e. impose a charge on your CPF savings to make payment to your ex-spouse in cash)
Payment can only be made to your ex-spouse when you become eligible to withdraw your CPF savings, typically when you turn 55.
Whether you need to set aside your Full Retirement Sum before payment and what CPF Account monies* can be paid, depends on your ex-spouse’s residency status (Singapore Citizen, Permanent Resident, or foreigner).
You may refer to more information relating to transfer and charging orders.
*On 19 January 2025, if you are aged 55 and above, your Special Account is now closed. If you turn age 55 after 19 January 2025, your Special Account will be closed on your 55th birthday. Once closed, it will not be possible to transfer or pay your Special Account savings to your ex-spouse.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What happens if my CPF savings are not enough to fulfil my ex-spouse's entitlement as required in the court order?
questions.text:
If your CPF savings are not enough to fulfil your ex-spouse’s entitlement as required in the court order, the Board can only effect the transfer or make the payment based on the available balances in your CPF account(s) as at date of transfer or payment.
You and your ex-spouse may wish to settle the shortfall amount privately or seek legal advice on the remedies available.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: As a member or an ex-spouse, what are my options if I am an undischarged bankrupt under division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text:
The Court may still grant a transfer order or a charging order; similar to a member/ or an ex-spouse who is not an undischarged bankrupt.
If you are the ex-spouse, and payment is to be made to you under a charging order, please check with the Official Assignee whether you can receive the CPF savings.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Under a transfer order, do I need to set aside my retirement sum before my ex-spouse can receive their entitlement?
questions.text:
The transfer of CPF savings to your ex-spouse can take place without you setting aside your retirement sum* first. This gives your ex-spouse certainty over the amount they can receive and they can use them immediately for approved purposes such as housing, investment and education. Your ex-spouse may also withdraw the CPF savings when they are entitled to.
In the event of a transfer of CPF savings upon the making of housing refunds pursuant to a disposal of the property, the Board will first transfer the amount to your ex-spouse. Thereafter, the remaining refunds will be used to make up your retirement sum, up to your applicable Full Retirement Sum. Any balance housing refunds will remain in your Ordinary Account, and you can decide how to manage it.
*Only applies to members aged 55 and above.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Is there a limit on the CPF transfers that can be made to my ex-spouse's CPF Accounts under the division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text:
There is no limit on the CPF transfers if so ordered by the Court. It is up to the Court to decide on the division of CPF savings and how much your ex-spouse's entitlement is.
Before the Court grants the court order, you should ensure that the Court is kept informed of any changes to the amount of CPF savings available for division or any planned utilisation of your CPF savings (e.g. deductions for housing payments) that would affect the division of the same.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I specify the CPF account in which my ex-spouse is to receive the CPF savings under a transfer order?
questions.text:
For the court order to be workable, it must specify which of your CPF account(s) the transfer of CPF savings are to be made from. There is no need to specify which CPF account(s) your ex-spouse is to receive the monies in. This is because the transfers will be done in accordance with Regulation 3 of the Central Provident Fund (Division of Fund-Related Assets in Matrimonial Proceedings) Regulations which specifies the CPF accounts of the receiving party.
Please refer to the table below for more details:
From member's CPF account
To ex-spouse's CPF account
Ordinary Account
Ordinary Account
Special/Retirement Account
Special Account (if below age 55)
*Retirement Account (if age 55 and above)
MediSave Account
MediSave Account
* Any amount in excess of the Full Retirement Sum that your ex-spouse needs to set aside in their CPF Retirement Account, will be transferred to their Ordinary Account.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use the CPF savings immediately upon the receipt of the transferred monies from my ex-spouse?
questions.text: Yes, you can use the CPF savings for approved purposes such as housing, investment and education. You may also withdraw the CPF savings when you are entitled to do so.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Under a transfer order, can I request the monies to be paid to me in cash, instead of transferring to my CPF account?
questions.text: Under a transfer order, the monies can only be transferred from your ex-spouse’s CPF account to your designated CPF account. If you wish to receive the monies in cash, you may consider applying to the Courts for a charging order instead.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What do I need to do to receive payment under a charging order?
questions.text:
You will first need to submit the court order for the division of CPF assets via the online service "Submit Court Order for Division of CPF Assets". We will write to you and your ex-spouse once we have reviewed the court order.
When your ex-spouse is entitled to withdraw their CPF savings, we will write to you to inform you of the withdrawal procedure.
Once we receive your withdrawal application and the necessary documents, we will process the application and the monies will be paid to you within 10 working days through Inter-Bank GIRO and 15 working days via Telegraphic Transfer.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: After the transfer or sale of the matrimonial property has been completed pursuant to the existing court order, I reached a different agreement with my ex-spouse on the division of CPF assets. Can we undo the transfer or sale?
questions.text:
The CPF Board has no power under the relevant legislation to reverse the transfer or sale of the property.
Please seek legal advice to amend the court order.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can the courts order the sale (as opposed to a transfer (other than by way of sale)) of my share of the matrimonial property to my ex-spouse without any CPF refund?
questions.text: Upon the sale of your share of the matrimonial property to your ex-spouse, the required CPF refund must be made to your CPF account. The Court can then order the transfer or payment of the refunded CPF savings from your CPF account to your ex-spouse’s CPF account or to you in cash if it so decides.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Do I need to make any CPF refunds if I sell my share of the property to my ex-spouse?
questions.text:
Yes, the required CPF refunds must be made in full to your CPF account upon the sale of your share of the property to your ex-spouse.
If you intend to transfer your share of the property to your ex-spouse with no or partial CPF refunds to be made to your account, you have to obtain a court order for a transfer of property instead. Please note that the relevant requirements in Part 3A of the CPF Act will apply.
View how much you need to refund on the sale of your property. For information on transferring the property, please go to the next section on Transfer of Property.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I transfer my share in the property to my ex-spouse?
questions.text:
Yes, you can do so if the Courts decide to make such an order. The amount of CPF refunds, who is required to make those refunds and at what point in time the refunds need to be made will depend on whether the court order provides for full, partial or no CPF refunds to your CPF account upon transfer of your share in the property to your ex-spouse.
We set out the CPF refund details in the table below:
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to make the required CPF refunds to my ex-spouse upon the transfer of property?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your Ordinary Account savings and cash to make the required CPF refund to your ex-spouse upon the transfer of the property.
Please note that for HDB flats, your CPF usage may be subject to the applicable housing withdrawal limits, which will be determined when we receive the detailed information regarding the transaction.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to pay for the cash consideration to my ex-spouse for the transfer of property?
questions.text: No, you cannot use your CPF savings for any cash consideration to your ex-spouse in a property transfer. You may, however, use your Ordinary Account savings to make the refunds to your ex-spouse’s CPF account upon the transfer of property.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What should I do if the Court has instructed me to use the cash consideration provided by my ex-spouse to make the required CPF refund upon the transfer of property?
questions.text:
You should check if the cash consideration is sufficient to make the required refund to your CPF account upon the transfer of property. If the cash consideration is not enough to cover the required refund, you will need to make up the difference in cash, in a lump sum, upon the completion of the transfer of the property to your ex-spouse.
On the other hand, if the cash consideration is more than enough to cover the required refund, the Board will only collect the required refund amount to your CPF account. For example, the Court has instructed your ex-spouse to pay you a cash consideration of $60,000 and you are to use this sum to make your required CPF refund amount. As at the date of transfer, your required refund is $25,000. In this case, the Board will only accept $25,000 to your CPF account.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: What are the ex-spouse's (remaining party) obligations following the transfer of the property under matrimonial proceedings?
questions.text:
If the Court so orders, the ex-spouse (remaining party) has to refund a sum (amount as decided by the Court) to the member’s (outgoing party) CPF Account(s) upon transfer.
The Court may also order the transfer of property with no refunds to the member’s CPF Account. If that is the case, upon the subsequent sale/transfer or otherwise disposal of the property, the ex-spouse would be required to refund to their own CPF Account(s), the CPF monies withdrawn (including the accrued interest) by them and the member for the purchase of the property, and any amount for which the property has been pledged to set aside their and the member’s retirement sums.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: I am required to give some of my CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments to my ex-spouse as specified in the Court Order. What should I do after receiving the Court Order?
questions.text:
You can submit your court orders for the division of CPF-related assets in divorce by following these steps.
For Members:
Scan or click the QR code, login with your Singpass, and complete the form:
Alternatively, you may submit the court order(s) using the following steps:
1. Go to “Division of CPF assets”
2. Under “Use these forms to submit court orders” > “Submit yourself”
3. Login with your Singpass and fill up the form
For Business Partners and Legal Aid Bureau (LAB):
You may scan the QR code, login with your Corpass, and complete the form:
Alternatively, you may submit the court order(s) using the following steps:
1. Go to “Division of CPF assets”
2. Under “Use these forms to submit court orders” > “Submit via lawyer”
3. Login with your Corpass and fill up the form
You should also proceed to execute the transfer or liquidation of your investments in accordance with the court order. Please refer to the step-by-step guide (PDF, 54KB) for more details on how a transfer or sale of CPFIS investments is effected from you to your ex-spouse.
Note: If you, your ex-spouse or your lawyers cannot submit the court order(s) online, you can schedule an appointment at our CPF Bishan Service Centre through Appointment@CPF. Our Customer Service Executive will assist you with the submission. Please bring a copy of your court order(s) and your identification document to the appointment.

(near Bishan MRT Station)

questions.title: Why do I have to effect the transfer or sale of investments under the division of CPF savings in a divorce? What happens if I do not come forward to effect the transfer or sale of investments?
questions.text:
You are solely responsible for presenting the court order and completing the necessary forms at the relevant financial intermediaries to effect the transfer or sale of investments because the financial intermediaries require authorisation and instruction from the owner, i.e. you.
If you do not sign the transfer form, your ex-spouse may apply to the Court for the Registrar of Court to sign the transfer form on your behalf. Your ex-spouse will need to furnish the required information (eg, Divorce Petition number, both of your names, contact numbers, CPF account numbers, Investment Account numbers, names of agent banks, name of your investments, name of financial intermediaries, etc) to complete the transfer form.
If you do not sell the investments as ordered, and the investments are such that they cannot be sold without instruction being given personally by you (as required by the financial intermediaries), your ex-spouse may request for the Court Order to be varied to transfer your investments to them instead. As this depends on the nature of the investments, your ex-spouse should make the necessary enquiries with the financial intermediaries concerned before obtaining the appropriate order.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Can the cash balance in my Investment Account be transferred under the division of CPF savings in a divorce?
questions.text: Cash balances in your Investment Account can be transferred but you have to initiate the transfer of cash balance from your Investment Account to your Ordinary Account first before CPF Board can transfer the balance to your ex-spouse's Ordinary Account.

questions.title: How can I submit an application to transfer CPF Investment Scheme investments sale proceeds in a divorce?

questions.title: What are the criteria to be fulfilled by my ex-spouse before my investments can be transferred to them under the division of CPF savings in a divorce? What are the options if my ex-spouse cannot fulfill the criteria?
questions.text: Before your investments can be transferred to your ex-spouse, they must be a CPF member who is Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) and 18 years old and above. If your ex-spouse is below 18 years old, they can consider requesting the Court to order your investments to be liquidated and the sale proceeds to be transferred to their CPF accounts.

questions.title: How does CPF Board protect and use my personal information? Is CPF Board bound by Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)?
questions.text:
There are strict policies, processes, and safeguards to ensure the proper use and protection of personal data within CPF Board. While the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) does not apply to government agencies, Government's data protection standards are aligned with, if not more stringent than, the requirements of the PDPA. CPF Board also requires the same high standards in third parties’ handling of CPF data to prevent inadvertent disclosure of CPF member’s details.
CPF Board is committed in ensuring that CPF members’ data are protected, while using the data to continuously understand members’ needs to refine and develop better policies and services.
You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Isn't it against the law for CPF Board to reveal a member's personal details publicly?
questions.text:
Members’ data are safe with the Board and there are high standards in place to prevent its unintended disclosure.
Where it is in the public interest, the law allows the CPF Board to release a member’s personal details. For example, where misleading information is put out and widely disseminated, we must be able to provide the public with relevant facts. This approach applies to all public agencies. It helps the public gain a fuller picture of the case and counter the misinformation, both of which are necessary to maintain the trust placed in public agencies.
CPF Board is committed in ensuring your data is protected. You may refer to our privacy statement for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: What is Central Provident Fund (CPF)?
questions.text:
The Central Provident Fund (CPF) is a comprehensive social security system that enables working Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to set aside funds for retirement. It also addresses healthcare, home ownership, family protection and asset enhancement.
Working Singaporeans and their employers make monthly contributions to the CPF and these contributions go into three accounts:
Ordinary Account - the savings can be used to buy a home, pay for CPF insurance, investment and education.
Special Account - for old age and investment in retirement-related financial products.
MediSave Account - the savings can be used for hospitalisation expenses and approved medical insurance.
Please refer to the CPF website for an overview of CPF.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen working in India. Do I need to contribute to the India's Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)?
questions.text:
The Singapore Government is aware that Singapore Citizens working in India have been required to contribute to India's Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and has been negotiating with India's Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to exempt Singapore Citizens from this requirement.
As of 1 January 2016, Singapore Citizens working in India will no longer have to contribute to the EPF. If you have previously contributed to the EPF, you will be able to withdraw your past contributions, but only after your employment contract in India ends.
Please visit Ministry of Foreign Affairs website for more information. The relevant forms should be sent to the Certifying Authority (MFA, MTI) for certification. Members can approach MFA or MTI for assistance.
For more information on the India-Singapore Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement or contributions to India's Employment Provident Fund by Singapore Citizens, please contact MTI at MTI_email@mti.gov.sg.

questions.title: What should I do if I face difficulty logging into my cpf digital services?
questions.text:
Here are some ways for you to troubleshoot when encountering login issues:
Check your internet connection to ensure it is stable.
Clear your browser cache before trying again (please refer to this link for instructions on how to clear the cache for all major browsers).
Relaunch CPF website and try to log in again.
Check that your browser is updated. my cpf digital services is compatible with the two most recent versions of commonly used web browsers such as Chrome and Safari.
Check that your device date-time setting is set to “Automatic” or the current date and time
Try logging in to other government websites to determine if the issue occurs on these other platforms.
If the issue persists, please write to us for further assistance.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What should I do if I can no longer locate an old digital service or if service has been discontinued?

questions.title: How can I update my subscription preferences for my CPF notifications?

questions.title: What is CPF Mobile?

questions.title: How can I download CPF Mobile?

questions.title: Why doesn't CPF Mobile offer all the services found on CPF website?

questions.title: What is the minimum requirement to access CPF Mobile on my mobile device?

questions.title: What should I do if I face difficulty logging into CPF Mobile?
questions.text:
Here are some ways for you to troubleshoot when encountering login issues:
Check your internet connection to ensure it is stable.
Relaunch CPF Mobile and try to log in again.
Make sure your device operating system and CPF Mobile are updated to the latest version. The latest version of CPF Mobile is available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
Check that your device date-time setting is set to “Automatic”.
Ensure that you did not block all cookies in your browser settings.
Set one of Singpass’ recommended browsers (Safari or Chrome) as your default browser.
If you are using Firefox browser, check that you have enabled the opening of links in app in your browser settings.
If the issue persists, you can write to us for further assistance. Alternatively, you may wish to check if this issue occurs for other Government website/apps, and contact Singpass Helpdesk directly to resolve any Singpass login issue.
In the meantime, you can still access our full suite of services through my cpf digital services on the CPF website, which is designed for seamless usage on mobile devices.

questions.title: Can I enable personalised push notifications on multiple mobile devices?
questions.text: No, you can only enable personalised push notifications on one mobile device at any time. If you had already enabled personalised push notifications on one device, enabling it on another device will disable the personalised notifications on your older device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How long will the message stay in the notification list?
questions.text: The content will be available for 15 months from the notification date and will be removed automatically thereafter.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I delete the messages in the notification list?
questions.text: You can delete the message by tapping on the ‘Bin’ icon in the notification detail page.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I read the full content of push notifications?
questions.text:
You can view the full content of the push notification via three ways:
Tap on the banner and it will bring you to view the full content of the notification.
Before logging into the app, tap on the ‘bell’ icon located at the top left corner.
After logging into the app, tap on the ‘bell’ icon located at the top left corner of the side menu.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Do I need to log in to access personalised notifications on CPF Mobile?
questions.text: Yes, Singpass login is required to view your personalised notifications.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Can I still view my past notifications if I change to a new mobile device?
questions.text: Yes, you will have access to your past personalised notifications after you have successfully enabled notifications on your new mobile device. Notifications sent in the past 15 months will be available.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I lost my mobile device. How can I disable personalised notifications?
questions.text: In the event that you lose your mobile device, you can enable personalised notifications on your new mobile device. By doing so, there will be no personalised notifications sent to your missing mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How do I disable personalised notifications before I sell my mobile device?
questions.text: You can disable personalised notifications at the app settings page. It is recommended that you uninstall CPF Mobile before selling your mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is CPF Board rolling out Chinese language in CPF Mobile?
questions.text: We are introducing Chinese language in CPF Mobile as a pilot to gauge customers’ usage and interest in vernacular features.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is some content in CPF Mobile still in English when my device language is set to Chinese?
questions.text: CPF Mobile has recently extended Chinese language to more services on the app. We are progressively extending this to more services.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why am I receiving push notifications on my mobile device when I did not enable them on CPF Mobile?
questions.text: For early detection of unauthorised changes to contact details, push notifications are enabled on CPF Mobile automatically. You can change your setting at the app settings page of your mobile device.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why am I unable to log in to CPF Mobile through the Singpass QR code?
questions.text:
The Singpass app is required in order to log in to CPF Mobile using the Singpass QR code. Singpass app is compatible with the following mobile browsers:
Safari versions: 12.1 and above
Chrome versions: 78 above
You may encounter login errors if you have set other browsers as your mobile device’s default browser. To ensure a seamless login experience, please set one of the browsers above as your mobile device’s default browser. Alternatively, you may log in without the Singpass app by selecting ‘Password login’ on the Singpass login page and logging in using your Singpass ID and password. If you continue to face issues pertaining to Singpass login, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for further assistance.
If you are experiencing other login issues, please refer to our FAQ on troubleshooting for more information.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I was previously able to use OCBC Pay Anyone app for payment. Can I continue to do so?
questions.text: Payment via OCBC Pay Anyone app will no longer be available on CPF Mobile from 22 Aug 2023. You can continue to make payment via OCBC Digital app. To do so, you need to download the OCBC Digital app on the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Thereafter, you will be able to select the OCBC Digital option under the ‘Payment Mode’ page in CPF Mobile after confirming the transaction details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why am I receiving a notice on potential vulnerabilities when I launch CPF Mobile?
questions.text:
To safeguard your data, CPF Mobile is equipped with security features to prevent unauthorised access to your CPF account. Access to CPF Mobile is disabled and a notice on potential vulnerabilities is displayed when we detect certain issues. These are categorised as follows:
Potential security threats
What you can do
Apps from non-official app stores
If the notice displays the names of the problematic app(s), uninstall the app(s) shown in the notice
If the notice does not display the names of the problematic app(s),
Android users: Use the V-Key Diagnostic app* to identify problematic apps and then uninstall them
iOS users: Write to us with troubleshooting ID for further assistance
Malware
Jailbroken/rooted devices
Write to us for further assistance
Enabled screen sharing access or screen recording
Stop your screen recording or close any screen sharing app to prevent potential scammers from seeing your personal information
Virtual space
Remove CPF Mobile from the virtual space app
Reinstall CPF Mobile app outside of the virtual space
Be aware that using CPF Mobile in a virtual space poses potential security risks
Access through emulator
Ensure that you are accessing CPF Mobile directly from your mobile device and not through an emulator
Developer options enabled
Go to device settings > Developer options > ensure “Developer options” is turned off
*This can be downloaded from the Google Play Store. Upon running the V-Key Diagnostic app, a pop-up notification will appear if there are malicious apps installed on your mobile device.
To better protect yourself, please only download apps from official app stores to avoid malware being installed. You can read up more on how to avoid falling prey to malware scams.
For further assistance, please write to us with a screenshot of the notice.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Do CPF Mobile's security features scan my device or collect my personal information?
questions.text: We take your privacy seriously. CPF Mobile's security features are limited to the detection of malware activity and no additional personal data from your device is collected. We seek your understanding that these features are necessary to protect CPF members from malware or suspected malicious apps. You can read up more on how to avoid falling prey to malware scams.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What security measures does CPF Mobile have in place to safeguard users from malware threats?
questions.text:
To safeguard your data and facilitate safe transactions, CPF Mobile is equipped with security features to prevent scammers from accessing your CPF account.
Access to CPF Mobile is restricted if your mobile device is rooted/jailbroken, contains known/potential malware apps or has granted risky app accessibility permissions on your device. These features are designed to help you to identify and prevent unauthorised access, thereby protecting you from potential exposure to malware scams and other security threats.
Our aim is to provide you with user-friendly services while ensuring a secure experience. You can be assured that CPF Mobile’s security features are limited to the detection of malware activity and no personal data from your device is collected.
For more information on what to do when you receive a notice on potential vulnerabilities and the anti-scam security measures available to you, please refer to the FAQs below:
Why am I receiving a notice on potential vulnerabilities when I launch CPF Mobile?
What are the new anti-scam security measures available to CPF members?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Can I make more than one payment using the same QR code?
questions.text: No, the QR code generated is unique to your submitted application. Should you require to make another payment, please submit another application. A new QR code with the required payment details will be generated for you to make another payment.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What if I made more than one payment using the same QR code?
questions.text: You should only use the generated QR code for one payment as the QR code generated is unique. If there is more than one payment, the subsequent payment will be refunded to you.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: How can I benefit from electronic payments?
questions.text:
You can benefit in the following ways with electronic payment modes:
Easy and convenient
Faster processing time
Secure and seamless transaction
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why is payment via eNETS discontinued with effect from 23 April 2023?
questions.text: CPF Board regularly reviews the services and payment options we provide to our customers. Payment via eNETS had been discontinued from 23 April 2023 because payments made by customers via eNETS are unable to be updated in the members’ accounts instantaneously. Customers can use PayNow QR or OCBC Digital via our digital services on CPF Mobile to make payment and these transactions will be processed instantaneously.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Why do I encounter a Security Warning Message when I login to my cpf Online Services or other online application?
questions.text:
The transaction you're performing makes use of a Secure Socket Layer (SSL) digital security certificate. This allows you to conduct safe e-transactions with 256-bit encrypted SSL connections.
Essentially, this digital certificate is an electronic document which your browser uses to authenticate our server and initiate the encryption processes. The certificate is like a stamp of approval that also carries the information needed to activate the SSL process.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What should I do when I see the Security Warning Message?
questions.text:
You can click "Yes" to proceed with your intended transaction. However, the message will appear when you login the next time. For a long-term solution, please do the following:
Click on the 'View Certificate' button.
Click on the 'Install Certificate' button.
Click on the 'Next' and 'Finish' buttons as required to accept and install the certificate.
Click "Yes" when you see 'Do you want to ADD the following certificate to the Root Store?'
Click 'Ok' as required.
Click 'Yes' to the Security Alert warning which may still be being displayed.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: What should I do if I think the information in my CPF statement is incorrect?
questions.text: Please notify us immediately via Write to Us if you think that the information is incorrect. Please note that it is your responsibility to carefully review your CPF statements.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I view my CPF Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text:
You can view, print and/or download your CPF Yearly Statement of Account for the past 10 years via Singpass login at my cpf digital services. As we do not provide CPF statements beyond the past 10 years, please download your statements in a timely manner to ensure that you always have a copy for your own records. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
For non-Singapore Citizens and non-Permanent Residents, please refer to our FAQ for more information.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: I would like a hardcopy of my CPF Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA). Where can I get it?
questions.text:
As part of our efforts to go green, CPF Board has transformed the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) into a digital statement. We strongly encourage you to view your YSOA online to enjoy a richer and more interactive user experience.
You may log in to my cpf digital services to view, download and save/print your YSOA for the past 10 years by clicking the "PDF icon". To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: What is the total employment contribution I received for the year?
questions.text:
You can sum up the “Employee Contribution” under the “You” category and “Employer Contribution” under “Employer” category to derive the total employment contributions for the year.
For more details on the rates, see rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I derive the breakdown of employer and employee's contributions indicated on my Yearly Statement of Account?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I derive the interest indicated in my Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: Please refer to the CPF interest page for more information on CPF interest. Details on extra interest and how CPF interest rates are determined can be found in our FAQs.

questions.title: How do I save or download a copy of my Digital Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: On the Digital Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) page, click on “PDF icon” to view, download and save a copy of your YSOA. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I stop receiving my hardcopy Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text: As part of our efforts to go green, we have transformed the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) into a digital statement. If you wish to go green and stop receiving a hardcopy YSOA, please submit a request to us. Singpass login is required.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Can I view my child's CPF statements online?
questions.text:
You can view your child’s Transaction History statement as well as the Healthcare Payments and Claims statement (if applicable) for the last 15 months online if:
1. You and your child are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents, and
2. Your child is below the age of 21 and has received CPF contributions (including Government Grants such as MediSave Grant for Newborns).
Simply login to my cpf Home > Child Dashboard with your Singpass to access this information.
If you do not see your child’s name listed in the Child Dashboard, you can write to us with the following supporting documents and we will be happy to assist.
Supporting documents required:
Birth certificate of your child
Citizenship certificate if your child was a foreigner at birth (where applicable).
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: If I am granted sole custody of my child following a divorce, can I request to remove my ex-spouse's access to our child's CPF statement?
questions.text: Yes, you can write to us using your Singpass and attach the Court Order as a supporting document.
