It is a serious offence to recover or attempt to recover any amount more than what is allowed from your employee’s wages.
If you failed to recover the employee’s share of CPF contributions due to your error (e.g. system glitch, omission of CPF contributions due to employer's oversight, wrong computation of employee's share) before paying your employee’s wages for the month, you cannot recover the employee’s share of CPF contributions from subsequent months’ wages.
However, if the failure to do so was not due to your error, you must do the following before you can recover the employee’s share of CPF contributions from wages payable by you to your employee:
you have paid the CPF contributions to the Board, and
you have either forwarded your employee’s written consent to CPF Board, or obtained CPF Board’s written permission on the matter.
This must be done within six months from the time the employee’s share of CPF contributions should have been recovered.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Where can I download the CPF contribution rate booklets?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution rate booklets are no longer available.
You can use our CPF Contribution Calculator to calculate the CPF contributions applicable to your employees. For more details on the CPF contribution rates, see rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
You can also use CPF EZPay to auto-compute your CPF contributions for greater convenience!
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Do the same CPF contribution rates apply to part-time/casual/temporary employees?
questions.text:
Like full-time employees, the CPF contribution rates for part-time, casual or temporary workers depend on your employees’ citizenship status, age group and wage band.
The nature of the employment does not affect the contribution rates applicable.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I have been contributing to my Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) employee's pension scheme in his home country?
questions.text: CPF contributions are mandatory for your Singapore Permanent Resident employee working in Singapore regardless of any contributions to another pension scheme in his home country.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: My Singapore Permanent Resident employee obtained his Singapore Citizenship in the middle of the month. When will the contribution rates for a Singapore Citizen apply?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution rates for Singapore Permanent Resident will apply on your employee’s wages until your employee obtains a Singapore Citizenship. Once your employee has obtained a Singapore Citizenship, the contribution rates for Singapore Citizen will apply from the day he becomes a Singapore Citizen.
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pro-rate your employee’s OW and apply the appropriate rates to determine the CPF contributions. You can write to us for assistance on the computation if the Ordinary Wages for the month exceeds the Ordinary Wage ceiling or if the pro-rated wages are below $750.
For Additional Wages (AW), you will need to apply the applicable contribution rate depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Example
Assuming your employee is in the second year of Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status and becomes a Singapore Citizen on 15 June 2020.
For OW
The second year SPR rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period 1 June to 14 June 2020.
The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the pro-rated wages for the period of 15 June to 30 June 2020.
For AW
The second year SPR rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 1 June and 14 June 2020.
The Singapore Citizen rate should be applied on the AW if it is payable between 15 June and 30 June 2020.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: How can I contribute more CPF for my employee who just obtained his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status?
questions.text:
You and your employee can contribute CPF at higher rates in the first two years after your employee has obtained Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status.
There are two options available:
1. You and your employee both contribute at full rates; or
2. You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates.
You can submit a joint application with your SPR employee based on your entity type:
For UEN-registered entities
For individuals trading under own name
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Must I contribute CPF at a higher rate for my Singapore Permanent Resident employee?
questions.text:
You are not required to contribute CPF at a higher rate for your Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) employee who is in the first two years of his SPR status. However, you are required to contribute CPF at the graduated rates.
If you and your SPR employee wish to contribute at higher rates, you can submit a joint application with your SPR employee based on your entity type:
For UEN-registered entities
For individuals trading under own name
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: When can I apply to pay CPF contribution at a higher rate for my Singapore Permanent Resident employee?
questions.text: You can start applying from the day your employee become a Singapore Permanent Resident.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: My Singapore Permanent Resident employee contributed CPF at a higher rate than stipulated ones in his previous employment. Am I required to pay CPF at the higher rate?
questions.text:
The higher contribution rate ceases upon a change of employment within the first two years of obtaining Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status i.e. the rates will go back to the graduated rates. Therefore, there is no need to contribute CPF at higher rates.
If you and your SPR employee wish to contribute at higher rates, you can submit a joint application with your SPR employee based on your entity type:
For UEN-registered entities
For individuals trading under own name
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: What happens if I do not pay Skills Development Levy (SDL) on time?
questions.text: There will be a penalty of 10% per annum for late contribution on the outstanding amount under the Skills Development Levy (SDL) regulations.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Skills Development Levy (SDL)

questions.title: Which categories of employees or workers are exempted from Skills Development Levy (SDL)?
questions.text: For information on which categories of employees are exempted from Skills Development Levy (SDL), please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on SDL at this webpage.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Skills Development Levy (SDL)

questions.title: Is Skills Development Levy (SDL) payable for students on vacation job?
questions.text: For information on whether Skills Development Levy (SDL) is payable for students on vacation job, please visit this webpage for more information on SDL.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Skills Development Levy (SDL)

questions.title: What are the contribution rates for the respective Self-Help Groups?
questions.text: You may refer to this page to find out the contribution rates for the respective Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: Must my employees contribute to the Self-Help Group (SHG) funds?
questions.text:
As an employer, you are expected to deduct your employees’ contributions to the Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from their wages. Employees who do not wish to contribute or wish to contribute a different amount can contact the respective SHGs for more information.
To find out which SHGs your employees should make their contributions to, you may refer to this page for more information.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: What does the Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF) comprise?
questions.text:
The Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF) comprises three components:
The Mosque Building component is used to build new mosques, upgrade and redevelop current mosques.
The Mendaki component is used to develop educational and social programmes to strengthen and uplift Malay/Muslim families.
The Religious Education component is used to support current and future religious education needs of the Muslim community.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: How do I determine which Self-Help Group my employee should contribute to?
questions.text:
You are expected to request for your employee's race/religion to determine the correct Self-Help Group (SHG) to contribute to. For employees with double-barrelled race, you can refer to the first component of the double-barrelled race on your employee’s NRIC to ascertain which SHGs fund your employee should contribute to.
Employees who do not wish to contribute or wish to contribute a different amount can contact the respective SHGs for more information.
You can refer to the following examples on how to determine the correct Self-Help Group (SHG) for your employees:
Employee’s race indicated on NRIC is Indian-Chinese
As the first component of the double-barrelled race indicated in your employee’s NRIC is Indian, your employee will need to contribute to the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) Fund.
However, your employee can choose to contribute to both funds, SINDA and Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC), by informing you of their preference.
Employee is a Muslim and race indicated on NRIC is Indian
Your employee will need to contribute to both SINDA and Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF).
Employee is a Muslim and race indicated on NRIC is Indian-Chinese
As the first component of the double-barrelled race indicated in the NRIC is Indian and your employee is a Muslim, your employee will need to contribute to both SINDA and MBMF.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: Why should contributions be made to the Self-Help Groups (SHGs)?
questions.text: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) were set up to uplift low-income households and the less privileged, in the Chinese, Eurasian, Muslim, and Indian communities in Singapore. Your employees’ contributions to SHGs can help their respective communities.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: How do I pay my employees' Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions?
questions.text: You are expected to deduct the Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions from your employees' wages and pay the SHG contributions together with the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: My employees do not wish to contribute to their respective Self-Help Groups (SHGs). What can my employees do?
questions.text: Your employees who do not wish to contribute to their respective Self-Help Groups (SHGs) can contact the respective SHGs for more information.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: What should I do if I have omitted or under-paid to the Self-Help Groups (SHGs)?
questions.text:
If you have omitted or underpaid to the Self-Help Groups (SHGs), please refer to the following SHGs to find out how to back pay the contributions.
For Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC) Fund, Eurasian Community Fund (ECF) and Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) Fund
Please back pay starting from January of the current year, even if there were omissions for past years. Please include the omitted amounts in your next contribution submission to CPF Board.
For Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF)
Please back pay starting from the day it was omitted (including past years’ omissions). Please include the omitted amounts in your next contribution submission to CPF Board.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: How would I know if my employee has changed religion and hence I would need to change my employee's Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions accordingly?
questions.text:
Only contributions to the Mosque Building Mendaki Fund (MBMF) is based on your employee’s religion. Contributions to other Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are based on your employee’s race indicated on the NRIC.
Your employees are responsible to update you on any changes. Any deduction should also be reflected in your employee’s payslip so that the employees can highlight to you if the contributions are not deducted correctly for the right SHG.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: Are Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions payable for 13th month wage?
questions.text: Contribution to the Self-Help Group (SHG) funds are based on the total wages payable to an employee in a calendar month, which include the 13th month wage.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: Is Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions deductible if my employee did not work for the full month?
questions.text: Contributions to the Self-Help Group (SHG) funds are payable as long as your employee is paid wages in the month. It does not depend on the number of days worked.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: Are Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions payable for an intern on an internship programme?
questions.text:
For Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC) Fund, Eurasian Community Fund (ECF) and Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) Fund:
Contributions to the Self-Help Groups (SHGs) funds are payable for interns on internship programme if CPF contributions are payable. You may refer to this FAQ for more information on whether CPF contributions are payable for student employees.
For Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund (MBMF):
Please refer to the section on "Student Pay" at the MUIS website to find out whether MBMF is payable for an intern.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: My employee has left the organisation. Are Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions still payable?
questions.text: Contributions to the Self-Help Groups are payable as long as there are outstanding wages payment to be made.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: If my employee is under multiple employment, is he/she required to contribute to the Self-Help Group (SHG) fund via all his/her employers?
questions.text: You are expected to deduct your employee’s contributions to the Self-Help Group (SHG) from his/her wages. However, your employee can choose to contribute through one employer only by informing his/her SHG.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: What is CPF Submission Number (CSN)?
questions.text:
CPF Submission Number (CSN) is a unique identifier used by employers to transact with CPF Board. This includes making CPF payments and making any request relating to employer matters.
A CSN consists of an Unique Entity Number (UEN) or NRIC/FIN (if you’re trading under your own name) and a CPF Payment Code.
You will need to apply for a different CSN for each type of payment you are making. Some examples include mandatory CPF contributions, Voluntary contributions, MediSave contributions under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: What is the CPF Payment Code?
questions.text: The CPF Payment Code in your CPF Submission Number (CSN) identifies the different types of payments made by employers to the Board such as mandatory CPF contributions, Voluntary Contributions, and MediSave contributions under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme. You will need to apply for a different CSN for each type of payment that you are making.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: How do I start contributing CPF as a new employer?
questions.text: You will need a CPF Submission Number (CSN) to transact with CPF Board. You can refer to this guide to learn how to apply for a CSN and submit CPF contributions via CPF EZPay in five steps.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: Is it mandatory for all companies to apply for a CPF Submission Number (CSN) with the CPF Board?
questions.text: All employers are required to apply for a CPF Submission Number with the Board before they can submit their CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: Can I use my Unique Entity Number (UEN) to perform transactions with CPF Board? Why do I have to use my CPF Submission Number (CSN)?
questions.text: You must use your CPF Submission Number (CSN) to perform transactions with CPF Board. The CSN is the Unique Entity Number (UEN) + CPF Payment Code. The UEN alone is not sufficient to identify the different types of CPF payments made by you.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if my subsidiary company has a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company?
questions.text: You are required to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if your subsidiary company has a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company. To apply for a CSN, please submit your application using Apply for CPF Submission Number.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: I have ceased engaging employee(s) for a period of time. Can I use my previously issued CPF Submission Number (CSN) to pay CPF contributions for newly hired employee(s)?
questions.text: You can use the previously issued CPF Submission Number (CSN) to pay CPF contributions for your employee(s), provided that your UEN remains the same for your business entity or you are an individual trading under your own name.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: If I do not have a Unique Entity Number (UEN), can I register with the Board to pay my employees' CPF contributions?
questions.text:
You can apply for a CPF Submission Number (CSN) as you are considered to be trading under your own name hiring Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident employees in your own capacity.
Some examples of employers trading under their own name include hawker hiring a hawker assistant, or a person who hires a personal driver, gardener, or domestic worker.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: How can the employees' CPF Account information under the old company be transferred to the new company?
questions.text: CPF Board is unable to transfer the CPF Account details of employees from the old to the new company. Employers must apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) for the new company and inform the Board to cancel the old company's existing CSN. When submitting the first CPF payment under the new CSN, employers must provide the CPF Account information for all employees.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: How long does it take to process the “Apply for CPF Submission Number” online application?
questions.text:
Service
Normal Processing Time
Apply for CPF Submission Number – Mandatory contribution
Immediately upon submission.
Apply for CPF Submission Number – Voluntary contribution/Additional MediSave contribution Scheme
Within seven working days.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: When and how do I obtain my CPF Submission Number (CSN) as a new employer?
questions.text:
You should apply for your CPF Submission Number (CSN) as soon as you intend to hire your first employee. You will need your Singpass and entity's Unique Entity Number (UEN) to complete the application.
You can refer to this guide on how you start contributing CPF as a new employer.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: How can I apply for an additional CPF Submission Number (CSN) for my MOM Work Permit or for payroll segregation purposes?
questions.text:
To apply for an additional CPF Submission Number (CSN) for MOM Work Permit purposes or for payroll segregation, please submit your application using the Apply for CPF Submission Number form.
Do note that you need to have obtained prior approval from MOM's Work Pass Division before proceeding with the application for additional CSN for MOM Work Permit purposes.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: What is new in the updated 'Apply for CPF Submission Number' form?
questions.text: With this updated form, you can receive your CPF Submission Number (CSN) instantly upon completing the application for mandatory contributions. The user-friendly design and intuitive user interface would make it easier and more convenient for you to navigate and complete the form.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Applying for a CPF submission number

questions.title: I have set up a new company and transferred my existing employees to that company. Do I need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN)?
questions.text:
You will need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) in order to make CPF contributions for a new company. The CSN is made up of the Unique Entity Number (UEN) and CPF Payment Code, which are unique to the entity.
You can apply for a new CSN on the CPF website, and once processed, a new CSN will be issued. Please provide the employees' account information when making the first payment under the new CSN, as CPF Board is unable to transfer the details from the old CSN. Refer to the "Apply for CSN and Setup CPF EZPay Quick Guide" for more information on CSN application.
You will also need to inform the Board if you cease to engage any employees under the old UEN to prevent late payment penalties.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: What should I do if there is a change in employee's particulars?
questions.text:
Please ensure that your affected employees inform the Board of any changes in their personal particulars which include:
1. Change in name
2. Change in Passport/ Identity Card / Special Pass number
3. Change in Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) or citizenship status
Your employee who has been issued with a new Singapore Identity Card will be given new CPF account. The new CPF account number is the same as his new Singapore Identity Card number. You should therefore pay CPF contributions into the new CPF account, and inform your employee to contact CPF Board to merge his previous CPF account (if any) with the new CPF account. This is to ensure that only one CPF account is maintained for the employee concerned. Submission of CPF contributions to accounts with an SA/SB/SD/SF/TC/TF prefix will be rejected.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: Do I need to update my employer's contact information at both the “Account settings” and CPF EZPay?
questions.text: You are only required to update employer's contact details under “Account settings”.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: I am the authorised payroll vendor representing the company, can I update the employer particulars on behalf of my client?
questions.text: If your Corppass Administrator has granted you access to the "CPF Services For Employers And Business Partners" e-Service via the Corppass portal, you can update the employer particulars on behalf of your client.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: How do I inform CPF Board when I am issued with a new Unique Entity Number (UEN)?
questions.text:
If you are issued with a new Unique Entity Number (UEN), you will need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) under the new entity to make your CPF contributions.
You are also required to inform us via Write to us if you no longer have any employees in your service under the old UEN.
After you are issued with the new CSN, you are required to set up your Direct Debit arrangement.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: How long does it take to update entity's particulars?
questions.text:
Service
Normal Processing Time
Update Employer's Particulars
Immediately upon submission.
An email notification will be sent to both the owner (or employer representative) and the person in charge of CPF contribution matters once the employer particulars have been updated.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: How can I view the status of my applications?
questions.text:
You can simply log in to "Other employer services – Activities" using your Singpass and 2-Step Verification (2FA) to view the status of your online transactions.
With the improved "Activities" feature, you can stay updated on the latest status of your online transactions, such as whether your application has been received, is being processed, or has been rejected or approved.
As CPF Board is progressively updating some features, you may find that some online transactions performed previously are not available for viewing. Please write to us if you require any details which are not viewable.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: What is CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
CPF EZPay is a free service provided by CPF Board where employers can submit their employees’ CPF contribution details and make payment electronically.
Find out how you can submit CPF contributions easily via CPF EZPay and make payment using Direct Debit.
To find out more about how to use CPF EZPay, you may refer to the User Guide (PDF, 2.0MB) or watch the Video Guide on YouTube.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How can I submit CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
You can submit your CPF contributions easily using CPF EZPay with Singpass. Enjoy hassle-free submission by making use of the auto-computation feature or set up an Electronic Standing Instruction (ESI) for recurring monthly submissions.
If you have 10 or fewer employees and would like to submit your CPF contributions on-the-go, you can do so using CPF EZPay Mobile. Simply download the app on your mobile phone to get started.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: If I have more than one CPF Submission Number (CSN), can I use CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
You can use CPF EZPay if you have more than one CPF Submission Number (CSN). There is no limit on the number of CSNs.
However, you must apply for Direct Debit for each CSN.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I appoint or change Administrator for CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
To appoint or change Administrator for CPF EZPay, please refer to the following options:
For UEN-registered entity
Your Corppass Admin or Sub-Admin can appoint or change your Administrator by assigning the “CPF EZPay” e-service to another authorised officer within Corppass portal. Please refer to this guide (PDF, 1.5MB) for more information.
For individual trading under own name
Your existing Administrators within CPF EZPay can add new Administrators. Please refer to our user guide (PDF, 3.7MB) for more information.
If you only have one Administrator who has left, you will need to write to us stating your reason for addition/removal of Administrator for us to assist you.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I update my employee database on CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
Please login to CPF EZPay to update your Employee Database. If the employee has left the company and no more CPF contribution is payable to him/her, please tick the checkbox beside the employee record and select Delete Employee Record to delete this employee from the database.
If you are still required to pay CPF for this employee, please perform the following steps:
Select Detail button corresponding to the employee record and Key/Update Staff Information screen will pop-up.
Indicate the Employment Status for that employee as Left and indicate the date employee left at the Date Left Employment column.
Once the employee record has been updated, please select Save Changes. A confirmation message "Employee Database saved successfully" will be displayed.
You can delete this employee from the database in the following month’s submission.
If your company no longer has any employees or ceased operations, please notify us immediately through write to us to avoid incurring late payment interest and composition amount.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I import my employee's details in CPF EZPay if I'm using Microsoft Excel?
questions.text:
Please follow these steps when importing your employee's details from Microsoft Excel Template File for submission via CPF EZPay:
Login to CPF EZPay
Select For UEN-registered entities or For individuals trading under own name and log in with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Submit Contribution, select CPF EZPay.
At Contribution Details For, key in the Month and Year.
Select Submit via Employee Database and select Continue.
Select Import Employee Details.
Select Import from MS Excel Template file.
Click on Choose File to select the file which you wish to import.
Next, select Import File and you will be directed to Preview of Imported Records. Select Confirm & Save.
A pop-up message "Importing this file will replace ALL employee details in your Employee Database. Do you want to continue" will be displayed.
Select OK and you will be directed to the Update Employee Database page.
The confirmation message "File imported successfully. Please update the field "PR Start Date" for all your Permanent Resident employees" will be displayed on the same page. Please ensure that you have keyed in the PR Start Date for any Singapore Permanent Resident employees to ensure correct auto-computation of CPF contributions.
Note: To understand the fields inside the sample template, please click on the help icon. Please fill up all the mandatory fields marked with "*" in our sample template and ensure that your file is saved as a .csv file. You may also copy and paste details from your payroll MS Excel file into our .csv template. To do so, please click on Download Sample Template to download our template, and copy the employee details from your existing spreadsheet into our template.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Can CPF EZPay calculate the CPF contributions for Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs)?
questions.text: CPF EZPay is able to calculate CPF contributions for SPRs. You will need to key in the SPR Start Date and select the Type (e.g. GG - Graduated or FG - full CPF contributions rates). This will allow CPF EZPay to track the SPR status of your employee and auto-update the CPF contribution to be paid (e.g. from SPR Year 1 to Year 2 or Year 2 to year 3).
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Does CPF EZPay compute Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling?
questions.text: CPF EZPay does not compute AW Ceiling as it does not track wages on an annual basis. You may use our CPF Additional Wage Ceiling Calculator to calculate the AW Ceiling or do so manually.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I print the CPF EZPay acknowledgement if I have closed the browser?
questions.text:
It is not possible to print the "CPF EZPay Acknowledgement" page once you have closed the browser.
Instead, you may login to our CPF EZPay to view the status of your submission.
You will also receive an email from the Board within the day acknowledging the receipt of your submission.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How can I view my CPF contribution details in CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
You can save a copy of the CPF contribution details by following these steps:
Select CPF EZPay
Select For UEN-registered entities or For individuals trading under own name and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Manage Records & Preferences, select View / Amend / Delete Submission
Click on the Submission Date to view the Contribution details.
You will be directed to the View Employer Submission Page.
To save this page, click on the Printer icon. You will be prompted to download a PDF file which you can save.
IMPORTANT!
If you wish to print a copy of the contribution details only, please do not use the Amend submission function as it will result in the withdrawal of your submitted file.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: If I have already made payment, can I amend or delete my submission?
questions.text:
The procedure to amend or delete your CPF EZPay submission depends on your payment method and submission status:
For Direct Debit
(i) Status: "Submitted"
You can still make changes in CPF EZPay. Go to View / Amend / Delete Submission. You can:
change amounts for employees,
delete an employee from the submission or
amend other payment amounts, such as CPF Late Payment Interest.
However, you cannot change Ordinary Wage, Additional Wage, or staff details such as date of birth. To update these, delete the submission and start a new one. After amending, re-submit your CPF contributions. An amended submission stays in Draft mode and it will not go through for Direct Debit deduction until you finish the full submission process.
(ii) Status: "Processed"
You can no longer amend or delete the submission. Submissions are processed at 5:15pm on the same day they are made.
If you underpaid: Use ad hoc CPF payments in CPF EZPay to pay the shortfall for the affected employee(s) and month(s). Enter the shortfall amount and declare the full wages earned for that month. Please refer to our CPF EZPay Quick Guide for instructions on how to correct errors after a submission has been processed.
If you overpaid or paid the wrong employee(s): Apply for a refund right away. You must do this no later than one year from the date of payment. Refunds are subject to the availability of funds in the member's CPF account.
For PayNow QR
Once you reach the payment page with the generated QR code, you cannot make any more changes.
If you underpaid: Use ad hoc CPF payments in CPF EZPay to pay the shortfall for the affected employee(s) and month(s). Declare the full wages earned for the month and the shortfall amount. Please refer to our CPF EZPay Quick Guide for instructions on how to correct errors after a submission has been processed.
If you overpaid or paid the wrong employee(s): Apply for a refund right away. You must do this no later than one year from the date of payment. Refunds are subject to the availability of funds in the member's CPF account.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of submissions I can perform each day using CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
There are different limits to the number of CPF submissions that you can perform each day.
CPF EZPay
You can submit up to 99 submissions within the day. If you try to make additional submissions, our system will prompt you with the message “A file with the same advice code has already been submitted”.
CPF EZPay (FTP)
Multiple file submissions within the same day are allowed, provided a different advice code is used in the submission file. If you are submitting a file using the same advice code or more than 99 files, you will be prompted with a message “A file with the same advice code has been already submitted. Please change the advice code and re-submit”.
For more information on how to assign an advice code, please refer to CPF EZPay FTP guide (PDF, 3.7MB).
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I make CPF back payments for my employees?
questions.text:
You can make back payments into your employees’ CPF accounts through CPF EZPay or CPF EZPay Mobile. Find out more about declaring accurate wage information.
CPF EZPay
You can submit CPF contributions as per normal via CPF EZPay but select the correct Month and Year for your back payments. Please note that changes made will be saved to your employee database in CPF EZPay for future CPF submissions.
If you do not wish to affect your employee database in CPF EZPay for future CPF submissions, you can make use of the Submit ad hoc CPF payments option to submit your back payments instead. Auto-computation is not available for this option. However, you can load employee details from submissions made up to six months ago.
Here’s how to use the Submit ad hoc CPF payments option in CPF EZPay:
Select CPF EZPay
Select For UEN-registered entities or For individuals trading under own name and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Submit Contribution, select CPF EZPay.
Key in the Month and Year.
Select Submit ad hoc CPF payments (For one-time CPF submission (no auto-computation), or other ad hoc payments e.g. late payment interest).
Enter the CPF contribution details for the affected employee. [Tip: You can use the CPF calculator to compute and verify the contribution amount.]
Enter total wages payable for the month.
After completing all of the contribution details and the summary portion, click on Continue.
Confirm submission by clicking on your pre-arranged payment mode with the Board (Direct Debit/PayNow QR).
CPF EZPay Mobile
You can also submit CPF contributions via CPF EZPay Mobile and make payment via PayNow QR by selecting the correct Month and Year for your back payments. You can refer to this guide on how you can make a submission.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: I currently submit CPF contributions using my own payroll software. How do I switch to CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
If you are currently submitting CPF contributions within your payroll software, you are already registered for CPF EZPay as well. Simply login to CPF EZPay from our CPF website to submit your monthly CPF contributions using CPF EZPay.
Find out more about the various ways you can submit your CPF contributions using CPF EZPay.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Is there an electronic submission mode I can use if I don't have a Singpass account?
questions.text:
You can use CPF EZPay Mobile to submit CPF contributions for 10 or fewer employees and pay via PayNow QR.
If you need to manage more employees, you should use CPF EZPay for your CPF submissions. You are encouraged to apply for Singpass or visit any of the Singpass counters located islandwide in-person.
If you are a UEN-registered entity, you will need Corppass access and perform a one-time setup before using CPF EZPay. Please refer to this guide for the steps.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: I am submitting CPF contributions via CPF EZPay. How can I link up my CPF data for the Auto Inclusion Scheme (AIS) under IRAS?
questions.text: You can visit IRAS website to sign up for the CPF Data Link-up Service.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: When and how can I submit CPF contributions after obtaining my new CPF Submission Number?
questions.text:
You may submit your CPF contributions via the following methods:
Submitting Your CPF Contributions via CPF EZPay Mobile
If your CSN application was submitted before 5pm, you can submit your CPF contributions via CPF EZPay Mobile the next day.
Submitting Your CPF Contributions via CPF EZPay
If your CSN application was submitted before 5pm, you can submit your CPF contributions via CPF EZPay two days later.
Note: For UEN-registered entity, please be reminded to perform a one-time setup at Corppass portal before you can login to CPF EZPay.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I submit CPF Contribution via CPF EZPay (ESI)?
questions.text:
If you're already on Direct Debit payment mode, and generally your employeess' wages do not change every month, you can set up Electronic Standing Instruction (ESI) within CPF EZPay. Once your ESI is set up, your monthly submission and deduction will be automatically made to us.
You’re required to amend your employee’s wages in ESI if there are changes so the CPF contributions to be deducted are updated.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I make additional or back pay CPF contributions for my employees if I am submitting CPF contributions via Electronic Standing Instructions (ESI)?
questions.text:
On top of your existing Electronic Standing Instructions (ESI) arrangement, you can make additional or back payments of CPF contributions for your employees by performing an additional submissions via the steps below:
At ESI Main Menu, select Perform Additional Submission.
Select the Month and key in the Year you are submitting for and click Continue to proceed.
Enter the contribution details for the affected employee (key in only the shortfall CPF amount) but enter the full wages earned for the month.
After completing all the contribution details and the summary section (key in CPF late payment interest, if applicable), click on Continue.
Verify the contribution details and click Direct Debit to complete the payment.
You will see the online acknowledgement screen after the submission is completed successfully. An email will also be sent to your email address(es) registered with the Board.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I pay CPF late payment interest if I am submitting CPF contributions via Electronic Standing Instructions (ESI)?
questions.text:
For CPF contributions that are submitted via Electronic Standing Instructions (ESI), you can make payment for CPF late payment interest by performing an additional submission via the steps below:
At ESI Main Menu, select Perform Additional Submission.
Select the Month and key in the Year you are submitting for and click Continue to proceed.
Scroll down to the summary section and key in the outstanding CPF late payment interest amount under ‘2. CPF Late Payment Interest’. Click Continue.
Verify the payment details and click Direct Debit to complete the payment.
You will see the online acknowledgement screen after the submission is completed successfully. An email will also be sent to your email address(es) registered with the Board.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: I am using a payroll software to compute CPF contributions, can I submit the file directly to CPF Board?
questions.text: You can upload the submission file for your CPF contributions directly via CPF EZPay (FTP) (PDF, 3.7MB) if your file complies with our file specifications. If you are unsure, please check with your payroll software vendor for more information.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Am I required to do any test submission before I start using my own payroll software to submit via CPF EZPay (FTP)?
questions.text:
You are not required to do any test submission to CPF Board.
To know more about the CPF EZPay (FTP), you may refer to our user guide (PDF, 3.5MB).
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Is there a limit on the file size for each submission via CPF EZPay (FTP)?
questions.text: For better performance, we have limited the file size to 2 mega-bytes. You will not be able to send the file if it exceeds the file size limit.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What are Advice Codes and how do I use them when I upload my submission file via CPF EZPay (FTP)?
questions.text:
If you are submitting more than one file within the same day for the same CPF Submission Number (CSN), you will need to assign a different Advice Code for each file. Advice Codes act as a file numbering system to differentiate files created for different groups of employees belonging to the same CSN.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide (PDF, 3.7MB)
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What file types are acceptable for submission via CPF EZPay (FTP)? Why do I keep getting a file extension error when trying to perform submission?
questions.text:
Only text files conforming to our FTP file specifications (effective 16 Jan 2025) (PDF, 0.3MB) which end with a ".dtl", ".txt" or ".dat" extensions are acceptable. Please check that your file ends with one of these extensions.
If you encounter file extension error when trying to perform submission, please check to see if any of the folders within the path contains ".". The reason is because the system will treat anything behind "." as the extension of the file.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide (PDF, 3.7MB).
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Is it safe to submit my employee details through the internet using CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
The information you submit is encrypted using 2048-bits SSL, which is a common standard used by major online merchants, financial institutions, and brokerages worldwide to transmit secured documents via the Internet.
Only designated staff assigned by you will be able to log in to use CPF EZPay. After each successful submission, an acknowledgement email will be sent to your designated email address. You can also log in to enquire about the submission status and view the Record of Payment online.
Therefore, it is safe to submit your employees’ details using CPF EZPay.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What are the supported web browsers for CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
CPF EZPay is best viewed using the following browsers :
Apple Safari 16.6 and above
Google Chrome 123 and above
Microsoft Edge 122 and above
Mozilla Firefox 123 and above
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What browser settings are required for me to use CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
Your browser’s default settings should be sufficient to allow you to use CPF EZPay. If you are unable to access CPF EZPay, please check that you have the following features enabled:
Cookies
Java Script
TLS (Transport Layer Security) Versions 1.0, 1.1 or 1.2
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What is CPF EZPay Mobile?
questions.text:
CPF EZPay Mobile is a mobile application suitable for submitting CPF contributions for 10 or fewer employees, anytime and anywhere.
Here’s what you need to know about CPF EZPay Mobile:
Registration is not required. Simply download the app from Apple App Store or Google Play to begin. Please ensure that the developer of the application is Central Provident Fund Board.
Save and load your employee’s details, and easily amend them for your monthly submissions.
Make payment via PayNow QR.
To find out more about how to use CPF EZPay Mobile, you may refer to the User Guide (PDF, 2.3MB) or watch the Video Guide on YouTube.
This app is now available for download from the Apple App Store or Google Play (only for Android phones running on Android OS. 5.0 and above)!
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay mobile

questions.title: What are the benefits of using CPF EZPay Mobile?
questions.text:
By using CPF EZPay Mobile, you will enjoy:
Fuss-free submission of your CPF contribution details via any mobile platform
Option to load the employee details and email address from the previous submission
Mobile optimised screen for positive user experience
Secure payment via PayNow QR
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay mobile

questions.title: How do I pay using CPF EZPay Mobile?
questions.text: After submitting the CPF contribution details via CPF EZPay Mobile, employers can pay via PayNow QR (supports personal or corporate accounts of participating banks).
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay mobile

questions.title: What are the available payment modes for CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Payments for CPF contributions can be made using any one of the modes listed below. Please note that CPF contribution details must be submitted together with payments for CPF contributions.
Direct Debit (Recommended)
PayNow QR (supports personal or corporate bank account of participating banks)
Find out more on these payment modes available to you. If your bank is not an eGIRO or a PayNow participating bank, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: If I submit my CPF contributions via CPF EZPay, can I switch from one payment mode to another at any one time?
questions.text: You can choose to pay via Direct Debit or PayNow QR at the point of submission.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: If I am paying via Direct Debit, when will CPF Board deduct from my bank account after my CPF submission?
questions.text:
Direct Debit deduction will only take place after you have submitted your CPF contribution details. If you are submitting via CPF EZPay, you can update the deduction date in the "Deduction On" field below the "Direct Debit" button.
If you have set up Electronic Standing Instruction (ESI) within CPF EZPay, the deduction date will be the 3rd working day from the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
Please remember to maintain sufficient funds for successful deduction. If your deduction fails, there will be a 2nd deduction seven calendar days later (or next working day if it falls on a public holiday). This may result in late CPF submission and incur late payment interest.
Please note that only one deduction will be made for voluntary contributions (i.e. Voluntary Contributions to three CPF accounts and Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme) submissions. You will need to resubmit the contribution details if the deduction fails.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: How do I terminate my Direct Debit arrangement for payment of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
If you no longer wish to pay your CPF contributions by Direct Debit, please submit your request to terminate your direct debit arrangement.
After the CPF Board has processed the request, we will inform you accordingly. Please also notify your bank on the termination so that they can update their records.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: How can I proceed to make payment if the PayNow QR code for paying my employees' CPF contributions expires?
questions.text:
The PayNow QR code to pay your CPF contributions must be scanned before 23:59 hrs on the day of submission. If your QR code has expired, you will not be able to make the payment, and you will need to resubmit your CPF contributions and get a new PayNow QR code.
After your payment has been made, your payment status will be updated as "Paid" in CPF EZPay instantly.
Please make sure you have sufficient funds in your bank account before the payment is processed. If you have set a PayNow payment limit with your bank, do ensure that the limit is sufficient to pay your CPF contributions. Some banks may charge an administrative fee for unsuccessful payment attempts.
Please perform a new submission and scan the QR code to make payment within the same day.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: How do I pay CPF contributions using PayNow QR?
questions.text:
PayNow QR is a quick way for you to make payment for CPF contributions by scanning a QR code, via existing mobile banking apps. PayNow QR allows you to use corporate or personal accounts to pay your CPF contributions. You would have to scan the PayNow QR code using a PayNow participating bank’s app in order for the payment to be processed successfully. Any payment made without using the issued PayNow QR code (e.g. making payment directly to CPF Board’s UEN or changing the details after scanning the PayNow QR code) or multiple payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded with the reference code “CPF”.
The maximum amount you can transfer via PayNow QR is $200,000, subject to daily and monthly limits set by your bank. If your total CPF submission amount exceeds $200,000, you will need to perform another submission via CPF EZPay. For example, if your total CPF submission amount is $300,000, you will need to make two separate CPF submissions via CPF EZPay consisting of $200,000 and $100,000 respectively.
Please make sure you have sufficient funds in your bank account before the payment is deducted. If you have set a PayNow payment limit with your bank, do ensure that the limit is sufficient to pay your CPF contributions. Some banks may charge an administrative fee for each unsuccessful payment attempt.
Personal bank account
On the day of submission, you must ensure that you scan the PayNow QR code and pay using your PayNow participating bank's app before it expires at 23:59 hrs. Once the QR code has expired, you will not be able to make the payment, and will need to resubmit your CPF contributions and get a new PayNow QR code.
After your payment has been made, your payment status will be updated as "Paid" in CPF EZPay almost instantly.
Corporate bank account
Two-level authorisation (Maker and Checker) is required for PayNow Corporate account users. Please make sure the Maker scans the PayNow QR code before it expires at 23:59hrs, following which the Authoriser should approve the payment immediately. Payment received after seven working days from date of CPF submission will be refunded. You will need to make a new CPF submission with a fresh PayNow QR payment.
If the Maker did not scan the PayNow QR code before it expires, you’ll need to resubmit your CPF contributions and get a new PayNow QR code.
After your payment has been approved, your payment status will be updated as "Paid" in CPF EZPay almost instantly.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: What are the types of Voluntary Contributions (VC) I can make for my employees?
questions.text:
You can make Voluntary Contributions (VC) to:
Your employee(s)' Special or Retirement Account under the Retirement Sum Topping Up Scheme (RSTU) (tax deduction available to employer and tax relief available to employee).*
Your employee(s)' MediSave Account (tax deduction available to employer and tax relief available to employee ). *
Your employee(s)' MediSave Account via the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme (AMCS) (tax free for employees and tax benefits available to employers). #
Your employee(s)' three CPF accounts (no tax deduction for employer and no tax relief for employee). #
Please note that your employees must be Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents only.
# The VC made will be treated as the current month's contribution. Backdating of VC to an earlier date is not allowed.
* If your employee is eligible to receive matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme or the Matched MediSave Scheme, he/she will not receive tax relief for the top-ups that qualify for the matching grants.
You can find out more on the types of VC you can make for your employees.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: What are the applicable limits if I wish to make Voluntary Contributions (VC) for my employees?
questions.text:
You can make four types of Voluntary Contributions (VC) for your employees:
Type of VC
VC Limit
i) Cash top-ups to your employee(s)’ Special or Retirement Account
For members below 55: up till the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS)
For members 55 and above: up till the current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)
Learn more about how you can earn tax deductions for cash top-ups made on your employee(s)’ behalf.
ii) Cash top-ups to your employee(s)' MediSave Account
Up to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) of the employee.
If the top-up amount exceeds the employee's BHS, the application will be rejected.
Learn more about how you can earn tax deductions for cash top-ups.
iii) VC to your employee(s)’ MediSave Account only under the Additional MediSave Contribution Scheme (AMCS).
Up to $2,730 per employee per year. Any VC exceeding this limit will be refunded without interest to the employer in the following year.
This VC is not limited by the employee's BHS. Any VC made above the BHS will be channelled to the employee's Special Account or Retirement Account, or Ordinary Account if the FRS has aso been met.
Use payment code "AMS" for the current CPF submission Number when making AMCS contributions.
Backdating of VC is not allowed..
iv) VC to your employee(s)' three CPF Accounts.
Up to the CPF Annual Limit ($37,740 per employee per year) less the mandatory contributions received by the employee for the calendar year.
Do consider the mandatory CPF contributions you will be making for your employee, before making VC. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and VC received by the employee exceeds the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, VC in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.
Use payment code "VCT" for the CPF Submission Number when making VC to three accounts.
Backdating of VC is not allowed.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: CPF Board encourages retirement savings but a limit was set for the contributions. Why is that so?
questions.text: There is a limit set as the CPF system is generally meant to cater to the needs of up to 80th percentile of workers in Singapore. Higher income earners would have other means to supplement their retirement income.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: What will happen if I pay late or do not pay CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
As an employer, you are legally obligated to pay CPF contributions correctly and promptly for your employees. Non-compliance of CPF contributions is an offence. Upon detection of such non-compliance, CPF Board will take enforcement actions to recover any CPF contributions owed to your employees and impose penalties (which include late payment interest and composition amount).
If employers do not pay all outstanding CPF contributions, late payment interest, and the composition amount (if any) by a given deadline, CPF Board will commence prosecution actions against you. Upon conviction, the court will order you to pay the outstanding CPF contributions, late payment interest as well as a court fine and/or be sentenced to imprisonment.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: What is the purpose of the late payment interest?
questions.text: The late payment interest, subjected to a minimum amount of $5, serves to deter employers from paying CPF contributions late for their employees.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: How much composition amount should I pay?
questions.text: The composition amount is indicated in the letter of offer/notice to attend court. Please refer to the penalties that may be faced by employers who do not comply with the CPF Act.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Why should I be jailed for non-payment of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
As an employer, you are legally obligated to pay CPF contributions correctly and promptly for your employees. Non-compliance of CPF contributions is an offence. CPF Board takes a serious view on employers who do not fulfil their CPF obligations to their employees. The jail term reflects the severity of CPF offences and serves as a strong deterrence to errant employers. It is also a reminder of the importance of employers’ legal obligation to pay CPF contributions correctly and promptly for their employees.
The penalties stipulated under the CPF Act for employers convicted of late payment offence are:
Up to $5,000 court fine and no less than $1,000 per offence and/or up to 6 months’ imprisonment for first conviction
Up to $10,000 court fine and no less than $2,000 per offence and/or up to 12 months’ imprisonment for subsequent convictions
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: I am unable to pay my outstanding CPF contributions/interest on late contributions for my employees now. Can I pay the composition amount first?
questions.text: You are required to pay all outstanding CPF contributions and interest on late contributions before the Board can accept payment of composition amount. For any clarification, please contact or email the case officer indicated in the Board's letter or Notice to Attend Court.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: My employee owes me money. Can I use the amount owed to me to offset the employer's share of CPF contributions that is payable on his wages?
questions.text: You are required to pay both the employer and employee’s share of CPF contributions based on the monthly wages payable to your employee at the prevailing CPF contribution rates.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Can I agree to my employee's request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay?
questions.text: You should not agree to your employee's request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay. Failure to pay CPF contributions to an employee (i.e. Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is employed in Singapore under a contract of service) is an offence under the CPF Act.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: What should I do if I am unable to pay my employees their CPF contributions on time?
questions.text:
It is the employer’s obligation to ensure that CPF contributions are paid on time and to communicate the CPF contributions payment dates to your employees. Your employees have the right to check with you on the non-payment of their CPF contributions, including asking for an explanation and when you will be making payment. CPF contributions are important to employees for their housing, healthcare and retirement needs. Information on the payment date and amount of CPF contributions will help them to better manage their financial needs and commitments.
If you are unable to pay your employees their CPF contributions on time, you have to ensure that the CPF arrears are paid as soon as possible and that the CPF contributions are accorded priority amongst the company’s outstanding payments. You should also inform your employees beforehand the reasons for being late and when they can expect the payment.
CPF Board takes a serious view of employers who default on CPF contributions. The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. The Board will take enforcement actions and impose penalties against employers who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month, composition amount and taking prosecution actions against employers.
Find out more on your obligations as an employer under the CPF Act and the Employment Act at the Workright website.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: I incurred late payment interest for my employee's late CPF contribution as he did not inform me of his Singapore Permanent Resident status. Can I recover the interest from him?
questions.text: The late payment interest is payable by the employer. It is an offence for employers to recover any sum in excess of the employee's share of CPF contributions from his wages.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: How is the application process for refund and adjustment of CPF contributions improved?
questions.text: The application form for refund and adjustment of CPF contributions simplifies data entry, performs upfront validation checks, and helps reduce errors and application rejection. For selected application types, you can include up to 20 employees in one application. The form also validates the refund payment arrangement before submission.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: My employee and I do not wish to apply for refund. Can the excess CPF contributions be retained in the employee's CPF account?
questions.text: You should rectify any errors in CPF contributions early while the documentary evidence is fresh. Any request for refund of CPF contributions paid must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I apply the Additional Wage ceiling for the following scenarios: a) Employee A is working for two companies concurrently? b) Employee B is transferred from another entity?
questions.text:
The Additional Wage (AW) ceiling is applied on a per employer per calendar year basis.
As such, if your employee is working for two companies concurrently or if your employee is transferred from another entity, you must apply the AW ceiling separately.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How are the excess CPF contributions derived and from which month of my employee's CPF contributions be refunded?
questions.text:
The excess CPF contributions are derived by subtracting the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740 from the total mandatory CPF contributions paid for the year, and refunded from the latest month which excess CPF contributions were paid on the Ordinary Wage.
You may refer to an example.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the refunded amount less than the excess CPF contributions made for the year?
questions.text: The refunded amount is based on the available balances in your employee’s CPF account(s). If there are insufficient funds for the full refund, you will receive a partial refund instead.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: When am I required to refund the employee's share of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text: For excess CPF contributions automatically refunded by CPF Board, you are required to refund the employee’s share of excess CPF contributions to the employee once you receive the refund from the CPF Board.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I refund the employee's share of excess CPF contributions if the employee has already resigned?
questions.text: You may wish to liaise directly with the resigned employee on the employee’s preferred mode of payment.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I have paid excess CPF contributions above the Additional Wage (AW) ceiling and the CPF Annual Limit, how can I apply for a refund in these situations?
questions.text:
CPF contributions above the Additional Wage (AW) ceiling
If you had paid excess CPF contributions exceeding the AW ceiling, you should apply for a refund.
Select:
Refund of contributions paid:
Single employee or platform worker; or
Multiple employees or platform workers,
followed by the refund reason 'Paid contributions above Additional Wage Ceiling'.
To apply for a refund of payment made more than two years from the current date, please write to us by selecting ‘Compliance and rectifications’ under Subject and ‘Applying for Refund of CPF contributions’ under Category.
You can use the AW ceiling calculator to derive the excess amount to be refunded.
The total refund amount (employer's and employee's share) will be refunded to you. You are responsible for refunding the employee's share of CPF contributions directly to your employee(s) before submitting the application.
CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit
Starting February 2024, CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit for the preceding year will be automatically refunded to the employer.
However, there is no need to wait for the annual automatic refund. If you have paid excess CPF contributions above the CPF Annual Limit, you should apply for a refund promptly.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: What are conditional wages?
questions.text:
Conditional wages are wages paid to employee with condition(s) attached. Depending on the terms of employment or mutual agreement, such wages are repayable to employer when the employee fails to fulfil the condition(s).
Below are some examples of conditional wages:
Conditional Wages
Condition
Reason(s) for Failure to Fulfil the Condition
Sign-on/Retention bonus
Fulfilment of minimum service period
(a) Resignation
(b) Termination
Conditional performance bonus
Paid annual leave
Resignation/termination resulting in a reduction of annual leave entitlement which has to be converted to no pay leave
Commission
Meeting of performance/sales target(s)
Did not meet the agreed target(s)
Conditional salary increments
Advance salary paid on sales of goods/services
Return of goods/services
Goods or services were returned, e.g. due to client’s cancellation of insurance policy during free-look period etc.
Paid study leave
Completion of course
Failure to complete course
Conditional salary increments
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do we determine the date of conditional wages repayable?
questions.text:
The date of conditional wages repayable is the date on which the employee's obligation to repay the conditional wages arises due to non-fulfilment of the condition(s) tied to the payment, under the terms of employment or mutually agreed between the employer and employee.
Below are the guidelines that can be used in determining the date of wages repayable:
Conditional Wages
Condition
Guidelines - Date of Wages Repayable
Sign-on/Retention bonus
Fulfilment of minimum service period
Last date of service
Conditional performance bonus
Paid annual leave
(a) Last date of service (for resignation/termination) or
(b) Commencement date of no pay leave (for staff still in-service)
Commission
Meeting of performance/
sales target(s)
(a) Repayable date as provided in employment contract or any other relevant agreement
(b) Computation date* if (a) is not applicable
*The date which employer is able to establish the amount of conditional wages repayable by the employee to the employer
Conditional salary increments
Advance salary paid on sales of goods/services
Return of goods/services
Paid study leave
Completion of course
(a) Course discontinuation date or
(b) Repayable date as provided in employment contract or any other relevant agreement
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Do I need to refund the employee's share of CPF contributions to employee before applying for a refund of the contributions paid in error/on conditional wages repayable?
questions.text: It is the employer’s responsibility to ensure that the employee’s share of CPF contributions is deducted correctly. Therefore, the employer must refund the employee’s share of CPF contributions (where applicable) to employee before applying for the refund. If the refund application is successful, both employer’s and employee’s share of contributions will be refunded to the employer.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Which refund reason should I select for my refund of contributions paid?
questions.text: You should select the reason which best describes your reason for overpayment of CPF contributions. You may refer to this list of reasons (PDF, 55KB) which illustrates some examples for each refund reason.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why must refund or adjustment of CPF contributions paid in error be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions?
questions.text: Any errors in CPF contributions should be rectified early while the documentary evidence is fresh. To encourage employers and employees to check their CPF contributions and come forward to rectify errors as soon as possible, any request for refund and adjustment of CPF contributions paid in error must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for adjustment of CPF contributions
Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: One of my staff had left service last month but I have wrongly used the previous template for submission, should I re-submit another template without that resigned staff's details again?
questions.text: You should apply for a refund of CPF contributions that were paid in error for the employee who resigned.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Five out of my 20 staff have salary revision this month and I have already submitted the CPF contributions using the previous template. Should I re-submit the correct details for all the staff?
questions.text: You should pay the shortfall of the CPF contribution for the five affected staff only.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How long does CPF Board take to process my application for refund of contributions paid?
questions.text:
Service
Normal Processing Time
Refund and adjustment of contributions paid
Within one month upon receipt of the necessary information*
*This excludes the two working days that banks require to credit the monies to your bank account.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: If I have accidentally submitted the CPF contribution twice, what should I do?
questions.text: If you have accidentally submitted your CPF contribution twice, you can apply for a full refund of the wrong submission immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for adjustment of CPF contributions

questions.title: How long does it take for CPF Board to process my application for adjustment of contributions paid?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table for the service standards in processing your application for adjustment of contributions paid.
Service
Normal Processing Time
Refund and adjustment of contributions paid
Within one month upon receipt of the necessary information
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for adjustment of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why did the Government introduce Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) enables self-employed persons (SEPs) to make small regular contributions as and when they earn income. This reduces the MediSave contributions they have to pay in the following year (after SEPs declare their net trade income and have their MediSave computed).
CAYE can also help SEPs grow their money as they can start to earn an interest of up to 6% on their MediSave savings earlier.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why is Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) only piloted on Government procurement entities?
questions.text: The Government, as a service buyer, has taken the lead to implement and pilot Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). There are currently no plans to extend CAYE to the private sector.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What is Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
Under the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme, a MediSave contribution is required as and when a self-employed person (SEP) earns a service fee. Every time a service fee is paid to the SEP, the corporate service buyers (CSBs) or intermediaries making the payment will first deduct and credit a portion of the service fee to the SEP’s MediSave Account, before paying the remainder of the service fee to the SEP.
CAYE does not change the amount of MediSave contributions SEPs have to make based on their net trade income.
SEPs who provide services to government agencies are automatically enrolled into CAYE.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn
Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: When are Government procurement entities required to implement Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Since January 2020, Government procurement entities are required to implement Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) for payment of service fee to self-employed vendors. Vendors@Gov will automatically identify vendors covered under CAYE when they log in through Corppass or Singpass. These vendors will be notified of their participation in CAYE via prompts.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme, will corporate service buyers only be making MediSave contributions for self-employed vendors?
questions.text: Under the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) scheme, corporate service buyers do not need to make MediSave contributions for self-employed persons (SEPs) as SEPs are required to contribute to their MediSave Account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn
