questions.title: If I am paying via Direct Debit, when will CPF Board deduct from my bank account after my CPF submission as a platform operator?
questions.text:
Direct Debit deduction will only take place after you have submitted your CPF contribution details. After you have made your submission via CPF EZPay as a platform operator, you will see the deduction date in the "Deduction On" field below the "Direct Debit" button.
Please remember to maintain sufficient funds for successful deduction. If your deduction fails, there will be a 2nd deduction seven calendar days later (or next working day if it falls on a public holiday). This may result in late CPF submission and incur late payment interest.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: How do I change my company's Direct Debit account to pay CPF contribution?
questions.text:
To change your Direct Debit account for CPF contributions, simply submit a new application for Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) for your new bank account.
CPF contributions will continue to be deducted from the existing bank account until the new Direct Debit Authorisation form has been approved. Once it is approved, the previous Direct Debit arrangement will then be terminated.
Please refrain from submitting a new online DDA application to change your bank account while the deduction for your current submission is pending. This is to avoid unsuccessful deduction which may incur late payment interest. If you wish to change the bank account for Direct Debit deduction, you should only submit the new online DDA application after the deduction is successful.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: Which of my platform workers do I include in my file submission?
questions.text:
In your monthly submission to query on your platform workers’ opt in status for increased CPF contributions, please include all platform workers who joined your platform up to the 15th of that month), except the following:
Platform workers in the mandatory cohort, i,e born in 1995 or later.
Platform workers whom status you have previously queried that returned a result of “opt in”. As opt-ins cannot be reversed, you do not need to query the status of platform workers who have already opted in, as their status will not change.
Illustration
Scenario
Include?
Platform worker A (Born on or after 1995) joined my company on the 15th of this month.
No need to include. (He is under mandatory cohort)
Platform worker B (Born before 1995) joined my company on the 15th of this month.
Include.
Platform worker C (Born before 1995 and previous query result reflected him as opted in)
No need to include. His status remains as opted in.
Platform worker D (Born before 1995 and previous query result reflected him as not opted in)
Include.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of platform workers’ opt-in status query

questions.title: What if my platform worker joined after I submitted the monthly query?
questions.text: If your platform worker (born before 1995) joins after the 15th of the month, you should use the non-opt-in rate for him until you can determine his opt in status from the next month’s query.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of platform workers’ opt-in status query

questions.title: I have updated my preference via the notification preference form. Does this preference apply to other notifications sent by CPF Board?
questions.text: The notification preference only applies to the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons. Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.title: I have previously chosen to receive my notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons in hardcopy. Can I still change my preference?
questions.text:
Yes. Regardless of your current preference, you can update your preference anytime by completing the notification preference form.
Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons thereafter.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to receive the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons in hardcopy?
questions.text:
If you wish to receive your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via hardcopy instead, you may update your notification preference via the notification preference form using your Singpass. The hardcopy notice will be mailed to you at your residential address.
Your updated notification preference will take effect for any subsequent notice of CPF contributions thereafter.

questions.title: How will I know when my digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready for viewing?
questions.text:
You will receive an email notification to view your digital notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons via the self-employment dashboard when it is ready. If you do not have a registered email with CPF Board, you will receive an SMS notification instead. If you do not have a registered email address or mobile number, your notice will be sent to you in hardcopy at your residential address.
To ensure you receive prompt alerts when your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons is ready, please update your contact details via the account services page after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Can I attend the Home Protection Scheme medical examination if I am currently pregnant?
questions.text:
You can proceed with the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) medical examination even if you are currently pregnant. Please notify the clinic staff and doctor that you are pregnant so that chest X-ray will not be conducted.
Find out more:
What tests am I required to undergo for the Home Protection Scheme medical examination?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What should I do if I am currently overseas and unable to attend the Home Protection Scheme medical examination appointment?
questions.text:
We are unable to assess your eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and process your application, if you are unable to attend the HPS medical examination.
You can submit a new HPS application online, using your Singpass, when you have returned to Singapore. A medical examination would be arranged for you thereafter.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why should I use the Probate eService instead of filing physically at the Singapore Courts Service Bureau?
questions.text:
The Probate eService is a step-by-step guided online service that a sole executor (named in the deceased’s will) can use to apply for a Grant of Probate. The eService will assist the sole executor in preparing and submitting the required probate documents to the court.
Applicants who use the Probate eService do not need to make multiple trips to the Singapore Courts Service Bureaus. In addition, applicants who use the Probate eService can request portions of their forms to be automatically filled in. The eService does this by retrieving an applicant’s personal information from other government systems through MyInfo.
The deceased’s information may also be automatically filled in if the information is available via official government sources.

questions.title: I am unable to complete my Probate eService application in one sitting. Is there an option for me to save and continue with this later?
questions.text:
You will need to first complete/pass the Probate eService eligibility questionnaire in order to start filling up the probate application. SingPass login is not required for the eligibility questionnaire. Simply click on "Run eligibility check" at the bottom of https://services.judiciary.gov.sg/probate/.
Once you have started the application proper, the details which you provide as part of the application are automatically saved and you may stop and resume at anytime thereafter.

questions.title: For Probate applications, what does ‘sole executor’ mean?
questions.text:
A Grant of Probate legally recognises an individual (named in the deceased’s Will) as the executor of the deceased's estate. The appointed individual manages the deceased's property. This includes distributing the estate to the beneficiaries after payment of the deceased's debts and other expenses.
Sole executor means that the deceased’s Will named only one executor.
Please note that if there are other person(s) named in the Will as executor apart from yourself, you may not be a “sole executor” and may not be eligible to use the Probate eService.
Some examples are as follows:
Example 1: Mr Tan and Miss Lim have been named in the deceased’s Will as joint executors. If Mr Tan has since passed away, will Miss Lim be considered the sole executor?
Answer: No, Miss Lim is considered the “remaining executor” due to the death of Mr Tan and is therefore not a named sole executor under the deceased’s Will. Miss Lim is not eligible to use the Probate eService.
Example 2: Mr Ang has been named in the deceased’s Will as the only executor. The Will further states that if Mr Ang passes away or is unable to act as executor, Miss Wong will be appointed as executor instead. If Mr Ang has passed away or does not wish to act as executor, is Miss Wong a named sole executor?
Answer: No, Miss Wong is considered the ‘substituted executor’, and is therefore not a named sole executor under the deceased’s will. Miss Wong is not eligible to use the Probate eService.

questions.title: What is a ‘codicil’?
questions.text: A codicil is an addition or supplement that explains, modifies, or revokes a Will or part of one. The original Will and codicils (if any) are required in order to complete a Probate application process.

questions.title: It is stated that the deceased needed to be domiciled in Singapore at the time of death in order to use the Probate eService. What is the meaning of "domicile"?
questions.text:
Domicile is a legal concept and generally refers to the place that the person treats as their permanent home, or lives in and has a substantial connection with. There are different types of domiciles, including domicile of origin, and domicile of choice.
If you are uncertain of what the Deceased’s domicile might have been, you may wish to consult a lawyer for independent legal advice.

questions.title: If the deceased had passed away outside of Singapore, am I still eligible to use the Probate eService?
questions.text: No, at this time, you may only use the Probate eService if the deceased had passed away in Singapore.

questions.title: In order to be eligible for the Probate eService, it is stated that the total estimated value of the deceased’s estate must not be more than $2 million Singapore dollars. Does the estimated value of the deceased’s estate include the deceased’s liabilities/debts?
questions.text: No, the estate value for purpose of the eService criteria refers to the overall estate value and does not factor in any liabilities/debts of the deceased.

questions.title: The Probate eService currently only supports simple and straightforward Probate applications. Does the Family Justice Courts have plans to extend this service to a wider range of probate applications in the future?
questions.text:
The Probate eService is a relative new initiative launched by the Family Justice Courts in 2023 for less complex probate cases. We may, in the future, consider extending the Probate eService to cover a wider range of probate cases.
In the meantime, we encourage you to use the eligibility questionnaire to assess if you are currently eligible to use the Probate eService.

questions.title: Who can I approach to get the deceased’s Will certified as a true copy?
questions.text:
You may approach a lawyer to get the deceased’s will certified as a true copy. A directory of practising lawyers can be found on the Ministry of Law’s website.
From 15 October 2024 onwards, under the new Family Justice Rules, the certification by the lawyer must be on every page of the Will (view the correct verification required here).

questions.title: If the death occurred before 29 May 2022 and the deceased’s death certificate is not a digital death certificate issued by ICA, who can I approach to get the deceased’s death certificate certified as a true copy?
questions.text:
You may approach a lawyer to get the deceased’s death certificate certified as a true copy. A directory of practising lawyers can be found on the Ministry of Law’s website.
Please view the sample of a certified true copy of the death certificate here.

questions.title: Why do I still need to physically swear or affirm the Supporting Affidavit and Administration Oath before a Commissioner for Oaths?
questions.text:
After the court processes the initial documents for your probate application, you will need to file your Supporting Affidavit and Administration Oath. You will be able to download the sample forms directly from the Probate eService.
An affidavit is a signed statement of fact made under oath. It is one of the main ways to present evidence to the court.
The Supporting Affidavit and Administration Oath must be sworn or affirmed before a Commissioner of Oaths (CFO). A CFO may be a lawyer, court interpreter, government official or any other individual who is authorised to administer oaths and affirmations.
A directory of CFOs may be found here. Some CFOs provide virtual commissioning services and you may enquire directly with the CFOs regarding these. These services are chargeable by the CFOs.
Please note that you do not need to specifically approach a CFO at the Family Justice Courts to get your Supporting Affidavit and/or Administration Oath sworn/affirmed. CFOs at the Family Justice Courts are also not in a position to certify true copies of documents.

questions.title: What are the total fees involved if I were to use the Probate eService?
questions.text:
While the Probate eService is made available without any additional costs, the usual Court document fees, processing fees, and transmission fees will still apply (collectively known as the “Filing Fees”). These are approximately S$300 and must be paid regardless of whether you:
a) Engage a lawyer, or
b) Physically file your application at the Service Bureau.
These filing fees exclude:
a) Any rejection fees which the courts may charge, for incorrect/erroneous filing of documents;
b) Fees payable to the Commissioner for Oaths (CFO) to swear or affirm affidavits;
c) Fees payable to a lawyer to obtain a certified true copy of the deceased’s will; and
d) Fees payable to a lawyer to obtain a certified true copy of the death certificate (if applicable).
When using the Probate eService, applicants will need to provide a deposit of S$400 upon filing their application. This S$400 is meant to cover the estimated Filing Fees. Any unutilised monies will be refunded after the application has been completed (please refer to the section in these FAQs on refunds).

questions.title: What are “rejection fees” and why do I have to pay them?
questions.text:
Incorrect/erroneous documents which are filed with the courts will be charged a rejection fee.
Starting from 15 October 2024, under the new Family Justice Rules, this rejection fee is set at S$10 per document for the 1st rejection, $25 for the 2nd rejection and $50 for the 3rd rejection. This is to discourage wastage of resources.
The following is an example of when a document may be rejected:
- Filing a copy of the deceased’s Will without the required certification on every page of the Will. (view the correct verification required here).
Users are hence strongly encouraged to check and review their documents prior to submission.

questions.title: How long would it typically take for a Grant of Probate to be granted when using the Probate eService?
Is a “Printed Grant” necessary?
questions.text:
When the Court issues the Grant of Probate through the eService, you will be able to download a PDF copy of the issued Grant. This Grant is an “Authentic Court Order” which can be verified at https://www.courtorders.gov.sg/.
A “Printed Grant” (with an embossed court seal) is therefore optional. This document along with the required processing fee will cost an additional S$35.60.

questions.title: When can I request for a refund of the monies deposited in the Probate eService, and how do I request for it?
questions.text:
Following payment and document submission at Step 6 of the eService, you may request a refund at any time if the following conditions are satisfied:
Scenario 1:
After submission at Step 6 and before the Grant of Probate is issued
a. There is a positive balance in your account.
You may check your account balance via the “Transaction History” button located at the top right of the screen.
b. You have submitted a withdrawal request and the request has been accepted by the Court.
You may submit a request for withdrawal via the “Transaction History” pop-up screen. Once you have submitted the withdrawal request, you will not be able to proceed with the probate application. You may return to the eService application to check the status of the withdrawal request.
c. There must be no documents under the “Pending” status.
Scenario 2:
After Grant of Probate has been issued
a. There is a positive balance in your account.
You may check your account balance via the “Transaction History” button located at the top right of the screen.
b. There must be no documents under the “Pending” status.
If the above criteria for the respective scenarios are met, the “Request for Refund” button will be shown on the “Transaction History” pop-up screen. You will be required to provide the necessary bank account information for the account to which the refund should be credited.
After submitting the refund request, you will be able to view the details of the refund on the "Apply for Grant of Probate" page.

questions.title: How long will the processing of refund of the Probate eService deposit take? How would I know when the refund has been processed?
questions.text:
The vendor administering the Probate eService, will take about 2 weeks from the day that the request is submitted to process your refund.
If you have signed up for your bank's email notification service, you will receive a notification from your bank when your refund request is approved, and the money is transferred to your account.
You may also login to the eService to check the details and status of your refund request.
If you have any queries regarding the refund process, you may contact:
TOPPAN Ecquaria (TECQ)
Tel: (65) 6436 6628
Email: eLitigation@toppanecquaria.com

questions.title: If I do not wish to continue filing the Probate application on the Probate eService and would like to hire a lawyer, how do I transfer the case to them?
questions.text:
If you would like to seek the help of a lawyer to complete the filing process for the probate application, you may click on the floating side tab available on the right side of each screen to retrieve the unique access code/case number.
Share the access code/case number with your lawyer. Your lawyer will be able to retrieve the information you have filled out thus far in the application using the access code or filing the necessary documents to be appointed to the case if a case number (e.g. FC/P XX/2023) has been assigned to the application.

questions.title: I am a lawyer appointed by the applicant to take over a Probate application they have filed in the Probate eService, how do I retrieve the relevant information?
questions.text:
If the applicant has drafted an application in the Probate eService but has not submitted the application yet, you will need to get the unique access code from him/her to retrieve the draft information entered by the applicant in the eService.
Login to eLitigation and navigate to the “Pre-Filing” tab. Click on the “Retrieve eService Draft” to retrieve the draft probate application that was filed by the applicant in the eService using the access code. Note this is the same button used for retrieval of Simplified Divorce eService drafts.
If a case number has already been assigned to the probate application (e.g. FC/P XX/2023), please file a Notice of Appointment of Solicitors in eLitigation instead.

questions.title: If an applicant is faced with difficulties while using the Probate eService, where can they seek assistance from?
questions.text:
General non-urgent enquiries regarding the Probate eService may be directed to the Family Justice Courts via this online form.
However, all technical and deposit refund related enquiries should be directed to the eService's technical provider: (65) 6436 6628 (Helpdesk Hotline), directly.

questions.title: What are the changes to the Family Justice Rules and Practice Directions 2024 and should I be concerned with the changes?
questions.text:
From 15 October 2024, the old forms (Originating Summons and Statement) are no longer in use and the new application form (called Originating Application) for submission for Grant of Probate has been updated in Probate eService.
Users only have to log in to the eService using their Singpass and key in details of the death certificate of the deceased.
The required court forms will be automatically filled in with these details.

questions.title: What are some of the changes/enhancement to Probate eService from 15 October 2024 onwards?
questions.text:
Users of Probate eService were previously unable to submit Affidavit of Due Execution (only applicable when the Court sends you an email for this document) through Probate eService.
We have made enhancement to the eService and users are now able to file this document through Probate eService instead of physically going down to the SG Courts Services Bureau to do the filing.

questions.title: I do not have details of all the assets of the deceased. Must I fill in the Schedule of Assets during the initial filing?
questions.text:
You are encouraged to fill in the details of all the assets of the deceased during the initial filing as it would save you time and cost of preparing a Supplementary Affidavit later in the process.
However, if you do not have the details of all the assets of the deceased, you will be able to file the Schedule of Assets after Order-in-Terms has been granted by the Court. The Probate eService is designed to accept the Schedule of Assets and Schedule of Assets – Supplementary Affidavit (with additional cost) after the matter is granted Order-in-Terms.

questions.title: How do I prepare the Schedule of Assets and Schedule of Assets – Supplementary Affidavit in Probate eService after my matter is granted Order-in-Terms?
questions.text:
Log in to Probate eService using your Singpass and follow the system prompt to key in the list of assets and submit to the Court. If you are using the Probate eService, the Schedule of Assets document will be automatically generated for you. An example of how a completed Schedule of Assets may look like can be found at https://go.gov.sg/samplesoa.
Once the Schedule of Assets is approved, prepare the Schedule of Assets – Supplementary Affidavit. You may view a sample here.
Bring the Supplementary Affidavit and swear or affirm before a Commissioner for Oaths. Once this is done, log in to Probate eService and submit the document. The court will process the document and if everything is in order, the Grant of Probate will be issued through Probate eService accordingly.

questions.title: My witnesses did not receive an SMS or email notification to witness my nomination. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can inform your witnesses to visit cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM to witness an online nomination. The SMS or email notification is not needed for witnesses to proceed with their declaration on cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM.
You and your witnesses can also refer to the video guide for more information on making an online CPF nomination.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if my platform is a subsidiary company with a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company?
questions.text: Yes, you are required to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN) if your platform is a subsidiary company with a different Unique Entity Number (UEN) from the parent company. To apply for a CSN, please refer to How do i obtain my CSN as a new platform operator?
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Applying for a CPF Submission Number

questions.title: How do I calculate CPF contributions on Additional Wages (AW) paid before the end of the year/last month of employment?
questions.text:
To determine the CPF contributions on Additional Wage (AW) payable, the AW ceiling has to be first calculated. The AW ceiling sets the maximum amount of AW on which CPF contributions are payable per year.
You should use current year's Ordinary Wages (OW) to estimate the AW ceiling whenever AW are payable for the current year.
Once the employee’s total OW for the year are known, usually at the end of the year or in the last month of employment, you should re-calculate the AW ceiling based on the total OW subject to CPF contributions. You can refer to these examples (PDF, 0.5MB) on the computation of the AW ceiling.
Any shortfall in the CPF contributions after the re-computation should be paid together with December's contributions or contributions for your employee's last month of employment, whichever is applicable. If you have overpaid the CPF contributions, you can apply for a refund by selecting 'Refund of contributions paid', followed by 'Single employee or platform worker' or 'Multiple employees or platform workers' as applicable.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions
Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I calculate the Additional Wage (AW) ceiling and the amount that attracts CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The Additional Wage (AW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of AW on which CPF contributions are payable per year. An employee's AW ceiling is computed on a per employee, per employer, per calendar year basis.
You can access the following resources to help you with the computation:
AW ceiling Calculator
Examples on the Computation of the AW ceiling (PDF, 0.5MB)
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I view the users authorised to transact on behalf of a Third Party Entity?
questions.text:
To view the users authorised to transact on behalf of your entity, follow these steps:
Log in to the Corppass Portal.
Navigate to Third Party > Manage Third Party Entities.
Select the Entity Name to view and manage the authorised e-Service(s) individually.
Go to the Third Party Users tab to see the users authorised to transact on behalf of your entity.

questions.title: Where can I find the list of e-services available in Corppass?
questions.text: You may find the list of digital services here.

questions.title: What is a UEN and who issues it?
questions.text:
UEN stands for Unique Entity Number, which is a standard identification number used by entities to interact with government agencies in Singapore. It uniquely identifies an entity, similar to how the NRIC is used for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
A UEN is issued by government agencies, known as UEN-issuance agencies, when an entity is officially registered. Some examples of these agencies include the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), Registry of Societies (ROS), and Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

questions.title: Why am I refunded half of the examination fees for the GCE-Level examination that I have withdrawn from?
questions.text: We seek your understanding that there are costs incurred for processing the withdrawal and refund applications for private candidates. Hence the full subject fees for the GCE-Level examinations will not be refunded.
topics: GCE N(T) / N(A) / O / A Level Examinations
GCE N(T) / N(A) / O / A Level Examinations / Private Candidates - Subject Amendment, Withdrawal

questions.title: Who can sit the PSLE?
questions.text: Students who are studying in government / government-aided / approved institutions in Singapore are eligible to sit the PSLE when they reach Primary 6 level.

questions.title: What does the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) do?
questions.text:
NCSS is the umbrella body for over 500-member social service agencies in Singapore. It's mission is to provide leadership and direction in enhancing the capabilities and capacity of our members, advocating for social service needs and strengthening strategic partnerships, for an effective social service ecosystem. Community Chest is the philanthropy and engagement arm of NCSS and Social Service Institute (SSI) is the sector capability and transformation arm of NCSS.
Find out more about NCSS.

questions.title: What should I do if my platform operator did not pay me the correct amount of earnings and CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The Platform Workers Act requires your platform operator to provide you with an itemised earnings slip, which will include any deductions from your earnings. You should verify the CPF paid as declared by your platform operator against the deductions shown in your earnings slip.
If there are any discrepancies or if you have any clarifications, please approach your platform operator immediately so that any errors can be rectified early while documentary evidence is fresh. Your platform operator is expected to self-rectify any errors immediately.
If you were not paid the right amount of earnings, you should approach your union if your platform operator is unionised or if you are a union member for advice. If you are not a union member, you could approach the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) for advice.
Once TADM has concluded assessing your claims and determined the earnings due to you, you can lodge a report with CPF Board. The Board will compute the CPF contributions payable.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How long does it take to process applications relating to GIRO matters?
questions.text:
Online applications to set up/reinstate/terminate GIRO for MediSave contributions submitted by the 15th of the month will take effect in the same month. Otherwise, the GIRO arrangement will take effect from the following month.
For example, if you submit an online application on 15 June to set up/reinstate a GIRO arrangement, your first GIRO deduction will take place on *25 June. If you submit the online application on 16 June, your first GIRO deduction will take place on *25 July.
Hardcopy applications to set up GIRO arrangement will require up to 21 working days to process. If processed by the 15th of the month, the first GIRO deduction will take place in the same month. Otherwise, the first GIRO deduction will take place from the following month.
If you had requested to terminate your GIRO arrangement via your bank, please inform us so that we can update your GIRO details accordingly.
*If the 25th is a Saturday, Sunday, or Public Holiday, the amount will be deducted on the next working day.

questions.title: Will I be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies if I earn more than $3,600?
questions.text:
The $3,600 figure refers to the household monthly income per person, which is based on the total income earned by a family staying in the same residential address, divided by the number of members of that family.
If the total income earned by family members is $14,000, and there are four members in the family, then the household monthly income per person is $3,500, and the family would qualify for subsidies.
Up to two-thirds of the population would qualify for Premium Subsidies. This is a fairer way of calculating the need for subsidies, because a family with more members may need more support, even if the total income they make is quite high. This is because the amount they can spend on each family member will be lower if there are more family members.
Families in a lower household income category will get a higher subsidy rate. In this way, we give more help to those who have less resources and need more help. This is part of being a compassionate and inclusive society.

questions.title: Can I still make payment for my outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums after the deadline stated in the Final Reminder notification?
questions.text:
We advise you to pay your outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums before the due date to avoid enforcement actions.
Please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Why does my Healthcare dashboard state that my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums may be recovered from my bankruptcy estate?
questions.text:
Outstanding MediShield Life/ CareShield Life premiums incurred prior to your bankruptcy date may be recovered from your bankruptcy estate. These premiums will therefore not be reflected as outstanding premiums payable in your Healthcare dashboard.
To pay your outstanding premiums incurred prior to the date of your Bankruptcy Order, please obtain approval from the Private Trustee or Official Assignee. You can contact them at 1800 225 5529 (during office hours) or visit www.mlaw.gov.sg.

questions.title: When will the changes to MediShield Life benefits / increased premiums take effect?
questions.text:
The changes to MediShield Life benefits will be implemented progressively from 1 April 2025.
Premiums will be adjusted from 1 April 2025 onwards upon policy renewal or inception. To cushion the premium increases, it will be phased in evenly over these three years. This will be effected through the Phased Support which is provided to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for two years. It is applied to the net premium increase between the new MediShield Life premium and the premium before 1 April 2025 (after any applicable Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies, or Merdeka Generation Subsidies).
The Government will also provide additional support measures, which include increase in premium subsidies, additional Medisave top-ups and expansion of Additional Premium Support. Please refer to the MediShield Life 2024 Review press release for more details.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming enhanced benefits and increased premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a national health insurance scheme that covers all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for life. As coverage is mandatory, the benefits and premiums apply to all policyholders and there is no opting out of this scheme.
With rising healthcare costs and changes in the healthcare landscape, MediShield Life benefits and premiums have to be reviewed periodically and updated to ensure the scheme remains sustainable and relevant to the needs of Singaporeans.
The Government will continue to ensure that premiums are kept affordable for all Singaporeans and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: What are the options for me if I am the 1 in 10 whose subsidised bill is not fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is designed to fully cover nine in ten subsidised bills, with the deductible and co-insurance covered by MediSave. This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Singaporeans can be assured that more people will see their subsidised bills fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave. For the minority of patients whose subsidised bills exceed the claim limit, they will still receive payouts from MediShield Life up to the relevant claim limit. Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund, or appeal to MOH for MediSave use beyond limits.

questions.title: Why is there an increase in the deductible?
questions.text:
The deductible sieves out smaller bills that can be paid via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic bills. This keeps premiums affordable for all policyholders. By avoiding first-dollar coverage, the deductible also encourages prudent use of healthcare.
The deductible has not been adjusted since 2015. With rising bill sizes, the deductible has become less effective over time in filtering out smaller bills. If the deductible is not increased, the scheme will pay out for many more smaller bills, and premiums will have to increase even more.
To help Singaporeans cope with the increase in deductible, MOH will increase MediSave limits such that those with sufficient MediSave will generally not see an increase in cash out of pocket.
For those with insufficient MediSave, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out of pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 Jan 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as long as you have sufficient MediSave.
For those with insufficient MediSave, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: What is the difference between the inpatient and outpatient deductible? Do I have to pay both the inpatient and outpatient deductible if I seek treatments in both settings?
questions.text:
The inpatient deductible is applicable for inpatient treatments, while the outpatient deductible will only apply for outpatient treatments.
The deductible paid for inpatient treatments in a policy year would also count towards the outpatient deductible and vice versa.
For example, if a patient has paid at least $500 towards their deductible in the inpatient setting in a policy year, they would have fulfilled the outpatient deductible for the same policy year.

questions.title: What happens to the deductible that I have paid for during my policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025?
questions.text:
The first phase of the increase in inpatient deductible, together with the refresh of existing MediShield Life claim limits, will take effect on 1 Apr 2025. These revised parameters will apply for all admissions on or after 1 Apr 2025.
Any deductible that you have paid for during your policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025 will be counted towards the new deductible. Assuming the same policy year, this means that if you have paid $1,500 in deductible before 1 Apr 2025, it would continue to count towards the new deductible that you have to pay for your admission on or after 1 Apr 2025.

questions.title: How did the Government decide which treatments, conditions, and care settings should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
Why is MediShield Life covering treatments such as CTGTPs and high-cost drugs that only benefit a small number of patients?
questions.text:
CTGTPs and high-cost drugs have significant potential to treat rare diseases and conditions. However, they can be expensive. Without any financing, Singaporeans will not be able to access these potentially effective treatments.
This is where MediShield Life and risk-pooling can play a useful role. Instead of having every individual save for a CTGTP, which only some may require, MediShield Life works by collecting smaller, annual premiums from individuals, and paying out when one requires high-cost, low-incidence treatments such as CTGTPs. To ensure the scheme remains affordable and sustainable, coverage will only be extended to treatments that are assessed by MOH to be clinically and cost-effective.

questions.title: How much will my premiums be once the premium changes take effect, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
You may refer to the premium & subsidy table here for the premium schedule for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
The extent of premium increases will vary across policyholders depending on age group. Information on your MediShield Life premium and applicable subsidies will be sent in writing to the payer of your premium about 1-2 months before your policy renewal date, by the Central Provident Fund Board or your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurer (if you are insured under an IP).
To help Singaporeans manage the premium increases, the Government will provide an additional $4.1 billion in premium support measures over the next three years. With this, more than nine in 10 Singaporeans will be able to more than offset their net increase in premiums for the next three years.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums are fully payable by MediSave. If there are insufficient monies in the MediSave account, policyholders can top up their account with cash or their family members with sufficient MediSave balance can step in to support their premium payments.
We understand that changes in one’s household circumstances may mean that one could require additional support for their healthcare expenditure including premiums. In such instances, individuals may call the MediShield Life hotline or visit the MediShield Life e-service website (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg).
Additional Premium Support (APS) is also available for those who face difficulty paying for premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. The Government will invite individuals with insufficient MediSave balances to apply for APS and help them with the process if they are unable to do so themselves. There is no need for individuals to apply for APS ahead of time.
If approved, APS will cover any outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums for the next two years.
Eligibility for APS is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his/her immediate family members’ financial means. Flexibility will be exercised for individuals who may not completely meet the criteria but need help because of extenuating circumstances.
No one will lose coverage from MediShield Life because of an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How is the proposed premium discount scheme similar to or different from a no-claims discount?
questions.text:
The idea of introducing incentives to encourage healthier behaviours has been considered in past reviews of MediShield Life. With the launch of Healthier SG and the growing emphasis on preventive health, it is now opportune to introduce premium discounts for MediShield Life policyholders to complement these national efforts.
For a start, we have tied the premium discount to health-seeking behaviours such as exercise. In particular, MediShield Life policyholders will be able to redeem premium discounts from Healthpoints earned from activities on the Healthy 365 app or completion of first Health Plan consult under Healthier SG.
This is different from “no-claims discounts” that some insurers offer to their policyholders, which provide discounts to those who do not make claims in the previous policy year. This approach was not adopted to avoid penalising Singaporeans, especially the elderly, for making claims for healthcare episodes that they may inevitably face throughout their lives. It could also discourage Singaporeans from seeking appropriate care, for fear of losing their discounts.

questions.title: How can I participate in the programme and earn premium discount?
questions.text:
A person, who on average, does 30 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) almost daily, could earn a total of 6,000 Healthpoints in a year if he clocks these activities on his Healthy 365 app. He can then redeem these Healthpoints for $80 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
For residents aged 40 and above who enrol in Healthier SG and complete their first Health Plan consultation, they would be able to redeem $40 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
Please refer to the HPB rewards programme FAQs for more information on Healthpoints.

questions.title: Will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text: Whether your IP benefits will be affected will depend on your insurer, as the IP benefits are set, reviewed and adjusted by insurers based on their own commercial and actuarial considerations.

questions.title: How will my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premium be affected by the MediShield Life review?
questions.text:
Your IP premium is made up of two components – the MediShield Life premium and the premium for the additional private insurance component.
Your MediShield Life premium component will increase.
Revisions to the private insurance component of your IP premium will depend on your insurer, who may make changes based on their own actuarial and commercial considerations, and after accounting for any changes in their product features, if any.

questions.title: How can I update my contact details to receive notification on my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.text: To receive notification via SMS or email on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment, you may update your mobile number via my cpf digital services - Account Settings with your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: I am under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, what happens to my CPF savings when I turn 55?
questions.text:
When you turn 55, if you have savings in your Special Account (SA), it will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) up to your Reduced Retirement Sum (RRS) and your SA will be closed.
Once you have set aside your RRS in RA, any remaining SA savings will be transferred to your Ordinary Account and can be withdrawn at any time.

questions.title: When will the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) be expanded to cover more members with certain pre-existing health conditions to obtain HPS coverage at a higher premium rate (i.e. with premium loading)?
questions.text: From 26 May 2025, the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) expands to cover members with certain pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe, such as certain types of stroke and heart disorder, who are currently not offered coverage. CPF Board will assess each application and offer eligible members an HPS cover with premium loading.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are some examples of pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe, which may now be eligible for Home Protection Scheme coverage, subject to premium loading?
questions.text:
Examples of pre-existing health conditions that may now be considered for coverage with premium loading include certain types of stroke and heart disorder.
A member’s eligibility for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will still be assessed based on overall severity, prognosis, control of the health condition, and the member’s health risk profile.
However, members with more severe health conditions, such as those currently receiving treatment for cancer and kidney failure are not eligible for HPS coverage, even with premium loading.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my health condition is such that I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, is it compulsory to take up this cover?
questions.text: Members who are offered Home Protection Scheme (HPS) covers with premium loading can decide whether or not to take up the HPS cover. Participation in this scheme will be on an opt-in basis for them.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If I am offered a Home Protection Scheme cover with premium loading, what will be my premium payable?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums are calculated based on several factors:
Outstanding housing loan on the flat
Loan repayment period
Type of loan (HDB concessionary or market rate)
Age and gender
Percentage share of cover of the outstanding housing loan
The amount of premium loading depends on the seriousness of your pre-existing health condition. If you are offered cover with premium loading, the Board will inform you of the total premium amount payable and you may decide whether to take it up.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will I continue to be covered under the same premium rates for my existing Home Protection Scheme cover if I have developed new health condition(s) after my cover has been issued to me?
questions.text: If you have developed new health condition(s) after your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover has been issued, you will continue to be covered at the same premium rate under your existing HPS cover.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Why is MediShield Life covering treatments such as Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs) and high-cost drugs which might only benefit a small number of patients?
questions.text:
Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs) and high-cost drugs have significant potential to treat rare diseases and conditions. However, they can be expensive. Without any financing, Singaporeans will not be able to access these potentially life-saving treatments.
MediShield Life and risk-pooling essentially make healthcare more accessible for everyone. Rather than having each person save individually for costly treatments like CTGTPs that only a few may need, MediShield Life collects smaller, annual premiums from all. This approach allows the scheme to provide financial support for high-cost, low-incidence treatments when they are needed.
To keep the scheme affordable and sustainable, coverage will focus on treatments that the Ministry of Health (MOH) has assessed to be clinically effective and cost-efficient. This ensures that everyone benefits from shared resources, reducing the financial burden on individuals while maintaining quality care for those who truly need it.

questions.title: How did the Government decide what should be covered under MediShield Life in this review?
questions.text:
In MediShield Life Council’s review, there were a few considerations:
First, MediShield Life was created as a national health insurance scheme to fully cover majority of the subsidised bills in public hospitals. Patients use their MediSave savings to pay the deductible and co-insurance. However, as medical bills have increased over the years, this coverage has dropped.
Second, the Government recognises that healthcare is now being provided outside of hospitals — like in outpatient, community, and home settings — areas that MediShield Life mostly doesn’t cover.
Lastly, new medical technologies have introduced life-saving treatments, like Cell, Tissue, and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTPs), which are also not covered by MediShield Life.
The recommended approach balances enhancing affordability for patients while keeping premiums manageable for everyone.

questions.title: What happens to the deductible that I have paid during my policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025?
questions.text:
The first phase of the increase in inpatient deductible, together with the refresh of existing MediShield Life claim limits, will take effect on 1 Apr 2025. These revised parameters will apply for all admissions on or after 1 Apr 2025.
Any deductible that you have paid during your policy year prior to 1 Apr 2025 will be counted towards the new deductible.
Assuming the same policy year, this means that if you have paid $1,500 in deductible before 1 Apr 2025, it would continue to count towards the new deductible that you have to pay for your admission on or after 1 Apr 2025.

questions.title: What is the difference between the inpatient and outpatient deductible? Do I have to pay both deductibles if I seek treatments in both settings?
questions.text:
The inpatient deductible applies to inpatient treatments, and the outpatient deductible applies to outpatient treatments.
Please note that the deductible paid for inpatient treatments in a policy year will also count towards the outpatient deductible, and vice versa.
For example, if a patient has paid at least $500 towards their deductible in the inpatient setting in a policy year, they would have fulfilled the outpatient deductible for the same policy year.

questions.title: What are the options for me if my subsidised bill is not fully covered by MediShield Life and MediSave?
questions.text:
For the minority of patients whose subsidised bills exceed the claim limit, they will still receive payouts from MediShield Life up to the relevant claim limit.
Examples of the claim limits that will be increased:
Intensive Care Unit ward from $2,200 to $5,140
Policy year claim limit from $150,000 to $200,000
Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund by approaching the Medical Social Workers at the MediFund-approved institution at which the treatment is received, or appeal to MOH at 1800 222 3399 or write to them at moh_qsm@moh.gov.sg for MediSave use beyond limits.

questions.title: Why is there a need for an increase in the deductible?
questions.text:
Although healthcare costs have increased, the deductible hasn’t changed since 2015. An increase in the deductible helps to keep premiums affordable for all policyholders.
The deductible sieves out smaller bills that can be paid via MediSave, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic bills. By not covering small healthcare costs right away (first-dollar coverage), the deductible encourages the prudent use of healthcare services.
To help Singaporeans cope with the increase in deductible, the Ministry of Health will increase MediSave limits such that those with sufficient MediSave will generally not see an increase in cash out-of-pocket.
For those with insufficient MediSave savings, the Government will provide additional support such as MediSave top-ups. There is also MediFund, an endowment fund set up by the Government to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave.

questions.title: Which vaccines are approved for use in Singapore? Which of these vaccines are included in the National Vaccination Programme (NVP)?
questions.text:
Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty, Moderna/Spikevax and Novavax/Nuvaxovid* are vaccines that are authorised by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) for use in Singapore.
* Current stock of JN.1 Novavax/Nuvaxovid vaccine has expired since 31 May 2026 and no longer available under the NVP.
Under the NVP, vaccines authorised by the HSA for use in Singapore are free for all eligible Singaporean Citizens, Permanent Residents, Long Term Pass holders and certain Short Term Pass holders.

questions.title: How do mRNA vaccines work?
questions.text:
The COVID-19 mRNA vaccine consists of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) that carry instructions to make the spike protein of the virus. The mRNA used in the vaccine is synthesised and not extracted from actual viruses.
After being given by intramuscular injection, the vaccine mRNA is taken up by cells which then produce the spike protein. This stimulates the production of a good antibody and cellular immune response to the spike protein that protects the vaccinated person because the spike protein is an important part of the SARS CoV-2 virus.
The spike proteins are however incapable of forming SARS CoV-2 viruses or causing COVID-19 infection. The vaccine mRNA only persists for two days before it is naturally broken down by the body. It does not enter the nucleus of cells and hence cannot interfere with the DNA of the vaccine recipient.

questions.title: Are mRNA vaccines a form of genetic modification?
questions.text:
No, they are not a form of genetic modification. The mRNA vaccine is in a form that is cannot be converted back to DNA. Since our human genome is made up of DNA, there is no possibility that the COVID-19 mRNA will interfere with or modify human DNA. The mRNA is completely degraded within 48 hours of introduction to the human body.
The spike protein generated through the introduction of the COVID-19 mRNA is recognised by the body’s immune system to develop an immune response (e.g. generation of antibodies), similar to what happens in a natural infection against COVID-19.

questions.title: Are the COVID-19 vaccines halal?
questions.text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS)’s position is that COVID-19 vaccines are permissible for Muslim use. Please refer to MUIS’ religious position on the COVID-19 vaccine by using this link.

questions.title: What are the differences between the updated vaccines (e.g. updated Moderna/Spikevax or Pfizer BioNTech/Comirnaty) and the previous vaccines?
questions.text: The updated COVID-19 vaccines target newer strains of virus compared to the older versions of vaccines, can provide a stronger immune response against emerging strains, and therefore may confer better protection against COVID-19. The safety profiles of the updated vaccines are comparable to that of previous versions.

questions.title: What is myocarditis and pericarditis? Can the vaccine lead to myocarditis and pericarditis?
questions.text:
Myocarditis and pericarditis are inflammatory conditions affecting the heart muscles and the outer lining of the heart, respectively. Patients may present with symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath or abnormal heartbeats. Local incidence rates remain low and the cases are usually mild and recover well. This rare risk is predominantly observed in men aged 12-29 years and largely occurs within the first week after vaccination.
Male vaccinees aged 12-29 years who are receiving any dose of Moderna/Spikevax or Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccines are advised to refrain from participating in strenuous physical activities for one week after vaccination. During this period, vaccinees should promptly seek medical attention if they experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or abnormal heartbeats.

questions.title: Is COVID-19 vaccination safe for those with chronic illness such as hypertension, high cholesterol and diabetes?
questions.text: Persons with chronic illnesses are recommended to receive the vaccine for personal protection. The participants of Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty’s and Moderna/Spikevax's clinical trials and other studies included persons with medical comorbidities, who were at risk of serious, life-threatening disease and death from COVID-19 infection, and demonstrated effectiveness with no safety concerns reported in this group.

questions.title: Will the COVID-19 vaccine cause infertility?
questions.text: There is currently no evidence that the COVID-19 vaccines can cause infertility in vaccine recipients.

questions.title: What are the side effects of COVID-19 vaccination? What should I do if I suffer from any side effects?
questions.text:
The vaccine has been assessed to be safe for use. However, you may experience common side effects, similar to other vaccines. Most side effects are mild or moderate, and usually get better within a few days. The table below lists some common side effects that have been reported with this vaccine, and how to manage them.
Side Effects
How to Manage
Pain, redness, swelling at the injection site
Those with fever are advised to self-isolate at home until the fever subsides.
Paracetamol 1 to 2 tablets for the other side effects every 6 hours for adults or dosed accordingly to the child's weight as needed.
Fever, chills
Headache, muscle pain, joint pain
Tiredness
Rest
Lymph node swelling at neck or arms
Usually gets better by itself in a week or so
See a doctor if:
The side effects persist or get worse
The fever persists for more than 48 hours (2 days)
Respiratory symptoms such as cough, runny nose, sore throat, shortness of breath or loss of sense of taste and smell develop
Heart or chest symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath or abnormal heart beats develop.
In very rare cases, this vaccine can cause a severe allergic reaction. Signs of a severe allergic reaction include difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, throat, eyes or lips, a fast heartbeat, dizziness and weakness, a bad rash all over your body. If you experience a severe allergic reaction, seek medical attention immediately. Call 995 or go to the nearest A&E immediately.

questions.title: What happens if I develop an allergic reaction to my first dose?
questions.text:
You should seek medical attention, if you experience a possible allergic reaction to the vaccine (e.g. eye or lip swelling, hives, generalised skin rashes, breathlessness). Fever, chills, muscle pain, headaches, injection site pain are not allergic reactions.
You should discuss your suitability for subsequent COVID-19 vaccinations with your doctor. Persons with an allergic reaction assessed to be caused by the vaccine and who are advised by a doctor that they should not take subsequent doses of the vaccine, should adhere to the advice of the doctor.

questions.title: How effective is the vaccine?
questions.text: Vaccinated persons can be infected. However, vaccination offers good protection from severe disease and hospitalisation.

questions.title: Can the vaccines protect me against all strains of COVID-19?
questions.text: The updated COVID-19 vaccines can provide better protection against current and emerging strains compared to previous versions of the vaccines.

questions.title: I have recovered from COVID-19. How soon can I receive my next vaccination dose?
questions.text: Recently recovered persons being vaccinated should receive a vaccine dose at the recommended interval after any previous dose(s), and at least 28 days after the infection although an interval of three months from the infection is recommended for better effectiveness.

questions.title: Do all vaccine doses need to be of the same brand?
questions.text:
For those who are taking more than one initial dose of the vaccine*, the initial doses should be of the same brand. Additional doses of the COVID-19 vaccine can be of different brands, where applicable.
From time to time, the composition of a COVID-19 vaccine may be updated to target more recent virus variants. If you are due for a vaccine dose, you are recommended to receive the updated version of the vaccine. There is no need for your vaccine doses to be of the same composition.
*Persons who should take more than one initial dose include:
Immunocompromised persons (three initial vaccine doses)
Children aged 6 months to 4 years (two initial doses)

questions.title: Can I receive other non-COVID-19 vaccines at the same time as the COVID-19 vaccine? How long do I have to wait before getting other vaccines?
questions.text: The vaccines can be administered together with other non-COVID-19 vaccines across all ages.

questions.title: I have received one or more additional dose(s) as recommended previously. Do I still need to receive another additional dose in 2025/2026?
questions.text:
Regardless of the number and composition of previous additional doses received, an additional dose of the updated vaccine around 1 year (and no earlier than 5 months) after the last dose received is:
(a) Recommended for individuals aged 60 years and above, medically vulnerable individuals aged 6 months and above, and residents of aged care facilities;
(b) Encouraged for healthcare workers and persons living or working with medically vulnerable individuals.
Other individuals aged 6 months and above who wish to receive the COVID-19 vaccine can continue to do so. Individuals may consider consulting their doctor to understand more about the benefits of the vaccine for their specific situation.

questions.title: Who should not get the mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines?
questions.text:
The mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines, Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty and Moderna/Spikevax, are currently not available for children under the age of 6 months.
Persons with a history of anaphylaxis to mRNA COVID-19 vaccine or its components SHOULD NOT receive the mRNA-based vaccine again. Anaphylaxis is a severe life-threatening reaction with two or more of the following three criteria:
a) Hives or face/eyelid/lip/throat swelling;
b) Difficulty breathing;
c) Dizziness.
Patients with the following high-risk allergic reactions to a previous dose of mRNA COVID-19 vaccine or its components SHOULD NOT be administered the vaccine:
a) Hives or face/eyelid/lip/throat swelling with onset within 4 hours post-vaccination
b) Painful swelling of the inner surfaces of the mouth and/or large blisters spontaneously occurring at any time after vaccination.
Persons with a history of allergic reactions (including anaphylaxis) to other vaccines CAN receive the mRNA-based vaccine, unless they have a confirmed allergy specific to PEG (which is a component of the mRNA vaccine).
Persons who were diagnosed with myocarditis/pericarditis after a dose of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines SHOULD NOT receive the mRNA vaccines again.

questions.title: Can individuals with a history of allergies or anaphylaxis to other medications, drugs, food, insect stings, or unknown triggers (idiopathic) take COVID-19 vaccine?
questions.text:
Individuals with a history of anaphylaxis to other medications, drugs, food, insect stings, or unknown triggers (idiopathic) CAN be vaccinated.
There is no evidence to suggest that individuals with a history of anaphylaxis to non-vaccine related triggers are at higher risk of anaphylaxis to the COVID-19 vaccines.

questions.title: Are the vaccines safe for pregnant or breastfeeding women?
questions.text:
Pregnant or breastfeeding women can receive the COVID-19 vaccines.
Internationally, a large number of pregnant and breastfeeding women have received a COVID-19 vaccination. There have been studies done to monitor women who were vaccinated when they were pregnant, and their babies. These studies were done on women at different trimesters of pregnancy and there is no evidence to suggest that the COVID-19 vaccines may cause harm to pregnant women or their babies.
Both Pfizer-BioNTech/Comirnaty and Moderna/Spikevax COVID-19 vaccines are mRNA vaccines. As mRNA vaccines are not live vaccines, they are biologically unlikely to adversely affect breastfed babies. In addition, the breast milk of vaccinated mothers may help to protect their babies from COVID-19 due to antibodies in breast milk. There have also been no vaccine-related side effects reported in the babies who were breastfed by mothers who received the vaccine while breastfeeding.

questions.title: Medically vulnerable persons are recommended for COVID-19 vaccination in 2025/2026. Who are considered medically vulnerable persons?
questions.text:
Medically vulnerable persons are individuals who are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 due to significant medical risk factors. These include persons with chronic diseases of the heart, lungs, kidneys, liver and other organ systems.
A list of specific health conditions that will classify one as medically vulnerable can be found by using this link. If you are unsure, you should consult your doctor.

questions.title: Who are immunocompromised persons? What vaccine doses should they receive?
questions.text:
Immunocompromised persons have significantly impaired immune system which include persons with the following conditions:
a) Transplant patients on medications that suppress the immune system, including solid organ and allogenic stem cell transplants
b) Cancer patients on active treatment with chemotherapy or on other therapies that suppress the immune system
c) Haematological cancers
d) Treatments for non-cancer conditions that suppress the immune system
e) End-stage kidney disease
f) Advanced or untreated HIV
Persons with the above conditions are recommended to receive the COVID-19 vaccine.
Immunocompromised persons who are unvaccinated should receive three initial doses of an mRNA vaccine. This comprises a second dose eight weeks after the first dose; and a third dose two months after the second dose as part of an enhanced three-dose primary series.
Immunocompromised persons who are vaccinated should, in 2025/2026, receive an additional dose of the updated vaccine at an interval of around one year (and at least five months) from their last dose. Immunocompromised persons can be considered to receive the additional dose of COVID-19 vaccine from 5 months after their last dose in consultation with their treating physician for better protection.

questions.title: Are there any children who should not get vaccinated?
questions.text:
There is no category of children or teens who absolutely should not get the vaccine, unless they have a known allergy to other vaccines or one of the vaccine’s components.
People with weakened immune systems, either from illness or medication, may still receive the vaccine because it is not a live vaccine i.e. a vaccine that uses a weakened form of a germ to prompt an immune response.
If your child has any medical condition that is not stable or is getting worse, he or she should postpone the vaccination until the medical condition is better controlled.
Parents are always encouraged to speak with their teen’s or child’s doctor/paediatrician if they have any questions or concerns.
topics: Covid-19 / Vaccine recommendations specific for children

questions.title: Could my child/ward use different types of vaccine?
questions.text:
For children aged 6 months to 4 years, the two initial doses of vaccines should be from the same brand. They should not use different vaccine brands for these doses.
After completing the two initial doses described above, they may then receive an additional dose of the updated vaccine at an interval of around 1 year (minimally 5 months) after their last dose based on prevailing recommendations.

questions.title: If my child/ward was recently infected with COVID-19, when should he/she take the vaccine?
questions.text: Recently recovered persons being vaccinated should receive a vaccine dose at the recommended interval after any previous dose(s), and at least 28 days after the infection although an interval of three months from the infection is recommended for better effectiveness.
topics: Covid-19 / Vaccine recommendations specific for children

questions.title: Who is eligible to receive fully-subsidised COVID-19 vaccinations under the National Vaccination Programme?
questions.text:
The following groups of residents and pass holders are eligible to receive fully-subsidised COVID-19 vaccinations under the National Vaccination Programme:
• Singapore Citizen
• Permanent Resident
• Employment Pass
• S-Pass
• Work Permit holders (including Confinement Nannies)
• Student’s Pass
• Dependant’s Pass
• MFA-issued IDs
• Long Term Visit Pass (and LTVP+)
• Training Employment Pass
• Training Work Permit
• Work Holiday Pass
• Special Pass
• Short-Term Visit Pass with a validity period of at least 60 days

The pass holder should bring along identification documents such as a passport or approval of extension of stay in Singapore for verification purposes.

questions.title: When can I receive my vaccine dose?
questions.text:
Unvaccinated individuals who are receiving COVID-19 vaccination in 2025/2026 should receive:
a. Ages 6 months to 4 years: Two vaccine doses, eight weeks apart; and
b. Ages 5 years and older: One vaccine dose.
Vaccinated individuals aged 6 months and above who are receiving an additional dose of COVID-19 vaccination in 2025/2026, should receive it at an interval of around one year (and at least five months) from the last vaccine dose.

questions.title: How can my child/ward receive his/her vaccine doses?

The nearest vaccination site and the types of vaccines offered at each site are listed at https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/vaccine.

questions.title: I would like to donate my Pioneer Generation - MediSave Top-Ups. How can I do so?
questions.text:
Thank you for your kind spirit of generosity. We are glad that you are considering donating. However, we regret that you cannot donate your MediSave top-ups because they are meant for your healthcare needs.
Instead, we encourage you to donate an equivalent cash sum (if you wish) to those in need. You may do so via online fundraising platforms such as Giving.sg (by the National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre) or to Community Chest (by the National Council of Social Service).

questions.title: I would like to appeal for the Pioneer Generation Package. can I do so, and how?
questions.text:
The Appeals Panel was set up in May 2014 and has carefully considered the criteria for assessing appeals.
If you were born after 31 Dec 1949, please note that no appeals will be received. As explained in response to queries in Parliament and during the debate on the Pioneer Generation Fund Bill, the Appeals Panel recognised that the Government had already adopted a more inclusive approach by extending the Pioneer Generation Package to all those born in 1949 or earlier. Whatever the age set, there will always be those who marginally fall short of it. It would therefore not be feasible or fair to allow age-related appeals without extending the new age criterion to all Singaporeans. Hence, as provided under the Pioneer Generation Fund Act, the Panel decided that it would only consider appeals relating to the citizenship criterion.
For citizenship-related appeals, the Panel considers whether the person had obtained Singapore citizenship shortly after 1986 – the year set as the citizenship cut-off date for eligibility of the Pioneer Generation Package. In addition, it looks at factors such as whether he or she had been in Singapore since the early years of independence, contributed to our society, and had demonstrated clear efforts to sink roots in Singapore.
If you marginally missed the citizenship date of 31 Dec 1986 and you feel that you meet the criteria, please contact us at 1800-2222-888 or contactus@pioneers.gov.sg with your NRIC number to file an appeal. If you would like to appeal on behalf of a relative, please obtain your relative's consent first.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation Member and have an Integrated Shield Plan, will I benefit from the MediShield Life subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes.
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), are made up of (i) MediShield Life and (ii) an enhanced portion providing better benefits and/or higher coverage (in private or Class A/B1 wards in public hospitals). For those with IPs, the special Pioneer Generation MediShield Life subsidies will apply to the MediShield Life component of their IP premium.

questions.title: I lost my Merdeka Generation card/welcome folder is damaged. How do I apply for a replacement?
questions.text: Please call 1800-650-6060 for assistance.

questions.title: Why is the Merdeka Generation Package only extended to those born in the 1950s?
questions.text:
Compared to younger cohorts, the MG had fewer opportunities and lower wages, and they were less able to save up for their healthcare needs. The MGP provides additional support to this group, who are reaching their retirement years.
Younger cohorts of Singaporeans would have benefitted more from the schemes introduced over the years (e.g. MediSave in 1984), and are in a better position to look after their own healthcare needs. At the same time, we recognise that some will still need more help. The Government continues to provide substantial support through permanent healthcare schemes, to ensure that healthcare remains affordable for all.

questions.title: I would like to appeal for the Merdeka Generation Package. Can I do so, and how?
questions.text:
Citizens aged 60 years and above in 2019 (i.e. born on or earlier than 1959) who became Singapore citizens after 31 December 1996, but have good claims to be counted among the MG, can appeal for the MGP.
Similar to the Pioneer Generation Package, the Appeals Panel will not consider appeals from those who miss out on the age criterion (i.e. born after 31 December 1959 in this case).
You can send your appeals to contactus@merdeka.gov.sg or call 1800 2222 888. You can also mail to Robinson Road P.O. Box 3060 Singapore 905060.

questions.title: I am a MG Senior and have an integrated shield plan, will I benefit from the MediShield Life subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes. Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of (i) a MediShield Life component managed by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and (ii) additional private insurance coverage managed by a private insurer. The IP premium comprises the MediShield Life premium and the premium for the additional private insurance coverage.
All MG seniors will benefit from the additional MG premium subsidies – for those with IPs, this will apply to the MediShield Life portion of their IP premium.
