questions.title: What is the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS)?
questions.text:
The National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) provides guidance on vaccinations that persons aged 18 years and older should receive to protect themselves against vaccine-preventable diseases.
Certain adult groups are more susceptible to, or at risk of, acquiring vaccine preventable diseases if they have not previously received the vaccination and are in contact with individuals who have the infection.
Vaccines recommended under the NAIS helps reduce risk of infections among susceptible individuals and related complications, morbidity and mortality.

questions.title: What is the National Childhood Immunisation Schedule (NCIS)?
questions.text:
The National Childhood Immunisation Schedule (NCIS) comprises childhood vaccinations recommended as the standard of care for protection against common vaccine preventable diseases that are of significant healthcare burden to Singapore.
Under the Infectious Diseases Act, it is compulsory for parents and guardians to have their child vaccinated against diphtheria and measles.
In consultation with the Expert Committee on Immunisation, MOH regularly reviews the vaccination policies and vaccines listed on the schedule, taking into consideration local disease burden, vaccine safety, clinical efficacy and cost effectiveness of the vaccines. This ensures that the national recommendations for vaccinations are up to date.

questions.title: What is the overall strategy to support Singapore’s ageing population?
questions.text:
The United Nations defines a country as ‘ageing’ if the share of its population aged 65 and above crosses 7%. It is considered ‘aged’ if the share exceeds 14%. Once the share reaches 21%, it is ‘super aged’. Singapore will be ‘super aged’ by 2026. By 2030, 1 in 4 citizens will be aged 65 and above.
To support Singapore’s ageing population, we announced Age Well SG at the National Day Rally in 2023. Age Well SG is a national programme led by the Ministry of Health, Ministry of National Development and Ministry of Transport to support seniors to age well in their homes and their communities. It aims to support our seniors to age actively, stay socially connected, and be cared for within their communities.
Age Well SG offers a comprehensive nationwide transformation across the areas of transport, housing, active ageing, and care services to anchor ageing in the community. The programme aims to:
a. Improve the physical living environment;
b. Encourage active ageing; and
c. Strengthen support for seniors with care needs in the community.
To support these changes, the Government will dedicate at least $3.5b from FY2024 to FY2035 to support the implementation of Age Well SG.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How does MOH keep seniors active and engaged? What are some key measures?
questions.text:
In tandem with Healthier SG, MOH adopts a tailored approach to support seniors to age actively and healthily.
A key strategy is to offer a wide range of Active Ageing Programmes (AAPs) to help seniors maintain their physical, mental, and social health. We launched the ‘Live Well, Age Well’ initiative in 2020 to offer a wide range of free and exciting activities for adults aged 50 and above. The AAPs are currently offered island-wide, in accessible community locations like Active Ageing Centres (AACs). We aim to reach over 550,000 participants from 2023 to 2027.
Another key strategy is to expand the reach and offerings of Active Ageing Centres (AAC) to promote healthy ageing among seniors living nearby in the community. An AAC is a drop-in social recreational centre for seniors aged 60 and above to: (a) build strong social connections (b) take part in recreational activities, and (c) contribute to the community. MOH is investing around $800 million from FY2024 to FY2028 to better resource AACs and benefit more seniors.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What Is HIV And How Is It Connected To AIDS?
questions.text: HIV is a virus that causes a currently incurable infection that attacks the immune system, making it harder for the body to fight infection. Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS refers to advanced HIV infection. Left untreated, AIDS is fatal.

questions.title: What To Do If You Think You Have HIV
questions.text:
Seek and adhere to medical treatment including anti-retroviral therapy, and monitor your HIV viral load closely with your doctor. With effective treatment, the HIV virus can be suppressed to undetectable levels. This benefits your health and also reduces the risk of HIV transmission.
Under the Infectious Disease Act, unless you have maintained a stable undetectable HIV viral load (see below), you must inform your sexual partner of the risks of getting HIV from you before having sex. This is to allow your partner to choose to take appropriate precautions.
You are considered to have maintained a stable undetectable HIV viral load if you satisfy the following criteria:
You have stable, consecutive undetectable HIV viral load test results (below 200 copies per millilitre of blood), for at least six months;
Your most recent HIV viral load test shows a result of undetectable (below 200 copies per millilitre of blood), and is dated nine months or less before when you have sex;
You have adhered to medical treatment for HIV infection up to the time of when you have sex; and
All the HIV viral load test results mentioned above are from a licenced laboratory in Singapore.
If you satisfy the above criteria, you do not pose a risk of transmission of HIV to your sexual partner. Therefore, you no longer need to inform your sexual partner of the risks of getting HIV from you.

questions.title: How Long Will It Be Between Infection And The Onset Of Symptoms?
questions.text: Not everyone will have symptoms after being infected with HIV. Flu-like symptoms, including fever, skin rash and tiredness, may appear between 2-4 weeks after infection. If you are concerned about your HIV status, the only way to know for sure is to go for a HIV screening.

questions.title: Do I Need To Tell My Sexual Partner That I Have HIV?
questions.text:
Yes, unless you have maintained a stable undetectable HIV viral load (see below), you must inform your sexual partner of the risks of getting HIV from you before having sex (when informing your partner of the risks, you cannot avoid telling your partner that you have HIV). This is to allow your partner to choose to take appropriate precautions.
It is an offence not to do so, under the Infectious Diseases Act.
You are considered to have maintained a stable undetectable HIV viral load if you satisfy the following criteria:
You have stable consecutive undetectable HIV viral load test results (below 200 copies per millilitre of blood), for at least six months;
Your most recent HIV viral load test shows a result of undetectable (below 200 copies per millilitre of blood), and is nine months or less before when you have sex;
You have adhered to medical treatment for HIV infection up to the time of when you have sex; and
All the HIV viral load test results mentioned above are from a licenced laboratory in Singapore.
If you satisfy the above criteria, you do not pose a risk of transmission of HIV to your sexual partner. Therefore, you no longer need to inform your sexual partner of the risks of getting HIV from you.

questions.title: How Do I Show That I Have Adhered To Medical Treatment For HIV Infection?
questions.text:
You should go for regular follow-up visits for HIV with your doctor, including regular HIV viral load testing, and prescription refills. Medical records documenting that you have done so, serve as evidence that you have adhered to medical treatment.
If you are alleged to have committed an offence, the strongest evidence that you have adhered to medical treatment is an undetectable HIV viral load test result (from a licenced laboratory in Singapore) at the next medical visit for HIV after the sexual activity in question (which should not be more than 9 months after the sexual activity in question). This is because maintenance of undetectable HIV viral load is not possible unless you have adhered to treatment.

questions.text: HIV screening is available at Department of Sexually Transmitted Infections Control Clinic (registration is required) or at any private/poly clinic.

questions.text: Anonymous screening is available at several private clinics in Singapore.

questions.text: Only Clinics Offering HIV Rapid Test Kits 2013 onwards on rapid HIV screening can offer this service. Please contact your preferred clinic in advance to check.

questions.text: For more information on sexually transmitted infections, visit the Department of Sexually Transmitted Infections Control Clinic website

questions.title: How Much Does It Cost To Make An AMD?
questions.text: To make an AMD, you will have to consult a doctor who, as a witness, is required to explain the AMD to you. You may have to pay the doctor for the services rendered.

questions.title: Who can be a witness?
Must both witnesses be present during the making of an AMD?
questions.text: Yes, both witnesses must be present together to witness the person signing the AMD, as well as to sign the AMD form. As the first witness is your doctor, the second witness may be his nurse or any other suitable person.

questions.title: What If My Family Objects?
questions.text: If you have made an AMD regardless of objections from members of your family, the doctors will have to respect your AMD. We encourage you to discuss it with your family members and loved ones. This will help them to understand and respect your wishes should you become terminally ill.

questions.title: How does the Hospital Know I Have Made An AMD?
questions.text: Hospital staff, including doctors and nurses, do not know who has made an AMD as it is confidential and they are NOT allowed to ask you if you have made an AMD. However, if your attending doctor has reasons to believe that you are terminally ill and unable to make your wishes known to him, he can check with the Registrar of Advance Medical Directives on whether you have made an AMD.

questions.title: When Will An AMD Be Enforced?
questions.text:
The AMD will only come into force once you have been determined to have a terminal illness and a Certificate of Terminal illness has been issued.
Three doctors, including the patient’s hospital doctor, must unanimously certify a patient’s terminal illness. Two of the doctors must be specialists.
If the first panel of three doctors cannot agree unanimously that the patient is terminally ill, the doctor-in-charge will review his diagnosis. If he is still of the opinion that the patient is terminally ill, the matter will be referred to a second panel of three specialists, to be appointed by the Ministry of Health.
If the second panel of doctors also cannot agree unanimously that the patient is terminally ill, the AMD CANNOT take effect. The patient’s life will continue to be sustained and he will receive medical treatment as normal.

questions.title: What If I Change My Mind And Want To Revoke The AMD Made?
questions.text:
An AMD can be revoked at any time in the presence of at least one witness. You should do so by completing AMD Form 3, which is the standard form for revocation of an AMD. (Those who have made an AMD will receive Form 3 together with Form 2, which confirms that their AMD has been registered by the Registry of AMDs).
Alternatively, you or your witness could write a simple letter to the Registrar of AMDs. The letter should contain the following information:
The name and NRIC of both the person revoking the AMD and the witness, along with their addresses and home and office telephone numbers.
Time, date and place where the revocation was made.
If the letter is written by the witness, the method of communication which the person used to communicate his intention to revoke the AMD (e.g. orally, sign language, etc.)
Revocations should be sent to the Registry of AMDs as soon as possible.

questions.title: What If I’m Unable To Write?
questions.text: In this case, the AMD can be revoked orally or in any other way in which you can communicate. It is then the responsibility of the witness to the revocation to submit the notice of revocation using Form 3 or the letter as described above. The witness should also state the reason why the person revoking the AMD could not do so himself.

questions.title: If I am referred to the Emergency Department (ED) / Urgent Care Center (UCC) under the GPFirst programme, will the fee at the ED/UCC cover all investigations and tests?
questions.text:
The attendance fee at the ED/UCC currently covers:
Consultation
General X-ray services. E.g. Chest and abdomen x-rays
Standard Blood Investigations
Standard Medications
Specialised investigations and non-standard medications required are not included and will be charged separately. This also applies to patients who go directly to the ED/UCC of participating hospitals.
Please note that there may be other services and procedures not mentioned above that are not included in the attendance fee. For more information, please enquire with the administrative staff at the ED/UCC of the respective hospitals.

questions.title: How does the GPFirst programme benefit patients?
questions.text:
Under the GPFirst programme, most patients will be able to save costs and receive appropriate care at participating GP clinics in a timely manner.
If you have mild to moderate medical conditions, receiving treatment from your GP will cost you less as compared to going to the emergency department. If you are referred to the Emergency Department (ED) / Urgent Care Centre (UCC) after assessment by your GP, you will be prioritised over non-emergency cases and receive $50 subsidy on the prevailing attendance fee at the EDs of CGH, KTPH, NTFGH, NUH, SKH, SGH, TTSH or AH UCC.

questions.title: Will the participating hospitals’ Emergency Department (ED) and Urgent Care Centre (UCC) reject patients if they have been referred inappropriately?
questions.text: No patient will be turned away at the ED or UCC. If patients are referred to the ED or UCC under GPFirst, the Terms and Conditions of GPFirst will apply to them, regardless of their medical condition.

questions.title: Is GPFirst applicable to Permanent Residents and Foreigners?
questions.text:
Yes. GPFirst applies to all patients referred to participating acute hospital ED or UCC via participating GP clinics using the original GPFirst Referral Form.*
*Terms and Conditions apply: https://ask.gov.sg/moh/questions/cm2owrtga00fp9apof6gm5d7l

questions.title: Will patients referred by polyclinics enjoy the GPFirst subsidy?
questions.text: GPFirst applies to General Practitioners participating under the programme, and does not include referrals from polyclinics. Patients referred by polyclinics will continue to be given priority at the emergency department.

questions.title: Is GPFirst applicable to CHAS patients, even though they have already received subsidised care at GP clinics?
questions.text: The subsidy under GPFirst will apply to patients, as long as they are referred to the emergency department by participating clinics with the original GPFirst Referral Form. This includes patients under CHAS.

questions.title: How does the participating acute hospital Emergency Department (ED) and Urgent Care Centre (UCC) identify patients referred under GPFirst?
questions.text: GPs from participating clinics will refer patients using a GPFirst Referral Form. Only patients who present the original GPFirst Referral Form when they register at the referred to ED or UCC will qualify for the GPFirst programme benefits.

questions.title: What if I lose my GPFirst Referral form?
questions.text: For GPFirst Programme to be valid, the original referral form must be fully completed and produced together with the NRIC/passport/work permit/foreigner pass, at the point of registration at the respective hospital’s ED or UCC. The referral date, referral time and clinic stamp must be clearly indicated on the original GPFirst Referral Form.

questions.title: Once the GPFirst Referral form is issued can I visit the ED the next day?
questions.text: Patients’ visit to the ED/UCC must be within the same day of the GP's referral or up to 0200hrs of the following day if the form is issued close to midnight (between 10pm to 12am).

questions.title: I visited a GPFirst participating clinic in Bedok and was given a GPFirst referral to CGH Emergency Department (ED) because my condition requires urgent treatment. However, I would like to go to the ED at KTPH as I live in Yishun. Will my GPFirst referral be valid?
questions.text: Through GPFirst Programme, patients will be referred to the ED/UCC which is deem most appropriate by the GP. However, patients are encouraged to adhere to GP’s advice of seeking immediate treatment at the referred ED to ensure he/she receives the required urgent care in a timely manner

questions.title: How much would I be charged at the participating GP clinics?
questions.text: Patients will pay the fees charged by their respective GPs.

questions.title: Is the GPFirst programme applicable at all EDs?
questions.text: The GPFirst programme is only applicable at the Changi General Hospital (CGH), Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH), Woodlands Health (WH), National University Hospital (NUH) (Adult ED only), Ng Teng Fong General Hospital (NTFGH), Sengkang General Hospital (SKH), Singapore General Hospital (SGH), Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH) Emergency Departments (ED) or Alexandra Urgent Care Centre (AH UCC).

questions.title: How do I know if my neigbourhood GP clinic is participating in this programme?
questions.text: This programme is available at the participating GP clinics within the regions of the above-mentioned participating hospitals. Click here to search for a participating clinic near you. < Find-a-GP (singhealth.com.sg)>

questions.title: What are the GPFirst Terms and Conditions?
questions.text:
The GPFirst programme is open to all residents living in Singapore, including PRs and foreigners.
This programme is only applicable at the Changi General Hospital (CGH), Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH), National University Hospital (NUH) (Adult ED only), Ng Teng Fong General Hospital (NTFGH), Sengkang General Hospital (SKH), Singapore General Hospital (SGH), Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH) Emergency Departments (ED) or Alexandra Hospital Urgent Care Centre (AH UCC).
This programme is available at the participating GP clinics within the regions of the above-mentioned participating hospitals. Click here to search for a participating clinic near you.
For GPFirst Programme to be valid, the original referral form must be fully completed and produced together with the NRIC/passport/work permit/foreigner pass, at the point of registration at the respective hospital’s ED or UCC.
The referral date, referral time and clinic stamp must be clearly indicated on the original GPFirst Referral Form.
Patients’ visit to the ED/UCC must be within the same day of the GP's referral or up to 0200hrs of the following day if the form is issued close to midnight (between 10pm to 12am).
Specialised investigations required and/or non-standard medications prescribed at participating hospitals’ ED or UCC will be separately charged
The programme's terms and conditions are subject to change without prior notice.

questions.title: If I participate in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, will my Taxi Driver Vocational Licence (TDVL) be automatically renewed?
questions.text:
No, Taxi Driver Vocational Licences (TDVL) will not be automatically renewed upon participation in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme.
While co-contributions under DAS will help to offset some of your mandatory MediSave contributions, you must have an active GIRO arrangement with the Board to settle your MediSave payable via monthly instalments, or have fully settled your MediSave payable, to renew your TDVL.
You may refer to the FAQ on how to make your MediSave contributions.

Savings in the Special, MediSave and Retirement Account (SMRA) earn the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities (10YSGS) plus 1%, subject to the current floor interest rate of 4% per annum. This is reviewed quarterly.

questions.title: How much extra interest can I earn on my CPF savings?
questions.text:
To help boost retirement savings, the Government pays extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances, which is capped at $20,000 for Ordinary Account (OA). Extra interest is structured so that all CPF members benefit, and members with lower balances benefit more. The amount of extra interest paid to you would depend on your combined CPF balances and age.
If you are below 55 years old, you will earn an extra interest of 1% per annum on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances (capped at $20,000 for OA). The extra interest earned on your Special Account (SA) and MediSave Account (MA) balances will go to the respective accounts, while the extra interest earned on your OA balances will go into your SA to enhance your retirement savings.
If you are 55 years old and above, you will earn an extra interest of 2% per annum on the first $30,000 and 1% per annum on the next $30,000 of your combined CPF balances (capped at $20,000 for OA). The extra interest earned on your Retirement Account (RA) and MA balances will go to the respective accounts, while the extra interest earned on your OA balances will go into your RA to enhance your retirement savings. If you have joined the CPF LIFE scheme, the extra interest earned will be paid into your RA or accumulated with the interest earned on the CPF LIFE premiums of all CPF LIFE members.
How is my combined CPF balance computed?
Your accounts are used to compute your combined CPF balances in the following order:
- 1st: Retirement Account (RA), including any CPF LIFE premium balance
- 2nd: OA, with a cap of $20,000*
- 3rd: Special Account (SA)
- 4th: MediSave Account (MA)
*A cap of $20,000 from OA is imposed because OA savings are short-term in nature and can be withdrawn on demand for a few purposes such as housing and education.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates

questions.title: How is my CPF interest computed and credited into my accounts?
questions.text:
CPF interest is computed monthly. It is credited to your respective accounts by the following year and compounded annually.
CPF balances used for interest computation are affected by the transactions in your account. For instance, contributions (including refunds) received this month start earning interest next month. Withdrawals/deductions in this month will not earn interest from this month onwards.
There are strict procedures in place to ensure the accuracy of members’ CPF accounts and transactions (including interest payments). To further ensure that our system is sound and robust, our statutory auditor performs regular reviews of formulas and computations in our systems for accuracy, and conducts independent verifications of the transactions and account balances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates

questions.title: Does my doctor need to complete the required Medical Assessment Report for my Home Protection Scheme claim if I already have a medical report from a previous insurance claim?
questions.text: If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient to assess your Home Protection Scheme claim and inform you accordingly.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When do I need to submit the supporting documents (Medical Assessment Report and employment information) for Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text:
The medical institution that you have approached and your employer are required to submit the completed Medical Assessment Report and your employment information respectively to CPF Board within 90 days of your Home Protection Scheme claim application. We will not accept Medical Assessment Reports submitted directly by CPF members.
If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. The application form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
Please note that your application will be cancelled if we do not receive the supporting documents by the given deadline.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out-of-pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 June 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as you may use MediSave to pay for the outpatient deductible.
There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: Does my doctor need to complete the required Medical Assessment Report for my Dependants' Protection Scheme claim if I already have a medical report from a previous insurance claim?
questions.text:
If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. The application form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
If you are claiming for DPS benefits only, you may submit the report directly to Great Eastern Life (GEL). GEL will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: When do I need to submit the documents (Medical Assessment Report and employment information) to support my application for Dependants' Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text:
If you had applied for Dependants’ Protection Scheme claim through the CPF website, the medical institution that you have approached and your employer are required to submit the completed Medical Assessment Report and your employment information respectively to CPF Board within 90 days of your application. The Medical Assessment Report and employment information will be used to process claims under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS), if you have applied for both. We will not accept Medical Assessment Reports submitted directly by CPF members.
Please note that your application will be cancelled if we do not receive the supporting documents by the given deadline.
To apply for withdrawal due to Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) only, please write to us for assistance. If you are applying for DPS benefits only, you can submit the supporting document to Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I get a document that shows I do not have a CPF account?
questions.text:
You can login to my cpf digital services via your Singpass. You will see a message "No information can be displayed here as you do not have a CPF account."
You can click on located above the graphic, to save or print a copy.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What is my CPF account number?
questions.text:
If you are currently/were previously a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident, your CPF account number is the Unique Identification Number (UIN) stated on your NRIC, Citizenship Certificate, or entry permit (e.g. S1234567F or T1234567F).
Otherwise, your CPF account number could begin with the letter ‘S’ or ‘T’, followed by the letter ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’, ‘D’ or ‘F’ (e.g. SA123456D or TC987654B).
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When do I have a CPF account?
questions.text: Your CPF account is automatically created when a first top-up or CPF contribution is received.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How do I inform CPF Board of a change in my address?
questions.text:
By default, CPF letters are sent to your residential address on your Singapore Identity Card. If you are residing at a new address and have been receiving your CPF letters at your old residential address, please apply for the change of your residential address (local or overseas) via Immigration & Checkpoints Authority’s (ICA) e-Services using your Singpass.
Participating government agencies and statutory boards (including CPF Board) will be informed of the change in address through the One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS) within one day. You will not be receiving an additional acknowledgement from CPF Board for updates via OSCARS.
Please visit ICA website for more information.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When and how should I inform CPF Board about changes to my particulars?
questions.text: For Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, you do not need to inform us separately as your latest particulars will automatically be updated in our records.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How can I inform CPF Board if I changed my name?
questions.text:
We use the principal name registered in your NRIC to transact with you. Principal name usually excludes variants such as hanyu pinyin, married name and other aliases.
If you have updated your principal name registered in your NRIC recently, you do not need to inform us separately. Your name will automatically be updated in our records.
If you have not updated the name registered in your NRIC or would like to transact with us using your hanyu pinyin, married or other aliases, you will need to update your principal name in your NRIC first.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What should I do if I receive mails from CPF Board that do not belong to me and my family member(s) at our address?
questions.text: If you received mails from CPF Board that do not belong to you and your family member(s) at your address, please state the reason for return, e.g. 'no such person' or 'change of owner', and drop the mail into SingPost's "Return Mail Here" mailbox. The undelivered mail will be returned to us.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How long does it take to update my particulars?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table for the service standards in updating your particulars.
ServiceNormal Processing Time
Update of Personal Particulars for Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents3 working days
Merging of CPF accounts7 working days
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Do I need to inform CPF Board of my new Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
You do not need to inform us of your latest particulars when you become a new Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. Your Singapore identity card number will be used as your CPF account number to transact with us.
However, if you are already holding an existing CPF account (example: SA123456D or TC987654B), you would need to inform us so that we can combine your CPF accounts. Please submit the following documents/information to us where applicable by post or in-person at our CPF Service Centres.
To facilitate your transaction with us, we will combine your CPF accounts within seven working days after we have successfully verified your identity.

Please bring along your original documents and book an appointment to visit us at our CPF Service Centres.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What should I do if I receive a notification that is not meant for me?
questions.text:
This could happen because:
You are sharing contact detail(s) with your next-of-kin for handling of CPF matters; or
Your contact detail is a recycled mobile number/email address registered by another member with us previously; or
You are using a common business mobile number/email address shared within a company.
If you did not intentionally share your contact details with another member or wish to stop this arrangement, please write to us with a screenshot of the notification you have received.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Would other members receive my CPF notifications if they have registered the same contact detail(s) as me?
questions.text:
Members will receive CPF notifications at their email address and/or mobile number registered with us.
Other members can receive your CPF notifications only if they share the same email address or mobile number as you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: I have reviewed my contact detail(s) and am aware that it is also registered under another family member. Can we continue to share contact detail(s)?
questions.text:
We understand that some CPF members require help from family members on their CPF matters, and could have registered the same contact details with us.
No further action is needed if your contact details are still valid.
Otherwise, you can update your new contact details via the Account settings page with your Singpass.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Do I have to provide my bank account details to CPF Board if I do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board?
questions.text:
No action is required from you if you do not intend to make any withdrawals or do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board.
However, if you expect upcoming payments from CPF Board, e.g. monthly payouts or refunds, please provide your bank account details to CPF Board so that you can receive your payments to your registered bank account. If you are nearing age 70 and have not already started your monthly payouts, you should expect to start receiving your monthly payouts when you turn 70 years old, and will need to provide your bank account details to receive your payouts to your registered bank account.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When do I need to update my bank account?
questions.text:
You should review and update your bank account details when there are any changes to avoid any delay or disruption in receiving your payments. If you have a pending withdrawal, consider updating your bank account after the withdrawal is complete, to enable successful processing of your withdrawal application.
Your monthly payouts and CPF savings withdrawn (see list of payments) will be paid to the bank account you have provided under your Account settings.
You can update your bank account details via my cpf digital services – Account settings with your Singpass.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Which CPF payments will I receive in the bank account provided under my Account settings?
questions.text:
The bank account provided under your Account settings will be used for CPF payments such as:
Withdrawals of CPF savings from age 55
Monthly payouts
Cash bonus received under Silver Housing Bonus scheme
Cash bonus received under Lease Buyback Scheme
Sale proceeds from Singtel SDS
Withdrawals of deceased member’s CPF savings
This does not include long-term care payouts (e.g. CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care) where application is made through the Agency for Integrated Care, and Government payments (e.g. GST Vouchers, Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support Scheme).
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What bank accounts can I use to update my bank account details?
questions.text:
You may update your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account as your registered bank account with CPF Board to receive payments via PayNow. Once updated, you do not need to update your registered bank account with CPF Board again if you switch to another bank account for PayNow. Your CPF payments will automatically be made to whichever bank account you have linked to your PayNow-NRIC.
Alternatively, you may use any POSB, DBS, OCBC and UOB bank accounts belonging to you. As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, we only accept accounts from these banks as they provide automated bank account verification to CPF Board. This ensures that payments are only made to accounts that belong to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How long does it take to activate my bank account details?
questions.text:
As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, your new bank account will be activated after a 12-hour cooling period or verification by banks:
Bank accountActivation time
PayNow NRIC-linked bank accountAfter 12-hour cooling period
Other bank account (POSB, DBS, OCBC, UOB)After your bank confirms that the account belongs to you which generally takes up to two working days
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How can I amend my bank account details or cancel the online application while it is pending activation?
questions.text:
You are unable to amend your bank account details by submitting a new application or cancel the online application while it is pending activation. You can update your bank account details after it has been activated, which will generally take 12 hours for PayNow NRIC-linked bank accounts, and up to two working days for other bank accounts.
If the changes made to your bank account details are unauthorised, please contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately and reset your Singpass. If you are age 55 and above, you can also activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to instantly disable online withdrawal.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Why do I need to update contact details to update my bank account?
questions.text: Notifications via SMS or email will be sent to you whenever there are updates to your bank account. As such, you will have to register or update your contact details under Account settings to receive these notifications and prevent any unauthorised updates from taking effect.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How will I be notified about the status of my update bank account application?
questions.text:
You will receive an SMS and email notification to the local mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board as well as a push notification on your CPF Mobile app upon the following:
Submission of the application to update your registered bank account
Successful update of your registered bank account
Unsuccessful update of your registered bank account
You can also check the status of your online application under Activities.
If the changes made to your registered bank account are unauthorised, please contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately and reset your Singpass. If you are age 55 and above, you can also activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to instantly disable online withdrawal.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What are the benefits of using a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account?
questions.text: PayNow NRIC-linked bank account is easy to set up as it only requires a one-time registration with your bank using your NRIC number. It also provides convenience as you can receive CPF payments in any PayNow participating local and foreign banks, without having to provide your bank account number.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What is a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account and how do I register for it?
questions.text:
PayNow is a secure funds transfer service that enables you to receive payment conveniently in your preferred bank account with only your NRIC number. It adopts the same high security standards as other trusted funds transfer services like FAST and GIRO.
You can register for a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account if you have a bank account with the PayNow participating banks in Singapore, which can be found on the Association of Banks in Singapore's website.
If your bank is a PayNow participating bank, you may refer to your bank's website for specific details on how to link your NRIC to PayNow.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Why do I need to link my bank account to PayNow using my NRIC number?
questions.text: Unlike mobile numbers, the NRIC number is an unchanged reference number issued by the Government and is the only accepted reference number for government payments via PayNow. Linking your bank account to PayNow using your NRIC number ensures that government payments will be made correctly to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Why I am unable to view my account information?
questions.text:
my cpf digital services is compatible with the latest two versions of these commonly used web browsers:
Chrome
Safari
For an optimal user experience, please use the latest version of the web browser. If you are using a mobile device, please ensure your device is updated to the latest operating system.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: Will taxi principal hirers who participate in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme have their Taxi Driver Vocational Licence (TDVL) be automatically renewed?
questions.text:
No, Taxi Driver Vocational Licences (TDVL) will not be automatically renewed upon participation in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme.
Taxi principal hirers must have fully paid their MediSave payable or are making monthly payments via GIRO to renew their TDVLs.
MediSave contributions1 and co-contributions from taxi operators will offset mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: What sources of MediSave contributions are eligible for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions?
questions.text:
MediSave contributions1 made by the taxi principal hirer to offset MediSave payable will qualify him for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution. CPF contributions received as an employee (from both employer and self) for taxi principal hirers who are concurrently employed, as well as government top-ups are excluded.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for admission into a nursing home? How do I apply for admission to a nursing home?
questions.text:
You can find out more information on nursing home admission and how to apply for admission to a nursing home at https://www.aic.sg/care-services/nursing-home/.
You can also speak to your healthcare provider and Medical Social Worker to find out more.

questions.title: What is the cost of staying in a nursing home?
questions.text:
You can find out more information about nursing home costs at https://www.aic.sg/care-services/nursing-home/.
Subsidies and financial assistance are available for eligible nursing home residents and more information can be found on the MOH website. You can also speak to your Medical Social Worker for assistance.

questions.title: Are nursing homes held to care standards? What measures are in place to ensure the safety of nursing home residents?
questions.text:
All nursing homes are licensed under the Healthcare Services Act. MOH conducts regular checks to ensure that nursing homes meet the licensing requirements. Licensing requirements include areas such as patient care, nursing home staff, and premises, equipment and sanitation.
MOH regularly reviews and enhances the care standards in our nursing homes.

questions.title: How are Long-Term Care (LTC) services made affordable for Singapore Citizens (SCs), Permanent Residents (PRs) and Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) Holders?
questions.text:
LTC services (such as those offered at Active Ageing Centres and Senior Care Centres) are either provided free or kept affordable through Government subsidies for Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs). Like many other countries, Singapore carefully considers the unique aspects of citizenship and differentiates the benefits that citizens, permanent residents, and foreigners receive. While LTVP holders are not eligible for subsidies, those in need may reach out to their service provider or the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for financial assistance.
For more information on accessing LTC services, you may reach out to AIC at enquiries@aic.sg or 1800-650-6060.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for Active Ageing Centres (AACs)?
questions.text:
1. Singapore Citizens (SC) and Permanent Residents (PR) aged 60 and above, regardless of housing types and socio-economic status,
2. SC/PR spouse aged below 60 of an SC/PR senior, and
3. Non-Resident (NR) spouse of SC senior.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How much does it cost to join an Active Ageing Centre (AAC)?
questions.text: Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PR) aged 60 and above do not have to pay any fee to join an AAC.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the range of active ageing programmes available at an Active Ageing Centre (AAC)?
questions.text:
As a drop-in social recreational space for Seniors, AACs conduct a range of programmes across physical, cognitive, social, learning and volunteerism domains.
For the physical domain, AACs offer fitness and strengthening exercises such as Yoga, Qigong, and Zumba.
For the cognitive domain, Seniors can participate in mind-stimulating activities such as puzzles and mindfulness-related activities.
For the social domain, Seniors can enjoy communal meals and games such as Bingo and Rummy-O to widen their social circles.
For the learning domain, AACs offer arts & crafts workshop and talks for Seniors to pick up new knowledge.
For the volunteerism domain, AACs offer opportunities for Seniors to volunteer in delivering meals or packing of goodie bags for the less privileged.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How does Active Ageing Centres (AACs) play a part in Healthier SG?
questions.text:
As part of the Healthier SG initiative, AACs deliver the 2S (Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, and Community Screening) which aims to empower Seniors towards healthy and active lifestyles.
As a Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, AACs assist Seniors to join relevant active ageing programmes as recommended in their Healthier SG health plan.
AACs also serve as a community node for Community Screening, such as vitals screening and functional screening.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How do I apply for my loved ones to receive the services at Senior Care Centres (SCCs)?
questions.text: You can approach the doctor at the hospital or polyclinic for assistance to submit an online application for the service or visit an AIC Link near you.

questions.title: What are the estimated costs for the services offered at Senior Care Centres (SCCs)?
questions.text:
For Day Care, the estimated cost ranges between $945 and $1,430 a month before subsidies, assuming daily attendance on weekdays, excluding transport.
For Dementia Day Care, the estimated cost ranges between $1,260 and $1,575 per month before subsidy, assuming daily attendance on weekdays and excluding transport services.
For active rehabilitation, the estimated cost ranges between $70 and $102 per rehabilitation session before subsidy, excluding transport services.
For maintenance rehabilitation, the estimated cost ranges between $52 and $65 per rehabilitation session before subsidy, excluding transport services.
Subsidies for both services and transport are available for application. The received amount varies depending on your family’s income.
You may visit an AIC Link near you for assistance on the application process.

questions.title: What are the volunteering roles available for seniors under the Silver Generation Office? What is the difference between volunteering at Active Ageing Centres (AACs) under the Silver Guardian Programme and the Silver Generation Ambassador programmes?
questions.text:
As a Silver Generation Ambassador, you will engage seniors through home visits, also known as Preventive Health Visits (PHVs). These visits allow us to understand how the seniors are in aspects of health, financial and social, and provide seniors with relevant information of government policies, schemes, community activities and health services which may be beneficial for the seniors.
As a Silver Guardian volunteering at Active Ageing Centres, you may be assigned as an Active Ageing Programme facilitator to help co-facilitate simple exercises or arts and craft activities, or become a befriender to vulnerable seniors, monitor their wellbeing and encourage/accompany them to attend community activities. You may also be assigned other roles within the AACs based on the needs within the centre.
If you would like to hear more about the volunteering opportunities at the AACs, you may sign up for an Information Sharing session with AIC via the link: https://for.sg/volunteer-with-us-today.
For more information about the Silver Generation Ambassador programme, visit https://www.aic.sg/about-us/be-sga-volunteer/.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: Will training be provided for Silver Guardians and Silver Generation Ambassadors prior to volunteering?
questions.text:
Yes, training will be provided to equip volunteers with the necessary skills for the volunteering roles, e.g., on effective communication with seniors.
The training structures and durations vary depending on the role.
For more information about the Silver Generation Ambassador programme, visit
https://www.aic.sg/about-us/be-sga-volunteer/
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the Silver Volunteer Fund under the Council for Third Age?
questions.text:
The Silver Volunteer Fund (SVF) was launched in 2016 as part of the National Senior Volunteerism Movement under the first Action Plan for Successful Ageing.
In 2023, the Council for Third Age (C3A) rolled out the Enhanced Silver Volunteer Fund (ESVF) to provide funding support for volunteer host organisations to offer a diverse range of volunteering opportunities for seniors.
Volunteer host organisations can tap on the ESVF to offer training and development opportunities and increase volunteer appreciation efforts for volunteers to better retain and grow their pool of senior volunteers. The ESVF also fosters exchanges to encourage sharing of knowledge and best practices amongst volunteer host organisations.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: Where can I get more information on Advance Care Planning (ACP)?
questions.text: You may wish to find out more here: (Link to AIC’s website on FAQs on ACP)

questions.title: Who can apply for the Seniors' Mobility And Enabling Fund (SMF) SMF - Devices Subsidy?
questions.text:
If you are a needy Singaporean aged 60 years and above, you can apply, subject to means-testing and needs assessment.
You must not be concurrently receiving (or apply for) any other public or private grants/subsidies that exceed the amount of co-payment should you get SMF subsidies for the device(s) you are applying for.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: How will seniors or Persons with Disabilities know if they are eligible for SMF or Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)?
questions.text:
Seniors and Persons with Disabilities will be served under one scheme throughout their lifetime. If the individual has tapped on ATF1 before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime. On the other hand, if the individual has not tapped on ATF1 subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime.
Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organizations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes. They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) or SG Enable (SGE) for assistance.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies
1 The ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living.

questions.title: What type of means testing will be done for SMF?
questions.text:
Means-testing will be conducted based on MOH’s SMF Device or Consumables Subsidy framework. To qualify for SMF subsidies, your household monthly income per person should be $2,000 and below OR Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC should be $21,000 and below for households with no income.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: What is the list of Assistive Devices covered under SMF - Devices Subsidy?
questions.text:
You can use SMF subsidies for assistive devices you are assessed to require for your care needs, including but not limited to:
Walking aids
Basic wheelchair / pushchair
Motorised wheelchair / scooter
Pressure relief cushion
Pressure relief mattress
Commode / shower chair
Geriatric chair
Hospital bed
Special equipment such as oxygen concentrator, suction pump or transfer board
Spectacles
Hearing aids
Prosthesis / orthosis
Vision and reading aids
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Who can apply for the SMF - Consumables Subsidy?
questions.text:
If you are a needy Singaporean aged 60 years and above, you can apply, subject to means-testing and needs assessment.
You must be receiving one of the following services: Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, Day Hospice, Integrated Home & Day Care (IHDC) services.
You will also need to go for a clinical needs assessment by your home healthcare provider to find out the types of home healthcare items you require.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: What consumables are covered under SMF?
questions.text:
You can use SMF subsidies for the following types of consumables (also known as home healthcare items):
Adult diapers
Catheters and catheter set
Milk feeds
Nasal tubing
Nasogastric tubes and pH indication test strips
Thickeners
Wound dressings
Milk feeds
Nasal tubing
Nasogastric tubes and pH indication test strips
Thickeners
Wound dressings
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: What are the enhancements to Caregivers Training Grant (CTG) from 1 April 2024?
questions.text:
From 1 April 2024, eligible beneficiaries will start off with an initial grant of $400. Each year, there will be a top up to care recipients’ CTG by $200, and unused monies can be carried forward, with the CTG monies for each care recipient capped at $400 per year.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Are Migrant Domestic Workers (MDW) eligible for the grant?
questions.text:
Yes, as long as they are the main caregivers of persons with disability or elderly who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: How do eligible caregivers receive the grant?
questions.text:
Eligible caregivers will receive the grant in the form of training fee subsidies.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: If there is more than one caregiver taking care of the same person, are they all eligible for the grant?
questions.text:
Yes, different caregivers of the same care recipient may utilise the grant to subsidise the caregiving training, up to the grant amount that each care recipient is eligible for per Financial Year.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Can more than one caregiver tap on the grant to attend the same training programme?
questions.text:
Yes. More than one caregiver of each care recipient can attend the same training and will be reimbursed only up to the grant amount care recipient receives per financial year, in the form of training subsidies.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Can I attend any training programmes that I think are useful?
questions.text: No; however, to tap on CTG for training fee subsidy, caregivers may choose from a list of more than 150 training programmes that have been pre-approved. The list of pre-approved training programmes can be found here.

questions.title: I did not use my grant monies this year. Can I carry it forward next year?
questions.text:
From 1 April 2024, unused monies can be carried forward with a cap at $400 within each account. Any amount exceeding the Cap of $400 will be forfeited.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Can I apply for Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) if my loved one is unable to provide consent for the application due to e.g. lack of mental capacity or below 21 years old?
questions.text:
Yes.
For care recipient who lacks mental capacity
Care recipent’s donee/deputy# may provide consent on the care recipient’s behalf. If the care recipient does not have such a donee/deputy, the caregiver* may make the application on care recipient’s behalf.
# Donee/deputy must be appointed in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act (Cap 177) and is authorised to make decisions on behalf of the care recipient in relation to the care recipient’s property and affairs.
* For successful applications without a donee/deputy, the caregiver or another family member has 12 months to obtain a court order appointing him/her as a deputy, failing which the payouts will be suspended. For more information on how to apply for a deputyship, please visit SG Courts Website.
Doctor’s certification for mental incapacity is only valid for six months, unless stated permanent.
You will also need to submit the following additional supporting documents:
Doctor’s certification that the care recipient lacks mental capacity OR court order of deputy appointment OR recent medical report stating that the care recipient lacks mental capacity; and
Copy of bank book or statement IF you are nominating an account belonging to a deputy or trustee of the care recipient.
For care recipient below age of 21 years old
The care recipient’s parent or legal guardian^ may make this application on behalf of the care recipient.
^ Legal guardian refers to a person who has been lawfully appointed in accordance with the Guardianship of Infants Act (Cap. 122).
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Why are individuals who own multiple properties and PCHI ≤ $1,500 ineligible for the Home Caregiving Grant’s (HCG) $400 payout and eligible only for the $250 payout?
questions.text:
Schemes such as the HCG are means-tested to provide support according to need. An individual who owns multiple properties and fulfils the HCG’s eligibility criteria can qualify for the lower tier $250 payout.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: What types of properties are considered for the multiple property ownership criterion for determining which Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) tier an individual is eligible for (i.e. $250 or $400 payout)?
questions.text:
All types of properties, e.g., HDB flat, private residential property, and non-residential property are taken into account in determining which HCG tier an individual is eligible for.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: When do I need to reapply for MDW Levy Concession (PWD)?
questions.text:
You do not need to re-apply for the scheme if there is a change in the MDW, MDW Employer or your address. However, if you employ the MDW to take care of another care recipient, you need to submit a fresh MDW Levy Concession (PWD) application for the new care recipient.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: How do I apply home care services for my loved to support their care at home?
questions.text: Seniors who require the services can visit an AIC Link located in the restructured hospital near you or call the AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060 for assistance.

questions.title: How much out-of-pocket fees do I need to pay for the home care services?
questions.text: The out-of-pocket fees that you need to pay will depend on the type of home care service you require. Eligible seniors can receive subsidies of up to 80%, based on the non-residential Long-Term Care subsidy framework. You may approach an AIC Link or call the AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060 for more details.

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for the Community Care Apartments?
questions.text:
Conditions
Age
Applicant(s) and their spouse (if any) must be 65 years old and above.
Income Ceiling
The average gross monthly household income cannot exceed $14,000.
Family Nucleus and Citizenship
Available to:
Families with at least 1 Singapore citizen applicant and
Singles who are Singapore citizens.
Property Ownership
Applicant(s) or any person listed in the HFE letter application aged 65 and above who owns any private residential property or an HDB flat must dispose of the property within 6 months from collecting keys to the Community Care Apartment (CCA). If they own not more than one non-residential property, they do not need to dispose of the property.
Previous Purchase
Those who have enjoyed two or more housing subsidies before, one of which was a Studio Apartment or short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or CCA, are not eligible.
Lease Length
The lease chosen must be able to cover all applicants and their spouse (if any) till at least 95 years old. Options range from 15 to 35 years (in 5-year increments).
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: Which group of seniors are suitable for the CCA?
questions.text:
CCAs cater to healthier seniors, as well as those with some care needs. Healthier seniors can be supported to keep well and stay active for as long as they can. As care needs increase, residents will not need to struggle with navigating care options as the appointed CCA operator will take care of their needs where possible, and facilitate their access to other care services as needed.
However, seniors who have a high level of care or nursing needs, or who have been diagnosed with severe mental illness and/or loss of mental capacity that require intensive support, may not be suitably cared for within the CCA.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What are the payment modes for the Basic Service Package?
questions.text:
For the Basic Service Package, you can choose between 2 regular payment plans of either:
a. Payment due every month, plus a 1-year security deposit at the start of the lease; OR
b. Payment due every 3 years.
Payment for the Basic Service Package can be done by cashier’s order, GIRO, or bank transfer.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is offered under the Basic Service Package?
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What are the optional services available?
questions.text:
The operator will provide the following optional services (list is non-exhaustive):
a. Shared Caregiving Service (SCS), for assistance with Activities of Daily Living, such as showering, medical reminders and assistance with simple errands
c. Housekeeping service;
d. Meals service (delivery);
f. Laundry service; and
g. Medical escort and transport service.
The operator will review the optional services available to residents regularly, to ensure adequacy of support.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How do I renew a Dependant's Pass? Can a Dependant’s Pass be renewed after adoption?
questions.text:
The steps to renew a Dependant’s Pass (DP) is the same as applying for a new DP. Please refer to the application form link and required documents.
The DP will only be renewed for valid reasons. If a DP extension is required, please make an extension application with MSF at least 1 month prior to the expiry date. Each extension is valid for 6 months.
All DP extension applications will be processed within 20 working days, provided all the required documents are submitted.
Once the DP application is approved, there is a payment of $225 for each DP issuance and $30 in multi-journey visa (if applicable) for the child to enter Singapore. The payment details will be specified in the IPA letter.
You cannot renew your DP once an Adoption Order has been granted. Please approach the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) for advice on applying for a suitable immigration pass applications (e.g. Student’s Pass) for the child to remain in Singapore, while waiting for the outcome of his Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency application.
You may contact ICA through their feedback form on their website.

questions.title: How is the scope of benefits determined? What other treatments have been considered for coverage under MediShield Life?
questions.text: The MediShield Life Council has assessed the scope of benefits and new areas to be covered by MediShield Life, taking in proposals from various stakeholders. Treatments which are recommended for MediShield Life coverage have been prioritised based on suitability for risk-pooling, clinical- and cost-effectiveness, having significant affordability gaps, and/or potential to encourage patients to receive care in appropriate settings.
topics: MediShield Life / Benefits Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How do I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
The medical institution will ask if you wish to make a claim and request for your authorisation to submit the claim to MediShield Life and your Integrated Shield Plan insurer (if any) on your behalf. If a payout is due, it will be made to the medical institution directly to offset your bill. The remaining balance can be paid by MediSave and/or cash.
To estimate the maximum amount that you can claim from MediSave or MediShield Life, click here
(https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/medisave-medishield-life-claims)
The list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life is available here.
https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/member/healthcare/documents/MSH_MedicalInstitutions.pdf
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: With the availability of the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements, will I still receive hardcopy statements?
questions.text:
You will not receive a hardcopy statement when deductions are made from your MediSave Account to pay for your dependents or your own medical bills. Instead, you will be informed of any deductions via one of the following mobile notifications:
a. If you have the Singpass Mobile App, you will be notified via the Singpass Mobile App Inbox;
b. If you do not have the Singpass Mobile App, but have registered your mobile number with Singpass, you will be notified via SMS.
If you still prefer to receive a hardcopy of your MediSave transaction statement, please write to us. If you do not have a Singpass account and or a registered mobile number, you will continue to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement. No further action is required.
If your claim was only for MediShield Life and there was no deduction made from your MediSave account for the claim, you will not receive a hardcopy statement. For these cases, you will be able to access the claim details from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements.
If you would like to have the claim statements but are unable to log in online, you may approach our customer service officers over the counter or contact us at 1800 222 3399 for assistance.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What is the pro-ration factor? How does it affect my claim?
questions.text: As private hospital bills and Ward A/B1 bills in public hospitals are generally higher than the Ward B2/C bills that MediShield Life is designed for, they are pro-rated to the equivalent level of a Ward B2/C bill before MediShield Life payouts are computed. This ensures comparable payouts for subsidised and private patients.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How do I view details of my MediShield Life claims from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediSave withdrawals and MediShield Life claim details for past 15 months online at www.cpf.gov.sg under "Latest healthcare payments and claims".
Following are the steps to take:
(1) Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
(2) Proceed to “Latest healthcare payments and claims”
(3) Click on “View past 15 months”
(4) Select the hospitalisation period
(5) Click on the amount at MediSave Payment or MediShield Life/Integrated Shield Plan Payment to view the claim details.
If you would like to view the details of claims prior to the past 15 months, please submit a request to the Central Provident Fund Board via www.cpf.gov.sg/eSvc/Web/FeedbackSubscription/Index .
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be able to view claim details of my dependant(s) from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You will be able to view claim details of your dependant(s) if
(i) You are the MediSave payer for your dependant’s hospitalisation; or
(ii) You are the MediShield Life premium payer for the dependant who is less than 16 years old.
If your dependants are 16 years old and above, they may apply for SingPass here and login to view their own healthcare payment details.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will my hospitalisation claims still be processed after renouncement or citizenship or permanent resident status?
questions.text:
If you are insured by MediShield Life only, you can claim for medical treatments consumed prior to the renouncement date of your citizenship.
Please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options, and on the processing of your claims under your Integrated Shield Plan.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: I am covered by Employer Medical Benefits. Can I claim from MediShield Life as well? Who pays first?
questions.text:
For members who are covered under multiple schemes, the Ministry of Health has set out the following claims protocol to avoid duplicative payouts:
1. Employer, private insurance, other third party pays first
2. Followed by MediShield Life (MSHL)/Integrated Shield Plan (IP)
3. Then MediSave
4. Then Cash
MSHL/IP will pay for the portion of the bill that is not covered by employer, private insurance and other third-party payers, subject to claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. If you have filed a claim under MSHL/IP first and subsequently with a third-party payer, you or the third party payer must reimburse the relevant amount to MSHL/IP, in line with the claims protocol. The public/private healthcare institutions and the insurance industry have been informed of this claims protocol.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What are the different types of Government subsidies to help Singaporeans with their MediShield Life premiums? Who is eligible for them?
questions.text:
The Government provides the following premium subsidies and support to keep premiums affordable.
Premium Subsidies (up to 60%) for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents with household monthly income per person of $3,600 and below and living in residences with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below. Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible. Permanent Residents (PRs) will receive half the applicable Singapore Citizens (SCs) rate.
Additional Merdeka Generation (MG) Subsidies of up to 10% for all MGs, on top of above premium subsidies.
Special Pioneer Generation (PG) Subsidies of up to 60% for all PG seniors, regardless of income of Annual Value of property. PGs will also receive lifetime annual MediSave top-ups of $300 - $1,200 a year, which can be used to pay premiums. With this, PGs born in 1934 and earlier will have premiums fully covered by the government, while younger PGs will have about two-thirds of premiums covered. Older PGs (born in 1939 and earlier) who have serious pre-existing conditions will also receive an additional one-off annual MediSave top-up of $50-$200 for five years, from 2021 to 2025.
Additional Premium Support is available for needy Singaporeans who cannot afford their premiums even after the above subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.

questions.title: The majority of Singapore Residents are covered under Integrated Shield Plans. Are they eligible for subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes, Singapore Residents covered under Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) will also receive the applicable subsidies for MediShield Life premiums if they meet the eligibility criteria.
IPs are made up of 2 components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component providing additional coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
Subsidies for those who are insured under IPs will be applied only on the MediShield Life component of the IP premiums.

questions.title: Will I receive premium subsidies even if I am not the one paying for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text: You will be able to receive subsidies if you meet the eligibility criteria, regardless of who is paying for your premiums.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation member. How much subsidies do I receive for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text:
All Pioneer Generation seniors receive special Pioneer Generation Subsidies of 40% to 60%, regardless of income or Annual Value of property. PGs also receive lifetime annual MediSave top-ups of $300 - $1,200 a year, which can be used to pay premiums. With this, PGs born in 1934 and earlier have premiums fully covered by the government, while younger PGs will have about two-thirds of premiums covered. Older PGs (born in 1939 and earlier) who have serious pre-existing conditions also receive an additional one-off annual MediSave top-up of $50-$200, from 2021 to 2025.
PGs who are unable to pay their remaining share of premiums even after the Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support, which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years. No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: How does the Government help those who cannot afford their MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
All Singapore Residents will remain covered under MediShield Life and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay premiums. The Government provides Singaporeans with premium subsidies and support, such as Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income, special Pioneer Generation subsidies, additional Merdeka Generation subsidies, and MediSave top-ups.
Policyholders who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support , which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years.
From 1 April 2025, enhancements will be made to several of these premium support measures to cushion the impact of premium increases. Please refer to press release for more details.

questions.title: If I am eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, does this apply for the rest of my life?
questions.text: Your eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies is subject to your household monthly income per person, Annual Value (AV) of residence, multiple property ownership and citizenship. All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are generally means-tested once a year, and will continue to receive MediShield Life Premium Subsidies as long as one continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Premium Subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households with their MediShield Life premiums. Pioneer Generation subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies are applicable for life, regardless of income or place of residence.

questions.title: To receive Premium Subsidies, why is the household monthly income per person criteria set at $3,600 (Applicable for Renewals From 1 October 2024)? Does this mean if I earn above $3,600, I am considered high income and cannot receive any Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The $3,600 figure refers to the household monthly income per person, which is based on the total income earned by a family staying in the same residential address, divided by the number of members of that family.
So, if the total income earned by family members is $14,000, and there are four members in the family, then the household monthly income per person is $3,500, and the family would qualify for subsidies.
This is a fairer way of calculating the need for subsidies, because a family with more members may need more support, even if the total income they make is quite high.
Families in a lower household income category will get a higher subsidy rate. In this way, more help is given to those who have less resources, in line with being a compassionate and inclusive society.
