questions.title: What is the difference between Operating Loss Ratio and Loss Ratio, which is a better measure? Why do some people cite the loss ratio as being low?
questions.text:
The loss ratio is a measure of premiums collected over the claims paid out in each year.
However, it omits future long-term claims and premium rebates, which are a large part of what MediShield Life premiums are meant to support. For example, MediShield Life covers a dialysis patient’s treatment over many years. These are future liabilities that will not be accounted for in the loss ratio, which only compares premiums collected against claims paid over a single year.
On the other hand, the Operating Loss Ratio also accounts for the premiums collected to meet the Scheme’s future liabilities, on top of the amount set aside to pay out for claims received each year. It represents a longer-term view of fund sustainability as it measures whether premiums collected are adequate to meet the scheme’s current and future commitments.

questions.title: What do the liabilities of the MediShield Life Fund support?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Fund needs to set aside enough monies to honour expected future commitments including:
i. Future premium rebates
To ensure that MediShield Life premiums remain affordable in old age, part of the premiums that policyholders pay when young is set aside ,and returned as premium rebates when they are old and less likely to be working. The contributions from each age cohort will be used to support their own rebates in old age. This helps to distribute premiums more evenly throughout policyholders’ lifetimes.
ii. Claims incurred but not yet submitted or paid
This is for expected claims, where the treatment has already taken place (and hence hospitalisation expenses have already been incurred) but have yet to be submitted or paid. This includes the projected future costs for those who have already started on multi-year treatments.
iii. Claims not yet incurred but expected to be paid in the future
This is for claims where treatments have not taken place but are expected to occur in the next few years based on actuarial projections and after allowing for future premium collections. This also includes an allowance for the fact that premiums typically remain constant between each scheme review, unlike average claim amounts that increase annually in tandem with rising medical treatment costs.

questions.title: Are the MediShield Life Fund’s liabilities necessary? Why is there a need to set aside liabilities for recurring claims when premiums are paid annually?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Fund is designed to be self-sustaining based on sound actuarial principles. Premiums are collected to cover current and future payouts, including amounts set aside to support future commitments. These commitments are largely made up of premium rebates that will be paid out in future to keep premiums affordable for Singaporeans in old age. They also include expected payouts for patients who have started on multi-year treatments (e.g. dialysis and chemotherapy), to provide them assurance that they will be covered for as long as they require their treatments.
The liabilities associated with these current and future claim commitments are computed by external actuarial experts in accordance with requirements set by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and are in line with industry standards.

questions.title: Given that the Fund already has significant assets, why is there a need to increase premiums for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Majority of the assets in the MediShield Life Fund are set aside as liabilities to honour future commitments such as premium rebates and future claims for patients who have started on multi-year recurrent treatments, such as dialysis and chemotherapy. In addition, capital is also set aside to ensure that MediShield Life can absorb the impact from adverse events and continue to pay out claims, without requiring sudden increases in premiums.
As payouts have increased over the years due to medical inflation and higher claims utilisation, premiums have to be increased in order for the Fund to continue meeting its commitments. Higher premiums will also support the higher claim limits for existing benefits and the expansion to new benefits.

questions.title: What is the MediShield Life Council? What is the purpose of the Council?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Council is an independent body set up to perform the following functions:
a. To make recommendations to the Minister for Health on policy and scheme parameters to ensure that the MediShield Life scheme provides effective protection for citizens and permanent residents of Singapore in an affordable and sustainable manner;
b. To review the administration of the MediShield Life scheme to ensure alignment with the directions of the Council; and
c. To advise the Minister for Health on matters related to the investment of the Fund, and any other matters related to the Scheme or the Fund as the Minister for Health may direct.

questions.title: Who are the Council members and how were they chosen?
questions.text: The MediShield Life Council currently comprises 11 members who have been appointed by the Minister for Health based on the relevance of their expertise, experience and public standing. The members come from diverse backgrounds, with professional experience in areas such as accountancy, insurance, investment, medicine, the law, union and government. This ensures that the Council can benefit from the wide-ranging expertise and experience of the members in the administration and review of MediShield Life. Please refer to this link (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-council) for the list of members and their profile.

questions.title: Why is permanent residency in our country of residence a supporting indicator for eligibility?
questions.text: The administrative arrangement is only for those who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. Obtaining permanent residency in another country is one of the indicators required to demonstrate an individual’s intention to reside in another country permanently.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can I submit foreign citizenship documents when applying for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
No. The Singapore Government does not allow Singapore Citizens, aged 21 and above, to hold dual citizenship. The suspension application will not be processed until your dual citizenship status has been resolved with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
For matters relating to resolving of Singapore Citizenship, please submit your enquiry to ICA.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can minors who hold dual citizenship apply for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
Minors aged below 21 who hold dual citizenship may apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection, subject to the eligibility criteria. Minor dual citizens (DCs) must possess a valid permanent residency permit in their country of residence, or other foreign residency documents permitting them to reside in their country of residence permanently with no end date.
This is considering that Singapore Citizens who have acquired a citizenship of a foreign country can only renounce their Singapore citizenship after they turn 21 years old. If the application is approved, minor DCs will be granted suspension of MediShield Life premiums starting from the next policy year at point of application until the age of 20 years (inclusive).
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: My child is less than five years old. How will he meet the overseas residency qualifying period of five years?
questions.text: Minors less than five years old will have their overseas residency qualifying period eligibility criteria correspondingly reduced, according to their age. All other criteria will apply. Parents may submit the application on behalf of minors below 21 years old.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Why is there a cap on the number of days I visit Singapore? How did you decide on 140 days over five years?
questions.text:
Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life is in line with our move to a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility. MediShield Life coverage is thus mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
The MediShield Life Council’s recommended administrative arrangement is targeted at overseas Singaporeans who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. The criterion of 140 days over five years was included to help to determine administratively who can be regarded as permanently away, save for short visits to Singapore. The duration takes into consideration the general length of stay granted to tourists coming to Singapore for short visits, but with flexibility to be assessed on a cumulative basis over five years.
For those who live abroad permanently but need to stay in Singapore for a longer period of time than the specified limit, we can review their specific circumstances on a case by case basis.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: I am planning to live overseas permanently from next year onwards. Can I apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection now?
questions.text: In order to qualify for suspension of premium collection, you must have resided outside Singapore for at least five years immediately preceding your application, except for short visits back to Singapore (not exceeding 140 days in total during the five years). As such, you may wish to apply only after you have fulfilled all the criteria.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If I received a payout from MediShield or MediShield Life during the past five years, can I apply for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text: The suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is meant for Singapore Citizens living outside Singapore permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. One of the eligibility criteria for the suspension of premium collection is that the applicant has adequate healthcare coverage in their country of residence and does not need to rely on MediShield Life. If you have received a payout and benefitted from MediShield or MediShield Life in the five years preceding your application, you will not be eligible for suspension of premium collection.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Can overseas Singaporean male minors apply for suspension of premium collection before National Service obligations are fulfilled?
questions.text:
National Service is a key institution that is vital to the security and defence of Singapore. Under the Enlistment Act, all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents above the age of 18 years are required to serve National Service.
In line with this, only the following overseas Singaporean males will be eligible to apply for the suspension of MediShield Life premium collection:
a) Those who have completed full-time National Service; or
b) Those who have been informed by MINDEF that they are not required to serve full-time National Service.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Are those insured with Integrated Shield Plans eligible for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans automatically include a MediShield Life component. You will have to pay the premium (inclusive of the MediShield Life component) to retain your Integrated Shield Plan coverage.
As coverage for Integrated Shield Plans are designed for local treatment, please consider if you wish to retain your Integrated Shield Plan if you are planning to move overseas permanently.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Are Singapore Permanent Residents eligible for suspension of premium collection?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a compulsory, basic health insurance which helps members meet the large costs of hospitalisation at Class B2 or C wards and certain outpatient treatments in Singapore’s approved medical institutions. All Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents are required to be covered under MediShield Life. The intent of this insurance is to give all Singapore residents assurance of universal healthcare coverage, including those with pre-existing conditions, for life.
Overseas Singapore Citizens who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore can apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. Singapore Permanent Residents will not be eligible for the suspension of premium collection. Permanent Residents have applied to reside in Singapore and should continue to meet their MediShield Life obligations.
topics: MediShield Life / Eligibility for Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Where can I find the application form? When can I start applying for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection?
questions.text: To apply for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection, please complete the application form (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/e-services-for-medishield-life/). When submitting your application, please ensure that your application form is duly completed with the necessary supporting documents uploaded. If you face any difficulty submitting the online application, please write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous).
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: When will I find out whether my application has been approved?
questions.text: The Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board will notify you once your application has been processed.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If my application is approved, when will suspension of MediShield Life premium collection start?
questions.text: If your application is approved, suspension of MediShield Life premium collection will start prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of the application by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: I have already submitted my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. It is pending approval. Why am I still receiving reminder letters to pay my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The premiums for your MediShield Life cover are still payable while your application is being processed. If your application is successful, premium collection will be suspended prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of your application.
Any outstanding premiums prior to the start of the Suspension Period remain payable. Please make payment promptly with the payment modes available on CPF's website (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/i-am-i-residing-overseas-or-ii-have-renounced-my-singapore-citizenship-permanent-resident-status-how-do-i-pay-my-careshield-life-eldershield-medishield-life-premiums) to avoid any further enforcement action.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: How can I inform if there is a change in my address?
questions.text:
All notification letters relating to MediShield Life will be sent to the last known address on your Singapore identity card (IC), which is the official address as registered with the Singapore Government. You may update your residential address by accessing the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority of Singapore’s (ICA) change of address e-Service (https://go.gov.sg/ic-address) using your Singpass. Any updates will automatically be transmitted to all participating government organisations via the One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS).
If you do not hold an identity card but wish to update your address, please write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous) and we will further advise you on your request.

questions.title: Under what circumstances would I be required to pay the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection with compound interest?
questions.text: You would only have to pay the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection with compound interest if (a) you choose to relocate back to Singapore, (b) no longer meet the eligibility criteria for suspension of premium collection, or (c) choose to claim and benefit from MediShield Life payouts. Once this happens, your suspension of MediShield Life premium collection will cease and you will have to pay the full sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What is the interest rate used to calculate the amount of premiums I have to pay if I choose to relocate back to Singapore?
questions.text: The interest rate is currently 4% per year and will be subject to applicable laws as may be amended from time to time. Interest will be imposed and computed on a compounded basis on full insurance periods that have passed.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I decide to renounce my Singapore Citizenship in the future, is any action required on my part to cancel my MediShield Life coverage?
questions.text: No further action is required from you. Your MediShield Life coverage will cease when you renounce your citizenship. The Central Provident Fund Board will automatically be updated about the change in your citizenship status. You will not receive any further notifications on MediShield Life coverage.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I later decide to relocate back to Singapore?
questions.text:
Suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is only for those who live outside Singapore permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore.
Please inform the Central Provident Fund Board once you have relocated back to Singapore. Your suspension of premium collection will cease and the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
Should you face any concerns with the affordability of premiums, you may apply to be assessed for financial assistance with your premiums. We will consider requests on a case by case basis.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What should I do if my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved and I do not renew my permanent residency permit in my country of residence in future?
questions.text:
Please inform the Central Provident Fund Board if your permanent residency permit in your overseas country of residence is no longer valid.
Suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is only for those who live abroad permanently with no intention to reside in Singapore. Obtaining permanent residency in another country is one of the indicators required to demonstrate an individual’s intention to reside in another country permanently. Therefore, if you do not renew your permanent residency permit in your overseas country of residence, it is an indication that you may not be able to permanently reside in that country. Your suspension of premium collection will cease and the accumulated sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest, will be payable.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: If my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection is approved, what happens if I wish to return to Singapore to seek medical treatment and claim from MediShield Life in future?
questions.text:
One of the eligibility criteria for the suspension of premium collection is that the applicant has adequate healthcare coverage in their country of residence and does not need to rely on MediShield Life. Hence, if you return to Singapore to seek medical treatment and claim from MediShield Life, your suspension of premium collection will be terminated. You will have to pay the full sum of premiums suspended from collection, with compound interest.
Please contact the Central Provident Fund Board for further information.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: Will overseas Singaporeans who relocate back to Singapore be eligible for the subsidies for all premiums?
questions.text:
Overseas Singaporeans approved for suspension of premium collection will be treated similar to other Singaporeans and receive all prevailing subsidies, if eligible. They will automatically receive Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Transitional Subsidies for the applicable policy years. They will receive Premium Subsidies if they apply and submit sufficient documentation for MOH to assess their eligibility for Premium Subsidies prior to the applicable policy year. These subsidies will be factored into the total net amount to be paid should the overseas Singaporean relocate back to Singapore.
Besides subsidies, financial assistance may be available on a case by case basis upon return and the Insured may apply for assessment.
topics: MediShield Life / Suspension of Premium Collection

questions.title: What are Integrated Shield Plans and should I consider getting one?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) provide additional coverage beyond MediShield Life. IPs comprise 2 components:
(i) the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund Board, and
(ii) the additional private insurance component by private insurers that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. There is no duplicate coverage between MediShield Life and IPs.
The list of IPs and comparison of their coverage and premiums can be found here.
As IPs provide additional coverage, premiums for IPs are higher than MediShield Life’s, and they are only payable by MediSave up to the Additional Withdrawal Limits below.

questions.title: What are IP riders and should I consider getting one?
questions.text:
IP riders are optional products designed to cover part of the deductible and co-insurance of your Integrated Shield Plan (IP). Even with a rider, patients will still need to co-pay a minimum of 5% of the claimable amount. Riders may also provide coverage for additional treatments, such as cancer drug treatments not covered under MediShield Life and IPs.
Riders premiums can only be paid in cash.
You may wish to consider the following when deciding whether to buy a rider:
Co-payment: Whether you are willing to pay more premiums to lower your co-pay in the unlikely event you incur hospital bills. If so, consider getting a rider, but do compare whether the rider premiums are worth the likely amount of co-payment they will cover.
Additional benefits: IPs and riders may cover additional treatments and services such as pre-/post-hospitalisation, emergency overseas treatments and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). Again, consider whether the additional premiums are worth the additional coverage.
Premiums: Most importantly, consider whether you can afford a rider in the long run. As you age, your premiums will increase and may strain your finances if not planned for adequately, leading to affordability issues in later years.

questions.title: I already have an Integrated Shield Plan. How is MediShield Life relevant to me?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) comprise 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
If you have an IP, you already have MediShield Life, as MediShield Life is a component of your IP.
MediShield Life will cover all pre-existing conditions, even if they are excluded by your private insurer from the additional private insurance coverage of your IP. Should you decide to terminate your IP one day, you will remain covered by MediShield Life.

questions.title: Will my Integrated Shield Plan premiums be affected by changes in MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of two components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. Correspondingly, IP premiums are made up of MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component.
Hence, your overall IP premium will be affected by both changes in the MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component:
If MediShield premiums increase/decrease, the premiums for the MediShield Life component of IPs will be increased/decreased accordingly.
Premiums for the additional private insurance component of IPs are set, reviewed and adjusted by private insurers based on commercial and actuarial considerations. Insurers may adjust their premiums upwards/downwards taking into account the impact of their claims experience, medical inflation and their own product changes if any. Insurers have an incentive to keep premiums competitive, to attract and retain policyholders. Singaporeans concerned with the affordability of IP premiums may wish to consider switching to more affordable insurance options, in line with their preferences for hospitalisation coverage.

questions.title: With the introduction of MediShield Life, should I continue to stay on my Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
MediShield Life is a basic scheme designed to cover subsidised bills such as Ward B2/C stays.
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are private plans that provide additional private insurance coverage on top of MediShield Life to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
We advise you to buy a plan that meets your needs taking into consideration your preferred ward class and affordability of premiums over the long-term.

questions.title: Will I receive subsidies even though I am insured under an Integrated Shield Plan? Do I have to downgrade my insurance plan to MediShield Life to receive subsidies?
questions.text:
You will still be able to receive the applicable MediShield Life subsidies (i.e. Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income; Pioneer Generation Subsidies; Merderka Generation Subsidies) if you meet the eligibility criteria, even if you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP). You do not have to downgrade your plan to receive the subsidies.
For IP policyholders who meet the eligibility criteria for the various subsidies, the subsidies will be applied on the MediShield Life component of their IPs.

questions.title: With MediShield Life, will the Integrated Shield Plans cover pre-existing conditions? Can I now get coverage under Integrated Shield Plans for my pre-existing conditions?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of two components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
You can get coverage for pre-existing conditions, and be assured of lifelong coverage, under the MediShield Life component of your IP.
This is even if the condition is excluded from the additional private insurance coverage by your IP insurer.
Underwriting decisions on the additional private insurance component of IPs are separately determined by the private IP insurers. Private insurers assess applications for the additional private insurance component of the IP based on their own risk assessment frameworks, as these are commercial decisions. You may wish to check with your private insurer or financial advisor on coverage for pre-existing conditions.

questions.title: What does it mean if I have an exclusion on the additional private insurance coverage component but not on the MediShield Life component? How do I find out what exclusion I have?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) comprise 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component.
As MediShield Life covers all pre-existing conditions, all IP policyholders will also enjoy MediShield Life coverage for any pre-existing conditions, even if the private insurer has imposed an exclusion for the pre-existing condition on the additional private insurance coverage component.
If you are hospitalised for the excluded condition, you will not be able to claim for coverage under the additional private insurance component under your IP, but you will be able to claim for coverage under MediShield Life.
To find out more about your specific exclusion, please contact your financial advisor or private insurer.

questions.title: If I downgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with lower coverage or switch insurers, will I need to go through health assessment / underwriting again?
questions.text:
You do not have to go through underwriting again if you downgrade your IP to a plan with lower coverage with the same insurer. However, you will need to undergo underwriting again if you wish to switch to a new insurer, even if the new plan is of the same or lower coverage than your original plan.
Upon the inception of your new plan under your new insurer, your original plan under your original insurer will be automatically terminated. Please note that you may hence lose coverage for existing medical conditions covered by your original plan, depending on the underwriting outcome of the new insurer, and may not be able to re-apply for your original coverage later.
Regardless of any change in your IP insurer, you will remain covered by MediShield Life without any exclusions, for life.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of switching plans before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.

questions.title: Why have my Integrated Shield Plan premiums increased?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of 2 components (i) the MediShield Life component, and (ii) the additional private insurance component that provides greater coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays. The overall IP premium may be affected by both changes in the MediShield Life premiums and premiums for the additional private insurance component.
The Ministry of Health sets the premiums for the MediShield Life component, and provides subsidies to keep MediShield Life premiums affordable.
Premiums for the additional private insurance component of IPs are set, reviewed and adjusted by insurers based on commercial and actuarial considerations. Insurers may adjust premiums upwards or downwards taking into account their claims experience, medical inflation and their own product changes if any. Insurers have an incentive to keep premiums competitive, to attract and retain policyholders. Singaporeans concerned with the affordability of IP premiums may wish to consider switching to more affordable insurance options, in line with their preferences for hospitalisation coverage.

questions.title: Can we use MediSave to pay for Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and Riders?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are payable by MediSave as IPs include both a MediShield Life component and an additional, optional private insurance component that sits on top of MediShield Life. Nevertheless, the payment of IP premiums using MediSave is still subject to the MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) for the private insurance component.
MediSave savings are intended to be sufficient for basic healthcare needs. The AWLs are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.
Rider premiums are only payable in cash as they are not part of IPs or MediShield Life. In addition, a key feature of riders is to help reduce co-payment. Insufficient co-payment may increase the risk of over-consumption and over-servicing, which could in turn lead to escalation in healthcare costs and insurance premiums for all Singaporeans.

questions.title: What are the Additional Withdrawal Limits?
questions.text:
The Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) refer to the amount of MediSave Singapore Residents can use to pay for the additional private insurance coverage component of their Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums (see Diagram below for illustration).
The AWLs apply to all IPs and differ by age, as follows:
· $300 for those with age next birthday 40 and below;
· $600 for age next birthday 41 to 70; and
· $900 for age next birthday 71 and above

questions.title: How were the Additional Withdrawal Limits determined?
questions.text:
The current Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) range from $300 to $900 depending on age, with higher limits for older policyholders.
The AWLs for IP premiums are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.title: How often will the Ministry of Health (MOH) be reviewing the Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs)? Will MOH be reviewing the AWLs taking into account Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premium increases over time?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health will review the Additional Withdrawal Limits from time to time as new data and evidence emerge.
The AWLs for IP premiums are set to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.title: Did the Ministry of Health increase MediSave contribution rates due to the introduction of the Additional Withdrawal Limits?
questions.text:
Employer MediSave contribution rates for MediSave were last increased by 1% in Jan 2015. This helps to ensure that Singapore Residents can afford their MediShield Life premiums.
There were no changes to MediSave contribution rates arising from the introduction of the AWLs. MOH will monitor and review the adequacy of MediSave contributions.

questions.title: Can the Government allow us to use more of our MediSave to pay for our Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums? Why aren’t withdrawal limits sized such that IP policyholders do not experience cash outlay for their IP premiums?
questions.text:
MediSave is designed to help with basic healthcare expenses, especially after retirement. MediSave contribution rates and withdrawal limits are set in line with this principle.
MediShield Life premiums are fully payable by MediSave, while there is a limit (the Additional Withdrawal Limit) set on the premiums for the additional private insurance component to strike a balance between helping Singapore Residents pay for IPs, which are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life, and conserving enough MediSave for basic healthcare expenses, especially in old age.

questions.title: What is the Standard Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) is an IP offered by private insurers targeted at covering Ward B1 or equivalent bills in public hospitals.
As the Standard IP benefits are set by the Government and identical across all IP insurers, the Standard IP gives Singapore Residents a standardised option for additional coverage beyond MediShield Life. It is also a viable option for those who want to switch from their Class A IP and Private Hospital IP to a more affordable plan.
Similar to other IPs, the Standard IP comprises the MediShield Life component and the additional private insurance component. Premiums for the additional private insurance component are set by the private insurers.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: What are the Standard Integrated Shield Plan benefits?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) covers large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatments, with coverage targeted at the Ward B1 or equivalent level at public hospitals, and has:
- Claim limits sized to fully cover 9 out of 10 Ward B1 or equivalent bills.
- Co-payment features of claim limits, deductible and co-insurance, in line with ongoing efforts to manage healthcare costs.
For more details, you may refer to the benefit schedule of the Standard IP under “Comparison of Standard IPs (for Class B1 coverage)” at go.gov.sg/moh-compare-ip.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why does the Standard Integrated Shield Plan not provide additional benefits (e.g. pre- and post-hospitalisation)?
questions.text:
In designing the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP), it was important to balance between providing adequate coverage and ensuring premiums remain affordable.
The Standard IP was thus intended to be a “no-frills”, affordable product targeted at large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why did the Government design the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) to have claim limits, instead of as-charged coverage? Since it is not as-charged, is the Standard IP enough for Class B1?
questions.text:
The Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) was designed with claim limits to balance between providing adequate coverage and ensuring that premiums remain affordable.
In general, claim limits in insurance plans are useful to serve as protection against over-servicing, over-consumption and overcharging, which contribute to claims escalation, premium increases and rising healthcare costs in the long-run.
The Standard IP’s claim limits are sized to cover 9 out of 10 Ward B1 bills. It will therefore be sufficient for most policyholders who stay in a Class B1 ward in public hospitals. Patients can tap on MediSave to help pay for the deductible and co-insurance.
The Ministry of Health will regularly review the Standard IP benefits to ensure that they continue to provide sufficient coverage at the Ward B1 or equivalent level.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: How often will the Government review the Standard Integrated Shield Plan claim limits?
questions.text: The Ministry of Health will regularly review the Standard IP claim limits to ensure that they continue to provide sufficient coverage for Ward B1 or equivalent bills in public hospitals.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Will the Government make any future changes to the Standard Integrated Shield Plan benefits?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health will review the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits from time to time to ensure that the benefits remain relevant to policyholders.
Any changes to the Standard IP benefits will apply across all insurers.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why are the Standard Integrated Shield Plan premiums different across all the insurers, even though benefits are the same?
questions.text:
While the Ministry of Health has worked with the private insurers to standardise the Standard Integrated Shield Plan’s (IP) benefits, the plan is provided and administered by insurers, and remains a private product.
Insurance companies compete in a competitive market and the products need to remain commercially viable. As such, similar to other existing IPs, premiums and underwriting for the additional private insurance component of the Standard IP are determined by insurers based on their own commercial considerations and risk assessment frameworks. There is therefore variance in the premiums, depending on each insurer’s approach and their respective risk pools.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: I want to get the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) but my insurer’s premiums are higher than other insurers. Should I switch to a Standard IP under another insurer?
questions.text:
If you switch to a Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with another insurer, your original IP under your original insurer will be automatically terminated.
You will also need to undergo underwriting when you switch to the plan under the new insurer. As such, you may lose coverage for existing medical conditions covered by your original plan, and may not be able to re-apply for your original coverage later.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of switching insurers before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I fully pay for the Standard Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums using MediSave at all ages?
questions.text:
Based on the current Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) for MediSave use and the current Standard IP premiums across insurers (as of Apr 2024), you can use MediSave to fully pay for the Standard IP premiums until age next birthday 74.
As the Standard IP is a private product that provides additional coverage at the Ward B1 or equivalent level, premiums are higher than MediShield Life premiums. As such, there will still be some cash outlay for older policyholders.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why does the Standard Integrated Shield Plan not cover pre-existing conditions with risk-loading?
questions.text:
Similar to all other Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), the additional private insurance component of the Standard IP is provided by private insurers. Coverage under the Standard IP is therefore a business decision based on the risk assessment framework of each insurer.
Since the launch of MediShield Life, the Ministry of Health has allowed all IP insurers to introduce risk-loading options for policyholders who would like coverage for their pre-existing conditions. You may wish to check with your insurer if risk-loaded options are available for your plan.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Why can’t the Government provide and administer the Standard Integrated Shield Plan, to ensure that premiums are more affordable and to cover pre-existing conditions with risk-loading, similar to MediShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government’s focus is to provide basic and affordable health insurance coverage for all Singapore Residents through MediShield Life, regardless of their health condition.
As the Standard IP is an optional plan designed for higher coverage in Class B1 wards and is not a basic product, it is provided by private insurers. Similar to all other IPs, premiums and underwriting decisions are determined by insurers based on their own commercial considerations and risk assessment frameworks. Nevertheless, the Standard IP was designed to have standardised features to facilitate comparison of premiums by consumers. IP insurers also have the incentive to ensure that their premiums remain competitive to attract new policyholders.
The Ministry of Health will continue to review MediShield Life and the Standard IP, to ensure that they remain relevant to Singapore Residents with different needs.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: I currently have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) that covers me for Class A wards / Private Hospitals, but the premiums are getting more expensive especially as I get older. Should I switch to the Standard IP?
questions.text:
If you are concerned with being able to afford the premiums of your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) as you get older, you can consider switching to a more affordable IP, including the Standard IP. If you wish to drop your IP altogether, you will remain covered under MediShield Life.
When switching IPs, you should take into consideration factors such as your preferred ward class and affordability of premiums over the long-term. You can refer to a comparison of IP benefits and premiums at this link.
You may also wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to advise on your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: If I switch from a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan (IP) to the Standard IP with the same insurer, will I need to go through additional underwriting and will my previous exclusions remain?
questions.text:
If you are intending to switch to a plan with lower coverage within the same insurer, you will not need to go through additional underwriting.
However, any exclusions on medical conditions you had on your original Integrated Shield Plan (IP) will be retained when you switch to a new plan.
You may wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to advise on your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I get a pro-rated refund of the premiums for my original Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if I downgrade or switch from a higher coverage plan to the Standard IP before my premium renewal date?
questions.text:
If the downgrade or switch takes place before your next premium renewal date, your insurer will provide you with a pro-rated refund of your original Integrated Shield Plan premium.
Please speak to your financial advisor to find out more about the implications of downgrading or switching insurers before making your decision. Please also highlight any medical conditions you have to your financial advisor.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: Can I upgrade to a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan (IP) in future, if I buy the Standard IP now?
questions.text: When policyholders apply to upgrade to a higher coverage Integrated Shield Plan, they will need to go through another round of underwriting for the new additional coverage that they are purchasing. The insurers are allowed to assess, approve with or without exclusions and/or risk-loading, or reject applications based on their own risk assessment frameworks, as these are essentially business risk decisions.
topics: MediShield Life / Standard Integrated Shield Plans (IPs)

questions.title: What is the difference between MediShield Life and CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Both MediShield Life and CareShield Life are insurance plans, but they serve different purposes. They complement each other in providing lifetime protection against different types of healthcare expenses.
MediShield Life helps to pay for large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer. Whereas CareShield Life provides cash payouts to help severely disabled individuals with their long-term care costs.

questions.title: How do I check if I have opted in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
If you are born before 1995, you can use platform worker opt-in form to check whether you have opted in. If you have not opted in, you may use the same form to opt in.
If you are born in 1995 or later, you are in the mandatory cohort and would automatically receive CPF contributions from your platform operators. You do not need to opt in.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the new outpatient treatments that will be covered by MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life has expanded coverage to more outpatient treatments to support the shift in healthcare delivery from hospitals to outpatient and home settings.
For instance, MediShield Life will cover Outpatient Parenteral Antibiotic Therapy which enables patients to receive antibiotic treatment intravenously in the outpatient setting, thereby avoiding prolonged hospital stays.
Home Ventilation and Respiratory Support Service will also be covered to provide patients with breathing insufficiency mechanical assisted ventilation in the comfort of their own home.

questions.title: Do I need to enrol my biometrics to use BIKES if I am a Singapore resident or Long-Term Pass (LTVP/STP) holder?
questions.text:
Singapore residents (Singapore citizens and PRs) and Long-Term Pass holders i.e. LTVP, STP or Work Pass holders, need not seek enrolment as the automated clearance facility is automatically extended to them if they have already registered their biometrics identifiers with ICA or MOM.
For non-Singapore passport holders, please ensure that the passport details you have provided at the time of the biometric registration remain unchanged. If you have renewed your passport, you will need to update the details with ICA or MOM (for work pass holder).

questions.title: Do I need to enrol my biometrics to use the automated lanes if I am a Singapore resident or Long-Term Pass holder?
questions.text:
Singapore residents (i.e. Singapore citizens and PRs); and Long-Term Pass holders (i.e. LTVP, STP or Work Pass holders) need not seek enrolment as the automated clearance facility is automatically extended to them as long as you have already registered your biometrics with ICA or MOM.
For non-Singapore passport holders, please ensure that the passport details you have provided at the time of the biometrics enrolment remain unchanged. If you have renewed your passport, you will need to update the details with the relevant ICA Services Centres or MOM (for work pass holders and dependants of work pass holders).

questions.title: How can I update the name for myself/my child in Parents Gateway?
questions.text:
Please approach the school with the deed poll for changes to names.
You may use the Student Details Form (SDF) portal to update other details such as:
Email
Phone number
Home address

questions.title: How do I edit a travel declaration that has been submitted?
questions.text: If there are changes to a previously submitted travel declaration, parents need to delete the existing declaration and submit a new one.

questions.title: Can I top up my retirement savings to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
If you are aged 55 or above, you have the option to top up your Retirement Account (RA) up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) as retirement becomes an even higher priority.
If you are aged below 55, you can start building up more retirement savings by topping up your Special Account up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Once you reach age 55, you can then choose to set aside more in your RA, up to the current year’s ERS.
You can check your top-up limit on your Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I plan to top up my Retirement Account to the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum. When can I make the top-up?
questions.text:
You can make your top-up anytime from 1 January 2026 onwards, once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.
Find out how you can check the amount that you can top up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How do I transfer the monies from my CPF Investment Account to my Ordinary Account?
questions.text:
You can perform this request by:
Following the steps on DBS website
Using OCBC’s internet banking (After login, Mouse over “Investments & Insurance” menu bar, click “Retirement Portfolio” from dropdown list, then click on “Refund to CPF Board” on left menu bar)
Using UOB’s internet banking (After login, click “Investment” on left menu bar, and click “Transfer to CPF” under CPFIS-Ord A/c)
If you do nothing, your monies in your CPF Investment Account (IA) will only be refunded at the end of the second month of inactivity. You will lose up to two months of CPF interest.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Why are my investment proceeds in my CPF Investment Account not transferred to my Ordinary Account immediately?
questions.text:
Your investment returns go to your CPF Investment Account (IA) with the agent banks to facilitate quicker reinvestments in assets like shares and bonds on the Singapore Exchange. If you did not make any transactions for 2 months, your IA balance will be automatically refunded at the end of the month.
If you do not plan to reinvest, you should request your agent bank to transfer the sale proceeds from your IA back to your Ordinary Account (OA). This allows your funds to start earning CPF interest earlier of up to 3.5% per annum from the next month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How do I request a copy of my recent Home Protection Scheme medical examination results?
questions.text:
As part of the Board’s digital transformation efforts, we no longer keep hardcopy medical examination results.
Please contact the clinic where you had your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) medical examination to request a copy of your laboratory test results. The clinic may charge a fee for additional copies. For interpretation of the test results, please consult your own doctor.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can the school delete a Student's Pass (STP) application from the STP e-Service?
questions.text: Schools can delete the Student's Pass (STP) application from the STP e-Service as long as the application status is "Pending Student Submission", "Pending Local Sponsor Submission" or "Pending Attendance Declaration".

questions.title: Do I need to submit supporting documents for my Student’s Pass application if my step-parent is a Singapore citizen/ PR and my natural parent is a foreign national?
questions.text: You are required to declare and provide additional information, such as official marriage number, divorce certificate number and custody details in e-Form V103 via the Student's Pass e-Service if your parent or step-parent is a Singapore citizen/ Permanent Resident. You may be required to provide these documents when requested by ICA.

questions.title: How can Private Education Institutions proceed with the application for “Student’s Pass for Transfer School” if the student’s former school did not complete Section B of the e-Form V36A in the e-Service?
questions.text: The e-Service for Student’s Pass (STP) application will send a notification to inform the former school to complete Section B of e-Form V36A when the e-Service receives an application for “Student’s Pass for Transfer School” from an approved Private Education Institution (PEI). If there is no response from the former school within 7 days, the PEI can proceed to submit the application with explanation in the remarks column, where applicable.

questions.title: How can schools provide additional explanation or clarification to ICA for a Student's Pass (STP) application through STP e-service?
questions.text: Schools may provide supporting details, explanation or clarifications at the ‘Remarks/ Explanation column’ when completing e-Form V36A at the Student's Pass e-Service for their students.

questions.title: How will the school know if an application for Student’s Pass is submitted successfully?
questions.text: A confirmation message will appear on the screen once an application for Student’s Pass is submitted successfully via the e-Service.

questions.title: What are the circumstances for a school to submit an application on “Renew Student’s Pass/ Transfer Course (within same school)”?
questions.text: The school can submit an application for “Renew Student's Pass/ Transfer Course (within same school)” if existing/ former students of the school are continuing or starting a new course with the school within 3 months from the expiry or cancellation of their previous Student's Pass.

questions.title: What are the circumstances for a school to submit an application on “Student’s Pass for Transfer School”?
questions.text: The school can submit an application on “Student's Pass for Transfer School” for students who are changing Kindergartens/Childcare Centres or changing Approved Private Education Institutions within 3 months from the expiry or cancellation of their previous Student's Pass.

questions.title: How do I apply for a refund of Self-Help Group (SHG) contributions if I have overpaid, or made payment to a SHG incorrectly?
questions.text: If you have overpaid contributions to a Self-Help Group (SHG) or made payment to the wrong SHG (i.e. payment was intended for another SHG), please contact the respective SHG directly to request a refund.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Contributions to self-help groups

questions.title: What rules and responsibilities apply to my ex-spouse when my CPF investments are transferred to them as part of our divorce settlement?
questions.text:
When your CPF investments are transferred to your ex-spouse, the following rules and responsibilities apply:
CPF Investment Scheme Rules: The transferred investments will be subject to the CPF Investment Scheme regulations. For example:
Adherence to stock and gold limits
Types of investments allowed using CPF savings
These rules are in place to safeguard your ex-spouse's retirement adequacy.
Sale Proceeds: If your ex-spouse sells the transferred investments, the proceeds will be credited to their respective CPF accounts. These funds will be subject to CPF rules and can only be withdrawn when your ex-spouse meets the withdrawal conditions under Sections 15 or 27 of the CPF Act.
Bank Charges: Your ex-spouse will be responsible for paying any bank charges associated with the investments they continue to hold in their CPFIS-OA Investment Account. These charges can be paid using their Ordinary Account savings.
It is important for both parties to understand these implications to ensure proper management of the transferred investments and compliance with CPF rules.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: During a divorce settlement, which types of CPF investments can be transferred and which have to be sold for proceeds to be transferred as well as the procedures involved?
questions.text: Please refer to the step-by-step guide (PDF, 55KB) for the details on the sale or transfer of investments under CPF Investment Scheme - Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA) and CPF Investment Scheme - Special Account (CPFIS-SA).
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: I can see my child’s booking but I can’t make any changes to it. Why?
questions.text:
Only the parent who booked or balloted on behalf of the child can edit and manage the booking, including:
Receiving ballot result notifications via SMS and/or email
Cancelling pending ballots
Paying for a successful ballot
If your child has bookings or ballots made by another parent, you can still view your child's:
Pending ballots
Ballot results
Upcoming bookings

questions.title: I am a self-employed person / platform worker. How will the Government assess my eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
As it is not mandatory for self-employed persons to contribute to their Ordinary and Special Accounts (OA and SA), and platform workers born in 1995 or later are only required to contribute to their OA and SA from 1 January 2025, self-employed persons and platform workers would naturally have made less CPF contributions than employees.
For seniors who were self-employed or platform workers in their working years, we will consider their average annual net trade income, as determined by their annual income tax assessments, in addition to the total CPF contributions they made by the age of 55.
To qualify for the Silver Support Scheme, their average annual net trade income should not be more than $27,600 between the ages of 45 and 54. The average annual net trade income threshold was increased from $22,800 to $27,600 in 2021 to strengthen support for seniors with lesser means. The Government will review the threshold from time to time, to ensure that the Silver Support Scheme is able to reach those who need it most.

questions.title: What should I wear for my solemnisation?
questions.text: You are encouraged to wear formal attire or customary wedding outfits. T-shirts, jeans, shorts, bermudas and slippers are inappropriate for solemnisations.
topics: Muslim Marriage / Solemnisation of Muslim Marriage

questions.title: Who can be a Wali to the bride?
questions.text:
Listed in the proper hierarchy, a Wali can be the bride's biological father, or male relatives from her father's side. The hierarchy is as follows:
• Father
• Paternal Grandfather
• Full brother (same father and mother)
• Consanguine brother (same father)
• Nephew (full brother’s son)
• Nephew (consanguine brother’s son)
• Uncle (father’s full brother).
If there is none available, then the Kadi will assume the role as a Wali. Generally, a Wali must be : � A Muslim � In good health physically and mentally � Have attained the age of puberty.
*If the bride is a convert and does not have Muslim male relatives from paternal side, the bride should choose "No Wali" in her application supported by documents (conversion card from Muslim Converts Association of Singapore or conversion documents with endorsement letter from MUIS).
topics: Muslim Marriage / Wali & Witness for solemnisation

questions.title: Do I need to update the Registry of Marriages (ROM) if my spouse had passed on?
questions.text:
You do not need to update the Registry of Marriages on the change of your marital status.
However, if you are a Singaporean or Permanent Resident, you may consider updating your marital status in MyInfo for ease of transacting with government agencies. To check your current marital status, please go to your Singpass app and view under My Profile-Family. If you wish to update your marital status, please click here.
topics: Civil Marriage / After Marriage - Change of Personal Details

questions.title: Do I need to update the Registry of Marriages (ROM) after divorce or annulment?
questions.text:
You do not need to update the Registry of Marriages on the change of your marital status.
However, if you are a Singaporean or Permanent Resident, you may consider updating your marital status in MyInfo for ease of transacting with government agencies. To check your current marital status, please go to your Singpass app and view under My Profile-Family. If you wish to update your marital status, please click here.
topics: Civil Marriage / After Marriage - Divorce/Divorce proceedings

questions.title: Is my foreign spouse entitled to long-term stay in Singapore after our marriage?
questions.text:
Marriage to a Singapore Citizen does not guarantee a non-resident spouse automatic right of entry into Singapore or approval for long-term stay in Singapore.
Couples who are interested in applying for a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) are strongly encouraged to submit the Pre-Marriage LTVP Assessment (PMLA) together before marriage.
The PMLA is a free online assessment tool for couples to find out more about each other, and if your prospective non-resident spouse is likely to qualify for LTVP after marriage. For more information on PMLA, please visit www.ica.gov.sg

questions.title: After marriage, how long will it take for us to obtain Permanent Residency (PR) for my spouse?
questions.text: For queries on Citizenship or Permanent Residence, you may contact the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA).

questions.title: My partner and I are Singapore Permanent Residents. Do we need to register our marriage in Singapore and our countries of origin?
questions.text:
If you and your partner are Singapore Permanent Residents, and you intend to get married overseas, you should check with the relevant authorities in that country on the proper procedures and documents required.
If you intend to get married overseas, you are not required to submit a marriage application with the Registry of Marriages (ROM) Singapore.

questions.title: Do we need to update our marriage application prior to our Verification of documents and Declaration (V/D) appointment if my spouse-to-be’s passport has been renewed?
questions.text: If your spouse-to-be’s passport has been renewed after you have submitted your marriage application, please bring both the old and new passports to your Verification of documents and Declaration (V/D) appointment.
topics: Civil Marriage / Verification of Documents & Declaration (V/D) Appointment

questions.title: Where can I obtain the summary of application?
questions.text: You may go to 'e-Services' on the 'Our Marriage Journey' website, and click on 'Find my summary of application' under ‘Civil’.

questions.title: My NRIC reflects both my principal name and hanyu pinyin name. Which name should I enter when submitting my marriage application?
questions.text: Please enter only your principal name when submitting your marriage application.

questions.title: Can I apply for a HDB flat with my non-citizen spouse?
questions.text: For questions on application or purchase of HDB flats, you may enquire directly with the Housing and Development Board (HDB).
topics: Civil Marriage / Marriage application - Singapore citizen and a foreigner

questions.title: I have applied for the pre-marriage Long Term Visit Pass (LTVP) but it will take 4 weeks of processing time. Can I proceed to submit my marriage application?
questions.text: You may submit your marriage application via the 'Our Marriage Journey' website. However, please note that marrying a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident will not automatically grant a foreigner a long-term stay in Singapore.
topics: Civil Marriage / Marriage application - Singapore citizen and a foreigner

questions.title: How do I make online declaration? Is there a guide on digital signing that I can refer to?
questions.text: You may refer to the infographics information guide here.
topics: Civil Marriage / Online declaration (without V/D appointment)

questions.title: Can I register for marriage while on Student's Pass?
questions.text: It is the prerogative of a Student's Pass holder to decide whether he/she wants to get married in Singapore. If you are a Student's Pass holder looking to marry a Singapore Citizen, you are strongly encouraged to submit a Pre-Marriage Long-Term Visit Pass Assessment (PMLA) to find out whether you qualify for a Long-Term Visit Pass. Please visit www.ica.gov.sg for more information to register for PMLA online.
topics: Civil Marriage / Rules for getting married in Singapore

questions.title: How much are the registration fees for a Marriage Licence?
questions.text:
If either party is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident: $42
If both parties are foreigners: $380

questions.title: How to legalise my Singapore marriage certificate for overseas use?
questions.text:
To show proof of your marriage to the relevant authority overseas, you may consider applying for a digital copy of the duplicate marriage certificate and you will receive a digital extract copy via email. The overseas authority may verify the document by scanning the QR code on it.
In the event the overseas authority requires the digital copy to be legalised, you may contact the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) for assistance. For more information, you may visit SAL's website and click the tab "News & Events" for details on the process and procedures.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their hospitalisation expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them. Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. They can be of any nationality except for grandparents and siblings who must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
It is important to note that while your approved dependants can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis. If they still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after using up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
For more information, please speak to the staff at the hospital's Business Office.
You should use your MediSave prudently to provide for your own and your approved dependants’ hospitalisation needs. This is because you may require more medical care in your old age.
Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ hospitalisation expenses, you may approach the hospital where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF). The hospital will then submit the claim to us and payment from your MediSave will be made directly to the hospital.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s outpatient treatment expenses?
questions.text:
If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their outpatient treatment expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them. Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings. They can be of any nationality except for grandparents and siblings who must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
While they can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per patient basis regardless of the number of payers. If they still have outstanding medical expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ medical expenses, you may approach the Medical Institution (MI) where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF). The hospital will then submit the claim to us and payment from your MediSave will be made directly to the MI.

questions.title: How do I apply for Right of Entry (ROE) or transfer ROE?
questions.text:
You can apply for the Right of Entry (ROE) at https://go.gov.sg/rightofentry.
Please refer to ICA website for full details and eligibility criteria to apply for ROE.
topics: Singapore Citizenship Related Matters / Right of Entry (ROE)

questions.title: How do I check my Silver Support Scheme eligibility?
questions.text:
If you are eligible for Silver Support Scheme (SSS), we will send you a letter in December to inform you of next year’s eligibility.
To check your eligibility status or contact us, log in to e-services.

questions.title: Can I make a one-time authorisation to use my MediSave for my immediate family members' medical expenses in different Medical Institutions without signing a new form at each Medical Institution?
questions.text: You will need to authorise the use of your MediSave for your immediate family member's medical expenses by signing the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (Single Institution) at each Medical Institution. This is to reduce the likelihood that your MediSave is used for subsequent treatments at the same institution and/or other institutions without your knowledge.

questions.title: Can I use more than one of my immediate family member's MediSave for my hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text:
You can tap on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
While you can tap on your family member's MediSave, the amount you can use is still subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per hospitalisation episode basis regardless of the number of payers. If you still have outstanding hospitalisation expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.

questions.title: I intend to use my immediate family member's MediSave for my hospitalisation expenses. Do I need to produce any proof of my relationship with my family member?
questions.text:
You will not be required to produce documentary proof of your relationship with your family member at the point of admission. However, your family member will need to complete a Medical Claims Authorisation Form to use his/her MediSave for your hospitalisation expenses, where he/she will be asked to declare his/her relationship with you.
You and your family member may subsequently be asked to submit documentary proof of your relationship as part of an audit. Please note that legal action may be taken against any member who makes a false declaration.

questions.title: Why can't I submit the online waiver application despite meeting the waiver conditions?
questions.text:
If you meet the waiver conditions, there are two reasons that may prevent you from submitting the waiver online:
1. The student is currently in the midst of their studies.
2. The student has completed or left their studies, but the educational institution has not yet notified us of their graduation or departure status.
In both circumstances, you can proceed to waive the student's repayment through these steps:
1. Revoke the use of CPF for education via cpf.gov.sg/RevocationForm if you have no intention to continue using your CPF savings for the student's current course of study.
2. Waive the student's repayment via cpf.gov.sg/edurevowaiver.
Upon receipt of both revocation and waiver applications, we will notify you of the application statuses. Please note that the waiver will include the total CPF savings withdrawn and the interest that would have otherwise been earned had the savings not been withdrawn under the CPF Education Loan Scheme. Once approved, the waiver application is irrevocable.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Will the interest rates on savings in the Special, MediSave and Retirement Account be maintained at a floor rate?
questions.text:
To help CPF members grow their savings, the Government has decided to further extend the 4% floor rate for interest earned on all Special, MediSave and Retirement Account (SMRA) savings for another year until 31 December 2026.
SMRA savings will earn a minimum 4% interest rate per annum until 31 December 2026.
Please refer to our FAQ on how CPF interest rates are determined for more information.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates
