questions.title: If I do not have my cohort’s Basic Healthcare Sum when I reach my Payout Eligibility Age and I intend to start receiving my retirement payouts, do I need to top up my MediSave Account?
questions.text: You do not need to top up your MediSave Account (MA) to the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in order to receive your retirement payouts. The BHS is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.

questions.title: Do I need an ECDC licence to operate an enrichment centre?
questions.text:
Section 2 of Early Childhood Development preschools (ECDC) Act defines an ECDC service as “the provision of care or education, or care and education, habitually of 5 or more children who are below 7 years of age, for a fee, reward or profit by a person who is not a relative or guardian of all the children”.
You may wish to refer to “The Schedule” in the Early Childhood Development preschools Act for the types of enrichment preschools that are exempted under the Act at https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/ECDCA2017#Sc-.
Should you wish to find out more about registering for private schools, you may also refer to Ministry of Education website at https://www.moe.gov.sg/private-education/register-school.

questions.title: What legislation or requirements are preschools subjected to?
questions.text: All ECDA-licensed preschools, including infant care, child care and kindergartens have to adhere to the Early Childhood Development Centre (ECDC) Act and Regulations and Code of Practice.

questions.title: Are preschool staff required to wear face masks?
questions.text:
In line with the national posture, preschool staff are not required to wear masks. Nevertheless, those who prefer to continue wearing masks due to personal circumstances (e.g. living with vulnerable persons, individual is immuno-compromised) may do so.
To facilitate children’s learning and development, educators who prefer to wear a mask may use clear face masks during language and literacy lessons, so that the children can see the educators’ lip movements, visual cues, and facial expressions. We encourage you to share your concerns with your child’s preschool so that they can also address them directly.
topics: Centre Operations / Health, Hygiene and Safety

questions.title: Why is my child not allowed to enter the preschool when he/she only has mild symptoms?
questions.text:
Any child who is unwell or displays symptoms of infectious diseases should seek medical attention and rest at home. As children in preschools are in close proximity with each other throughout the day, and are more susceptible to falling ill, those who are unwell should remain at home to recover.
Your child should only return to the preschool after the duration indicated on the MC, and no longer shows any symptom of illness.
topics: Centre Operations / Health, Hygiene and Safety

questions.title: Does my child need to complete his/her vaccinations before enrolment into preschool?
questions.text:
All children must have received the necessary immunisation as recommended by the Ministry of Health (MOH), including vaccination against diphtheria and measles which are compulsory under the Infectious Diseases (Diphtheria and Measles Vaccination) Regulations 2021, before enrolling in a preschool. All local and foreign children must have at least 1 dose of MMR, and primary series of diphtheria (comprises of 3 doses) vaccination for enrolment. They must complete the second dose of MMR at a scheduled date specified by the medical practitioner.
For infants who have yet to reach the required age for specific immunisations, they may still be enrolled in the preschool but parents should bring them for the vaccinations as scheduled.

questions.title: Why must documents be certified as true copies by a third neutral party for educator certification applications submitted by the educator?
questions.text: For applications submitted by the centre administrator on behalf of a staff, the centre administrator is required to verify and declare online in ONE@ECDA that the documents submitted are true and correct. Therefore, for self-submission of application, we would need a third neutral party to verify the authenticity of the documents to be submitted (except for documents in OpenCerts format).

questions.title: Must centres sign and certify true copy on each page of the supporting documents for upload?
questions.text: Centres do not need to sign and certify true copy on each page, as there is an online declaration confirming that all the details furnished are true and correct.

questions.title: What is the duration of the new term of the Partner Operator (POP) scheme?
questions.text: The new term for the POP scheme will commence on 1 Jan 2026 and end on 31 Dec 2030.
topics: Anchor and Partner Operator Schemes (AOP and POP)

questions.title: What has happened to MoneyOwl?
questions.text: MoneyOwl ceased its operations in December 2023 and transferred its business to iFast, which already holds the records of all its clients.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Why are the property tax rates higher for let-out residential properties?
questions.text: Let-out or rented residential properties are considered investment assets and are taxed at a higher rate than owner-occupied properties. The tax structure ensures that higher-value properties are subject to higher tax rates.

questions.title: To give me an idea of whether the Annual Value (AV) of my property is fair, where can I find more information of the rental amount on private residential properties or HDB flats?
questions.text: You can refer to rentals of private residential properties at URA website (Rentals for Private Residential Developments) and rentals of HDB flats at HDB website (Rentals for HDB Flats).

questions.title: We have been trying hard to sell my deceased brother's residential property, but we are unable to get a buyer and the house is currently vacant. Can IRAS continue to apply the lower owner-occupier tax rates for this property?
questions.text: No. For residential properties held under deceased ownership, IRAS will extend the concessionary rates for a period of two years from date of the owner’s demise to allow some time for the property transfer/sale arrangements to be made before the non-owner-occupier residential tax rates are applied.

questions.title: My residential property is owner-occupied after completion/TOP obtained, but I have been billed for non-residential tax rates. How do I revise my tax rates?
questions.text:
If the property has obtained TOP, please let us have the following:
(a) A copy of Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP)/Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC), whichever is earlier (Please indicate if it is a direct CSC)
(b) Site area of the land plot
(c) Gross floor area of the property
(d) A copy of the constructed floor plans in A4 size (please ensure that the floor plans are clear and the wordings in the plans are of readable font size.)
IRAS will review the assessment on the new building after receiving the required information and the owner-occupier tax rates will be granted once the assessment on the new building is finalised. You may also request your architect to submit the relevant information to us directly.

questions.title: Our late brother's property was rented out prior to his passing. As the tenancy has ended, can we apply for the onwer-occupier tax rates (OOTR)?
questions.text: No. As the owner-occupier tax rates were not applied on the residential property prior to the owner’s passing (i.e. the property was rented out or vacant), the concession is not applicable, and the property will continue to be taxed at the non-owner-occupier residential tax rates. Please arrange to have the property legally transferred to the beneficiaries. IRAS will review the OOTR based on the new owner’s eligibility.

questions.title: How many days can a foreign visitor stay in Singapore?
questions.text:
If you are eligible for entry, you will receive a Visit Pass or e-Pass which will indicate the period of stay granted. The granting of visit passes to visitors is determined by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers at the point of entry.
You may refer to Visit Pass Validity Tool (for visit pass endorsement) or the e-Pass Enquiry Portal (for e-Pass issued) for more information on your stay validity. Alternatively, you will receive a Visit Pass or e-Pass through the email which you have provided when submitting the SG Arrival Card at the point of entry.
The Visit Pass or e-Pass will expire after the last day of validity or when the traveller departs Singapore.

questions.title: How and when will I be notified on my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.text:
If you have registered your contact details with CPF Board, you will receive a notification via email or SMS when your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment has been credited.
If you have registered your email address with CPF Board, you will receive the notification for the payment via the registered email. Otherwise, you will receive the notification via the mobile number you registered with the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can I withdraw my CPF savings if I have unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: If you have unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums, we may be appointed by IRAS to recover the unpaid amount from the CPF savings you are withdrawing. If we are appointed to do so, you will receive an appointment notice from IRAS and we will pay IRAS the outstanding amount from your withdrawable savings to settle your unpaid taxes or MediShield Life/CareShield Life premiums before the balance (if any) is paid to you.

questions.title: Will you inform the students if they have not been shortlisted for an interview?
questions.text: Yes. We will inform students if they are not shortlisted for an interview.

questions.title: What is the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
The Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) in 2026 is $440,800. This is the maximum amount that members aged 55 and above can top up their Retirement Accounts (RA) to in 2026. From 1 January 2026, the ERS amount is double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and provides members the option to top up more for higher payouts.
The ERS amount is not dependent on your age or the year you turn 55 years old. It increases yearly on 1 January. Here are the ERS amounts for 2026 to 2027.
Year
2026
2027
Enhanced Retirement Sum
$440,800
$456,400
You can top up more to your RA every year when the ERS increases. To illustrate, a member aged 55 and above in 2026 would be able to top up to $440,800. In 2027, when the ERS is increased to $456,400 the member will be able to top up a further $15,600 (i.e. $456,400 - $440,800).
You can top up your RA with cash or your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. Topping up your RA allows you to receive higher monthly payouts in retirement. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts through CPF top-ups. For example, a member who is 55 in the current year could receive up to $3,440 monthly for life when they turn 65. Learn more about the payouts you can receive if you top up to the ERS.
You may check the maximum amount you can top up on your Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am an employer or platform operator who made cash top-ups to my employees or platform workers’ CPF Accounts on their behalf. How do I claim corporate tax deductions?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups made to your employees or platform workers’ CPF Retirement Accounts/ Special Accounts only or MediSave Account only, on the employees or platform workers’ behalf, are tax-deductible.
You are able to claim tax deduction on the cash top-ups as part of your allowable business expenses when filing the income tax return (Form B) for self-employed person or (Form C-S/ Form C-S (Lite)/ Form C) for company.
For more information, you may refer to the IRAS website on Top-Up of Employees’ CPF Retirement Accounts/ Special Accounts/ MediSave Accounts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I received an email notification on topping up my and/or my loved ones’ retirement savings. How do I know if the notification is indeed sent by CPF Board?
questions.text:
Members will receive email notifications at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address which you have earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
To verify if the email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on has a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why is there a lifetime cap of $20,000 to the matching grant when the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is enhanced from 2025?
questions.text:
The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is targeted at seniors with lesser means and lower retirement savings to help them save more for retirement. The enhancements to provide $2,000 matching grant annually, capped at $20,000 over a lifetime, are a significant increase from the current scheme, and can increase eligible members’ CPF savings by at least $48,000 in 10 years, which translates to about a $260 increase in monthly CPF payouts*.
While it may not help all eligible seniors meet the Basic Retirement Sum, it is part of a broader set of schemes providing retirement adequacy support. Other schemes, such as the Majulah Package and the Silver Support Scheme, will also help boost the retirement adequacy of seniors.
*Estimation for a male member who starts payout at age 65 on the CPF LIFE Standard Plan.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if I am below 55 years old?
questions.text:
The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) helps boost the retirement payouts of older Singaporean Citizens aged 55 and above with lower retirement savings, who have a shorter runway to build up more retirement savings. MRSS is extended to them to help accumulate retirement savings.
For those who are younger and have a longer runway to build their retirement savings, the Government provides various other support. These include the Workfare Income Supplement, which supplements the income and retirement savings of lower-wage workers, and the Retirement Sum Topping-Up scheme (RSTU), which provide tax relief on cash top-ups. These schemes boost retirement savings, allowing members to benefit from compounding interest and higher monthly payouts in retirement.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why is there an annual cap of $2,000 of matching grant. Would the Government consider allowing eligible members to top up $20,000 at once and receive the lifetime matching grant of $20,000?
questions.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is targeted at Singaporeans with lower retirement savings to help them save more for retirement. As member’s circumstances such as income and housing can change over time, the annual cap ensures that the scheme will help seniors who require the support over a longer period.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Can I make the top-up by cash or NETS under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
No, you can use PayNow or GIRO instead to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ Retirement or Special Account.
For PayNow, your cash top-up will generally be credited almost instantly upon successful payment.
Consider making regular monthly or yearly cash top-ups conveniently via GIRO, without the hassle of completing the application form every time you top up.
You may refer to this FAQ “How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme" for the guide on how to top up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How do I change or delete my recurring cash top-up arrangement to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
If you want to change your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement such as the amount and frequency, you can follow the steps below:
Delete your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement in the Manage recurring cash top-ups for retirement form.
Create a new recurring arrangement via the same form with your revised amount and/or frequency of the top-ups.
If you want to delete your existing recurring cash top-up arrangement, you can do so via the Manage recurring cash top-ups for retirement form. Your application will generally be processed instantly upon submission.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring cash top-up arrangements for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring cash top-up arrangements, including the recipients, amount of cash top-ups, and frequency (monthly or yearly) by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Will I still receive the full matching grant of $2,000 if my retirement savings exceed the current Basic Retirement Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the full matching grant of $2,000 as long as you are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for the year, and the total amount of cash top-ups you received was at least $2,000.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I received Matched Retirement Savings Scheme matching grants in the past, before the $20,000 lifetime cap took effect in 2025. Will the past matching grants count towards this $20,000 lifetime cap?
questions.text: The lifetime cap will only be applied from 2025 onwards. Matching grants received in the past for cash top-ups made prior to 2025, will not count towards the $20,000 lifetime cap.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How do I check the amount of matching grant that I will receive?
questions.text:
To find out the grant amount that you will receive at the beginning of the next year on the cash top-ups which you had received, you can log in to your Retirement Dashboard.
In addition, the Dashboard will provide you with the remaining grant amount, if any, which you can receive if you make further top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including yourself, loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help members who are eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to receive the matching grant by making cash top-ups to their Retirement or Special Account.
Learn more on how to make a cash top-up.
You may refer to this FAQ for more information on how to check your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I missed the deadline to top up for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme grant last year. Can I make a top-up this year for last year's grant?
questions.text:
No, to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) grant, the PayNow cash top-up must be made by 31 December or the cash top-up via GIRO must be submitted by 31 October in the year of eligibility. This is stated in the eligibility notification sent at the beginning of the year of eligibility, and on the website.
You can still make a top-up to earn interest rates* of up to 6% per annum and boost your monthly payouts. You can also enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups made to yourself and your loved ones in each calendar year. Please note that cash top-ups which attract MRSS grant will not qualify for tax relief.
*Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How do I read my Digital Yearly Statement of Account?
questions.text:
You can view the guide on the Digital Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) in your preferred language below:

questions.title: If a residential property in Singapore is purchased under a trust with a US citizen beneficiary, will the trust be eligible for the full 65% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission, assuming all other remission conditions are met?
questions.text:
Under the Free Trade Agreement ABSD Remission, US citizen beneficiaries receive the same stamp duty treatment as Singapore citizens. Therefore, if this is the beneficiary's only residential property, the full 65% ABSD will be remitted, provided that all other remission conditions are met.
Information is available on Remission of ABSD (Trust).
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is re-stamping required when adding a new tenant to an already stamped lease agreement?
questions.text: Stamp duty is a tax on documents (physical or electronic). Fresh stamping is required if a new tenancy agreement is executed to include the new tenant.

questions.title: After my HDB flat's buyer has exercised the Option to Purchase (OTP), will I still incur Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) when purchasing a private condo?
questions.text:
A property is considered acquired by the buyer and sold by the seller when the option to purchase, or sale and purchase agreement is executed, even if the sale has yet to be legally completed or if the property is not completed at the time of purchase.
ABSD liability depends on the buyer's profile and number of residential properties owned at purchase. Assuming you are a Singapore Citizen, ABSD is not payable if the option to purchase for the sale of your HDB flat is executed before the purchase of your private condo and you do not own any other residential properties.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: For a married couple (a Singapore Citizen and a Singapore Permanent Resident) currently owning a 4-room HDB flat, will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable if they purchase a 5-room HDB flat in the near future?
questions.text:
ABSD will be fully remitted under the HDB Acquisition Remission.
For more information on this remission, please refer to the IRAS website: Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Do we need to pay Additional Buyer's Stamp (ABSD) when buying our first home in Singapore if I'm a Singapore PR and my wife is a US citizen?
questions.text:
For purchases made jointly by two or more buyers of different profiles, the highest applicable ABSD rate will apply on the entire value of the property purchased.
However, under the Free Trade Agreement ABSD Remission, US citizens will be accorded the same stamp duty treatment as Singapore Citizens.
As such, ABSD Remission for a Married Couple will apply for joint purchase of your first matrimonial house.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission available for engaged couples purchasing a resale HDB flat under the Fiancé/Fiancée Scheme?
questions.text:
ABSD liability is determined by the buyers' profiles and the number of residential properties owned at the time of purchase.
For joint purchases of HDB flats (both BTO and resale):
1. Full ABSD remission is granted if at least one of the joint purchasers is a Singapore Citizen, under the Acquisition of HDB Flats and New Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission.
2. For joint purchases by Singapore Permanent Residents and Foreigners, ABSD remission is not applicable. The highest applicable ABSD rate will be imposed in such cases.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Do I need to pay Additional Buyer's Stamp (ABSD) upfront when buying a smaller private property if I'm over 55, currently own one private property, and plan to sell it within 6 months of the new purchase?
questions.text:
ABSD liability depends on the buyer's profile and number of residential properties owned at the point of purchase. As you currently own one private property, ABSD will be payable upfront when you purchase the second private property.
However, Single Singapore Citizens aged 55 years and above may be eligible for a refund under the ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen (SC) Seniors Remission, provided all remission conditions are met.
One of the eligibility conditions for ABSD refund is that the value of the second residential property is less than the value of the first residential property sold.
Do ensure that all conditions are met before applying for a refund under this remission.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: As a Singapore PR marrying a Singaporean, can we get Additional Buyer's Stamp (ABSD) remission on our first jointly bought private property if we marry within 6 months of purchase?
questions.text:
For purchases involving two or more buyers with different profiles, the higher applicable ABSD rate will apply.
ABSD Remission for a Married Couple is not applicable for joint purchases made before marriage.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Will Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable if an individual or a company inherits a residential property (HDB or private), especially when the beneficiary already owns one or more residential properties?
questions.text: Stamp duty is not payable for properties acquired by way of assent to the beneficiaries (whether an individual or an entity) in accordance to the Deceased's Will, Intestate Succession Act or Muslim Law of Inheritance.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If the seller and I mutually agree to cancel the property transaction before the completion of sale, am I eligible to request for stamp duty refund?
questions.text:
BSD, ABSD and SSD remission in excess of $50 is applicable to rescinded or aborted sale and purchase agreements if the remission conditions are met under Aborted Sale and Purchase Agreements Remission.
If you meet all the remission conditions, you may submit a refund application via the e-Stamping Portal as follows:
1. Proceed to myTax Portal.
2. Click on "Stamp Duty".
3. Log in "Individual User/Business User".
4. Select "Request" > "Apply for Refund".
Refund application is generally processed within 30 days.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: How do I make amendments to the stamping record?
questions.text:
The stamping information should reflect the details as per the dutiable document. If you need to revise or amend the stamping information due to a typographical error, please submit an amendment request via the e-Stamping Portal by selecting "Request > Revise/Amend Stamping Record".
If the amendment relates to the starting date of a tenancy period, please submit your amendment request via the e-Stamping Portal inbox:
1. Go to "Inbox" > "Compose Mail".
2. Include a copy of the tenancy agreement with your request.

questions.title: Is additional stamp duty required if the rent is increased after the initial stamp duty was paid on the original tenancy agreement?
questions.text:
Yes, additional stamp duty is payable on the document that was executed to affect the rent increase, even if stamp duty was previously paid on the original lease agreement.
You can stamp the variation of the lease via the e-Stamping Portal:
1. Go to "Stamping".
2. Select "Lease/Tenancy".
3. Under Nature of Transaction, select "Variation of Lease".

questions.title: Can a Singapore Citizen married couple claim an Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) refund if they sell their jointly owned HDB flat before their newly purchased condominium receives its Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) or Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC)?
questions.text: ABSD refund may be applicable under the ABSD Remission for Married Couple, if the HDB flat is sold before the TOP/CSC of their jointly purchased condo if all other conditions of the remission are met. ABSD will be automatically refunded within 6 weeks from the stamping of the sale of their first property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: When does Stamp Duty liability arise for a lease agreement, and can it be paid before the contracting parties have signed?
questions.text:
Stamping can be done before the document is executed.
However, if the lease agreement has been executed, it has to be stamped within the following timeframes:
1. Within 14 days after signing the document if it is signed in Singapore, or
2. Within 30 days after receiving the document in Singapore if it is signed overseas.
If the contracting parties signed on different dates, the stipulated timeline will be from the date the date of first signing.

questions.title: Will a Singapore Citizen purchasing an HDB flat jointly with a spouse who is either a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) or a Foreigner incur Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)?
questions.text:
ABSD is fully remitted under the Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission, if any of the joint acquirers/ purchasers is a Singapore Citizen.
1. Remission is granted automatically upon approval of the acquisition by HDB.
2. Remission is not applicable for Resale EC.
Therefore, ABSD is not payable for the joint purchase of a Singapore Citizen and a SPR/Foreigner.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: A Singapore Citizen who owns an HDB flat wishes to purchase a private condominium. Will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable if the HDB flat is sold upon the condominium's Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) or Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC) issuance?
questions.text:
ABSD liability is determined by the buyer's profile and the number of residential properties owned at the time of purchase.
As the individual still owns an HDB flat when purchasing the private condominium, ABSD will be payable at the time of purchase. There will be no refund of ABSD even if the HDB flat is sold after the purchase of the condominium, upon issuance of the TOP or CSC.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If stamp duty has been paid on a tenancy agreement for the whole property, is stamping still required when subleasing one of the rooms?
questions.text:
Stamp duty is a tax on documents (physical or electronic) relating to immovable properties, stocks, and shares.
Therefore, if there is an agreement to sublease the room, stamping will be required for the document, and lease duty is payable.
Lease duty is computed based on the contractual rent or market rent, whichever is higher, at a rate of 0.4%.

questions.title: If the landlord lowers the monthly rent, can I claim refund on the stamp duty paid on my tenancy agreement.
questions.text:
Lease duty is computed based on the contractual rent or market rent, whichever is higher, at a rate of 0.4%.
The lease duty paid will not be refunded in the event the monthly rent was lowered.

questions.title: Is stamping required and stamp duty payable when a new tenant takes over the remaining lease period from an outgoing tenant, with a 1.5-month extension but no consideration paid.
questions.text:
Stamping is not required, and stamp duty is not payable if there is a Novation agreement, provided that:
1. The incoming tenant takes over the remaining lease period from the outgoing tenant, with no change in the lease terms and monthly rent
2. There is no consideration between the parties.
However, as there is an extension of lease, stamping will be required on the novation agreement and stamp duty is payable.

questions.title: For a 36-month lease agreement that includes a one-month rent-free period, should the stamp duty calculation be based on 35 or 36 months?
questions.text: Stamp duty on leases is calculated based on the higher of contractual or market rental for the full lease term, including rent-free periods. Therefore, for a 36-month lease with a rent-free month, stamp duty is computed on the full 36 months.

questions.title: My spouse and I, both Singapore Citizens, purchased an HDB flat in which I am registered as an occupier. If I acquire a private property, will this purchase be counted as my second residential property and will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable?
questions.text:
Occupiers of HDB flats are not considered beneficial owners of the flat; they are merely authorized by HDB to live there.
As a result, the HDB flat will not be counted as part of your property ownership for ABSD purposes. Therefore, ABSD will not be payable on the purchase of the private property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) couple jointly owns a private condominium unit and has already paid Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) upon the initial purchase, is ABSD payable again when one party sells/transfers their share to the other party?
questions.text:
Generally, when an individual acquires any interest in a property, it counts as an additional property for ABSD purposes.
However, if an individual acquires additional interest in a property, they already co-own, the "Transfer of Interest in Property which Buyer has Interest" rule may apply.
Under this provision, the ABSD rate is calculated based on the existing property count, rather than treating the transfer as a new property acquisition.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is re-stamping required when a new tenant replaces the original tenant, with all other terms, conditions, and rent remaining unchanged?
questions.text: If a new tenancy agreement is executed for the change of tenant, stamping is required, and stamp duty is payable on the document, even if the terms, conditions, and rent remain unchanged from the original tenancy.

questions.title: As a platform worker, if I make a top-up to my three CPF accounts, how will my top-up be allocated to the respective accounts?
questions.text: As a platform worker, your top-up will be allocated to your Ordinary, Special/Retirement and MediSave account according to this allocation table.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the increase in platform workers’ share of CPF Ordinary and Special or Retirement Account contribution rates, which is used to compute Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)?
questions.text:
From 2025 to 2028, platform workers’ own share of CPF contributions rates will increase by up to 2.5%-points each year, until it reaches up to 20% in 2029, to align with employees. This applies to platform workers born in or after 1995, or born before 1995 and opted in to increased CPF contributions (see illustration for example).
Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) will offset a percentage of this year-on-year increase of up to 2.5%-points in contribution rate. The offset percentage will taper down from 2025 to 2028. In 2029, when platform workers’ CPF contributions are completely aligned with that of employees, PCTS will cease.
*Infographic shows CPF contribution rates for platform workers in the “35 & below” age group, with net earnings above $750 in a month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: What are the available payment modes for CPF contributions as a platform operator?
questions.text:
Payments for CPF contributions as a platform operator can be made using any of the modes listed below. Please note that CPF contribution details must be submitted together with payments for CPF contributions.
Direct Debit (Recommended)
PayNow QR (supports personal or corporate bank account of participating banks)
Find out more on these payment modes available to you. If your bank is not an eGIRO or a PayNow participating bank, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: What are the benefits of using Direct Debit to pay for my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
You will enjoy the following benefits if you pay CPF contributions via Direct Debit:
You do not need to provide your payment details each time you pay CPF contributions.
You may set the payment deduction date when you submit your CPF contribution details.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: How do I update CPF Board of changes to my platform company’s particulars?
questions.text:
Write to us to update your platform company’s particulars (e.g. principal place of business, contact details, name of platform company).
The normal processing time is within three working days. An email notification will be sent to both the platform operator representative and the persons in charge of CPF contribution matters for platform workers once the particulars have been updated.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Updating platform operator’s particulars

questions.title: What is CPF EZPay File Transfer Protocol?
questions.text:
The CPF EZPay File Transfer Protocol (FTP) enables platform operators to prepare CPF submission details offline, and only log in to CPF EZPay when platform operators are ready to make the submission.
The file should be prepared according to these specifications. The file size for uploading is limited to 2 mega bytes and the file extension should end with "dtl", ".txt" or ".dat". If you require assistance to clarify or verify the file you have prepared, you can write-to-us.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How should I submit CPF contributions using CPF EZPay as a platform operator?
questions.text:
To submit CPF contributions using CPF EZPay (FTP), you should:
Select CPF EZPay.
Select “For UEN-registered entities” and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
Select “CPF EZPay (FTP)”.
Upload your FTP file and click on “Direct Debit” under the payment method.
As a platform operator, you will need to make a separate submission for each of your CPF Submission Numbers (CSNs) .
To find out more about how to use CPF EZPay (FTP), you may refer to the CPF EZPay User Guide for platform operators.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I use CPF EZPay as I have more than one CPF Submission Number (CSN) as a platform operator?
questions.text:

questions.title: Can I use the same CPF EZPay (FTP) file format that I currently use for my employees to make contributions for my platform workers?
questions.text: No. You will need to use the CPF EZPay (FTP) file format for platform workers to make contributions for your platform workers.

questions.title: What are Advice Codes and how do I, as a platform operator, use them when I upload my submission file via CPF EZPay (FTP)?
questions.text:
If you are submitting more than one file within the same day for the same CPF Submission Number (CSN), you will need to assign a different Advice Code for each file. Advice Codes act as a file numbering system to differentiate files created for different groups of platform workers belonging to the same CSN.
To know more about CPF EZPay (FTP), you can refer to our user guide.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: Which code should I use for the employment status field in my CPF EZPay FTP file submission?
questions.text: Employment status N is to be used for platform operators making CPF contributions to the platform worker for the first time. This is regardless of which platform operator CPF Submission Number is used. If not, employment status E is to be used.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I make ad hoc CPF submissions for my platform workers?
questions.text:
You can make ad hoc CPF submissions into your platform workers’ CPF accounts through CPF EZPay.
CPF EZPay
You can submit CPF contributions via CPF EZPay and select Submit ad hoc CPF payments option. Then, select the correct Month and Year for your ad hoc payments. Auto-computation is not available for this option. However, you can load platform worker details from submissions made up to six months ago.
Here’s how to use the Submit ad hoc CPF payments option in CPF EZPay:
Select CPF EZPay
Select “For UEN-registered entities” and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Submit Contribution, select CPF EZPay.
Key in the Month and Year.
Select Submit ad hoc CPF payments (For one-time CPF submission (no auto-computation), or other ad hoc payments e.g. late payment interest).
Enter the contribution details for the affected platform worker.
After completing all of the contribution details and the summary portion, click on Continue.
Confirm submission by clicking on your pre-arranged payment mode with the Board (Direct Debit/PayNow QR).
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How should I indicate contributions details for platform workers when making ad hoc CPF submissions?
questions.text:
When submitting CPF contributions for platform workers using CPF EZPay, you should:
Input platform workers’ net earnings (after FEDA) in the “Ordinary Wages” field.
Leave the “Additional Wages” blank as these do not apply to platform workers.
Input the total CPF contributions payable.
For details, please refer to CPF EZPay user guide for platform operators.

questions.title: How do I know if I have completed my CPF submission?
questions.text:
Once you have completed your submission, you will see an acknowledgement page called “CPF EZPay Acknowledgment”. You can view or save this page by clicking on the printer icon which you will be prompted to download a PDF. You will not be able to save or print this acknowledgment page if you closed your internet browser.
You will also receive an email acknowledgement if your email address is registered in 'Account settings'.

questions.title: How do I check the status of my submission? What do the different Submission Statuses under the View / Amend / Delete Submission screen mean?

Please refer to the chart below for the different submission status.
Submission StatusWhat it Means
DraftThis submission is incomplete and CPF has not received your submission yet.
SubmittedThis submission will be processed after 5.15pm daily. Therefore, if there are any errors in the submission, you may amend or delete your submission before it is processed.

questions.title: How can I view my submission history in CPF EZPay as a platform operator?

Select “For UEN-registered entities” and login with your Singpass.
Key in your CPF Submission Number (CSN).
At Manage Records & Preferences, select “View / Amend / Delete Submission”.

questions.title: If I have already made payment, can I amend or delete my submission as a platform operator?
questions.text:
If you are making payment via:
Direct Debit
1. Submission status shows “Submitted”
CPF EZPay (FTP)
You can login to CPF EZPay View / Amend / Delete Submission to delete your submission. Do remember to re-submit your CPF contributions after you have deleted your submission to avoid incurring late payment interest.
CPF EZPay
You can login to CPF EZPay View / Amend / Delete Submission to amend or delete your submission. You can change CPF contribution amounts for platform workers, delete platform worker, or amend other payment amounts e.g. CPF Late Payment Interest.
However, you will not be able to amend or update platform worker’s information such as name or NRIC. If you wish to change them, please delete the current submission and create a new submission instead.
Do remember to re-submit your CPF contributions after you have amended or deleted your submission. Any amended submission will remain in draft mode and will not be sent for direct debit deduction until it has been re-submitted.
All CPF submissions are processed at 5:15pm on the same day, after which the submission status will be updated to "Processed". You can no longer amend or delete the submission after it has been processed. For submissions made after 5:15pm, you can amend or delete the submission before 5:15pm the next day.
2. Submission status shows “Processed”
You can no longer amend or delete the submission as your submission has been processed. All CPF submissions are processed at 5:15pm on the same day, after which the submission status will be updated to "Processed".
If you have underpaid CPF contributions, you may pay the difference using a Submit ad hoc CPF payments in CPF EZPay for the affected platform worker(s) in the affected month(s). You should key in the CPF shortfall amount you wish to pay but still declare the full wages earned for the month.
If you have overpaid the CPF contributions or paid for the wrong platform worker(s), you may apply for a refund immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment, subject to the availability of funds in the member's CPF account.
PayNow QR
You can no longer make amendments to the submission after proceeding to the payment page with the generated QR code.
If you have underpaid CPF contributions, you may pay the difference using Submit ad hoc CPF payments CPF EZPay for the affected platform worker(s) in the affected month(s). Declare the net earnings earned for the month and the CPF shortfall amount.
If you have overpaid the CPF contributions or paid for the wrong platform worker(s), you may apply for a refund immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment, subject to the availability of funds in the platform worker's CPF account.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: The platform worker’s name I submitted is different from the name in his/her NRIC, what should I do?
questions.text:
CPF contributions will be credited to platform workers’ CPF accounts based on the NRIC provided in the CPF submission.
If you have paid CPF contributions to the intended platform worker
Please remember to update your platform worker’s name as shown in his/her NRIC in your next CPF submission.
Kindly note that only the platform worker’s principal name is required, there is no need to include variants such as hanyu pinyin and aliases.
If you have paid CPF contributions to the wrong platform worker
Please submit request for refund or adjustment of CPF contributions immediately.

questions.title: I have made duplicate CPF submissions for the same month in error. Can I request refund of the payment made for the incorrect submission?

questions.title: How do I calculate the total excess CPF contributions which I can apply for a refund, and what is the portion of excess CPF contributions which I need to refund to my platform workers?
questions.text:
If you have made CPF contributions on net earnings in excess of the CPF annual earnings ceiling of $102,000, you should apply for a refund on your excess CPF contributions.
You can use the applicable platform worker CPF contribution rate to determine how much CPF contributions to refund to your platform workers.
If your platform worker is born before 1995, and did not opt in for increased CPF contributions, any excess CPF contributions should be fully refunded to your platform worker, since you would not have made any platform operator share of CPF contributions. Otherwise, if your platform workers are born in or after 1995, or born before 1995 and have opted in to increased CPF contributions, you would need to compute the share of excess CPF contributions to be refunded to your platform worker.
For example, for a platform worker aged 31 years old in 2025 and has received CPF contributions on net earnings of $140,000 in 2025, the steps to compute the excess CPF contributions, and the amount to refund to the platform worker are as follows:
Step 1: Total excess CPF contributions to apply be refunded
= (Total net earnings on which CPF contributions were paid – CPF annual earnings ceiling) x applicable total contribution rate
= ($140,000 – $102,000) x 14%
= $5,320
Step 2: Platform worker’s share to be refunded
= (Total excess CPF contributions refunded ÷ applicable total CPF contribution rate) x applicable platform worker CPF contribution rate
= ($5,320 ÷ 14%) x 10.5%
= $3,990* (cents should be dropped)
You are required to refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions, if any, directly to the platform worker.
*You can also verify the platform worker’s share of refund by computing the difference between the total platform worker’s share of contributions paid and platform worker's share of contributions payable. The platform worker’s share of contributions payable can be computed using the platform worker CPF contribution calculator.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: When am I required to refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text: You are required to refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions to the platform worker once you receive the refund from the CPF Board.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I refund the platform worker’s share of excess CPF contributions if the platform worker has stopped working with the platform?
questions.text: You may wish to liaise directly with the ex-platform worker on his/her preferred mode of payment for his/her share of excess CPF contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount refunded for excess CPF contributions less than the total excess CPF contributions made to the platform worker for the year?
questions.text: The refunded amount for excess CPF contributions is based on the available balances in your platform worker’s CPF account(s). If there are insufficient funds for the full refund, you will receive a partial refund instead.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I overpaid the late payment interest. Must I apply for a refund of the excess amount?
questions.text:
CPF Board will automatically refund the excess late payment interest to:
Your bank account maintained with the Board if you have an existing Direct Debit arrangement with the Board; OR
Your Corporate PayNow bank account.
You will receive a letter informing you of the outcome of the refund.
