Employer - Platform Operator / Adjustment/Refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: When is the due date to submit CPF contributions?
questions.text: The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken if CPF contributions are not paid by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: How does CPF Board calculate interest on late payment?
questions.text:
The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action will be taken if CPF contributions are not paid by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date. The minimum interest payable is $5.
Example
XYZ Company made a CPF contribution of $3,000 for the month of October on 20 November. This payment is late by 19 days. Therefore, the amount of late payment interest will be:
= $3,000 x 1.5% x 19/30 (stop at the fourth decimal)*
= $28.50
*Number of days the payment is late/number of days in the month.
The final figure is to be rounded down to the nearest dollar, i.e. the cents should be dropped for the interest. Hence, the late payment interest payable will be $28.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance
Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Why is composition amount imposed on employers or platform operators?
questions.text:
It is an offence under the CPF Act for late and/or non-payment of CPF contributions and late payment interest. The composition amount is offered to allow defaulting employers or platform operators to settle their CPF offences out of court, after settling the CPF arrears.
Prosecution actions will be taken against employers or platform operators who do not settle the CPF arrears and compound the offence out of court, before the deadline given.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance
Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: My platform worker owes me money. Can I use the amount owed to me to offset the platform operator's share of CPF contributions that is payable on his net earnings?
questions.text: You are required to pay both the platform operator and platform worker’s share of CPF contributions based on the monthly net earnings payable to your platform worker at the prevailing CPF contribution rates.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Can I agree to my platform worker’s request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay?
questions.text: You should not agree to your platform worker’s request not to be paid CPF contributions so that he can get higher take-home pay. Failure to pay CPF contributions to a platform worker (i.e. Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is providing ride-hail or delivery services under a platform work agreement) is an offence under the CPF Act.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: What should I do if I am unable to pay my platform workers their CPF contributions on time?
questions.text:
It is the platform operator’s obligation to ensure that CPF contributions are paid on time. Your platform workers have the right to check with you on the non-payment of their CPF contributions, including asking for an explanation and when you will be making payment. CPF contributions are important to platform workers for their housing, healthcare and retirement needs. Information on the payment date and amount of CPF contributions will help them to manage their financial needs and commitments.
If you are unable to pay your platform workers their CPF contributions on time, you have to ensure that the CPF arrears are paid as soon as possible and that the CPF contributions are accorded priority amongst the company’s outstanding payments. You should also inform your platform workers beforehand the reasons for being late and when they can expect the payment.
CPF Board takes a serious view of platform operators who default on CPF contributions. The due date for CPF contributions is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken against platform operators who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: How do I recover the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
As a platform operator, you need to pay both the platform operator’s and platform worker’s share of CPF contributions to CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions when paying your platform worker’s earnings for the month. For example, the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions for January can only be deducted from the platform worker’s earnings in January.
It is a serious offence to recover or attempt to recover any amount more than what is allowed from your platform workers’ earnings.
If you failed to recover the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions due to your error (e.g. system glitch, omission of CPF contributions due to platform operator’s oversight, wrong computation of platform worker’s share) before paying your platform worker’s earnings for the month, you cannot recover the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions from subsequent months’ earnings.
However, if the failure to do so was not due to your error, you must do the following before you can recover the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions from earnings payable by you to your platform worker:
You have paid the CPF contributions to the Board, and
You have either forwarded your platform worker’s written consent to CPF Board, or obtained CPF Board’s written permission on the matter.
This must be done within six months from the time the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions should have been recovered.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: If I am 55 and would like to make a CPF transfer to my loved ones, in what order will my savings be transferred?
questions.text:
If you are 55 or above, your CPF savings will be transferred to your loved ones in the following order:
OA
RA*
*If you use your RA savings for the transfer, you may no longer have enough savings to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). In that case, the next time you apply for a withdrawal from your OA, a portion or all of the savings will be used to meet your FRS in the RA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: If there are adjustments under CPF Investment Scheme in my Ordinary, Special or Retirement Account, what interest rate will be used?
questions.text: Any adjustments under the CPF Investment Scheme in your Ordinary, Special or Retirement Account will be based on the CPF interest rates for the respective account. The interest rate will not include the extra 1% interest that is paid on the first $60,000 of your combined balances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I receive notification in advance about my Ordinary Account savings being annuitised and streamed out as higher monthly CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text: If you are among those whose Ordinary Account savings will be annuitised, we will send you a notification about one month before the annuitisation.

questions.title: Why is there a need to annuitise the non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings as CPF LIFE monthly payout?
questions.text:
If you have not met your Full Retirement Sum, your Ordinary Account (OA) savings may not be withdrawn as a lump sum and are meant to be streamed out as monthly payouts.
Currently, if you are an existing CPF LIFE member, you need to instruct us to annuitise your OA savings to receive higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
With the changes from October 2023, we will automate this process and make it easier for you to enjoy higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.

questions.title: How will the annuitisation of the non-withdrawable Ordinary Account (OA) savings as CPF LIFE monthly payout affect my eligibility to withdraw or service the housing commitments that are financed by my OA savings?
questions.text:
Your eligibility to make lump sum withdrawals from your Ordinary Account (OA) will not be affected. This is because only the OA savings that cannot be withdrawn in a lump sum will be annuitised to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
The purpose of your CPF savings is to provide you with a stream of retirement income. If you still have housing obligations after starting your monthly payouts, you can use your monthly payouts or monies in excess of your Full Retirement Sum after this transfer to meet your housing needs.

questions.title: How much will my CPF LIFE monthly payouts increase after my non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are annuitised?
questions.text: After your non-withdrawable Ordinary Account savings are successfully annuitised, we will send you a notification to inform you of the revised CPF LIFE monthly payout.

questions.title: I do not wish to wait for the next automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account. Can I perform the transfer manually and boost my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
Yes, you can. Here are the steps to perform the transfer of your non-withdrawable monies from your Ordinary Account (OA) to your Retirement Account:
1) Access the Plan my monthly payouts service.
2) Under ‘Use more CPF savings to increase payouts’ in the second page, select the OA amount to be transferred to increase your CPF LIFE payout.
You may perform the above any time, as long as you have monies in your OA.

questions.title: How will I be eligible for the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account?
questions.text: To be eligible for the automatic transfer, your non-withdrawable monies in your Ordinary Account must be sufficient to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts by at least $10.

questions.title: When will the automatic transfer of non-withdrawable monies from my Ordinary Account to my Retirement Account take place?
questions.text: For members who are eligible, the automatic transfer will take place once a year. You will receive a notification one month before the transfer occurs.

questions.title: I was a foreigner who was on CPF LIFE. What happened to my CPF LIFE plan?
questions.text:
The purpose of the CPF system is to help Singapore Citizens (SC) and Permanent Residents (PR) retire with peace of mind. In line with this, CPF members who are not SC or PR will have to close their CPF accounts and their participation in CPF schemes such as CPF LIFE will cease.
Find out more about closing your CPF accounts.

questions.title: Can I choose to retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of automatically disbursing them as payouts when my Retirement Account is depleted?
questions.text:
No, you cannot choose to retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. CPF is designed to provide you with an income in retirement. The auto-disbursement of your OA savings ensures that you continue to receive a steady stream of retirement income even when your Retirement Account has been depleted.
With the monthly payouts, you also have greater flexibility for your daily living expenses or your monthly housing instalments (if applicable).
If you wish to retain the monies in your CPF accounts to earn higher interest, you should consider options outside of CPF.

questions.title: How can I extend my stay upon the expiry of my STP (e.g. waiting for my exam results, etc.)?
questions.text:
You are required to cancel your Student's Pass (STP), and surrender any physical STP card that was issued to you for cancellation, within 7 days of the cessation of, or termination of your studies.
Upon STP cancellation, you may be granted a visit pass to remain in Singapore. You may apply for an extension of visit pass if you require a longer stay. The grant of short-term visit pass is subjected to approval.
You may wish to apply for a new Student’s Pass through your school should you wish to continue your studies in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I continue to use my CPF savings for the property or withdraw my Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in cash after discharging the CPF charge?
questions.text: No, after the CPF charge is discharged, no further CPF savings can be used for the property. If you are above 55, the property cannot be pledged for the withdrawal of your Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum. If you wish to do so, a new CPF charge is required, and legal costs will be incurred in the creation and lodgement of the new CPF charge.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: How do I discharge my CPF charge after making a full voluntary housing refund?
questions.text:
If you are not selling your property, there is no need to discharge the CPF charge. If you do sell the property in the future, your lawyers will complete the discharge of CPF charge as part of the sale transaction.
However, if you would still like to discharge the CPF charge, please engage a lawyer to assist you with the discharge process. The lawyer will assist you with the legal documents required by Singapore Land Authority (SLA) and any conveyancing matters involved in the discharge process.
The CPF charge was lodged with the SLA by your lawyer when you first withdrew your CPF towards your property. Similarly, the discharge of this charge, requires careful legal documentation and lodgement of documents with SLA. Legal costs will be incurred in this process.
For queries on the discharge process, which is a legal conveyancing procedure, please contact Ministry of Law or a law firm of your choice.
Important considerations after discharge
Once the CPF charge is discharged, no further CPF transactions can be made for the property. This means you cannot:
use CPF savings for the property
make voluntary housing refunds to your CPF account for this property
pledge the property for withdrawing Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum if you are above 55. Should you wish to pledge the property at a later date, you will need to create a new CPF charge which will involve additional legal costs for creation and lodgement of the new CPF charge.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: How do I discharge the CPF charge on my private property?
questions.text:
When you use your CPF savings to purchase a private property, a CPF charge is created and lodged with the Singapore Land Authority (SLA). To discharge this charge, you must first refund the full amount used for your property, plus accrued interest, to your CPF account.
The discharge process depends on your situation:
If you are selling your property
Your lawyers handling the sale will complete the discharge as part of the sale transaction.
If you are not selling your property
After making a full voluntary refund, you will need to engage a lawyer to lift the CPF charge. The lawyer will assist with the legal documentation required by SLA and handle any conveyancing matters involved in the discharge process.
The CPF charge was lodged with the SLA by your lawyer when you first withdrew your CPF towards your property. Similarly, the discharge of this charge, requires careful legal documentation and lodgement of documents with SLA.
Please note that you will incur legal costs for this process, which must be paid in cash. For queries on the discharge process, which is a legal conveyancing procedure, please contact Ministry of Law or a law firm of your choice.
Important considerations after discharge
Once the CPF charge is discharged, no further CPF transactions can be made for the property. This means you cannot:
use CPF savings for the property
make voluntary housing refunds to your CPF account for this property
pledge the property for withdrawing Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum if you are above 55. Should you wish to pledge the property at a later date, you will need to create a new CPF charge which will involve additional legal costs for creation and lodgement of the new CPF charge.

questions.title: Can I select my preferred deduction date instead of the default direct deduction date, which is set at two working days after the submission date?
questions.text: You can select your preferred deduction date. Please click on the calendar icon under the Direct Debit option to change the date before submitting the contributions.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: How do I appeal for Home Protection Scheme coverage if my health condition has improved?
questions.text:
If your health condition has improved and you would like to be considered for Home Protection Scheme coverage, please submit a new application along with an up-to-date medical report detailing all your medical conditions. Please note that the cost of the medical report will be borne by you.
Find out more:
I would like to submit a medical report to support my Home Protection Scheme application. What is the information required in the medical report?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I just received my CareShield Life (CSHL) renewal letter. I do not remember receiving any notifications about being enrolled into CSHL and note that my free-look-period (FLP) has ended. Can I still opt out of the scheme?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979 who was covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme, you would have been enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. A welcome notification package would have been sent to you in November 2021, informing you of your coverage and that after the end of the free-look-period (FLP) on 31 December 2023, you would continue to be covered under the scheme. We are unable to accede to opt-out requests for members whose FLP had ended on 31 December 2023.
CareShield Life offers lifelong protection against the costs of long-term care in the event of severe disability. Find out how CareShield Life protects you for life.

questions.title: What is Baby Bonus?
questions.text: The Baby Bonus Scheme supports parents in their decision to have more children by helping to manage the costs of raising children. It was introduced on 1 April 2001 and continuously enhanced to better support families. For more information on Baby Bonus Scheme and the application, please visit LifeSG or LifeSG mobile app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: How is the platform worker's share of CPF contributions on my CPF Contribution Alert derived?
questions.text:
Your platform worker’s share of CPF contributions on the CPF Contribution Alert is derived by applying the applicable CPF contribution rate to the total CPF contributions made by your platform operator.
You will receive one Contribution Alert for each contribution made by your platform operator(s). As the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions indicated on the CPF Contribution Alert is meant to be indicative, please use the platform worker CPF Contribution Calculator to determine the exact breakdown of your platform worker's share of CPF contributions based on your net earnings per month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I apply for refund of excess CPF contribution paid above Additional Wage (AW) ceiling?
questions.text:
From 1 April 2025, if contributions have been made in excess of the AW ceiling, you should apply for a refund by selecting ‘Refund of payments made for 1 employee/platform worker’, followed by the refund reason ‘Paid CPF above additional wage ceiling’.
This change is designed to streamline the application process, such that the employer only needs to provide the requested refund amount and payment details for the affected month(s) instead of for 12 months of the year. You can use the AW ceiling calculator to derive the excess amount to be refunded.
The total refund amount (employer and employee's share) will be refunded to you. You are responsible to refund the employee's share of CPF contributions (where applicable) directly to your employee.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I am holding an LTVP as a parent or parent-in-law of a work pass holder. Can I work in Singapore?
questions.text:
Yes, if you have a valid work pass, you can do so.
Learn more about working in Singapore as a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holder.
topics: Work passes and permits / Long-Term Visit Pass

questions.title: What happens if I am not provided a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) from my employer for my medical treatment?
questions.text:
If you are a Work Permit holder, your employer should bear the costs of providing medical treatment (inpatient and outpatient), regardless of whether the conditions are work-related.
If you are denied from having medical treatment, you should contact MOM immediately.
MOM will take appropriate enforcement actions against errant employers who fail to provide medical treatment.

questions.title: I have been approved to be a Asbestos-removal Contractor. When will I receive the certificate?
questions.text:
The approval letter and certificate will be emailed to the email address indicated in your online application upon approval of your Asbestos-removal Contractor application.
If you have not received it after 7 working days, the appointed eService User of your company would have to send us an official request letter using your company letterhead, stating that you have not received the certificate.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Notify for asbestos work

questions.title: Must I reimburse my employee if their medical expenses were paid out of their MediSave or MediShield?
questions.text:
If medical costs were paid by your employee using cash, MediSave or MediShield, you must reimburse payment in the following order:
Reimburse the cash portion.
Reimburse the MediSave portion directly into your employee’s MediSave account.
Reimburse the MediShield portion directly to the MediShield insurer.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: I received a notification on the refund of CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit for platform workers but I have yet to receive my share of the excess contributions from my (ex-)Platform Operator, what should I do?
questions.text: Your (ex-)Platform Operator has been notified to refund your share of excess CPF contributions to you, if any. You should contact your (ex-)Platform Operator directly regarding the refund.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I lodge a report for non-payment or underpayment of CPF contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
For discrepancies in CPF contributions:
If you suspect any non-payment or underpayment of CPF contributions, you may use the platform worker CPF calculator to verify the CPF contribution rates applicable to you. Please note that certain types of payments do not attract CPF contributions.
If there are discrepancies, you should approach your platform operator immediately, while the documentary evidence is fresh. Your platform operator is expected to rectify the errors without delay.
If your platform operator does not provide you with a satisfactory response, you can lodge a report with CPF Board. Please enclose all available supporting documents to support your claim (e.g. earnings slip). Claims made without any supporting documents would require a longer time to investigate.
If you would like to lodge a report, please click this link. Please note the likelihood of recovery for any non/underpayment of CPF contributions beyond 1 year is low as the parties’ recollection of the facts or availability of evidence may diminish over time.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why are platform commissions not deducted from gross earnings before Fixed Expense Deduction Amount is applied?
questions.text:
The Fixed Expense Deduction Amount (FEDA) takes reference from the Fixed Expense Deduction Ratio developed by IRAS, which is based on actual expense ratios, which includes any platform commissions that platform workers pay to platform operators. Hence, the FEDA is applied on gross earnings (including platform commissions), to derive net earnings.
For more details, please see How much to contribute as a platform worker.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: The seller has terminated their extension of stay early. Can I apply for the Owner-Occupier Tax Rates?
questions.text: If the seller terminates their extension of stay early (i.e. before 3-month period is over), you must update HDB by logging in to My HDBPage with your Singpass within 7 days of the termination. The information will be transmitted to IRAS and IRAS will notify you of the tax adjustments in the following month.

questions.title: I would like to terminate my GIRO arrangement as I will be selling my property. What should I do?
questions.text:
You may terminate your GIRO payment plan by contacting your bank directly. However, if you have an existing GIRO arrangement that allows you to make payment for more than 1 of your own taxes (e.g. Income Tax, Property Tax or GST) or for property tax for more than 1 of your properties, please call IRAS on 1800 356 8300 or email us to terminate the relevant GIRO arrangement pertaining to the property that you have just sold/ in the process of selling.
Please ensure that all outstanding taxes are settled in full, before you terminate the GIRO arrangement.

questions.title: How can I verify the amount of my share for the excess CPF contributions refunded by my employer?
questions.text: You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to verify the amount of your share for the excess CPF contributions refunded by your employer.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount refunded to me by my employer less than the amount deducted from my CPF account(s) for the refund of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text: Generally, the amount deducted from the employee’s CPF account(s) for the refund of excess contributions above the CPF Annual Limit comprises both the employer and employee’s shares of the excess. As your employer is required to refund you the employee’s share, the refund you received from your employer may be lower than that deducted from your CPF account(s). You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to verify the amount of your share.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is the amount deducted from my CPF account(s) for the refund less than the excess CPF contributions made for the year?
questions.text: The final refunded amount is based on the available balances in your CPF account(s). If there are insufficient funds in your account(s) for full refund of the excess contributions, the excess will be partially refunded.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I check if my employer has correctly capped the CPF contributions on the Additional Wages (AW) payable at the AW ceiling and/or CPF Annual Limit?
questions.text: You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to check the CPF contributions payable on the Additional Wages paid.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I request CPF Board to refund the employee's share of excess CPF contributions directly to my employee?
questions.text:
The full excess CPF contributions will be refunded to the employer. The employer is required to refund the employee’s share of excess CPF contributions, if any, directly to the employee.
You can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator to calculate the excess contributions. The calculator will help you determine the total excess amount, and the breakdown for employer and employee’s shares.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: What is the CPF Annual Limit?
questions.text: The CPF Annual Limit sets the total mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions that can be made to an employee’s CPF accounts in a calendar year; the current CPF Annual Limit is $37,740.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I find out if my Large Family MediSave Grant is successfully credited?
questions.text: You can log in to your CPF account using your Singpass to view your Transaction history to check if the Large Family MediSave Grant has been credited into your MediSave Account.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Large Family MediSave Grant (LFMG)

questions.title: What happens if the child's mother passes away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment?
questions.text: For persons who have passed away after receiving the Large Family MediSave Grant payment, their Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings, including MediSave balance, will be distributed to their beneficiaries in cash according to their CPF nomination or through the Public Trustee's Office if no CPF nominations were made.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Large Family MediSave Grant (LFMG)

questions.title: Why is the QR code unsupported when I tried to make payment with my LifeSG credits?
questions.text: Only NETS QR and PayNow UEN QR codes from supported merchants will be accepted. Please check that it’s a QR code that can be recognised by the LifeSG app.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Technical queries relating to the usage of Credits

questions.title: Why am I not able to spend my credits even though the merchant accepts PayNow QR?
questions.text: The credits in the LifeSG application can only be spent at merchants who accept payment by “Scan and Pay” via PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR. PayNow QRs registered to their personal mobile numbers or NRIC instead of a company UEN are not accepted.
topics: Large Families Scheme / Technical queries relating to the usage of Credits

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to persons with disabilities to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text: Anyone such as the person with disability, their loved ones, employers or members of the community, can make the cash top-ups to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do employers / platform operators enjoy tax benefits if they top up to their employees / platform workers' CPF accounts?
questions.text: Employers / platform operators will enjoy 1:1 corporate tax deduction, which will be deductible against their taxable income. This encourages employers to make cash top-ups to their employees' retirement accounts, thereby helping to build retirement adequacy.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: For persons with disabilities below age 55, where will the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) grant be credited?
questions.text: For persons with disabilities below age 55, the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will be credited into their Special Account (SA), to grow their retirement savings as per the policy objective of MRSS. This is credited at the beginning of the following year. For persons who have a Retirement Account (RA) such as those who are under the Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) scheme, the matching grant will be credited into their RA.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What can I use the top-up monies and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) matching grants for?
questions.text: Top-ups and matching grant from the Matched Retirement Savings Schemes are meant to boost your retirement savings and monthly payouts in retirement. In keeping with this purpose, such top-up and matching grant monies will form the retirement savings in your Retirement Account (which is created for you at age 55) and paid to you as higher monthly payouts in retirement from age 65. These top-up monies and matching grant cannot be withdrawn for other purposes (e.g. withdrawn in a lump sum, withdrawn from the Retirement Account using property, transferred to loved ones or other CPF schemes such as education investment, insurance).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a person with disability aged 55 and above and had received Matched Retirement Savings Scheme matching grants before its expansion to include persons with disabilities of all ages. Will my past grants count towards the $20,000 lifetime limit?
questions.text: Matching grants received for cash top-ups made prior to 2025 will not count towards the $20,000 lifetime limit. Matching grants received for cash top-ups made in 2025 or after will count towards the same $20,000 lifetime limit. This aligns with the intent of Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) to help those with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts, which remains relevant regardless of whether these members have benefited from MRSS in the past.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why is the Government expanding the coverage of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) to Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will be expanded to include younger Singaporeans with disabilities to give them a greater boost for retirement by helping them to start building up their retirement savings earlier via cash top-ups to the CPF Special Account (SA).
Eligible persons with disabilities can receive a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $2,000/year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000 from the Government on cash top-ups received in their CPF SA.
Singaporeans below age 55 will need to have their disability status verified with MSF* before 1 November of the current year to be considered for MRSS eligibility in the following year. Other MRSS eligibility criteria such as CPF balances, monthly income and Annual Value of their residential property will also apply.
*For more information on the disability verification process or to check whether you are already verified, please refer to this FAQ.
Here is some useful information related to MRSS:
1. What are the eligibility criteria of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) from 1 January 2026 when the scheme is expanded to Singaporeans with disabilities?
2. Do I need to get my disability status verified to be assessed for MRSS eligibility?
3. What is the submission deadline for the Disability Verification Form (DVF) to be included in the eligibility assessment for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) in the following year?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How do I make a cash top-up to persons with disabilities to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
Anyone who is aged 16 and above may make cash top-ups to their own or their loved ones' Retirement or Special Account (RA or SA) via the CPF website or CPF mobile app to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS).
You can also top up your child's Special Account using the same form. When doing so, select "Others" in the declaration of relationship section of the cash top-up application.
Consider making regular monthly or yearly cash top-ups conveniently via GIRO, without the hassle of completing the application form every time you top up.
Anyone under the age of 16 who wish to top up to their SA should ask their parents to make cash top-ups on their behalf.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do I enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups made to persons with disabilities?
questions.text:
If you are making a cash top-up to a member eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS), including persons with disabilities, the first $2,000 of your cash top-up will enable your recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $2,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief.
You can continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for your cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
Find out more on the conditions to qualify for tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What is the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) aims to help Singapore Citizens aged 55 to 70 (inclusive) with lower MediSave savings to boost their healthcare savings by matching voluntary cash top-ups made to their MediSave Account (MA). The scheme is implemented in 2026 for a period of five years.
Under the MMSS, the Government will match every dollar of cash top-up to the MA of eligible members up to $1,000 per year. The matching grant by the Government will be disbursed to eligible members in the following year.
The scheme helps eligible members pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What are the benefits of the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), the Government will match every dollar of cash-top up to the MediSave Account (MA) of eligible members up to $1,000 per year.
Please see below examples for illustration:
Your cash top-upMatching grant from the Government (disbursed the following year)Total increase in your healthcare savings
$2,000 in a lump sumCapped at $1,000$3,000 ($2,000 + $1,000)
$100 monthly for 6 months = $600$600$1,200 ($600 + $600)
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who is eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens who meet the following criteria will be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme for the year. Eligibility is automatically assessed annually. Eligible members will be notified by CPF Board at the beginning of the year. No application is needed to participate in the scheme.
AgeBetween 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year
MediSave Account SavingsLess than 50% of the current Basic Healthcare Sum
Average Monthly IncomeNot more than $4,000
Annual Value of ResidenceNot more than $21,000
Property OwnershipOwn not more than one property
Self-Employed Persons onlyMust have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for MediSave payable
For more information on how to check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How does the Matched MediSave Scheme work?
questions.text:
Members’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will be automatically assessed annually. No application by members is needed.
Each year, if you are eligible, we will notify you at the beginning of the year. You can also check your eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard.
Cash top-ups to MA can be made by yourself, loved ones, employers or members of the community.
If you are eligible and have received cash top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA) by 31 December of the year, you will receive a matching grant at the beginning of the following year.
MMSS is implemented from January 2026. Cash top-ups made before 2026 is not eligible for matching grants under this scheme.
Individual givers will not receive tax relief for cash top-ups that attract the MMSS matching grant.
Members may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000 per year for eligible cash top-ups to their own Special Account, Retirement Account or MA, and another $8,000 per year for cash top-ups to such accounts of their loved ones, that do not attract the matching grant for MMSS or the Matched Retirement Saving Scheme (MRSS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: When will my eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme be assessed and do I need to apply?
questions.text:
Members’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will be automatically assessed annually. You do not need to apply for the scheme.
MMSS is implemented in January 2026 for five years. You will be notified at the beginning of each year if you are eligible for the scheme for the year via email or post. Eligibility information will be available around the 2nd or 3rd week of January of each year and notifications to eligible members will be sent out around end January.
You can also check your eligibility for the MMSS via the Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Who can make cash top-ups to recipients who are eligible to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including the member himself/herself, his/her loved ones, employers or members of the community, can help the eligible member receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme by making cash top-ups to the member’s MediSave Account.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What should I do if I have already submitted a refund application prior to the refund initiated by the CPF Board?
questions.text: No further action is required by you. The CPF Board will consider the total contributions paid for the year and automatically refund any excess contributions paid above the CPF Annual Limit and/or Additional Wage ceiling.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How do I check if I have paid excess CPF contributions for my employee?
questions.text:
You can refer to the monthly CPF Record of Payment at CPF EZPay to check the total CPF contributions paid for your employee. Your employee would have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit if the total amount contributed for the year is more than $37,740.
To calculate the share of excess CPF contributions paid by the employer and employee respectively, you can use the Additional Wage ceiling calculator.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: Why did I receive a refund of excess CPF contributions paid to my employee(s) when I did not apply for the refund?
questions.text:
Starting February 2024, CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit for the preceding year will be automatically refunded to the employer’s bank account under the Direct Debit arrangement maintained with CPF Board.
You are required to refund the employee’s share of excess contributions, if any, directly to your employee.
As employers, you are required to ensure accurate CPF contributions up to the CPF Annual Limit per year for each employee by applying the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling and Additional Wage (AW) ceiling.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: How will the employer be notified about the auto refund of excess CPF contributions, and what information will be provided?
questions.text:
Employers will receive two notifications regarding the auto-refund of excess CPF contributions. In the first notification, employers will be notified on the impending refund of the excess CPF contributions paid for the relevant year. After the refund is successfully processed, employers will receive a second notification with the refund details such as the affected employee’s details, refund month(s) and refunded amount.
The affected employee(s) will also receive two similar notifications.
It is important to note that refund details are only available in the second notification, as the refund is subject to the availability of funds in the employee’s CPF account(s).
To ensure notifications are received, employer particulars must be up-to-date. Employers can update their contact details under “Account settings”.
topics: Employer - Compliance and Rectifications / Applying for refund of CPF contributions

questions.title: I was notified that the total CPF contributions received have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740, and the excess CPF contributions will be refunded to my employer. When should my employer return my share of excess CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Generally, the refund of the excess contributions will be processed and paid to your employer within 10 days after you are first notified of the impending refund unless further assessment is required.
We will notify you and your employer after the refund is successfully processed. Your employer is required to compute and return your share of the excess CPF contributions, if any, after receiving the notification.
You should contact your employer directly regarding the refund.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the eligibility criteria of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) from 1 January 2026 when the scheme is expanded to Singaporeans with disabilities?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, you will be eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for the year if you are a Singapore Citizen residing in Singapore only and meet the following criteria.
Age
55 or above as of 31st December of the year; or
Below age 55 with disability status verified+ with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).
*Disability status verification with MSF is a one-time process.
Ordinary and Special Account (OSA) Savings / Retirement Account (RA) Savings*#
Less than $110,200^.
Average Monthly Income#
Not more than $4,000.
This covers the majority of senior workers and verified Singaporeans with disabilities.
Annual Value of Residence#
Not more than $21,000.
Property Ownership#
Own not more than one property.
+For information on the disability verification process or to check whether you are already verified, please refer to this FAQ.
*RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.
^Basic Retirement Sum for 2026.
#Previous year’s data is utilised to assess your eligibility as these are the latest data available.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: As a work pass holder, how do i get a Singpass?
questions.text:
To obtain a Singpass, you can either:
Visit Singpass website to apply for your Singpass online
Visit any of the Singpass counters located islandwide in-person.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: How do I change the share of my Home Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
To change your share of Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover:
If you have an existing HPS cover:
Submit an application online using your Singpass. Select your existing property and the reason “I need to adjust my share of cover”.
If you have recently applied for an HPS cover and your application status is "Pending Processing":
Write to us using your Singpass to inform us of the new share of cover. You can check your application status via “Activities”.
Please note that reducing your share of cover will lower your HPS premium, while increasing your share of cover will raise your premium.
Find out more:
Why should my share of Home Protection Scheme cover minimally match my share of responsibility to service the housing loan?
Do I need to declare my health when I apply to adjust my Home Protection Scheme cover?

questions.title: Will I still be considered opted-in if I stop doing platform work for a while or change platform operator after opting in?
questions.text: Yes, your opt-in status is permanent after opting in and applies to all platform operators you work with.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have an instalment arrangement for my MediSave contributions. Why do I need to continue with my instalment deductions if I am also making monthly contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
The monthly CPF contributions made by your platform operator are for your income earned from platform work from 2025 onwards. You will not need to make your own MediSave contributions on these platform earnings, since your platform operator would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions for you every month (see FAQ).
Your instalment arrangement via GIRO is for MediSave contributions on your income earned prior to 2025 (i.e. income earned in 2024 and before).
Hence, your monthly GIRO instalment deductions will continue, as this is for your past MediSave contributions.
If you are facing difficulties keeping up with your instalment, you may reach out to CPFB to arrange affordable instalment plans on your past MediSave obligations.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is my final MediSave deduction amount different from the amount provided to me before my hospital admission/in my care cost form?
questions.text:
The final MediSave deduction amount may differ from the estimated amount provided during financial counselling at the medical institution due to various reasons, such as changes to the treatment, longer than expected stay etc.
For clarifications on your final medical bill, please approach the medical institution where you received treatment at for assistance.

questions.title: Why are my MediSave and MediShield Life claims not processed after my visit/hospital discharge?
questions.text:
Medical institutions may take up to about two weeks from the date of your visit/hospital discharge to submit your MediShield Life and MediSave claims. If you are on an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), it may take longer than two weeks as your claim(s) will first be submitted to your IP insurer for assessment.
Please refer to the table of processing time from the day CPFB receives the claims from your Medical Institution or insurer.

questions.title: I have a Letter of Guarantee (LOG) from my employer/insurer. How do I use it to pay for my medical expenses?
questions.text:
You may provide the Letter of Guarantee (LOG) to the hospital at admission. The hospital will be able to advise you on the billing arrangements and send the bill to your employer/insurer. If your employer/insurer is paying only part of your hospital expenses, the hospital will also assist you to submit the MediShield and MediSave claims on your behalf.
Please review the terms of your LOG carefully. For clarifications about your LOG or payment arrangements, please approach the hospital and/or employer/insurer directly.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to top-up my family member’s MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You may use your MediSave for your family members in different ways. Here are the options depending on your intent :
1. If you would like to pay for your family member's hospitalisation/outpatient expenses,
You can approach the Medical Institution (MI) where your immediate family member is receiving treatment, to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF) and authorise the use of your MediSave directly. Find out more on how to pay for your family member’s hospitalisation and outpatient expenses.
2. If you would like to pay for your family member's Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums,
You can use your MediSave to pay for your family member's IP premiums by changing the payer. Find out more on how to pay for your family member's premium.
3. If you would like to make voluntary cash top-ups to your family member’s MediSave Account (MA),
You can find out more on voluntary cash top ups to MA.
4. If you are 55 and above and have withdrawable savings in your Ordinary Account (OA) that you would like to top up your own or a loved one’s MA using savings from your OA,
You can complete the “Top up My / My Loved Ones’ MediSave Account using CPF Savings” form.

questions.title: How do I know if my MediSave can be used for the medical treatment that I have received or will be receiving?
questions.text: Please approach the medical institution where you have received or will be receiving medical treatments from to check if MediSave can be used to pay for the expenses. Please refer to the list of medical institutions participating in the MediSave scheme. The medical institution is best-placed to advise you whether MediSave can be used for the specific medical treatment it is providing and the expected expenses.

questions.title: I paid my medical bill in full using cash, but my employer or insurer has since made a payment to the medical institution for the same bill. How can I be reimbursed for the cash I paid?
questions.text:
Cash reimbursements for medical claims are handled between the patients and their employers or insurers.
You may wish to contact your Medical Institution and/or employer or insurer for assistance in processing the reimbursement for the cash you paid.

questions.title: What can I do if my family member has been abusing me?
questions.text:
You can seek help from a Family Service Centre or a Protection Specialist Centre (PSC). If you wish to report the violence, you can contact the National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline (NAVH) at 1800-777-0000 or the police.
You may also wish to file an application for a personal protection order (PPO) to protect yourself.
You can file a PPO application in person at any PSC, Pave Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre (ISIFPSC) or at the Family Protection Centre (FPC) located in the Family Justice Courts.
You may also file an application online via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS). However, you will still have to visit the FPC, ISIFPSC or PSC to complete the application after submitting your information online.
If you are under 18 years of age, you will not be able to file the application on your own and will need a family member, guardian, or carer to file on your behalf. If you are married or previously married but under 18 years of age and do not have a family member to apply for you, you may appoint another adult person to apply as your litigation representative.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is Family Violence?
questions.text:
Family Violence is defined in the Women’s Charter as (i) physical abuse, (ii) sexual abuse, or (iii) emotional or psychological abuse, against a family member.
It includes any of the following acts:
Physical Abuse
(a) Causes or threatens to cause personal injury or physical pain;
(b) Threatening one with death or injury; or
(c) Wrongfully confining or restraining one against his/her will
But does not include force lawfully used in self-defence or by way of correction towards a child below 18 years of age.
Sexual Abuse
(a) Coerces or attempts to coerce one to engage in sexual activity
Emotional or Psychological Abuse
(a) Acts which torments, intimidates, harasses, or distresses a person; or
(b) Acts which causes or may reasonably be expected to cause mental harm to one, including thoughts of suicide or inflicting self-harm
Family members include:
• Spouse or ex-spouse
• Child, including an adopted child or step-child
• Parents
• Parents-in-law
• Brothers or sisters
• Any other relative who in the court’s opinion should be regarded as a family member
Abuse can either be a single instance of conduct/behaviour or continuous in nature.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/protection-against-family-violence and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: My spouse has been violent towards my child. I am worried for the safety of my child. Can I apply for a personal protection order (PPO) on behalf of my child against my spouse?
questions.text:
Yes, you can file for a PPO on behalf of your child if he/she is below 18 years of age.
You can file a PPO application in person at any Protection Specialist Centres (PSC), Pave Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre (ISIFPSC) or at the Family Protection Centre (FPC) located in the Family Justice Courts.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.
You may also file an application online via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS). However, you will still have to visit the FPC, ISIFPSC or PSC to complete the application after submitting your information online.

questions.title: What is the court process for obtaining a personal protection order (PPO)?
questions.text:
The court process is as follows:
• File your application in person at the Pave Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre, any Protection Specialist Centres, or at the Family Protection Centre of the FJC. If you have a police report, a medical report, or an Emergency Order (issued to you by the Protector), you should include them. Relevant court orders such as orders relating to arrangements for access to children are also required for application for protection orders for such children.
• Once the application is filed, it would be referred to a duty judge who will review it. The duty judge may ask you further questions or clarifications on your application. If your complaint is accepted, a summons (which is an order to attend court) will be issued to the respondent (i.e., the person against whom the order is asked for). The court will arrange to have the summons delivered to the respondent.
• You and the respondent will have to appear in court on the first court date which is referred to as a court mention. The allegations made in your application will be read to the respondent. If he does not admit to any of the allegations, a Court Family Specialist will see and speak with both of you.
• If the respondent admits and agrees to a protection order being issued to you after the allegations are read to him or after seeing the Court Family Specialist, both you and the respondent will be brought before a judge for a Consent Order to be issued with or without any additional orders (such as a Counselling Order). The court will issue such an order if satisfied that the order is necessary for your protection and safety.
• If there is no Consent Order, the court will make directions for you to file documents and fix a hearing date for the matter.
• At the hearing, the judge will consider the merits of the case, taking into account all the evidence before deciding whether to issue a PPO.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I applied for a personal protection order (PPO) against my family member. The court informs me that I need to attend a court mention. What is a court mention?
questions.text:
A court mention is a court session where the court gives the parties in the PPO application directions on the next steps to be taken on the application.
It is compulsory for you to attend the mention. If you are absent from the court mention, the court may strike out your application.
If you are unable to attend the court mention on the stated date, you can make an application to change it via iFAMS accompanied by supporting documents. This must be done at least 5 working days in advance. Alternatively, you may contact the Family Justice Courts Registry at fjc_maintpos@judiciary.gov.sg or 6435 5471.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I no longer wish to pursue the personal protection order (PPO) application which I filed against my family member. Can I withdraw the application?
questions.text:
If you no longer wish to pursue the case, you can withdraw the application by informing the court at the court mentions. Once the court gives you permission to withdraw your case, your case will end.
However, if you wish to apply for another PPO in the future, you cannot rely on the same incidents or facts which you have used to support the earlier PPO application which has been withdrawn.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I filed an application for personal protection order (PPO) against my family member. My family member informed me that he consents to a PPO being granted against him. Do we still need to go through trial?
questions.text:
If your family member admits partially or fully to the allegations and consents to the PPO application, the court needs to be satisfied that family violence is committed, and the order is necessary for your protection and safety before a PPO will be issued. You and your family member will not be required to go through a hearing.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I received a summons for a personal protection order (PPO) application. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you received a summons issued by the court stating that you are the respondent in a PPO application, it means that a family member (the applicant) has filed a PPO against you.
The summons will state the date and time for you and the applicant to attend a court session known as a court mention. At the court mention, the court officer will inform you of the contents made in the application by the applicant. You will then be given the opportunity to give your response to the application. Please note that if you have been served with the summons but do not attend the court mention, the court may issue a Warrant of Arrest against you.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/respond-personal-protection-order-application and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: The court directed my family member(s) and I to attend a family conference for the personal protection order (PPO) application which I filed against my family member(s). What will happen at the family conference?
questions.text:
The family conference session is usually held if there are multiple parties involved in cross or connected applications. The session will be facilitated by one or more Court Family Specialist (CFS). The CFS will:
• Assist you and your family member(s) to understand more about the matters of the PPO application.
• Seek to address any safety concerns: the CFS may make necessary referrals to the appropriate community and support agencies if necessary.
• Assist you and your family member(s) reach a resolution on the PPO application, if deemed suitable. If you and your family member(s) are able to reach a resolution on the application, a hearing will not be needed for the case.
At the family conference session, the CFS may decide to see all parties in a joint session or individually subject to the nature of the case, and the dynamics between parties involved.
During the family conference session, you or your family member(s) may:
• Take the opportunity to clarify with the CFS any concerns or questions that you may have regarding the PPO application.
• Take up the necessary referrals that the CFS may assist in, if necessary.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: My family member continues to be violent towards me even though I have obtained a personal protection order (PPO) against my family member. What should I do?
questions.text:
You should make a police report about the incident and inform the police about your PPO. The police will investigate and decide whether to charge your family member for breaching the PPO.
A breach of a PPO is punishable by a fine and/or an imprisonment term.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What are the types of orders that the court can make at the end of a personal protection order (PPO) application hearing?
questions.text:
Depending on the types of application applied for and the orders that the court deem fit to issue, the court can make the orders below:
• PPO - an order restraining the respondent from committing family violence against the protected person.
• Domestic Exclusion Order – an order excluding or restricting the respondent from entering all or part of the protected person’s residence.
• Stay Away Order – an order prohibiting the respondent from entering or remaining in areas frequented by the protected person, e.g., void deck of the protected person’s residence, or workplace.
• No Contact Order – an order prohibiting the respondent from visiting or communicating with the protected person.
• Counselling Order – an order referring the protected person and/or the respondent to counselling conducted at an agency assigned by the Protector.
• Mandatory Treatment Order – an order requiring the respondent (who is suffering from a treatable psychiatric condition which contributed towards the violent behaviour) to undergo psychiatric treatment.

questions.title: Can I apply for an Electronic Monitoring Order (“EMO”) against my family member when making an application for personal protection order?
questions.text:
No, the Women’s Charter provides that only the Protector (a person appointed by the Director-General for Social Welfare, Ministry of Social and Family Development) can apply for an EMO.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I am afraid that my family member will hurt me when I am going through the court proceedings to obtain a personal protection order (PPO). What can I do?
questions.text:
The court may, if it is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that there is a danger of the respondent committing family violence against you whilst the protection order application is pending, grant an Expedited Order for a PPO. An Expedited Order for PPO is a temporary PPO restraining your family member from committing family violence against you while the PPO proceedings are pending. In addition to an Expedited Order for PPO, the court may also grant an Expedited Order of the following, if it is satisfied on a balance of probabilities that these orders are necessary for your protection or personal safety:
(a) Domestic Exclusion Order
(b) Stay Away Order
(c) No Contact Order
You can file a PPO application in person at any Protection Specialist Centres (PSC), Pave Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre (ISIFPSC) or at the Family Protection Centre (FPC) located in the Family Justice Courts.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/how-to-file-personal-protection-order-application and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is the difference between an Emergency Order (EOR) and Expedited Order (EO)?
questions.text:
An EOR is issued by the Protector (a person appointed by the Director-General for Social Welfare, Ministry of Social and Family Development) if it is assessed that there is imminent danger to the survivor. The EOR is valid for 14 days to give the survivor time to make an application to the Family Court for a personal protection order (PPO). An EOR is not a court order but breaching it is a criminal offence punishable by a fine and/or imprisonment.
An EO is a temporary PPO (issued by the Family Court) restraining the respondent from committing family violence, while the PPO application is pending. The applicant can ask for an EO to be issued when applying for a PPO. The EO will cease on whichever of the following dates occurs first:
(a) After 28 days from the date of the order was made unless extended by the court
(b) The date the PPO application hearing commences unless extended by the court
A breach of an EO is punishable by a fine and/or imprisonment.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How long does a personal protection order (PPO) last?
questions.text:
A PPO has effect either: a) indefinitely, or b) for a specified period.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and refer to the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I am worried that my identity will be revealed in the public domain when I apply for a personal protection order. What can I do?
questions.text:
Your identity and personal information (which can identify you) would not be revealed in the public domain. Should an individual post such information without your consent, it will be an offence and you can apply to the court for the information to be taken down.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/protection-against-family-violence.

questions.title: What can I do if I am not satisfied with the outcome of the personal protection order (PPO) application?
questions.text:
If you are not satisfied with the outcome of your PPO application, you may file an appeal to the Family Division of the High Court. To find out more about the appeal process and the timelines involved, please visit this website - https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/appeal.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-personal-protection-order and the various guides available under "Resources" at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Can I file for a personal protection order (PPO) online?
questions.text:
You may file an application online via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS). However, you will be required to come down to the Family Protection Centre at the Family Justice Courts, any Protection Specialist Centres (PSC), or the Pave Integrated Services for Individual And Family Protection Specialist Centre (ISIFPSC) to complete the application after submitting your information online.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/how-to-file-personal-protection-order-application.

questions.title: What are the procedures required to bring a few bottles of liquor into Singapore for personal consumption?
questions.text:
The importation of liquor exceeding duty-free concession is subject to the payment of duty and Goods and Services Tax (GST) even if it is meant for personal consumption. Click here for information on duty-free concession.
If the quantity in excess of the duty-free concession is less than 10 litres, you can make an advanced declaration and payment of duties and GST on our Customs@SG web application. An e-receipt will be provided for reference and verification purposes if you are stopped for checks. Alternatively, you may also proceed to our Customs Tax Payment office to declare and make payment. Click here for more information on the declaration and payment of taxes.
If the quantity in excess of the duty-free concession exceeds 10 litres, you are required to arrange with a local freight forwarding agent to obtain a Customs In-Payment "Duty and GST" (IPT-DNG) permit. Click here for more information on Customs permit application.
topics: Arrival / Declaration and Payment of Taxes

questions.title: What are the required procedures when a container is affixed with a Singapore Customs red seal?
questions.text:
When a container is affixed with a Singapore Customs red seal, you must submit an online application for Customs Supervision for unstuffing within one working day of the container's clearance from the checkpoint. Schedule the intended unstuffing operation for at least one working day after submitting the e-file application.
It is crucial that you do not break the red seal until you receive further instructions from Singapore Customs. Adhering to these procedures ensures compliance with Customs regulations and maintains the integrity of the sealed container.

questions.title: How can I distinguish between Singapore Customs seals and shipper seals?
questions.text:
Singapore Customs uses two types of seals: Customs red seals and Customs green seals. Both types prominently display 'Singapore Customs' on them, which is the key distinguishing feature that helps differentiate Customs seals from shipper seals.
For visual reference, images of Customs red and green seals can be found in Annexes B and D of Customs Circular No. 11/2018 respectively.

questions.title: Is Customs supervision required for unstuffing a container with a Singapore Customs green seal if no 'Notice to Haulier' was received?
questions.text:
Customs supervision is not required for containers affixed with a Customs green seal. The requirement to apply for Customs supervision for unstuffing is only applicable to containers affixed with the Customs red seal. No approval is needed from Singapore Customs to break a Customs green seal, and you may proceed with unstuffing without applying for Customs supervision.
For more detailed information on seal types and associated procedures, please refer to Customs Circular No. 11/2018.

You may view and/or pay your bills via Health Buddy*, HealthHub, or https://for.sg/mpay (with or without SingPass).

questions.title: How can dependants of IEO holders, who are issued with a valid IEO, take up employment in Singapore?
questions.text:
Dependants of IEO holders, who are issued with a valid IEO, and who wish to take up employment during their stay here are required to apply for Letter of Consent (LOC) with ICA prior to the commencement of their employment.
Please ensure that you have the following documents for the LOC application:
a) Completed LOC application form duly endorsed by the employing company
b) Letter from the Embassy/Organisation
c) A copy of the applicant's passport biodata page and the page showing the valid IEO endorsement
d) A copy of the main IEO holder's passport biodata page and the page showing the valid IEO endorsement
e) A copy of the Practicing Certificate. Letter of Registration with the local Registration Body, e.g. Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, etc, where applicable.

questions.title: How much interest would I save if I start my education loan repayment early?
questions.text:
Based on a principal amount of $12,000, interest per month is $25 (based on 2.5% p.a1). If you were to repay the education loan upon graduation or leaving your course of study instead of over 10 years, you would have saved $4,010.
1Interest is calculated monthly and compounded (i.e. added to principal amount and accrued interest) on a yearly basis, pegged at the prevailing CPF Ordinary Account interest rate of 2.5%.
Please inform us of your intention to start early repayment of your education loan through this form and we will process your request accordingly.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: My education loan repayment is deferred. Would the interest on the outstanding loan amount continue to accrue during the deferment period?
questions.text:
Yes, interest will continue to accrue until the education loan is fully repaid. The amount withdrawn for education, plus the accrued interest must be repaid using cash, to fully restore your lending member’s CPF savings. This ensures that the member would not lose out on the interest they would have earned had the money not been withdrawn for education purposes.
To reduce the interest payable, you can still make repayment during the deferment period through the "Manage education loan repayments" form and check the latest outstanding amount by accessing your Education Dashboard.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What should the Sender ID of the CDC Vouchers link be? Is it gov.sg or RedeemSG?
questions.text:
From 1 July 2024, the Singapore government has launched a new security measure - gov.sg, a single SMS Sender ID to be used across government agencies. This whole-of-government effort to transition to a single SMS Sender ID will make it easier for the public to verify authentic government communications, with greater confidence and accuracy. Moving forward, the public can expect SMSes from government agencies to come from the gov.sg SMS Sender ID, and not from individual government agencies' Sender IDs.
PA/CDC aligns with this national effort to help residents access and respond to legitimate communications from the government, such as the CDC Vouchers Scheme.
topics: CDC Vouchers (Residents) / Claiming of CDC Vouchers
