If the worker's CPF accounts have insufficient balances, a cash refund in lieu of CPF will be required. Interest accrued on the outstanding cash amount may also be recovered. If the WIS payments are not refunded, the worker will receive a Notice to Attend Court .
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I change the mode of payment for my Workfare Income Supplement (WIS)?
questions.text:
There are two options to update the mode of payment for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS):
Option 1: Link your NRIC to PayNow
You are encouraged to link your NRIC to PayNow as government cash benefits will be credited to your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account. To find out more on how to link your NRIC to PayNow, please refer to this FAQ.
If your NRIC is linked to your PayNow, there is no need for you to provide your bank account details.
Option 2: Provide your bank account details
You can submit your bank account details by logging in to our e-services with your Singpass. The bank account that you provide will only be used if you do not have a PayNow-NRIC linked bank account.
Bank crediting is available only via the three local banking groups DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB, and your bank account must be a personal or joint account linked to your NRIC number.
The Government will verify the bank account details you have registered with your bank. If you have closed your bank account, ceased being a joint account holder, or provided incorrect bank account details, you will be asked to update your bank account details. A letter will be sent to your NRIC address.
No further action is required if you have already linked your NRIC to PayNow with a participating bank.
Citizens who are on GovCash will receive their cash benefits 1-2 weeks later than those who have linked their NRIC to PayNow or have provided a valid bank account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How will I get the Workfare Income Supplement payment?
questions.text:
You will get the cash portion of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) via one of the following payment methods.
i. PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account (by default)
By default, the WIS cash portion will be paid to your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account. To check your bank account details, please approach your bank.
ii. Bank Transfer (if you do not have a PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account)
If you do not have a PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account with a PayNow-GIRO-participating local or foreign bank in Singapore but have provided your DBS/POSB, OCBC or UOB bank account to the Government previously, you will get your cash portion of WIS via bank transfer. You can check and update your bank account details registered with us by logging in to our e-services with your Singpass.
iii. GovCash (if you do not have a bank account)
GovCash is a payment mode that allows Singaporeans to receive their benefits from Government agencies more quickly and conveniently. Nonetheless, you are encouraged to link your NRIC to PayNow with a PayNow-GIRO-participating local or foreign bank in Singapore to get your benefits earlier*.
If you do not have a PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account nor a bank account registered with us, you will get the WIS cash portion via GovCash.
*If you have linked your NRIC number to your bank account after the 16th of the month or submitted your bank account details after the 14th of the month, your updates will only be effective in the following month.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: I lost my letter containing the Payment Reference Number, can someone else access my money?
questions.text:
To ensure security, it is not possible to withdraw the money using only the Payment Reference Number. GovCash uses the Singpass Face Verification technology during the withdrawal process at OCBC ATMs. This technology incorporates a liveness-detection, which prevents the use of photographs, videos or masks for verification.
This security feature prevents fraudulent withdrawals of Government benefits by third parties using photographs or videos of the beneficiary. It ensures that only eligible Singaporean can access and withdraw their Government benefits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Can you re-send my Payment Reference Number to me?
questions.text: You can log in to the e-services with your Singpass to view your Payment Reference Number (PRN). Select “GovCash PRN” from the menu on the left. The PRN will be available after the payment has been processed through GovCash.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What is GovCash?
questions.text:
GovCash is a payment mode that allows Singapore citizens to withdraw their Government benefits in cash from over 500 OCBC ATMs located across Singapore.
For Singaporeans who need assistance with GovCash withdrawals, OCBC provides support at its ATMs where Digital Ambassadors are available during operating hours to guide recipients. In addition, GovCash offers convenient digital options such as the scan-and-pay function and PayNow transfers through the LifeSG mobile app. This allows recipients to easily access their benefits with various assistance options available to suit their needs.
GovCash adopts the Singpass Face Verification technology to authenticate users, including a liveness-detection capability that blocks the use of photographs, videos, or masks during the verification process. Users are also required to key in their unique 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN) during the withdrawal of the Government benefits at the OCBC ATMs.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Is there a specific time frame for me to withdraw or use my GovCash?
questions.text: You can withdraw or use your GovCash at your convenience, as there is no specific time frame. However, you are encouraged to do so as the intent of the scheme is to supplement your income and retirement savings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: How do I get my cash benefits via GovCash?
questions.text:
There are three options for receiving your cash benefit via GovCash:
Option 1: Use LifeSG to transfer to PayNow-NRIC linked bank account
If you have an existing bank account, you can link your account to PayNow-NRIC with your bank. Thereafter, login to LifeSG mobile app (LifeSG) using your Singpass to transfer your GovCash to your PayNow-NRIC linked bank account. The LifeSG app can be downloaded from the Apple App store or Google Play Store.
Option 2: Use LifeSG for Scan & Pay
You can use LifeSG to scan participating merchants' QR codes for purchases or scan your friend's/family’s QR code to transfer your GovCash to them. Purchases are only allowed at merchants that accept PayNow/NETS QR codes using the LifeSG app. Look out for the PayNow/NETS logo on the SG QR label displayed by merchants.
Once your GovCash balance is deducted on the LifeSG mobile app, the payment cannot be cancelled.
Option 3: Withdraw from OCBC ATMs
You can withdraw your cash benefit at OCBC ATMs islandwide. You just need to enter:
(i) your unique 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN)
(ii) your NRIC number; and
(iii) pass the facial verification
You do not need to have an OCBC bank account to use this service.
You will receive the Payment Reference Number (PRN) via letter, your Singpass app (if any) or SMS after your cash benefits have been paid. You can also log into the e-services with your Singpass and select “GovCash PRN” from the left menu to view your PRN. This will only be available after the payment has been made.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is my participation incentive $0 for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Participation Incentives were only extended to Singapore Citizens (SCs) born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024. However, both SCs and Permanent Residents (PRs) will be entitled to Government subsidies, if you are from a lower- to middle-income household. PRs enjoy half the applicable subsidies that SCs enjoy.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later, who can be covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.

questions.title: Why not allow insureds to choose from different CareShield Life plans depending on their ability to pay?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is intended to provide better protection for basic long-term care needs, when payouts are taken together with other long-term care financing sources.
If you wish to have additional coverage beyond what CareShield Life provides, you can consider purchasing Supplements from private insurers.

questions.title: What should I do if my Home Protection Scheme cover has lapsed due to non-payment of premium?
questions.text:
You may continue receiving financial protection on your outstanding housing loan through Home Protection Scheme (HPS) by reinstating your lapsed cover or applying for a new one, depending on your eligibility:
When did your HPS cover lapse or end*?Next steps
Ended 6 months or lessApply to reinstate your HPS cover online.
Ended more than 6 months but less than or equal to 1 year ago
Apply to reinstate your HPS cover online with supporting reason and health declaration.
Your eligibility to reinstate your previous HPS cover is subject to approval.
Ended more than 1 year ago
Apply for a new HPS cover with health declaration.
Your eligibility for the new HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health.
*You may check your HPS cover end date from the hardcopy lapse letter (Ref: HPS/Lapse) sent to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is premium loading for Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: Premium loading means additional premium is charged on top of the standard premium to provide insurance coverage for pre-existing medical conditions, given the higher likelihood of claims.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I choose to port my previous Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover to my new flat instead of taking up a new HPS cover with premium loading?
questions.text:
Yes, you can decline the offer for a new Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover with premium loading if it does not suit your needs. We will then consider porting your existing HPS coverage (remaining sum assured and term of loan) to your new flat, subject to eligibility conditions.
Find out how you can qualify for porting your previous HPS cover:
How do I qualify for the porting of my previous Home Protection Scheme cover to my new property?
Alternatively, you may also consider applying for insurance coverage from private insurers.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How is the amount of premium loading determined for my Home Protection Scheme?
questions.text: The amount of premium loading depends on the severity of your pre-existing health condition. If you are offered cover with premium loading, you will receive a notification which shows the total premium amount payable.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am currently covered under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS) at standard premium rates. Will my premium increase after the introduction of premium loading?
questions.text: There will be no impact on your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premiums. Your HPS premium will remain the same.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: If my medical condition has improved, how can I request a review of the premium loading on my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover?
questions.text:
If your medical condition has improved, you may request a review of your Home Protection Scheme premium loading. Write to us with your request and provide a medical report at your own cost.
Your medical report must be up-to-date from a medical institution in Singapore, clearly indicate improvement in your medical condition and include the following information:
Diagnosis and diagnosis date
Reason(s) of hospitalisation, if any
Details of treatment(s)
Date(s) and details of surgery, if any
Details of complications, if any, and treatment rendered
Current condition and treatment(s)
Investigation test results
If your current condition still presents similar health risks, your premium loading will remain unchanged. We will assess your request and notify you of the outcome.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: I am unemployed. How does it affect my Workfare Income Supplement eligibility?
questions.text:
The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme supports lower-wage Singaporean workers by supplementing their income and CPF savings, encouraging continued employment and retirement savings.
You must be working to receive WIS. If you require assistance in looking for a job, or are seeking more information on training and skills upgrading under the Workfare Skills Support scheme, please contact the Workfare Skills Support hotline at 1800 536 8333 or visit their website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What should I do if I notice missing or incorrect CPF contributions?
questions.text:
First, check if CPF contributions are required in your situation:
Employees: Your employer must contribute CPF if you earn more than $50 a month, regardless of whether you are employed on a permanent, part time, contract or casual basis.
Platform workers: Your platform operator must contribute to CPF on your behalf if you earn more than $500 a month (or $50 if you are opted in to increased CPF contributions)
If CPF contributions should be made but are missing or incorrect:
Check with your employer or platform operator first
There may be a delay or administrative error. Ask them to explain the discrepancy.
If you do not receive a satisfactory response,
you can report the issue to CPF Board using this form/contact link.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How and when will I be notified about my Workfare payment amount?
questions.text:
You will be notified via letter and/or SMS closer to the payment dates. You can also log in to the e-Services with your Singpass to check your payment.
To receive SMS notifications, you must register or update your mobile number with CPF Board via my cpf digital services - Account Settings. We will only send SMS notifications on Workfare payments to the mobile number that you have registered with CPF Board.
If you have previously opted out of receiving SMS notifications, you can log in to our e-Services with your Singpass to opt-in again.
If you need assistance with Workfare notifications, please write to us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why does the government send SMS notifications instead of hardcopy letters?
questions.text: The shift to SMS notifications is part of the Government's efforts to provide timelier and more responsive services. It also allows us to be more environmentally friendly. With SMS notifications, you can quickly receive details about your Workfare payments, including the payment mode and date, without waiting for a hardcopy letter. Older Workfare Income Supplement recipients will continue to receive both SMS notifications and hardcopy letters.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What happens to the Workfare Income Supplement paid via GovCash if the beneficiary passes away?
questions.text: If the beneficiary passes away before fully using their GovCash, the remaining balance will be credited to their CPF Ordinary Account. This amount will form part of their CPF monies and will be distributed according to their CPF Nomination. If there is no CPF nomination, the CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution in accordance to the intestacy or Muslim inheritance laws.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary with medical condition(s) to appeal to receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
Eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is automatically assessed and no action is required. However, if the beneficiary’s circumstances have changed, you may assist a beneficiary with medical condition in appealing for WIS, if you are:
aged 21 and above; and
a next-of-kin or appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), or court-appointed Deputy of the beneficiary.
To assist the beneficiary to appeal for WIS, you will need to provide the following supporting documents:
If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are a parent/guardian who is helping your child, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
birth certificate of your child; or legal document to verify the guardianship between the legal guardian and child;
documentary evidence stating your child’s medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
your child’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court appointed deputy, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are unable to fulfil any of the options, you can write to us for further advice.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary with medical condition(s) to withdraw their GovCash?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What is the difference between LPA and ACP? If I have made a decision related to my health in the ACP, can the person nominated in my LPA overturn the decision?
questions.text:
An LPA grants your Donee the legal rights to make decisions for you if you’re unable to do so, but it does not tell your Donee what to do for your Personal Welfare.
An ACP helps you to communicate to your Donee, your healthcare team and your loved ones, what decisions they should make for your Personal Welfare. This includes decisions such as where you should live, who you should live with, your daily lifestyle and healthcare decisions.
Appointing the same person as your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers and ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson is strongly encouraged as it will help to avoid conflicts amongst your loved ones. However, you do not have to do so, and in that situation, the LPA Donee with Personal Welfare remains the legal decision maker while the NHS is who the healthcare team will consult on healthcare decisions and discussions as the NHS is meant to be your spokesperson.

questions.title: How do I join ElderShield?
questions.text:
The ElderShield scheme is no longer open for new applications.
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and do not have disability, you may join CareShield Life via the Application to join CareShield Life form and log in using your Singpass to complete the application.
If you are born in 1980 or later, you will be automatically covered under CareShield Life.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Will I have to pay extra premiums if I join CareShield Life with pre-existing medical conditions?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier and do not have disability, you can choose to join CareShield Life. You will not need to pay additional premiums for pre-existing medical conditions.
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.

questions.title: Should I opt out of ElderShield if I would like to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You do not need to opt out of ElderShield if you wish to join CareShield Life. Your existing ElderShield cover will be upgraded to CareShield Life and the premiums paid for ElderShield will be taken into account.
Access the Application to join CareShield Life form using your Singpass. We will notify you on the outcome of your upgrade.

questions.title: The current ElderShield scheme has a maximum entry age of 64 years old. Can I join CareShield Life if I am older?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life at any age as there is no maximum entry age for CareShield Life.
As premiums increase with age, please check your personalised premium payable using the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass before applying, so that you can make an informed decision.

questions.title: I have applied to join CareShield Life online. Where do I check my application status?
questions.text: You can view the status of your CareShield Life application through Activities.

questions.title: I have applied to opt out of CareShield Life as I belong to the optional group (i.e. born in 1979 or earlier) and the cover is still within my free-look period. When will my application be approved?
questions.text:
Your application to opt out of CareShield Life will be processed after one working day. You will receive a notification once your application has been processed.
You may view the status of your application via Activities (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: As a pensioner, can I receive any special benefits under CareShield Life?
questions.text: There are no special benefits for pensioners under CareShield Life. As a pensioner, your participation in CareShield Life is optional. You can join CareShield Life if you do not have severe disability. If you are interested in CareShield Life, you may access information on your personalised premiums and premium support using the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service (Singpass login is required).

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I choose to receive the CareShield Life participation incentive as one lump sum?
questions.text: The participation incentive was provided to Singapore Citizens who joined and were covered under CareShield life by 31 December 2024. It was introduced to encourage Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier to join CareShield Life by helping to offset the annual premiums payable. As such, the Government has designed it to be spread over 10 years of premium payment. It cannot be received as one lump sum payment.

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Premium Support under MediShield Life. Would I be given Additional Premium Support under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) status applies to both CareShield Life and MediShield Life schemes. If you currently receive APS for MediShield Life, you will automatically be granted APS for CareShield Life during your existing APS validity period.
Your premium notification letter will inform you of your APS status.

questions.title: What is the difference in treatment between Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents for CareShield Life premium subsidies?
questions.text: For means-tested CareShield Life premium subsidies, Permanent Residents will receive half the means-tested premium subsidy rates applicable to Singapore Citizens, in line with MediShield Life.

questions.title: I had previously disallowed access to my financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks. How do I change this arrangement?
questions.text: To allow access to your financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks, please update your status via this link and click "login to access your household information". If you need further assistance, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2).

questions.title: What should I do if one of my household members has disallowed access to his financial information for the purpose of CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility checks?
questions.text:
If a household member disallows access to their financial information, we are unable to assess your household's eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and other assistance measures. As such, we are unable to extend any CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and other assistance measures to all members of your household.
Please discuss with your household member if you have concerns regarding his/her disclosure status. If your household member now wishes to allow access to his financial information, please call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2). Otherwise, you may visit the link and click "login to access your household information".

questions.title: I logged in to the Household Check e-Service but could only view my household information. How do I make changes to my household information?
questions.text:
We are currently processing changes to your household information submitted by a household member. During this time, you will not be able to make changes to your household information.
Please write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 or +65 6222 3399 from overseas (after selecting your preferred language, press 3, and then 2), from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) if you need more information.

questions.title: How do I know how much subsidies I will receive for the long-term care service(s) that I use?
questions.text: Qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.

questions.title: What is long-term care?
questions.text: Long-term care is the personal and medical care needed if an individual develops disability due to age or adverse health conditions. It includes a range of services which individuals may choose depending on their care needs and support available, either at home or institutions like nursing homes.

questions.title: How do I report a death that has occurred overseas?
questions.text:
If a Singapore citizen or permanent resident had passed on overseas, you should register the death and get a death certificate from the foreign authorities in the country where the person had passed on. You can then report the death to ICA with the foreign death certificate to update ICA's records.
If you are also bringing ashes home, please refer to this webpage.
Please refer to ICA website for more information on Reporting a Death that Occurred Overseas.

questions.title: I missed downloading the digital death certificate from My Legacy within 30 days from the date of death. How can I get a copy of the death certificate?
questions.text: Please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA using this form.

questions.title: Can I submit a claim for both CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care concurrently?
questions.text: You can submit a claim for both schemes concurrently as CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediSave Care are not mutually exclusive.

questions.title: Does having dementia automatically qualify an individual for CareShield Life/ElderShield claims?
questions.text: Applicants with dementia or other cognitive impairments will not automatically qualify for CareShield Life/ElderShield claims and must still undergo a severe disability assessment, as the impact of dementia/cognitive impairment on their functional abilities may vary.

questions.title: Who are the MOH-accredited severe disability assessors for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care and where can I find the list of assessors if I need to arrange an assessment?
questions.text:
MOH-accredited severe disability assessors are Singapore-registered doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who have undergone a rigorous training programme to assess a patient’s level of disability.
You can find the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors on the AIC website if you need to arrange a CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care assessment.

questions.title: I would like my monthly payouts for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care to be made to an overseas bank account. How can I do so?
questions.text: You are encouraged to nominate a local bank account for your monthly payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care as this is the default payment option.

questions.title: Who should I approach at the nursing home should I need assistance with application for schemes to support long-term care costs?
questions.text: If you are in a nursing home, you may wish to consult a medical social worker (or equivalent) from the nursing home for financial counselling and assistance to apply for long-term care schemes.

questions.title: Does the nursing home charge for performing the Resident Assessment Form (RAF) for the applicant?
questions.text: Nursing homes do not charge for performing the Resident Assessment Form (RAF) for their residents. If an individual resides in a nursing home and would like to undergo the RAF in place of a disability assessment conducted by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor, he/she should approach the nursing home for further assistance.

questions.title: Why is CareShield Life universal coverage not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier?
questions.text:
CareShield Life universal coverage is not extended to those born in 1979 or earlier due to several reasons:
This is a diverse group - some may have previously opted out of ElderShield, or decided not to upgrade to ElderShield. Others could have bought Supplements or insurance plans.
They would face higher entry premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payment over.
The higher prevalence of severe disability in older cohorts make it challenging to maintain affordable premiums for everyone.
From 1 January 2026, those who are born in 1979 or earlier and have disability will not be able to join CareShield Life. The Government will assist them through:
Government subsidies
Other schemes like the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund
Tap on ElderFund and MediSave savings
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund, ComCare can also provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield/ElderShield Supplement policyholder. Do I have to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979, who were covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, were auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021.
Those who were not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life.
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties.
You may refer to the types of premium support available for more information. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: How can I join CareShield Life if I am a foreigner?
questions.text: CareShield Life is applicable only to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Why do I have to go through the quarterly survivorship check for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care?
questions.text: The quarterly survivorship check for an individual living overseas is to verify one’s continued eligibility for payouts under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care. If you are required to undergo this check, Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will send you a letter with the review date and instructions on how to complete it.

questions.title: Can I nominate a joint bank account with the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: A joint bank account with the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient can be nominated to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts, provided the MI patient remains a joint account holder. You will need to specify in the application form that the patient is a joint owner of the account.

questions.title: I already went for a severe disability assessment recently, why is the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) requesting me to go for another?
questions.text: Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) may require you to attend a disability review to ascertain your continued eligibility for scheme payouts. Your letter will include instructions on how to complete the disability assessment.

questions.title: Can I nominate the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient’s own bank account to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: You can nominate the Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient's bank account to receive the monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts and should specify in the application form that the account belongs to the MI patient.

questions.title: I am paying ElderShield premiums for myself and my dependants. How do I check the transaction details?
questions.text: If you are paying the ElderShield premiums for yourself and your dependants using your MediSave, you may view the deduction and refund transactions for the policies via Transaction History.

questions.title: What happens when there are insufficient funds in my MediSave to pay for my ElderShield premium?
questions.text: Please note that the ElderShield policy will lapse if premiums are not paid. We encourage you to promptly top up your MediSave Account (visit Top up MediSave Account form with your Singpass) to pay the ElderShield premiums or ask a family member to help you pay the premiums using his/her MediSave. To do so, your family member may visit the Change Payer for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield form and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the transaction.

questions.title: Which agencies will administer ElderShield?
questions.text: ElderShield will be jointly administered by the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

questions.title: Should I upgrade to/join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The Government encourages Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1979 or earlier without disability to consider joining CareShield Life for basic lifetime financial protection for long-term care. CareShield Life provides monthly cash payout in the event of severe disability, for as long as you are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
The Government also provides support to help make premiums affordable.

questions.title: If I am currently on ElderShield 300/400 and choose to upgrade to CareShield Life, can I opt out or downgrade to ElderShield 300/400 subsequently?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born between 1970 and 1979, you will be automatically enrolled in CareShield Life from 1 December 2021, if you are currently covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and do not have severe disability at the point of auto-enrolment. You can opt out of CareShield Life by 31 December 2023 if you do not wish to join the scheme and you will automatically be placed back onto your ElderShield 400 scheme.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are an ElderShield insured in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to review your decision. If you choose to opt out, you will be given a full premium refund and will be automatically placed back onto your original ElderShield 300/400 scheme.
You will not be able to opt out from the scheme after the applicable opt-out/free-look periods.

questions.title: Will I get higher subsidies if I am of an older age since my CareShield Life premiums will be higher?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1979 or earlier, you will receive means-tested subsidies of up to 30% on your base premiums for CareShield Life. Given that premiums increase with age, the annual subsidies for older Singaporeans will also be higher to offset the higher annual premiums.
Those who need more assistance with their premium payment after subsidies will receive Additional Premium Support.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: Can my MediSave be used to pay for severe disability assessments?
questions.text:
MediSave cannot be used to cover the cost of any severe disability assessments.
However, all severe disability schemes (i.e. CareShield Life, MediSave Care, ElderShield, ElderFund and IDAPE) use the same severe disability assessment. If you are a CareShield Life policyholder undergoing a severe disability assessment for the first time, the cost of that assessment by an MOH-accredited assessor will be waived.
In other cases, the full cost of the severe disability assessment will be reimbursed if you are assessed to have severe disability. AIC will send you a letter with details of the reimbursement and the bank account it will be credited to.

questions.title: I am staying in a nursing home. Can I use MediSave Care/CareShield Life/ElderShield payouts to pay for the monthly bills?
questions.text: If you qualify to claim under MediSave Care/CareShield Life/ElderShield, you can arrange for the payouts to be paid directly to approved healthcare institutions, such as nursing homes, to cover your monthly bills.

questions.title: Will all ethics-related CME programmes offered by SMC approved MME CME providers qualify for MME core points?
questions.text:
CME programmes offered by approved MME CME providers that are not under any of the following 15 topics in the approved MME curriculum will not be regarded as MME CME activities (however they may be awarded normal CME points).
1. Professionalism / Medical Professionalism
2. Ethics (e.g. Four Boxes Approach, Ethical Analysis in Medicine, Public Health Ethics, Research Ethics)
3. Informed Consent and Medical Decision Making
4. Medical Records, Privacy and Confidentiality
5. Notification, Certification, & Dispensing
6. Medicine and the Law
7. Important Issues in Clinical Ethics – eg End of Life Issues, Transplant Ethics, Assisted Reproduction, Big Data
8. Professional Accountability, Medical Negligence and Risk Management
9. Communication Skills, Medical Report Writing and Personal Development
10. Practice Issues
11. Setting up Practice
12. Conflicts of Interests
13. Collegiality and Working in Teams
14. Telemedicine
15. Novel Therapy and Experimental treatment
Please note that for new MME CME providers, only approved MME CME activities offered from 1 January 2026 onwards will be eligible for the award of MME Core points.
topics: Continuing Professional/Medical Education / Mandatory Medical Ethics CME

questions.title: How do I view the Record of Payment (ROP)?
questions.text:
You can view up to 24 months of electronic ROP via CPF EZPay. To access this service, your company's authorised officers must be assigned the 'CPF EZPay' e-Service through Corppass portal, which enables access control at CSN level. For setup instructions, please visit cpf.gov.sg/corppassuserguide. Once configured, you may refer to our guide on viewing ROP within CPF EZPay.
As good record keeping practice, you should save a copy of your ROP. We do not provide retrieval of past ROPs. If you did not retain a copy of your past ROPs, you can seek other documents (e.g. company’s bank statement, payroll or financial statement).
Please write to us if you encountered technical difficulties to view the ROPs.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Can I opt out from the CareShield Life scheme after joining (e.g. if I cannot afford the premiums)?
questions.text:
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979, who were covered under the ElderShield 400 scheme and did not develop severe disability, were auto-enrolled to CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. You will not be able to opt out of CareShield Life as the deadline to opt out was 31 December 2023.
Those who are not auto-enrolled can choose to join CareShield Life. If you are in this group, you will have a 60-day free-look period from the commencement of your CareShield Life coverage, for you to review your decision.
The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to those who join CareShield Life, to ensure that no one who joins the scheme loses coverage due to financial difficulties. For this reason, after the applicable free-look periods, you will not be able to opt out from the scheme.
You may refer to the types of premium support available for more information. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.
CareShield Life is also mandatory for foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards and are born in 1979 or earlier, provided they do not have severe disability (if granted residency status from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025) or any disability (if granted residency status from 1 January 2026 onwards).

questions.title: If I have finished claiming my ElderShield 300/400 payouts, can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can choose to join CareShield Life even if you have already completed claiming your payouts under ElderShield 300/400. However, you may be required to undergo a disability assessment. Please note that you will not be eligible to join CareShield Life if you are unable to perform one or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).
However, you can tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes such as Home Caregiving Grant and ElderFund, and MediSave Care to complement your personal savings and family support, in meeting your long-term care needs. Government assistance schemes such as the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund can also help defray the cost of consumables and assistive devices.

questions.title: Can I join both CareShield Life and ElderShield to get double the protection?
questions.text:
You will not be able to be on both CareShield Life and ElderShield.
However, upgrading to CareShield Life will not affect your ElderShield Supplement plan if you already have one. If you are currently covered under ElderShield, you can upgrade to CareShield Life for higher and lifetime payouts. Your ElderShield coverage will be terminated upon joining CareShield Life. For more coverage, you can also purchase Supplement plans from private insurers.

questions.title: I do not have a CPF account. Can I still join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you do not have a CPF account, you will still be able to join CareShield Life. You can make your first premium payment via the following methods:
Opening a CPF account by making a top-up to your MediSave Account
A family member* can apply to take over as your premium payer using his/her MediSave savings. To do so, he/she may visit the Change Premium Payer e-Service and log in using his/her own Singpass to complete the "Change Premium Payer" transaction.
*Family member refers to the Insured's spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren.

questions.title: I have already paid for ElderShield premiums for this year. Will I get any refund if I apply to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The ElderShield premiums will be refunded if you join CareShield Life and your CareShield Life commencement date is in the same year as your ElderShield policy renewal.
For example, if you paid ElderShield Premiums in September 2021 (for your ElderShield policy renewal in 2021), and later joined CareShield Life in December 2021, the ElderShield premiums you have paid in September 2021 will be refunded to you.
The refund of ElderShield premiums (if any) will take place upon collection of the first CareShield Life premium.

questions.title: What Government subsidies or incentives are available to help me with my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
To ensure that CareShield Life premiums are affordable, the Government provides means-tested premium subsidies of up to 30% of premiums of CareShield Life, to help lower- to middle-income households.
The Government also provides Additional Premium Support for Singaporeans who are unable to pay their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: How often will the CareShield Life premiums increase?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums increase annually to support the annual increases in payouts, which help protect the value of payouts over time and keep up with rising long-term care costs.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. What are my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.
For those born in 1979 or earlier, your premium may have two components:
1. Base premium
All those born in 1979 or earlier and join CareShield Life will pay a base premium. Base premiums are paid from the age you join until age 67, or for a period of 10 years for those who join at age 59 or older.
Base premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts but will remain flat after age 67 if they remain payable.
2. Catch-up Component
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if your ElderShield profile is any of the following prior to joining CareShield Life:
You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life from 1 January 2022 onwards.
Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
The catch-up component ensures consistency with those in the same cohort who had been consistently insured under the ElderShield 400 scheme and joined CareShield Life earlier.
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is a flat amount paid across 10 years and is paid on top of the base premium.

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for older cohorts higher than younger cohorts?
questions.text:
The estimated CareShield Life premiums for all cohorts are actuarially determined and are designed to be not-for-profit.
CareShield Life premiums are meant to be paid from age 30 to 67, or until the insured makes a claim. Older cohorts joining CareShield Life will face higher annual premiums as they have fewer years to spread their premium payments as compared to younger cohorts. Older cohorts also have a higher risk of developing severe disability.
The Government will provide premium support for those born 1979 or earlier:
Lower- to middle-income Singapore residents will receive Means-tested Subsidies. Up to two-thirds of Singapore resident households will be eligible for CareShield Life subsidies of up to 30%.
Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier will receive Participation Incentives, spread over the first 10 years of their policy if they joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024.
Those in financial need who are unable to pay for their premiums after premium subsidies can apply for Additional Premium Support from the Government.
For more information on the types of premium support available, you may refer to this page. For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you may access the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why are CareShield Life premiums for females higher although their payouts are the same as males?
questions.text:
CareShield Life provides the same amount of expected benefits per dollar of premium paid for both women and men over their lifetimes. Compared to men, women generally live longer and have higher chances of developing severe disability, hence they are likely to receive longer CareShield Life coverage and more payouts over their lifetime. As men and women pay premiums for CareShield Life for the same number of years, the annual premiums for women need to be higher to account for their longer expected duration of payout over their lifetime.
We will provide support to lower-income women through the existing social support schemes for lower-income Singaporeans. For CareShield Life, the Government will also provide premium subsidies and support based on one's financial circumstances to ensure that premiums are affordable.

questions.title: How will Singaporeans' eligibility for CareShield Life means-tested premium subsidies be assessed?
questions.text: Means-tested premium subsidies for CareShield Life will depend on Singaporeans' household per capita income, the annual value of his or her residence, and the number of properties owned. Lower- and lower-middle income Singaporeans who own no more than one property, and live in residences with annual values up to $31,000 will be eligible for means-tested premium subsidies.

questions.title: I am covered under CareShield Life. What is Additional Premium Support and who can qualify?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help Singaporeans who cannot afford CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and payment by MediSave and have insufficient family support to rely on.
Please note that you will not be eligible for APS if you have an additional private medical insurance cover under an Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield. You will also not be eligible for APS if you are paying the premiums of someone else's Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under CareShield Life/ElderShield.

questions.title: How do I check the premiums payable under CareShield Life?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service allows individuals to view their personalised CareShield Life premiums and subsidies for the current policy year, and their estimated premiums and subsidies for upcoming policy years.

questions.title: Can the Supplements work with both CareShield Life and ElderShield?
questions.text: Specific Supplements may work with either ElderShield, CareShield Life, or both schemes. For more information on specific Supplement product, please approach your insurer or financial advisor.

questions.title: What happens if I do not pay the premiums I owe for ElderShield?
questions.text:
If you have paid the minimum required premiums for ElderShield, your policy will be converted to a paid-up policy.
Your potential payouts in the event of severe disability will depend on the total premiums paid. For more details on your payouts, please log in to Healthcare Dashboard using your Singpass.
However, if you have not paid the minimum required premiums, your policy will be terminated.

questions.title: How long will I be covered under ElderShield?
questions.text: ElderShield provides lifetime coverage to its insureds. You will be covered under ElderShield once you start paying your premiums. Coverage continues for the rest of your life upon completion of all premium payments under the Regular Premium Plan or a lump sum premium under the Single Premium Plan. You can submit a claim if you develop severe disability, so long as your total claims have not exceeded 60 months (for ElderShield 300) or 72 months (for ElderShield 400).

questions.title: What are the benefits of the ElderShield scheme?
questions.text:
ElderShield is a long-term care insurance scheme targeted at severe disability, especially in old age. ElderShield provides monthly payouts of $300 or $400 per month, for up to 72 months. Your plan's benefits depend on when you joined ElderShield.
Table 1: Payouts for ElderShield
If you joined ElderShield from September 2007 (inclusive)If you joined ElderShield between September 2002 and August 2007
ElderShield 400ElderShield 300
Payout Amount$400/month$300/month
Payout DurationUp to 72 months (six years)Up to 60 months (five years)
If you are also covered under ElderShield Supplements, you will receive additional benefits.

questions.title: How do I terminate my ElderShield policy?
questions.text: You can terminate your ElderShield via the Termination of ElderShield e-Service if you do not wish to continue to be covered under the scheme. However, you will lose all existing benefits, and you may have to go for a medical assessment if you wish to join CareShield Life. We encourage you to consider keeping your ElderShield policy to ensure you continue to have basic protection for long-term care.

questions.title: When is the last premium payable for ElderShield? Why did I receive a request for premiums payment after I turned 65 last year?
questions.text:
The ElderShield scheme collects premiums based on the insured's age as at their last birthday. The annual premium is payable until the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year.
For example, for a 40-year-old male (date of birth: 30 June 1978) on ElderShield 400, the final premium payable will be for the policy starting 30 April 2044. This is because the insured is still age 65 on 30 April 2044 even though he turned age 65 on 30 June 2043.

questions.title: Do I still need to pay premiums if I am eligible for ElderShield benefit claim payout?
questions.text: If you qualify for ElderShield benefit claim payout, you do not need to pay premiums if there is no change in your disability status.

questions.title: How much is my ElderShield premium?
questions.text: ElderShield premiums are based on the age at which you join the scheme, and the final premium payable is for the policy year in which you are still age 65 at the start of the policy year. The premium amount does not increase with age. You can find your premiums for ElderShield 400 and ElderShield 300.

questions.title: Which organisations are responsible for administering the CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care schemes?
questions.text: CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care are jointly administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) and Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB).

questions.title: When am I eligible to make a CareShield Life/ElderShield claim?
questions.text:
You are eligible to make a claim if you are covered under CareShield Life/ElderShield and have been assessed by an MOH accredited assessor as being unable to perform three or more of the following six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
Washing – the ability to wash in the bath or shower (including getting into and out of the bath or shower) or wash by other means
Dressing – the ability to put on, take off, secure and unfasten all garments and, as appropriate, any braces, artificial limbs or other surgical or medical appliances.
Feeding – the ability to feed oneself food after it has been prepared and made available.
Toileting – the ability to use the toilet or manage bowel and bladder function through the use of protective undergarments, such as diapers or surgical appliances if appropriate.
Moving or Walking Around – the ability to move indoors from room to room on level surfaces.
Transferring – the ability to move from a bed to an upright chair or wheelchair, and vice versa.

questions.title: How do I update my bank account details for my CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text:
You can log in to AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) with your Singpass on and go to “Manage My Schemes” > “Change in Scheme Details” to update your bank account information for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claim payouts.
If you are updating the bank account on behalf of a care recipient who lacks mental capacity, you will need to submit a Mental Incapacity Certification if you have not already done so. For more details, please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions on AIC’s website.

questions.title: How do I make a CareShield Life claim?
questions.text:
If you are covered under CareShield Life and would like to make a claim, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated CareShield insured, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: What is MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is a long-term care scheme that allows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 30 and above with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their own and/or their spouse’s MediSave for their long-term care needs. This is provided they have set aside a minimum amount to ensure sufficient MediSave for other medical expenses.
The table below shows the required MediSave balances and the corresponding monthly withdrawal quantum for eligible individuals.1
MediSave BalanceMonthly Withdrawal Quantum
$20,000 and above$200
$15,000 and above$150
$10,000 and above$100
$5,000 and above$50
Below $5,000Nil
1Eligible individuals can withdraw from their spouse's MediSave Account if their own MediSave balance is insufficient, provided the spouse has a MediSave balance of at least $5,000. Withdrawals from the spouse's MediSave are also subject to the same balance thresholds, and the total combined withdrawal from both accounts is capped at $200 per month.

questions.title: How do I apply for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
To apply for MediSave Care, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated member, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: When am I eligible to withdraw under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
You are eligible to withdraw under MediSave Care if you have been assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor as being unable to perform three or more of these six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
Washing – the ability to wash in the bath or shower (including getting into and out of the bath or shower) or wash by other means.
Dressing – the ability to put on, take off, secure and unfasten all garments and, as appropriate, any braces, artificial limbs or other surgical or medical appliances.
Feeding – the ability to feed oneself food after it has been prepared and made available.
Toileting – the ability to use the toilet or manage bowel and bladder function through the use of protective undergarments, such as diapers or surgical appliances, if appropriate.
Walking or Moving Around – the ability to move indoors from room to room on level surfaces.
Transferring – the ability to move from a bed to an upright chair or wheelchair, and vice versa.

questions.title: Can I withdraw under MediSave Care for overseas treatment?
questions.text: Withdrawals of up to $200 per month under the MediSave Care scheme are provided in cash, and claimants have the option to use the cash for their long-term care needs, either locally or overseas.

questions.title: Why do I need to set aside the MediSave balance of at least $5,000 to be eligible for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is designed to help Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents set aside sufficient savings for their hospitalisation expenses and certain high-cost outpatient treatments such as cancer treatments.
The minimum balance of $5,000 required by MediSave Care ensures that individuals have MediSave available to cover medical expenses such as MediShield Life premiums or hospitalisations.

questions.title: Will ElderShield insurers continue selling Supplements?
questions.text: The ElderShield insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern Life & Income Insurance) will continue administering Supplements that complement the current ElderShield schemes.

questions.title: Can I purchase CareShield Life Supplement(s) if I have pre-existing illnesses?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are products by private insurers who set the underwriting decisions based on commercial and actuarial considerations.
You may refer to a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). For more information about Supplement plans, you may consider speaking to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers.

questions.title: What happens if I stop paying for my Supplements if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: Supplement plans will lapse if you stop paying premiums. For more information, refer to your specific Supplement policy documents or consult your insurer.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. If I have private insurance coverage similar to CareShield Life, can I be exempted from universal coverage?
questions.text: CareShield Life will be universal for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later. Private insurance can still play a complementary role by providing additional benefits above and beyond such basic coverage.

questions.title: If my Supplements overlap with CareShield Life, will insurers provide a refund if I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As Supplement policies are separately administered by the private insurers, they will remain active as long as you continue paying your premiums and do not terminate your coverage. Your existing Supplement policies will not be affected by CareShield Life. You will also be able to make a claim under both CareShield Life and your Supplement.
For further advice, consider speaking with your financial advisor.

questions.title: Should I join CareShield Life if I already have an existing ElderShield & ElderShield Supplement plan that provides similar coverage, e.g. lifetime payouts?
questions.text:
Your existing Supplement plan will not be affected, even if you join CareShield Life. You will continue to pay the same premiums for your Supplements and enjoy the same benefits for as long as you are covered. You will also be able to make claims under both CareShield Life and your Supplement plan.
You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support, and consider speaking to your financial advisor on whether you should upgrade to CareShield Life.

questions.title: How do I update my residential address with ICA if I am a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) holder?
questions.text:
The LTVP holder may submit a request for the change of residential address using his/her Singpass at the e-Service.
You may contact us via the enquiry form for further assistance.
topics: LTVP-Related Matters / Update Passport Details/ Address For LTVP Holder

questions.title: How can I update my local address as a Student's Pass Holder?
questions.text:
Students, with valid Singpass account, can access the e-Service to report change of address with their Singpass.
You may contact us via the enquiry form for further assistance.

questions.title: What happens to my MediShield Life/CareShield Life cover if my premium payer passes away?
questions.text: When your premium payer passes away, you will automatically become the payer for your own Healthcare coverage. If you have insufficient MediSave, you will be notified to either top up your MediSave (visit Top up MediSave Account form with your Singpass) or approach a family member to help you pay the premiums using his/her MediSave by visiting the Change Payer e-Service to complete the transaction.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay MediShield Life, CareShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums for my family members?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay the MediShield Life, CareShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums for yourself and your family members (spouse, parent, child, sibling or grandparent).
You can also pay for other family members (e.g. uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces, parents in-laws), if they meet the following conditions:
They are financially dependent on you; and
Both they and their family members (spouse, parent, child, sibling or grandchild) do not have sufficient MediSave for their premiums.
To become a premium payer, you can submit a Change Payer for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield.

questions.title: Why are Singaporeans not covered by CareShield Life from birth?
questions.text:
The priority of CareShield Life is to provide protection against severe disability during old age, when Singaporeans are most likely to need long-term care.
There are various support schemes available for families caring for their loved ones below age 30 who have severe disability, e.g. subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), and subsidies for therapy services at KK Hospital and the National University Hospital.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after Government subsidies and other means of support.

questions.title: CareShield Life is still targeted at those with severe disability i.e. unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. Why was this retained?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is targeted at severe disability, so that premiums can be kept affordable for all insured.
If you are a Singaporean with mild or moderate disabilities, and need long-term care, you can tap on means-tested Government subsidies for long-term care services, as well as other Government assistance schemes (e.g. the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund) to complement your personal savings and family support.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund/ComCare can also help you pay for these long-term care costs, should you be unable to afford long-term care services.
If you wish to cover yourself for less severe disabilities, you can consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: If I reside overseas, can I suspend my premium payment for CareShield Life?
questions.text: Premium payments for CareShield Life cannot be suspended for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents residing overseas. Individuals insured under CareShield Life will receive monthly cash payouts in the event of severe disability even when residing overseas. Similarly, insured under ElderShield can file claims from abroad and receive payouts to support their care costs wherever they may be. This applies even for those who have permanently relocated abroad.

questions.title: If I am born in 1979 or earlier and have severe disability, can I join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are unable to perform one or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. have disability), you will not be eligible to join CareShield Life.
If you are currently insured under ElderShield and have not made a claim yet, you may claim from ElderShield instead. Depending on the plan you have, ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts of $300 per month for up to 60 months (under ElderShield 300 plan), or $400 per month for up to 72 months (under ElderShield 400 plan).
If you have received all your ElderShield payouts, you may tap on Government subsidies and various Government assistance schemes (such as the Home Caregiving Grant, ElderFund) for assistance. You may also approach the Medical Social Workers at the health institution you are seeking medical treatment from or your nearest Social Service Office (SSO). For more information, please refer to this page on MediFund or this page on ComCare.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen born in 1979 or earlier and was covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024. How much CareShield Life participation incentives am I eligible for?
questions.text:
The Total CareShield Life Participation Incentives you are eligible for will be spread equally over 10 years and will be used to offset the annual premium payable in that year.
