These Participation Incentives will not apply if you are covered under CareShield Life after 31 December 2024.

questions.title: Why are Government subsidies provided for CareShield Life and not for ElderShield?
questions.text:
Government subsidies are provided for CareShield Life as it is a mandatory scheme for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or after, unlike ElderShield which is optional.
While CareShield Life is also optional for those born before 1979, they would not be able to cancel their CareShield Life cover after 60 days free-look period. Premium subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households pay their CareShield Life premiums. On the other hand, ElderShield policyholders have the option to opt out or cancel their policy anytime.

questions.title: I am going to be 29 years old when CareShield Life is launched. If I have severe disability, will I be able to join the scheme earlier?
questions.text:
Under CareShield Life, premiums paid by insureds are designed to be risk-pooled within their own generation, and used to cover their claims in the event of severe disability.
As there is no risk pool for your cohort when the scheme is launched, your cohort will be covered under CareShield Life when you turn 30 years old, even if you have severe disability.
You may refer to Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans who have developed disability and their caregivers on the SG Enable's website or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.

questions.title: Why is there a need to start CareShield Life earlier at age 30?
questions.text:
Starting CareShield Life at age 30 provides insureds with earlier coverage protection and allows them to spread premium payments over a longer period, hence reducing the annual premiums payable.
By age 30, most Singaporeans would have started working and contributing to their MediSave. They should be able to cover their CareShield Life premiums without out-of pocket expenses. Hence, this is a good time to start planning for their long-term care needs.

questions.title: Do I have to continue paying for CareShield Life premiums in the event of severe disability?
questions.text:
If you have developed severe disability and are eligible to claim under CareShield Life, you will not need to pay premiums as long as there is no change in your disability status. However, please note that the first premium payment is still required if you have developed severe disability in the first policy year.
Premium payment will resume if you no longer have severe disability.

questions.title: How can I apply for Additional Premium Support to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their CareShield Life premiums after premium subsidies and have limited family support.
There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time. You will be invited to apply for APS should you have insufficient MediSave savings and limited family support to pay your premiums.
If you are assessed to be eligible for the scheme, the Government will grant APS to you to pay for your MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) premiums.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: If there are insufficient funds in my MediSave Account, can I use my Ordinary Account/Special Account monies to pay for my MediShield Life, CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
The savings in your CPF accounts are for specific uses. Savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account are primarily for housing and retirement, while savings in your MediSave are for the payment of selected healthcare insurance premiums (such as MediShield Life and CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums) and hospitalisation expenses.
Thus, you are unable to use the savings in your Ordinary Account and Special Account to pay for your healthcare insurance premiums.
If you do not have sufficient MediSave to pay your premiums, you will be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS).
Alternatively, you may also top up your MediSave Account (visit Top up MediSave Account form with your Singpass) or approach a family member to help you pay the premiums using his/her MediSave by visiting the Change Payer e-Service to complete the transaction.

questions.title: I have fully paid off my housing loan. Why is my title document not released to me?
questions.text: Effective 3 Nov 2014, if you have fully paid off your housing loan and used your CPF monies to buy your property, your title document will be safe-kept at the Land Titles Registry, Singapore Land Authority (SLA) after the mortgage is discharged pursuant to an arrangement with CPF Board under the Paperless Title Scheme.
topics: Registration of Property Transaction / Title Document

questions.title: Who can I contact for more assistance or to give feedback?
questions.text: You can contact the SLA staff indicated in the Tender Documents if you need further help on the tender. For enquiries on other SLA services and other general enquiries, you can call 6323 9829 or submit them here.

questions.title: How do I find out the particulars of the owner of a HDB flat?
questions.text: You can find out the particulars of the owner of the HDB flat by applying for "Image of HDB Leases" in INLIS. The photocopy of the Lease will show the name of the owner and any encumbrances affecting the property. As Leases are not available in digital format, SLA will send a hardcopy to you by fax. You can also request for it to be delivered by post.
topics: Requisition of Land Information / Land Register Search

questions.title: I lost the title deed for my HDB flat a few years back and I have not applied for a new one. Will I be able to get a photocopy for my records?
questions.text:
Yes, you can apply for a copy via INLIS. As Leases are not available in digital format, a hardcopy will be sent to you by fax or alternatively, you can request for it to be delivered to you by post. Please contact INLIS Helpdesk at 6238 9353 if you require assistance.
As a photocopy of Lease is not a document of title, it cannot be used for registration purpose. If you need the Lease for registration purpose, you will have to apply for the issue of a Subsidiary Certificate of Title (SCT). Please engage a lawyer or check with HDB on the Application for SCT.
topics: Requisition of Land Information / Land Register Search

questions.title: How does SLA determine the premium of the remnant land?
questions.text:
The premium payable for remnant land will be as follows:
a) For Place of Worship and Civic and Community Institution use, remnant land will be valued for sale based on 50% of the full land value, determined by applying the factor of 5/7 to the applicable Land Betterment Charge (LBC) rate.
b) For Residential, Commercial, Industrial uses and uses other than those set out in subparagraph (a) above or where the sale of the lands would result in gross floor area transfer, the lands will be valued for sale based on 100% of the full land value, determined by applying the factor of 10/7 to the applicable LBC rate.
c) SLA reserves the right in all cases to determine the land premium payable in consultation with the Chief Valuer. This can occur in situations where the use does not clearly fit into any of the existing Use Groups or where the remnant land is assessed to have synergistic value.
Remnant Lands with Synergistic Value
Where the remnant land adds considerable value when amalgamated with the adjoining land parcel, such land is deemed to create synergistic value to the amalgamated land. Examples include enabling the adjoining private land to achieve a higher Gross Plot Ratio or allowing a substandard private land to be redeveloped into a development with standard plot size. The rate for remnant lands with synergistic value will be based on the higher of:
a) 50% of the enhancement in land value of the amalgamated site as assessed by the Chief Valuer, or
b) 100% of the full land value determined by applying the factor of 10/7 to the applicable LBC rate.
Formula to determine Land Premium
The formula to determine the land premium of remnant land based on LBC rates is as such:
Land premium = Area of Remnant Land x Master Plan GPR (A) x Applicable LBC Rate (B) x 5/7 or 10/7 x Leasehold Factor (C)
1. Master Plan Gross Plot Ratio
Identify the Master Plan gross plot ratio and zoning from URA’s Master Plan from URA Space (URA SPACE).
2. Applicable LBC rate
Step 1 – Determine Geographical Location of Subject Property
Find out from OneMap the major roads surrounding the subject property.
Next, identify the geographical sector number of the subject property from URA SPACE (URA SPACE)
Step 2 – Determine Use Group of the Subject Property
Identify the use group of the subject property from the Use Group Tables from URA SPACE (URA SPACE) e.g. residential (landed dwelling-house) comes under use group B1.
Step 3 – Determine applicable LBC rate for the Subject Property
Determine the applicable LBC rate for the subject property from the Table of LBC Rates. The applicable LBC rate at the date of Notice of Preliminary Terms and Conditions, offer, or closed tender (whichever is applicable) will be used.
Once you have selected the appropriate Table of LBC rates, match the geographical sector number of the subject property against the use group of the subject property to determine the applicable LBC rate.
3. Leasehold Factor
The leasehold factor is only applicable for leases that have 99 years or less in tenure. Where remnant lands are sold on a leasehold basis for a tenure less than or equal to 99 years, the premium will be adjusted accordingly using the Leasehold Table as attached here.
topics: Sale of Land / Sale of Remnant Land

questions.title: Where can I find more information on Additional Premium Support?
questions.text: For further information on Additional Premium Support, please visit this link or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: I am receiving other disability assistance schemes such as Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme or Home Caregiving Grant. Can I qualify for CareShield Life or ElderShield claims?
questions.text:
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS) and Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) are moderate disability schemes, which support individuals who require some assistance with three or more Activities of Daily Living.
In contrast, CareShield Life and ElderShield are severe disability schemes that require individuals to be unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (i.e. they must require significant assistance) in order to be eligible for a claim.
As the eligibility criteria for CareShield Life and ElderShield are more stringent, an assessment by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor is required to determine if an individual qualifies for these claims.

questions.title: Why can’t CareShield Life/ElderShield automatically reimburse long-term care costs the way MediShield Life does for hospital bills?
questions.text:
Unlike MediShield Life, which covers large hospital bills, CareShield Life/ElderShield provides monthly cash payouts to offer individuals and their caregivers greater flexibility in choosing their preferred care arrangements. This ensures that they are not restricted to specific long-term care services in order to receive support.
For example, some may prefer to stay in a familiar home environment and opt for home-based care, while others may choose to receive care from a healthcare provider such as a nursing home.
Given long-term care needs and preferences differ widely, cash payouts allow you to decide how best to use the support.

questions.title: Will my ElderShield premiums change due to Government administration?
questions.text: Since November 2021, the Government has taken over the administration of ElderShield from insurers. You will continue to pay the same premiums and enjoy the same benefits under ElderShield for as long as you are covered. In the event that the actual claims are lower than projected, premium rebates will be given to eligible ElderShield insureds.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later and am terminally ill but do not have severe disability. Can I be exempted from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As CareShield Life is universal for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, there are no exemptions even though you are terminally ill. As long as you are covered under CareShield Life, you can still receive monthly payouts in the event of severe disability.
The Government will support Singaporeans who are unable to afford their premiums, so that no one will lose their coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: When do I have to pay for my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life premium is payable annually. The premium payable will be automatically deducted from you or your premium payer’s MediSave within one month from your policy anniversary.
You can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to view your or your dependant(s)’s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life coverage and premium information under the “CareShield Life/ElderShield” and “MediShield Life” section respectively.

questions.title: I am born in 1980 or later. What do I need to do to be covered by CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are born in 1980 or later, you are automatically covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020, or when you turn 30, whichever is later.
If you are born between 1980 and 1990 (i.e. aged 30 to 40 in 2020), you would have received a CareShield Life welcome package informing you of your CareShield Life cover, by 2 September 2020 or up to two months before your 30th birthday, whichever is later.
If you are born after 1990 (i.e. aged below 30 in 2020), you will receive a CareShield Life Welcome Package before you reach age 30.

questions.title: What will be the rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
The rate of premium and payout increases for CareShield Life will be reviewed regularly based on actuarial principles, taking into account factors such as changes in claims experience and longevity. This is important to keep the fund sustainable.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. Actual future premiums and monthly payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. With the premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases* from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
*Premiums increase per year excludes GST.

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life payouts stop increasing once insureds stop paying premiums (e.g., when they make a claim or turn 67)?
questions.text:
Increases in CareShield Life payouts are supported by premium adjustments to ensure the scheme remains financially sustainable. Those who wish to have payouts that continue to increase throughout their lifetime may consider purchasing Supplements. Insurers designing these Supplements may also take into account the features of CareShield Life.
CareShield Life payouts are designed to complement existing Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, helping the insured meet their basic long-term care costs. Additionally, they can make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account(s) under MediSave Care.
For Singaporeans who are still unable to afford their care even after Government subsidies, CareShield Life payouts and personal savings, further assistance is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.

questions.title: How was the starting payout of $600 per month for CareShield Life determined?
questions.text:
Long-term care costs vary depending on an individual's needs, care arrangements, and available financial resources.
In determining the enhanced payout amount, the ElderShield Review Committee considered the basic long-term care costs across different services and settings, other sources of long-term care funding, such as Government subsidies and assistance schemes, community support, personal savings, family support and Government-funded safety nets like MediFund or ComCare, as well as the need to balance benefits with premium affordability. As part of the overall enhancements to long-term care financing, CareShield Life provides better protection and assurance for Singaporean's basic long-term care needs.
If you would like additional coverage, you may consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: What is the monthly payout amount for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Successful CareShield Life claimant can receive monthly payouts for as long as they develop severe disability and remain insured under CareShield Life. This is designed to provide better protection against the uncertainty of long-term care costs.
The monthly payout is $689 in 2026, and increases annually until the insured reaches age 67 or makes a successful claim, whichever comes first.
For example, if a 30-year-old individual joins CareShield Life in 2026, develops severe disability and makes a claim in 2026, he/she will receive $689 per month for the entire duration of severe disability. However, if a 30-year-old individual joins CareShield Life in 2026, and only develops severe disability at age 67 or later, he/she will receive $2,941 per month upon a successful claim, for the entire duration of severe disability.
For insureds born in 1954 and earlier who joined CareShield Life at age 67 or above, the monthly payout will be fixed at $612 per month once a successful claim is made.

questions.title: Can lump sum payouts, death benefits or "No-claim Bonus” be provided as incentives for healthy living or meeting the two Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) criteria under CareShield Life/ElderShield?
questions.text:
CareShield Life/ElderShield is designed to provide basic financial protection against long-term care costs through monthly cash payouts to insureds with severe disability to cover their ongoing costs. It is not designed or priced to cover payouts to insureds who remain healthy.
If you would like additional coverage such as lump sum payouts and death benefits, you can consider purchasing Supplements from the private insurers.

questions.title: If I top up my MediSave to pay my Healthcare premiums, does it count towards the MediSave amount that a self-employed person needs to contribute?
questions.text: The top-up to your MediSave for the purpose of paying your Healthcare premiums, cannot be used to offset your MediSave payable under the Self-Employed scheme. For self-employed persons who wish to make payment for your outstanding MediSave payable, please visit Manage your MediSave payable.

questions.title: If I am self-employed/retired/become unemployed before age 67, will I be able to afford CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text: The Government will provide CareShield Life premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income insureds. For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support. No one will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: What if CareShield Life premiums result in me not meeting the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is an estimate of what you need for your basic subsidised healthcare expenses in old age. As CareShield Life premium payments will stop at the re-employment age of 67 for most Singaporeans, the Government does not expect premiums to have a significant impact on the BHS.
While you are not required to top up your MediSave if you do not meet the BHS, you and your family members are strongly encouraged to consider doing so.

questions.title: Why not extend premium payment for life for CareShield Life, like MediShield Life?
questions.text: The current premium payment duration is sufficient to improve CareShield Life premium affordability, while still keeping premium payment largely during one’s working years.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. Why are there no subsidies for the catch-up component when it looks so substantial?
questions.text:
The catch-up component is not subsidised to ensure parity in premium subsidies across different groups within those born in 1979 or earlier.
If you are unable to afford your CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support to help you with your CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: What is the catch-up component under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You will need to pay a catch-up component, on top of the base premium, if your ElderShield profile is any of the following prior to joining CareShield Life:
You are an existing ElderShield 300 insured.
You are not insured under ElderShield or have opted into ElderShield late.
You are an existing ElderShield 400 insured who joined CareShield Life from 1 January 2022 onwards.
Your ElderShield 300/400 policies have become reduced paid-up (i.e. you stopped paying premiums after a minimum number of years of premium payment, which qualifies you for a lower payout amount).
The catch-up component ensures consistency with those in the same cohort who had been consistently insured under the ElderShield 400 scheme and joined CareShield Life earlier.
The catch-up component will also be applicable to foreigners who become Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards.
The catch-up component is a flat amount paid across 10 years and is paid on top of the base premium.

questions.title: Will the 2025 increase in Annual Value (AV) impact my eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The disbursement of social support schemes (e.g. CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, MediShield Life Premium Subsidies) will not be affected by the revision of Annual Values (AVs) in 2025 as AVs as of 2024 will be used to determine scheme eligibility in 2025. The Government will continue to review our social support schemes to ensure that Singaporeans in need of support receive it.

questions.title: How are CareShield Life premiums calculated?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are calculated such that each age cohort of insureds pay sufficient premiums to support their expected payouts as a cohort. This ensures the long-term sustainability of the insurance fund.
While CareShield Life insureds are younger, premiums collected are naturally more than payouts in that year due to fewer claims. However, the premiums collected will be carried over to support the payouts in the event of severe disability in the future.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews factors like changes in claims experience and longevity and advises the Government on premium adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the Council’s advice on premium adjustments.
CareShield Life is managed by the Government on a not-for-profit basis. Any excess premiums will be used to benefit insureds and there are legal safeguards to ensure the Government cannot divert CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund monies for non-prescribed uses.

questions.title: What will be my total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term?
questions.text:
To ensure sustainability and affordability of CareShield Life, the CareShield Life Council will consider the prevailing trends and regularly advise the Government on adjusting the premiums and payouts in line with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
Hence, the Government is unable to provide the total CareShield Life premiums payable for the full premium payment term, as actual future premiums and payouts will vary depending on the regular adjustments.

questions.title: I have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Why is it not reflected in the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text: If you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, your appeal may still be processing and the outcome may not be reflected. If you require assistance with your latest appeal or form submission, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: I have existing private insurance that covers permanent/total disability. Can I claim from both my private insurance and CareShield Life?
questions.text:
You can claim from both your private insurance and CareShield Life at the same time. These are separate insurance policies with different coverage terms, so claiming from one does not affect your eligibility to claim from the other.
The assessment criteria for disability may vary between your private insurance and CareShield Life. Please consult your private insurer for details on your specific coverage.

questions.title: How are my monthly CareShield Life payouts determined?
questions.text:
Monthly CareShield Life payouts are designed to help cover basic long-term care costs, which can vary depending on your care needs and arrangements, whether you live at home, go to a care centre, or move into residential care. Individuals finance these costs differently, depending on their personal financial resources and circumstances.
The starting payout from CareShield Life is about $600 per month. This helps reduce out-of-pocket expenses by supplementing your personal savings (including MediSave) and family support. Additional support is also available through government subsidies, assistance schemes, and community support, especially for lower income Singaporeans. If you wish to have additional insurance coverage, you can consider purchasing supplements on top of CareShield Life.
You are strongly encouraged to plan early and consider your future income, long-term care arrangements, and how much insurance coverage and personal savings you may need to support your choices.

questions.title: Can the pool of assessors for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care be expanded to include Singapore-registered doctors, therapists or nurses?
questions.text:
If you have developed severe disability and wish to make a claim, you will need to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.
A trained and accredited severe disability assessor will determine whether you meet the criteria for being unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). To enhance accessibility, we have expanded the pool of assessors to include trained therapists and nurses.
All assessors have undergone a rigorous training programme to learn how to assess a patient’s level of disability. Through the training, assessors are equipped to assess an individual’s ability to perform the six ADLs, including specific components of each ADL to take into account, what factors to consider when an individual is cognitively impaired, and what should be done if any individual’s functional ability fluctuates over time. As this is a complex process, the training and accreditation is necessary to ensure that disability assessments are conducted with a high degree of rigour and consistency.
The Government is also exploring the recognition of equivalent assessments conducted by qualified healthcare professionals such as doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who are providing care to the patient. In such cases, the patients do not need a separate disability assessment. Today, residents of nursing home can approach their nursing home to submit the Resident's Assessment Form in place of the disability assessment.
MOH and AIC will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will publish more information on their respective websites.

questions.title: What does it mean that CareShield Life payouts remain fixed based on the year you start receiving them?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life payouts will increase by 4%* each year, reaching $689 per month in 2026 and will stop increasing once you make a successful claim or turn 67 years old (whichever comes first).
For example, if you start claiming from CareShield Life in 2026 at age 67 or younger, you will receive $689 per month for as long as you have severe disability.
*The payouts will increase by 4% each year until 2030, after which they will be subject to review.

questions.title: How much should I set aside for my long-term care needs?
questions.text:
Long-term care costs will vary across individuals due to differing care needs and arrangements.
Individuals will also have different financing sources. For instance, Singaporeans with higher incomes will qualify for a lower level of subsidies for their care, and will need to draw more from other financing sources. In addition to existing Government subsidies and assistance schemes, those who require additional funding can also make monthly cash withdrawals of up to $200 from their MediSave from 1 October 2020. You can also consider supplementing your basic CareShield Life/ElderShield insurance with private savings or Supplements from the private insurers.
You are strongly encouraged to plan early and consider your future income, long term care arrangement preferences and how much insurance coverage and personal savings will be needed to finance these arrangements.

questions.title: Why is CareShield Life/ElderShield necessary for Singaporeans' long-term care needs?
questions.text:
Growing need for long-term care
As Singapore's population ages, more people will need long-term care. As one ages, the risk of severe disability increases. The expected median duration for which individuals with severe disability remain in disability is around four years, but three in ten remain in severe disability for 10 years or more.
Savings alone may not be enough
It is increasingly challenging to rely only on personal and family savings to pay for your long-term care needs, as not only are family sizes shrinking, the duration of severe disability and the costs of long-term care will vary for each individual.
Managing the cost of long-term care with CareShield Life/ElderShield
Long-term care insurance schemes like CareShield Life and ElderShield help Singaporeans to pool their risks together within their cohort so that each Singaporean within that cohort has basic financial protection against the uncertainty and variability of the cost of long-term care. They complement other long-term care financing sources, such as Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support.

questions.title: Are we eligible for higher subsidies if I/my family member am/is placed in a nursing home with higher fees?
questions.text:
For individuals who require nursing home care, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will work closely with the individual and family members to identify a suitable nursing home, taking into account the individual's needs and family's preferences, including financial considerations.
The Government provides subsidies to help with the costs of long-term care. The amount of subsidies each individual is eligible for is determined by means-testing and is not dependent on the fees charged by the nursing homes. Individuals from lower-income households who meet the eligibility criteria will receive higher subsidies under the means-testing framework.
If you require additional assistance, you can tap on financial assistance schemes such as MediFund. Many nursing homes are also run by voluntary welfare organisations, and they may tap on charitable donations to provide further financial support to their residents after all other means of financial assistance and resources are exhausted.

questions.title: How do I access long-term care services?
questions.text:
If you have long-term care needs assessed by qualified healthcare professionals, medical social workers and/or administrative staff at public hospitals and/or Government-funded long-term care service providers can assist you with your referral to long-term care services. They can also assist with your application for Government subsidies for long-term care services, and advise on the subsidy quantum you are eligible for.
You can also contact the Agency for Integrated Care at 1800-650-6060 or via the AIC website to find out more about long-term care services.

questions.title: Do I need to pay for the CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care disability assessment?
questions.text:
The fees for clinic-based and non-clinic-based severe disability assessments are $100 and $250 respectively.
If you are applying for CareShield Life:
The fee for your first severe disability assessment will be waived, regardless of the outcome. For any subsequent assessments, you will only be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.
If you are applying for other severe disability schemes (i.e., ElderShield or MediSave Care):
You will need to pay the assessment fee upfront to the MOH-accredited assessor. The fee will be reimbursed if you are assessed to have a severe disability.

questions.title: If I develop severe disability, can I withdraw up to $200 per month from my own MediSave and another $200 from my spouse’s MediSave under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
If you are eligible for MediSave Care, you can only withdraw up to a combined total of $200 per month from your own and/or your spouse’s MediSave.
Example
Husband applies to withdraw $200 monthly from his own MediSave. That is the maximum withdrawal limit allowed from his own and/or his spouse’s MediSave.
If the husband has $12,000 in his MediSave, he can withdraw $100 monthly from his own MediSave. If his wife’s MediSave balance is at least $10,000, he can apply to withdraw an additional $100 monthly from her MediSave, totalling $200 per month in MediSave Care withdrawals.
MediSave Balances and corresponding Monthly Withdrawal Quantum

Monthly Withdrawal Quantum

questions.title: Can an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor certify the applicant’s mental capacity for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims?
questions.text:
A mental capacity assessment can be carried out by any doctor registered with the Singapore Medical Council for the purpose of claiming under CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care. If you require a mental capacity assessment, it is advisable to check with your assessor beforehand to confirm whether they are able to perform it, before booking a disability assessment appointment.
Depending on the applicant’s condition and needs, some cases may require a more detailed or complex mental capacity assessment that could take more time. In such cases, the assessor may charge an additional fee on top of the disability assessment fee.

questions.title: I am the family member or caregiver of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) Patient. Can I receive CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on their behalf?
questions.text:
You may nominate your own bank account to receive monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts on behalf of a Mentally Incapacitated (MI) patient. However, if the payout is not made to the patient or their nursing home, the family member or caregiver must obtain a deputyship within 12 months to prevent the suspension of payouts. This measure is in place to safeguard the patient’s interests.
For more details, please refer to the Frequently Asked Questions on AIC’s website.

questions.title: Can I withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care?
questions.text:
MediSave is a personal savings Account without risk-pooling benefits, and withdrawals are limited to the amount saved during your working years. The $200 monthly withdrawal limit under MediSave Care was set to ensure that sufficient MediSave is set aside for other medical purposes such as hospitalisation expenses and selected outpatient treatments. Hence, you will not be able to withdraw more than $200 per month under MediSave Care.
If you are unable to pay for your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, additional assistance is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.
The Government also regularly reviews the MediSave Care withdrawal limits to ensure that basic long-term care costs remain affordable for Singaporeans.

questions.title: Are there alternative documents I can submit for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claims in place of a severe disability assessment?
questions.text:
The Government is exploring the recognition of equivalent assessments conducted by qualified healthcare professionals such as doctors, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, and registered nurses who provide care to the patient. In such cases, patients need not undergo a separate severe disability assessment. Today, patients staying in a nursing home can already seek assistance from their nursing home to submit the Resident’s Assessment Form in place of the severe disability assessment.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will progressively roll out the use of such equivalent assessments and will publish more information on their respective websites.

questions.title: Can I be assessed by my own doctor or therapist for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care claim eligibility?
questions.text: To apply for any of the severe disability schemes, you need to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. You can check whether your family doctor (GP)/own doctor/healthcare professional is on the list of MOH-accredited severe disability assessors available on the AIC website. If they are not, you will need to make an appointment with one of the assessors on the list for the assessment.

questions.title: Why is the ElderFund payout ($250) higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount ($200)?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is designed to complement insurance schemes such as CareShield Life/ElderShield/Supplement payouts, Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support, to help individuals better meet their long-term care financing needs. The Government determined the MediSave Care withdrawal amount by considering the basic long-term care costs across various services and settings, other available sources of long-term care funding, and the need to maintain MediSave adequacy.
In contrast, ElderFund is targeted at helping lower-income Singaporeans who are unable to benefit from CareShield Life or ElderShield and have low MediSave balances for their long-term care needs.
That explains why the ElderFund payout of $250 is higher than the MediSave Care withdrawal amount of $200.

questions.title: What if I have insufficient MediSave balances for my healthcare and long-term care expenses?
questions.text:
If your MediSave Account is depleted, you may tap on your spouse's MediSave for MediSave Care withdrawals, and use your family members' MediSave for other healthcare treatments.
You may also apply for additional support through means-tested Government assistance schemes such as ElderFund and Home Caregiving Grant to cover your long-term care costs. If you are still unable to afford your care even after Government subsidies and other means of support, further assistance are available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: Why is the withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care based on my MediSave Account balance?
questions.text:
MediSave is used to cover a wide range of expenses, including health insurance premiums, hospitalisation, day surgery and outpatient bills such as chemotherapy and dialysis.
The withdrawal quantum under MediSave Care is carefully calibrated to ensure that Singaporeans have sufficient savings in their MediSave Account to meet their basic healthcare needs.

questions.title: Why am I unable to undergo a severe disability assessment for CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care during my hospitalisation?
questions.text:
While you are receiving treatment at the hospital, your disability condition may still be changing, which can affect the outcome of your long-term care scheme application. As such, severe disability assessments are not recommended while you are hospitalised.
Instead, our focus is on accrediting healthcare professionals in the community, such as the GPs, and clinicians within the long-term care sector who can assess your disability status once your condition has stabilised.

questions.title: If I have developed severe disability, can I make MediSave Care withdrawals from my spouse's MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR) with severe disability, you can make MediSave Care withdrawals from your own and your spouse’s MediSave.
Non-SC or PR who wish to make MediSave Care withdrawals from your SC or PR spouse's MediSave may be assessed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to approval.

questions.title: Why is MediSave Care restricted to individuals aged 30 and above?
questions.text:
MediSave Care is not applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents below the age of 30 as they are significantly less likely to develop severe disability and need long-term care. They also tend to have lower MediSave balances based on employment history.
Those under the age of 30 who require assistance can tap on various support schemes such as subsidies for early intervention programmes under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), subsidies for therapy services at the KK Women's and Children's Hospital and National University Hospital, and means-tested Government assistance schemes such as the Home Caregiving Grant (HCG), in meeting their long-term care needs.
For Singaporeans who are unable to afford care even after receiving Government subsidies and support from other schemes, additional help is available through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.

questions.title: Will I continue getting ElderShield premium rebates in the future?
questions.text: This will depend on the claims experience of the ElderShield scheme. Premium rebates are only given if subsequent ElderShield claims are lower than projected.

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I join CareShield Life, will I get premium rebates?
questions.text:
Premium rebates are dependent on the recommendations of the CareShield Life Council. The independent council has been set up to regularly review and recommend premium and payout adjustments for CareShield Life, in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework.
If there are fewer claims than expected, you might receive premium rebates or have your future premiums adjusted lower. However, if there are more claims than expected, your premiums might need to increase to keep the scheme sustainable.

questions.title: How long do I have to pay for CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are age 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will not have to pay premiums after 10 years.
If you are age 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: Why did the CareShield Life Welcome Package state that I was previously invited to apply for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) is designed to help members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support. As you have an outstanding MediShield Life premium, a letter (Ref: APCINV) was sent earlier to invite you to apply for APS if you need assistance to pay your outstanding premiums. Alternatively, you may visit cpf.gov.sg/APSapplication to apply for APS online. This link does not require Singpass login.
For more information on APS, please visit the MediShield Life website or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 for assistance.

questions.title: Why is the premium information shown on the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service different from details in my welcome letter?
questions.text: The CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service is based on the latest information available when you log in while your welcome letter is accurate as of the date shown on the first page. The information may differ if you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and the appeal was successful. For further enquiries, please contact us at Write to us or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: Where can I seek advice on financial planning for old age or seek financial assistance for long-term care needs?
questions.text:
For an overview of options for long-term care financing and services, you may visit this link.
To find out more about long-term care services, specific Government subsidies for long-term care services and other Government assistance schemes for long-term care that older Singaporeans (age 65 and above) may tap on, you may reach out to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) through AIC website or 1800-650-6060. You can also speak to a Care Consultant at AIC Links located at the public hospitals and Maxwell. You may find the list of AIC Link locations via this link.
For Government support schemes specifically for younger Singaporeans with severe disability and their caregivers, you may refer to SGEnable website or speak to SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.
For more information on retirement planning, Singaporeans can visit the following websites:
CPF website to learn about CPF schemes.
Be Ready with CPF website to understand how CPF savings can support Singaporeans through the key stages of their life and learn how they can work towards a better retirement.

questions.title: I have mild or moderate disabilities or I can perform more than three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). How can I get help for my long-term care costs?
questions.text:
If you have mild or moderate disabilities and need long-term care, you can tap on various means-tested Government subsidies and assistance schemes to complement your personal savings and family support.
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare can provide further assistance to you if you are unable to pay for your care after Government subsidies and other means of support. The Government will continue to look at ways to support the needs of Singaporeans with less severe disabilities.
To find out more about long-term care services, specific Government subsidies for long-term care services and other Government assistance schemes for long-term care that Singapore Residents may tap on, you may reach out to the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) through the AIC website or 1800-650-6060. You can also speak to a Care Consultant at AIC Links located at the public hospitals and Maxwell.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to make MediSave Care withdrawals to cover my parent or children’s long-term care needs?
questions.text:
The duration of severe disability can vary significantly, potentially leading to substantial withdrawals over a long period. Allowing individuals with severe disability to tap into their parent or children’s MediSave for withdrawals could potentially impact their parent or children’s MediSave adequacy and compromise their ability to afford their own healthcare needs.
Singaporeans who need financial assistance and have low MediSave balances may apply for ElderFund. If they are still unable to afford their long-term care costs, additional assistance is available through schemes such as MediFund and ComCare.

questions.title: If I nominatd an organisation, what would happen to my CPF savings if the organisation no longer exists or is no longer a legal entity?
questions.text:
If the organisation no longer exists or is no longer considered a legal entity at the point of your passing, your CPF savings will be redistributed to surviving nominees in the same proportion you have specified for them. If there are no surviving nominee(s), your nomination is considered revoked, and your savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee for distribution under the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims).
We encourage CPF members who had nominated organisations, to review their nominations regularly. If an organisation had ceased to exist or is no longer a legal entity, members should make a new nomination to decide how their CPF savings should be distributed.

questions.title: For platform workers who opt in, why is the allocation of CPF contributions into the MediSave account higher than the Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts in 2025? How will platform workers be better off by opting in?
questions.text:
It is important that platform workers (PWs) have sufficient savings to meet their healthcare needs, unlike salaried employees who have healthcare protections from their employers.
Hence, the MediSave allocation rate of between 8% – 10.5% remains the same whether PWs opt in to increased CPF contribution or not (see chart below).
The increase in PWs’ CPF contributions will then be allocated to the Ordinary and Special or Retirement accounts respectively. You can view the allocation rates for 2025 - 2028.
By opting in for increased CPF contributions, PWs will receive the platform operator (PO) share of CPF contributions of 3.5% in 2025 which increases to up to 17% in 2029. These are additional savings for platform workers’ housing and retirement needs.
PWs who use the Ordinary account (OA) contributions for mortgage instalments can free up more cash for other expenses. This is because the CPF contributions allocated to the OA (PW and PO share) will be higher than the increase in CPF contributions that the PW has to make.
For example, in 2025, a 40-year-old PW with monthly net earnings of $3,000 who opts in to higher CPF contributions would receive 4.5% of his net earnings ($135) in his OA – which can be used to pay for his mortgage instalments. This is higher than the total increase in his own share of CPF contributions, at 2.5% of his income ($75).
In other words, for every additional $1 in CPF that he contributes, he gets $1.80 in his OA which can be used to pay for his mortgage instalments!
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I am born in 1979 or earlier. If I paid ElderShield 300/400 premiums previously but my policy lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, how will my CareShield Life premiums be affected?
questions.text:
As your ElderShield 300/400 policies have lapsed due to non-payment of premiums, you are no longer covered under ElderShield 300/400. Your premiums for CareShield Life will be based on the premiums for an uninsured individual.
Those who need assistance with their premium payment after subsidies and incentives will receive Additional Premium Support, and no one who joins CareShield Life will lose coverage due to financial difficulties.

questions.title: Can I sign up for CareShield Life on behalf of my parent/spouse/sibling?
questions.text:
Your family member’s Singpass will be required to sign up for CareShield Life.
You can guide your family member to use his/her Singpass to apply for CareShield Life via the Application to join CareShield Life form. Some applicants may need to undergo a disability assessment. Your family member will be informed by Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if a disability assessment is required, after his/her application.
If they are facing difficulties, you can accompany them to the Community Clubs/Centres to sign up.

questions.title: Do I still need to complete ACP if I had already completed AMD and/or LPA?
questions.text:
Yes, it is best to complete an ACP even if you have completed AMD and/or LPA as these tools will benefit you in different ways.
AMD and LPA are legal documents, while ACP is not.
AMD is to inform the doctor treating you (in the event you become terminally ill and unconscious) that you do not want any extraordinary life-sustaining treatment to be used to prolong your life.
LPA allows you to appoint one or more trusted persons (Donees) to act on your behalf for personal welfare and/or property and affairs matters should you lose mental capacity to make your own decisions.
ACP is useful because it would serve as a guide for your loved ones and healthcare team to act according to your best interests in the event that you are unable to make decisions or speak for yourself. The ACP will include healthcare preferences such as extent of treatment, pain control options etc. It also allows you to appoint up to 2 Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons (NHS) to speak on your behalf when you cannot speak for yourself.

questions.title: What is myACP?
questions.text:
myACP is an online service on MyLegacy@LifeSG that allows individuals to complete their ACP without having to speak to an ACP facilitator. It aims to make the ACP process more accessible and convenient for those who are generally healthy, by empowering them to complete their ACP independently, anywhere and at their own time.
Upon completion of myACP and NHS's acceptance, the ACP will be registered in the National ACP IT system and linked to the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) for viewing by ACP facilitators and healthcare team.

questions.title: What should I do if I accidentally reported a number as scam?
questions.text:
Please note that the ScamShield app only blocks phone numbers that have been marked as scam in the ScamShield database. These numbers are marked by the authorities based on reports from the community about suspicious or scam-related activity.
Please be assured that a single report alone does not automatically mark a phone number as a scam. Our system uses multiple data points and verification processes to determine if a number is suspicious.
If this is a legitimate phone number, you don't need to worry. The phone number won't be incorrectly marked as a scam based on a single report.
If you've accidentally reported a number as "scam", you may use the Check for Scams feature to check if the phone number is marked as scam in the ScamShield database.
A phone number is only blocked if the check outcome appears red with the message "Beware, this looks like a scam."
Only phone numbers from government and healthcare institutions that have been whitelisted will be marked as "Safe".
If you get an outcome saying “Be careful, we're not sure about this one”, the number has not been marked as "Scam" or blocked.
If you believe a phone number has been wrongly marked as scam, please reach out to the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.
In addition, please submit a new scam report on the ScamShield app for the suspicious phone number you have come across.
Hope this helps!

questions.title: How will top-ups boost my CPF monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you are on CPF LIFE* in retirement, topping up your Special or Retirement Account will allow you to enjoy higher monthly payouts for life. Please refer to this FAQ for examples on the increase in payouts.
If you are not on CPF LIFE* in retirement, the top-ups will generally allow you to receive higher payouts or receive payouts for a longer time. Find out more.
*Members born in 1958 or later will be placed on CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account when they commence their monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How will topping up my Special or Retirement Account boost my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
If you are not on CPF LIFE* in retirement, topping up your Special or Retirement Account will generally increase your monthly payouts. However, if your remaining payout duration is short, the top-up will extend your payout duration instead so that your Retirement Account can continue to provide you with monthly payouts during your retirement.
For more personalised estimates, use the CPF Monthly Payout Estimator. This tool helps you project your monthly CPF payouts in retirement and simulate the effect of different top-up amounts on your monthly payout.
*Members born in 1958 or later will be placed on CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account when they commence their monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How will topping up my Special or Retirement Account increase my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you are on CPF LIFE, the top-ups to your Special or Retirement Account will be used for your CPF LIFE premium in order to increase your CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
The extent of increase depends on a few factors including your age when you make the top-up. The earlier you make the top-up, the more your monthly payouts will increase. This is because your top-up amount grows with compound interest over time, which means it earns interest, and then that interest also starts earning interest.
Here are some examples of the expected increase in payouts:
One-Time Top-Ups:
A $2,000 top-up made at age 65 will increase your monthly payout by about $10*.
The same $2,000 top-up made at age 25 will increase your monthly payout by about $50.
Regular Monthly Top-Ups of $100:
Monthly top-ups from age 55 to 65 (over 10 years) will result in an increase of about $70 in your monthly payout.
Monthly top-ups from age 25 to 35 (over 10 years) will result in an increase of about $240 in your monthly payout.
For personalised estimates, use the CPF Retirement Payout Planner. This tool helps you project your monthly CPF payouts in retirement and simulate the effect of different top-up amounts on your monthly payout.
*The actual revision may take up to two months following your top-up, and we will notify you on the changes in your monthly payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What types of license plates can I add to the app?
questions.text:
You can add license plates for vehicles that belong to you/family (eg. family car)
These will be associated with the registration details you provided when filling up our form
Please do not register the following types of license plates:
Car-sharing vehicles (eg., BlueSG, GetGo)
Private-hire vehicles where you are riding as a passenger (eg., Taxi, Grab, Gojek, Tada)
Public transport vehicles (e.g., buses)
Vehicles not owned by you/family
You will only be able to add 5 license plates in the app.

questions.title: I have been charged for a crime. Should I engage a lawyer for my criminal case?
questions.text:
The decision to engage a lawyer is a personal one. It is important for you to consider the pros and cons of representing yourself versus engaging a lawyer before making a choice.
When representing yourself, you need to familiarise yourself with the legal procedures and substantive criminal law. The Court cannot relax its procedural rules and standards for you, and you must be prepared to present your case as if you have engaged a lawyer. The Court cannot act as your lawyer or advise you on how to represent yourself.
If you are confident with preparing for and conducting your own case, you may consider representing yourself.
If you are unsure, you may wish to consider engaging a lawyer to represent you in Court for your Criminal case or at least consult one before making your decision.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Where can I get legal advice for my criminal case?
questions.text:
Your rights as an accused
You have the right to obtain legal advice, seek legal assistance or engage a lawyer to represent you in court at your criminal proceedings.
You may wish to find out:
(If you are representing yourself in court) Your rights and responsibilities.
What is a criminal case.
The courts are not able to provide legal advice. Legal advice is when you are provided specific information about your legal matter and guidance on the legal options available to you.
You can obtain legal advice through several available options:
(A) Engage a lawyer: The Law Society of Singapore has an online directory listing the names, addresses and other useful information of all practising lawyers in Singapore.
(B) The Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS): CLAS is a programme offered by Pro Bono SG for accused persons who cannot afford legal representation facing criminal charges for non-death penalty offences under statutes covered by CLAS. Eligible accused persons will receive legal assistance from a volunteer lawyer if they meet specific criteria. Please refer to Pro Bono SG’s website (https://www.probono.sg/) for the necessary criteria to be fulfilled.
(C) Public Defender’s Office (PDO): If you are Singaporean or Permanent Resident, and unable to afford a lawyer, you may also seek legal assistance from the PDO. Similar to CLAS, you will need to satisfy PDO’s specific criteria and face offences covered under the Public Defender’s Office Act. You may find more information on PDO from their website or contact them by phone or visiting them at their office.
(D) Remand Clinic: If the accused is currently remanded in prison because of not being able to post bail, he/she may attend the Remand Clinic to obtain free legal advice from a volunteer lawyer. More information can be obtained through the officers in the Singapore Prisons Service. Please note that the lawyer that the remandee sees will not be able to represent him/her in Court.
Note: The courts are not in a position to recommend lawyers for your case. Contact a law firm or organisation of your choice directly to understand their fees and the services they provide.

questions.title: What should I do if I want more information of the criminal process or contact the State Courts?
questions.text:
For more information of the criminal process, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.
You may also contact the State Courts at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/contact-us.

questions.title: What are the Criminal Mentions Courts?
questions.text:
Mentions Courts are the first courts where an accused person in a criminal case must personally attend to be formally charged for an offence and to give their plea, whether guilty or not guilty. These include both Day Mentions Courts and Night Mentions Courts (Night Courts). The Mentions Court that you are required to attend is stated on the Notice, Summons or Bail Bond issued to you. It will also state the date and time you are required to appear in Court.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a Criminal Charge?
questions.text:
A charge is an official document prepared by the Prosecution. It includes information such as the date, time, place, and nature of the offence alleged to have been committed by the accused person.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Do I have to attend Court?
questions.text:
Attendance at the Court is compulsory. If you fail to attend Court for your Criminal Case, a Warrant of Arrest may (WTA) be issued against you. If you do not attend Court while on bail, your bailor will need to explain to the court why the bail amount should not be forfeited.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What should I bring when I attend a hearing at the Mentions Courts?
questions.text:
When attending a Mentions Court, you must bring the following:
Identification Document: If you are charged in your personal capacity, bring an identification document bearing your photo and personal particulars (e.g., NRIC or driver's license). If you are appearing on behalf of an accused company or corporate entity, bring your identification document along with a valid Letter of Authorization (LA).
Relevant Documents: Bring related documents such as the Notice to Attend Court, Summons, Bail Bond, or other related paperwork.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: I wish to request for an adjournment of the hearing of my Criminal Case. How do I make the application?
questions.text:
If you wish to request for an adjournment or postponement of the Court hearing of your criminal case to another date, you will need to make an application to the Court before the hearing date. Any requests must be supported by valid reasons or may be rejected by the Court.
The request(s) can be made via https://icms.judiciary.gov.sg/.
If your application is rejected, you must attend the hearing originally scheduled, otherwise a Warrant to Arrest may be issued against you.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens during the hearing at a Criminal Mentions Court?
questions.text:
At the Mentions Courts hearing, the following proceedings typically occur:
Being Called for Mentions: This is the first stage of the process where the Prosecution officially charges the accused. The Mentions Court that you are required to attend is stated on the Notice, Summons, or Bail Bond issued to you, along with the date and time.
During the Mentions:
Listen for your name to be called.
Show your identification document to the court officer.
Stand in the dock when instructed.
An interpreter will ask for your preferred language, and the charge(s) and prescribed punishment will be read and explained to you in that language.
After reading of the Charge(s):
The Judge may make any of the following orders:
Indicate your Plea: The Court may ask whether you wish to plead guilty or claim trial.
Order of Remand:
You may be remanded in custody if the Prosecution applies for remand for investigation purposes, and the Court grants the application based on merits and established legal principles.
Alternatively, you may be remanded if no bail is offered or if bail is offered but not furnished. In such cases, you will remain in prison until bail is furnished or the case concludes.
Adjourn the Case to a later date: The Judge may adjourn the case to a later date upon application by either you or the Prosecutor. The application will be considered based on its merits and in accordance with the law.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What does pleading guilty mean?
questions.text:
Pleading guilty (PG) means that you admit to committing the offence(s) as stated in the charge(s) and agree with the essential facts of the case as stated in the Statement of Facts (SOF).
When you choose to plead guilty, the following applies:
Conviction Without Trial: - You will be convicted by the Judge without a trial if the admitted facts make out every element of the charge. You can plead guilty at any stage of the proceedings before the Judge delivers his or her verdict
No Contest to Charges After Conviction: - Once convicted and sentenced, you will not be allowed to contest the charge(s) or claim trial.
Appeal Options: - You can appeal against your sentence but not your conviction.
Discount on Sentence: - You may receive a discount on your sentence for an early plea of guilt.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What does claiming trial mean?
questions.text:
Claiming trial means that you dispute and contest the charge(s) in respect of the offence(s) against you or, disagree with essential facts stated in the Statement of Facts (SOF).
When you claim trial, the following applies:
Trial Date Fixed: - A trial date will be fixed for the Prosecution to prove the charges and for you to defend yourself.
Right to Contest Charges: - You will have the opportunity to contest the charge(s) and present your defence during the trial.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens if I decide to plead guilty at the Mentions Courts?
questions.text:
If you decide to plead guilty (PG) at the Mentions Court, the following will typically happen:
Hear the Case for PG: For certain types of cases, the Mentions Court may hear the case, decide on whether you are guilty of the offence, and pass sentence.
Transfer to Sentencing Court: If the case cannot be concluded at the Mentions Court, it will usually be transferred to a Sentencing Court (commonly referred to as the PG Courts). Your next hearing will be referred to as the PG Mention for you to plead guilty.
Notification of Next Hearing: The Mentions Court will inform you of the next date, time, and venue for your PG Mention.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens if I decide to claim trial at the Mentions Courts?
questions.text:
In the event you decide to claim trial, your case will be fixed for a Pre-Trial Conference (PTC). The case will be transferred from the Mentions Court to the PTC Centre. The Mention Courts will inform you of the next date, time and venue of your PTC.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens if I request for an adjournment during the hearing at the Mentions Courts?
questions.text:
At the hearing in the Mentions Courts, you may wish to request for an adjournment to for example engage a lawyer, make representations to the Prosecution, raise funds to pay any Court fine or settle personal affairs before pleading guilty.
You can apply to the Judge during the Court hearing.
If approved, you will receive a mention slip with the Court Number, Date, and Time of your next Court hearing. If the case is adjourned, the Judge will decide if you can be released on bail until the next hearing. If you are on bail, your existing bail may be extended or you may be offered Court bail.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How do I make representations to the Prosecution?
questions.text:
To make representations to the Prosecution, you may wish to:
Prepare Your Representations: Representations are formal written requests to the Prosecution to consider alternatives, such as withdrawing or reducing the charge(s), or offering a composition. You should clearly state your reasons and any supporting evidence.
Submit Representations: Representations can be submitted directly to the Prosecution. The Prosecution will review your representations and respond accordingly. If you are unsure of the process, you may seek legal advice or assistance, or visit https://www.agc.gov.sg/contact_us/representations.

questions.title: What are the Night Courts?
questions.text:
The Night Courts primarily handle cases involving regulatory offences and minor traffic offences and operate during the evening hours to provide convenience to members of the public, especially those who might otherwise need to take a day off from work.
Key details about Night Courts:
Commencement of Proceedings: Cases are typically commenced via a Notice to Attend Court or Summons, which will specify the required Court, date, and time. Depending on the nature of your traffic or regulatory offence, you will have to either pay the offer of composition or attend court.
Court Attendance: Attendance is compulsory, and failure to attend may result in a Warrant of Arrest being issued.
Transfer to Day Courts: If you decide to claim trial or if the Judge deems it more appropriate, the case may be transferred to the Day Courts.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How do I compound an offence?
questions.text:
"Compounding" an offence means settling it out of court, typically by paying a monetary sum, without admitting guilt or facing a conviction.
If you wish to compound an offence:
(a) Check Eligibility for Composition: Composition is offered at the discretion of the prosecuting agency. You may compound an offence if composition is offered by the agency responsible for prosecuting your case.
(b) Payment of Composition Fee: Payment should be made before the expiry date of the offer of composition given and, in any event, before the date of the Night Court hearing. If the offer of composition lapses or is withdrawn, you will have to attend court to plead guilty or claim trial.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is Bail?
questions.text:
Bail refers to property or money offered to the Court to ensure that an accused will continue to attend all Court hearings after being arrested and charged before being released from remand. If bail is granted, a surety or bailor must be willing and able to provide security for the bail ordered by the Court.
Once bail is furnished, the accused will be released on bail. The bailor has a duty to ensure the accused attends Court as required. If an accused is a minor, the Court may require the bailor to be a parent or legal guardian.
You may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/bail for more information relating to bail matters. There are also downloadable guides for "Understanding Bail" under the "Resources" section of the page.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a Personal Bond?
questions.text:
A personal bond allows an accused to be released from remand, without requiring a surety or bailor, by providing his or her own property or money to the Court as security to ensure that he or she will continue to attend all Court hearings as required.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Are there any conditions I must follow if I am released on bail or personal bond?
questions.text:
There are specific conditions that you must follow when released on bail or personal bond. Some conditions may include (and are not limited to):
Surrendering Your Travel Document
Be Available for investigations
Not to Commit Offences
Not to Contact any Victims
Time Curfew to remain indoors
Failure to comply with any conditions may lead to the bail or personal bond being revoked by the Court and you will be remanded pending the outcome of your criminal case.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How is the bail or personal bond amount determined by the Court?
questions.text:
The bail amount is determined by the Court based on several considerations. Such considerations may include:
Nature, number, and seriousness of the offence(s) committed
Severity of the prescribed punishments for the offence(s)
Character (including criminal history), financial means and standing of the accused
Potential Flight Risk or threat to public safety
Likelihood of compliance with the bail or personal bond conditions
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What type of security may be furnished for the bail or personal bond?
questions.text:
The type of security that may be furnished for bail or personal bond depends on the amount involved. The general guidelines are as follows:
For Bail/Personal Bond Amounts of $15,000 and Below: Security may be provided by pledging personal property, including items such as jewellery or furniture if they have been fully paid for.
For Bail/Personal Bond Amounts Above $15,000: Security is generally provided by means of cash or cash equivalent, such as a cashier's order.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Who can be my bailor?
questions.text:
To qualify as a bailor, the person must generally meet the following criteria:
Citizenship/Residency: Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.
Age: 21 years old and above.
Must not be a bankrupt or facing criminal charges.
The Court has the ultimate discretion in determining whether a person is suitable to act as a bailor. If the Court does not believe that the proposed bailor can secure the accused's attendance for Court events, it may disqualify the person from being one.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.
