questions.title: What must my bailor do to bail me out?
questions.text:
If bail is granted, the accused will be permitted to make two local phone calls to arrange for a bailor. The proposed bailor must go to the Bail Centre at Level 4 of the State Courts Towers for the bail application to be processed. If the application is approved, arrangements will be made for the accused to be released.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens if an accused fails to attend court or has absconded?
questions.text:
If an accused fails to attend Court or has absconded, the following actions may be taken by the Court:
Revocation of Bail or Personal Bond and Issuance of a Warrant of Arrest: A Warrant of Arrest will be issued against the accused to arrest and produce him/her in Court.
Court Appearance for Bailor to Show Cause: The bailor will be issued with a Notice to attend Court to Show Cause. If the Court is satisfied that the accused had no reasonable excuse for failing to attend Court as required, the bailor may be called upon to explain why the Court should not forfeit the bail bond.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Will the bailor get a bail refund?
questions.text:
If the accused attends all required court proceedings and fulfil all the bail conditions, the bail amount will be returned to your bailor after your criminal case concludes or when the Court has granted permission to your bailor to be discharged as a bailor for you.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How will my bailor receive the bail refund?
questions.text:
If physical cash was pledged, cash via NETS or cashier’s order as security, the total bail amount will be credited back into the bank account your bailor has provided when posting bail. If monies in your bailor’s savings account were pledged in fixed or time deposits as security, the Court will inform the bank to unfreeze that account.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens after I claim trial?
questions.text:
If you claim trial in the Mentions Court, the Court your case will be fixed for a Pre-Trial Conference (PTC). The case will be transferred from the Mentions Court to the PTC Centre. The Mentions Court will inform you of the next date, time and venue of your Criminal PTC.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a Criminal pre-trial conference?
questions.text:
The purpose of the Criminal PTC is to prepare you and the Prosecution for trial and to settle any administrative matters before the trial date is fixed.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What should I expect during the pre-trial conference?
questions.text:
The purpose of the Criminal PTC is to ascertain whether the case is ready for trial. You have to attend this PTC together with the Prosecution. At this conference, the Judge will be informed of the nature of the evidence that will be tendered by you and by the Prosecution. The witnesses will also be made known. Once all the administrative matters, including a Criminal Case Disclosure Conference (if applicable), have been sorted out, the Judge will then give a date for the trial.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What should I prepare for the Criminal pre-trial conference?
questions.text:
Prior to the Criminal PTC, you should consider whether you wish to address the following matters during the PTC:
Check if the Prosecution intends to make use of any written statement given by you to the police and if so, you may request for a copy of the statement.
Indicate to the Court the number of witnesses that you wish to call at the trial.
If you require a translator for yourself or your witnesses, you should inform the Judge that you would require the assistance of an interpreter for the trial. The Judge may also ask you for an indication of the legal defence that you intend to rely on. It would therefore be useful for you to think about this before the Criminal PTC.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a Criminal Case Disclosure Conference (CCDC)?
questions.text:
A Criminal Case Disclosure Conference is a formalised system of reciprocal disclosure to enable parties to know ahead of the trial the case that they have to meet. This means that both you and the Prosecution will be under a duty to reveal aspects of your cases and the evidence that each of you intends to rely on at the pre-trial stage.
A CCDC will only apply to specific types of cases where the charges are brought under certain statutes. The Judge will inform you if CCDC applies to your case and will ask you to indicate whether you wish to participate in the CCDC. For all other cases, the CCDC will only apply if all parties involved in the proceedings consent.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: Should I participate in the CCDC?
questions.text:
Participation in the Criminal Case Disclosure Conference (CCDC) is optional.
If you decide to participate in the CCDC, it will help you gain a better understanding of the Prosecution’s case against you, and help you decide the best course of action to take.
If you decide not to participate in the CCDC, the Court will fix a date for trial once the administrative matters have been dealt with, and you will not have a chance to consider the Prosecution’s evidence before the trial. Similarly, the Prosecution will not have a chance to consider your evidence, which may, in certain instances, lead to a reduced charge.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens if I choose to participate in the CCDC?
questions.text:
If you decide to participate in the Criminal Case Disclosure Conference, the Court will give a series of directions to facilitate the discovery procedure.
First, the Court will direct the Prosecution to prepare and provide the “Case for the Prosecution” to you, which contains the evidence that the Prosecution will be relying on to prove your guilt.
At the next CCDC, the Court will direct you to prepare your “Case for the Defence”, which would consist of these documents:
a summary of your defence and the relevant supporting facts you wish to rely on;
a list of your Witnesses;
a description of the documents and items you intend to produce in Court as evidence; and
any objections you may wish to raise to the Case for the Prosecution.
Your Case for the Defence must be prepared in English. You must provide a copy of your Case to the Court as well as the Prosecution within the timeline stipulated by the Court. If there are any co-accused persons who are claiming trial, you will need to serve the Case for the Defence on the co-accused as well.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens after I have submitted my Case for the Defence?
questions.text:
After you have submitted your Case for the Defence to the Court and the Prosecution, the Prosecution will give you copies of the documents found in the Case for the Prosecution. If you wish to view any audiovisual recordings of statements given by you, you may make a request to the Prosecution, who will then arrange for a viewing of the audiovisual recording.
At the next CCDC, the Judge will ask you and the Prosecution to indicate your respective positions. If the Prosecution decides to proceed with the charges, and if you decide to claim trial, the Judge will fix a date for the trial.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a trial?
questions.text:
A criminal trial is held for the purpose of determining whether you are guilty of the charges brought against you. During the trial, the Judge will hear the evidence produced by you and the Prosecution in accordance with the law. Exhibits may be produced, which may take the form of witness testimonies, documents, videos, photographs, and objects.
The Judge will try to find out the truth of what happened by assessing the accuracy and credibility of the evidence presented. After hearing all the evidence presented, the Judge will then decide whether to convict or acquit you.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How should I prepare for a trial?
questions.text:
The Judge can only consider evidence presented in Court. You must therefore bring along evidence, including witnesses (if any), in support of your defence on the day of the trial. Both sides have a right to call witnesses. All witnesses will be sworn and affirmed under oath and will be subjected to questioning by you and the Prosecution. If you want to rely on what someone else says or knows, that person must come to Court so that the Prosecutor will be able to ask him/her questions.
If disclosure of the Case for the Prosecution and the Case for the Defence has been conducted previously, you would need to give notice in writing to the Court and all other parties if you wish to call any witness or produce any exhibit that has not been disclosed in your Case for the Defence.
If you are going to introduce a new witness, the written notice must state the name of the witness and an outline of what he or she will be testifying on. If you are introducing any exhibits, the written notice must provide a description of the exhibit.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What do I do if I want to present witnesses?
questions.text:
You must make sure that all your witnesses turn up for the criminal trial. If you are not sure whether the witnesses are willing to turn up, you should apply at the Central Registry (State Courts Towers Level 2) for a “Summons to a Witness” to be issued against that witness. A fee of $20 is payable for every Summons issued. A Court process server will then help you to serve the document on the witness.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What do I do if I want to present documents?
questions.text:
Prepare the documents and all the evidence that you intend to rely on for your defence. You need to prepare at least 4 copies of the documents/evidence. One (the original) for the Court, one for the Prosecution, one for the witness and one for yourself.
Generally, you should also ensure that the maker of any document is in Court. Otherwise, the document may not be admitted as evidence for the trial. For instance, if you are seeking to introduce a WhatsApp message or Facebook message sent by another person, you may wish to consider calling the person as a witness, so that he can state in Court whether he was the sender of that message. Your documents should be prepared well in advance of the trial. This is particularly important as the Court may direct you (and the Prosecution) to submit these documents before the actual trial date.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens during a criminal trial?
What are some possible objections I could have against the questions and evidence presented by the Prosecution?
questions.text:
During the Prosecution’s examination-in-chief, cross examination or re-examination, it is possible for you to object to certain questions being asked or certain evidence being given. When you object, you do so by standing up and saying “I object, your honour”. You will then explain why you objected and the other party has a chance to respond to the objection and the Judge will then decide if the question should be allowed.
Some examples of the types of questions that may be objectionable include:
Irrelevant evidence that does not relate to the charges;
Character (as a general rule, the Prosecution cannot lead evidence to show that you are a person of bad character, including your past criminal record); and
Hearsay (Hearsay is a statement by a person who is not in Court as a witness tendered to prove the truthfulness of the facts therein).
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What will happen after the Prosecution has set out their case?
questions.text:
After the Prosecution has called all their witnesses, the Court will decide if the Prosecution has presented a sufficient case such that you must answer the charge. You may make a submission of no case to answer if you think that there is insufficient evidence to support the Prosecution’s case.
If there is sufficient evidence to support the Prosecution’s case, the Court will ask you to present your defence. You will be given two options by the Judge:
give evidence from the witness stand; or
remain silent.
If you choose to give evidence, you will have to give evidence from the witness box, on oath or affirmation, and be subject to cross-examination by the Prosecution.
If you choose to remain silent, the Court may draw all reasonable inferences, including those unfavourable to you. The Court may take your silence into account when deciding whether you are guilty or not.
Whichever you choose, you can call other witnesses to give evidence to support your case.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How do I give evidence in my defence?
questions.text:
Assuming that you have chosen to give evidence, you will be the first person to go on the stand. You may ask the Judge for some time before you begin your case to think about what you want to say in your defence. You may then begin by giving a summary of the reasons why you are not guilty. After taking the oath, you should state your full name, age, and current occupation. Then, you can go on to give your version of what happened. This is the “Examination-in-Chief of the Accused”, and is an opportunity for you to present your version of the matter.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What do I do at the end of the trial?
questions.text:
At the end of the criminal trial, you and the Prosecutor will be given the opportunity to make closing submissions. The purpose of this is to let parties summarise the evidence and arguments to persuade the Judge to decide the case in their favour.
You will be asked to make your closing submissions first, followed by the Prosecution. If you need time to prepare your closing submissions, you may ask the Judge for some time. If you cannot remember what was said at trial, you may apply for a copy of the Notes of Evidence via the Central Registry (State Courts Towers, Level 2).
Notes of Evidence is a word-for-word transcript of what had been said by the different people in Court.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What happens at a Plead Guilty (PG) Mention?
questions.text:
At a Plead Guilty (PG) Mention:
The charge(s) will be read to you. You need to state whether you admit to the charge(s) and wish to plead guilty.
The Prosecution will read a statement of facts which contains relevant information of your offence. You need to state whether you accept the full facts.
There may be other charges that need to be taken into consideration for sentencing. But the Court will not impose any individual sentences for these charges. You need to state whether you admit to the charge(s) and consent to have them considered by the Court.
The Prosecution will state your past criminal record, if any.
If you admit to the charge(s) and the facts, the Court will convict you of the offences.
After that, the Court will hear submissions from the Prosecution and you before deciding on the sentence to be imposed.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What are antecedents?
questions.text:
After you have been convicted, the Prosecution will inform the Court of your antecedents or antecedent records, which are your previous criminal records. You will be asked to confirm if your antecedents are correct. If you agree, you will move on to the next step of the hearing. If you do not agree, the Prosecution will have to prove the contents of your criminal record through a Newton Hearing.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a Newton Hearing?
questions.text:
A Newton hearing may be convened at any stage of the sentencing process when there is a dispute to any fact that may materially affect your sentence. For example, conflicting medical reports on whether you have a mental illness or whether there is a link between your mental illness and the offence, disputes over your criminal records.
It will be conducted like a trial, where you and the Prosecution will be given a chance to call their respective witnesses before making submissions. At the end of the Newton Hearing, the Judge will pronounce his decision on the disputed issue of fact. Once the decision has been made, the Judge will proceed with the rest of the sentencing process.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What are Submissions or Address on Sentence?
questions.text:
The Prosecution will make proposals on the sentence to be imposed by the Court on you. They may refer to past cases decided by the Courts. This is known as Submissions or Address on Sentence.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is a mitigation plea?
questions.text:
After the Prosecution has made their Submissions on Sentence, you will be asked to present your mitigation plea to the Judge. This is for you to raise relevant mitigating facts so that the Judge can consider your case and decide if leniency may be exercised.
If you disagree with the Prosecution’s proposed sentences, you should inform the Court during your mitigation plea and explain why.
The Prosecution will then have a chance to reply to your mitigation plea.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: How do I prepare a mitigation plea?
questions.text:
A mitigation plea is an oral or written statement containing information about yourself or the circumstances of the offence that may result in a lower sentence imposed.
The purpose of your mitigation plea is for you to convey relevant mitigating factors so that the judge can arrive at a fair and just sentence. These can be reasons, facts or circumstances that seek to persuade the judge to exercise leniency or explain why your punishment should be lower.
You may wish to refer to this page on how to prepare a mitigation plea: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/prepare-mitigation-plea#how-to-prepare-it

questions.title: What is a sentence?
questions.text:
A sentence is the punishment that you will have to bear after you have been convicted of an offence by the Court.
These are the common types of sentences imposed by a Court:
Fines
A term of imprisonment
Caning
Preventive Detention
Corrective Training
Probation
Reformative Training
Community Based Sentences
Disqualification from driving
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is a fine?
questions.text:
A fine is a monetary penalty imposed on you by the Court. Fines are payable in full immediately after sentencing. If you are unable to pay the fine in full, you may ask the Court for your fine to be paid by instalments. This is subject to the Court’s approval. If you are unable to pay the fine at all or by the due date given by the Court, you may have to serve an imprisonment term decided by the Court.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is a term of imprisonment?
questions.text:
An imprisonment term means that you will be sent to prison for a period of time that the Court determines.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is caning?
questions.text:
Caning can or must be imposed by the Court for certain offences. The Court will decide on the number of strokes of the cane to be imposed. Caning can only be imposed on male offenders below 50 years old. At any one time, the maximum number of strokes of cane that you can be sentenced to is 24.
For females and male offenders aged 50 or above, the sentence of caning may be replaced with an additional sentence.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is preventive detention?
questions.text:
Preventive detention is a separate regime from imprisonment. It involves the confinement of a repeat offender for a minimum of 7 years and a maximum of 20 years. Preventive detention is imposed if the Court is satisfied that the detention is expedient to protect the public.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is corrective training?
questions.text:
Corrective training is a separate regime from imprisonment. It involves the confinement of a repeat offender for a minimum period of 5 years and a maximum period of 14 years. Corrective training is imposed if the Court is satisfied that the detention is expedient for reformation of the offender, and further prevention of crime.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is probation?
questions.text:
Probation is an alternative to sentences like imprisonment and fine. Probation is a common sentencing option available to young offenders below 21 years of age. The Court can make a probation order for a period between 6 months and 3 years. During the probation period, you need to comply with the conditions (for example: to not reoffend, comply with time restrictions) and be supervised by a probation officer.
Any breach of the probation order may lead to the order being revoked and you may be sent to prison to serve the original sentence.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What is reformative training?
questions.text:
Young offenders above 16 years old but under 21 years old may be sentenced to reformative training. It requires the offender to be detained in a structured environment, and the offender will be required to attend programmes or counselling to deal with his offending behaviour.
The Court can impose a minimum detention period for 6 or 12 months depending on the offender and the facts of the case.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/types-sentences

questions.title: What are Community Based Sentences (CBS)?
questions.text:
The Court will usually order CBS (instead of sentences such as imprisonment or a fine) for selected cases. If CBS is successfully completed, the offender is deemed to have no record of that conviction.
These are examples of CBS orders that can be made by a Court:
Mandatory Treatment Order (MTO)
Day Reporting Order (DTO)
Community Work Order (CWO)
Community Service Order (CSO)
Short Detention Order (SDO)
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website for more information on the types of Community Based Sentences: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/community-based-sentences

questions.title: Can I postpone my sentence?
questions.text:
You have to start serving your sentence immediately after it is imposed on you. However, you may request the Court to postpone the commencement of your sentence. You should inform the Court immediately upon the pronouncement of the sentence if you wish to defer the sentence and provide valid reasons in support.
If you are on bail, your bailor must be present and consent to your request. The Prosecution may object or consent to your application to postpone the commencement of your sentence.
If your request for postponement is granted, there may be additional bail conditions imposed. You must surrender to the Court on the date and time directed by the Judge.

questions.title: What can I do if I am dissatisfied with my sentence?
questions.text:
If you are not satisfied with the sentence, you may file an appeal within 14 calendar days from the pronouncement of the sentence.
For more information, you may wish to visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/charged-with-crime and download the Guidebook for Accused in Person (available in 4 languages) found at the bottom of the page.

questions.title: What is an appeal?
questions.text:
An appeal may be filed by an accused person or the prosecution to reverse one or more of the following types of court decisions:
Conviction or acquittal: Whether you are guilty of an offence.
Sentence: The punishment imposed on you, such as an imprisonment term or fine.
Court Order: Certain types of other orders made in the trial or mention.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website on criminal appeal for more information, at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/appeal-overview

questions.title: What can I appeal against?
questions.text:
You can only appeal against a decision made by the court. If you were convicted after pleading guilty, you cannot appeal against your conviction. You can only appeal against your sentence, or any other order made by the court.
If you were convicted after a trial, you can appeal against your conviction, sentence and/or any other order made by the court.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website on criminal appeal for more information, at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/appeal-overview.

questions.title: How do I file an appeal?
questions.text:
You are required to complete and submit one copy of the Notice of Appeal. This document must be submitted to the Central Registry, which is located on level 2 of the State Courts Towers. When submitting your Notice of Appeal, you will need to pay a fee. This fee is due at the time of submission.
Your Notice of Appeal must include several important pieces of information:
You must provide an address where any notices or documents related to your appeal can be served.
A copy of your NRIC must be attached to the Notice of Appeal.
You need to include your contact number in the document.
If you have legal representation, you should include your lawyer's details in the Notice of Appeal. This includes their name, reference number, address, telephone number, and fax number.
If you are filing on behalf of a company, you must attach a valid letter of authorisation from your company. In this case, you will need to sign the Notice of Appeal on behalf of the company.
In an appeal against conviction, or an appeal against conviction and sentence, to start the appeal process, you must file a Notice of Appeal within 14 days after the date of the sentence.
If you wish to appeal against conviction, you should not file the appeal until the lower court imposes a sentence for the offence.
In any other case, you must file a Notice of Appeal within 14 days after the date of the judgment, sentence or order.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website on criminal appeal for more information, at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/appeal-overview.

questions.title: What happens after my Notice of Appeal is filed?
questions.text:
Once you have filed your Notice of Appeal, the Court will prepare the Grounds of Decision for your case. This document outlines the Judge's reasoning behind their decision. When ready, a copy of the Grounds of Decision will be sent to you or your lawyer. The time needed varies depending on the complexity of the case.
Upon receiving this document along with the Notes of Evidence, you should carefully consider whether you want to continue with your appeal. It may be beneficial to seek legal advice regarding the merits of your appeal before deciding to proceed.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website on criminal appeal for more information, at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/appeal-overview.

questions.title: What is a stay of execution and bail pending appeal?
questions.text:
If you are appealing against your sentence, you may wish to apply for a stay of execution. This is a court order that temporarily suspends the execution of the sentence pending appeal. This allows you to postpone the start of the sentence to after the court decides on your appeal.
At the same time, you can apply to the Judge for bail pending appeal. The Court will consider the Prosecutor's input before deciding on your application.
Even if there is no objection to your application, the Prosecution may seek to increase your bail amount. If you can't provide the bail, your sentence will begin immediately. Should you be granted bail pending appeal, you must comply with the bail conditions. This typically includes surrendering to the Court to serve your sentence if you choose not to pursue the appeal.
If you do continue with the appeal, you must attend the appeal hearing. Failing to surrender will result in a Warrant of Arrest being issued. You will be arrested, brought to Court, and then transferred to the Prisons Department to serve your sentence.
Please refer to the Judiciary’s website on criminal appeal for more information, at https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/criminal/appeal-overview.

questions.title: What if self-employed persons do not respond to the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons?
questions.text:
CPF Board informs self-employed persons (SEPs) of their MediSave payable via the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons.
If SEPs do not respond to the notice of CPF contributions after repeated reminders, CPF Board may issue them a Letter of Demand and Offer which requires them to pay up their outstanding MediSave contributions, together with the payment of the composition amount offered. If there is still no payment, the Board may issue them a Notice to Attend Court (NTA). A sample is appended.
NTA for offences on or after 31 Dec 2021 (PDF, 0.1MB)
SEPs who are brought to court may face a fine of up to $5,000 or imprisonment of up to six months or both for first time offenders, and up to $10,000 or imprisonment of up to 12 months or both for subsequent offences.

questions.title: What information can I find in each section of my Home ownership dashboard?
questions.text: Your Home ownership dashboard summarises your personalised CPF housing information to help you make informed decisions. Here's what each section contains:

questions.title: What are the GST Voucher, 2025 MediSave Bonus, and Assurance Package payouts that the Government is giving out?
questions.text: Please visit the govbenefits website for more information on the GST Voucher, 2025 MediSave Bonus and Assurance Package payouts.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on other government agencies

questions.title: What's the difference between LPA Form 1 and Form 2?
questions.text:
LPA Form 1 is a standard form used by most people to make an LPA. It allows you to:
appoint up to 2 Donees
appoint 1 Replacement Donee (optional)
grant your Donees powers to decide on your personal welfare, property and affairs, or both
The online LPA Form on My Legacy is Form 1, which you can prepare by yourself.
LPA Form 2 is the non-standard form to make an LPA, for those who want to:
appoint more than 2 Donees
appoint more than 1 Replacement Donee
grant your Donees specific or customised powers
A lawyer must be consulted to prepare an LPA Form 2. The lawyer will do this online, and you'll be asked to review and accept your LPA draft online.

questions.title: What are the fees involved when making an LPA?
questions.text:
There are two types of fees when making an LPA.
A. LPA application fee
LPA Form 1
LPA Form 2
Singapore Citizens
Free
$30
Singapore Permanent Residents
$30
$30
Foreigners
$160
$160
The LPA application fee is paid to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG), and you can make payment online with a Visa or Mastercard credit card. You do not have to complete the payment transaction when drafting your LPA form on My Legacy as OPG will inform you separately if a fee is required for your LPA application and the steps to complete the payment.
B. LPA certification fee
The LPA certification fee is paid to the certificate issuer. The amount charged depends on the complexity of the case, as well as your choice of certificate issuer. You can make an appointment with a preferred CI and view their fees here.

questions.title: What happens to my savings used for CPF LIFE when I pass away? Will it go to my beneficiaries?
questions.text:
Upon your passing, your CPF LIFE premium balance and any remaining balances in your CPF accounts will be paid to your beneficiaries. The remaining CPF LIFE premium balance refers to the amount of Retirement Account (RA) savings deducted for the CPF LIFE premium when you joined CPF LIFE minus the total amount of CPF LIFE payouts you received during your lifetime.
*Not applicable to members under the CPF LIFE Income Plan, which does not have a refund feature. As such, beneficiaries will not receive any unused CPF LIFE premium balance upon the member's passing.
Refer to the infographic for detailed examples of how the CPF LIFE premium balance amount is computed, as well as steps to check your CPF LIFE premium balance in the Retirement Dashboard.
You can also access the following links for more information:
Retirement Dashboard: Check your CPF LIFE policy details, including your premium balance.
CPF Nomination: Make a CPF nomination to ensure your savings are distributed according to your wishes quickly.
Check CPF Nomination Details: Review or update your CPF nomination details.

questions.title: Why do I need the Singpass mobile application to make an LPA?
questions.text:
The Singpass app is required for you to digitally sign on your LPA during your visit to the LPA certificate issuer.
If this is your first time signing with Singpass, follow the step-by-step instructions on the app to activate your signing certificate.
If you're not eligible for Singpass or do not have a smart device that's compatible with the Singpass app, you may submit a hardcopy LPA form instead. Mail in or drop off the completed hardcopy LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) at 3 Bishan Place #03-00, CPF Bishan Building, Singapore 579838.

questions.title: I require assistance with my LPA application. Is there any place I can go to get some help?
questions.text:
If you require assistance with making your LPA, you may approach any ServiceSG Centre where officers are able to assist you with drafting of your online or hardcopy Form 1 LPA.
Form 2 LPAs can only be drafted by lawyers and you would need to engage one if you wish to make an LPA Form 2.
ServiceSG One Pungol and Our Tampines Hub also offer a Life Planning Service if you would like to book an appointment to discuss legacy planning matters in general.

questions.title: I have a hardcopy of the registered LPA. Can it be used for transactions?
questions.text:
If the hardcopy is the original registered LPA and not a print-out of a digitally registered LPA, yes, you can.
However, it's recommended that you use the digital LPA to make transactions.
This is because the hardcopy LPA may not be updated to reflect changes due to events such as death or bankruptcy of a Donee. This affects the time it takes for you to complete a transaction as the organisation needs to manually verify the validity of a hardcopy LPA with the Office of the Public Guardian.
To use the digital LPA to make transactions, log in to Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) with your Singpass and share the LPA with the organisation you're transacting with. You may refer to the OPGO Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) for step-by-step guidance on how to send the LPA.

questions.title: Can I use myACP online service if I have a chronic condition?
questions.text:
Yes, you can.
Following the submission of your ACP, especially if you've chronic conditions (for example, diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease) or any other medical concerns, you may also consult your regular doctor.
They'll be able to advise on appropriate treatment goals and preferences based on your medical condition. If you wish to make changes to your ACP later, you can do so using the myACP service.

questions.title: What are the fees involved when making an ACP?
questions.text:
There are no fees involved to complete and register your ACP using the myACP online service.
If you make an appointment with an ACP facilitator, some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Cost may vary, so please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: What if I am unable to finish my ACP in one sitting when using the myACP online service?
questions.text:
The myACP online service supports a "save draft" feature. You may save drafts at any time and come back to it later.
However, you'll need to complete your ACP and obtain consent from your Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons (NHS) within 6 months of creating your online ACP to register your ACP.
If this is not done within the 6 month window, your application will expire, and you'll need to start over.

questions.title: What if I want to speak to someone when using the myACP online service?
questions.text:
While filling out the form, you might want to seek guidance from loved ones, an ACP facilitator, your healthcare team, or a religious community. You can save a draft and return within 6 months of creating it to register your ACP.
If you plan to complete your ACP with an ACP facilitator, bring a copy of your inputs for discussion and confirmation. Once confirmed, they'll register your ACP. Some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: If I want to speak to an ACP facilitator, must I visit in person?
questions.text:
You can speak to a certified ACP facilitator in person or virtually via video conferencing.
You can choose to find an ACP service provider that offers online services. You can meet then meet with the facilitator virtually via video conferencing.

questions.title: What happens if an appointed Donee dies and you need to appoint a replacement Donee? Do you still need to revoke your existing LPA or is there another process to make it simpler?
questions.text:
If your LPA has 2 Donees appointed to act jointly and severally, with the same powers conferred to both, and 1 Donee dies, the remaining Donee is still able to act on the LPA and the LPA remains effective. If each Donee was only given specific powers, the remaining Donee can only act on the power that was granted to them, and the replacement Donee (if named within the LPA) will replace the Donee who has passed on. If no replacement Donee was named, the existing Donee can only act within the powers that was granted. To include a new Donee to cover the other powers not granted to the remaining Donee, you must revoke your LPA and make a new LPA.
If your LPA only had 1 Donee and a replacement Donee was also indicated, the replacement Donee will replace the Donee who passed on and the LPA remains effective. If no replacement Donee was named within the LPA, then the LPA will become invalid and a new LPA must be made to appoint a new Donee.
If your LPA had 2 Donees appointed to act jointly on your LPA, the Donees must act together and not individually. When any one Donee is no longer able to act, all the Donees in the joint appointment will be terminated. If there was a replacement Donee stated in the LPA, the replacement Donee will replace the 2 Donees who were appointed to act jointly. Otherwise, the LPA will no longer be in effect. Should the LPA no longer be effective, rather than revoke the LPA, you would have to make a fresh LPA to appoint new Donees to act on your behalf.

questions.title: What is the Wills Registry?
questions.text:
The Wills Registry is a service provided by the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) that allows you to search for as well as deposit new will records. Details of the person making the will (i.e. testator), date of the will, details of the person who drew up the will and details of where the will is held will be recorded. The registry does not store your actual physical will. The validity of your will also does not depend on whether you have deposited your will information. Information stored in the registry will be kept for 120 years from the date of birth of the person making the will.
You may read more FAQs via the SAL website.

questions.title: Do I have to update my CPF Nomination record when there are changes to my circumstances (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee)?
questions.text: If your circumstances have changed (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee), your current CPF nomination may no longer meet your wishes. You are encouraged to update your CPF nomination to keep it relevant with your current circumstances.

questions.title: If I have already made a Will, do I still need to make a CPF Nomination?
questions.text:
Your CPF savings are not covered under your will and hence cannot be distributed by way of will.
CPF savings do not form your estate (a will covers distribution of a deceased's estate) and are protected from creditor claims on any outstanding debts. This arrangement protects your CPF savings and ensures that your nominees receive your CPF savings expeditiously.
You are encouraged to make a CPF nomination if you want to distribute your CPF savings according to your wishes. Otherwise, your CPF savings will be distributed by the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) in accordance to the intestacy laws (for non-Muslims) of Singapore or the inheritance certificate (for Muslims) to your family members. Administrative fees apply and your next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration.

questions.title: What happens if one, or all, of my CPF nominees pass away?
questions.text:
The deceased nominee's share will be given to the surviving nominees in the same proportion as you have specified. If you have no surviving nominees, then your CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to your family members under the Intestate Succession Act or the Inheritance Certificate (for Muslims). The PTO charges your beneficiaries an administration fee for the distribution of your CPF savings.
You can also make a new CPF nomination and specify new nominee(s) or reallocate your shares to your surviving nominee(s) in accordance with your preference at any time. You are encouraged to regularly review your CPF Nomination and update it so that it continues to fit your intentions.

questions.title: Can I collect cremated ashes on the same day?
questions.text: If the cremation is in the morning, the ashes will be ready for collection by the afternoon. If the cremation is in the afternoon, the ashes will be ready the next day.

questions.title: Can a foreigner apply for a niche at NEA Columbarium?
questions.text: Due to space constraints, only the cremated ashes of individuals who are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents and foreigners whose immediate next-of-kin are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents may be stored in a government managed columbarium.

questions.title: Can I complete an Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before I see a doctor?
questions.text: You can fill in your details on the Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before seeing a doctor. However, your two witnesses and you must sign the form at the same sitting.

questions.title: Is there any cost involved in making an Advance Medical Directive (AMD)?
questions.text: To make an AMD, you will have to consult a doctor who, as a witness, is required to explain the AMD. You may have to pay the doctor for the services rendered. However, the AMD form itself is free.

questions.title: Can family members overrule or object my Advance Medical Directive (AMD) from being carried out?
questions.text: If you have made an AMD, regardless of objections from members of your family, the doctors will have to respect your AMD. Hence, while making an AMD is a very personal decision, we encourage you to discuss it with your family members and loved ones. This will help them to understand and respect your wishes should you become terminally ill.

questions.title: Does the Human Organ Transplant Act (HOTA) allow me to opt out from donating a specific organ?
questions.text: Yes. Anyone who does not wish to donate a particular organ can register his objections using the form and send it to the National Organ Transplant Unit. The registrant can opt out of any or all of the four organs under HOTA.

questions.title: If all organs, skin and bones are pledged for transplant, education and research (MTERA), what would be the delay for family members to make funeral arrangements? Would the whole body be used for research or education, in which case there is no body left for cremation?
questions.text: While making the pledge under MTERA, you can specify the purpose of your donation (i.e. transplant and treatment only, or education and research only, or transplant, treatment, education and research). If you wish to donate only specific organs and body parts, your next-of-kin will receive your body after the pledged parts have been removed in accordance with your wishes.

questions.title: Will the Human Organ Transplant Act (HOTA) apply to citizens who pass away overseas?
questions.text: HOTA does not apply to deaths that occur overseas.

questions.title: If I had not opted out of the Human Organ Transplant Act (HOTA) and I die at home, will my body be transported to a hospital for transplantation purposes?
questions.text: HOTA applies only to deaths in the hospitals which fulfill specific conditions.

questions.title: How will the body be recovered under a whole body donation?
questions.text: If death occurs at the hospital, the body will be transferred to the mortuary, and collected by the assigned hospitals or university on the same day. If death occurs at home or other locations other than the hospital, the next-of-kin should contact the National Organ Transplant Unit (NOTU). NOTU will inform the assigned hospitals or university to make arrangements to collect the body from the location on the same day.

questions.title: My next-of-kin just passed away at home. What should I do?
questions.text:
You should engage a doctor to verify the cause of death. The doctor will certify the death online, which will be automatically registered with the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
You will be given the death document number, date of death and deceased's ID (that was used by doctor during death certification), which are needed to download the digital death certificate from My Legacy.

questions.title: My next-of-kin just passed away overseas. Do I need to register the death in Singapore?
questions.text: No. The death should be registered with the relevant local authorities where the death occurred. Thereafter, you should report the death to the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA, to update the live status of the deceased. This will facilitate the settlement of probate/estate matters of the deceased with the relevant government agencies. The reporting can also be done by a proxy with a letter of authorization from the deceased's family.

questions.title: What are the documents required for reporting overseas death?
questions.text:
To report a death that occurred outside Singapore, you will need to provide the following documents:
Your identification document (NRIC or passport)
Death certificate issued by the foreign authority (or certified true copy of the death certificate)
Deceased's Singapore identification documents (NRIC, Singapore passport or Long Term Pass card)
Coffin import/export permit (if available)
Burial/cremation permit (if available)
If you are a proxy, a letter of authorisation and identification document of the deceased's next-of-kin.
You may report the death of your family member (Singapore resident or Long-Term Pass holder) who died overseas to ICA via FormSG.

questions.title: Who can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
Death certificate
You can download the digital death certificate if:
you are a next-of-kin of the deceased; or
you are authorised by a next-of-kin
Stillbirth certificate
You can download the digital stillbirth certificate if you are the parent of the stillborn baby,
you are the parent of the stillborn baby; or
you are authorised by the parent

questions.title: Who is considered next-of-kin for the purposes of downloading a death certificate?
questions.text:
You'll be considered a next-of-kin who's allowed to download the digital death certificate if your relationship to the person who has died is listed here:
Parent
Spouse
Child or step-child
Sibling
Step or half-sibling
Grandparent
Grandchild
Uncle
Aunt
Niece or nephew
You'll be asked to declare your relationship when you make a request to download the digital death certificate.

questions.title: What information do I need to download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
For death certificate
You'll need to provide:
deceased's NRIC, FIN, or passport number (as per what the doctor used during death certification)
death document number
date of death
For stillbirth certificate
You'll need to provide:
mother's NRIC, FIN, or passport number (as per what the doctor used during death certification)
stillbirth document number
date of stillbirth
These information will be given to you by the hospital or doctor.

questions.title: Where can I get the death or stillbirth document number?
questions.text:
You can get it from the hospital or doctor.
In most cases, this can be found on a document issued by the hospital or doctor. This could be a confirmation of death, confirmation of stillbirth or a similar document.
Depending on the document, the document number will come in the following formats:
6-digit number, followed by a letter (000001A) when the digital death certificate is ready for download
5-digit number, followed by a letter (01234A) when a digital stillbirth certificate is issued
the letter D, followed by a 5-digit number (D10000) when a temporary death document is issued
the letters SB, followed by a 4-digit number (SB0123) when a temporary stillbirth document is issued
If the death or stillbirth was certified outside of a hospital, you may receive a printscreen via WhatsApp instead of a printed document. However, the doctor will still provide you with the 3 information required to download the digital certificate.
If you did not receive the document number, contact the doctor or hospital within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth.
If it has been more than 30 days since the date of death or stillbirth, please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA.

questions.title: How many people can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of persons who can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate. However, to download a death certificate, they must be a next-of-kin, or are authorised by a next-of-kin. To download a stillbirth certificate, they must be the parent of the stillborn baby, or are authorised by the parent.

questions.title: How many times can I download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of times you can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate, if you are authorised to do so.
However, you can only download it within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth. You should save a copy of the certificate in your personal device.

questions.title: Will the death or stillbirth certificate be available for download indefinitely?
questions.text: No, you can only download it within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth. If there is a replacement certificate, it will be available for download 30 days from the date of issuance. You should save a copy of the certificate in your personal device.

questions.title: It's been more than 30 days since the death or stillbirth. How can I retrieve the death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text: Please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA who will be able to assist with your request.

questions.title: I was unable to download the digital death or stillbirth certificate as I was told the record cannot be found. What should I do?
questions.text:
Check the date of death
Firstly, check whether the death occured on or after 29 May 2022 and that it has been less than 30 days since the date of death or date of issuance of new certifcate should this be an updated death or stillbirth certificate.
For deaths that occured before 29 May 2022, physical death certificates remain valid and no digital death certificate will be issued. If one has misplaced or damaged this death certificate instead and wishes to obtain it, please apply for a death extract instead. Relevant fees will apply.
Check the details
Next, make sure that the NRIC, FIN, or passport number that you've entered is correct. If you're downloading the death certificate, you should enter the deceased's identification number. If you're downloading the stillbirth certificate, you should enter the mother's identification number.
The identification number should also match the one that was recorded by the hospital or doctor. For example, if the doctor certified the death with the deceased's FIN number, you should not enter the deceased's passport number.
You may also wish to verify the death or stillbirth document number with the hospital or doctor.
If details are accurate
Please try again 24 hours later. The doctor or hospital may not be able to submit the information online. If this happens, the certificate will not be available for download yet.
Meanwhile, any of these alternative documents issued by the hospital or doctor:
Confirmation of Death (COD),
Confirmation of Stillbirth (COS)
NEHR printout document
can be accepted for
Funeral Arrangements & Wake Space Booking
Burial & Cremation
Documents such as the eRBD printout and Certificate of Cause of Death (CCOD) cannot be used as alternative documents for funeral arrangements and other immediate post-death matters. Please see samples of these alternative documents here.
If you are still unable to download after 24 hours, please proceed to submit a query to us.

questions.title: I am unable to download the death or stillbirth certificate because the service is down. What should I do?
questions.text:
You'll have to wait for the service to be back up again to download the death or stillbirth certificate.
Meanwhile, any of these alternative documents issued by the hospital or doctor:
Confirmation of Death (COD),
Confirmation of Stillbirth (COS)
NEHR printout document
can be accepted for
Funeral Arrangements & Wake Space Booking
Burial & Cremation
Documents such as the eRBD printout and Certificate of Cause of Death (CCOD) cannot be used as alternative documents for funeral arrangements and other immediate post-death matters. Please see samples of these alternative documents here.
If you're having trouble applying for the permit to bury or cremate, call NEA at their 24-hour hotline 6225 5632.
We're sorry for the inconvenience in this time of loss. Do check back again later to download the death or stillbirth certificate. You should do so within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth.

questions.title: I noticed incorrect information on the death or stillbirth certificate. What should I do?
questions.text:
If it is within 6 months from the date of death or stillbirth, please notify the doctor or hospital to correct the information and issue a replacement certificate. Once a replacement certificate is issued download the replacement death or stillbirth certificate online, within 30 days from the date of issuance.
Please delete the version with incorrect information from your personal devices thereafter, as it will not be valid.
If it has been more than 6 months, please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA.

questions.title: I received a Confirmation of Death (COD) or Confirmation of Stillbirth (COS) document. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can proceed to use the document to apply for a burial or cremation permit with NEA. If you wish to hold a funeral wake at an HDB void deck, you can use this document to book a wake space with the town council.
You can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate 24 hours later, after arranging the funeral.
If you're having trouble applying for the permit to bury or cremate, call NEA at their 24-hour hotline 6225 5632.
About COD and COS
The Confirmation of Death (COD) and Confirmation of Stillbirth (COS) are official documents that are manually filled out by hand. They are issued by the hospital or doctor when the electronic death registration system is down for maintenance.
View sample COD and COS document (PDF)

questions.title: What document will I receive from the hospital or doctor who registered the death?
questions.text:
After a death or stillbirth has been certified, you'll receive 1 document from the hospital or doctor.
This can be any of the following:
National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) printout
Electronic Registration of Births and Deaths (eRBD) printout
Confirmation of Death (COD) or Confirmation of Stillbirth (COS)
If you received a Certificate of Cause of Death (CCOD), please contact ICA at Go.gov.sg or 6391 6100 for assistance.
View sample documents (PDF)
If the death was certified outside of a hospital, you may receive a photo of the document instead of a printout.
No matter which document you receive, you should download the digital death or stillbirth certificate. You'll need it to arrange the cremation or burial, manage estate settlement, and more.
However, you can also use the NEHR printout, COD, or COS to:
apply for a burial or cremation permit with NEA
book an HDB wake space with the town council

questions.title: Upon the death of a co-owner of a HDB flat under joint tenancy, what should the family do?
questions.text: Under the Land Titles Act, the surviving owner(s) is/are required to lodge a Notice of Death (NOD) with Singapore Land Authority (SLA) so that the ownership of the whole flat is vested in the surviving owner(s). Visit HDB's website for more information on retaining a flat following life events.

questions.title: Upon the death of a sole owner or co-owner of a HDB flat under tenancy-in-common, what should the family do?
questions.text: The deceased's family needs to apply to the Courts for the Grant of Letters of Administration (if the deceased did not leave a Will) or Grant of Probate (if there is a Will). With the document, the appointed person can then follow up to effect the change in the name of the flat from the deceased owner to the appointed person. Visit HDB's website to learn more.

questions.title: Must I engage a lawyer to carry out the transmission and transfer processes of a HDB flat to an executor/administrator of a deceased's estate? Can the executor / administrator sell the flat once the transmission has been carried out?
questions.text:
Yes. You need to appoint private solicitors to act for you in the transmission and transfer of the flat. HDB's solicitor may act for you, if eligible, and fees apply.
Transmission is the process where the executor or administrator registers their legal right to manage the deceased’s HDB flat (i.e. transfer ownership of the flat to the beneficiaries or sell the flat).
The eligibility for sale of flat depends on whether the deceased has met the minimum occupation period (MOP) for the flat at point of demise.
Executor
If the MOP for the flat is met before the demise of the late owner, the Executor may sell the flat in accordance with the Will. If the MOP of the flat Is not met, then special approval from HDB is needed for the sale of the flat.
Administrator
If the MOP for flat is met before the demise of the late owner, the Administrator may sell the flat on the open market in accordance with the order stated in the Grant Letters of Administration. If the MOP of the flat is not met before the demise of the late owner, special approval is needed from HDB.
You may read more information at HDB's webpage.

questions.title: How do I transfer / deregister a vehicle whose registered owner has passed away?
questions.text:
If the registered owner of a vehicle has passed away, the administrator(s) or executor(s) of the estate of the deceased/beneficiary may apply to transfer the vehicle to his/her name using LTA's "Apply to Transfer Asset of Deceased Owner" digital service (you will be prompted to log in via Singpass).
Required Documents
Original or Certified True Copy of the 'Grant of Probate' with a copy of the will, or 'Letters of Administration'
Original motor insurance certificate in the new owner's name, covering the full period of the vehicle's road tax
Transfer Fee
A $25 transfer fee applies.
Important Notes
If the vehicle is under hire-purchase, you should settle all outstanding financial matters with the hire-purchase company before submitting a transfer application.
If the Public Trustee is assisting on the administration of the Estate, they will apply to LTA to transfer the vehicle.
Get help for settling vehicle ownership
If you're in the process of applying for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration and need to manage the deceased's vehicle, visit the LTA website to learn about vehicle ownership transfer and deregistration. You can also contact LTA for assistance.

questions.title: Can I renew the road tax of a vehicle that belongs to a deceased owner?
questions.text:
Check that all the applicable road tax renewal prerequisites, such as having valid motor insurance coverage (at least third-party risk), passing of vehicle inspection, etc., are fulfilled at least 3 working days before renewing the vehicle's road tax.
As the registered owner of the vehicle has passed away, you are also advised to check that the insurance policy is issued under "The Estate of (deceased vehicle owner's name)". Road tax can be renewed via Internet, AXS Stations, AXS m-Station (mobile), AXS e-Station (internet) or Road Tax Collection Centres.
For road tax renewal at Road Tax Collection Centres, please bring along original supporting documents such as the hard copy insurance certificate/cover note and inspection certificate (if applicable) etc.
As long as a vehicle is registered in Singapore, the vehicle licence (i.e. road tax) of the vehicle remains payable regardless of whether the vehicle is being used or not. This includes vehicles that are registered under the name of a deceased vehicle owner.
Visit www.onemotoring.com.sg for more information.

questions.title: What if I do not wish to share my legacy plans with anyone?
questions.text: If you do not share your legacy plans with anyone and you pass away, no one will be able to retrieve or view the information you have within your dashboard.

questions.title: Can I share my legacy plans with a service provider?
questions.text:
There is no restriction in sharing your legacy plans with people you trust, so long as there is a personal Singpass login that can be associated with the Trusted Person logging in to view your shared documents.
However, it is recommended to keep your Singpass ID, password and 2FA details confidential.

questions.title: Can my Trusted Person(s) invite other people to access My Legacy dashboard?
questions.text: No. Only people you have personally added as a Trusted Person can see the contents of your dashboard.

questions.title: Are there requirements for who my Trusted Person can be e.g. only next-of-kin?
questions.text: No, there are no requirements and you may add any person who has a Singpass account. However, as the contents of your dashboard may be sensitive, you should only add individuals whom you trust.

questions.title: Does my Trusted Person know who else I have added to My Legacy vault?
questions.text: No. Trusted Persons can only see your Legacy vault contents. They cannot see who you have added. It is good practice to keep your Trusted Persons, next-of-kin and important others aware of who you have added as a Trusted Person.

questions.title: Does my Trusted Person(s) have any legal power?
questions.text: No, your Trusted Persons do not have any legal powers. If you would like to legally appoint them to carry out your wishes, consider a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and naming an executor in a will.

questions.title: Will my Trusted Person(s) be notified whenever I change something in My Legacy vault?
questions.text: Yes, your Trusted Persons will receive an email or SMS (depending on their preferred mode of communication) to inform them of the changes you have made for plans that you have shared with them.

questions.title: I'm having trouble using Text Us. Where can I find help?
questions.text:
You can refer to the Text Us Flow Chart to understand how our chat service works and how to navigate through each step.
Click the link below to see our detailed Text Us guide for solutions to common issues and tips for the best experience.
Learn more (PDF, 3MB)
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Can I receive the Child LifeSG Credits for my step-child?
questions.text: Step-parents who are Child Development Account (CDA) trustees can receive the credits. Step-parents who are not CDA trustees are required to legally adopt their eligible step-children to receive the Child LifeSG Credits.

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. Can I contribute to my MediSave together with my employees' CPF using CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
As self-employed person, you are required to make your MediSave payable separately from your employees' CPF. This is because payments made using CPF EZPay will be credited as employer contributions and will not be recognized as self-employed payments.
If you would like to make CPF contributions as a self-employed person, there are various ways to do so.

questions.title: How can I view or download my CPF LIFE monthly payout statement?
questions.text:
You can access your CPF LIFE monthly payout information through these steps:
Log in to cpf.gov.sg with your Singpass
Click on "my cpf" at the top navigation bar
Under "My dashboards", select the Retirement dashboard
Scroll to the 'Monthly payouts' section
Click on “Monthly payout history”
Select your preferred period to view the payout history
You may click the “PDF icon” to download your monthly payout statement for your selected period.

questions.title: What is PLAN with CPF?
questions.text:
Plan Life Ahead, Now! (PLAN) with CPF is a one-stop financial guidance platform that helps members take charge of their financial health across different life stages.
Members can access their personalised PLAN with CPF dashboard via Singpass login. The dashboard is designed to guide members on their financial planning journey, track their planning progress and identify next steps. Members can use the dashboard for quick access to the following:
CPF planners and tools to guide them in making informed decisions across different planning areas, such as the Retirement Payout Planner, Home Purchase Planner and Health Insurance Planner;
curated educational resources to help members deepen their understanding of various financial planning areas that may be relevant at different life stages; and
a financial fitness questionnaire to allow members to do a quick self-assessment on their financial health beyond CPF. This was developed in collaboration with MoneySense, based on the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) Basic Financial Planning Guide
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: Who can use PLAN with CPF?
questions.text:
PLAN with CPF is available to all Singaporeans aged 16 and above. They can log in via Singpass to access their personalised PLAN with CPF dashboard.
As the contents of PLAN with CPF are less relevant for those aged below 16 or non-Singaporeans, it is not available to these CPF members. They can view other contents in the CPF website that do not require Singpass login.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access my PLAN with CPF dashboard?
questions.text: You will need to log in using Singpass to access your PLAN with CPF dashboard because the contents are personalised based on your profile and planning progress. In addition, your previous inputs and plans will be saved for your future visits to your PLAN with CPF dashboard, making it easier for you to review your plans and track your planning progress over time.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: How do I use the PLAN with CPF dashboard?
questions.text: The PLAN with CPF dashboard helps you track your planning progress across five financial planning areas. You can easily take actions within each planning area, such as accessing relevant planners or viewing curated educational resources.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: What is the Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire?
questions.text:
The Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire enhances members’ awareness of common financial planning rules of thumb that go beyond CPF matters. It was developed in collaboration with MoneySense, based on the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) Basic Financial Planning Guide.
You can access the questionnaire by clicking the “Financial fitness beyond CPF” icon in your PLAN with CPF dashboard.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: How are the tips and insights in the Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire determined?
questions.text:
The tips and insights in the Financial fitness beyond CPF questionnaire are based on common financial planning rules of thumb in the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) Basic Financial Planning Guide. The Guide was created together with key industry stakeholders including the Association of Banks in Singapore, the Association of Financial Advisers (Singapore), and the Life Insurance Association.
The Guide provides a comprehensive set of rules of thumb for key aspects of a holistic financial plan, namely emergency funds, insurance protection, investment/retirement and legacy planning. While it provides members with guidance on how they can meet their key and basic financial planning needs, this guidance is not designed to be exhaustive. For detailed information on the Guide, you may refer to MoneySense’s FAQs.
topics: PLAN with CPF / General information on PLAN with CPF

questions.title: What is the Home Purchase Planner?
questions.text:
The Home Purchase Planner is an online tool that provides an estimated personalised budget for your home purchase if you are aged 21 and above. It provides the following insights to help you make informed decisions about buying a home:
The budget you can afford based on your current financial and housing situation
Different loan options
Illustrations on how your retirement payout may be impacted by your home purchase, including the amount of CPF savings used for your monthly housing loan repayments (Singpass log-in required)
If you are looking at buying a new home, start with the Home Purchase Planner to understand your options. For more accurate estimates:
log in to your CPF account and SGFinDex to save time and autofill your financial profile and housing information
prepare your HDB Flat Eligibility letter or in-principle approval letter from your bank if available.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: How does the Home Purchase Planner compute my budget?
questions.text:
The Home Purchase Planner helps you compute a home purchase budget by considering:
your Ordinary Account (OA) balance, cash savings and cash proceeds (if you sell an existing property); and
key financial parameters (e.g. Mortgage Servicing Ratio, loan tenure, and Loan-To-Value limit). See assumptions via this link.
The calculated budget provides a conservative estimate that helps you buy a home within your means. Here is an example:
John has:
$50,000 in his OA
$30,000 in cash
Based on his profile, John qualifies for a maximum housing loan of $400,000. With a loan-to-value limit of 75%, he technically has a budget of $532,000.
However, John’s actual budget is lower because:
He needs to make a minimum downpayment of 25%.
Assuming John uses his capital consisting of OA savings and cash of $80,000 for his downpayment, the maximum he can afford is $320,000. This is based on a loan of $240,000 covering the remaining 75% of the property price.
Therefore, the planner shows John’s purchase budget as $320,000, ensuring he buys a property within his financial means.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: How does the Home Purchase Planner determine the impact of my home purchase on my future retirement payouts?
questions.text:
The Home Purchase Planner (HPP) determines the impact of your home purchase on your future retirement payouts by considering:
your retirement goal – the monthly payout you need at age 65 to support your retirement lifestyle, after factoring in inflation
your retirement savings – the amount of CPF savings you are projected to have at age 65, after paying for your property (e.g. downpayment, monthly instalments)
If your retirement savings at age 65 fall short of what is needed to meet your retirement goal after factoring the estimated purchase budget, you should consider:
using less CPF savings and more cash to service your monthly instalments where possible
buying a more affordable property
boosting your retirement savings by making cash top-ups or CPF transfers.
The HPP also allows you to see the impact of using less CPF savings for your monthly housing instalments on your retirement savings.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: Do I need to log in to CPF with my Singpass to access the Home Purchase Planner?
questions.text:
It is recommended to log in to CPF using Singpass to use the Home Purchase Planner as:
your CPF information will be automatically filled, which helps save time and allows you to obtain a more accurate estimate of your home purchase budget; and
your latest CPF account balances will be used to project your retirement savings and monthly payouts.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: Do I need to log in to SGFinDex to access the Home Purchase Planner?
questions.text: It is recommended to log in to SGFinDex using Singpass to use the Home Purchase Planner as your financial data will be automatically filled, which helps save time and allows you to obtain a more accurate estimate of your home purchase budget.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Home Purchase Planner

questions.title: What is the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is an online tool that helps you make informed decisions about your health insurance coverage in about 15 minutes. Through a four-step process, HIP will allow you to:
have personalised projections of your long-term MediSave savings and health insurance premiums;
compare benefits, features, and premiums across Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) for your preferred ward type; and
have long-term premium projections for your selected IP and its rider.
