These features provide you with a consolidated view to better review and plan your healthcare coverage.
To use the HIP, members will need to prepare the name of their IP and rider, as well as the number of years left to pay for their CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplements, if applicable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Who can use the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is available to members aged 16 to 85. The minimum age of 16 is in line with the minimum age required by Singaporeans to access other CPF post-login e-services such as top-ups to MediSave. This also accounts for the fact that children below 16 are typically covered under their parents' health insurance plans and do not make independent coverage decisions.
The planner provides projections up to age 90, which is in line with the general life expectancy in Singapore, allowing for a more meaningful comparison for the majority of members.
The planner supports your financial planning needs across different life stages. As a young adult, you can evaluate insurance options while managing other financial commitments like education loans and home purchases. As your responsibilities change over time, you can continue using HIP to review your coverage needs and long-term affordability through to retirement.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Singpass login is required for the Health Insurance Planner to access your personal information, including your MediSave Account balance, MediShield Life and CareShield Life or ElderShield premiums, and details about your dependants. This information is needed to be used for projections. Through the Singpass login feature, the planner can also save your personalised inputs for future sessions, making it more convenient when you return.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Does the Health Insurance Planner include riders?
questions.text:
Similar to Ministry of Health (MOH)'s website, the Health Insurance Planner (HIP) focuses on comparing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) that are MediSave-payable and complement your MediShield Life coverage.
While HIP shows premium projections for co-payment riders if you choose to include them, it does not compare rider features and benefits. If you have other types of riders such as deductible cover, additional cancer coverage, daily cash, or global riders, your actual premiums may be higher than projected.
For existing policies, HIP uses your current rider information for projections. For new plans you are considering, it shows estimates based on the most expensive rider available for each IP. This helps you understand the potential cash outlay for rider premiums.
Please contact your insurer or financial advisor for detailed information about rider coverage and options.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What are the assumptions used in the projections within the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: For more information on assumptions used within the Health Insurance Planner (HIP), refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: How does the Health Insurance Planner project my insurance premiums?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) uses current age-based premium tables for MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans (IPs), and riders to calculate your projections. These rates may change over time and will be updated in HIP annually in January. Please note that the projections do not include premium loading, discounts, or claims-based pricing.
To provide realistic estimates, the planner factors in inflation for healthcare costs. You can adjust the inflation rates to customize your projections. The private medical insurance component of the IP and rider premiums are subject to the annual inflation rate set by you for medical insurance premiums, while CareShield Life and Supplement Plan premiums are subject to the annual inflation rate set by you for long-term care premiums.
For more information on assumptions used in these calculations, you may refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why do my Projected MediSave Savings differ when comparing MediShield Life (Projection 1) versus Integrated Shield Plan (Projection 2) and Integrated Shield Plan with Rider (Projection 3)?
questions.text:
Your Cumulative MediSave Savings are calculated differently based on your insurance coverage choices. If you have an existing Integrated Shield Plan (IP) with rider, the planner will show you three scenarios:
1. Projection 1: MediShield Life only
2. Projection 2: Existing IP
3. Projection 3: Existing IP with rider
Your Cumulative MediSave Savings include your current MediSave Account balance plus projected inflows for up to 30 years or age 90 (whichever comes first), rounded to the nearest decade (e.g., 50, 60, or 70).
The differences between Projection 1 and Projection 2 can arise for two reasons. When your MediSave reaches the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS), paying IP premiums creates room for additional MediSave contributions, potentially increasing your savings. However, these higher premium payments can also reduce your MediSave balance and earned interest, potentially decreasing your savings. These effects can happen at the same time, and their overall impact depends on your specific circumstances.
The projections for IP with and without riders show the same MediSave savings because rider premiums cannot be paid using MediSave.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner provides illustrative estimates to help with your financial planning. Your actual premiums and coverage may vary if you have special circumstances such as exclusions, premium loading, discounts, or claims-based pricing from your insurer. The projections also may not reflect costs of additional riders beyond co-payment riders, such as deductible cover, cancer coverage, daily cash, or global riders.
Please note that these projections should not replace professional financial advice. For specific guidance about your situation, please consult a financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: If I am not the payer for my health insurance policies, will I be able to use the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: Yes, you can use the Health Insurance Planner even if someone else pays for your policies. The planner will create projections as if you were the payer, allowing you to compare your current plan with other available options in the market.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Does the Health Insurance Planner account for the cost of dependants’ premiums?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner includes premium costs for dependants you currently pay for, based on CPF Board’s records. You can specify how many years you plan to continue paying premiums for each dependant.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why are my future MediShield Life premiums so high?
questions.text:
The projected MediShield Life premiums you see reflect expected medical inflation over time and increases with age. Your actual future premiums may differ based on factors like real medical inflation, how much people claim, and any changes in coverage benefits.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) works with the MediShield Life Council to actively review MediShield Life coverage and premiums to ensure that healthcare remains accessible and affordable.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: The Health Insurance Planner shows that I may have insufficient MediSave for my healthcare expenses and insurance premiums. Will I lose my insurance coverage?
questions.text:
No one will lose coverage to MediShield Life, our national health insurance scheme, due to an inability to pay their premiums.
If you face difficulty paying for MediShield Life premiums even after subsidies and MediSave, help is available through schemes like Additional Premium Support.
When choosing or renewing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders, consider both your coverage needs and long-term financial ability. Think about whether you have enough income and cash savings to cover expenses beyond what MediSave can pay.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Where does the Health Insurance Planner obtain information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders?
questions.text: The information on Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders is provided by the insurers and is updated annually in January. For a comparison of IPs across all insurers, you may refer to Ministry of Health (MOH)’s website.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Some riders have claims-based pricing, where premiums are adjusted based on claims made by the policyholder in the preceding year. Is this considered in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text: The Health Insurance Planner does not account for claims-based pricing in riders. For specific information about how your claims history might affect your rider premiums, please contact your insurer or financial advisor.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Why does the Health Insurance Planner not display all benefits in the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparison?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner focuses on the most commonly used benefits to make comparisons simpler and more user-friendly. For a complete comparison of all Integrated Shield Plan (IP) benefits across insurers, please visit Ministry of Health (MOH)'s website.
The list of key benefits are:
Inpatient benefits
Daily ward and treatment charges (Normal ward)
Daily ward and treatment charges (ICU)
Outpatient benefits
Cancer drug treatment
Cancer drug services
Kidney dialysis
Pre-hospitalisation
Post-hospitalisation
Co-payment and other features
Deductible
Co-insurance
Pro-ration factors
Pre-authorisation
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Can the Government allow us to use more of our MediSave to pay for our Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums? Why aren’t withdrawal limits sized such that IP policyholders do not have to pay cash for their IP premiums?
questions.text: MediSave's main purpose is to help you save enough for basic healthcare needs, particularly after retirement. While Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) provide additional coverage, they are optional commercial products beyond MediShield Life. The MediSave Additional Withdrawal Limits (AWLs) are carefully balanced to help make IPs more affordable while ensuring you have enough savings for both current and future healthcare needs.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Many individuals purchase Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders despite MediShield Life provides adequate protection for subsidised care in public hospitals. What is being done to improve consumer education around IPs and riders?
questions.text:
Ministry of Health (MOH) and CPF Board (CPFB) are enhancing public education about healthcare financing through several initiatives.
The Health Insurance Planner helps you evaluate your coverage needs and long-term affordability based on your care preferences and financial situation.
MOH launched a healthcare financing education campaign in June 2024 to explain how different insurance schemes work together. They also started publishing comparisons of lifetime premiums across Integrated Shield Plans (IPs). These complement existing resources on MOH's website about IP benefits, features, premiums, and insurer service indicators like claims processing times.
Additionally, MOH and CPFB collaborate with MoneySense, Singapore's national financial education programme, to provide guidance on IP purchases through educational articles and resources.
These efforts aim to help Singaporeans understand how MediShield Life coverage can meet their needs for subsidised care in public hospitals, and to weigh the costs and benefits of additional private coverage.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Are Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders which are closed to new business included in the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
If you currently have a closed Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or rider, you can select it in the "Current Plan" section and compare it with other available options.
However, if you are not already covered under a closed plan, these plans will not appear in the IP comparison since they are not open to new subscribers.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: What should I do if I want to get advice or make changes to my coverage (e.g. Integrated Shield Plan (IP) and rider) after using the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
After using the Health Insurance Planner, you can download a report containing your personalised projections and Integrated Shield Plan (IP) comparisons for reference during discussions with your insurer or financial advisor.
Please note that the planner's projections are for illustration only and should not be taken as financial advice from CPF Board or Ministry of Health. To make changes to your coverage:
If you are staying with your current insurer but want to downgrade to a lower ward class IP, no new premium loading or exclusions will apply.
If you are switching insurers, you may need new medical underwriting, which could result in premium loading, new exclusions, or application rejection.
Before making any changes, please consult your financial advisor to understand all implications.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Can I bring my pet to the event?
questions.text: Pets, except for service animals, are not allowed at the event venue due to safety and hygiene considerations.

questions.title: Will military assets be showcased for Heartlands?
questions.text: The Mobile Column to the Heartlands, comprising of 12 assets from SAF, SPF and SCDF, will be making their way from the city centre and travel along five different routes to reach the Heartland sites. The convoys will form up as static displays at each site. There are limited assets that can travel on the road, and we evaluate the capacity that each site can hold them.

questions.title: Why is my stamping submission still under pending approval?
questions.text:
If your authorised role under Corppass for stamp duty e-Services is set as 'Preparer', you are only authorised to prepare the stamping record and submit it to an "Approver" within your organisation for final submission to IRAS. Please contact your company’s appointed Approver to complete the submission.
However, if your company has authorised you to handle both the preparation and submission, please ask your Corppass administrator to update your role to "Approver". An approver can handle both data entry and submission of the stamping record.
Note: If you are assigned both the 'Preparer' and 'Approver' roles, you will only be granted the access of a 'Preparer'.

questions.title: I had have inherited a property. Will this be included in my property count for ABSD purposes?
questions.text:
Yes. For ABSD purposes, your property count includes not only properties that are purchased, but also those acquired or transferred through other means such as:
- Inheritance
- Gift
- Release
- Settlement
- Declaration of trust (where the beneficial owners are identifiable)
- Letter of authority
- Exchange
As such, an inherited property will be included in your property count when determining ABSD liability.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I own an HDB shophouse, will it be included in my property count for ABSD purposes?
questions.text: Yes. An HDB Shophouse with living quarters will be included in the property count for the purpose of calculating ABSD.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am a Singapore citizen planning to jointly purchase our first matrimonial home with my foreign spouse. As this is our first property, are we required to pay Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)?
questions.text:
No. ABSD is not payable on the joint purchase of a residential property by a married couple where at least one spouse is a Singapore citizen, provided neither spouse owns any residential property at the time of purchase.
This is in accordance with the Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: How do I cancel my Permanent Resident status if I intend to close my CPF account upon leaving Singapore?
questions.text: As cancellation of Permanent Resident status is administered by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA), you may submit your request via ICA | Feedback.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: How do I view, save or download my monthly transaction statement?
questions.text:
Members can now view their monthly transactions in 'Transaction history' under ‘My statements'.
Upon receiving your monthly email notification, follow these steps to view, save and download your statement:
Click the "View now" button in the email and you will be redirected to the Singpass login page.
Log in with your Singpass to authenticate your identity.
Once authenticated, your CPF Transaction history statement will be displayed. To obtain a statement for a specific month, use the filter option to enter the same month for both the start and end month in the Transaction history (e.g. to generate the monthly statement for Jun 2026, select “Jun 2026" for both the start and end month). For detailed guidance, please refer to our step-by-step guide below.
To save or download your monthly transaction statement, click the PDF icon on the top right corner. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Can I appoint a non-Singaporean as my LPA Donee?
questions.text:
A non-Singaporean can be a Donee. You may appoint a foreign Donee in your LPA, so long as they meet the requirements of being a Donee e.g. 21 years old and above. If the foreign Donee has a Singpass account, the donor may make an LPA online. The Donee may log in to OPGO via Singpass to accept the appointment.
If the Donee does not have a Singpass account, the donor may submit a hardcopy LPA form together with the cover letter on why a hardcopy LPA is submitted. Mail in or drop off the completed hardcopy LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) at 3 Bishan Place #03-00, CPF Bishan Building, Singapore 579838.

questions.title: How do I declare my annual net trade income as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
From Work Year 2023 onwards
All net trade income (NTI)1 declarations can be made with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) by filing a tax return. There is no need to file separate declarations with CPF Board.
1NTI is your gross trade income minus all allowable business expenses, capital allowances and trade losses as determined by IRAS.
If you have earned income from more than one trade, you should declare each source of income separately when filing your tax return with IRAS. Each trade should be reported under its own appropriate nature of business category. Refer to IRAS’ step-by-step guide to declare your income(s).
When IRAS has completed the income assessment for the year, you will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board informing you of your MediSave payable. You will be able to view this notice on the self-employment dashboard after logging in with your Singpass.
For Work Year 2022 or earlier
If you were not issued with a Notice of Assessment by IRAS and wish to declare your NTI for work year 2022 and earlier, you can write to us using your Singpass.
If you have declared your NTI with IRAS, you do not need to declare your income again to CPF Board.

questions.title: Can I still request information regarding my CPF balances, CPF interest earned or, my CPF transaction statement after renunciation of my Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you have recently renounced your Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency, please log in to my cpf digital services while you still have access to your Singpass account. You may wish to download any CPF information you need, including your Yearly Statement of Account for the past 10 years (if applicable), and settle any outstanding matters related to your CPF account.
Please note that we do not provide CPF statements beyond the past 10 years.
Due to difficulties in authenticating a caller’s identity over the phone and email, we seek your understanding that the Board is unable to disclose any information relating to a specific CPF account over phone or email. This is for your own protection.
The Board would like to assure that your full CPF balances will be transferred to your bank account upon your request, after the closure of your CPF account.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: I am not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, how do I receive my CPF savings?
questions.text:
You will need to submit an application to receive your CPF savings if you are no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. For details on the various application modes, please refer to this FAQ. When submitting your application, you may choose to receive your CPF monies via one of the following two options:
1. Bank transfers via Interbank GIRO (IBG) to your Singapore bank account
2. Telegraphic transfer to your bank account overseas
Please ensure that the bank accepts payment in Singapore dollars. Otherwise, we will convert the payment to US dollars. You will need to bear all bank charges, including any foreign exchange rate differences and conversion charges:
i. for telegraphic transfer to an overseas bank account
ii. if you provide insufficient bank account details resulting in an unsuccessful telegraphic transfer.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What are some good practices to follow when contributing CPF to my platform workers?
questions.text: For more details regarding good practices to follow, and common mistakes to avoid when contributing CPF to your platform workers, please refer to this document.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Are CPF contributions for platform workers rounded to the nearest dollar?
questions.text:
For mandatory/opted-in platform workers
The total contributions for the calendar month should be rounded off to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents. Amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar.
The cents should always be dropped for the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions.
For not-opted-in platform workers
As there is no platform operator share of CPF contributions, the total contributions payable by platform workers for the calendar month should be rounded off to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents. Amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar.
You can use our PW CPF Contribution Calculator to calculate the CPF contributions applicable to your platform workers.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Why can’t I book an LPA appointment online with some Certificate Issuers?
questions.text:
Only Certificate Issuers (CIs) who are onboarded to the Health Appointment System (HAS) and have enabled the LPA service offering will have a “Book an Appointment” button for online booking.
For other CIs, please contact them directly using the phone number or details provided in the "Browse all certificate issuers" list.

questions.title: My mobile number/email address is outdated. How can I update my records in Singpass?
questions.text:
To update your mobile number/email address with Singpass, please complete the following steps:
Login to the Singpass website
Select ‘Menu’ > ‘Update profile’ (under the ‘My Account’ tab) and follow the instructions on the website to complete the updating of your mobile number/email address
Please ensure that you have access to your mobile phone/email as a One-Time Password (OTP) will be sent to your updated mobile number/email address for verification.
If you require further assistance, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly. The operating hours are from 8am to 8pm (Mondays to Fridays) and from 8am to 2pm (Saturdays) excluding Sundays and public holidays.

questions.title: What if I had declared a wrong net trade income to IRAS or CPF Board?
questions.text:
If you had wrongly declared your net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS)
If you need to make changes after filing your Income Tax Return with IRAS, please refile your return at myTax Portal using your Singpass within seven days of your previous submission or by 18 April, whichever is earlier. If you miss this deadline to refile your returns, please visit the IRAS website at www.iras.gov.sg, call them at 1800-356 8300, or write to them via myTax Mail on myTax Portal using your Singpass.
[For Work Year 2022 or earlier] If you had wrongly declared your NTI to CPF Board
Please write to us using your Singpass.
Once CPF Board has received your revised income declaration, you can check your updated NTI records by logging in to the self-employment dashboard with your Singpass.

questions.title: I am not a self-employed person. Why did I receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board?
questions.text:
You will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons if you had declared a net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and your NTI1 exceeds $6,000. The notice of CPF contributions will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
If you disagree with the assessed income by IRAS, you may approach IRAS for further clarifications.

questions.title: Why are the retirement sums increasing yearly?
questions.text:
The increase in retirement sums is due to the following:
Increase in cost of living
As prices of goods and services rise over time, we will need to save more for retirement to ensure that our savings will still be sufficient to cover higher expenses in the future.
Increase in life expectancy
As people are living longer, we will need more savings to last throughout our retirement.
Increase in standard of living
As incomes increase over time, our basic retirement expectations and expenses will also naturally increase. Setting aside more savings allows us to receive higher monthly payouts to afford higher retirement expenses in future.
However, if you are already 55, the yearly increase won't affect you. The retirement sum you need to set aside depends on when you turn 55 and is fixed for the rest of your life.
It's important to keep in mind that the amount needed for retirement has increased over the years. For example, if the Full Retirement Sum had remained unchanged from $30,000 when it was first introduced in 1987 (previously known as the Minimum Sum), it would only provide a monthly payout of about $300 today. This amount would not be enough to cover daily living expenses and rent.
Overall, the goal of increasing retirement savings is to help individuals build a financial foundation that will enable them to support themselves through retirement.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What are the retirement sums - Basic Retirement Sum (BRS), Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
The CPF Retirement Sum is the principal amount1 of savings in your CPF Retirement Account (RA). The more savings you have in your RA, the higher your monthly payouts will be in retirement.
There are three Retirement Sum reference points to guide you on the Retirement Sum to set aside based on your retirement needs.
Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) provides you monthly payouts for basic living needs, excluding rental expenses2.
Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is double your BRS and is the default amount to set aside in your RA when you turn 55.
Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) is double the current year’s FRS and is the maximum amount you can top up to your RA if you are aged 55 and above. The ERS increases yearly, and topping up to the current year’s ERS allows you to get the highest CPF monthly payouts.
If you are age 55 and above, visit the Retirement Dashboard to find out whether you have set aside your FRS and the amount you can top up to your RA for higher monthly payouts.
1This includes CPF contributions, top-ups and transfers from other CPF accounts to the RA, but generally excludes government grants. Interest earned on RA savings is excluded.
2If you own a property in Singapore with remaining lease that lasts you until you are 95 or older, you may apply to withdraw RA savings down to your BRS.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What happens if I have used my CPF savings to pay for my home and do not have enough CPF savings left to set aside Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
You can set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of CPF savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and CPF savings used for your property. At age 55, if your RA savings is less than your FRS, the CPF savings used for your property (including accrued interest) will automatically be counted towards meeting up to half of your FRS.
For example: John turns 55 in 2025 and has $113,000 in his RA. He had used $200,000 of his CPF for his property (including accrued interest). His FRS of $213,000 would be set aside with the $113,000 in his RA and $100,000 of the CPF used for his property.
When you sell your property, you will need to refund the CPF savings (including accrued interest) used for your property to your CPF accounts. This will be used to set aside your FRS in cash.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Will my CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme be used to make up my Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme will not be used to make up your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Your FRS is made up using your Special Account (SA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings.
Find out how your FRS is set aside when you turn 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How are the Basic Retirement Sum and Full Retirement Sum determined for each cohort?
questions.text:
The Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) takes reference from a person's expenditure from a lower-middle retiree household, according to the latest Household Expenditure Survey (HES). It assumes that the member owns a property that lasts him up to 95 and he does not need to pay rent in retirement.
The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is set at two times of the BRS.
The BRS or FRS you need to set aside depends on when you turn 55 and is fixed for the rest of your life.
Find out why the retirement sums are adjusted yearly for successive cohorts.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is the current Enhanced Retirement Sum?
questions.text:
The current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) for 2026 is $440,800.
The ERS is increased yearly. For members 55 and above who wish to have higher monthly payouts in retirement, they can top up their Retirement Account up to the current ERS. To find out how much you can top up, log in to your Retirement dashboard.
From 1 January 2025, the ERS was raised to double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum to enable members to voluntarily commit more savings for even higher payouts. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts of up to $3,440 for life from age 65 through CPF top-ups. Learn more about the payouts you can receive.
Here are the ERS amounts for 2026 to 2027 to enable you to plan your top-ups:

topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How are the CPF LIFE payouts calculated?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE payouts are computed based on the following factors:
FactorHow it affects your monthly payout
Your Retirement Account (RA) balance when you join CPF LIFEYour RA savings are used to pay for the CPF LIFE premium. The higher your RA balance when you join CPF LIFE, the higher your payout will be.
When you start payouts For each year that you defer starting payouts, your payouts will increase by up to 7%.
CPF interest ratesCPF LIFE payouts factor in the CPF interest rate, with a floor of 4%, and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances.
Life expectancy / Mortality rates
Since CPF LIFE pays monthly payouts for life, longer life expectancies would result in lower monthly payouts as the payout duration is longer on average.
Hence, males receive higher payouts compared to females as they have a shorter average life expectancy.

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 65?
questions.text:
The amount of CPF savings you can withdraw from age 65 depends on your birth year and whether you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). The withdrawal criteria differ across cohorts and generally:
You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA) savings if you have set aside your FRS, or up to $5,000 if you have not.
If you are born from 1957 onwards, you may also withdraw an additional amount from your Retirement Account (RA) savings, depending on your RA savings at age 65.
Refer to the infographic on the withdrawal criteria and an example on the additional withdrawal from RA.
You can log in to the withdrawal application form to check how much you can withdraw.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive my CPF savings partially when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore citizenship/ permanent residency?
questions.text: No, your CPF savings will be paid to you in full.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Can I attend and vote at meetings for shareholders, bondholders, or unit holders under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.text:
You can attend and vote at meetings for shareholders, bondholders, or unit holders if you hold these investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS):
Shares of Companies incorporated in Singapore (click this link to check if a company is incorporated in Singapore)
REITs
Corporate bonds
Unit trusts
If you hold shares, REITs, or corporate bonds under CPFIS, you generally do not need to inform your agent bank of your attendance. Your agent bank will automatically appoint you as a proxy to attend and vote at the meetings. You will be appointed to exercise the rights attached to the shares, REITs, or corporate bonds held by you.
However, for specific events such as schemes of arrangement, where only one proxy is allowed, you will need to pre-register your attendance with your agent bank. This ensures that you can be appointed as the proxy for these special circumstances.
If you are unable to attend the meeting, you cannot appoint a proxy to attend on your behalf. Instead, you may indicate your voting preference to your agent bank, who will vote on your behalf.
If you hold other investments like shares of foreign-incorporated companies or business trusts and wish to attend the meeting, you need to pre-register your attendance with your agent bank. Thereafter, you may attend the meeting as an observer only. However, you may indicate your voting preference to your agent bank, who will vote on your behalf.
If you hold unit trusts, you will be notified by the registrars, and you can attend the meeting directly.
Identification requirements
CPFIS investors must bring their NRIC/passport for identity verification at the registration counter(s) outside the meeting venues. Companies reserve the right to refuse admittance to their meetings if attendees' identities cannot be verified.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 55 to 64?
questions.text:
You can check the CPF savings you can withdraw from age 55 by logging into your Retirement dashboard.
The amount that you can withdraw is determined as follows:
If you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash:
You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA)
If you have not set aside your FRS:
You can withdraw $5,000 from your OA
Upon your withdrawal, non-withdrawable amounts in your OA may be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to make up your FRS. This transfer occurs with each withdrawal until you have set aside your FRS.
For example: John turned 55 in 2026 with $100,000 in his RA and $5,000 in his OA. His OA savings later grew by $2,000 from contributions and interest earned, bringing the total to $7,000. As he has not set aside his FRS of $220,400, he can only withdraw up to $5,000 from his OA. The remaining $2,000 in his OA cannot be withdrawn and will be transferred to his RA subsequently to help him set aside his FRS.
You can withdraw an additional amount of your retirement savings from 65. The amount you can withdraw depends on your birth year and generally excludes any cash top-ups, CPF transfers and government grants.

questions.title: How do I add, remove or share documents with a Trusted Person on My Legacy vault?
questions.text:
1) Adding a Trusted Person
To add a Trusted Person, login via Singpass to My Legacy vault. Under “Secure Sharing”, click on “View Trusted Persons”.
Then, click on “Invite new person” and key in the details as prompted before clicking on “Invite” to confirm the invitation. If your trusted person does not receive the notification via SMS / Email, please ask them to login directly to Vault to accept the invitation. Note that invites expire in 3 weeks and you only can add the same person up to 5 times before you are unable to add them anymore.
Once successful, you should see a pending invite which will shift into the “Accepted” tab, once your Trusted Person has accepted the invite.
2) Removing a Trusted Person
To remove a Trusted Person, click on the Trusted Person (under “Accepted” or “Pending”), then click “More”, and finally click “Remove Trusted Person”. Do note that edit only allows you to edit sharing access. If you need to amend the details of a Trusted Person, this will be done by removing them and adding them back with the amended details.
3) Sharing Documents with Trusted Persons
Once a Trusted Person has accepted the invite, click on the added Trusted Person, then click “Share Documents”. Under the Share Documents page, select between “Now, After Death or Never” to choose which access the Trusted Person has.

questions.title: When should I receive my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Your employer must pay your CPF contributions for each month's wages by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
Enforcement action will be taken against employers who fail to pay CPF contributions by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday).
Once CPFB has received the payment, the contributions will be credited to your CPF accounts within three working days, and you will be able to view the amounts through the CPF transaction history using your Singpass.
If you notice that your CPF contributions are not paid accurately or timely, you should check with your employer immediately.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens after I lodge a police report for scam-related cases?
questions.text:
If you've lost money to a potential scam, please immediately file a police report online or in person at the nearest Neighbourhood Police Post.
Please refer to our guide on what to include when you file a police report.
If you have already made a police report, please follow up with SPF using this Enquiry Form.
Please also contact your bank immediately to cancel the fraudulent transaction(s).
Please refer to this list for your Bank's Anti-Scam Hotline.
How long does a police investigation for a scam-related case take?
The time taken to complete an investigation into a scam-related case depends on several factors, such as the type of scam, how well the scammer covers his tracks and whether the monies have been transferred overseas. If monies have been transferred overseas — which often is the case when it comes to scams that happened in Singapore — then the time taken is necessarily longer. In view of the factors highlighted above, the time taken for each case may differ.
When will I obtain updates for my police case?
An acknowledgement letter/email will be sent to you within seven working days after you have reported your case. The Investigation Officer (IO) in charge of your case will update you when there are significant developments to the case. We seek your understanding that every case is unique and the time taken to investigate each case differs. If urgent police assistance is required, please call ‘999’.
I was a victim of an online scam and was cheated of my money. Will the Police be able to recover my money?
A typical modus operandi by scam syndicates is to move scammed monies quickly between multiple bank accounts, including to overseas bank accounts. If the money is transferred overseas, fund recovery can be challenging as different jurisdictions have different recovery process and legislation. The chances of recovery once the funds have been transferred out of Singapore are very low, and it is likely that the money may no longer be recoverable.
Why is it so challenging for the Police to recover my money if it has been transferred out of Singapore?
Overseas accounts reside outside of Singapore’s jurisdiction and the Singapore Police Force will not be able to exercise any legal powers to freeze or seize the account or compel a foreign-based bank to reverse the transactions. In such cases, the Police can only notify our foreign counterparts of the incident and seek their assistance to investigate into the matter. It also depends on the laws of the foreign country and the internal business policies of the foreign banks involved. The chances of recovery once the funds have been transferred out of Singapore are very low, and it is likely that the money may no longer be recoverable.
How long does the Police take to return my money if it is recovered?
The Police will only be able to return any seized monies to victims upon the conclusion of investigations. The amount of time it takes to complete investigations, and correspondingly, the amount of time it takes for seized monies to be returned to the victims, depends on many different factors and differs across the various types of scams. For example, whether there are multiple claimants and whether the monies are still relevant for the purposes of investigation, court trial or other court proceedings.
Where can I seek support?
If you require emotional support during the investigation and/or court process, inform your Investigation Officer (IO) who will arrange for you to speak to a Victim Care Officer (VCO). VCOs are volunteers who are trained in providing emotional and practical support to victims of crime as they undergo the criminal justice process.
Please refer here for more community support avenues. Remember, you are not alone in this!
For more information:
Please refer to our Anti-Scam Resource Guide in all 4 national languages here.

questions.title: Why is a conveyancing lawyer required when using CPF savings to purchase a private property?
questions.text: A conveyancing lawyer is required when you would like to use your CPF savings for purchase of a private property for the first time. The lawyers would typically manage all legal aspects of your transaction, including preparing and submitting required documents needed by the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), creating and lodging a CPF charge. This legal representation protects both your CPF savings and your interests in the property, which is critical in high-value transactions such as buying a property.

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next-of-kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I apply to withdraw his CPF savings?
questions.text:
Make an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centre and bring along the following original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order;
Trust bank account statement or passbook; and
Your NRIC.
*If the original medical report has been submitted to the Court, you can retrieve a copy via IFAMS and note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on “Mental Capacity Act Application”
Click on the tab “Other Matters”
Click on “File Other Applications or Requests”
Log in via SingPass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select “File request for copy of documents” and fill up the required information.
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents so that you can receive your loved one’s CPF savings smoothly.

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next-of-kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I apply to withdraw his CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme?
questions.text:
You may apply to withdraw your next-of-kin’s CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme by following the steps below:
Step 1: Submit online application
Complete and submit the online withdrawal application form. You can also use the same form to concurrently apply for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) benefits.
Step 2: Submit supporting documents
After submitting your online application, provide these original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order; and
Trust bank account statement or passbook.
You can submit the documents by making an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centres or mail them to us at:
Central Provident Fund Board
Retirement Withdrawals Department
Privy Box No. 920651
Singapore 929292
*If the Court Order was applied through iFAMS, you can retrieve a copy of the medical report via iFAMS. Please note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on “Mental Capacity Act Application”
Click on the tab “Other Matters”
Click on “File Other Applications or Requests”
Log in via SingPass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select “File request for copy of documents” and fill up the required information.

questions.title: What is the voluntary top-up limit to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up is the difference between the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740 and the mandatory CPF contributions made for the calendar year.
Do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest in the following year to your registered bank account in our records. For top-ups made on behalf of others, the excess top-up amount will be refunded directly to the recipient's registered bank account in our records.
Please keep your bank account in Account settings up to date. If your bank account details are not updated, the refund will be made to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account by default.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Is my voluntary top-up to the 3 CPF accounts reversible?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
However, if the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest. Therefore, do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones' 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
You can make a top up via Top up your 3 CPF accounts using PayNow QR1.
You will be prompted to key in your Recipient's NRIC/CPF Account Number if you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf.
All applications and payments should reach CPF Board by the last day of the calendar year for it to be counted as the year’s CPF Annual Limit. Backdating of top-ups to previous years is not allowed.
Tax relief is only applicable if you are a self employed-person with assessable net trade income for the year of assessment, when you make a self top-up or receive a top-up from another person.
You can find out more on the different voluntary top-ups.
For self-employed persons, amounts allocated to your MediSave Account from these top-ups will be used to offset your MediSave payable and meet the MediSave requirement for Workfare Income Supplement (if eligible).
1Subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded. To ensure that your cash top-ups are processed successfully, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once. You will need to submit a new application each time you wish to make another top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why is there a limit set for top-up to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text: There is a limit set as the CPF system is generally meant to cater to the needs of up to 80th percentile of workers in Singapore. Higher income earners would have other means to supplement their retirement income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How long does it take to process voluntary top-ups applications to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
The application relating to voluntary top-ups to your 3 CPF accounts will be processed as stated in the table below.
Service

If the top-up amount is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Can I voluntarily top-up to my Ordinary Account only?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups cannot be made solely to the Ordinary Account.
You can make voluntary top-ups to your:
Special / Retirement Account only under the Retirement Sum Topping Up Scheme (RSTU) (tax relief available).
MediSave Account only (tax relief available)1
3 CPF accounts2
Voluntary top-up is applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents only.
You can find out more on the different voluntary top-ups.
1For self-employed persons who wish to make a voluntary top up to MediSave Account, you must have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable as a self-employed person.
2Tax relief is only applicable to self-employed persons, based on their assessable net trade income for the year of assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups only refunded in the following year?
questions.text:
The CPF Annual Limit (AL) consists of both the Mandatory Contribution (MC) from your employer and Voluntary Contributions (VC) paid by you, if any. You are allowed to top up VC up to the CPF Annual Limit (AL) of the year.
As the MC for December can be paid by January of the following year, any excess VC top-ups made for the preceding year can only be finalized and refunded in the following year.
If your mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit during the year, you can write to us to request for refund of the excess voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups refunded with no interest?
questions.text: The excess voluntary top-ups can only be determined after all your mandatory contributions have been received for the year. This is usually after the month of January in the following year. The interest on the excess voluntary top-ups which should not be earned by the member will be returned to the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I check the status of my top-up application?
questions.text:
You may login to your CPF account and check the status of your online application under “Activities”. If your top-up application is successful, it will be reflected in your CPF accounts.
If you have made multiple top-up applications, do check the status of all your applications to see which transactions have been successfully processed and make a new application if necessary.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: My top-up via PayNow QR is not reflected in my CPF account. Why is my CPF account balance(s) not updated immediately?
questions.text:
Your top-up via PayNow QR will generally be processed immediately upon successful deduction from your bank account.
If your top-up is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: With the closure of my Special Account, how will the top-up to my 3 CPF accounts be allocated?
questions.text:
For CPF members aged 55 and above, the voluntary top-up to your 3 CPF accounts after the closure of the Special Account will be made to your Ordinary Account (OA), Retirement Account (RA) and MediSave Account.
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
You may refer to the CPF allocation rate table (PDF, 0.1MB) for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How do I find my downloaded CPF documents on my mobile phone or tablet?
questions.text:
When you download your CPF documents (e.g. statements) your device saves it automatically. Here's how to find it:
For iPhone or iPad:
Look for the blue "Files" app on your screen
Tap on "Files"
Tap on "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For Android phones or tablets:
Look for "My Files" or "File Manager" app
Tap to open it
Look for "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For more information, please see:
Where to find downloads on your iPhone or iPad
Where to find downloads on Android devices
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next of kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I receive monthly payouts on behalf of my next of kin?
questions.text:
Make an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centres and bring along the following original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order;
Trust bank account statement or passbook; and
Your NRIC/Foreign Passport.
*If the Court Order was applied through iFAMS, you can retrieve a copy of the medical report via iFAMS. Please note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on "Mental Capacity Act Application"
Click on the tab "Other Matters"
Click on "File Other Applications or Requests"
Log in via Singpass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select "File request for copy of documents" and fill up the required information.
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents so that your application can be processed promptly for you to receive your next-of-kin’s CPF savings.

questions.title: How do I check the voluntary top-up limit to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
When you make a cash top-up online, you will be shown the amount of top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
You can follow these steps to check how much you can top up to your 3 CPF accounts:
Go to the Top up your 3 CPF accounts form
Log in with your Singpass
Select “I wish to make a top-up to Myself” under “Recipient details”
Your top-up limit will then be displayed.
If the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, the excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest the following year. Therefore, do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups.
If you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: What is the CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender?
questions.text:
The CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender is a tool designed to assist employers to easily identify a CPF EZPay submission mode that is assessed to be suitable for them.
The Recommender would recommend one of the available submission mode (i.e. CPF EZPay (Employee Database), CPF EZPay (FTP), CPF EZPay (ESI), and CPF EZPay Mobile) based on information the employer provides. Employer may find out more on the submission mode recommended to see if it meets their needs.
Regardless of the recommendation by the Recommender, employers may continue to use any of the CPF EZPay submission mode they prefer.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: What is an authentic court order ("ACO")?
questions.text:
An authentic court order (ACO) is a court order verified to have been issued by a Singapore court.
Previously, parties that need to show their court order to others may be asked to provide a certified true copy ("CTC"). They have to apply for the CTC and this can take several days and require more than one trip to the court. A fee needs to be paid for every hardcopy CTC. The hardcopy CTC may also be inadvertently misplaced, or the party may not have sufficient CTCs and may need to obtain additional CTCs.
The ACO system simplifies this.
If your Court Order was issued after 2013, you may be able to retrieve an Authentic Court Order (ACO) from https://courtorders.gov.sg/ . An Authentic Court Order (ACO) is an official, digitally verifiable court document issued by the Singapore Courts. Accessible via www.courtorders.gov.sg, it replaces the need to request, pay for, and collect physical Certified True Copies (CTCs).
If your Court Order HAS a QR code on it:
Scan or Visit: Scan the QR code printed on your document, or go straight to www.courtorders.gov.sg. No login is required.
Verify: Enter the Access Code shown on your document. If prompted, additionally type in the Case Number (without any alphabets).
Download & Share: Instantly view, download, share, or print out the verified digital PDF.
If You Have Misplaced Your Court Order, or Your Court Order DOES NOT have a QR Code
Log In: Go to www.courtorders.gov.sg and log in securely using your Singpass.
Enter Details: Input your Case Number and Document / Court Order Number. Our system will need to ensure that you are a legitimate party in the case.
Request & Retrieve: Submit the details to generate and retrieve your digital authentic court order version for free. The request may take some time to be processed, so please return to check the status regularly.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: What Court Orders are included in the Authentic Court Orders (ACO) system?
questions.text:
Court orders that are included in the ACO system can be validated online. These include court orders that are:
Made after 2 Jan 2020 for civil cases in the State Courts and High Court.
Made after 2 Jan 2020 for family cases filed in eLitigation.
Made after 8 March 2021 for tribunal cases filed in the Community Justice and Tribunals System (CJTS).
Made after 12 March 2021 for family cases filed in the Integrated Family Management System (iFAMS).
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: Will anyone be able to access any other person's court order using the Authentic Court Orders system?
questions.text:
An individual will need both of the following to retrieve a document from the ACO portal:
The QR Code or the access code
The case number.
In addition, the CAPTCHA mechanism detects bot "attacks" on the ACO portal. It is very unlikely that a person who has not been given the access code and the case number can randomly "guess" the relevant information to obtain access to a Court order.
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: Can certified true copies still be obtained, even though a Court Order may already have an "Authentic Court Order" available?
questions.text:
Certified True Copies (CTCs) will still be available upon application.
A fee needs to be paid for every hardcopy CTC. The hardcopy CTC may also be inadvertently misplaced, or the party may not have sufficient CTCs and may need to obtain additional CTCs.
The introduction of the ACO system is intended to simply this and to reduce the need for CTC hardcopies.
If your court order is included in the ACO system:
Special information (such as a QR code and access code) will be printed on the court order.
You can show a photocopy, email, fax or a screenshot of the ACO to the organisation that requires it. The organisation can also retrieve a validated copy of the court order directly from the ACO website. This service is free of charge.
If you encounter an organisation who does not accept the ACO and/or insists on a physical CTC copy of the Court Order, please write to us at https://go.gov.sg/writetosgcourts.
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: Why should a person go to the ACO portal if they already have a soft/digital copy of a court order?
questions.text:
Retrieving the court order from the ACO portal can provide added confidence that the Court Order can be obtained from the official court repository. The person retrieving the Court Order can also visually the compare the contents of the document to assure himself that the contents have not been authored by unauthorised persons.
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: If the court order I receive after 2 Jan 2020 does not have a QR Code and access code, does it mean that it is a forgery?
questions.text:
It is possible that the court order in question has not been included in the ACO system. It may still be a genuine court order. You may wish to check with the courts about the matter, or ask for a certified true copy in such a case.
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: Can I still require parties to produce a certified true copy, even if their court order is an Authentic Court Order?
questions.text:
Yes, but you should be aware that a certified true copy is less secure than an ACO. It is possible for certified true copies to be forged. When an ACO is available, it can be a better guarantee of authenticity, as you can be sure you are obtaining it directly from the court and that it has not been tampered with.
For more information on ACO, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/e-platforms/authentic-court-orders-(aco).

questions.title: How do I search for hearing details?
questions.text:
To search for information pertaining to a specific hearing, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/hearing-list.
By default, you will see only cases scheduled for today and tomorrow. You can change this using the Date selector. Note that Hearings schedules are subject to change at the court’s direction.

questions.title: Can I use generative AI like ChatGPT to prepare my court documents for me?
questions.text:
The Singapore Courts have issued the "Guide on the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools by Court Users" (the "Guide"), which applies from 1 October 2024, to all matters in the Supreme Court, the State Courts (including the Small Claims Tribunals, the Employment Claims Tribunals and the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals) and the Family Justice Courts.
Generally, the Court does not prohibit the use of Generative AI tools to prepare Court Documents, provided that the Guide is complied with.
The Guide does not change a Court User’s duty to continue to comply with the relevant legislation, rules, codes of conduct and Practice Directions.
(a) Where the Court User is a lawyer, the lawyer’s duty to comply with the rules of professional conduct remains. Lawyers continue to have a professional obligation to ensure that materials they put before the Courts are independently verified, accurate, true, and appropriate.
(b) Where the Court User is a Self-Represented Person, he or she is also responsible for ensuring that all information provided to the Court is independently verified, accurate, true, and appropriate.
The Court maintains a neutral stance on the use of Generative AI tools. It is important to emphasise that Generative AI is a tool, and any output generated should only be used on the basis that the Court User assumes full responsibility for the output. Unless specifically asked for by the Court, pre-emptive declaration of the use of Generative AI is not required, as the responsibility for any resulting content ultimately rests with the Court User.
Please refer to the full Guide for more details and additional elaboration.

questions.title: I am not sure about the language or words to use when drafting Court Orders for matters in the Family Justice Courts. Where can I get some guidance or assistance?
questions.text:
The Family Orders Guide (FOG), initiated by the Family Justice Courts, seeks to provide guidance to Court users on the language of commonly used orders. The FOG is not intended as, nor should it replace, legal advice. The FOG user should ensure that the legal effect(s) of the order(s) that he/she chooses to adopt is well understood. In the event that there are questions or concerns, legal advice should be sought.
Currently, the Family Orders Guide has suggested draft orders for matters relating to:
Divorce -
Maintenance Orders
Division of Matrimonial Assets Orders
Child-Related Orders
Procedural Orders
Probate Orders
Mental Capacity Act Orders
Adoption Orders
The Family Orders Guide (2024 Edition) can be downloaded here.

questions.title: What can or cannot be reported about Court cases? Where can I find further information about this?
questions.text:
If you are a member of the media, refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/news-and-resources/media-guide to understand the court processes and how you can report accurately on court matters.
The guide includes information on:
Key pointers for court reporting.
The life cycle of court proceedings.
The types of hearings in the courts.
How to behave in court.
How to inspect court documents (for the media).

questions.title: Can my employer update my employment details with the Board on my behalf?
questions.text: No. You must submit an Update Particulars application through the Professional Registration System using your Singpass credentials to update your employment details.

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of questions I can add to each form?
questions.text:
The limit for the number of items you can add is 100 items.
The 100-item limit remains in place to ensure platform stability and prevent performance issues. A survey that has more than 100-item would also increases the chance of survey fatigue which would decrease the reliability of your survey.
A possible work-around is to have 2 forms, and link them together at the end of Part 1 of the form, clearly labelling both (e.g. “Part 1 of 2”, “Part 2 of 2”) to help ensure smooth completion.

questions.title: Can collaborators from my school make changes to the form?
questions.text: Collaborators from your school with "Editor" rights will be able to edit the form.

questions.title: Can I pay my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium by instalments?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums cannot be paid by instalments. The premium is structured to be paid in full at the beginning of each policy year so that the scheme remains viable and the premiums kept affordable for all insured members.
You can find out more on the available payment options.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I request an extension for my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium payment if I am facing financial difficulties?
questions.text: If you are unable to pay the outstanding Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium within the given two months grace period due to financial difficulties and need more time for payment, you may request to extend the HPS premium payment deadline online. Your request is subject to approval.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the differences between topping up my retirement savings, making a Voluntary Housing Refund, topping up my MediSave Account and topping up my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
Find out the differences between the various types of top-ups in the table below:
Topping up your retirement savings
Voluntary Housing Refund
Topping up your MediSave Account
Topping up your 3 CPF accounts
Top up/refund to
Special Account (SA) for members below 55; or
Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above.
Ordinary Account (OA); and/or
RA for members 55 or above and have not met their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in their RA.
MediSave Account (MA)
Ordinary Account (OA)
Special Account (SA) for members below 55 or Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above
MediSave Account (MA)
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
Eligibility for tax relief
You can enjoy tax relief if you made cash top-ups to yourself or your loved ones up to the current year's FRS.
However, please note that tax relief would not apply if you made a CPF transfer.
You will not be eligible for tax relief.
For non self-employed persons:
You get to enjoy tax relief for voluntary top-ups to MA.
If you are self-employed, you will enjoy tax relief on your MediSave contributions based on your annual net trade income (NTI). There will be no tax relief for your MediSave contributions if your assessed NTI for the year of assessment is zero or negative.
For non self-employed persons:
You are not eligible for tax relief
For self-employed persons who made self top-up or received a top-up:
You can enjoy tax relief based on your assessable net trade income for the year.
Top-up limit
What is the maximum amount of top-ups I can receive?
If you are below 55, you may top up your SA up to the current year's FRS.
If you are 55 or above, you may top up your RA up to the current year's Enhanced Retirement Sum.
You can check your top-up limit in your Retirement Dashboard.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
You can make a refund of any amount, capped at the full principal amount you have withdrawn for the property, along with the accrued interest.
You may check the amount that you can refund through the Home Ownership Dashboard.
Do note that after making a full voluntary housing refund of the CPF savings withdrawn and accrued interest, all CPF withdrawals including monthly housing loan instalments (if any) for the property will stop.
What is the voluntary top-up limit to my MediSave Account?
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up to your MA is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MA balance. Once your BHS has been reached, no further voluntary top-ups can be made to your MA. If you exceed your BHS from the top-up, the full amount of your top-up will be refunded to you.
You can check your top-up limit with these steps.
Top-ups cannot exceed the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740, which includes your mandatory CPF contributions for the calendar year.
When you make a cash top-up online, you will be shown the amount of top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
If you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.
Top-ups in excess of the recipient’s Annual Limit will be refunded.
Withdrawal
Top-ups are meant to boost your retirement income. They will be streamed out to you as monthly payouts and cannot be used for other purposes.
You can continue to use your OA savings for the current or next property after making a voluntary housing refund.
However, if you would like to use your OA for the same property, after making a voluntary refund of the full principal amount used and the accrued interest, you will need to re-apply to use your CPF savings.
After turning 55 and setting aside the FRS, you can withdraw the remaining balance in your OA in full or in part at any time.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn as cash.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
Top-ups to your SA and RA are meant to boost your retirement income while MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn in cash.
Application
Top-ups can be made using cash and/or CPF transfers.
How do I apply to make a top-up?
Refund can only be made via cash.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
Top-ups can only be made via cash.
How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones’ MediSave Account?
Top-ups can only be made via cash.
How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones' 3 CPF accounts?
Click this link to find out what the CPF interest rates are.

Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme
