questions.text: You may submit a photo of your PIN mailer via this form for our verification.

questions.title: Will my spouse lose their existing Work Permit if I change from an Employment Pass to an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass?
questions.text:
Yes. Your spouse's existing Work Permit will no longer be valid as it is tied to their Dependant’s Pass (DP). Once your Employment Pass (EP) is cancelled, the associated family passes will also be cancelled.
To avoid this, you should only cancel your EP after your application for an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass is successful.
You will need to reapply for a DP for your spouse once your Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass is approved as it takes 4 weeks to process. Your spouse should make the necessary arrangements for his/her work for this transition.
topics: Work passes and permits / Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass

questions.title: How do I convert an Employment Pass or S Pass holder to a Work Permit?
questions.text:
You may consider converting your EP or S Pass holders to Work Permit holders if they no longer meet the prevailing EP or S Pass criteria.
However you must ensure that the following requirements are met:
Quota requirements
Eligibility requirements
Employers can submit a Work Permit application for them on myMOM Portal.
You do not need to cancel the existing pass before applying for a Work Permit. If the application is approved, you need to ensure that:
The EP or S Pass is cancelled before getting the Work Permit issued (within the same day).
The worker has valid stay throughout.
Family members of Work Permit holders are not eligible for Dependant's Passes. Those with dependants should make the necessary arrangements before converting to a Work Permit.
topics: Work passes and permits / S Pass

questions.title: Can a work pass holder work in multiple jobs?
questions.text:
All work pass holders must only work for their designated employer. They must not take on additional jobs or engage in activities to earn additional income in Singapore.
This also applies to training pass holders doing on-the-job training.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: If the salary is paid by an overseas employer, will the foreign employee be taxed in Singapore?
questions.text:
Generally, salaries paid for services rendered on behalf of an overseas employer are taxable in Singapore even if the salaries are not paid in Singapore.
A Letter of Guarantee is required by Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for foreigner who is employed by overseas employer. Please visit IRAS website to find out more about working for an overseas employer.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: Why are platform workers not counted towards my Work Permit and S Pass quota?
questions.text:
Only Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents who are employed under a contract of service and are paid at least the Local Qualifying Salary will count towards your foreign worker quota.
Platform workers are not employees under a contract of service and are therefore not counted towards your foreign worker quota.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: How do I know if I am engaged under a contract of service or contract for service?
questions.text:
Whether you are an employee hired under a contract of service or a self-employed person (SEP) under a contract for service depends on the actual relationship between you and the company.
Employers hire employees under a contract of service, entitling them to benefits such as sick and annual leave as well as CPF contributions.
If you work as an SEP, there is no employer-employee relationship under such an arrangement. You would not be covered under the Employment Act and the Work Injury Compensation Act, and the company does not need to make CPF contributions to you.
Examples of SEPs include:
Healthcare providers on platforms like Homage
Freelancers and Independent contractors
Sole proprietors
You can also use our self-assessment tool to assess your employment status.

questions.title: Can I download or print the results from the KETs verification tool?
questions.text: You can save the results by selecting the “Save as PDF” option under Print.

questions.title: How do I request a new address sticker for my IC?
questions.text: You may submit your address sticker request via our enquiry form. Please attach photo(s) of your current sticker and state the reason for replacement in your request for ICA's consideration.

questions.title: Can I apply to be a Singapore permanent resident (PR) if I hold an Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass?
questions.text: Yes, you are eligible to apply for Singapore PR. You can apply through the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) website.

questions.text:

Latest 3-month average number of local employees earning the local qualifying salary (LQS).

questions.title: Can I extend the validity of my MDW’s Temporary Work Permit (Notification letter)?
questions.text:
Yes, you can request to extend the validity of her Temporary Work Permit (Notification letter).
We will email you the outcome within 1 week.

questions.title: What should I do if I do not trust the doctors appointed by my employer?
questions.text: If you have a valid concern, you should lodge a case with MOM or raise this issue to the case officer who is assisting with your claims.

questions.title: I purchased an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for my employee. Can they downgrade to MediShield Life again?
questions.text: Yes, employees can choose to downgrade from their IP to MediShield Life at any time. Their MediShield cover will not be subject to further underwriting.

questions.title: My employee is currently covered under MediShield Life. What will happen to their MediShield Life cover if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for them?
questions.text: All Integrated Shield Plans (IP) have a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance component. Hence, your employee’s MediShield Life cover will continue when you buy them an IP. In addition, they will not have exclusions for their MediShield Life cover, even if there are exclusions for the additional private insurance component of their IP.

questions.title: What happens to the additional MediSave contribution if my employee has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted yearly to ensure Singaporeans have sufficient savings to meet their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age.
Any MediSave contributions in excess of the BHS will be transferred from the MediSave Account to the other CPF accounts to help with retirement expenses.

questions.title: Is salary during an employee's notice period subject to CPF deductions?
questions.text:
Yes, Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions must be made by both employer and employee if:
The employee is working during the notice period.
The employee hasn't yet joined their new company.

questions.title: My employer hasn't paid my salary, or has made an unauthorised deduction. What can I do?
questions.text:
You should make a claim as early as possible as this will give you a higher chance of recovering the salary owed to you.
To be eligible to file a claim, you need to:
Be covered by the Employment Act.
File the claim within 1 year of the non-payment.

questions.title: If my employee has acute respiratory infection (ARI) symptoms but hasn't seen a doctor, how should I handle their absence?
questions.text:
Employees should see a doctor if they:
Are medically vulnerable (such as seniors and those with chronic medical conditions) and have ARI symptoms
Have severe, prolonged or worsening ARI symptoms
Under the Employment Act, eligible employees will be entitled to paid sick leave when they are certified unfit for work by a doctor.
As part of your talent attraction and retention strategies, you may grant paid sick leave for employees with mild acute respiratory infection (ARI) symptoms without requiring a medical certificate (MC).
In such instances, employees should maintain open communication with you and use such concessions mindfully, while ensuring that the company’s business needs are fulfilled.
If there are disputes over the period of absence, you may require your employees to produce an MC so that they can be granted paid sick leave according to the Employment Act.

questions.title: What information do I need to prepare before making an incident report to MOM?
questions.text:
The following information are required when reporting an incident to MOM:
Informant's personal particulars and organisation details, where applicable.
Accident details, e.g. when, where and how did the incident happen.
Occupational disease details.
Injured person's details, e.g. personal particulars, employment, nature of injury, insurance policy details and other pre-existing accident condition information.
topics: Workplace safety and health / WSH incident reporting

questions.title: I have outstanding MediSave payable but I am unable to contribute the full amount. Can I make a partial contribution using the Manage your MediSave Payable form (MMSP)?
questions.text: You can make contributions of any amount using the Manage your MediSave Payable (MMSP) form, if you are contributing to your MediSave monthly via an instalment plan. This enables you to shorten your instalment duration and fulfil your MediSave payable sooner by making additional contributions as and when you wish to.

questions.title: What are Special Assistance Lanes (SAL) and who can use them?
questions.text:
Special Assistance Lanes (SAL) are automated clearance lanes which are wider and designed to clear up to 4 persons at a time.
Travellers using wheelchairs as well as those travelling as a family, including with the elderly or young children or who require special assistance, are eligible to use the SAL.

questions.title: How will the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) and GRIT@Gov Programmes help fresh graduates? What are the expected outcomes of GRIT?
questions.text:
GRIT and GRIT@Gov are initiatives by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and Public Service Division (PSD) respectively that offers fresh graduates with traineeship opportunities for a period of 6 months across various sectors.
The programme supports structured traineeships for trainees to gain hands-on industry-relevant experience and skills, preparing them for successful transition into full-time employment.

questions.title: How will I receive my monthly payouts if my combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are less than the minimum sum of $350?
questions.text: You will receive monthly payouts as long as you have at least $350 in your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings. If your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: What happens if my Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted and I receive new inflows in my RA and OA?
questions.text: If you are not on CPF LIFE, your monthly payouts will stop when your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted. When you receive any new inflows in your RA or OA, your monthly payouts will automatically resume from the following month. However, if your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your account balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: Will there be changes to the technical format when IRAS makes changes to the Form IR8A and/ or appendices?
questions.text: Tax changes and new government initiatives may result in changes to the technical format/ specifications. We will publish the changes on our website by Sep each year and inform all AIS payroll software vendors via email.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Technical file format/specifications

questions.title: There are differences between the hardcopy forms and the requirements stated in the technical format/ specifications. Which template should I follow to customise the printouts from my software?
questions.text:
AIS employers do not need to issue Form IR8A and/ or appendices to their employees. However, if an electronic copy of the form(s) is requested or required by AIS employers, i.e. the payroll software users, the payroll software may cater for this feature by mirroring the fields in the official copy of the income tax forms (https://go.gov.sg/iras-formir8a) to customise the printouts. The payroll software should be able to capture the input for these fields based on the format specifications and generate the printout accordingly.
For clients who are in the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS), the following statement must be displayed at the top header of the form(s):
“This statement can only be issued by an employer in the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) and is for your retention. The information in this statement will be automatically included in your income tax return, so you need not declare them in your tax form. You can check if your employer is in the AIS at IRAS website, https://go.gov.sg/iras-ais-search.”
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Technical file format/specifications

questions.title: How do I check the eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for myself or my loved ones?
questions.text:
For self:
You can check your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) via these ways:
1. By checking your personalised Retirement Dashboard, under the “Matching grant for cash top-ups” section.
Please refer to the following illustration.
2. When you are making your cash top-up, the online application form will display information on your eligibility.
For loved ones:
When you are making a cash top-up for your loved one aged 55 and above, the online application form will display information on their MRSS eligibility and the estimated matching grant that your loved ones may receive on your intended cash top-up. questions.title: Why is there a need to double CareShield Life payout growth rate?
questions.text: CareShield Life works alongside other Government subsidies and grants to support long-term care costs. With rising long-term care costs, the enhancements in the payout growth rate are necessary to ensure that CareShield Life continues to meaningfully support the varied care needs of those with severe disability.

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life payout if I have been receiving payouts prior to 1 January 2026?
questions.text: Existing CareShield Life claimants will not be affected by the enhanced CareShield Life benefits and increased premiums, and will continue to receive their existing CareShield Life payouts for the duration of severe disability.

questions.title: Why does the CareShield Life claim threshold remain at severe disability?
questions.text:
Expanding CareShield Life coverage to those with milder forms of disability would require premiums to at least double, due to the longer claim duration and higher claim incidences for these individuals. As this would have come at the expense of premium affordability for more policyholders, the CareShield Life Council has recommended not to vary the scheme’s scope of coverage.
Importantly, the CareShield Life Council notes that those with mild or moderate disability can continue to access Government subsidies and grants that have been designed with them in mind. These include long-term care subsidies and grants such as Home Caregiving Grant that the Government will enhance progressively from 2026.
Those who wish for additional insurance coverage can also consider Supplements offered by private insurers.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life premiums be after the premium changes take place, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
With the CareShield Life premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
CareShield Life premiums will continue to be fully payable via MediSave, which will minimise out-of-pocket payments for policyholders.
Lower- and middle-income policyholders will have smaller CareShield Life premium increases, as they will receive means-tested premium subsidies.
Individuals may check their personalised premiums through the CareShield Life premium checker from November 2025 onwards.

questions.title: How is the Government Transitional support different from the CareShield Life premium subsidy?
questions.text: Unlike CareShield Life premium subsidies, which are means-tested and targeted at the lower- and middle-income policyholders, all policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums will benefit from the transitional support to help manage the premium increases from the CareShield Life 2025 Review.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Government provides means-tested premium subsidies targeted at the lower- and middle-income individuals.
Policyholders’ loved ones may also help with premium payment for policyholders through their MediSave or by topping up to the MediSave accounts of their loved ones.
For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How will my CareShield Life Supplement premiums be affected by the CareShield Life changes?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are offered by private insurers, and CareShield Life Supplement premiums are independent of CareShield Life.
Most Supplement benefits also stack independently on top of CareShield Life benefits, and would not be affected.
Supplement policyholders may wish to contact their insurers to enquire about any potential changes or impact to their Supplement policies.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming CareShield Life enhancement?
questions.text:
Maintaining the enhancement as a standard feature for all policyholders helps keep the scheme fair and sustainable, and premiums affordable. This helps to:
Reduce adverse selection risk, where those who are more likely to claim are more likely to opt into the scheme.
Keep administrative processes simple and efficient.
Hence, the CareShield Life Council has recommended to apply the enhancements to all policyholders, striking a fair balance between stronger protection and premium affordability for all.

questions.title: Why is the enrolment criterion being reinstated for CareShield Life application?
questions.text:
When CareShield Life was launched, older Singaporeans with less severe disability were allowed to join as a time-limited concession, so that more seniors could enrol in and benefit from CareShield Life.
However, this also meant that premiums for all older Singaporeans had to be priced higher, to account for the possibility that those with milder forms of disability were more likely to join the scheme.
This concession period lasted 4 years, over twice as long as what MOH had announced when the concession was rolled out. In this time, application rates have also decreased over time.
Thus, the CareShield Life Council views that this is an appropriate juncture to reinstate the underwriting criteria, which will moderate the extent of premium increases for all older policyholders, keeping the scheme fair and sustainable.

questions.title: Who can still enroll in CareShield Life after 1 January 2026?
questions.text:
After 1 January 2026, individuals born in 1979 or earlier can still enrol into CareShield Life if they do not have any pre-existing disabilities.
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will continue to be automatically enrolled when they turn age 30.

questions.text: On 27 August 2025, Ministry of Health announced the changes related to the CareShield Life 2025 Review. You can read more about the changes by clicking on this link.

questions.title: When will the enhancements to CareShield Life take effect?

The revised payouts and premiums under the CareShield Life 2025 Review will take effect from 1 January 2026.
Changes to other aspects of the scheme such as improvements in scheme administration will take place progressively.

questions.title: I have registered my 15-year-old child's IC online. Why is the application status still pending?
questions.text:
After your 15-year-old child has registered for IC online, your child must complete the biometrics enrolment before we can process and produce the IC. The application status will remain pending until this step is completed.
If your child attends a government/ government-aided school, biometrics enrolment will be arranged by and done at his/ her school on a designated day.
If your child does not attend a government/ government-aided school or has missed the biometrics enrolment at his/ her school, please make an appointment for biometrics enrolment on behalf of your child via ICA e-Service after your child has registered for IC online.
If your child is currently overseas, you may make an appointment on behalf of your child for biometrics enrolment via ICA e-Service upon their return to Singapore.
If your child has passed his/ her 16th birthday, he/ she is required to walk-in for biometrics enrolment at ICA Services Centre after he/ she has registered for IC online. Please expect a waiting time of at least 2 hours.

questions.title: How do I stop monthly deductions from my CPF for my housing loan?
questions.text:
You can stop your housing monthly deduction through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Apply or Change CPF Payment for Housing Loan or Upgrading Cost
Processing Time: three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB.
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB.
If you have a bank loan
Online Application
Visit CPFB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: Select your property > Select Cease Monthly Instalment
Processing Time: generally within three working days.
In-person at CPF Service Centre
Make an appointment at any CPF Service Centre to submit your request.
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches and CPF Service Centres require prior appointments.
If you have fully redeemed your housing loan
Once HDB or your financier informs us that your housing loan has been fully redeemed, we will automatically stop your monthly deductions. There is no need to submit a request to stop the deductions.
You can confirm that the deduction has stopped by checking your Home Ownership Dashboard under “Monthly CPF deduction” section. If your housing loan has been fully redeemed this month, your monthly CPF deduction status on the dashboard will be updated next month.

questions.title: I am paying the premium for my family member's CareShield Life policy. How can I find out more information about their policy?
questions.text: If you are paying for your family members' CareShield Life premiums, you can log in to Healthcare dashboard 'CareShield Life/ElderShield' section for information on your and/or your dependants' CareShield Life premiums and subsidies.

questions.title: Won't natural immunity be better than getting vaccinated?
questions.text:
Our immune system produces immunity following vaccination, similar to how it would after a "natural" infection.
The difference is that you do not get sick first when you get the vaccination. Vaccines help strengthen your immune system and protect you from potentially life-threatening complications.
Hence, it is highly recommended that you and your loved ones get vaccinated according to the national immunisation schedules.

questions.title: What are the recommendations for pneumococcal vaccines for adults?
questions.text:
Under the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS), persons who are recommended to be vaccinated can either receive (i) PCV20, or (ii) PCV13 and/or PPSV23.
Persons aged 65 or above who have not received any pneumococcal vaccine can either receive:
One dose of PCV20 (regardless of age or conditions); or
One dose each of PCV13 (regardless of age) and PPSV23; PCV13 should be given first, followed by PPSV23 a year later (or at least after a minimum interval of 8 weeks) for better protection.
Persons aged 65 or above who have received PCV13 and/or PPSV23 but have not completed the recommended vaccination series can either receive:
One dose of PCV20 to complete the vaccination series; or
Complete the vaccination series using PCV13 and/or PPSV23.
If you have previously received PPSV23 before age 65 years, you are recommended to get another dose of PPSV23, at least one year after the most recent PCV13 and at least 5 years from the previous dose of PPSV23.
If you have already received PCV13 as an adult (regardless of age) and one dose of PPSV23 on or after 65 years of age, there is no further need for either of the pneumococcal vaccination.
For persons aged 18 to 64 years who are recommended for vaccination, please consult your doctor for more details on the type of pneumococcal vaccine and number of doses recommended.
Individuals should consult their doctor for vaccination advice specific to their age and medical conditions.

questions.title: What does the Varicella vaccine do?
questions.text:
The Varicella vaccine helps prevent chickenpox, a highly infectious disease caused by the Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV).
Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through direct contact, respiratory droplets, or contaminated items. It causes an itchy rash across the body (except palms and soles), fever, fatigue, loss of appetite and headache. While typically lasting a week, it can also lead to serious complications including skin, lung, blood, bone and joint infections, as well as inflammation of blood vessels and neurological tissues such as brain and spinal cord coverings.

questions.title: How many varicella vaccine doses are required, and what are the intervals?
questions.text: Two doses are recommended, given 4 to 8 weeks apart.

There are no penalties for missing an appointment, but please inform the clinic in advance if you need to cancel or reschedule.
If you have deleted the previous appointment's confirmation SMS, you can reach out here - https://go.gov.sg/has-support to share your details so we can provide better help.

questions.title: What is the difference between a maintenance enforcement application and a maintenance order?
questions.text:
A maintenance order refers to an order for the provision of support (financial in nature) for wives, children, incapacitated husbands or parents.
A maintenance enforcement application refers to an application to enforce an existing maintenance order if the respondent does not comply with it.

questions.title: With scams on the rise, how will be parties verify that the persons writing to the parties are duly authorised Maintenance Enforcement Officers?
questions.text:
The name of each individual who has been appointed as Maintenance Enforcement Officer will be published on Maintenance Enforcement Division's website.
SMSes sent by Maintenance Enforcement Officers will be aligned with the Whole-of-Government approach in relation to SMS communications and will be sent under "gov.sg".
Emails sent by Maintenance Enforcement Officers will be from oneminlaw@mlaw.gov.sg.

questions.title: Do I need a lawyer in the maintenance enforcement process?
questions.text: A lawyer is not necessary to apply for the enforcement of a maintenance order. Parties may nevertheless engage a practising lawyer for the purposes of the enforcement application, if they wish to do so.

questions.title: What are the fees involved in the Maintenance Enforcement Process?
questions.text:
Applicants do not need to pay fees when making a maintenance enforcement application to the Family Justice Courts (FJC).
Respondents (the party against whom a maintenance enforcement application is made) will be charged a fee of $180 (inclusive of GST) for the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's services in the first phase of implementation. This fee will be charged after the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report is submitted to the Family Justice Courts.
If you have difficulty paying the fees, please contact the Maintenance Enforcement Officer through https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw, or call 1800-2255-529*.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones. For overseas numbers, please call +65 6225 5529.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Applying for Enforcement

questions.title: What will happen if the Respondent does not attend the conciliation session?
questions.text:
Parties should inform the Maintenance Enforcement Officer if the scheduled date and time for the first conciliation session is not suitable.
If the Respondent does not attend the conciliation session, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will reschedule the conciliation session for both parties.
If the Respondent is absent again without a valid reason, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will inform the Court. The Court may direct the Respondent to attend a second rescheduled conciliation session, failing which a Warrant of Arrest may be issued.

questions.title: What will happen if the Respondent says that he wants to vary the court order during the conciliation session?
questions.text:
Maintenance arrears between the date of the previous order(s) and the present remain payable in full.
A variation of maintenance order for future maintenance payments can be discussed during the conciliation session with the Maintenance Enforcement Officer.

questions.title: How long will it take for the Maintenance Enforcement Officer to conduct fact-finding and conciliation?
questions.text:
The first conciliation session will be scheduled by the court in about three weeks from the date of the Summons issued by the court. Each conciliation session is estimated to be in the duration of between one and one and a half hours.
If parties do not reach a settlement at the first conciliation session, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will conduct fact-finding with third-party agencies which may take up to a further three to four weeks. A second conciliation session, if necessary, will only be fixed after the Maintenance Enforcement Officer completes the necessary fact-finding with the third-party agencies.

questions.title: How is the conciliation session conducted?
questions.text: The conciliation session(s) are conducted virtually, or in-person at 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing) Singapore 069118.

questions.title: What can I do if my conciliation session is to be conducted virtually but I have no access to the Internet?
questions.text:
Please contact the Maintenance Enforcement Officer through https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw, or call 1800-2255-529* for assistance to attend the conciliation session via Zoom from a computer station located at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing) Singapore 069118.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones. For overseas numbers, please call +65 6225 5529.

questions.title: What if I do not understand English?
questions.text: Please answer "No" to the question "Will you be able to communicate in English in Court?" in the enforcement application form submitted through https://ifams.gov.sg. We will arrange for the conciliation to be conducted in your preferred language.

questions.title: What is contained in a Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report?
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: What am I supposed to do with the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report upon receiving it?
questions.text: If you did not reach an agreement with the other party, the court would consider the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report in determining what order(s) ought to be made on the maintenance enforcement application. Thus, you should read the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report and understand the information in the report before the hearing.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: Can I disclose the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Report to my friends or family members?
questions.text: No. It is an offence under section 91S of the Women's Charter to disclose the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report or any information in the report without the written consent of the other party.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: What can I do if I disagree with the facts reflected in the Maintenance Enforcement Officer's report?
questions.text:
Parties must substantiate any disagreement with supporting documents. Please contact the Maintenance Enforcement Officer through https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw, or call 1800-2255-529*.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones. For overseas numbers, please call +65 6225 5529.

questions.title: How can I submit my documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer?
questions.text:
The STREAM system enables you to submit documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer (MEO) assigned to your case.
Before you start
You will need:
For Applicant:
Calculations of outstanding maintenance
Bank statements
For Respondent:
Current calculation of unpaid maintenance amounts
Respondent's monthly expenses with supporting documents
Beneficiary's monthly expenses paid by respondent with supporting documents
Employment status and income details for last 6 months, including contracts and pay slips
Income tax information and assessment notices for last 3 years
Bank account details (local and overseas): balances, transactions during non-payment periods and 6 months before application, with statements
CPF account transactions for last 6 months
Investment details with statements from CDP and financial institutions
Property information (local and overseas), including property tax details
Motor vehicle details: make, model, purchase date, and COE expiry
Private company shareholdings and ACRA "People Profile" search results
Current debts with supporting documents
Active debt repayment schemes under insolvency laws
Bankruptcy status, including orders and monthly contribution requirements
Any other supporting documents for the above information
You need to log in with SingPass to use the STREAM system.
How to submit your documents
Step 1: Go to the STREAM portal Visit https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/stream/
Step 2: Log in using your SingPass
Step 3: Upload your documents by clicking 'Upload Documents', choose your files, ensure each file is under 5MB
Step 4: Click 'Submit'
What happens next
After you submit, MEO will share an Interim Report with you before the scheduled conciliation session.
Need help?
If you have problems submitting documents:
Call 1800-2255-529* (free from Singapore landlines)
For mobile or overseas calls, dial +65 6225 5529 (charges may apply)
Office hours: 8:30am to 5:00pm
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones. For overseas numbers, please call +65 6225 5529.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: What will happen if the Respondent refuses to submit documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer?
questions.text: If the Respondent refuses to submit documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will exercise powers to conduct fact-finding to obtain information about the Respondent's financial circumstances. The Maintenance Enforcement Officer will also update the Court that the Respondent failed to submit documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer. Thereafter, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will prepare a report with the information obtained from the third party agencies, and submit it to the court.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: What happens if the Respondent is in the Debt Repayment Scheme or an undischarged bankrupt?
questions.text: The Respondent will be directed by the Family Justice Courts to provide a copy of his Debt Repayment Plan if he is on the Debt Repayment Scheme or his Notice of Determination of Monthly Contribution if he is an undischarged bankrupt. If the Respondent does not submit these documents to the Maintenance Enforcement Officer, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer will conduct fact-finding to obtain the information from the Official Assignee.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Maintenance Enforcement Officer's Reports

questions.title: What if I require financial assistance, whilst awaiting the outcome of the Maintenance Enforcement Process?
questions.text: The Maintenance Enforcement Officer can refer suitable parties for financial assistance. Please notify the Maintenance Enforcement Officer that you require financial assistance, at any time during the Maintenance Enforcement Process.
topics: Maintenance Enforcement Division / Referrals to Assistance

questions.title: What if the Respondent refuses to pay despite conciliation?
questions.text:
If the Court finds that the Respondent has not paid maintenance without good reason, the Court will make an order specifying the amount of maintenance arrears to be enforced against the Respondent, and how the Respondent is to pay the arrears.
In contested cases, the Court will also make a Show Payment Order. The Show Payment Order requires the Respondent to show proof of payment to the Court for a specified period of time. Unless special circumstances exist, the Order will also state that the Respondent is liable to imprisonment if he or she fails to show proof of payment.
If the Respondent fails to show proof of payment, the Respondent will be imprisoned unless the Respondent can show good reason for failing to do so.

questions.title: What can I do if the Respondent intends to dispose his properties in order to avoid paying maintenance?
questions.text: Pursuant to section 139M(1)(b) of the Women's Charter 1961, the court has the power on application to grant an injunction preventing any disposition of property by a person (A) - if the court is satisfied that A is disposing the property to reduce A's means to pay maintenance or to deprive A's wife, former wife, incapacitated husband, incapacitated former husband or child, of any rights in relation to the property.

questions.title: What if the Respondent has been transferring away his properties in order to avoid paying maintenance?
questions.text: Pursuant to section 139M(1)(a) of the Women's Charter 1961, the court has the power on application to set aside any disposition of property by a person (A) - if the court is satisfied that the disposition of property has been made within the preceding 3 years immediately before the date of the making of the application, and that A has disposed the property to reduce A's means to pay maintenance or to deprive A's wife, former wife, incapacitated husband, incapacitated former husband or child, of any rights in relation to the property.

questions.title: What does the Community Mediation Centre (CMC) do?
questions.text:
The Community Mediation Centre (CMC), a centre under the Ministry of Law,
offers mediation service to residents in Singapore facing relational and
community disputes.
There is no cost for the service.

questions.title: What are the benefits of mediation?
questions.text:
Mediation at the CMC offers the following benefits:
Cost: It is free.
Privacy: Matters discussed during mediation and identity of the parties
are kept confidential.
Time: A mediation session takes about 2 to 4 hours. It is available on
Mondays to Fridays and on Saturday mornings.
Location: We offer in-person mediation at 21 locations islandwide.
Virtual mediation is an option for less complex disputes.

questions.text: Virtual mediation can be offered for less complex cases.

questions.title: What are the disputes that are suitable for mediation at the CMC?
questions.text:
Mediation at the CMC is a viable option for resolving disputes between neighbours, family members, friends, co-workers, landlords, tenants or other interpersonal relationships.
However, it is not suitable for contractual or commercial disputes.
For a more comprehensive list of the types of disputes that are appropriate for mediation at the CMC, please click here.

questions.title: Why is the CMC accepting a mediation application without carrying out any investigations?
questions.text:
The CMC does not carry out investigations. Our primary focus is on facilitating discussions between disputing parties.
Through mediation, we aim to help parties communicate effectively, explore solutions and reach mutually beneficial agreements.

questions.title: Can the CMC accept cases involving neighbour disputes in private condominium or landed property?
questions.text: We accept cases involving neighbour disputes both in public and private estates which include landed properties, condominiums and private apartments.

questions.title: Can the CMC mediate if I have a dispute with my main tenant or landlord?
questions.text:
We provide mediation service for non-contractual disputes between landlords and tenants and between co-tenants.
Do check with us on the specific eligibility criteria and procedures related to your dispute, before applying for mediation.

questions.title: Do I need evidence to lodge a case with the CMC?
questions.text: You do not have to produce any evidence before applying for mediation at the CMC.

questions.title: How many people can attend the mediation session?
questions.text:
Excluding family disputes, we allow up to two persons from each party, who are directly involved with the dispute, to attend the mediation session.
For a satellite mediation session, only one person from each party will attend the session.

questions.title: Can I get my family members/agent to attend the mediation session on my behalf?
questions.text:
If your family member or agent has been issued with a Power of Attorney to manage your affairs, you can authorise them to attend the session on your behalf.
For all other reasons, please contact us.
For Court-Directed Mediation, only parties named in the Order of Court will attend the mediation session.

questions.title: Can I get a lawyer to attend the mediation with me?
questions.text:
At the CMC, lawyers are not allowed to attend the mediation sessions with the parties.
If you require legal advice, it is advisable to seek it separately before the mediation session.

questions.title: What happens after I apply for mediation?
questions.text:
When an application for voluntary mediation is received at the CMC, the process is as follows:
Acknowledgment: You will receive an acknowledgment of your application.
Assessment: We will assess your case to determine its suitability for
mediation.
Invitation to the other party (Respondent): If your application is found
suitable for mediation at the CMC, we will invite the Respondent for
mediation and update you on the outcome of the respondent.
Scheduling: When both parties agree to attend mediation, we will schedule
a mediation session and inform you of the date, time and location.
Mediation Session: On the scheduled date, you and the Respondent will
meet with our mediator(s). The mediator(s) will facilitate a discussion
between both parties, in an attempt to foster greater understanding and
possibly an amicable resolution.
Outcome: Once an agreement is reached, our mediator(s) will document
the terms. You will have the opportunity to review the document before
signing it. You will also receive a copy of the signed agreement. If an
agreement cannot be reached, we will close the session respectfully.
You may choose to explore other options to address the dispute, which
may include seeking legal advice or proceeding to file an application with
the Courts.
Follow-up: If required, the CMC may offer follow-up mediation sessions.

questions.title: If the Respondent ignores or declines the CMC invitation, what are my other options? Can I bring the case up to the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal (CDRT)?
questions.text:
For voluntary mediation, we can only proceed to arrange a mediation session when both parties are willing to participate.
Non-neighbour Disputes
If the Respondent declines or fails to respond to a mediation invitation, you may choose to explore other options to address the dispute, which may include seeking legal advice or proceeding to file an application with the Courts.
Neighbour Disputes from Tampines (During Pilot)
If the Respondent declines or fails to respond to a mediation invitation, you can seek the assistance of the Community Relations Unit (CRU) by calling their hotline at 3300 3300, between 9am to 9pm on weekdays.
Neighbour Disputes from all other Towns (During Pilot)
If the Respondent declines or fails to respond, we will issue you with a Certificate of Waiver. You have the option to file a claim at the CDRT.

questions.title: What happens during mediation?
questions.text:
This is the CMC mediation process.
1. Registration: Arrive at least 20 minutes before the session. Our officer will receive you, verify the identities of the parties and make sure everything is in order before the start of the mediation session.
2. Opening Statement: Our mediator(s) will invite you into the mediation room where you and the other party will be seated. The mediator(s) will then begin with an opening statement which includes an explanation on the mediation process and some ground rules.
3. Joint Session: The Applicant will start with his/her sharing of the issues that have come for mediation. Then the Respondent will have an opportunity to respond. Our mediator(s) will help to summarise the key issues raised.
4. Private Session: If there are sensitive matters that require a private discussion, the mediator(s) may speak to each party separately. Matters revealed during a private session is kept confidential unless permission is given to reveal such information.
Our mediator(s) may alternate between joint and private sessions to explore different solutions with both parties.
5. Conclusion:
Settlement with an agreement
Once an agreement is reached, our mediator(s) will document the terms. You will have the opportunity to review the document before signing it. You will also receive a copy of the signed agreement.
No settlement
If an agreement cannot be reached, we will close the session respectfully. You may choose to explore other options to address the dispute, which may include seeking legal advice or proceeding to file an application with the Courts.

questions.title: Can I record the mediation session?
questions.text:
The mediation at the CMC is a confidential process, as outlined in the CMC Act, Cap 49A.
To maintain confidentiality and to provide a safe space for parties to share without fear, no photography, videography or audio recording is allowed during the mediation session.
Should we realise that a recording has taken place, the party responsible will be asked to delete the content, in the presence of the mediators or the CMC officer.

questions.title: Is a CMC Settlement Agreement legally binding?
questions.text: Once a Settlement Agreement is signed, it is binding on the parties who signed it, which means that you can use the document as evidence to support legal proceedings.

questions.title: What happens if the other party breaches the agreement?
questions.text:
You can apply for voluntary remediation one month after the last mediation session through our online application form. You can also apply by calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line at 1800 2255 529* during office hours
Non-neighbour Disputes
If remediation does not materialise, you may choose to explore other options to address the dispute, which may include seeking legal advice or proceeding to file an application with the Courts.
Neighbour Disputes from Tampines (During Pilot)
If voluntary remediation does not materialise because the Respondent declines or fails to respond, you can apply for Directed Remediation by calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line at 1800 2255 529* during office hours. This means attendance at a CMC mediation session is compulsory for both parties.
Neighbour Disputes from all other Towns (During Pilot)
IIf voluntary remediation does not materialise because the Respondent declines or fails to respond, we will issue you with an outcome letter. You have the option to file a claim at the CDRT.
*Please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones.

questions.title: Who are the CMC mediators?
questions.text:
The CMC mediators are volunteers who are appointed by the Minister for Law.
They have been carefully selected, trained and assessed before they are
appointed to their role. They are also required to remain relevant in their role through regular mediations and training.

questions.text:

questions.text:
The CMC recruits new volunteers every year, with applications closing at the end of September.
Only shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend the Selection Interviews, which are usually held from October to November each year.
There is a 5-stage process to qualify as a CMC mediator:
Application

Appointment

questions.title: What are the criteria to be a CMC mediator?
questions.text:
To apply as a volunteer CMC mediator, you will have to meet the following
criteria:
A Singapore Citizen or a Singapore Permanent Resident.
Aged 30 years or older.
Fluent in both written and spoken English.
Proficient in a local language or dialect.
Proficient in using the Zoom platform for conducting mediation.
Involved in community or voluntary work.
Have completed 5-day mediation training from a recognised training provider in Singapore.
Have an interest in contributing to building a gracious and harmonious community in Singapore.
You can apply here.

questions.title: What happens if I do not meet the financial means criteria but still cannot afford to pay for a private lawyer?
questions.text:
If you have certain reasons or information that you think makes your situation different or special, you may provide the necessary information and documents when submitting your application. For example, if you have a very serious illness and cannot afford legal services as you need to pay for major medical procedures etc.
Please also note that we will not accept any appeals for rejected applications.

questions.title: Can I apply on behalf of my relative/friend?
questions.text:
No. A person who is aged 21 and above and seeking criminal defence aid must apply by himself/herself.
If your relative/friend is in Prison or in remand, please inform them that they may only apply directly through Singapore Prisons Services.

questions.title: I have already submitted my application but how will I know if the Public Defender's Office is assessing my application?
questions.text:
We will contact you through the phone number or email address provided in your application form. Please ensure that you are available during the scheduled interview slots.
If you are in Prison or in remand, we will contact you via Singapore Prisons Services.

questions.title: I am under 21 years old. Can I apply for criminal defence aid with the Public Defender's Office?
questions.text:
Your parent or legal guardian will have to submit the application on your behalf, if you are under 21 years old.
If your parent or legal guardian is applying in-person at the MinLaw Service Centre or State Courts HELP Centre, it is recommended that you accompany your parent or legal guardian as you may be asked questions relating to your criminal proceedings. Alternatively, you may ask your parent or legal guardian to submit an online application.
If you do not have a parent or legal guardian, you will need to ask an appropriate adult to make the application on your behalf as a guardian. This adult should be someone you live with, such as an extended relative.

questions.title: What is per capita household income (PCHI)?
questions.text:
PCHI is calculated by dividing the total gross household income by the total number of household members.
"Gross income" refers to the gross wages or salaries before deduction of CPF contributions and personal income tax. It comprises basic wages, overtime pay, commissions, tips, other allowances, and bonuses. For self-employed persons, gross income refers to profits from their business, trade or profession (i.e., total receipts less business expenses incurred) before the deduction of income tax.
"Household members" refers to persons related by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption and have the same residential address reflected on the NRIC as the applicant.
For applications for criminal defence aid, we will examine the average PCHI over the last 12 months.
Example:
For a household of four with two working adults earning $3,000 and $2,800 monthly, and two non-earning children, the average PCHI would be calculated as follows:
Average Per Capita Monthly Household Income (PCHI) = [($3,000 x 12) + ($2,800 x 12)] / (4 x12) = $1,450

questions.title: What does the merits test interview entail?
questions.text:
The merits test assesses whether there are reasonable grounds for bringing or defending your case in Court. The assessment will consider:
whether you require legal representation to plead guilty;
whether there are reasonable grounds for defending your case in Court; or
whether there are merits to any criminal appeal or criminal application made or intended to be made by you; or to defend any criminal appeal or criminal application brought by the prosecution, as the case may be.
During the interview, you will be asked about the facts of your case, your intended defence (if any) and for supporting documents.

questions.title: I am eligible for criminal defence aid. Why was my case referred to Pro Bono SG?
questions.text:
The Public Defender's Office is co-delivering criminal defence aid with the Pro Bono SG and their volunteer lawyers.
All applications for criminal defence aid will be assessed by the Public Defender's Office. If your application is successful and your case is referred to Pro Bono SG, you will pay the contribution amount to them directly before a volunteer lawyer is assigned to your case.
You will not be able to choose or decide whether to be represented by a Public Defender or a volunteer lawyer from Pro Bono SG.

questions.title: Why must I pay a contribution amount before being granted aid?
questions.text:
To foster greater ownership over your legal case, you are required to make a small financial contribution to the Public Defender's Office.
The contribution amount is based on your financial eligibility, and will be made known to you when you are informed of the application outcome.
You will only be granted aid and assigned a Public Defender, after you pay the contribution amount.

questions.title: What happens if I am unable to pay the contribution amount?
questions.text:
Please call 1800-225-5529* if you cannot meet the payment deadline and need more time to pay.
You may also request for a waive or reduction of contribution amount. This request is however, assessed on a case-by-case basis.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800-225-5529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones.

questions.title: Can I discharge or request to change my lawyer after granted aid from the Public Defender's Office?
questions.text:
No. You will need to seek permission from the Chief Public Defender before doing so.
If you opt to discharge your assigned Public Defender on your free will, your case will not be re-assigned to another Public Defender.
In the event of a discharge, you may be required to reimburse the Public Defender's Office for the expenses incurred on your behalf.

questions.title: Does the Exclusion by Law under section 165A of the Casino Control Act 2006 apply to me if I have been receiving criminal defence aid under the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme ("CLAS") administered by Pro Bono SG ("PBSG")?
questions.text:
Yes. The Exclusion by Law applies if you are receiving Government-funded criminal defence aid under CLAS.
Foreigners receiving criminal defence aid from PBSG are, however, not subject to the Exclusion by Law.

questions.title: Does the Exclusion by Law under section 165A of the Casino Control Act 2006 continue to apply to me after my case has concluded in Court?
questions.text: Exclusion by Law will be revoked automatically within two (2) weeks after your case has concluded in Court and/or no longer receiving criminal defence aid from the Public Defender's Office or Pro Bono SG.

questions.title: What if I am receiving Government-funded criminal defence aid but need to enter casino(s) or jackpot machine room(s) for work¹? ¹This refers to the scope of "defined work" under Casino Control Act.
questions.text:
For casinos:
You will need to inform the National Council on Problem Gambling (NCPG) via go.gov.sg/ncpg-ebl, and provide a soft copy of your company's HR letter/email as supporting document. NCPG will review the request and you will receive a notification on the outcome via SMS or the NCPG e-Portal, within 5 working days from the application date.
