questions.title: What if I am receiving criminal defence aid and had bought an Annual Levy to enter the casinos in Singapore?
questions.text: You will not be allowed to enter the casinos even if you have paid the Annual levy. The Annual Levy will not be refundable.

questions.title: Is there an expiry date for an exemption granted by the Ministry of Law for admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
Applicants who have been exempted for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations are advised to take the necessary next steps (e.g. apply for admission to the Singapore Bar or take the Foreign Practitioner Examinations) as soon as possible, as applicable requirements may change over time.
Applicants are reminded that their exemption may be granted, subject to such conditions as the Minister may think fit to impose, which may include the requirement that applicants apply for admission to the Singapore within a specified time frame.

questions.title: Can I seek an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar in advance of commencing my law degree?
questions.text:
Before embarking on a law degree, you should check the relevant legislation and/or with the Singapore Institute of Legal Education to ascertain that it will be recognised for admission to the Singapore Bar.
If the degree is not a recognised degree, but you would nonetheless like to try to obtain an exemption for it, you should submit an application for exemption before accepting an offer from the university.
If you have already embarked on the course and realise that it is not recognised for admission to the Singapore Bar, you should submit an application for an exemption as soon as possible.
Each person's circumstances are unique, and each application is considered on its individual merits. We are therefore unable to advise you on your chances of obtaining an exemption. The onus is on the applicant to make a strong case for the exemption sought. Please note that exemptions are granted sparingly.

questions.title: How do I submit an application for an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
Applications for an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations must be submitted using the online Application for Exemption Form. We do not accept hardcopy applications.
The list of supporting documents required can be found within the online form and on our webpage: Supporting Documents for Applications for Exemption. Supporting documents must be submitted, in softcopy, via Contact Us @ OneMinLaw within 7 calendar days after the submission date of the online application.
Each person's circumstances are unique, and each application is considered on its individual merits. We are therefore unable to advise you on your chances of obtaining an exemption. The onus is on the applicant to make a strong case for the exemption sought. Please note that exemptions are granted sparingly.

questions.title: Where can I find information about the recommendations made by the Committee for Professional Training of Lawyers and the new admission framework?
questions.text:
For more information on the recommendations made by the Committee for the Professional Training of Lawyers, please refer to the report of the Committee for the Professional Training of Lawyers and the Ministry of Law's press release.
The new admission framework took effect from 17 July 2024 onwards. For more information on the requirements for admission to the Singapore Bar, the Part B Course and Examinations, and practice training requirements, please contact the Singapore Institute of Legal Education.

questions.title: How long does it take for an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar to be assessed or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examination to be assessed?
questions.text:
It can take 6-8 weeks for an application for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations to be processed, which will commence only after we have received all required supporting documents. Incomplete applications will take longer to process.
You can check the status of your application by logging in to our exemption e-Services with your email address and password.
Please note that the decision letter will be emailed to the applicant. We do not issue hardcopy letters.

questions.title: Am I eligible to apply for an exemption from Part B of the Singapore Bar Examinations and the practice training period?
questions.text:
You may submit an application to the Ministry of Law to be considered for an exemption from Part B of the Bar Examinations and the practice training period if you fulfil all the following requirements:
1. You obtained an approved law degree from an approved university and you fulfil all the other "qualified person" requirements;
2. You are admitted to practise in a common law jurisdiction; and
3. You have obtained at least 2 years of "relevant legal practice or work" and/or "relevant legal training" as defined in Rule 2 of the Legal Profession (Qualified Persons) Rules.
However, please note that exemptions from Part B and the practice training period are not granted automatically, even if you fulfil all the above requirements. All applications for exemption are considered case-by-case on their individual merits.
For more information on applying for an exemption, please refer to our webpage on Applications to the Minister for Law for Exemption (see 'Exemption from Part B and the Practice Training Period').
For more information on being a 'qualified person', approved universities and degrees, and relevant legal practice or training, please refer to the website of the Singapore Institute of Legal Education.

questions.title: Why was my application for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar unsuccessful?
questions.text:
Each application for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations is considered case-by-case on its individual merits.
We are unable to disclose the reasons why an application was successful or unsuccessful. Where an application has been unsuccessful, reapplication on the same facts is unlikely to produce a different outcome.
If you were not granted an exemption, you may wish to consider some alternatives for working in the legal field in Singapore.

questions.title: What are the supporting documents required for applications for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
The list of supporting documents required for applications for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations can be found within the online Application for Exemption Form and on our webpage: Supporting Documents for Applications for Exemption.
Applicants are required to submit all supporting documents, in softcopy, via Contact Us @ OneMinLaw. If we do not receive your supporting documents within 7 calendar days after the submission date of the online application, your application will be deemed to have lapsed and you will be required to submit a new application and pay the applicable administrative fees.

questions.title: Are Juris Doctor degrees from Australian universities recognised for admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
From 1 December 2017, Doctor of Jurisprudence (J.D.) degrees (also known as Juris Doctor degrees) conferred on or after 1 December 2017 by approved Australian universities will be recognised for admission to the Singapore Bar, provided all other admission requirements are met.
Individuals who were conferred J.D. degrees from approved Australian universities before 1 December 2017 may wish to apply to the Minister for Law for an exemption.
For more information about J.D. degrees, approved universities and the requirements for admission to the Singapore Bar, please refer to the Singapore Institute of Legal Education's website.

questions.title: What are the requirements for admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
Please refer to relevant legislation and the website of the Singapore Institute of Legal Education for information on the requirements for admission to the Singapore Bar, such as:
The 'qualified person' requirements
Nationality requirements - Approved universities and degrees (including queries about "converting" non-law degrees)
Omitted UK universities
Class of honours / ranking
Juris Doctor degrees
Dual and combined degrees
External courses -
Twinning programmes
Accelerated courses
Relevant legal training and/or work
Practice training period (training contract)
Part A and Part B of the Singapore Bar Examinations
Admission or call procedures.

questions.title: Can I appeal or re-apply if my application for an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar was unsuccessful?
questions.text:
Where your application for exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations was unsuccessful, re-applying on the same facts is unlikely to produce a different result.
You should consider re-applying only if there are new material facts or circumstances that demonstrate a stronger case for the particular exemption sought.
Please note that repeat applications must also be submitted using the online Application for Exemption Form.

questions.title: Will my law degree be recognised for admission to the Singapore Bar if I undertook remote/online learning due to the COVID-19 pandemic?
questions.text:
Please refer to the Singapore Institute of Legal Education's (SILE) guidance note on undertaking overseas law degree programmes remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic, which can be found on their website.
For more information, please contact the SILE at enquiries@sile.edu.sg.

questions.title: Where can I find details of the Foreign Practitioner Examinations (FPE)?
questions.text: For details of the Foreign Practitioner Examinations (FPE), please refer to the Singapore Institute of Legal Education's website.

questions.title: Do I need to re-submit all my documents if I re-apply for exemption admission to the Singapore Bar?
questions.text:
If you are re-applying for an exemption for admission to the Singapore Bar or in relation to the Foreign Practitioner Examinations, you will generally not be required to re-submit your supporting documents if your previous application was submitted within the last 12 months.
However, please submit via Contact Us @ OneMinLaw any new or updated documents that you wish to be taken into consideration for your re-application. If we do not receive your supporting documents within 7 calendar days after the submission date of the online application for exemption, your application will be deemed to have lapsed and you will be required to submit a new application and pay the applicable administrative fees.

questions.title: What are the ways to close a company?
questions.text:
There are several ways to close a company:
(a) Voluntary winding up
Members' Voluntary Winding Up - For solvent companies that can settle their debts.
Creditors' Voluntary Winding Up - For insolvent companies that cannot pay their debts.
Simplified Winding Up - Insolvent companies that meet a set of specific criteria can apply for this programme
(b) Court-ordered Winding Up - An application is made to the Court.
For more information on the different ways to close a company, please refer to ACRA's website.

questions.title: What does winding up of a company mean?
questions.text:
Winding up is a process in which the assets of a wound-up company are disposed of or realised to pay off its debts. Any surplus is distributed to its contributories or shareholders. After which, the company is dissolved and ceases to exist.
For more information, please refer here.

questions.title: Who is the Official Receiver?
questions.text:
The Official Receiver is a public official appointed by the government. His role includes:
(a) Overseeing the private liquidators, ensuring the administration is in compliant with legislation.
(b) Acting as liquidator in compulsory winding up cases and for unincorporated entities.
(c) Acting as a representative for companies that have been struck off or dissolved.
For more information, please click here.

questions.title: What type of winding up process is suitable for my company?
questions.text: We are unable to provide legal advice. You may wish to seek your own legal advice on this matter.

questions.title: How do I find out if a company is compulsorily wound up?
questions.text:
To find out whether a company is in compulsory winding up, please conduct an insolvency search via our website.
Alternatively, you may also check the status of the company at ACRA's website.

questions.title: What are the charges of liquidators in winding up a company?
questions.text: A private liquidators' fees can be approved by the creditors or through an application to the Court. You may consult the private liquidators directly for specific questions on fees.

questions.title: What are the charges of the Official Receiver?
questions.text:
The fees chargeable by the Official Receiver are stipulated in the Schedule under the Fees (Winding up and Dissolution of Companies and Other Bodies) Order 2005, including and not limited to the following:
(a) Administrative Fee
(b) Realisation Fee
(c) Distribution Fee
For further details of the full list of fees, please refer to the Fees (Winding up and Dissolution of Companies and Other Bodies) Order 2005 here.

questions.title: How do I apply for a company to be wound up compulsorily?
questions.text:
Compulsory winding up is where the Court makes an order for the winding up of a company.
The Court makes the winding up order on specific grounds. The reasons for the winding up of a company are broadly based on company‑initiated or constitutional grounds, failure to comply with statutory requirements, or the financial insolvency of the company wherein it cannot repay its debts etc.
The Official Receiver from the Insolvency Office under the Ministry of Law, oversees the compulsory winding up process in Singapore.
Who can apply for compulsory winding up?
Who
Applicant to prove
Company, Company directors and shareholders
Directors or shareholders who have paid for their shares in full, including the Official Assignee of a bankrupt who is a shareholder.
Company cannot continue operating
Creditor
Anyone the company owes money to, including suppliers, contractors, banks, or employees owed salaries.
Company owes them at least $15,000 and cannot pay
Government agency
Any government agency such as a Ministry or Statutory Board
Company is being used for an unlawful purpose, has carried on multi-level marketing or pyramid selling, etc
Court-appointed officer
Liquidator or judicial manager
To specify grounds as to why the company should be wound up
Note: As there are various grounds for winding up, consult a lawyer for advice on what applies and the supporting documents required in the given circumstances.
What comes first?
Obtain legal advice - This is a legal process. Consider consulting a corporate insolvency lawyer or a licensed insolvency practitioner for assistance and advice. They can:
Assess whether there are valid grounds for application
Advise on the evidence required
Determine if compulsory winding up is the right option for the situation as alternative options exist – The lawyer can explain other options like voluntary liquidation (the company chooses to close down on its own), judicial management (a court-appointed manager tries to save company) or scheme of arrangement (the company negotiates with its creditors).
Documents and fees in a winding up application:
1. The lawyer will prepare the following court papers:
(a) Originating Application (the main application form)
(b) Affidavit in Support of Application (sworn statement explaining why the company should be wound up)
(c) Consent to Act as Liquidator (agreement from insolvency practitioner who will administer the winding up of the company)
(d) Memorandum of Advertisement (notice to be published)
(e) Affidavit of Service (proof that documents were delivered to the company)
(f) List of Parties (individuals or entities involved in the case who intend to attend the winding up hearing)
(g) Registrar’s Memorandum (formal confirmation from the Court indicating that all required documents have been filed and are complete)
2. Supporting documents: The appointed lawyer will advise on documents or evidence required.
Costs involved
Winding up deposit of $10,400 to be paid to the Official Receiver
Court filing fees (Mandatory fees charged by the Court)
Professional fees (as agreed with the lawyer and/or insolvency practitioner)
How to apply
Step 1: Find a lawyer. The list of all Singapore solicitors with a current practising certificate from the Supreme Court of Singapore can be found at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/.
Step 2: Legal consultation. The lawyer will review the case, advise if the applicant has valid grounds, explain the process and costs, and prepare all required documents.
Step 3: File application. The lawyer will pay the $10,400 deposit to the Official Receiver via the MinLaw e-services eCollection Portal at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/ecoll/, file the application at the High Court, and pay court filing fees.
Step 4: Service of documents. The lawyer will deliver copies of the documents to the company and relevant parties in the winding up.
Step 5: Court hearing. The High Court sets a hearing date for the winding up application which the lawyers attend on the applicant’s behalf. The first hearing date is typically set within 3 weeks from the date of the application.
What happens at the winding up application Court hearing
The Registrar will review the application and consider any objections raised by the company before determining whether to grant the winding up order.
If approved:
The winding up order is made and a liquidator is appointed.
The liquidator sells the company’s assets, pays its creditors if there are funds for distribution, and brings the company to an orderly dissolution
If rejected:
The application is dismissed.
The applicant may have to pay the company’s legal costs.
The applicant can appeal the decision. Please discuss with the lawyer on the timeline for the appeal.
If adjourned:
The Court needs more information or time.
New hearing date will be set.
The lawyer will advise on the next steps.
What to do next
Obtain legal advice – This process should not be undertaken without legal representation, as the courts require compliance with formal procedures that can only be properly managed by qualified lawyers.
Find a lawyer. The list of all Singapore solicitors with a current practising certificate from the Supreme Court of Singapore can be found at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/.

questions.title: Is a deposit payable for all applications to wind up a company? How do I pay the deposit for a winding up application?
questions.text:
Yes, a deposit of $10,400 is required to be paid to the Official Receiver prior to the filing of an application with the Court.
Applicants can pay the deposit via MinLaw e-services eCollection Portal at this link. Applicants will receive a system-generated payment acknowledgement upon successful payment as proof of payment.

questions.title: How do I find out who is the liquidator?
questions.text:
To find out who is the liquidator for a company in a compulsory winding up, please conduct an insolvency search via our website.
For a company undergoing voluntary winding up, you may conduct a company profile search via ACRA's website.

questions.title: How long does it take to complete a winding up?
questions.text: The duration of the liquidation process varies and has no fixed duration, depending on the complexity of the company's affairs and the time taken to realise the company's assets.

questions.title: How can I claim for outstanding salaries due from a company in liquidation? How do I file a proof of debt against a wound-up company?
questions.text:
You may conduct a search to find out who is the appointed liquidator of the company.
Where the Official Receiver is the appointed liquidator of the wound-up company, you may file your proof of debt via our website here. A filing fee of $5 is payable for the online submission. Please click here for more information.
If insolvency practitioner(s) have been appointed as the liquidator(s) of the wound-up company, please contact them directly for the filing of the proof of debt form.

questions.title: Are shareholders or contributories of wound-up companies required to file their claims for return of contributories with the liquidator?
questions.text: No, shareholders or contributories need not file a proof of debt against the wound-up company to make a claim on their share capital. Where there are surplus funds after the liquidator pays all expenses of liquidation and dividends to creditors, the balance amount will be distributed to the shareholders according to the proportion of their contribution in the company's share capital.

questions.title: Who are the preferential creditors in the case of a corporate winding up scenario?
questions.text:
The preferential creditors in a company winding up include employees, CPF Board, and IRAS.
Please refer to the relevant Act here for more details.

questions.title: Do I include interest on my debt in the proof of debt form?
questions.text: You may include the interest in your proof of debt, but this is subject to adjudication for dividends from the assets of the wound-up company, if any.

questions.title: Will I receive payment for the debts owed by the company that has been wound up?
questions.text:
The debts of the company are prioritised according to the law and will be paid in the following sequence:
1. Costs associated with the winding up proceedings and liquidation expenses.
2. Debts owed to preferential creditors, such as employees, CPF Board, and IRAS.
3. Admitted claims of unsecured creditors.
4. Distribution to shareholders from the remaining assets, if any.

questions.title: What can creditors / shareholders do if they are not satisfied with the services provided by the private liquidator?
questions.text: The creditors / shareholders should seek their own legal advice to assess whether there are grounds to initiate an action to replace the liquidator. Alternatively, they may inform the Official Receiver the reasons why the services provided by the private liquidator have not been satisfactory.

questions.title: What are the obligations of directors and corporate secretary of a wound-up company?
questions.text:
When a company is being wound up, the directors and corporate secretaries have to assist the liquidator with his administration and investigations into the affairs of the company (if any). Their key responsibilities are as follows:
(a) Submit a Statement of Affairs, detailing the company's assets, liabilities, and financial status.
(b) Hand over all company's books, records, documents, and physical assets to the liquidator.
(c) Cease acting and transacting on behalf of the company, such as collecting money owed to the company, or paying out money to those the company owes.
(d) Refrain from using or disposing of any of the company's property or assets.

questions.title: If I need to submit the Statement of Affairs, where can I obtain it from?
questions.text: You may download a copy of the Statement of Affairs and the schedules here.

questions.title: If a company that is dissolved still owns a vehicle which is currently in use, what can I do?
questions.text:
When a company is dissolved or struck off, any outstanding assets, including vehicles, are vested in the Official Receiver. The Official Receiver then acts as a representative of these companies to administer their assets.
The handling of the vehicle may vary depending on the specific circumstances of the case. Please submit an enquiry form to the Official Receiver and attach a copy of the vehicle log card here before we could advise further.

questions.title: How can I lay claim to assets of a defunct company? How can I claim for tax refund of a company that had been dissolved?
questions.text:
You may lay claims on the assets (e.g. tax refund) of a defunct company as its shareholder or its creditor via our e-Services here.
Please click here for more information on laying claim to the assets belonging to a defunct company.

questions.title: Can directors be personally liable for company debts?
questions.text:
Directors may be held personally liable if:
(a) They have engaged in wrongful or fraudulent trading.
(b) They have breached fiduciary duties.

questions.title: What happens if the company cannot pay all its debts?
questions.text: Unpaid debts are written-off unless the directors are found personally liable for them.

questions.title: What is the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS") and when did it start?
questions.text:
The Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS") is a pre-bankruptcy scheme which is administered by the Official Assignee ("OA").
It seeks a win-win outcome for both the debtor and his creditor. Debtors with unsecured debts not exceeding $150,000 will be able to enter into a debt repayment plan ("DRP") under the DRS with their creditors and avoid bankruptcy, along with its restrictions and social stigma.
The proposed DRP must ensure that the interests of creditors are adequately safeguarded. These debtors will commit to the DRP and repay their debts over a fixed period of time of not more than 5 years. When the debtor meets his financial obligations under the DRS, he will be released from his debts provable under the scheme and have a fresh start thereafter.
The Scheme came into operation on 18 May 2009, and is applicable to bankruptcy applications made on or after 18 May 2009.

questions.title: How do I apply for the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text:
It is not possible to sign up or apply for the DRS as it is only initiated when a bankruptcy application is made against you in the High Court ("the Court"), either by yourself or your creditor.
The Court may then refer your case to the Official Assignee ("OA") if your total liabilities do not exceed $150,000, for an assessment of your eligibility and suitability for the DRS.
While the Court refers your case to the OA, there are other criteria that you must meet to determine your suitability for the DRS.
For more information on the DRS, see our Introduction to DRS video (English subtitles) (mlaw.gov.sg) and Information for Debtors (mlaw.gov.sg).

questions.title: How will a debtor be eligible and suitable for the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
What happens once a debtor is referred by the Court to the Official Assignee ("OA")?
questions.text:
When a debtor is referred by the Court to the OA, the hearing of the bankruptcy application will be adjourned for up to 6 months to enable the OA to assess the debtor's suitability for the DRS.
The debtor will receive a notice from the OA informing him to watch an Introductory Video on the DRS. He will then be required to submit the following forms and documents online:
a. Statement of Affairs ("SA")
b. Income & Expenditure Statement ("I & E")
c. Debt Repayment Plan ("DRP")
d. Supporting Documents ("SD")

questions.title: List of supporting documents for Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS") debtor to submit during the period of assessment?
questions.text: For the list of supporting documents for DRS debtor to submit during the period when the debtor is being assessed for the DRS ("period of assessment"), please refer to Annex B at Forms for Administration (mlaw.gov.sg).

questions.title: What is the duration within which the repayments under the Debt Repayment Plan ("DRP") must be completed?
questions.text: The maximum duration of a DRP is 5 years (60 months). In any given case, the length of a DRP may vary depending on the total debt size and the monthly instalment amount.

questions.title: Is there a minimum repayment amount?
questions.text:
There is no fixed minimum repayment amount. It is determined by taking into account the debtor's financial circumstances, his income and expenses.
Debtors will also need to contribute a portion of their nett bonuses if they receive.

questions.title: What makes a debtor unsuitable for the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text: The debtor is unsuitable for the DRS when he fails to comply with the Official Assignee ("OA")'s instructions. By not complying with the OA's instructions (e.g. failure to submit or complete the documents required of him or pay the required fees, or if his liabilities exceed $150,000 at any stage of the period of assessment), he will be deemed unsuitable for the DRS and his case will be referred back to Court for the bankruptcy application against him to be heard again. In such an event, the Court, the debtor and the applicant-creditor will be informed of his unsuitability for the DRS.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text:
Before the commencement of the DRS, the debtor can opt out of the DRS by declining to be assessed for the DRS. The case will then be referred back to High Court where the bankruptcy order will be made.
If the debtor opts out of the DRS after commencement of the DRS, it will be considered as a failure from the scheme and he will be given a Certificate of Failure.
For both situations, IPTO will inform the debtor's creditors of this.
The creditors may then file a fresh bankruptcy application against the debtor.

questions.title: What are the fees and charges that will be incurred in the Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)?
questions.text:
Before DRS commences:
a. Preliminary Admin Fee: $350.00 (At the submission of documents to the Official Assignee ("OA"))
b. Review Fee: $250.00 (At the submission of documents to the OA)
After DRS commences:
a. Annual Admin Fee (Year 1 and 2): $300.00 (At the start of each admin year)
b. Annual Admin Fee (Year 3, 4 and 5): $350.00 (At the start of each admin year)
c. Appeal Fee: $100.00 (Upon filing of Appeal Form 2)
d. DRP Modification Fee: $50.00. (On or before Creditor's Meeting for modification of DRP)
Other fees:
a. DRS Search Fee: $6.00
b. Proof of Debt Fee: $5.00
c. Document Search Fee: $25.00
d. Photocopying of document: $1.00 (per page)
e. Collection fee for payments made by debtors: 1.5% of amount collected
f. Distribution fee for payments made by OA: 3% of amount distributed

questions.title: How will a creditor or a member of public know if a debtor is under the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text:
The Official Assignee ("OA") does not inform the debtor's family or employer of his DRS status.
A creditor who has been disclosed by the debtor will receive a notice from the OA to file an electronic Proof of Debt against the debtor.
Any creditor or member of public may also conduct an online search with the debtor's NRIC number here to check if he is on the DRS.

questions.title: How does a creditor file a proof of debt against a debtor and what are the relevant supporting documents to submit?
questions.text: You may wish to refer to our website at Information for Creditors (mlaw.gov.sg) and Forms for Administration (mlaw.gov.sg) for more information.

questions.title: What are the charges for the filing of Proof of Debt?
questions.text:
Filing fee for proof of debt is S$5.
The filing fee is not claimable as part of the debt incurred. The Proof of Debt can be filed at the Creditor's Portal here.

questions.title: Does a creditor need to attend the meeting of creditors?
questions.text:
A creditor may choose whether or not to attend the meeting. If a creditor chooses not to attend the meeting, the creditor may raise questions through the Official Assignee ("OA") or request their solicitors to attend the meeting on their behalf.
If the creditor wishes to raise questions in relation to the debtor's Statement of Affairs, Income and Expenditure Statement and the Debt Repayment Plan, he is required to submit his list of questions to the OA at least 7 days before the meeting.
The OA will examine the questions to determine if they are relevant. The OA will disallow questions which are irrelevant, scandalous, frivolous or vexatious or which cannot be substantiated. A creditor must bring all documents in support of his claim of a debt against the debtor. Where a creditor has yet to submit his proof of debt, he must also bring a copy of the proof of debt. Creditors may respond to the OA on their attendance for the meeting.

questions.title: Do I have to repay my creditors before commencing the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text:
During the period of assessment and prior to the commencement of the DRS, the debtor's creditors have the right to recover payment from him and institute legal action. As such, the debtor is still obliged to pay his creditors. A debtor must inform the case administrator and provide the receipts as proof of payment.
Upon commencement of the Debt Repayment Plan, creditors will receive periodic payments and the debtor should not make any preferential payments to his creditors. These will continue until the completion of the payments as set out in the terms of the Plan.

questions.title: How and when will the debtor be informed that he can commence the Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text:
Debtors may be informed of the outcome of the assessment of their suitability after the Creditors' Meeting via email and/or upon the fulfilment of specific instructions given to them. The Official Assignee ("OA") will also advise them of the amount of instalment the debtor will be required to pay.
The debtor will need to prepare the sum required (first month instalment amount and the first annual fee) and fulfil any other conditions or instructions which are specifically given to him by the OA. Otherwise, the debtor may be found unsuitable for the DRS and his case will be referred back to the Court.
The sooner a debtor starts on the DRS, the less he will be paying in the long run as interest on the claims made by his creditors will stop running on the day the Debt Repayment Plan starts. If the debtor commences on the DRS, the OA will inform the debtor, the Court the applicant-creditor and his creditors of the commencement. The bankruptcy application made against the debtor will be deemed withdrawn if the assessment is successful.

questions.title: What are some of the duties that a debtor must comply with?
questions.text: A debtor must pay his instalments, bonuses from his salary and fees when required. He must not make any preferential payments to his creditors after his Debt Repayment Plan has commenced. In addition, he must not incur further liabilities that he does not have the ability to repay. He must also keep the Official Assignee updated of any change in his address and contact details at all times.

questions.title: Do debtors on Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS") have any travel restrictions to adhere to?
questions.text: A debtor will not face any travel restrictions, so he is not required to submit a travel application to leave Singapore. However, it is important to note that this must not be used as an excuse for any default in the DRS monthly instalments or failure to attend any meetings scheduled by the Official Assignee.

questions.title: Will my bank account be frozen if I am a debtor on Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text: The Official Assignee will not freeze the debtor's bank account, as the debtor is not a bankrupt. However, the bank may choose to do so in order to protect its own interests upon learning of the debtor's DRS status.

questions.title: What if a Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”) debtor has entered into a hire-purchase agreement or a mortgage loan?
questions.text:
If a debtor has entered into a hire-purchase agreement before the bankruptcy application was made against him or has an existing mortgage loan on a property, he is to inform the Official Assignee of this when he is being considered for the Scheme.
The debtor should continue to make payments to the hire-purchase company or the bank in accordance with the terms of the hire-purchase agreement or the mortgage agreement.

questions.title: Is the main hirer or the guarantor liable for the debt?
questions.text: The main hirer is liable for the debt. If the guarantor's liability has arisen pursuant to the terms of the guarantee agreement with the hire purchase company, the guarantor will also be liable for the debt. The Official Assignee will ensure that no over payment is made to the creditor.

questions.title: What happens if a third party wish to pay the debt on my behalf?
questions.text: You must inform the administrator of such arrangement and provide us a letter of undertaking of such payments or receipts of payments.

questions.title: What if debtor's financial circumstances change after the commencement of his Debt Repayment Plan ("DRP")?
questions.text:
The debtor or the creditor should inform the Official Assignee ("OA") of any change in the debtor's financial circumstances, particularly where the change may affect his ability to comply with the terms of the DRP. The OA may then consider modifying the DRP. This is on a case-by-case basis.
The debtor's creditor(s) will be informed of any changes in the debtor's circumstances that may affect the debtor's ability to fulfil the terms of the DRP.

questions.title: Can creditors still take action against the debtor after the commencement of the Debt Repayment Plan ("DRP")?
questions.text:
During the period when the DRP is in effect, no creditor to whom the debtor is indebted in respect of any debt provable under the Debt Repayment Scheme has any remedy against the person or property of the debtor in respect of that debt.
Creditors whose debts were incurred prior to the commencement of the DRP should file a Proof of Debt with the Official Assignee, notwithstanding that the DRP has commenced.

questions.title: What if I become unemployed while on Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)?
questions.text:
If the debtor is out of job, the Official Assignee ("OA") may suspend the monthly repayment for a maximum of 3 months but this is subject to the OA's approval. The debtor may also be granted an arrears instalment plan once he has found a new employment.
The debtor has to submit documents to substantiate the unemployment such as a letter of retrenchment from the employers or the latest CPF contribution statement indicating zero contribution in his last month of employment.

questions.title: How does a debtor in Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”) repay his debts to his creditors?
questions.text:
Debtors have to make payments of their monthly instalments to the Official Assignee ("OA"). The OA will disburse dividends to the creditors who have submitted their claims when there are sufficient funds in the debtors' account. The disbursement of dividends is on an annual basis.
Debtors' payments will be fractionalized and paid to the creditors. These dividends will continue until the completion of the payments set out in the terms of the Debt Repayment Plan.

questions.title: What if I finish repaying my instalments before the end of my Debt Repayment Plan (“DRP”) as a debtor on Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)?
questions.text: If a debtor is able to make full payment before the end of his DRP, his DRS records will be removed upon making his full repayment and receiving his Certificate of Completion from the Official Assignee.

questions.title: How and when will the Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”) cease?
What is a Certificate of Completion for Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”)?
questions.text:
The debtor will receive a Certificate of Completion once he has completed the DRS successfully.
The Notice and Certificate of Completion will be sent to the address of the debtor.

questions.title: What happens if a debtor on Debt Repayment Scheme (“DRS”) defaults on his instalment payment?
questions.text: The Official Assignee may issue a Certificate of Failure against the debtor and will inform his creditors of this. The creditors may then start fresh bankruptcy proceedings against the debtor. The debtor may be adjudged a bankrupt thereafter.

questions.title: Is the non-payment of the monthly instalments the only reason for the Official Assignee (“OA”) to issue the Certificate of Failure?
questions.text:
The non-payment of the monthly instalments is not the only reason for the OA's consideration before issuing the Certificate of Failure.
The OA may also issue the Certificate of Failure if the debtor furnishes information or documents which are false or misleading or contain any material omission, if the debtor has made preferential payments to any of his creditors, or if the debtor managed to obtain the approval for a lower monthly instalment by means of fraud, false representation or the concealment of any material fact, etc.

questions.title: What is a Certificate of Inapplicability for Debt Repayment Scheme ("DRS")?
questions.text: The debtor will receive a Certificate of Inapplicability once the debtor's total liabilities have been determined to exceed $150,000 after the commencement of his Debt Repayment Plan ("DRP"). This can happen anytime during the period when the DRP is in effect.

questions.title: Can I appeal against the Certificate of Failure or the Certificate of Inapplicability issued against me?
questions.text: The Certificate of Failure and the Certificate of Inapplicability cannot be rescinded once they have been issued. The repayment plan on the Debt Repayment Scheme has ceased and the debtor is no longer required to make payments to the Official Assignee. The Debt Repayment Plan also cannot be reinstated once the certificates have been issued.

questions.title: Can I apply for loans or credit facilities after being discharged from bankruptcy?
questions.text: Yes, you can apply for loans or credit facilities after you are discharged from bankruptcy. However, you may wish to note that this is subject to the financial institution's approval.

questions.title: How do I make a complaint about a bankrupt?
questions.text:
For bankruptcy-related offences, you may wish to submit a First Incident Report ("FIR") to the trustee in bankruptcy with the relevant supporting documents.
For non-bankruptcy-related offences, you may wish to lodge a Police Report with the Singapore Police Force.

questions.title: How do I avoid bankruptcy?
questions.text: Please refer to Alternatives to Bankruptcy.

questions.title: How can I obtain a Letter or Certificate of Discharge?
questions.text:
You may obtain a Letter of Discharge from the Insolvency Office if your bankruptcy was discharged by the High Court.
If your bankruptcy was discharged by the Official Assignee, a Certificate of Discharge will be sent to your registered address via post after your discharge from bankruptcy.
A duplicate of the Certificate of Discharge is available at a fee.

questions.title: What happens to my HDB flat when I am made bankrupt?
questions.text:
Under the Housing and Development Act, as long as one of the owners of the HDB flat is a Singapore Citizen (SC household), the HDB flat will not vest in the trustee in bankruptcy i.e., the HDB flat owner(s) would not be required to realise the HDB flat for the benefit of the creditors.
However, if none of the owner(s) is a Singapore Citizen, the bankrupt's share of the HDB Flat would then vest in the trustee in bankruptcy for the benefit of the creditors.

questions.title: How do I check whether someone is bankrupt?
questions.text:
Insolvency Search Service
To check if someone is made bankrupt, you can conduct a search using the Insolvency Search Service on our website for a fee of $6.00.
With effect from 1 April 2010, records of bankruptcy orders which have been annulled will no longer be available from Insolvency Search Service.
With effect from 1 June 2010, records of bankruptcy orders which have been discharged for 5 years or more will no longer be available from Insolvency Search Service.
What to prepare
You will need:
ID/Passport number of the person whom you are enquiring on
Email address to receive search result (optional)
How to search
Step 1: Go to the Insolvency Search Service at https://go.gov.sg/bankruptcy
Step 2: Enter the person's details
E.g., NRIC, Name or Passport Number
Step 3: Make payment of $6.00
E.g., Debit Card, Credit Card or eNets
Note that if you did not receive the Insolvency Search Result(s) after making your payment, please follow the steps below before lodging an online enquiry:
If you have provided your email address for the E-service to send you the results, check your email to see if you have received a copy.
If there are no results in your inbox or spam folder, please provide us with the following details below through https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw and our officers will send the search results to you after we verify that the search fee payment is successful within 3 working days.

questions.title: What is the Individual Insolvency Administration Information (IIAI)?
Are family members liable for the debts incurred by a bankrupt?
questions.text: Family members are not liable for debts incurred by a bankrupt unless they are co-borrowers or guarantors for the debt.

questions.title: What are the responsibilities and rights of a bankrupt?
questions.text: Please refer to information on Responsibilities and Rights of a Bankrupt.

questions.title: How do I obtain a discharge from bankruptcy?
questions.text: Please refer to information on Discharge from Bankruptcy.

questions.title: What is bankruptcy?
questions.text:
In Singapore, bankruptcy is a legal process involving an individual or firm that is declared unable to repay debts amounting to at least $15,000.
Once an individual is declared a bankrupt, the bankrupt's property will be vested in the trustee in bankruptcy, who will manage the bankrupt's financial affairs.

questions.title: Can creditors seize a bankrupt's assets?
questions.text:
Upon bankruptcy, the property of the bankrupt vests in the trustee in bankruptcy.
Creditors cannot seize the bankrupt's property except by Court Order or if they are a secured creditor.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt travel for work?
questions.text:
Bankrupts are not allowed to leave or remain or reside outside Singapore without the previous permission of the trustee in bankruptcy.
Bankrupts are advised to submit their travel applications online, via the Insolvent Person's Portal, at least 14 days before the intended date of travel for consideration by the trustee in bankruptcy.

questions.title: How long will it take the Insolvency Office to remove a bankrupt's information from the online search service after the annulment of his bankruptcy?
questions.text: The Insolvency Office requires seven working days (beginning from the day a copy of the order of court annulling the bankruptcy order is received) to update the records.

questions.title: What is the Official Assignee's role in bankruptcy administration?
questions.text: Please refer to Who is the Official Assignee.

questions.title: Will I lose my job if I declare information on my bankruptcy to my employer?
questions.text: Bankrupts may wish to check their employment contracts on the required declarations if made bankrupt.

questions.title: How long does it take for a Bankruptcy Application to be processed?
questions.text:
The court will inform parties of the hearing date once it has been fixed.
Please note that not all bankruptcy application will result in the bankruptcy of the individual.
The court may dismiss the application or adjourn the hearing, for up to 6 months or such other period as the court may direct, for the debtor to be assessed for Debt Repayment Scheme suitability.

questions.title: How do I obtain information about my own bankruptcy matters online?
questions.text: Bankrupts can obtain information about their bankruptcy online via the Insolvent Person's Portal.

questions.title: How can a creditor obtain information about the bankrupt's estate?
How can a debtor apply for his own bankruptcy?
questions.text: Please refer to the Singapore Courts website on debtor's bankruptcy application.

questions.title: How do I obtain an annulment of the Bankruptcy Order made against me?
questions.text:
A bankruptcy order can either be annulled by the court or by the Official Assignee.
Please refer to (1) the Singapore Courts website on how to apply to the court to annul a bankruptcy order and (2) the Insolvency Office's website on the annulment of a bankruptcy order by the Official Assignee.

questions.title: How does an annulment of a Bankruptcy Order differ from a discharge of a Bankruptcy Order?
questions.text:
An annulment cancels the Bankruptcy Order that was made against the debtor.
Any assets which were not disposed of prior to the annulment of the Bankruptcy Order will be returned to the debtor. After an annulment of a Bankruptcy Order, the debtor will continue to be liable for any debts that had not been proven against him when the bankruptcy was in force.
However, after a discharge from bankruptcy, the bankrupt will no longer be liable for debts that were provable in his bankruptcy (except for debts due to the Government, debts arising from personal injuries caused to a person and debts arising from any order made under the Women's Charter relating to family matters).

questions.title: Can bankruptcy records be deleted?
questions.text:
If a bankruptcy order has been annulled, the records will be removed from the bankruptcy register and would not appear on the Insolvency Office's online search service.
If a bankrupt is discharged from bankruptcy after meeting the target contribution, the bankruptcy record will be removed from the bankruptcy register after a period of 5 years.
However, if the bankrupt did not meet the target contribution, the bankruptcy record would be placed on the bankruptcy register permanently.

questions.title: What can I do if a bankrupt borrows from me without informing that he is an undischarged bankrupt?
questions.text: You should submit a First Incident Report to the trustee in bankruptcy to provide the facts and details of the case.

questions.title: Where can I find the bankruptcy-related forms?
questions.text: The bankruptcy-related forms can be found on our website at Forms for Administration.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt have a bank account?
questions.text:
Bankrupts are only allowed to maintain 1 personal savings bank account with the consent of their trustee in bankruptcy.
Bankrupts are not allowed to open a joint bank account.
If you do not have an existing bank account and wish to open one, please contact your trustee in bankruptcy.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt purchase insurance policies?
questions.text: Bankrupts are allowed to purchase insurance policies that has no investment component(s) and no surrender / maturity value.

questions.title: How will a bankrupt make his monthly contributions if he loses his job?
questions.text:
Bankrupts are encouraged to make regular monthly contribution to their bankruptcy estate.
Bankrupts should contact their trustee in bankruptcy if there are significant changes to their income to discuss and re-assess their monthly contributions.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt use his salary to pay bills?
questions.text: A bankrupt can utilise the remainder of his monthly income, after payment of his monthly contribution, to pay his bills.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt borrow money?
questions.text: It is an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to obtain a loan of more than $1,000 from any person without informing the person, at the time the credit is obtained, of his status as an undischarged bankrupt.

questions.title: Will I have to terminate my insurance policy if I become a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Upon the making of the Bankruptcy Order, a bankrupt's assets vest in the trustee in bankruptcy without any further conveyance, assignment or transfer; and become divisible among his creditors.
The trustee in bankruptcy will take the necessary action to realise the insurance policies for the benefit of the creditors.

questions.title: What is an applicant creditor?
questions.text: The applicant creditor is the creditor who filed the bankruptcy application against the debtor.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt apply for a debit card?
questions.text: Bankrupts can apply for a debit card. However, the application is subject to the approval of the financial institution.

questions.title: How do I recover a loan to a bankrupt?
questions.text: You may wish to file a proof of debt against the bankrupt's estate if the debt was incurred prior to his bankruptcy.

questions.title: What is the minimum debt amount to file a bankruptcy application?
questions.text: A bankruptcy application can be filed against any individual or firm that is unable to repay any outstanding debt of at least $15,000.

questions.title: When do I receive a certificate of annulment?
questions.text:
If your bankruptcy was annulled by the Official Assignee, a Certificate of Annulment will be sent to your registered address via post after the annulment of your bankruptcy.
A duplicate of the Certificate of Annulment is available at a fee.
If your bankruptcy was annulled by the Court, you would need to file a request for an Order of Court.

questions.title: When can I be discharged from bankruptcy if it is my second bankruptcy?
questions.text:
A repeat bankrupt can be discharged from bankruptcy after 60 months if he/she has met the Target Contribution and if the creditors' objections to his/her discharge from bankruptcy does not exceed the statutory threshold (50% by number or 25% in value).
Furthermore, the administration of the bankrupt's affairs, e.g. realisation of assets for the benefit of his/her creditors and investigation into any bankruptcy offences that were committed, would have to be completed before the bankrupt can be discharged from bankruptcy.

questions.title: When does a Bankruptcy Order take effect?
questions.text: A Bankruptcy Order takes effect immediately.

questions.title: What is the difference between corporate insolvency and individual insolvency (bankruptcy)?
questions.text: Corporate insolvency is the winding up of a corporate entity (a company) while individual insolvency is the making of a bankruptcy order against an individual (a person) or a sole proprietorship or a partnership.

questions.title: How long is the discharge process?
questions.text: The discharge process generally takes about 3 to 6 months depending on the complexity of the case.

questions.title: What is the Individual Insolvency Search?
questions.text:
The Individual Insolvency Search is a service that allows members of public to conduct a search to determine the following:
(a) if an individual is on the Debt Repayment Scheme;
(b) if an individual is an undischarged bankrupt; or
(c) if the individual was discharged from bankruptcy in the past 5 years.
Please note that a fee of $6.00 is payable for each search.

questions.title: How can I prove my loan against a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Please refer to Information for Creditors on how you can file a Proof of Debt and the information required when filing a Proof of Debt.
Please file the Proof of Debt via the Creditor's Portal.

questions.title: What steps should a person who has had a Bankruptcy Order made against him/her take to ensure that any information relating to the annulled Bankruptcy Order is removed from the Insolvency Office's Individual Insolvency Search service?
questions.text: The bankrupt should provide the Insolvency Office with a copy of the Order of Court annulling the Bankruptcy Order.

questions.title: How long is the annulment process?
questions.text: The annulment process generally takes at least three months but may vary depending on the complexity of the case.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt pawn his valuables?
questions.text:
Upon the making of the Bankruptcy Order, a bankrupt's assets vest in the trustee in bankruptcy without any further conveyance, assignment or transfer; and become divisible among his creditors.
The bankrupt is required to declare and surrender all valuables in his possession to the trustee in bankruptcy.
The trustee in bankruptcy will take the necessary actions to realise the valuables for the benefit of the creditors.

questions.title: Can a bankrupt apply for credit cards or loans?
questions.text:
A bankrupt can apply for credit cards or loans. However, the application is subject to the approval of the financial institution.
Please also note that it is an offence for an undischarged bankrupt to obtain a loan of more than $1,000 from any person without informing the person, at the time the credit is obtained, of his status as an undischarged bankrupt.

questions.title: When will dividends be paid?
questions.text: Dividends will be paid when there are sufficient funds in the bankrupt's estate or upon the bankrupt's discharge from bankruptcy.

questions.title: Where can the bankrupt find the list of creditors who have filed proof of debts against him?
questions.text: The bankrupt can find the list of creditors in the Insolvent Person's Portal.

questions.title: What are my alternatives to bankruptcy?
questions.text: Please refer to Alternatives to Bankruptcy.

questions.title: What should I do if there is a pending court action while I am still a bankrupt?
questions.text: Please contact your appointed trustee in bankruptcy with the details of the pending court action.

questions.title: Can I still execute a Writ of Summons against my debtor after he is made a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Upon the making of the Bankruptcy Order, a bankrupt's assets vest in the trustee in bankruptcy without any further conveyance, assignment or transfer; and become divisible among his creditors.
You may wish to file a Proof of Debt against the bankrupt's estate instead.

questions.title: Can the annulment of the Bankruptcy Order against me be revoked?
questions.text: The annulment order may be revoked if you failed to comply with the repayment terms, or if fraud was involved in obtaining the annulment order.

questions.title: What is the cost of a bankruptcy application?
questions.text:
A deposit of $1,850.00 is to be paid to the Official Assignee for every bankruptcy application.
However, please note that this does not include any costs of bankruptcy proceedings, solicitor's fees and disbursements incurred or fees that might be incurred when filing the bankruptcy application.

questions.title: What are the functions/roles of the Licensing Officer?
Can the Licensing Officer provide legal advice for corporate and individual insolvency matters?
questions.text: No, you may wish to seek independent legal advice on such matters.

questions.title: Am I required to hold an insolvency practitioner's licence to be appointed to act in cases commenced under the Insolvency Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018 (“the Act”)?
questions.text:
Yes, in order to accept officeholder appointments whether in personal or corporate insolvency and debt restructuring cases commenced under the Act, you are required to hold a valid insolvency practitioner's licence, see section 47(1) of the Act.
It is an offence under section 48(2) of the Act for any person to act as an insolvency practitioner for an individual or corporation or to accept officeholder appointments without a valid licence

questions.title: What are the criteria that must be fulfilled in order to be eligible to hold an insolvency practitioner's licence?
questions.text: Please refer to our webpage on Applying for an Insolvency Practitioner's Licence.

questions.title: How do I apply for an insolvency practitioner's licence?
questions.text: You can apply for an insolvency practitioner's licence through the Whole-of-Government's GoBusiness Dashboard.

questions.title: What are the documents that must be submitted in support of my licence application?
questions.text: Click here for the Licence Application Process which provides a list of the required supporting documents.

questions.title: Are appointments in members' voluntary winding up or schemes of arrangement cases considered as relevant work experience required for the purpose of the licence application?
questions.text: No, such appointments are not considered as "relevant work experience" for the purposes of the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution (Insolvency Practitioners) Regulations 2020.

questions.title: Do I need to hold an insolvency practitioner's licence if I intend to continue with and complete the administration of cases commenced under the Bankruptcy Act (Cap. 20) and/or Companies Act (Cap. 50)?
questions.text:
No, you are not required to hold an insolvency practitioner's licence. However, you will need to continue to maintain the necessary qualifications required under the Bankruptcy Act (Cap. 20) and / or Companies Act (Cap. 50):
Regime
Qualifications
Bankruptcy and Voluntary Arrangements
Public Accountant (“PA”);
Solicitor; or
Any other person the Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, prescribe
Creditors’ Voluntary Winding Up
Approved liquidator (unless a resolution is passed)
Court-Ordered Winding Up
Approved liquidator
Receivership
Judicial Management
PA;
Non-PA if appointed by Court or nominated by Minister

questions.title: What will happen to the insolvency and debt restructuring cases commenced under the corresponding previous laws which have yet to complete administration?
questions.text: The Bankruptcy Act (Cap. 20) and Companies Act (Cap. 50) will continue to apply to existing insolvency and debt restructuring cases commenced under the Bankruptcy Act (Cap. 20) and Companies Act (Cap. 50).

questions.title: My insolvency practitioner's licence will expire on 30 June. When can I renew my licence?
questions.text:
You may submit your application for renewal between 1 March to 30 April of the year in which your licence expires, should you intend to continue acting or undertake insolvency officeholder appointments. If you fail to submit your application before 30 April, you will be required to submit your application as a new applicant.
Please refer to our webpage on renewal of licence, for more information.

questions.title: I have submitted an application for the renewal of my insolvency practitioner's licence, and it is currently pending approval. Can I continue to act as an insolvency practitioner even though my existing insolvency practitioner's licence has expired?
questions.text: Yes, you can continue to act as an insolvency practitioner because under section 51(6) of the Act, the licence continues to be in force until you are informed of the outcome of your application for renewal.

questions.title: How do I submit a complaint or provide information relating to the improper conduct of an insolvency practitioner?
questions.text:
You can provide the details by completing the Insolvency Practitioners Complaints Form and submit it together with the relevant supporting documents via https://www.go.gov.sg/contactminlaw.
Alternatively, the documents may be sent via post addressed to the:
Attn: Licensing Officer
MinLaw Mailroom
45 Maxwell Road
#06-01 The URA Centre (East Wing)
Singapore 069118

questions.title: Is there a register of individuals holding a valid insolvency practitioner's licence?
questions.text:
You can refer to the register of insolvency practitioners with valid licences here. For licences which have expired, please click here.
For any licensing action imposed against an insolvency practitioner, click here.

questions.title: How do I find out who is the insolvency practitioner appointed for a specific individual or corporate insolvency case?
questions.text:
You may conduct the following paid insolvency searches via https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/io/:
a) Individual Insolvency Search for persons; and
b) Corporate Insolvency Search for companies that have been compulsorily wound up by the Court. For companies that were not wound up by the Court, you may wish to conduct an ACRA Bizfile search.

questions.title: How do we log in to LSRA e-Services?
questions.text:
Law practices with existing licences should log in to LSRA e-Services using "Registered Entities (with UEN)" via Singpass and select relevant UEN/Entity (if applicable). Please ensure that the person logging in is an authorised Singpass user for LSRA e-Services for the law practice (in Singpass login and select relevant UEN/Entity (if applicable)).
Applicants who wish to set up a new law practice should log in using their Singpass. If you do not have a Singpass account or have forgotten your Singpass login details, you may apply for one or reset it via the Singpass website. If you are not eligible for Singpass, you can engage a Singapore law practice or a corporate services provider to submit the application via LSRA e-Services on your behalf.

questions.title: How do we check the status of our application to the Legal Services Regulatory Authority ("LSRA")?

Please note that making multiple calls and enquiries to check on the status of applications may delay the processing of applications.

questions.title: Can we view or retrieve previous LSRA applications and documents submitted by our law practice?

Law practices will not be able to view or retrieve previous applications and supporting documents submitted via LSRA e-Services. Nor will LSRA be able to provide you a copy.
Please keep a copy of all applications and supporting documents submitted by your law practice for your own records.

questions.title: How do we delete or withdraw an application to the Legal Services Regulatory Authority?
questions.text: You can delete your pending application in LSRA e-Services if it has not been submitted (i.e. its status is "Draft", "Pending Declaration" or "Pending Application Fee"). If the application has already been submitted (i.e. its status is "In-Progress", "Pending Further Information", "Re-submitted", "Pending Licence/Issuance Fee" or "Pending Licence/Certificate Issuance"), please write to us at Contact Us @ OneMinLaw with your request to withdraw the application, including the reason.

questions.text: Please refer to our webpage on Request a Certificate of Good Standing or a Letter of Confirmation for more information.

questions.title: What are the fees for LSRA applications, licences and certificates?
questions.text:
The fees are set out in the First Schedule of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015 (for law practice entities) and the Second Schedule of the Legal Profession (Regulated Individuals) Rules 2015 (for individuals).

questions.title: Are foreign lawyers ("FLs") and foreign law practices ("FLPs") allowed to write articles on Singapore law?
questions.text:
FLs and FLPs may publish factual, informative client briefings and commentaries about Singapore law, provided they do not hold out that they are qualified to practise Singapore law beyond what is permitted under their registration and licence.
Therefore, if an article has been written by or with input from a Singapore solicitor, the article should be properly attributed to the Singapore solicitor and his/her law practice. If the Singapore solicitor is a member of an affiliated Singapore law practice, the full name of the Singapore law practice should be used.
Where a FLP has independently produced the article, a suitable caveat should be included, such as the sample provided below.
Sample Wording:
"[Name of foreign law practice] is licensed to operate as a foreign law practice in Singapore. Where advice on Singapore law is required, we will refer the matter to and work with licensed Singapore law practices where necessary."

questions.title: What are the "permitted areas of legal practice"?
questions.text: Please refer to section 36A of the Legal Profession Act, read with rule 4 of the Legal Profession (Regulated Individuals) Rules 2015, and section 168 of the Legal Profession Act with rule 50 of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015.

questions.title: How do I submit a complaint about a law practice entity or its lawyers?
questions.text:
Complaints in relation to the provision of professional services by lawyers or their professional conduct (e.g. overcharging, lateness, incompetence) are managed by the Law Society of Singapore. For more information, please refer to the guides on the Law Society's website, which set out their processes for submitting complaints.
If you wish to report a breach by a law practice entity of its business criteria or licence conditions under the Legal Profession Act (e.g. a law practice practising Singapore law when it is not permitted to do so, or a law practice marketing or publicising itself as providing legal services in areas of legal practice which it is not permitted to provide), please submit it here.
If you suspect an entity or an individual to be providing legal services in or from Singapore in breach of the Legal Profession Act, you may wish to make a police report.

questions.title: What to do if I encountered an IT issue?

Please use Edge browser and clear the cache (go to Setting > Privacy, search, and services > Clear browsing data), then close all browser window(s). Thereafter, access LSRA e-Services again, login and submit your application.
If the issue persists, please provide the screenshot of the error and let us know your login date and time via Contact Us @ OneMinLaw so that we can forward the details to our IT team for their investigation.

questions.title: Why can't I find the "Update/Terminate" options under the 'Action' button for my existing licence/lawyer's registration?

If so, please delete the current draft application and you should then be able to see the application option under the 'Action' button.

questions.title: The lawyer has already left the law practice. Why is his/her record still showing in my licence update application?

If the licence update application is created before the lawyer updates Supreme Court via eLitigation, please:
Delete the draft licence update application that is still pending under the 'Pending Applications' section of your law practice's dashboard; and
Generate a new draft licence update application under the 'Licences/Registrations' section of the 'Entities' tab.
However, if the record is still showing incorrectly and in view that the licence update application is for the purposes of updating your law practice's particulars, you may wish to indicate the correct number of lawyers in your law practice (as of the date of submission) under the 'Information on Singapore law practice' section and proceed to submit the application via LSRA e-Services.

Please note that search results are based on the data available at the time of the search.

questions.title: I need legal advice. Can MinLaw recommend a law practice or lawyer?

If you require the services of a law practice, you can search for law practices and lawyers by name, licence/registration type, size and practice area using the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's online search function.
You may also wish to contact the Law Society of Singapore.

questions.title: How do we set up a law practice in Singapore?
questions.text:
Please see an overview of the process for setting up a law practice in Singapore:
a) Apply via LSRA e-Services for a law practice entity licence.
b) Upon receiving in-principle approval from LSRA, you will have 3 months to register the business entity with Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority ("ACRA") and obtain a Singpass for the law practice.
c) Purchase the professional indemnity insurance for the law practice.
d) Submit a copy of the purchased professional indemnity insurance policy and the UEN details via LSRA e-Services.
e) Submit a copy of the ACRA business profile of your law practice via Contact Us @OneMinlaw.
f) Thereafter, the law practice licence will be issued.
g) Apply via LSRA e-Services for a Certificate of Registration for the foreign lawyers who will be practising in the law practice. Singapore solicitors should apply to Supreme Court for their Singapore practising certificates via eLitigation.
h) Apply to the Ministry of Manpower for a work pass for the foreign lawyers who will be practising in the law practice.
i) Commence operations of the law practice within 6 months of the licence validity date.
Estimated processing time is 30 working days. Applications with incomplete supporting documents/information, submitted during the peak period from December to April, and/or that are complex, will take longer to process. Complex applications include those involving concurrent appointments, foreign interests in Singapore law practices and/or collaborations between Singapore law practices and foreign law practice entities.
For more information, please refer to our website.
topics: Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals
Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / Law Practice Entities

questions.title: What are the requirements for naming of Singapore law practices ("SLP")?
questions.text:
For the legislative requirements for the naming of SLPs:
Law firms (sole proprietorships and partnerships): Section 132 of the Legal Profession Act and Part 2 of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015.
Limited liability partnerships (LLP): Section 139 of the Legal Profession Act and rule 15 of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015.
Law corporations (LLC): Section 154 of the Legal Profession Act and rule 29 of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015.
One of the requirements for the name of a SLP is that it must not be so similar to the name of another law practice entity as to be likely to be confused with it. With over 1,000 law practices currently licensed in Singapore which can be found on our search function, there is an increased likelihood of similar names being proposed, especially where the proposed name consists solely or mainly of initials.
When applying to the Legal Services Regulatory Authority for a licence for your law practice, you should therefore propose three name choices (including explanations of choice) that are clearly distinguishable from that of existing law practices to increase the likelihood of your preferred name being approved.

Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / Law Practice Entities

questions.title: What are the threshold requirements for a Singapore law practice ("SLP")?
questions.text: The threshold requirements for a SLP are set out in rule 3 of the Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015.

questions.title: Do we need to submit a draft constitution as part of an application to set up a law practice?
questions.text:
Yes, if the proposed law practice will be structured as a Singapore law practice law corporation (LLC). The draft constitution should be uploaded as a supporting document in your online application via LSRA e-Services.
You may use LSRA's specimen clauses when drafting your constitution, and should submit the document in Word format with tracked changes. Please note that your application may require more time to process if your draft constitution contains significant deviations from our specimen clauses and/or does not satisfy the legislative requirements.
You can refer to the relevant provisions in the Legal Profession Act and Legal Profession (Law Practice Entities) Rules 2015 for the requirements relating to an LLC's constitution.

Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / Law Practice Entities

questions.title: How much insurance coverage must a foreign law practice ("FLP") entity licensed in Singapore maintain?
questions.text:
A licensed FLP entity must maintain, throughout the period while its licence is in force, insurance cover of at least SGD 2 million for each and every claim in respect of civil liability in connection with the provision of legal services in or from Singapore by the FLP.
The amount is the same regardless of the legal structure of the entity or the number of directors.
topics: Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals
Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / Law Practice Entities

questions.title: Does a foreign law practice ("FLP") need to have a resident lawyer in Singapore?
questions.text:
Yes, a FLP will need to have at least one lawyer registered with the Legal Services Regulatory Authority ("LSRA") who is ordinarily resident in Singapore (i.e. their usual place of residence is in Singapore).
A lawyer who is a Singapore citizen or permanent resident, or who holds a valid work pass from the Ministry of Manpower ("MOM"), will be accepted as being "ordinarily resident in Singapore".
For more information on work passes, please refer to the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM) website. Please note that foreign lawyers who require a work pass will need to be registered with the LSRA before the law practice can apply to the MOM for a work pass for them.
topics: Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals
Licensing or Registration of Law Practice Entities/Individuals / Law Practice Entities

questions.title: Does a law practice need the approval of the LSRA to rent space from or use the address of a serviced office or a co-working space?
questions.text:
The law practice entity will need to seek approval by submitting an update application via LSRA e-Services and providing details of the arrangement in the "Sharing of Premises" section of the online form.
Please refer to our webpage on Approval to Share Premises for more information.
