questions.title: What is the time limit for me to redeem the jewellery which I have pledged?
questions.text: A pawner should take note of the expiry date of the pawn ticket. A pawner can redeem his/her jewellery before the pawn ticket expires, i.e. within 6 months. Within this 6-month period and at any time after the end of the redemption period but before the pledge is forfeited, a pawnbroker is not allowed to dispose of the pledge. The period of redemption can be extended subject to the agreement between both the pawner and the pawnbroker. A Notice of Forfeiture will be served to the pawner by the pawnbroker within 2 months upon the expiry of the redemption period and the pledge is forfeited in the event that the pawner does not redeem it within one month after the Notice Forfeiture is served.

questions.title: How much do I have to pay in order to redeem the goods which I have pledged to a pawnbroker?
questions.text: To redeem the goods which you have pledged to a pawnbroker, you must pay an aggregate amount comprising the loan quantum and the profit (i.e. interest on the loan). The profit is capped at 1.5% of the loan amount per month.

questions.title: What should I do when I receive a Notice of Forfeiture from the Pawnbroker?
questions.text: A Notice of Forfeiture informs you of the impending event that your pledge will become the absolute property of the pawnbroker. You should pay attention to the deadline indicated on the Notice of Forfeiture and approach the pawnshop on or before that date to redeem your pledge. Once the deadline has passed, you would no longer have the right of redemption and the pledge becomes the pawnbroker's absolute property.

questions.title: What should I do if I lose my pawn ticket?
questions.text: If you lose your pawn ticket, you may go to the pawnshop concerned to make an application to prove that you are a person entitled to redeem the pledge. The pawnbroker will then make reasonable inquiries as to the truth of the matters stated in the application and issue a replacement pawn ticket once they are satisfied that you have the right to redeem the pledge under the Pawnbrokers Act 2015.

questions.title: I have reached the age of majority, and I live overseas. What documents are required to claim my money held in trust?
questions.text:
If you are living overseas
In order for us to pay the monies to you via telegraphic transfer, please let us have the following documents via to https://go.gov.sg/pto:
a) the page of your passport which shows your name, passport number and other particulars; and
b) the page of your personal bank account passbook or your personal bank account statement which shows the following information:
i) Your bank account number;
ii) Sort code of your Bank;
iii) Swift code of your Bank;
iv) Name of your Bank & Bank Branch (if any); and

Please let us know your preferred payment currency and overseas residential address.
Note: You will have to bear the bank charges for the telegraphic transfer of the monies to you and any cost of exchanging the monies into a foreign currency. The amount to be paid to you will be net of the bank charges.

questions.title: Could I know the breakdown of the figures deducted from the monies distributed ?
questions.text: Eligible beneficiaries, claimants, or guardians can view the statement of account for the administration of a deceased person's CPF, Baby Bonus, Edusave, or PSEA money. Information on the Administration of Deceased Estate (assets other than CPF, Baby Bonus, Edusave, or PSEA money) can be obtained from https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on the Public Trustee?
questions.text: Please refer to https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/.

For all other documents, you may submit them via the online e-services at https://go.gov.sg/pto select 'Submission of Supporting Documents')."

questions.title: What is considered as unclaimed funds?
questions.text:
Upon the conclusion of the administration of the estate of a deceased, if there are monies in the hands of the Public Trustee which cannot be disposed of by distribution in accordance with the law, the Public Trustee shall credit those funds to the Unclaimed Estate Account.
These funds shall be kept in the account for 7 years and if the monies remain unclaimed at the expiration, the funds together with any interest earned shall be paid into the Consolidated Funds. If any claim is made to the satisfactory of the Public Trustee, the amount shall be paid to the claimant without the interest from the Consolidated Funds.

questions.title: What is presumption of death?
questions.text: Presumption of death occurs when a person is legally assumed to be dead after being absent for seven years, and the petitioner has no reason to believe that the person is still alive. This presumption must be granted by the court.

questions.title: Is there a deadline to claim the monies left by a deceased person?
questions.text:
There is no time limit as to when a beneficiary should claim the monies left behind by a deceased from the Public Trustee.
The unclaimed monies will be kept by the Public Trustee with no interest given.

questions.title: What is oath?
questions.text: An oath is to swear by the truth; to have made a solemn promise to tell the truth.

questions.title: How can I contact the Public Trustee?
questions.text:
Please contact us via https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw or call us at 1800 225 5529*.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones

questions.title: How can I receive the trust monies?
questions.text:
If you have a Singapore bank account
In order for us to pay the monies to you electronically, submit them via the online e-services at https://go.gov.sg/pto select 'Submission of Bank Account/PayNow Details').
The required documents are:
a) your identity card (front and back); and
b) front page of the bank passbook or bank statement. For a payment request to a third party bank account, both the beneficiary and the account holder(s) must execute the appropriate indemnity form (Form 15), which is available for download at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/. For other non-electronic modes of payment, the beneficiaries will have to bear all the charges imposed by the bank(s) which will be deducted directly from the inheritance.

questions.title: Is the deceased going through separation with his spouse considered as lawful next-of-kin?
questions.text: Without the Decree Nisi Absolute / Final Judgment, a separated spouse remains as a lawful next-of-kin of the deceased.

questions.title: What is the meaning of vesting?
questions.text: This means conferring the power of authority upon someone to act on behalf.

questions.title: When will the monies be paid to me?
questions.text: As a general rule, we will distribute the monies within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation or the date of receipt of the deceased's monies, whichever is later.

questions.title: What do you mean by representation?
questions.text: One person is said to represent another when he acts in his place. Thus, an agent represents his principal, and an executor represents his testator.

questions.title: What is a will?
questions.text: A will is a legal document expressing a person's wishes regarding who shall administer and receive the person's assets after the testator's death.

questions.title: Can the Public Trustee pay me the monies via cheque?
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not issue any cheque payment. All payments made by the Public Trustee are done electronically via PayNow (account must be registered with your NRIC) or Direct Credit (fund transfer) to your designated account. For payment request via Direct Credit, the recipients are required to submit a copy of the front page of the bank passbook or online bank statement which reflects the name of the recipient and the bank account number.
(Note: For a payment request via Direct Credit to a joint or third party bank account, both the beneficiary and the account holder(s) must execute the indemnity form (Form 15) which is available for download at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/forms/ .)

questions.title: What is a Trust?
questions.text: A trust is a responsibility created by the donor transferring his assets to a person (trustee) to hold and control for the benefit of a third party (beneficiary). The trust can be created during the lifetime of the donor or by his will.

questions.title: What is resealing of grant?
questions.text:
Resealing of grant is to seal over an overseas grant for distribution of assets.
When an individual passes, leaving behind Singapore assets, these assets are frozen and cannot be dealt with. If the deceased's overseas grant is obtained in the Commonwealth, the grant must be re-sealed and deposited with the Singapore Court. Resealing means to have the overseas grant sealed with the Singapore Court’s seal and all such applications for resealing are made to the High Court (family division) in Singapore.

questions.title: Can I declare myself as the only beneficiary of a deceased person's monies even if there are other surviving beneficiaries?
questions.text:
You are required to declare ALL the beneficiaries of a deceased's person monies.
The Rules of Distribution under the Intestate Succession Act (1967) can be found at: https://go.gov.sg/cpf-estate.

questions.title: How do I submit my interbank GIRO details and bank documents to the Public Trustee?
questions.text: To submit bank documents to the Public Trustee, select "Submission of Bank Account / PayNow Details" via the eService at https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: Who is a Trustee?
questions.text: A trustee is a person responsible for the trust where the person holds and controls the assets for the advantage of someone else.

questions.title: Which form should I fill in if I wish to renounce my share of the deceased's CPF/ estate?
questions.text:
Beneficiaries whose shares are renounced will go into the common pool for distribution to all non-renouncing beneficiaries. If a beneficiary wishes to renounce his/ her share of the deceased person's CPF money/ estate, he/ she must either:
(i) complete the hardcopy Form 18 (Renunciation and Indemnity Form), which can be downloaded from https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/forms/. Submit the completed form together with a copy of his/ her NRIC, or
(ii) log in via his or her SingPass to complete Form 18 electronically. A copy of the renouncing beneficiary's NRIC is not required if Form 18 is executed electronically.

questions.title: How do I obtain a copy of a Birth, Death or Marriage Certificate?
questions.text:
To obtain (or "extract") a copy of a person's Birth Certificate or Death Certificate, please submit an online application to the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) via https://www.ica.gov.sg/documents.
For Marriage records, please submit an online application to the Registry of Marriages (ROM) via https://www.marriage.gov.sg/civil/marriage-records .

questions.title: What is renounce?
questions.text:
A lawful beneficiary giving up his/ her rights of inheritance.
Beneficiaries whose shares are renounced will go into the common pool for distribution to all non-renouncing beneficiaries. If a beneficiary wishes to renounce his/ her share of the deceased person's CPF money/ estate, he/ she must either:
(i) complete the hardcopy Form 18 (Renunciation and Indemnity Form), which can be downloaded from https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/forms/. Submit the completed form together with a copy of his/ her NRIC, or
(ii) log in via his or her SingPass to complete Form 18 electronically. A copy of the renouncing beneficiary's NRIC is not required if Form 18 is executed electronically.

questions.text: Please refer to https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member for information on CPF-related matters.

questions.title: Why is there a waiting period for claims against bona vacantia estate?
questions.text: The waiting period is a safeguard to ensure that the entitled next-of-kin has sufficient time to claim from the Public Trustee.

questions.title: Who can make an equitable or moral claim on the bona vacantia estate of the deceased?
questions.text: Anyone (including charities and other bodies) can make an equitable or moral claim on the estate of the deceased if he / she is able to produce the necessary documents and evidence required to support his / her claim. However, before a claim can be considered by the Public Trustee, the claimant must prove that the deceased has no surviving next-of-kin who is eligible to inherit the deceased's property and/or monies under the Intestate Succession Act 1967.

questions.title: I do not know if the Deceased has any assets. Can the Public Trustee assist me in my search?
questions.text:
No, the Public Trustee’s Office will not help you search for assets of the Deceased. You must find and provide details of all assets yourself before making a claim.
What you need to provide
Asset details required:
List of all assets the Deceased owned
Estimated value of each asset
Supporting documents to prove the assets exist
Why you need this information: The Public Trustee’s Office needs the complete asset information to assess the total estate value.
How to search for assets yourself
Check common places for asset information
Personal documents:
Bank statements and passbooks
Property documents (title deeds, HDB documents)
Insurance policies and investment statements
CPF statements and nomination forms
Tax returns and financial records
Estate planning documents
Digital records:
Email accounts for bank and investment notifications
Mobile banking apps on the Deceased's phone
Online investment platforms and trading accounts
Important things to know
You are responsible for the search: The Public Trustee’s Office expects you to conduct thorough searches before submitting your claim.
Incomplete information may delay your claim: Missing asset details can slow down the assessment process.
What happens after you find the assets:
Your next steps depend on two things:
Estate value (less than or more than $50,000)
Whether there is legal beneficiary (family members who can inherit)
To know more about Bona Vacantia you may visit the link: Ministry of Law | What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
For estates worth $50,000 or less
If there ARE legal beneficiary: Apply for estate administration which you can refer to Ministry of Law | How PTO can help to administer a Deceased's estate (bank account, shares, motor vehicles, etc.)
If there are NO legal beneficiary (Bona Vacantia): Follow detailed instruction at: Ministry of Law | How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate that is ≤ $50,000?
For estates worth more than $50,000
If there ARE legal beneficiary: The Public Trustee's Office cannot help with large estates. You must approach a lawyer for assistance.
If there are NO legal beneficiary (Bona Vacantia): Follow detailed instructions at Ministry of Law | How to make an equitable or moral claim on an estate that is > $50,000 without immovable property?

questions.title: Can I make an equitable or moral claim on a Muslim estate with no entitled next-of-kin?
questions.text:
No, you cannot make an equitable or moral claim on a Muslim estate. The law specifically excludes Muslim estates from this type of claim.
Why you cannot make a claim
The law excludes Muslim estates: Section 27(6) of the Civil Law Act 1956 specifically states that equitable or moral claims cannot be made on Muslim estates.
Different inheritance system: Muslim estates follow Islamic inheritance laws, which are different from civil inheritance laws.
What happens to Muslim estates with no entitled beneficiary
The Deceased’s estate goes to Baitulmal which is managed by Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS) in Singapore.
If you have questions about a Muslim estate with no entitled beneficiary, visit MUIS: Contact us | Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura

questions.title: How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate that is ≤ $50,000?
questions.text:
Upon meeting the eligibility conditions set out in the question "When can the Public Trustee administer on a bona vacantia estate?" and adhering to the prescribed waiting period of at least 6 months, please submit the following documents to the Public Trustee via https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw:
a) Death Certificate of the Deceased
i) If the cause of death was unnatural, provide a copy of the coroner's inquiry and findings (if any).
b) A Statutory Declaration from you stating the following:
i) Your relationship with the deceased.
ii) Whether you are aware of any entitled relatives and whether the deceased had died intestate.
iii) Whether you are aware of any prior petition of administration being filed.
iv) The basis of your equitable or moral claim on the estate (with the supporting grounds – see question on "What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?").
v) Your estimate of the value of the estate, with a breakdown of the assets by their type and estimated value.
vi) Whether there are any other potential claimants (e.g. other adopted children) and whether the potential claimants have disclaimed their share and interest in the estate.
vii) Any other information which will support your claim.
c) Statutory Declarations from other interested persons (e.g. other adopted children) stating the following:
i) Their relationship with the deceased.
ii) Whether they are renouncing their claims to the estate.
d) Documents supporting your equitable or moral claim (e.g. receipts showing proof that you have incurred expenses for the benefit of the deceased).
e) Full details of the deceased's estate (i.e. assets and valuation with documentary evidence).
[*Due to a conflict of interests, we are unable to assist you or the other interested persons in drafting the Statutory Declarations. You may either a) draft the Statutory Declaration on your own and our Commissioners for Oaths can assist in the swearing / affirmation of the Statutory Declarations. A copy of the Statutory Declaration is available at pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/Claims_against_BV_Estate_Page/Template_StatutoryDeclaration.pdfor b) obtain the Statutory Declaration from a law firm.]

questions.title: How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate with immovable property?
questions.text:
You will have to engage a lawyer to assist in your claim. You will have to adhere to the prescribed waiting period of at least 3 years. Your lawyer will have to take out the advertisements in a major English-language newspaper and a major vernacular newspaper for the next-of-kin of the deceased (a sample of the advertisement is at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/SampleAdvertisement.pdf) and to conduct probate searches.
Please submit the following documents to the Public Trustee via https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw:
a) Death Certificate of the Deceased
i. If the cause of death was unnatural, provide a copy of the coroner's inquiry and findings (if any)
b) Information stating the following:
i. Your relationship with the deceased
ii. Whether you are aware of any entitled relatives and whether the deceased had died intestate
iii. Whether you are aware of any prior petition of administration being filed;
iv. The basis of your equitable or moral claim on the estate
v. Your estimate of the value of the estate, with a breakdown of the assets by their type and estimated value
vi. Whether there are any other potential claimants (e.g. other adopted children) and whether the potential claimants have disclaimed their share and interest in the estate
vii. Any other information which will support your claim
c) Information of other interested persons (e.g. other adopted children) stating the following:
i. Their relationship with the deceased
ii. Whether they are renouncing their claims to the estate
d) Documents supporting your equitable or moral claim (e.g. receipts showing proof that you have incurred expenses for the benefit of the deceased)
e) Full details of the deceased's estate (i.e. assets and valuation with documentary evidence)
f) The details of the property, in particular, who is occupying the flat and the person paying the conservancy or other relevant charges.
g) Results of search for caveats on the property with SLA.
h) A Certificate / letter from the Commissioner of Estate Duties on any estate duty payable for the deceased (Applicable for deaths before 15 Feb 2008).
i) A copy of newspaper advertisements and the probate search results

questions.title: What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
What are the assets of the Deceased against which I can make an equitable or moral claim?
questions.text:
You can make an equitable or moral claim against all the assets of the Deceased if they have no surviving beneficiary who can legally inherit.
To know more about Bona Vacantia you may visit the link: Ministry of Law | What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
What assets can you claim against
All assets are included, example:
Bank accounts and savings
Property (HDB flats, private property, land)
Investments (shares, bonds, insurance policies)
Un-nominated CPF moneys (CPF savings with no named beneficiary)
Personal belongings (jewelry, vehicles, furniture)
Requirement
No surviving beneficiary. You must prove that the Deceased has no surviving beneficiary who can legally inherit under the Intestate Succession Act 1967 (the law that decides who inherits when someone passed away without a will).
Whether the claim will succeed against all or only part of the assets will depend on the facts and circumstances.
For the detailed step-by-step instructions on submitting your claim, if the estate is than ≤$50,000 visit:Ministry of Law | How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate that is ≤ $50,000?
For detailed step-by-step instructions on submitting your claim, if the estate is than >$50,000 visit:Ministry of Law | How to make an equitable or moral claim on an estate that is > $50,000 without immovable property?
Important things to know
No guarantee of success: Meeting the requirements does not guarantee you will receive moneys. Each case is assessed individually.

questions.title: When can I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
questions.text:
You can make a claim only after the expiry of the waiting period stated in the table below.
Type of Estate
Waiting Period
Estate not involving immovable property e.g. bank monies, CPF monies
Not less than 6 months from the date of death
Estate involving immovable property e.g. HDB flat, landed property, condominiums
Not less than 3 years from the date of death

questions.title: What should other potential claimants do if they don't want to claim the bona vacantia estate?
questions.text: Other potential claimants must sign a statutory declaration to affirm that they are not the interested parties in the bona vacantia estate.

questions.title: How to make an equitable or moral claim on an estate that is > $50,000 without immovable property?
questions.text:
You will have to engage a lawyer to assist in your claim. You will have to adhere to the prescribed waiting period of at least 6 months. Your lawyer will have to take out the advertisements in a major English-language newspaper and a major vernacular newspaper for the next-of-kin of the deceased (a copy of the advertisement can be found at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/SampleAdvertisement.pdf) and to conduct probate searches.
Please submit the following documents to the Public Trustee via https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw:
a) Death Certificate of the Deceased
i. If the cause of death was unnatural, provide a copy of the coroner's inquiry and findings (if any)
b) Information stating the following:
i. Your relationship with the deceased
ii. Whether you are aware of any entitled relatives and whether the deceased had died intestate
iii. Whether you are aware of any prior petition of administration being filed;
iv. The basis of your equitable or moral claim on the estate
v. Your estimate of the value of the estate, with a breakdown of the assets by their type and estimated value
vi. Whether there are any other potential claimants (e.g. other adopted children) and whether the potential claimants have disclaimed their share and interest in the estate
vii. Any other information which will support your claim
c) Information of other interested persons (e.g. other adopted children) stating the following:
i. Their relationship with the deceased
ii. Whether they are renouncing their claims to the estate
d) Documents supporting your equitable or moral claim (e.g. receipts showing proof that you have incurred expenses for the benefit of the deceased)
e) Full details of the deceased's estate (i.e. assets and valuation with documentary evidence)
f) A copy of newspaper advertisements and the probate search results

questions.title: Can I make an equitable or moral claim on the bona vacantia estate if the Deceased has entitled beneficiary, but they do not wish to deal with nor claim the estate?
questions.text:
No, you cannot make an equitable or moral claim against the estate because the Deceased has next of kin who are legally entitled to inherit. An estate only becomes bona vacantia when the Deceased has no living beneficiary and no valid will naming beneficiary.
To know more about Bona Vacantia, you may visit the link: Ministry of Law | What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
What happens if beneficiary does not claim the estate
The property and moneys still legally belong to the entitled beneficiary.
What you can do instead
If you believe you deserve something from the estate:
Option 1: Get legal advice and speak to a lawyer about your situation. They can explain if you have any legal options.
Option 2: Contact the entitled beneficiary and try to speak directly with him / her.
Important notes
No guarantee of success: Even in true bona vacantia cases, equitable or moral claims are not guaranteed to succeed.
Legal costs: Making any legal claim involves costs. Consider this carefully before proceeding.

questions.title: Is there a time limit for making an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
questions.text:
No, there is no time limit for making a Bona Vacantia claim where the Deceased has no surviving beneficiary who can legally inherit. You can make your claim at any time, even many years after the person passed away.
Important things to consider about timing
Earlier claims may be easier to process. Why sooner is better:
Documents are easier to find when they are more recent
Bank records and financial information are more accessible
How to make your claim
For estates worth $50,000 or less: Follow the detailed instruction at: Ministry of Law | How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate that is ≤ $50,000?
For estates worth more than $50,000: Follow the detailed instructions at Ministry of Law | How to make an equitable or moral claim on an estate that is > $50,000 without immovable property?

questions.title: What happens if the actual size of bona vacantia estate turns larger than declared?
questions.text:
Bona Vacantia estate means an estate where the Deceased has no surviving family members who can legally inherit.
If the estate value turns out to be more than $50,000:
The Public Trustee’s Office will require you to follow a different process with additional documents.
What you need to do:
Submit additional documents as specified in: Ministry of Law | How to make an equitable or moral claim on an estate that is > $50,000 without immovable property?
Expect processing delays while your case is reassessed under the new requirements
How to avoid delays
Provide accurate estimates from the start
Why accuracy matters: Providing an accurate estimate of the estate value helps ensure your claim is processed under the correct requirements from the beginning.
How to estimate accurately:
Check the current market values for investments and shares
Include all assets even if you are unsure of the exact values
Round up rather than down if you are uncertain
Better to overestimate than underestimate to avoid reclassification delays.
What to do if your estate value increases
If you discover additional assets after submitting your claim:
1. Notify the Public Trustee’s Office immediately at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
2. Provide and submit details of the newly discovered assets with supporting documentation
3. Be prepared for your case to be reclassified if the total exceeds $50,000
Remember: It's better to report additional assets promptly than to have them discovered later, which could cause more significant delays.

questions.title: I am not related to the Deceased, but I did help the Deceased in later years by running errands and generally looking after the Deceased. Can I be reimbursed for this?
questions.text:
It depends on whether the Deceased has any beneficiary or a will.
If the Deceased has beneficiary or a will
No, you cannot be reimbursed if the Deceased has:
Beneficiary who are legally entitled to inherit
A valid will naming beneficiary
Why: The estate legally belongs to these entitled people, even if they choose not to claim it immediately.
If the Deceased has no beneficiary or will (bona vacantia)
You may be able to get reimbursement if the Deceased died with no beneficiary and no valid will. This is called a bona vacantia estate (which means "ownerless goods").
To know more about Bona Vacantia you may visit the link: Ministry of Law | What is an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
How it works and claim
The Public Trustee's Office will assess each claim individually on a case-by-case basis. For detailed step-by-step instructions on submitting your claim, visit Ministry of Law | How do I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate that is ≤ $50,000?
When you can make a claim
For detailed information about the waiting period, visit: Ministry of Law | When can I make an equitable or moral claim on a bona vacantia estate?
Important things to know
No guarantee of success, each claim is assessed individually. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee you will receive reimbursement.

questions.title: What is the process after Minister for Law has approved equitable or moral claim against a bona vacantia estate?
questions.text:
For cases where the Public Trustee acts as the administrator of the estate, we will put up a warrant for the Minister for Law to sign once the estate administration is completed. The ministerial warrant will transfer the estate or that part of the estate which is allowed to the claimant.
For estates which we cannot administer due to reasons stated in "What are the situations where the Public Trustee cannot act?", you will have to engage a lawyer to apply for Letters of Administration so that you can administer the estate on your own. We will provide you with a renunciation letter renouncing the Government's right to apply for Letters of Administration. Once the estate administration is completed, you will need to inform the Public Trustee and we will put up a warrant for the Minister for Law to transfer the rights to the claimant.

questions.title: How can I claim for reimbursement of funeral expenses out of the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies?
questions.text:
You can indicate the amount of funeral expenses which you would like to claim from the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies in the online application form.
Generally, claims of up to $6,000 are allowable.
Only a beneficiary is eligible to claim for reimbursement of funeral expenses from the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies.
The claimant will have to submit the following supporting documents:
a) Other identification documents (for non-Singaporeans) of claimant and applicant who submitted the Online Application Form.
b) Death Certificate (if the Deceased passed away outside Singapore)
c) If claimant is:
i) Spouse of deceased – Marriage Certificate; or
ii) Child of deceased – Birth Certificate of Child and Marriage Certificate of parents; or
iii) Parent of deceased – Birth Certificate of deceased and Marriage Certificate of parents; or
iv) Sibling of deceased – Birth Certificate of deceased, Birth Certificate of sibling and Marriage Certificate and Death Certificates of deceased's parents.
d) "Declaration Form (CPF monies) for funeral expenses". You may obtain a copy of the form via https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/forms/ (deceased CPF / Estate monies > Forms).
e) Payment will be made to the claimant via PayNow (which has to be registered with your NRIC) or Direct Credit to the bank account. To receive payment via GIRO to a non-DBS / non-POSB bank account, please submit a copy of the beneficiary’s bank passbook or statement showing the bank account and holder’s name. No documents required for payment via PayNow.
f) Relevant receipts incurred for Funeral Expenses.

questions.title: Who can claim for the un-nominated CPF monies as reimbursement of funeral expenses?
questions.text:
If the deceased person did not make a valid nomination for his / her CPF monies, the monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee for distribution.
The rules of distribution for non-Muslim deceased domiciled in Singapore can be found at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/information-for-next-of-kin-cpf-monies/.
If the deceased person was a Muslim, the Public Trustee will distribute the monies in accordance with s112 of the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966 according to the school of the Muslim law. The Certificate of Inheritance issued by the Syariah Court will list down the beneficiaries and their share of inheritance.

questions.title: What do I need to do for the CPF monies of my loved one to be distributed to me?
questions.text:
You will need to make an online application at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg so that the Public Trustee can distribute the monies.
You will need to have your Singpass ready in order to access the online application form. You may apply for your Singpass at https://go.gov.sg/ptologin if you do not have one.

questions.title: CPF Board has notified me that the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee but a check with the Public Trustee reveals that there are no CPF monies in the case account.
questions.text:
Upon receiving notification of the death of the CPF member, the CPF Board typically requires 17 working days to transfer the moneys to the Public Trustee.
You will only be able to submit an online application for the administration of the Deceased’s un-nominated CPF moneys after we have received the CPF moneys from the CPF Board.
Once we have received the moneys from the CPF Board, we will write to the person who had notified the CPF Board of the death of the CPF member or his next of kin, to make an online application to us to distribute the un-nominated CPF moneys.

questions.title: What happens to the Deceased’s un-nominated Central Provident Fund (“CPF”) moneys
questions.text:
When a CPF member passed away without nominating anyone to receive his / her CPF moneys, the CPF Board will transfer these moneys to the Public Trustee for distribution to the rightful beneficiary.
Step 1: CPF Board processes the payment after the death
Upon being notified of the death, CPF Board takes around 17 working days to transfer the moneys to the Public Trustee.
Step 2: Public Trustee contacts the informant / next of kin
Public Trustee will write to:
The person who informed CPF Board about the death, and/or
The Deceased's next of kin
Step 3: Next of kin / friends on behalf of the next of kin makes an online application
The next of kin can then apply online for the Public Trustee to distribute the moneys.
When to apply:
Only after the Public Trustee has received the moneys from CPF Board.
How to apply:
Go to https://go.gov.sg/pto and select "Administration of CPF / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA Moneys"
You will need to have your Singpass ready in order to access our online application form. You may apply for your Singpass at https://www.singpass.gov.sg if you do not have one.
If you are ineligible to apply for a Singpass, you may apply for a login ID and password through our website: https://go.gov.sg/pto.
Examples of documents that may be required:
Documents about the Deceased:
Birth certificate
Marriage certificate
Divorce papers (i.e., decree nisi absolute) if the person was divorced
Documents about the beneficiary (person receiving moneys):
Birth certificate
Identity Card
Death certificate (if the beneficiary also passed away)
For Muslim families only:
· Certificate of inheritance
Note: The type of documents required varies based on who the beneficiary is and the period/country where those documents were issued. A case administrator will get in touch with you if there are any missing documents required.
For detailed information, visit: https://go.gov.sg/cpf-estate.

questions.title: When will the CPF monies be paid to me?
questions.text: As a general rule, we will distribute the monies within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation from the beneficiaries.

questions.title: How would the Public Trustee distribute the CPF monies of a non-Muslim?
questions.text:
If the person who died was not a Muslim, we will distribute the CPF monies in line with the Intestate Succession Act 1967. The Act states that the movable property (for example, monies in a bank account) will be distributed according to the law of the country in which the person was domiciled at the time of his death. When we refer to where the person was domiciled, we meant where they intended their permanent home to be. It does not refer to their nationality or address.
If the person who died was domiciled in Singapore at the time of his / her death, we will distribute the CPF monies in line with the rule of distribution under the Intestate Succession Act 1967. Please see information in https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/AnnexB_NonMuslims_Oct20.pdf.

questions.title: What are the fees charged by the Public Trustee for the distribution of un-nominated CPF monies?
questions.text:
The fees charged for distributing the CPF monies under the Public Trustee (Fees) Rules 2010 are:
Amount of CPF Monies
Charge
For the first $1,000
2.400%
For the next $9,000
1.500%

0.750%

0.300%
The fees include GST and cannot be waived. A minimum fee of $15 is chargeable.

questions.title: How do I know if my loved one has any CPF monies and if they had made a valid nomination?
questions.text:
The monies from the CPF Board of a person who has died will be distributed in line with the nomination they made during their lifetime.
You will need to check with the CPF Board whether the person had made a valid nomination for their CPF monies. If they had, the CPF Board will pay the monies direct to the nominee if they are above 18 years old.
If there is no valid nomination, the CPF Board will send the un-nominated CPF monies to the Public Trustee, as required by law.
The CPF Board will also send to the Public Trustee the nominated CPF monies of a person under 18 years old (unless she is a widow).

questions.title: The Deceased had nominated his CPF moneys to a person (i.e. nominee) who has passed on. What should I do?
questions.text:
Nominated CPF Moneys
For CPF moneys nominated in favour of a person ("the nominee") who passed away, the moneys will form part of the estate of this deceased nominee. If you are a next of kin of the nominee, you may apply to the Public Trustee for the administration of the deceased nominee’s estate if his / her estate is below $50,000.
If the deceased’s nominee’s estate is more than $50,000
If the deceased nominee's estate is more than $50,000, you will need to apply to court for Letters of Administration or Grant of Probate to deal with the nominee's estate, including the CPF moneys payable to the nominee. You will need to engage the services of a lawyer or apply for legal aid to do this.
Legal Aid
If you qualify for legal aid, you may apply to the Legal Aid Bureau for assistance in obtaining Letters of Administration. If you do not qualify for legal aid, you will need to hire a lawyer.
Online Application
You may make an online application via our e-services at https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: What fees charge for holding in trust nominated CPF monies for a minor?
questions.text:
The fees charged for holding nominated CPF monies in trust for a minor under the Public Trustee (Fees) Rules 2010 are:
Amount of CPF monies
Charge
For the first $1,000
2.400%
For the next $9,000
1.500%

0.750%
For the next $250,000
0.450%
For amounts over $500,000
0.300%
These are one-time fees, which we will take from the nominated CPF monies. The fees include GST and cannot be waived. A minimum fee of $15 is chargeable.
The monies held in trust for the minor is invested by the Public Trustee according to law. The investment earns interest for the minor from year to year. Whenever interest is to be paid to the minor, a fee is imposed on the amount of the interest. The net interest amount (less the fee) is paid into the minor's trust fund. The fees charged on the interest under the Public Trustee (Fees) Rules 2010 are:

The fees include GST and cannot be waived.

questions.title: How do I make or change a CPF nomination?
What happens to the CPF monies of a deceased CPF member?
questions.text:
The CPF monies of a deceased will be distributed according to the nomination they made during their lifetime. You will need to check with the CPF Board on whether the deceased had made a valid nomination for his / her CPF monies. If there is a nomination, the CPF Board will pay the monies directly to the nominees (if they are older than 18 years old). Otherwise, the CPF Board will forward the deceased's CPF monies to the Public Trustee to hold in trust if the nominee is below 18 years old (unless she is a widow).
If the deceased person did not make a valid nomination, the CPF Board will send the deceased's CPF monies to the Public Trustee for distribution, under the law. The un-nominated CPF monies paid to the Public Trustee will be distributed according to the Intestate Succession Act 1967 for non-Muslims. Un-nominated CPF monies belonging to Muslim CPF members will be distributed according to the Administration of the Muslim Law Act 1966.
For distribution of the un-nominated CPF monies, you will need to make an online application via https://go.gov.sg/pto . You will only be able to submit an online application after the un-nominated CPF monies are remitted to the Public Trustee. Once the un-nominated CPF monies are received by the Public Trustee, a letter will be sent to the person who has notified the CPF Board of the death and/or the deceased person's next-of-kin next-of-kin.
If you have submitted an online application and has not receive any update after a month from the application, you may submit an online enquiry form at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/ or call us at 1800 225 5529* to check on the status.
*When calling the MinLaw Enquiry Line using the 1800 2255 529, please note that airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones

questions.title: How would the Public Trustee distribute the CPF monies of a Muslim?
questions.text:
If the person who died was a Muslim, the Public Trustee will distribute the un-nominated CPF monies in accordance s112 of the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966.
The Application for Inheritance Certificate issued by Syariah Court will list down the beneficiaries and their share of inheritance

questions.title: What is the maximum value of an estate that Public Trustee can administer?
questions.text: The maximum value of an estate that Public Trustee can administer is $50,000 in value (excluding CPF monies).

questions.title: What are the criteria and fees charged for estate administration?
questions.text:
The Public Trustee's Office assists to administer the Deceased's assets (which means the Deceased’s moneys, property, and assets) and distributes them to the beneficiary in accordance with the intestacy law.
This service is for families who need help managing a Deceased's estate where the total value is $50,000 or less.
The Public Trustee cannot assist in certain situations: What are the situations where the Public Trustee cannot act?”.
Administration fees
The Public Trustee's Office charges fees to administer a Deceased’s estate.
Value of Estate
Charge
For the first $5,000
6.50%
For the next $2,000
6.00%
For the next $3,000
4.25%
For the next $10,000
2.75%
For the next $30,000
2.25%
Fee examples
Example 1: Estate worth $3,000
Fee: $3,000 × 6.50% = $195
Beneficiary receives: $3,000 - $195 = $2,805
Example 2: Estate worth $10,000
First $5,000: $5,000 × 6.50% = $325
Next $2,000: $2,000 × 6.00% = $120
Next $3,000: $3,000 × 4.25% = $127.50
Total fee: $572.50
Beneficiary receives: $10,000 - $572.50 = $9,427.50
Important fee information
Minimum fee: $15 (even for very small estates)
GST included: All fees already include GST
Cannot be waived: Fees are set by law and cannot be waived
Deducted automatically: Fees are collected from the estate moneys before distribution. For transfer of assets, the fees are collected before any transfer of the asset
What to do next
To apply for estate administration:
Visit our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto
Click on “Deceased’s estate other than un-nominated CPF moneys / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA”
Log in with your Singpass
Need help with the steps? Download the step-by-step guide.
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: When will the estate monies be paid out?
questions.text: As a general rule, the monies will be distributed within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation or the date of receipt of the deceased's monies, whichever is later.

questions.title: Will the Public Trustee be able to administer an estate with a Grant of Probate?
questions.text: If a Grant of Probate has been extracted, the Public Trustee will not be able to assist in the administration of the estate. Please engage a lawyer to assist in the matter.

questions.title: How would the Public Trustee distribute the estate of a Muslim?
questions.text:
If the person who died was a Muslim, the estate will be distributed in accordance with s112 of the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966.
The Application for Inheritance Certificate issued by Syariah Court will list down the beneficiaries and their share of inheritance.

questions.title: How long does the Public Trustee take to administer a deceased's estate?
questions.text: The Public Trustee will take about 1 - 6 months to administer a case, depending on the assets to be administered after receiving the completed application form and the required documents.

questions.title: What are the documents to be submitted to the Public Trustee?
questions.text:
Annexes A (for Muslims) and B (for non-Muslims) (available at at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/information/) set out the list of required documents. For a reimbursement of funeral expenses from the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies / Estate, Annex C (available at https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/deceased-cpf-estate-monies/information/) sets out the list of required documents.
The required documents are:
a) Deceased’s Information (or other identification document, for non-Singaporeans)
i) Birth Certificate (if the Deceased did not have any child, or was a Muslim, or was domiciled in Malaysia)
ii) Death Certificate (if the Deceased passed away outside Singapore)
iii) Certificate of Inheritance (if the Deceased was a Muslim)
b) Documents evidencing the Deceased’s relations, such as the immediate family
i) Identification Documents (for non-Singaporeans)
ii) Birth Certificate
iii) Death Certificate (if the relation has passed away)
iv) Marriage Certificate (where applicable)
v) Court order for the dissolution of marriage or decree nisi absolute (where applicable)
c) If the deceased was domiciled outside of Singapore and Malaysia, please also submit:
i) Intestacy law of the country of domicile
ii) Legal opinion on how the Deceased’s estate should be distributed in accordance with the relevant country’s intestacy law
d) To receive payment via GIRO to a non-DBS / non-POSB bank account, please submit a copy of the beneficiary’s bank passbook or statement showing the bank account and holder’s name (No documents required for payment via PayNow)
e) Supporting documents for the Assets which you require the Public Trustee’s assistance to administer
You will be assigned a case officer after you have submitted your online application. Please inform your case officer if you do not possess some of the required documents. Your case officer will advise you on what to do after you have submitted your online application.

questions.title: What is the meaning of tenants in common?
questions.text: When a property is owned under tenants in common, the deceased's share does not automatically pass on to the surviving owner(s). The deceased's share is distributed according to the terms of the will. Where there is no will, the deceased's share will be distributed according to intestacy laws.

questions.title: How are the monies from a deceased's estate administered by the Public Trustee distributed?
questions.text: The Public Trustee will distribute the monies in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act 1967 for non-Muslims and the Inheritance Certificate from Syariah Court for Muslims.

questions.title: Public Trustee's assistance in resealing Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate from overseas?
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not assist in resealing in the Singapore Courts for Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that were obtained overseas. You will have to engage a Singapore lawyer to assist you.
You can search for a Singapore law practice or lawyer using the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's online search function at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/. Please note that the search results are based on information provided by law practices and lawyers. The Ministry of Law does not make any warranty or representation as to their accuracy, completeness or reliability.

questions.title: What happens after I have submitted an online application for the administration of a deceased's estate?
questions.text: A case administrator will be assigned to handle your application. If any further documents are needed, the case administrator will write to you for those documents. Payments will be made to the beneficiaries within 4 weeks from the date when all the documents are in order / the monies are received whichever is later.

questions.title: Can the Public Trustee pay outstanding credit card debts from a deceased's estate?
questions.text: The Public Trustee is unable to administer a deceased's estate if the deceased person has outstanding debts.

questions.title: Domiciled overseas for non-Muslim.
questions.text: A legal opinion must be obtained from a solicitor who practices law in the country of domicile. The legal opinion should set out the distribution of the estate to the lawful beneficiaries and the proportion each heir is entitled to. The solicitor should provide his / her interpretation of the intestate law governing the distribution of estate, drawing reference to the relevant section of the Act. An English version of the Act should be submitted with the legal opinion.

questions.title: Who are the beneficiaries to claim the estate or unnominated CPF monies of a deceased (non-Muslim)?
questions.text: You may refer to the rules of distribution under the Intestate Succession Act 1967 (for non-Muslims). Please see information in https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/Information_Page/AnnexB_NonMuslims_Oct20.pdf.

questions.title: What are the realised assets by Public Trustee in the administration of deceased's estate?
How to claim the Deceased's bank account balances?
questions.text:
You will need to make an online application via https://go.gov.sg/pto and select "Deceased’s Assets other than Un-nominated CPF Moneys / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA" for the Public Trustee to administer the Deceased’s estate. Please note that you will be required to disclose information on the Deceased’s shares, bank savings account, death gratuity, insurance policies and vehicles owned (if any) in the online application.
You will need to have your Singpass ready in order to access our online application form. You may apply for your Singpass at https://www.singpass.gov.sg if you do not have one.
If you are ineligible to apply for a Singpass, you may apply for a login ID and password through our website: https://go.gov.sg/pto.
Bank account balance $5,000 or below
For your convenience and in order to save costs at your end, you may approach the bank directly to claim the Deceased’s bank moneys.
Bank account balance of more than $5,000 to $50,000
The Public Trustee’s Office may assist to administer such cases on a case-by-case basis.
Common types of documents required are:
Death Certificate of Deceased
Birth Certificate of Deceased
Marriage Certificate of Deceased
Decree Nisi Absolute (if the Deceased was divorced)
Birth Certificate of Beneficiary
Identity Card of Beneficiary
Death Certificate of Beneficiary (if Deceased)
Marriage Certificate of Deceased’s Parents
Death Certificate of Parent (if Deceased)
Certificate of Inheritance (For Muslims only)

questions.title: How are the Public Trustee's fees paid?
questions.text: Payment of fees to the Public Trustee's Office for administration of a deceased's estate must be made electronically through our e-services under "Payments for various services such as Amount Received for Administration and Fees". Payment can be made via Credit Card, Nets, or Paynow. The link to the e-payment is: https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: What are the situations where the Public Trustee cannot act?
How would the Public Trustee distribute the estate of a non-Muslim?
questions.text:
If the deceased was a non-Muslim, the estate will be distributed in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act 1967, which states that the distribution of any movable property (for example, monies in the bank account) will be regulated by the law of the country in which the person was domiciled at the time of their death.
The place of domicile refers to the place where the deceased intended his permanent home to be. It does not refer to his nationality or residence.
If the person who died was domiciled in Singapore at the time of his / her death, the estate will be distributed in accordance with the rules under the Intestate Succession Act 1967. Please see information in https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/AnnexB_NonMuslims_Oct20.pdf.

questions.title: What do I need to ensure before applying to the Public Trustee?
questions.text: You will need to ensure that the estate does not fall under one of the situations stated in the question "What are the situations where the Public Trustee cannot act?" where the Public Trustee cannot act.

questions.title: Does the Public Trustee deduct its fee before paying out the estate monies to the beneficiaries?
questions.text:
Yes, the administration fee, mandated by law, is deducted from the deceased's estate monies before the distribution is made.
The fees chargeable under the Public Trustee (Fees) Rules 2010 for the administration of estate are:
Value of Estate
Charge

6.50%
For the next $2,000
6.00%
For the next $3,000
4.25%
For the next $10,000
2.75%
For the next $30,000
2.25%
The fees include GST and cannot be waived. A minimum fee of $15 is chargeable.

questions.title: Can the Public Trustee tell me how much monies and property was left behind by the deceased?
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not provide the service of tracing a deceased person's assets.
The Public Trustee is able to assist with the administration of a deceased person's estate valued up to $50,000.

questions.title: Does the Public Trustee assist in the administration of a deceased's share in a HDB flat?
questions.text: On a case-by-case basis, the Public Trustee does administer a deceased's share in a HDB flat if it is of small value (≤ $50,000). You will first have to submit an online application at https://go.gov.sg/pto (Deceased's Assets other than Un-nominated CPF Monies / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA) for the Public Trustee to administer the deceased's estate so that we may consider your request.

questions.title: How do I know the interest rates earned for a minor's held-in-trust fund?
questions.text: The annual interest rates earned for the held in trust fund can be found in the Singapore Gazette.

questions.title: Can I get a reimbursement of extra expenses more than the minor's maintenance allowance?
questions.text:
We may reimburse you, out of the child's monies, for the expenses of the education and welfare of the child, if these are not covered by the maintenance allowance.
We consider each request on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: What happens to the monies held in trust by the Public Trustee for minors?
questions.text:
The monies held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments like fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee’s administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
Parent or legal guardian of the minor and minor can view the Statement of Accounts online through https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: What are the fees charged for the investment of monies held in trust for minors?
questions.text:
The monies held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments like fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee’s administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
You can view the Statement of Accounts online through https://go.gov.sg/pto.
What are the fees charged by the Public Trustee for the investment of monies held in trust?
The statutory fees charged by the Public Trustee on the amount of interest earned for the investment of monies held in trust are as follows:
Amount of Interest Earned
Charge
For the first $1,000
5.50%
For the next $1,000
4.50%

3.50%
For amounts in excess of $3,000
2.25%
The fees include GST and cannot be waived.

questions.title: Can I apply for maintenance allowance from the monies held in trust?
questions.text:
Under sections 68 and 70 of the Women's Charter 1961, it is the duty of the parent / guardian of a child to maintain or contribute to their maintenance if they cannot look after themselves.
If you are the parent / legal guardian of a child and you face financial difficulties in supporting the child, you may apply for a maintenance allowance out of the child's monies.
In deciding the amount of the maintenance allowance, the following will be considered:
a) Your income, property and other financial resources;
b) Your financial needs and responsibilities;
c) The financial needs and the age of the child; and
d) The way in which the child is being or is expected to be educated or trained.

questions.title: How will the maintenance allowance for be paid?
questions.text: The maintenance allowance will be credited into a joint savings account, maintained by the parent / legal guardian with the child, via GIRO every three months in January, April, July and October.

questions.title: Who can access the child's online Statement of Account?
questions.text:
The following persons can view the Statement of Account:
a) The parent or legal guardian of the beneficiary; or
b) The child (provided that he / she is eligible for a SingPass¹).
¹The minimum age to apply for a SingPass is 15 years.

questions.title: I will be turning 18 / 21 years old next month. How do I make a claim for the monies held in trust?
questions.text:
A notification letter will be sent 2 months before you attain age of majority at 18 / 21 with instructions on the steps and documents required to claim the monies. If you do not receive our notification letter before your birthday, please drop us a query at https://go.gov.sg/pto Contact Us @ OneMinLaw so that we may check and advise you accordingly.
You will receive the monies within 4 weeks after your birthday / the date of our receipt of your documents when you attain the age of majority, whichever is later.
Please note that if you do not claim your trust monies after you have attained your age of majority, the monies will be treated as unclaimed monies until such time when you come forward with documentary proof to claim the monies. Your trust monies will no longer be invested by the Public Trustee and no interest will be payable on the trust monies after you have attained your age of majority.

questions.title: What are the documents that I need to send to apply for a child's maintenance allowance?
questions.text:
You will be required to provide proof that you are not able to support the child (for example, your monthly payslips) and documents relating to the child's financial needs.
For us to make payment, you will also need to give us evidence of a joint savings account opened with the child. We will accept a copy of the bank statement with the joint bank account number with the account holders' names on it.

questions.title: If the child is below 21 years old will he / she be entitled?
questions.text:
The monies that is held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments such as fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee's administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
You can view the Statement of Accounts for the monies which were held in trust by the Public Trustee online through: https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have problems accessing the online Statement of Account?
questions.text:
If you cannot access your Statement of Account online, the Public Trustee's Office can help you resolve the issue.
How to contact us
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM
What information to provide
When you contact us, please include:
Screenshot of the error - Take a picture of your screen showing the exact error
Your details - Your full name and identity card number and email address
Deceased's identity card or child’s identity card or Case reference number
Your relationship - How you are related to the Deceased or child (parent, guardian, etc.)
What happens next
How you'll be notified: You will receive our reply through email.
What we'll do:
Review your case and the error message
Check your account access permissions
Provide step-by-step instructions to fix the problem
Try these steps first
Before contacting us, you can try:
Download the step-by-step guide to see if this helps
Clear your browser cache and cookies
Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)
Check if your Singpass is working by logging into other government services
Try accessing the service at a different time (system may be temporarily down)
If these steps do not work, then contact us using the above methods.

questions.title: Minor's CPF monies held in trust.
questions.text:
The Public Trustee will hold in trust, monies of minors who have yet to attain the age of majority.
The monies that is held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments such as fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee's administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
Statement of Accounts for the monies held in trust by the Public trustee can be viewed online through https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: How do I apply for a child's maintenance allowance?
questions.text:
You will need to make an online application for maintenance allowance via https://go.gov.sg/pto (select "Application for Maintenance Allowance").
You will also need to have your Singpass ready to access the online application form. You may apply for your Singpass at https://go.gov.sg/ptologin if you do not have one.

questions.title: How do I apply for reimbursement of a minor's extra expenses?
questions.text:
You will need to provide documents to your case officer showing proof of payment.
Common proof of payment documents are:
a) A letter of acceptance from the child's school showing the amount of school fees; and
b) Receipts showing proof of payment to the school.

questions.title: How do I view the minor's online Statement of Account?
questions.text:
Parent or legal guardian of the minor and minor will need to log on to our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto (select "Statement of Account") to be able to view the child's Statement of Account
You will need to have your SingPass of ready in order to access our eService. If you do not have a Singpass, you may obtain one at https://go.gov.sg/ptologin.

questions.title: What are the documents required to assess the adequacy of out of court compensation for motor accident?
How does the Public Trustee protect motor accident victims?
questions.text: In cases where the relevant amount exceeds $5,000, the lawyer for the accident victim is required to obtain the agreement of the Public Trustee for the Solicitor and Client costs and disbursements payable by the accident victim. The Public Trustee checks to ensure that these costs and disbursements are reasonable. If the accident victim is not represented by a lawyer, the Public Trustee will check to ensure that out of court compensation payment for the accident victim is adequate.

questions.title: When must a motor accident case be referred to the Public Trustee for an assessment?
What are the fees charged for the administration of a Motor Accident Compensation case?
questions.text:
The fees charged by the Public Trustee are as follows:
For a Judgement obtained / Settlement Agreement made on or after 1 August 2014:
Type of Fees
Amount¹
Fee for assessment of reasonableness of Solicitor-and-Client costs
$225.00
Fee for assessment of adequacy of compensation payment pursuant to a settlement agreement for an unrepresented victim
$300.00
¹Inclusive of GST

questions.title: Negotiation of solicitor and client costs.
questions.text: The plaintiff must refer to their representation or appointed counsel for information on the status updates.

questions.title: Who pays the fees charged to assess the adequacy of out of court settlement for motor accident victim?
questions.text: The insurer of the motor vehicle will make payment of the Public Trustee's fees together with the online application to seek the Public Trustee's agreement on the adequacy of the terms of the out of court settlement for the unrepresented victim.

questions.title: Court's direction on solicitor and client costs.
questions.text: The solicitor may seek the Court's assessment of the solicitor and client costs and the solicitor is not compelled to apply to nor inform the Public Trustee of such an application to the Court.

questions.title: How much solicitor and client costs will a motor accident victim need to pay their lawyers?
questions.text: Please speak with your solicitor who acted or will act on your behalf in respect of your motor accident compensation claim. Your solicitor will explain to you the solicitor and client costs he / she charges.

questions.title: What are the documents required when applying to Public Trustee to assess solicitor and client costs and disbursements for motor accident claims?
How do we pay the fees charged for the administration of motor accident compensation cases?
questions.text:
For a Judgment obtained / Settlement Agreement made on / or after 1 August 2014:
Payment of the fees must be made online by debit card, credit card or direct debit. The fees must be paid together with the submission of the online application to the Public Trustee.
Lawyers may recover these fees as disbursements.

questions.title: What is a Summary Judgment?
questions.text: A Summary Judgment is a process where a substantial claim results into a judgment without a full trial.

questions.title: What does subrogation mean?
questions.text: Subrogation refers to the substitution of one person or thing for another, so that the same rights and duties which are attached to the original person or thing is / are transferred to the substituted.

questions.title: What do special damages compensate?
questions.text: Special damage compensates the plaintiff for quantifiable monetary losses such as medical bills, the cost to repair and lost earnings.

questions.title: What are Solicitor-and-Client costs? What are Party-and-Party costs?
questions.text:
These are two different types of legal costs you may need to pay if you are involved in a motor accident case.
What Solicitor-and-Client costs mean
Solicitor-and-Client costs are the legal fees you pay to your own lawyer.
What this cover:
Your lawyer's time spent working on your case
Meetings and phone calls with you
Negotiation with the insurance company or in court
Preparing documents for court or to insurance company
What Party-and-Party costs mean
Party-and-Party costs are legal fees that one side pays to the other side in a court case.
What this covers:
Court filing fees
Other legal expenses related to the court case

questions.title: Who are "specified persons" in a motor accident?
Motor accident compensation case refer to the Public Trustee if the relevant amount is below $5,000.
questions.text: If the relevant amount does not exceed $5,000, there is no need to refer the case to the Public Trustee.

questions.title: What should be included in determination of relevant amount for motor accident compensation case?
questions.text:
In determining the relevant amount, only damages that is directly related to the injuries suffered by the motor accident victim should be taken into account.
Examples of items that should be included:
a) General Damages
b) Loss of earnings
c) Medical expenses
Examples of items that should NOT be included:
a) Property Damage
b) Cost of Vehicle Repair

questions.title: How will lawyers receive their costs payment and disbursements for motor accident compensation cases?
questions.text: Lawyers for a motor accident compensation case should liaise directly with the respective insurer(s) on their mode of payment.

questions.title: When will the lawyers receive the Public Trustee's agreement to the solicitor and client costs in motor accident cases?
questions.text: The Public Trustee will inform the lawyers of its views on the solicitor and client costs within 3 weeks from the date of receipt of the complete set of supporting documents or clarification from the lawyers.

questions.title: What is stay of proceedings?
questions.text: Stay of proceedings is suspension of proceedings in an action, which may be temporary until something requisite or ordered is done, or may be permanently, where proceeding would be improper.

questions.title: Who will pay the fees charged for the assessment of reasonableness of solicitor and client costs?
questions.text: Lawyers are required to pay the Public Trustee's fees when they make the online submission seeking the Public Trustee's agreement to the proposed solicitor and client costs and disbursements. Lawyers may recover these fees as disbursements.

questions.title: Will the Public Trustee's approval for solicitor and client costs be required for time-barred cases when there are no damages?
questions.text: The Public Trustee may assess solicitor and client costs in cases where there is no relevant amount and damages.

questions.title: Can a solicitor advance payment of solicitor and client costs and disbursements to himself before the Public Trustee's approval?
questions.text:
Unless costs are assessed in default of an agreement with the Public Trustee on the same, a solicitor must not receive or accept any payment of costs and disbursements until costs are agreed with the Public Trustee.
Until an agreement is reached, any payment received by the solicitor must be made into the client's account.

questions.title: Who needs to register as a regulated dealer?
questions.text:
Any person that:
(a) carries on a business of regulated dealing; or
(b) carries on business as an intermediary for regulated dealing, wholly or partly in Singapore.
Regulated dealing includes:
(a) manufacturing, selling, offering for sale, importing for sale, possessing for sale or purchasing for the purposes of resale any precious stone, precious metal or precious product ("PSPM");
(b) selling any instrument backed by PSPMs that entitles the holder to the PSPM or part of it (e.g. certificates or tokens); or
(c) acting as an intermediary for (a) or (b).
Under the PSPM Act, regulated dealers must apply for registration as a registered dealer.
A self-assessment questionnaire to help you ascertain whether you are a regulated dealer is at https://form.gov.sg/5cd3efbbd64f830010e00ea9. Please note that the contents of the questionnaire do not constitute legal advice. If you are uncertain, you should seek legal advice on whether you need to register.

questions.title: I am considering registering as a Class A dealer, but I have concerns about potential price fluctuations and future business changes. What happens if I register as a Class A dealer now and my product prices increase due to future market changes or if I want to deal in items priced at S$2,000 or more in the future? Do I need to apply for a new registration under Class B?
questions.text:
Class A dealers are only allowed to sell precious stones, precious metals and precious products up to S$2,000. While conducting business, if you find that your prices are going to exceed S$2,000, you can apply to amend your registration to Class B by paying a prorated registration fee as per Regulation 18 of the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Regulations.
To amend your registration from Class A to Class B, you will need to submit an amendment application via GoBusiness Dashboard.
The additional registration fees are payable through GoBusiness Dashboard using e-payment options. Cash is not accepted.
For the latest fees for registration and renewal, visit:
Registration: https://acd.mlaw.gov.sg/registration/
Renewal: https://acd.mlaw.gov.sg/renewal/

questions.title: I am a new applicant for registration. I intend to carry out a business of regulated dealings only via the online platforms. This business could be conducted via my own website and/or via a 3rd party platform/s. I may also plan to have a physical outlet for the business. How many "places of business" (i.e., outlets) do I need to register in my application?
questions.text:
If you plan to conduct the regulated dealings only via the online platform(s), you will need to register 1 place of business (i.e., outlet) in your application.
If you plan to conduct the regulated dealings via the on online platform(s) as well as via a physical retail store(s), you only need to register the physical retail store(s) and select the physical store address as the outlet address in your application.
There is no requirement to register an additional place of business for online platforms. This is regardless of how many online platforms you operate on.

questions.title: I suspect that a cash transaction that exceeds S$20,000 is related to criminal conduct. What reports do I need to submit?
questions.text:
If the cash transaction exceeds S$20,000, you must submit a Cash Transaction Report not later than 15 business days after the date on which the transaction is entered into.
If you have a reason to suspect that the cash of any amount is related to criminal conduct, you are required to submit a Suspicious Transaction Report.
* A "business day" is defined as a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday.
