questions.title: What are some examples of "cash equivalents" in the context of receiving payment from customers?
questions.text:
Cash equivalents refer to anything that is used as currency as a payment mode. This includes cash cheque or traveller's cheque, payment account that contains e-money, any physical or electronic form of vouchers, tokens, and other articles the redemption of which entitles the holder to receive any precious stone, precious metal or precious product up to the value stated on or recorded in or in respect of the voucher, token or other article.
As a general guide, a payment mode would be considered as a cash equivalent if it allows anonymity and the identity of the payer cannot be traced.
Some examples of a 'cash equivalent' include:
a) Cheques
Cash cheque
Traveller's cheque
b) Cards
Stored value cards
NETS FlashPay, EZ-Link cards, CashCards
c) Vouchers
As an example, vouchers may be issued by shopping malls or regulated dealers, and may be passed from one individual to another multiple times before it is used.
d) Payment account that contains e-money
As an example, virtual wallets may be used by providers such as Grabpay, Shopeepay, Lazada, YouTrip, Wise, EZ-link and contain electronic stored value.
topics: Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers
Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers / Regulatory Regime - CTR Filing / CDD matters

questions.title: I am a foreign incorporated business/ company/ individual. Do I need to register (e.g. I am the supplier of precious stones and precious metals to a regulated dealer in Singapore. I do not carry out sales in Singapore)?
questions.text:
Foreign dealers carrying on a business of regulated dealing, or business as an intermediary for regulated dealing, in Singapore on a transitory basis (i.e. for not more than a total of 90 days in a year) are exempted from the requirement to register under Part 2 of the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Act ("PSPM Act") and Section 19 of the PSPM Act.
However, foreign dealers are still required to comply with all other regulatory requirements in the PSPM Act and Regulations which include filing of Cash Transaction Reports for designated transactions exceeding S$20,000 received as payment in cash or cash equivalent and Suspicious Transaction Reports.
You may wish to refer to the PSPM Act and Regulations on http://www.go.gov.sg/acd for details of the aforesaid requirements.
topics: Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers
Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers / Regulatory Regime - CTR Filing / CDD matters

questions.title: A customer trades-in jewellery/gold bar/s or any other precious stone and precious metal ("PSPM"). The total cash received from the customer, for payment, is below the threshold of S$20,000. Is there a need to file a Cash Transaction Report ("CTR")?
questions.text:
If the cash received from the customer is below the threshold of the S$20,000 cash requirement for filing of CTR, there is no requirement to file a CTR.
For example, a regulated dealer sold PSPM worth S$25,000 and the customer makes partial payment for the transaction by trading in a PSPM worth S$13,000. The amount of cash received for the remaining payment is S$12,000. In such a case, there is no requirement to file a CTR.
A designated transaction refers to transaction where payment exceeding S$20,000 in value is received in cash or a cash equivalent. Regulated dealers are required to conduct customer due diligence before entering into a designated transaction and file a cash transaction report on that transaction.
topics: Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers
Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers / Regulatory Regime - CTR Filing / CDD matters

questions.title: Can I consolidate the submission of Cash Transaction Report ("CTR") (e.g. on a monthly basis)?
questions.text:
A regulated dealer should submit one CTR for each customer based on the total value of cash transactions with the customer in a single day.
For example, a customer made four cash purchases of gold as follows:
1 December: S$35,000
3 December: S$15,000
5 December: S$15,000 from Branch A and S$15,000 from Branch B
The regulated dealer should submit two separate CTRs:
One CTR for the transaction on 1 December
One CTR for the two transactions on 5 December (total sum exceeds S$20,000)
A CTR is not required for the transaction on 3 December as it did not exceed the cash threshold of S$20,000.
topics: Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers
Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers / Regulatory Regime - CTR Filing / CDD matters

questions.title: After submitting the Cash Transaction Report ("CTR"), can I still proceed to transact with my customer?

questions.title: As a precious stones and precious metals dealer, are there individuals and entities that I am prohibited from dealing with? Where can I find the relevant information / lists of such individuals and entities?
questions.text:
The list of prohibited individuals and entities can be found on:
1) Ministry of Home Affairs: Inter Ministerial Committee-Terrorist Designation ("IMC-TD") website for persons designated as terrorists (google "IMC-TD + MHA" for https://www.mha.gov.sg/inter-ministry-committee-terrorist-designation-(imc-td);
2) Monetary Authority of Singapore ("MAS") website for persons designated on relevant UN Sanction Lists (google "targeted financial sanctions + MAS" for http://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/anti-money-laundering/targeted-financial-sanctions/lists-of-designated-individuals-and-entities)
Please ensure that you are not dealing with prohibited individuals and entities.

questions.title: I am a wholesaler. Do I need to perform customer due diligence ("CDD") if I received payment in gold bar or scrap gold bar? Do I need to submit a Cash Transaction Report ("CTR") if the transaction involved payment in gold bar/scrap gold/gold jewellery?
questions.text:
All Regulated Dealers are required to perform CDD measures for transactions involving payments in gold bars (IPM or scrapped) exceeding S$20,000 in total value.
For example, you must perform CDD measures on a customer if customer pays for 1kg of gold chains sold at S$96,000 using 1 kg of gold bars (IPM/ scrapped gold bars valued at S$84,000) and S$12,000 in cash as payment.
You are not required to submit a CTR if the transaction involved payment in gold bar/scrap gold/gold jewellery, as it is not a designated transaction.
A designated transaction involves payment in cash and cash equivalent exceeding S$20,000 in total value.

questions.title: Who can I appoint as the Compliance Officer? How many Compliance Officers can I appoint?
questions.text:
You must appoint at least 1 Compliance Officer, an employee or officer in a management level of a regulated dealer who is responsible for ensuring that the regulated dealer complies with the regulatory requirements under the Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Act.
A regulated dealer can appoint other staff/employees to assist the appointed Compliance Officer as deemed fit.
A management level staff from your business can be appointed as a compliance officer. The compliance officer is responsible for handling all anti-money laundering, countering the financing of terrorism and countering proliferation financing compliance matters for your business.
You should therefore appoint an appropriate person who can be delegated the responsibility of ensuring that your business has proper Internal Policies, Procedures and Controls.

questions.title: I am unable to obtain all the identity of the individuals with senior management position of my corporate customer. Can I just proceed to transact with the corporate customer by obtaining and verifying the ACRA BizFile report only? What if customer refuses to provide his identifying information for customer due diligence?
questions.text:
All Regulated Dealers are required to identify and verify the identity of the customer by obtaining the required information as stipulated in the Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Act and Regulations from reliable and independent sources (e.g. ACRA BizFile report or certificate of incorporate or any other corporate documents from reliable and independent sources).
If you are unable to complete customer due diligence, you must not enter into a transaction with that customer and terminate any transaction entered into with that customer. Failure to comply is an offence that is punishable on conviction by a fine not exceeding S$100,000.
MinLaw has provided brochures to help regulated dealers explain their obligations to their customers at http://www.go.gov.sg/acd.
If the customer declines to provide his identifying information you should also consider whether to submit a Suspicious Transaction Report ("STR") to the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office. Provide a short description of the person, identifiers or any other particulars that you may have and any other documentation that will help us identify him.
A copy of the STR should be submitted to the Anti-Money Laundering/Countering Financing of Terrorism Division of the Ministry of Law (for regulated dealers).
topics: Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers
Precious Stones and Precious Metals Dealers / Regulatory Regime - Guidance

questions.title: Will the Registrar automatically cancel my registration if any of the circumstances in Regulation 21A of the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Regulations exist?
questions.text:
The registration might not be automatically cancelled even if the circumstances in Regulation 21A exist.
This is because the Registrar may consider the relevant facts, events or circumstances of each case when determining whether a dealer is carrying out regulated dealing.
This includes the reasons why and how the circumstances under Regulation 21A have come about before making a determination.

questions.title: Does the Personal Data Protection Act ("PDPA") allow regulated dealers to ask customers for their particulars?
questions.text:
The data protection provisions in the PDPA does not prohibit the collection, use or disclosure of personal data (including NRIC number) as long as it is required for compliance with the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing) Act ("PSPM Act") and Regulations.
However, regulated dealers are required to ensure that reasonable security arrangements are in place to protect personal data in their possession or under their control.
Other than for purposes of compliance with the Act and Regulations, the personal information obtained cannot be used or disclosed for other purposes (e.g. marketing) without the consent of the individual.
For guidance on how personal information should be obtained, handled and stored, you may wish to refer to the Personal Data Protection Commission's website at https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/.

questions.title: What is an example of a "precious product" under the updated definition of "precious product" as of 1 May 2024?
questions.text:
As of 1 May 2024, the updated definition of precious product includes jewellery, watch, apparel, accessory, ornament or other finished product containing precious stones and/or precious metal, that is priced above the prescribed value of S$20,000.
An example of such a precious product is watch containing gold and has net sales price above S$20,000, even when the value of the gold in the watch is less than 50% of the net sales price.

questions.title: I have submitted an application to cancel my registration. Do I need to submit the semi-annual return to the Registrar?

Reporting Period
Submission Period
1 January to 30 June
1 July to 31July
1 July to 31 December
1 January to 31 January
(of the following year)
The cancellation of registration does not affect your legal obligation to submit the semi-annual return for the current reporting period by the submission deadline.

questions.title: What are the Small Claims Tribunals?
questions.text:
Established in 1985 under the Small Claims Tribunals Act, the Small Claims Tribunals ("SCTs") were set up to provide an avenue for consumers to seek quick redress against errant merchants in a less formal and inexpensive forum where they self-represent themselves to file their claims.
The SCT resolve specific types of low-value disputes between consumers and suppliers in a quicker and less expensive way than if the same dispute went for a civil trial.
Common types of small claims include disputes that involve goods, services or residential tenancy agreements not exceeding 2 years. The claim limit is $20,000 (or $30,000 if there is a Memorandum of Consent (PDF, 91 KB) signed by both parties).
For more information, visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/file-small-claim.

questions.title: When will I receive an SMS reminder for my appointment?
questions.text:
You will receive an SMS whenever:
A new booking is confirmed
An appointment is cancelled
An appointment is rescheduled

questions.title: How many SMS reminders will I get before my appointment?
questions.text: You will receive reminders 30 days, 7 days, and 24 hours before your scheduled appointment.

questions.title: If I do not opt in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker, will I be subject to the same CPF contribution rate as before 1 January 2025?
questions.text:
The maximum CPF contribution rate for platform workers who do not opt in will remain at 8% to 10.5%, depending on their age and income. They will also only need to make MediSave contribution if they earn above $500 in a month from a platform.
Some platform workers may see a difference in CPF contribution rate due to changes in the way CPF contribution is computed and collected. Before 1 January 2025, platform workers’ earnings are aggregated across platforms and assessed annually when computing the applicable MediSave contribution. From 1 January 2025, platform operators will be making CPF contribution on a monthly basis and based on earnings on each platform.
CPF contribution rates are tiered based on income – a platform worker earning below $750 will have a lower CPF contribution rate. Overall, whether platform workers’ CPF contribution rate is lower or higher as compared to today depends on their individual circumstances. For example, if platform workers have multiple income streams from different platforms, and if their income for each platform is low, platform workers will be subject to the lower CPF contribution that is now applied on a per platform basis.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on traineeship allowance given to your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme if you are the host company?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on traineeship allowance for your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme so long as the trainee is not employed under a contract of service.
You and your trainee may enter into an employer-employee relationship at any time, including upon completion of the GRIT programme, in which case, CPF contributions would be payable on wages given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: Do I need a Yellow Fever (YF) Vaccination Certificate to enter Singapore?
questions.text:
To reduce the risk of importation and transmission of Yellow Fever (YF) in Singapore, all travellers (including Singapore residents) with travel history to countries with risk of YF transmission (regardless of area, city or region,) in the 6 days prior to arrival in Singapore, are required to have a valid International Certificate of Vaccination for YF and present it to the ICA officer upon arrival to Singapore.
A valid International Certificate of Vaccination for YF is also required for travellers who have transited in these countries for more than 12 hours.
The International Certificate of Vaccination for YF becomes valid 10 days after vaccination and has a lifetime validity for the person vaccinated. (e.g., if the YF vaccine was administered on 1 January 2021, the vaccination certificate is considered valid from 11 January 2021 onwards).
Please refer to the Communicable Diseases Agency website for more information on yellow fever.

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary who is illiterate, digitally unable or has medical condition(s) and does not have Singpass to check their eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement benefits?
questions.text:
To safeguard citizens’ confidentiality, beneficiaries must check what benefits they are eligible for on the govbenefits website using their Singpass. Citizens who are illiterate or unable to use the website may seek assistance at any ServiceSG centres or community centres. However, if the beneficiary has a medical condition and is unable to do so, you can help them check their eligibility for Government benefits if you are:
aged 21 and above; and
a next-of-kin or appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), or court-appointed Deputy of the beneficiary.
To assist the beneficiary in checking their eligibility for Government Benefits, you will need to provide the following supporting documents:
If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are a parent/guardian who is helping your child, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
birth certificate of your child; or legal document to verify the guardianship between the legal guardian and child;
documentary evidence stating your child’s medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
your child’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

bank book/statement reflecting that the account is held in trust for the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
Option 2: To update to a personal or joint bank account in the beneficiary’s name
If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). the beneficiary’s NRIC.

documentary evidence stating your child’s medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
your child’s NRIC.

Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.

questions.title: What happens to the Silver Support paid via GovCash if the beneficiary passes away?
questions.text: If the beneficiary passes away before fully using their GovCash, the remaining balance will be credited to their CPF Ordinary Account. This amount will form part of their CPF monies and will be distributed according to their CPF Nomination. If there is no CPF nomination, the CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution in accordance to the intestacy or Muslim inheritance laws.

questions.title: How do I view, save or download my Transaction History or my CPF contribution details, including records beyond 15 months?
questions.text:
You can access your CPF Transaction History, through CPF Mobile app or my cpf digital services.
CPF Transaction History provides a record of your CPF transactions which includes contributions, withdrawals, transfers, etc. for the latest 15 months. By default, your latest 3 months transactions are displayed.
You can customise your view using the filter option to:
1) Display your CPF contributions such as
Employment and Platform Contributions
Self-Employed Contributions
2) Display your latest transactions for
3 months
6 months
12 months
Custom range up to 15 months
To view and save your statement, please refer to this guide (PDF, 1.4MB). To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
For records beyond 15 months, you can refer to your Yearly Statement of Account, which covers up to the past 10 years.
Please note that we do not provide CPF statements beyond the past 10 years. It is your responsibility to carefully review your CPF statements and download your statements in a timely manner to ensure that you always have a copy for your own records.
If you do not have a Singpass and/or 2FA, please visit the Singpass website to obtain one.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How are Healthier SG vaccinations selected for inclusion under NAIS?
questions.text:
Healthier SG vaccinations listed under NAIS are selected based on recommendations by the Drug Advisory Committee and Expert Committee on Immunisation which takes into consideration public health needs, local disease burden, vaccine efficacy and safety and cost-effectiveness. If the vaccine effectively prevents vaccinated individuals from infection or minimises complications if infected and is found to be cost-effective for its intended target population, the vaccine will be considered for inclusion under the NAIS.
MOH, in consultation with the Expert Committee on Immunisation, also monitors newly registered vaccines or those in the development pipeline to assess their relevance for Singapore, taking reference from international guidelines.

questions.title: What are the common side effects for PCV20?
questions.text: The vaccine has been assessed to be safe for use. However, similar to other vaccines, individuals may experience common side effects which include injection site reactions (e.g., pain, redness, swelling), headache, body aches, fatigue and fever. While most side effects are mild or moderate and usually resolve within a few days, individuals should consult a doctor if the side effects persist or worsen.

questions.title: Will I need to verify my disability status every year to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text: No, verification of your disability status will be a one-time process. If you are a person with disability below 55 and are verified with MSF, we will automatically assess your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) at the beginning of each year. If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post at the beginning of each year. You can also check your eligibility via the Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I have just been verified as a person with disability. As my medical condition existed way earlier, do I also qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for my cash top-ups made in previous years?
questions.text:
The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) has been expanded to include verified Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55 who meet the eligibility criteria from 2026.
This does not change your MRSS eligibility in previous years. No back-payments will be made as newly eligible persons with disabilities below 55 would still be able to make cash top-ups and receive MRSS matching grants up to the same $20,000 lifetime limit as those who are currently eligible for MRSS. Cash top-ups made in the previous years would have enjoyed tax relief and continue to benefit from the stable interest rate in the Retirement or Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do I need to have my disability status verified before I can be assessed for eligibility under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
Whether you need to have your disability status verified for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility depends on your age and if you are already a verified person with disability with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).
Profile
What to do?
If you are 55 years old and above
No action required. You will automatically be assessed for MRSS eligibility every year even if your disability status is not verified with MSF.
If you are below 55 years old and have verified your disability status before 1 November of the current year
No action required. You will automatically be assessed annually for MRSS eligibility.
If you are below 55 years old and have not verified your disability status
You will need to have your disability status verified with MSF before 1 November of the current year to be assessed for MRSS eligibility annually from the following year.
For example, a member age below 55 who had verified his disability status with MSF before 1 November 2025 will have his MRSS eligibility automatically assessed annually from the following year (2026) onwards.
For more information on the disability verification process, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What is the submission deadline for the Disability Verification Form (DVF) to be included in the eligibility assessment for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) in the following year?
questions.text:
If you are below age 55, you will need to have your disability status verified with MSF before 1 November of the current year to be assessed for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility for the next year. For example, you will need to have your disability status verified before 1 November 2025 for CPFB to assess your eligibility for MRSS for 2026. Please allow sufficient time for the verification process. Refer to the Enabling Guide for information on the disability verification process and when you can expect your disability status to be verified following the submission of the Disability Verification Form (DVF).
If you are not verified in time, you will be assessed for MRSS in the subsequent year. If eligible, you can continue to receive a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $2,000/year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000 from the Government on cash top-ups received in your CPF Special Account (SA).
If you are above age 55, you do not need to have your disability status verified with MSF. Your MRSS eligibility will be assessed with the senior cohort.
Find out more on whether you need to verify your disability status to be assessed for MRSS eligibility.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: When will the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) be expanded to include Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) will be expanded to include verified persons with disabilities below age 55 who meet the other MRSS eligibility criteria such as Singapore Citizenship status, residing in Singapore, CPF balances, monthly income and Annual Value of their residential property.
Cash top-ups made in 2025 to the CPF Special Account of persons with disabilities under the age of 55 will not enjoy the matching grant but will continue to benefit from the stable interest rate.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do employers need to fill in ‘Date of Commencement’ and ‘Date of Cessation’ field(s) in the Form IR8A?
questions.text:
Employers will need to provide the date of commencement if the employee commenced employment in the year or before 1 Jan 1969. Fill in the ‘Date of Cessation’ if your employee ceased employment in the year.
To fill in the Form IR8A for 2025 (Year of Assessment 2026):
1. If employee joined on 1 Dec 1968 but did not cease employment, the employer should fill in ‘Date of Commencement’ as ‘01/12/1968’ and leave the ‘Date of Cessation’ as blank
2. If employee joined on 15 Jan 2025 and ceased employment on 20 Aug 2025, the employer should fill in the ‘Date of Commencement’ as ‘15/01/2025’ and ‘Date of Cessation as ‘20/08/2025’
3. If the employee joined on 25 Feb 2017 and ceased employment on 1 Nov 2025, the employer should leave the ‘Date of Commencement’ as blank and fill in the ‘Date of Cessation’ as ‘01/11/2025’
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Reporting Employee Earnings (IR8A, Appendix 8A, Appendix 8B)

questions.title: Must the employer complete the ‘Bank Salary is credited to’ field in the Form IR8A?
questions.text: If the employee's salary is credited to a bank account, employers will need to indicate the bank name (e.g., POSB). However, indicate as ‘Others’ if the salary payment was made in cash or cheque in the Form IR8A.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Reporting Employee Earnings (IR8A, Appendix 8A, Appendix 8B)

questions.title: How do employers determine the number of employees for compulsory AIS participation? (E.g. number of employees at the beginning of the year or end of the year)
questions.text:
In determining the number of employees for AIS participation, employers should include the total number of employees for the year (e.g. 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026 for YA 2027), including employees who left the organisation during the year. However, when submitting the employment income information, employers should exclude employees for whom tax clearance had been sought.
Employers identified by IRAS to join the AIS will receive a notification letter. Employers that fall within the gazette under S68(2) of the Income Tax Act (PDF, 204 KB) but have not received any notification for YA 2027 should come forward and register for AIS and submit the employees’ income information by 1 Mar 2027.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Join the Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income

questions.title: What is the maximum number of records I can enter in the Submit Employment Income Records digital service?
questions.text:
You can enter up to 200 records per submission.
If you have more than 200 records to submit, you can make more than one submission, with each submission limited to 200 records.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Submit employment income records

questions.title: If work was completed in 2024 but the AGM approving directors' fees is held in 2025, should the directors' fees be reported for YA 2025 or YA 2026?
questions.text:
Please report the director’s fees based on the approval date at the company’s AGM/EGM in that calendar year.
Example: Fees approved on 30 Jun 2025 should be reported in Form IR8A for the year ended 31 Dec 2025 (Year of Assessment 2026).
If multiple meetings approved the same year’s fees, use the date of the final approval meeting held that year.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Amend Submitted Records

questions.title: Can I submit the revision/amendment file using a different mode from the original file (e.g., to submit via myTax Portal under the ‘Submit Employment Income Records’ when the original file has been submitted via payroll software with API)?
questions.text: Yes, you may submit an amendment file using a different AIS mode.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Amend Submitted Records

questions.title: Why am I asked to attend Home Protection Scheme medical examination but not my co-owner?
questions.text: Each Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application is assessed individually. The medical examination will allow us to assess your eligibility for HPS coverage.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What is this volunteer and partner engagement about?
questions.text:
In line with the Singapore Together movement to encourage Singaporeans to partner the government in building a shared future, we are involving individuals like you, to share CPF information with members to support their retirement planning. Through a Community Paying it Forward movement, you can do good by helping others within your social circles to improve their understanding of CPF schemes and make informed decisions on the use of their CPF savings. Training will be provided to facilitate accurate sharing of CPF information.
If you are interested in joining this initiative, you can download our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app and register with us by tapping on “Sign up now”. It is available on both App Store and Google Play (search for keyword: CPFV).
You can also scan the QR code to download the app and register with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What are the roles and responsibilities of a CPF volunteer?
questions.text:
Unlike conventional volunteering, there is generally no upfront time commitment and CPF volunteers have the flexibility to choose when or how they would like to share CPF information with people around them. However, do take reference to our code of ethics, by being impartial and objective when sharing information about CPF and to keep yourself updated on CPF matters.
As the CPF Volunteering (CPFV) initiative grows, we are also expanding the opportunities in which volunteers can contribute their personal stories, skills etc. As a volunteer, you may participate in our outreach co-creation efforts, which could include serving as a guest speaker in CPF webinars, contributing to user testing sessions, joining focus group discussions, or collaborating on other initiatives to improve our services and communications. Active and interested volunteers can also submit ground-up co-creation requests via the CPFV app to organise community events and activities that help fellow CPF members improve their understanding of CPF schemes.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What does the CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app offer?
questions.text:
Our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) app serves as a one-stop platform for volunteers and partners of CPF Board to:
Register with us as a volunteer of CPF Board
Receive CPF updates and access onboarding and training resources on CPF
Network with other like-minded individuals
Be guided on how they can pay it forward through various opportunities to do good
View personal achievements and impact of one’s contributions
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: I am interested to register as a CPF volunteer. How do I sign up?
questions.text:
You can sign up with us as a CPF volunteer in a few easy steps:
1. Download the CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile application, available on both Apple App Store and Google Play Store. You can also scan the QR code to download the app and register.
Enter your mobile number to get started on registration
2. Complete the Sign-up form to be a volunteer:
Your orientation and training resources will be availed to you via our CPFV app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: I have previously signed up as a CPF volunteer via an online form. Do I need to sign up again?
questions.text:
You need to download and sign up via our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile application even though you had previously signed up via our online form. By doing so, you will be able to participate in the Community Paying it Forward movement with like-minded individuals, access CPF online resources on the go, experience a gamified journey, view your personal achievements and the impact of your contributions.
You can download our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app and tapping on “Sign up now”. It is available on both App Store and Google Play (search for keyword: CPFV).
You can also scan the QR code to download the app and register with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Is it necessary to input the referrer's details in the CPF online services?
questions.text:
We strongly encourage you to provide the referrer's details if someone has introduced you to our CPF schemes or services. This will allow us to express our gratitude to the person who has made a positive impact on you and our volunteering movement.
If your referrer has not registered with us as a volunteer, they can sign up by downloading our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app from the App Store or Google Play (search for keyword: CPFV) and tap on “Sign up now”.
They can also scan the QR code to download the app and register with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will the “Referrer Name” field affect my CPF application or request in any way?
questions.text: The “Referrer Name” field will not affect your application nor request.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: I received a recommendation for this e-service from a family member or friend, but I am uncertain if they have registered as a CPF volunteer. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can ask your family member or friend who recommended the e-service to you for their referrer’s details.
If they had not signed up to be a volunteer, you can encourage them to do so by downloading our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app from the App Store or Google Play (search for keyword: CPFV) and tapping on “Sign up now”.
You can also scan the QR code to download the app and register with us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I show my appreciation to the CPF Board staff who recommended this e-service to me?
questions.text: You may provide the referrer’s details of the staff in your application form. Alternatively, you can also express your appreciation for our CPF officer by submitting a compliment through our website. Simply visit cpf.gov.sg/writetous and select "Compliments/Feedback" from the drop-down list of options.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How does CPF Board appreciate volunteers under the Community Paying it Forward movement?
questions.text:
Through our CPF Volunteering (CPFV) mobile app, volunteers can enjoy a gamified experience and gauge the impact of their sharing through fun elements to understand how this act of “Paying it Forward” has helped members in their retirement planning. Volunteers can earn badges, titles and in-app points for completing tasks, missions and participating in CPFV events. The in-app points can be used to redeem physical rewards (such as exclusive CPFV merchandise) and digital accessories to customise their avatars.
We are deeply appreciative of these extraordinary individuals who have stepped forward to help fellow CPF members be better prepared for their retirement. Apart from an annual appreciation event, we are constantly looking out for ways to show appreciation to our active volunteers who have contributed to the movement.
To encourage our volunteers to do more in spreading kindness and spurring more Singaporeans to take actions to plan for their retirement, our volunteers are also entitled to CPFV seasonal event prizes and benefits from our corporate partners, such as Resorts World Sentosa, Shopee, ComfortDelGro Taxi, Ya Kun, Lazada, NTUC Income and MoneyOwl, an NTUC Social Enterprise.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will I be paid for my efforts as a CPF volunteer?
questions.text: In the spirit of the Community Paying it Forward movement, CPF volunteers are not paid when they do good by helping others within their social circles better understand CPF schemes and make informed decisions on the use of their CPF savings. Nevertheless, the CPF Board acknowledges the efforts of volunteers and show appreciation to them in many other ways, such as digital rewards, seasonal sponsored prizes and appreciation event.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How did the “Community Paying it Forward” movement come about?
questions.text:
This movement rides on a widely popular concept known as “Pay it Forward”. A simple way of explanation is that by helping three people, who in turn each help three more people and so on, we can help many more people collectively.
As CPF is an essential component in planning for our retirement, it is important for us to understand how we can maximise our CPF savings. Therefore, after benefitting from this information ourselves, we can also pay it forward by sharing it with others, so that they too, can make the most of what the CPF system has to offer.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Where can I find out more about this CPF Volunteering initiative?
questions.text:
To learn more about the purpose of CPF Volunteering initiative, watch why and how our volunteers have been paying it forward.
Alternatively, you can also read our infographic for more information on Community Paying it Forward.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What is a Self-Help Lobby Guide and how do I register to be one?
questions.text:
CPF Board has introduced the Self-Help Lobby and E-Xperience Space at the service centres for members to learn and conveniently access the Board’s digital services. The Self-Help Lobby is equipped with self-service kiosks where members can perform tasks such as making CPF withdrawals and updating of personal information independently. The E-Xperience workshops are held at Bishan Service Centre, Tampines Service Centre and Woodlands Service Centre to guide and empower members to effectively utilise CPF’s digital services and online tools.
The role of a Self-Help Lobby Guide is to assist members with their inquiries at the Self-Help Lobby and conduct the E-Xperience workshop. Volunteers who are keen in this role should download the CPFV mobile app and complete the E-Xperience Training topics (Beginner and Advanced) in the Learn Module.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How do I delete my account on the CPFV app?
questions.text:
You can delete your account on the CPFV app by following these steps:
1. Navigate to your account under your profile and tap on Delete Account.
2. Complete the exit feedback form.
3. Confirm that you would like to exit and delete your CPFV account. Note that account deletion is immediate and irreversible.
4. You will receive a confirmation that your CPFV account has been deleted successfully.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I request for a CPF volunteer's contact details after an event if I have further queries?
questions.text: Our volunteers are not allowed to share their contact details. If you have further queries, please contact us via our customer service channels.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What is the purpose of providing referrer's details in the CPF Online services?
questions.text:
The Community Paying it Forward movement was launched in April 2021 to encourage individuals to share useful CPF information with others. This will help members better understand CPF and make informed decisions on the use of their CPF savings.
To thank volunteers who have made a positive impact, we have introduced a “Referrer Name” field in selected CPF online services. If someone has shared a CPF scheme or service with you, please provide the referrer’s details, which can include the referrer’s name, email address, or mobile number registered under the CPFV mobile app. By doing so, we can extend our appreciation to these individuals and assess the effectiveness of this initiative.
It is important to note that inputting referrer's details will not affect your application nor request.
*List of selected online services that contain the referrer's details section:
Cash top ups and CPF transfer
Voluntary housing refund
CPF nomination
Plan my monthly payouts
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: If I discover any wrongdoing by a CPF volunteer, what action should I take?
questions.text:
We do not tolerate any wrongdoings by volunteers in their course of advocating for CPF. If you come across any wrongdoings, it is important that you report so that appropriate action can be taken.
By reporting the wrongdoing, you can help to ensure that our volunteers are held accountable for their actions and that steps are taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.
All reports should be made in good faith, without any personal agenda, or ulterior motive, and when there are reasonable grounds to suspect that an incident of wrongful practice has occurred.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What are the types of wrongful practices?
questions.text:
Examples of wrongful practices include, but not limited to the following:
Violation of CPFV’s code of ethics (PDF, 0.1MB),
Fraud or deliberately providing false or incorrect information,
Violation of intellectual property rights,
Financial and non-financial malpractices
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What information do I need to provide when I report a wrongdoing?
questions.text:
We have outlined the key information to provide when you report a wrongdoing by following the 4Es:
1. Elaboration of the wrongdoing: Describe the nature of the wrongdoing. Include when and where it occurred, who was involved, whether any money or assets are involved.
2. Evidence: Provide any evidence you may have, such as photographs and emails, that support your claims of wrongdoing.
3. Eyewitnesses: If there are witnesses to the wrongdoing, provide their names and contact information so that they can be contacted for further information.
4. Essential contacts and your identity: Providing your identity and contact information will allow us to verify your claims and follow up on any additional information if required. Reports made anonymously may lack credibility and hinder follow-ups.
Please be assured that all reports will be treated with confidence and every effort will be made to ensure that confidentiality is maintained throughout the process.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: How can I provide new information or make changes to a previous report on wrongdoing?
questions.text:
To provide us with new information or make changes to a previous report on wrongdoing, please email us at volunteer@cpf.gov.sg and include the following information:
1. Your name
2. Contact number
3. FormSG response ID that you submitted previously
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will I be further involved after making a report on wrongdoing?
questions.text: We may contact you for more information after you made a report on wrongdoing. Please ensure that you have the necessary evidence or supporting documents if you are being contacted.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Why do I need to update the CPFV app?
questions.text: We have upgraded the CPFV app and volunteers can expect exciting new features. Updating the app will ensure that you stay on top of app updates so that you have the best possible experience with the app. We appreciate your patience and understanding as we strive to improve your volunteering journey.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: When will the CPFV app update be available for download?
questions.text: On 14 July 2023, there will be a CPFV app update for you to download through your Mobile Devices’ App Store.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will my data from the previous version of the CPFV app be carried over to the new update?
questions.text: Yes, your profile and data will be migrated to the new CPFV app. Any badges and points earned before 30 June 2023 will be recorded and reflected there. Do note that some data and progress information (e.g. challenges and topic completions) may not be compatible or relevant to the new app's features or functions. Hence, these will not be available in the new app.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Will my login credentials remain the same after the transition to the new CPFV app?
questions.text: You do not need to re-submit your user information. However, when you download and enter the updated CPFV app, you are required to enter your mobile number and email address that were used in the app’s previous version. OTPs will be used in place of passwords moving forward. All past and present password data are not stored in the CPFV app nor able to be accessed by us.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What do I need to do on 14 July 2023 for my CPFV app?
questions.text: You will need to update the CPFV app from 14 July 2023 to keep up with the latest happenings and updates in the app. If you do not update the app, you will not be able to access its latest content.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Is support available if I encounter problems with the new release of the CPFV app?
questions.text: If you experience any technical difficulties using the new CPFV mobile app, please refer to the error pop-up in-app and follow the FAQ guide displayed to troubleshoot. Alternatively, if you have questions on the Community Paying it Forward movement, please email us at volunteer@cpf.gov.sg.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: What should I do if I can't connect to the CPFV app?
questions.text:
You can try the following methods:
Check that your internet connection is stable
Relaunch the CPFV app and try to login again
Make sure your device operating system and CPFV app are updated to the latest version
Restart your mobile device
Delete and reinstall the CPFV app
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering

questions.title: Why are the deductible and co-insurance features necessary under the MediShield Life scheme?
questions.text:
The deductible sieves out smaller medical bills that can be paid via MediSave or cash, and focuses MediShield Life coverage on larger, catastrophic medical bills to keep premiums sustainable and affordable. The co-insurance encourages responsible and appropriate consumption of healthcare services, while managing the financial burden on the patient. Both the deductible and co-insurance can also be covered by MediSave, up to respective withdrawal limits. This strikes a balance between protecting Singaporeans against the vast majority of healthcare bills, while keeping premiums affordable.
Those who have difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave can also apply for financial assistance such as MediFund.

questions.title: Can I use my redeemed premium discounts for my Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
You can redeem MediShield Life (MSHL) premium discounts if you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP). Your IP premiums are made up of two components – the MSHL portion and the additional private insurance coverage. The premium discounts you redeemed will be applied to the MSHL premiums of your IP policy.
IP policyholders may check with their IP insurers if they separately offer premium discounts or rewards which incentivise healthier behaviours.

questions.title: Why is the pilot only open to individuals who are 40 years old and above? Are there plans for the programme to be rolled out to younger individuals in the future?
questions.text:
This pilot programme is introduced in support of Healthier SG. As such, for a start, the pilot will focus on those aged 40 and above, which is the age criteria for the Healthier SG enrolment programme.
We will study the outcomes of the pilot before deciding whether premium discounts should be made a permanent feature of the MediShield Life scheme, and whether the discounts should be extended to younger individuals.
Under Healthier SG, all Singapore residents are encouraged to stay active and live healthily, such as by participating in programmes offered by the People’s Association (PA), Sport SG and the Health Promotion Board (HPB). All Singapore residents can participate in Healthy 365 programmes and challenges, to earn and redeem Healthpoints. Regardless of age, healthier lifestyles generally lead to better health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: When will the pilot end?
questions.text: The three-year pilot programme will start on 18 September 2025 and end on 17 September 2028. This means that the last day to redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts would be 17 September 2028. Premium discounts redeemed on and before 17 September 2028 will still be valid for 12 months from redemption, even after the pilot ends.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: How can one participate in the programme to redeem premium discounts?
questions.text:
Individuals can earn Healthpoints by participating in healthy lifestyle programmes and challenges on the Healthy 365 app, such as tracking their steps, sleep and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). For participants 40 years old and above, they can redeem these Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts at a conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $2, higher than the regular conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $1.
For instance, an individual who averages 150 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity weekly for the entire year, could redeem almost $70 worth of discounts off his or her MediShield Life premiums.
Healthier SG enrollees who have received 3,000 Healthpoints from completing their first Health Plan consultation can also redeem these for $40 worth of MediShield Life premium discounts.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: What is the maximum amount of premium discounts that could be redeemed?
questions.text:
Under the regular conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $1, the maximum value of cumulative Healthpoints that an individual can earn in a calendar year is worth $270.
As the MediShield Life premium discounts have a higher conversion rate of 150 Healthpoints to $2, the maximum value of premium discounts that could be redeemed per calendar year is $540. Please refer to this webpage for more details.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Why is the validity period of the premium discounts capped at 12 months?
questions.text: Once the premium discounts have been redeemed, they are valid for a period of 12 months. The discounts will automatically apply to the policyholder’s premium payment at the next MediShield Life policy renewal, which takes place every 12 months.
topics: MediShield Life / MediShield Life Premium Discount

questions.title: Can I use my MediShield Life premium discount to pay for my outstanding MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text: Premium discounts can only be used for your next MediShield Life premium payments from 18 September 2025 onwards. They cannot be applied to any outstanding premiums from previous policy years.

questions.title: How will the MediShield Life premium discounts I have redeemed be used for my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Any premium discounts you redeem on the Healthy 365 app before and on your MediShield Life (MSHL) or Integrated Shield Plan (IP) renewal date will be applied to your upcoming MSHL premiums, up to the net premium payable. Premium discounts redeemed after your MSHL or IP renewal date will be used for your next policy renewal, so long as these remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).
The premium discount will be reimbursed to you or your payer’s account after the full premium has been paid at policy renewal. You or your payer may check the reimbursement in the CPF Transaction History or contact your IP insurer directly. For information on your premium discounts, you may login to your Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: Why is there a difference between the premium discounts shown on my MediShield Life/ Integrated Shield Plan Premium Notice Letter and the amount I redeemed?
questions.text: The premium discount shown on the Premium Notice Letter reflects the amount you had redeemed as of the letter printing date. If you had redeemed more premium discounts after receiving the Premium Notice Letter, these will be reflected in your Healthcare Dashboard. Please log in for more details. The information is available under “Health insurance – MediShield Life premium discount”.

questions.title: I have redeemed my Healthpoints on the Healthy 365 app for MediShield Life premium discounts. Can I use it to pay for my dependant’s MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan premiums?
questions.text:
The premium discounts you earn are designated for your own personal MediShield Life (MSHL) premiums and cannot be used to pay for your dependant’s MSHL or Integrated Shield Plan premiums.
Similarly, the premium discounts redeemed by your family members can only be applied to their respective MSHL premiums, regardless of who their premium payer is.

questions.title: I only turn 40 in December, but my policy year renewal is in November, will I be able to redeem premium discounts before that?
questions.text: You will be able to redeem MediShield Life premium discounts in the year that you turn 40, regardless of when your birthday is.

questions.title: What happens to my premium discounts if I switch my Integrated Shield Plan (IP) or terminate my existing IP?
questions.text: If your redeemed premium discounts have already been used for your MediShield Life (MSHL) premiums before you switched Integrated Shield Plan (IP), no further action would be required. Any unused premium discounts or premium discounts redeemed after you switched IP, will be carried forward and used for your MSHL premiums at your next policy renewal, so long as they remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).

questions.title: I have redeemed $70 worth of premium discount but only $50 was used for my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to the remaining $20 of premium discount?
questions.text:
Any unused premium discounts will be carried forward and used for your MediShield Life premium at your next policy renewal, so long as these remain valid (premium discounts are valid for one year from the date of redemption).
For information on your premium discount, you may login to your Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: I am a nominee. How do I apply to withdraw the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text:
We will contact the nominee(s) within 10 working days after the Board is notified of the member’s demise.
The CPF savings will be automatically paid to the nominee(s) (i.e. you do not need to submit a withdrawal application), if you meet the following criteria, subject to additional eligibility requirements:
are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
aged 18 and above
have a local residential address
have a registered bank account with CPF Board
If you do not qualify for automatic disbursement, you will receive instructions on how to submit the withdrawal application in our notification to you.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Why is the pilot only open to individuals who are 40 years old and above? Are there plans for the programme to be rolled out to younger individuals in the future?
questions.text:
This pilot programme is introduced in support of Healthier SG. As such, for a start, the pilot will focus on those aged 40 and above, which is the age criteria for the Healthier SG enrolment programme.
We will study the outcomes of the pilot before deciding whether premium discounts should be made a permanent feature of the MediShield Life scheme, and whether the discounts should be extended to younger individuals.
Under Healthier SG, all Singapore residents are encouraged to stay active and live healthily, such as by participating in programmes offered by the People’s Association (PA), Sport SG and the Health Promotion Board (HPB). All Singapore residents can participate in Healthy 365 programmes and challenges, to earn and redeem Healthpoints. Regardless of age, healthier lifestyles generally lead to better health outcomes and reduced healthcare utilisation.

questions.title: I am on one of the original CPF LIFE plans (Basic, Balanced, Plus or Income). Can I change to one of the newer plans (Standard or Escalating)?
questions.text:
The Basic, Balanced, Plus and Income plans were introduced when CPF LIFE was first launched in 2009. Under these plans, extra interest earned on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances is credited to your Retirement Account (RA) and factored into your monthly payouts. As your balances are withdrawn over time to provide you with monthly payouts, the amount of monthly payouts and extra interest will decrease when your balances fall below $60,000.
If you are currently on any of the above original plans, you have the option to change to either the Escalating Plan or Standard Plan. Changing to the Escalating Plan will provide you with increasing payouts over time, while changing to the Standard Plan will provide you with level payouts. You can make the change anytime.
It is important to note that:
Once you have changed to the Standard or Escalating Plan, you cannot change back to an original plan.
All your RA savings, including the premium refunded from your original plan, will be deducted as CPF LIFE premium when the Standard or Escalating Plan is issued to you.

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly payouts?
questions.text: The monthly payouts of all members are deducted on the 2nd of the month, and the crediting of the monthly payouts to members’ bank accounts will depend on the bank's processing time. You will receive the monthly payouts in your bank account generally by the 4th working day of the month. You will generally receive your payouts earlier if your bank supports Fast And Secure Transfer (FAST).

questions.title: What will cause my CPF LIFE monthly payouts to be adjusted and when will payout adjustments be effected?
questions.text:
We want to ensure that your CPF LIFE monthly payouts are sustainable over the long term. As such, our actuarial consultant reviews them yearly and take into account the following:
Deviations in mortality experience. If more people live longer than expected in the long term, the monthly payouts might be lower, and vice versa.
Deviations in interest rates. If interest rates are higher than expected, the monthly payouts might be higher, and vice versa.
The revised payout, if any, will take effect every July of the year. We will notify you if there is an adjustment in your monthly payouts. Rest assured that any changes are expected to be small and gradual.

questions.title: When can I apply to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text: You can submit your instructions to start your monthly payouts anytime from three months before the month you turn 65, up to age 70. We will notify you three months before you turn 65 to guide you in exploring the options for your monthly payouts.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on what happens to my CPF accounts when I turn 55 and the available options I have in planning for my retirement?
questions.text:
You can log in to the Retirement Payout Planner to view your personalised retirement details before turning 55. This information is available from six months before your 55th birthday up to the day before you turn 55.
You will receive a notification from CPF Board around three months before your 55th birthday, providing you with information about the CPF rules that will affect you when you turn 55. It will include details on how to make an appointment to attend the CPF Retirement Planning Service, a one-to-one session at our CPF service centres where our Customer Service Executives will walk you through the CPF rules and options available to you when you turn 55.
You can also watch our webinars to learn more about planning for your retirement.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Why do I need to log in with my Singpass to access the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
You must log in with Singpass to use the Retirement Payout Planner as it enables the planner to personalise your experience.
Once logged in, the planner will
use your CPF balances to project your retirement savings and monthly payouts,
save your goals and details so you can continue from where you left off on future visits.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: The Retirement Payout Planner is available for members from age 16, up to 4 months before 65. Members who are reaching or have reached 65 can use the Plan my monthly payouts service to make key decisions related to their payouts.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The Retirement Payout Planner is a digital tool that helps you plan for your retirement in three ways:
Set your retirement payout goal
Project your retirement savings and payouts, and
Explore how different actions could bring you closer to your goal.
Did you know? The Retirement Payout Planner was enhanced in September 2026. Find out what’s new in the Retirement Payout Planner.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: How accurate are the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text:
The results provided in the Retirement Payout Planner are estimates, based on various assumptions and your inputs. They are meant to facilitate your planning of your CPF retirement savings and payouts, and should not be regarded as advice by CPF Board.
For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I use the Retirement Payout Planner if I am self-employed?
questions.text: Yes, you can. The Retirement Payout Planner is accessible by members from age 16, up to 4 months before turning 65. Self-employed members can input their monthly net taxable income (NTI) under the monthly salary field. As the projections are based on working contributions from employment calculated using the salary figures provided, they may not fully reflect the circumstances of self-employed members.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What are the assumptions used in the projections within the Retirement Payout Planner?
questions.text: For more information on assumptions used within the Retirement Payout Planner, refer to our detailed notes.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Retirement Payout Planner
Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: I am below 55. Can I use this Monthly Payout Estimator to estimate my monthly payout?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is designed to help members between the ages of 55 and 79 to estimate their monthly payout based on their desired retirement lifestyle.
If you are below 55, you can log in with your Singpass and try out the Retirement Payout Planner. This online tool can help you in setting your retirement income goal, visualising your projected retirement savings and payouts, and simulating the impact of actions you can take to achieve your goal. You may also perform selected transactions such as making retirement top-ups.
With the planner, retirement planning is easy with just a few steps and takes only 15 minutes to complete.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Can I access the Monthly Payout Estimator if I do not have a Singpass?
questions.text:
You will need to log in via Singpass to access the Monthly Payout Estimator.
If you do not have a Singpass account, you can register for one by following the instructions on the Singpass website. Alternatively, if you have questions on your payout amounts, please write to us.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Why do I need to log in using my Singpass to access the Monthly Payout Estimator to estimate my CPF LIFE monthly payouts now?
questions.text: From July 2024, you will have to log in using Singpass when using the Monthly Payout Estimator. By logging in, your CPF account details, such as birth year and CPF balances, will automatically be retrieved to estimate your monthly payouts, providing you with a more seamless experience when using the estimator. You can still adjust the CPF details.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: Who can use the Monthly Payout Estimator?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is primarily designed for CPF members aged 55 to 79. However, you can also adjust the details and use it to simulate payouts for your family members or loved ones.
How It Works:
For Yourself: If you are aged 55 to 79, you can log in using your Singpass and estimate your monthly payouts based on your Retirement Account balance.
For Others: You can simulate payouts for your family members or loved ones by:
logging in with your Singpass.
updating the birth year in the tool to match the person you are helping.
entering their Retirement Account balance or the amount you wish to simulate.
If you are below age 55, you can use the Retirement Payout Planner to set your retirement payout goal, project your payouts, and explore personalised actions to help you reach your goal.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the Monthly Payout Estimator?
questions.text:
The Monthly Payout Estimator is an online tool designed to help CPF members aged 55 to 79 plan their monthly payouts. It allows you to estimate your monthly payouts based on your Retirement Account balances and desired retirement lifestyle.
Key Features:
Estimate Monthly Payouts:
Calculate your monthly payouts based on your current Retirement Account balance.
Choose from different CPF LIFE plans to see how they impact your payouts.
Simulate Deferred Payouts:
Explore how different payout start ages could impact your monthly payouts.
Top-Up Calculator:
Simulate the amount you need to top up to achieve your desired monthly payout.
topics: Retirement Income / Retirement Income Planning Tools and Services

questions.title: What is the CPF Retirement Planning Service about?

The CPF Retirement Planning Service (CRPS) is part of the Board’s efforts to help CPF members understand our policies and enable them to make informed decisions about their CPF savings in retirement.

questions.title: Who is eligible for the CPF Retirement Planning Service and how do I make an appointment?

questions.title: Who can use the Plan my monthly payouts service?
questions.text:

If you are younger, you can use the Retirement Payout Planner to set your retirement payout goal, project your payouts, and explore personalised actions to help you reach your goal.

questions.title: What is the Plan my monthly payouts service?
questions.text:
The Plan my monthly payouts service is an online service for CPF members reaching age 65 (Payout Eligibility Age) and above to apply to start their monthly payouts and customise their monthly payouts to suit their desired retirement lifestyle. This online application allows you to submit your instructions, view your estimated payouts and find out how your choices will affect your payouts.
Key Features:
1. Choose to start your monthly payouts anytime between 65 and 70:
Explore how different payout start ages impact your monthly payouts.
2. Choose your CPF LIFE plan and receive payouts for life:
Visualise how different CPF LIFE plan impact your payouts.
3. Option to increase your monthly payouts:

questions.title: How do I find out more about the Singapore Infrastructure Dispute-Management Protocol (SIDP)?
questions.text:
The Singapore Infrastructure Dispute-Management Protocol (SIDP) 2018 sets out a carefully-tailored procedure for the appointment and involvement of a Dispute Board (DB) to assist in the effective management of differences or disputes that may arise in the context of mega construction or infrastructure projects.
The SIDP is designed and recommended for construction or infrastructure projects of more than S$500m in value, and can be easily incorporated into any construction or infrastructure contract using the standard clause provided in the Appendix.
It is strongly recommended that the SIDP be adopted from the start of the project, as a collaborative tool, to enable early and efficient resolution of differences and disputes.
The SIDP provides parties with the flexibility to opt for a DB comprising one, two or three expert professionals depending on the complexity and needs of the project. The members of the DB can be selected by agreement of the parties or failing such agreement, they may be appointed by the Authorised Appointing Body (as defined in the SIDP).
For more information on the SIDP, please refer to the websites of the Authorised Appointing Bodies:
• The Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC); and
• The Singapore Mediation Centre (SMC).
A copy of the SIDP is available at these websites.

questions.title: My GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions has been stopped due to two unsuccessful deductions. How do I reinstate my GIRO deductions using my existing bank account registered with the Board?
questions.text:

Your monthly deductions will resume once your application to reinstate your MediSave GIRO deductions has been processed. To avoid future interruption, please maintain sufficient funds in your bank account for the deductions.

questions.title: I've used up my Flexi-MediSave limit of $400, but my spouse needs medical treatment too. Can I use my MediSave for his/her medical bills?
questions.text:
Seniors aged 60 and older can use up to $400 per year under Flexi-MediSave for their own outpatient treatments, using their own MediSave or their spouse’s MediSave (spouse has to be aged 60 and older too).
If a senior has already used up their own $400 limit for outpatient treatments, they may still use their MediSave savings to pay for their spouse’s outpatient treatments, subject to the spouse’s $400 limit.
The $400 withdrawal limit applies to each patient per year, regardless whose MediSave account is used.
