Assessment or reassessment of your net trade income by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore
Previous unsuccessful GIRO deductions
Refunds of MediSave contributions
Additional MediSave contributions made or received

questions.title: Why was my GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions unsuccessful and how can I ensure my future deductions are successful?
questions.text:
Your GIRO deductions may be unsuccessful due to insufficient funds in your bank account, or if the 'Payment Limit' or 'Amount Allowed' set with your bank during your GIRO application is lower than your current monthly instalment amount. You can check your current monthly instalment amount on the Self-employment dashboard.
Some banks may impose administrative charges for unsuccessful deductions. To ensure future deductions are successful:
Ensure you have sufficient funds in your bank account before the scheduled GIRO deductions, which take place on the 25th of each month (or the next working day if the 25th falls on a weekend or public holiday)
Ensure that the GIRO payment limit which you have set with your bank is higher than your monthly instalment, or leave the 'Payment Limit'/'Amount Allowed' field blank during GIRO application to accommodate any future changes in your monthly instalments
If your GIRO deduction was unsuccessful, the next deduction will take place in the following month. You will be notified of your revised instalment plan before the subsequent month’s deduction. Your monthly instalment amount will be revised based on the total outstanding MediSave contributions and the remaining duration of your instalment plan.
If your GIRO deductions were suspended following unsuccessful deductions, you can reinstate your GIRO deductions within 14 days of the suspension via the “Reinstate GIRO deduction for MediSave contributions” form.

questions.title: How much CPF payouts can I get every month?
questions.text:
Your monthly payout amount depends on the amount of savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and your age at the point you start your payouts. Under CPF LIFE, you can receive up to $3,440 per month for life starting from age 65. For each year that you defer, your payouts will increase by up to 7%. This means that you can receive up to $4,580 if you choose to start your payout at age 70. You can use the Retirement Payout Planner to estimate how much you need every month to support the retirement lifestyle you want and project your CPF payout based on your CPF balances.
The table below provides a reference on how much you will receive under the CPF LIFE1 Standard Plan based on the amount of savings in your RA at age 55, if you start your monthly payouts from age 65 or 70.
Savings in your RA at age 55Savings in your RA at age 65 (factoring in CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum to grow your RA savings through compound interest)Monthly Payout2 from 65Monthly Payout2 from 70
$50,000$82,400$490$670
$110,200 (Basic Retirement Sum for members turning 55 in 2026)$170,100$950$1,280
$150,000$227,900$1,250$1,670
$220,400 (Full Retirement Sum for members turning 55 in 2026)$330,100$1,780$2,380
$300,000$445,600$2,380$3,170
$440,800 (Current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum)$650,100$3,440$4,580
1If you are not under CPF LIFE, you will receive monthly payouts of at least $350 until your CPF savings are depleted.
2Payout figures are based on a male member on CPF LIFE Standard Plan and may also be adjusted to account for long-term changes in interest rates or life expectancy. Such adjustments (if any) are expected to be small and gradual.

questions.title: What are the penalties for failing to report a work-related accident, Dangerous Occurrence or Occupational Disease under the Workplace Safety and Health (Incident Reporting) Regulations?

questions.title: Is the CPF payout eligibility age linked to the retirement/re-employment ages?
questions.text:
The CPF payout eligibility age is not linked to either the retirement or re-employment age.
Today, you can start your CPF payouts at any time from age 65. There is no link to the current retirement age of 63* or the re-employment age of 68. Even if the retirement age and the re-employment age are raised, the CPF payout eligibility age would remain unchanged.
* The current retirement age and re-employment age of 63 and 68 will be raised to 64 and 69 respectively from 1 July 2026.
For more information:
Information on the CPF Payout Eligibility Age
Information on the retirement age
Information on re-employment age

questions.title: What is my payout eligibility age?
questions.text:
Your payout eligibility age is the age where you can start receiving your retirement monthly payouts.
If you were born in 1954 or later, your payout eligibility age is 65. This means that you can start receiving your monthly payouts any time between the ages of 65 and 70.
If you were born before 1954, the table below shows your payout eligibility age.
Year of birth
Payout eligibility age
Before 1944
60
1944 to 1949
62
1950 and 1951
63
1952 and 1953

Please note that your payout eligibility age is not linked to your retirement or re-employment age. You can still receive payouts from your payout eligibility age even if the retirement age or re-employment age is raised.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF when I turn 65?
questions.text:
You can start to receive monthly CPF payouts from age 65.
Three months before your 65th birthday, we will notify you about your monthly payouts options. You will be guided to the personalised Plan my monthly payouts (PMP) service where you can:
1. choose to start or defer your payouts
2. view your estimated payouts
3. explore ways to increase your payouts using available CPF savings.
Find out more about what happens when you are reaching age 65.

questions.title: Why does CPF Board not start my payouts automatically at 65?
questions.text:
We understand that every member has unique retirement goals and needs. That is why we do not assume that everyone wants to start their payouts at 65.
Your CPF savings earn risk-free interest rates* of up to 6% per annum, which means the longer you wait to start your payouts, the more your retirement savings will grow. This increase in savings will result in higher monthly payouts under CPF LIFE.
Starting payouts automatically at 65 means denying members this option.
That is why we always encourage our members to instruct us when they want to start their payouts, as they would be the best judge of their own circumstances.
Here's an interesting fact: For every year that you defer your CPF LIFE payouts, your monthly payout amount increases by up to 7%. This means that if you defer for five years, your monthly payout could increase by up to 35%. Hence, weigh your options and make the decision that is best for you and your retirement goals.
* Based on the current 4% interest rate floor on Special and Retirement Account monies.

questions.title: What will happen to my CPF savings when my monthly payouts start?
questions.text:
If you are born on or after 1958, the following will happen when your monthly payouts start:
Transfer of Ordinary Account savings: If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), your Ordinary Account savings will be transferred to your Retirement Account to make up your FRS in cash. This will help you receive higher payouts.
CPF LIFE premium deduction: When you join CPF LIFE, your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used to pay your CPF LIFE premium. Your premium will continue to earn interest and the interest earned will be factored into your lifetime monthly payouts.
Additional withdrawable amount of up to 20% of RA savings at 65: Up to 20% of your RA savings at 65 will be available for your immediate withdrawable from age 65. If this withdrawable amount is not withdrawn nor used to increase your payouts, it will be transferred to your Ordinary Account for future cash withdrawals.

questions.title: What will happen if I do not instruct CPF Board to start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
If you do not provide instructions to the CPF Board using the "Plan my monthly payouts" service, your monthly payouts will start automatically when you reach age 70. These payouts will be paid to the registered bank account provided in your Account settings.
Find out more on what happens to your CPF savings when your monthly payout starts.

questions.title: Why is there another transfer of monies from my Ordinary Account (OA) to my Retirement Account (RA) before I start my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
As Singaporeans are now working longer, CPF contributions made after age 55 become an essential part of their retirement savings. The increase in senior worker CPF contribution rates further reinforces this. This additional transfer will help to boost your retirement savings and provide you with higher monthly payouts.
If you have already set aside your Full Retirement Sum in cash in your Retirement Account, the transfer will not occur.

questions.title: What are some common causes of dysphagia?
questions.text:
Dysphagia can result from various conditions including:
Stroke Neurological conditions (like Parkinson's disease)

Age-related changes

questions.title: How long does it take to recover from facial palsy?
questions.text: Recovery time varies greatly depending on the extent of nerve damage and type of diagnosis. It can take anywhere from days to 4 months or even longer. Each person's recovery journey is unique, so patience is essential during this process.

questions.title: How do regular MediSave co-contributions received under the Drive and Save Scheme benefit me?
questions.text:
Under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme, the regular MediSave co-contributions from your taxi operator can:
Offset your mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme
Earn up to 6% interest per annum on your MediSave savings
Use of MediSave savings to pay for medical expenses and healthcare insurance
Qualify for Workfare Income Supplement scheme for lower-wage workers

questions.title: My family member is covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS). Can I pay their DPS premium using my CPF savings?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings cannot be used to pay your family member's Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premium. This is to ensure that your CPF savings, which are generally meant to meet your retirement needs, are not depleted prematurely.
However, if you wish to help your family member, you may do so by paying their premium in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life (GEL). Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: If a US citizen acquires property in Singapore under the FTA agreement and later renounces US citizenship before selling it, what are the stamp duty implications for the sale?
questions.text:
The liability for Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) is determined at the point of purchase.
Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) may apply if the property is sold within the specified holding period.

questions.title: How can I cancel duplicate or double stamping?
questions.text:
If payment has been made for both stamping submissions, please proceed to request for refund for the duplicate record via the Stamp Duty Portal under "Request" > "Apply for Refund".
However, if payment has not been made for the duplicate record, please submit a request to invalidate the record via the Stamp Duty Portal as follows: "Request" > "Apply for Assessment/Appeal" > select "Assessment". Enter the Document Reference No. to retrieve the stamping record.

questions.title: Do I need to pay stamp duty if I receive a property by way of gift?
questions.text:
Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD) and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) (if applicable) is payable when there is a transfer of interest in a property.
Stamp duty will be computed based on the market value of the property where there is no consideration.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Do I have to restamp the tenancy agreement when there is a change in property ownership?
questions.text: Stamping is required if a new tenancy agreement is executed with the new landlord or if an Assignment of Lease between landlords is executed with consideration paid between the parties.

questions.title: Is stamp duty payable on a share sale and purchase agreement or share transfer instrument?
questions.text: If the share Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) is not subject to Additional Conveyance Duty (ACD), stamp duty would be remitted on the share SPA. Stamp duty remains payable on the Share Transfer Instrument.

questions.title: If my spouse and I, as co-owners of an HDB flat, purchase a resale condo before selling the HDB, is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable and can we qualify for remission?
questions.text:
Yes, ABSD is payable on the purchase of the resale condo. ABSD remission may be applicable to a married couple, which includes a Singapore Citizen, if the property is jointly purchased by the couple and all other remission conditions are met.
You may refer to Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple for more information on the remission conditions.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I am a foreigner buying a Singapore property in trust for my daughter, who is also a foreigner, is ABSD (Trust) remission applicable?
questions.text:
ABSD (Trust) remission may be granted if the conditions under the Stamp Duties (Trusts for Identifiable Individual Beneficiary) (Remission of ABSD) Rules 2022 are met.
The amount refunded will be the difference between the ABSD (Trust) paid and the ABSD based on the highest profile of the beneficial owner(s) of the property.
You may refer to Remission of ABSD (Trust) for more information on the remission conditions.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I solely own a HDB flat for 10 years. Will adding my spouse as an occupier affect the Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) liability if I sell my HDB flat immediately after?
questions.text:
No, occupiers of HDB flats are not considered owners of the flat.
Since there is no change of ownership and you have owned the flat for more than 10 years, SSD does not apply.
You may refer to Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for more information on SSD and its stipulated holding period.

questions.title: Will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) apply when a Singaporean and a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) jointly purchase their first HDB flat?
questions.text: ABSD is not payable on a joint purchase of an HDB flat under Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission, if at least one of the purchasers is a Singapore Citizen.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I currently own an HDB flat and partial interest of a condo purchased before Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) was introduced. If I now acquire additional interest in the condo, do I need to pay ABSD?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore citizen who owns two properties (albeit partial interest in one property), the acquisition of the additional interest would be counted as your third property and subject to the prevailing ABSD rate.
However, as you are a Singapore citizen who owns two properties and acquiring additional interest in one of the two properties which you already have a partial interest in, partial ABSD remission may be applicable.
Please note that BSD is still payable on the acquisition of the additional interest in the property.
You may refer to Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) for more information on ABSD.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: How do I renew my pawnbroker’s licence?
questions.text:
The renewal of the pawnbroking licence is subject to the good conduct of the licensee. Licensees should have the following document ready and forward it to the Registry upon notification; no later than two months before the expiry of the licence:

questions.title: Where can I get vaccinated?

questions.title: Why is my polyclinic only offering one type of vaccine?

questions.title: What are the types of Voluntary Contributions I can make for my platform workers?
questions.text:
You can make Voluntary Contributions (VC) to:
your platform workers’ Special or Retirement Account, under the Retirement Sum Topping Up Scheme (RSTU) (tax deduction available to platform operator and tax relief* available to platform worker)
your platform workers’ MediSave Account, either through:
cash top-ups to their MediSave Account, up to the Basic Healthcare Sum, which can qualify your platform workers for Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) (tax deduction available to platform operator and tax relief* available to platform worker); or
Voluntary Contributions to their MediSave Account, up to the CPF Annual Limit, which will not qualify your platform workers for MMSS. Tax exemption is available to the platform worker, and tax deduction available to platform operators
your platform workers’ three CPF accounts (no tax deduction for platform operator and platform worker
The VC made will be treated as the current month's contribution. Backdating to an earlier date is not allowed.
You can find out more on the types of VC you can make for your platform workers.
You can refer to this FAQ on the tax deductions available to you if you make VC.
* If your platform workers are eligible to receive matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme or the Matched MediSave Scheme , they will not receive tax relief for the top-ups that attract the matching grant.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Making voluntary CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I make Voluntary Contributions for my platform workers?
questions.text:
To make Voluntary Contributions (VC) for your platform workers, you have four options:
For cash top-ups to Special or Retirement Account under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme, you do not need to apply for a new CPF Submission Number (CSN). You can make the cash top-up via Top up Retirement Savings for Employees and platform workers.
For cash top-ups to MediSave Account (up to the Basic Healthcare Sum), you do not need to apply for a new CSN. Contributions made will qualify your platform worker for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS). You can make the cash top-up via Make MediSave top-up to employees and platform workers.
For VC to MediSave Account (up to the CPF Annual Limit), please apply for a new CSN with payment code "MSE" to make VC for your platform workers, e.g., 123456789-MSE-01. This VC will not qualify your platform worker for the MMSS.
For VC to all three CPF accounts, please apply for a new CSN with payment code “VCT” to make VC for your platform workers, e.g. 123456789-VCT-01.
After you receive the CSN for VC to MediSave Account or to all three CPF accounts, you can submit and make VC using CPF EZPay, in the same way you make mandatory CPF contributions for your platform workers.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Making voluntary CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the applicable limits for Voluntary Contributions for my platform workers?
questions.text:
Please refer to the table showing the types of Voluntary Contributions (VC) as well as their corresponding contribution limits for your platform workers.
Type of VCVC limit
(i) Cash top-ups to your platform workers' Special or Retirement Account
(Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme)
For platform workers below 55: up to the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
For platform workers 55 and above: up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS).
Learn more about how you can earn tax deductions for cash top-ups.
Note: Cash top-ups to Special or Retirement Account are not limited by the CPF Annual Limit.
(ii) Cash top-ups to your platform workers' MediSave Account
(Eligible platform workers can qualify for Matched MediSave Scheme)
Up to the platform worker’s Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS).
Learn more about how you can earn tax deductions for cash top-ups.
Note: Cash top-ups to MediSave Account are not limited by the CPF Annual Limit.
(iii) VC to your platform workers’ MediSave Account
(will not qualify your platform workers for the Matched MediSave Scheme)
Up to the CPF Annual Limit ($37,740 per platform worker per year) less any mandatory contributions and voluntary contributions to three CPF accounts received by the platform worker for the calendar year.
Do consider the mandatory CPF contributions you will be making for your platform worker, before making VC. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and VC received by the platform worker exceeds the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, VC made to your platform workers’ MediSave Account in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.
This VC is not limited by the platform worker’s Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). Any VC made above the BHS will be channelled to the platform worker’s Special Account or Retirement Account, or Ordinary Account if the FRS has also been met.
The CPF Submission Number to make VC to MediSave Account should have the payment code “MSE”.
(iv) VC to your platform workers’ three CPF Accounts
Up to the CPF Annual Limit ($37,740 per platform worker per year) less any mandatory contributions and voluntary MediSave contributions received by the platform worker for the calendar year.
Do consider the mandatory CPF contributions you will be making for your platform worker, before making VC. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and VC received by the platform worker exceeds the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, VC made to your platform workers’ three CPF Accounts in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded without interest.
The CPF Submission Number to make VC to three accounts should have the payment code of “VCT”.
Backdating of VC (including cash top-ups) to an earlier date is not allowed.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Making voluntary CPF contributions

questions.title: Why did CPF Board and MOH launch the Health Insurance Planner?
questions.text:
The Health Insurance Planner (HIP) is a joint initiative by CPF Board (CPFB) and Ministry of Health (MOH) under PLAN with CPF, our one-stop guidance service for financial and retirement planning.
Making decisions about health insurance coverage and comparing Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) can be challenging due to the complexity of information. As healthcare costs rise, members need to ensure their coverage matches both their care preferences and financial circumstances.
The HIP uses members' personal data to generate long-term projections of their MediSave savings, healthcare expenses, and insurance premiums. Working alongside existing information on MOH, CPFB and insurers' websites, the planner helps members make better-informed decisions about their health insurance coverage.
topics: PLAN with CPF / Health Insurance Planner

questions.title: Do I need to pay my NSmen employees' CPF contributions?
questions.text: You should continue to pay your employees' CPF contributions based on their usual remuneration, as though they are not away for their ORNS/SV activity. The CPF contributions payable by both employer and employee remain the same and are based on prevailing CPF Board guidelines.

questions.title: If you are a Third party service provider: How do I edit the access rights of my employees who are transacting on behalf of my company's client?
questions.text:
Select 'Manage Clients' under the 'Third Party (Clients)' tab. You can view a list of clients your entity is authorised to transact for. Click on the client you wish to view. To view the list of users authorised to transact on your client's behalf, click on the 'Authorised users' tab. To remove user access to a client's digital services, select the user and click 'Remove e-Service Access'.
Your client cannot edit the access rights of your employees who are transacting on their behalf.
topics: Employer / NS Pay - Third Party Service Provider

questions.title: Are there any fees imposed for the replacement of SAF Card?
questions.text:
Cardholders shall pay a replacement fee in the following situations:
Defacement/damage of the SAF Card through the cardholder's negligence;
Changes in personal data (except for Service Status, Military Rank Status and Address); and
Loss of the SAF Card
The SAF Card replacement fee of $20 shall be charged for each replacement, except in the case of replacement for the loss of your SAF Card. The replacement fee to be imposed shall be $20 and $30 respectively for first time and second time losses. For third and subsequent losses, the replacement fee to be imposed shall be $40 each time.

questions.title: Can I still use my Singpass to log in?
questions.text: Yes. Users can always log in via Singpass, even if biometric login is enabled or fails.

questions.title: How will I know that I have successfully spent the cash credits in the LifeSG application?
questions.text: You will see a payment success screen at the end of each transaction if your payment has been successful. You will also be able to view your credit balance and past transactions on the LifeSG mobile application.

questions.title: Can I cancel my payment after I have confirmed the payment on the LifeSG application?
questions.text: No, your credits will be deducted once the payment is successful.

questions.title: I am on the contract service and I understand that my CPF contribution rates are different from the Full CPF rates. How is the CPF contribution computed for both employee's and employer's portion?
questions.text: Pensionable components like Basic Rank Pay, Basic Pay Supplement (if any), MVC, etc attract a lower CPF rate while Non-Pensionable Components like NPVP and NPC, etc attract the full CPF rates. These rates are subject to changes from time to time.

questions.title: Can I use my property or CPF money to furnish the Banker's Guarantee?
questions.text: CPF funds or properties cannot be used to furnish a Banker's Guarantee.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR). Do I still need to serve National Service (NS)? Why?
questions.text: Under the Enlistment Act, all male Singapore Citizens and SPR will be scheduled for enlistment upon reaching the age of 18 years. Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)'s granted under the Professionals/Technical Personnel and Skilled Workers (PTS) Scheme are administratively exempted from NS. NS is a key institution that is vital to the security and defence of Singapore. Like citizens, SPRs also enjoy the security and stability made possible by the contributions of National Servicemen. As such, it is the duty of every Singapore male citizen and SPR to serve NS under the Enlistment Act. This obligation to serve NS is made known to SPRs at the point of application for Permanent Residence.

questions.title: I hold dual citizenship. Do I need to serve National Service (NS) in Singapore too?
questions.text: Singapore does not recognise dual citizenship. All male Singapore citizens are liable to serve National Service (NS).

questions.title: I want to apply for Singapore Permanent Residency (SPR). Can I know if I need to serve National Service (NS) if I obtain the SPR status?
questions.text: Under the Enlistment Act 1970, all male Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR) will be scheduled for enlistment upon reaching the age of 18 years. SPRs granted under the Professionals/Technical Personnel and Skilled Workers (PTS) Scheme are administratively exempted from National Service (NS).

questions.title: Can I report for the pre-enlistment medical screening if I did not complete the medical screening questionnaire?
questions.text: It is important to complete your medical screening questionnaire prior to your pre-enlistment medical screening date. The questionnaire helps our Medical Officers to determine your fitness for full-time National Service and to consider your medical condition(s) during military training.

questions.title: I am residing overseas and when do I need to register for National Service (NS)?
questions.text: Overseas pre-enlistees will receive a NS Registration Notice upon reaching 16.5 years old. This notice will provide you with the necessary information and instructions on how to proceed with your NS registration.

questions.title: What is National Service (NS) registration?
questions.text: NS registration is a requirement for all male Singapore citizens and Permanent Residents under the Enlistment Act 1970. It is the first step for all pre-enlistees when they begin their pre-enlistment procedures.

questions.title: How do I update any change in my residential/official address?
questions.text: For changes in official home address, you can update online.

questions.title: What should I wear on National Service (NS) enlistment day?
questions.text: You should wear a collared shirt, long trousers and shoes. Singlets, bermuda shorts, shorts, slippers or sandals are not allowed as you will be taking your oath of allegiance and it is a formal ceremony. The same restrictions apply to your parents and friends as well.

questions.title: There is an error when I tried submitting my Deferment application.
questions.text: Please save the screenshot of the error message and email it to contact@ns.gov.sg for further assistance.

questions.title: Can I submit my deferment application via hardcopy?
questions.text: Hardcopy submission of deferment application is not available. All deferment applications must be submitted through ICT and Manning eService on OneNS.

questions.title: How to update my child birth details?
questions.text: You do not need to update your child's birth details as the information will be updated upon the registration of your child's birth at ICA (Immigration & Checkpoints Authority.You may visit the informative ICA sites for local child birth https://www.ica.gov.sg/citizen/birth/citizen_birth_register) and for Overseas child birth https://www.ica.gov.sg/citizen/overseas/birth-registration/citizen_overseas_birth_childbornoverseas.

questions.title: Who can I contact regarding queries about my attendance for my In-Camp Training (ICT)?
questions.text: Please contact your unit commanders directly. You may also email contact@ns.gov.sg or call the NS Contact Centre via 1800 3676767 for assistance.

questions.title: Why do I need to link my NRIC number to my PayNow registered bank account to receive my IPPT incentive award? Can I link my mobile number instead?
questions.text: NRIC/FIN is the only accepted proxy for Government disbursements via PayNow. Unlike mobile numbers which are subject to change, the NRIC/FIN is an unchanging identifier assigned by the Government. Linking your NRIC/FIN to your PayNow account will ensure that Government disbursements are sent to the correct payee.

questions.title: I have multiple bank accounts. How do I know which bank account I have linked PayNow to?
questions.text: To check which bank account(s) you have linked PayNow to, you may approach your bank for assistance, or go to the PayNow interface on the internet banking platform or mobile banking app for any bank that you are registered with. The bank account(s) that is linked to your NRIC number and/or mobile number will be displayed. Your NRIC number and mobile numbers can be linked to different bank accounts.Please note that your NRIC number can only be linked to one bank account for PayNow at any one time.

questions.title: I'm experiencing problems registering for PayNow, how do I resolve this?
questions.text: If you are experiencing problems registering for PayNow or linking your NRIC number to your PayNow account, please approach your bank for assistance.

questions.title: What details will I need to provide when filing an injury claim?
questions.text:
You will need to submit your personal particulars, date, time, and place of the incident and circumstances leading up to your injury.
You will also need to submit the following documents to substantiate your injury:
Witness statements\
* Medical documents or reports
Training programmes or Admin Instructions\
* Traffic police report/Outcome of Traffic Police Investigation (if the circumstances of your injury involve a traffic accident)
* Any other relevant documents
\* To be provided by units
Please contact MINDEF/SAF HR Shared Services Centre at InjuryMgt@defence.gov.sg if you require further advice.

questions.title: How do I know my payment has been accepted?
questions.text: If your payment is successful, a payment confirmation page with a transaction reference will be displayed. You will also receive an acknowledgment via email and SMS. Alternatively, you may view your past payments under the payment history page in both MINDEF Payment Services (MIPS) and PayFlow Online.

questions.title: Can I be assured that the personal data provided to MINDEF via Form.SG will be secured?
questions.text: The care and protection of information, including the personal data of servicemen, is of utmost importance to MINDEF. Servicemen are regularly educated on the guidelines on personal data protection, and the need to handle personal data carefully and sensitively. These include the requirement to seek proper approval for the collection, use, and disclosure of personal data.

questions.title: What should I do if I am using one of the recommended browsers but the site is not displaying correctly?
questions.text:
Please clear your browser cache. This simple step can often resolve display issues. If you are accessing the site via Proxy or Firewall, contact your IT department regarding available proxy ports. If the problem persists, please report your issue here and provide the following details:
Browser information
Details of error messages
Screenshots of the issue

questions.title: How do I contact MINDEF/SAF/CMPB?
questions.text:
You can contact the NS Contact Centre (NSCC) for all enquiries via the following channels:
Webform
Send us your enquiry via the webform.
Hotline
1800-367-6767 (1800-eNSNSNS)
If you are calling from overseas: +65 6567 6767
Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 8.00am to 5.30pm. Closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays.
Email
Write to us at contact@ns.gov.sg
topics: General / CMPB Location and Operating Hours

questions.title: Who contributes the employers CPF during training?
questions.text: Under the Enlistment Act 1970, when the employee is away from work performing training, his employer is required to continue paying CPF contributions based on his usual civilian remuneration. The employer has to pay the CPF contributions on the wages given by the employer and the payments given by MINDEF/SPF/SCDF as though the employee has not been away from work. The CPF contributions payable by the employer and the amount which the employer can recover from the employee's wages are based on the CPF Board's guidelines.

questions.title: How do I select the correct car park?
questions.text: You can find the car park code on the signboards at all car parks. We've installed new signboards and enhanced existing ones within car parks and along kerbside lots to make the car park codes more visible.
topics: App Usage & Functionality / Location & Car Park

questions.title: Why can't I find nearby car parks on the app?
questions.text: Please ensure you've enabled location access for the app, so it can locate car parks in your area.
topics: App Usage & Functionality / Location & Car Park

questions.title: What is the list of food and food products, including approved sources, quantity and value allowed, that I can bring from overseas into Singapore for private consumption?
questions.text:
Travellers can bring back food products from their overseas travels, if the quantity is within the limits and the food product is allowed to be brought into Singapore.
For private consumption, travellers may bring in limited quantities of the following food and food products, subject to the specific rules and limits that apply:
Meat
Fish
Fruits and Vegetables
Eggs
Processed Food
Please refer to the List of Food & Food Products Allowed for the rules and limits on quantity of food allowed to be brought in for private consumption.
topics: Bring Food for Private Consumption from Overseas
Bring Food for Private Consumption from Overseas / General Rule to Bring Food into Singapore

questions.title: What fruits and vegetables, including the quantity, can I bring from overseas into Singapore for private consumption?
questions.text:
Travellers can bring in a small and reasonable quantity (i.e. hand-carry size) of all fruits and vegetables, for example not more than 5kg as a general guide, from any country/region into Singapore for private consumption.
Please refer to the List of Food & Food Products Allowed for more information.
topics: Bring Food for Private Consumption from Overseas
Bring Food for Private Consumption from Overseas / List of Food & Food Products Allowed

questions.title: I do not have enough MediSave to pay for my outpatient treatment expenses. How else can I pay for it?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient MediSave for your outpatient treatment expenses, you may consider tapping on one or more of your immediate family member's MediSave. Immediate family members include your spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and siblings. You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident if you wish to tap on your grandchildren or sibling's MediSave.
You may claim up to $700 (for patients with complex chronic conditions) or $500 (for non-complex chronic patients) per patient per year. Each MediSave claim is subject to a 15% co-payment in cash except for treatments received at your enrolled Healthier SG clinic. You may find out more about Healthier SG and search for a clinic near you to enrol into one.
While you can tap on your immediate family member's MediSave, the amount you can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per patient basis regardless of the number of payers. If you still have outstanding medical expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, you would have to pay the remainder in cash.

questions.title: What is HOMES?
questions.text:
HOMES is the Household Means Eligibility System, a Government system that supports public schemes in conducting means tests as part of their assessment to determine the level of assistance for applicants. HOMES officers will contact parents to request supporting documents or information needed to determine means test eligibility. Parents must respond to contact made by HOMES officers for HOMES to assess eligibility for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA).
HOMES outbound calls are made from 6015 5700. An SMS from gov.sg will be sent requesting for follow up/callback in the event, applicant is uncontactable.

questions.title: Do legal guardians have to fulfil working requirement that is imposed on biological parents for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA)?
questions.text: Yes, like biological parents, legal guardians must fulfil all SCFA eligibility criteria.

questions.title: How is income calculated for Student Care Financial Assistance (SCFA) subsidy?
questions.text:
For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income derived from the CPF contributions made over the last 12 months or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years).Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 calendar years), or income declared to CPF Board.

questions.title: What happens when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency and I have yet to transfer my CPF savings to my bank account?
questions.text:
Once your CPF account is closed, any remaining savings in your account will stop earning the prevailing CPF interest.
As a transitory measure, these savings will earn interest based on the 3-month average of the three local banks’ savings account interest rates. This is because non-Singapore Citizens and non-Permanent Residents can transfer these monies to their bank account at any time. The applicable rate is 0.05% per annum from April 2024 and will be fixed for a 3-year period until 31 March 2027. From 1 April 2027, any remaining savings will no longer earn any interest.
You can still transfer the remaining savings to your bank account at any time.
Your participation in all the schemes administered by the CPF Board will also cease. Please refer to the section "Schemes' participation upon account closure" for more information regarding schemes’ participation when your CPF account is closed.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) cover when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
Your Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage will be terminated on the date of Singapore Citizenship/Permanent Residency renunciation, as the scheme is only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
Your DPS insurer will refund any unused DPS premiums for the current policy year to your CPF account. The refund amount is calculated on a pro-rated basis. This means that you will receive a refund for the remaining months of coverage in your current policy year after your DPS termination date. For example, if your policy year runs from January to December and your DPS is terminated in June, you would receive a refund for the unused premium covering July to December.
The unused DPS premiums will be paid to you together with your CPF savings when you transfer your CPF savings to your bank account.
If you wish to find out more about your specific refund amount or have questions about the calculation, please contact your DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: When you have renounced your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency, your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover will cease upon the sale of your HDB flat or at the end of the current HPS policy year, whichever is earlier. There will be no further renewal of your HPS cover, even if you are in the process of selling your HDB flat, as the scheme is only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my MediShield Life/ElderShield plans when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you are a non-Singapore Citizen/non-Permanent Resident covered under MediShield Life/ElderShield before 1 April 2024,
(i) your cover(s) will cease unless you inform us of your intention to continue your cover(s) via Write to Us and make alternative payment arrangements for the premiums to be paid.
(ii) ElderShield policyholders with paid-up policies will remain covered. No further action is required.
For more details on MediShield Life
For more details on ElderShield
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if I have an outstanding CPF education loan when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you have used another CPF member’s CPF savings for your education and have an outstanding CPF education loan owed to him, your CPF savings may be used to pay the education loan before the remaining CPF savings are transferred to your bank account. In the event that your CPF savings are not sufficient to cover your full education loan, your repayment liability remains even after your CPF account is closed.
If you have used your CPF savings for your education or your child/spouse/siblings/relative’s education, the repayment of all such outstanding CPF Education Loans to you will be waived.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to the top-ups I had received in my Special or Retirement Account when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Any remaining monies which you have received through CPF transfers and cash top-ups will be paid to you, along with your CPF savings, when you transfer your savings to your bank account. This is subject to safeguards to prevent premature withdrawals.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF LIFE plan when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Your CPF LIFE plan will be terminated, and you will receive your CPF LIFE premium balance (if any) together with your CPF savings when you transfer your savings to your bank account.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Do I have to refund the sale proceeds when I sell my property after my CPF account is closed upon my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text: Yes, you must refund your CPF principal amount withdrawn with accrued interest or amount you have pledged to refund if you have not transferred your CPF savings to your bank account upon renunciation, by the time you sell your property.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my investments when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
The treatment of your investments when your CPF account is closed will depend on the investment scheme you have participated in.
CPF Investment Scheme – Ordinary Account (CPFIS-OA)
We will inform the agent bank to close your CPF Investment Account. The agent bank will then contact you for the withdrawal# of your investments and cash balance (if any). Your investments will be transferred to your own name and you may thereafter continue servicing your investments using cash or liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.
Once transferred, your CPFIS investments and cash balance in your CPF Investment Account will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.
# Central Depository (Pte) Ltd (“CDP”) imposes a transfer fee of $10.00 (excluding GST) for every share counter transferred from your CPF Investment Account to your CDP Account.
CPF Investment Scheme – Special Account (CPFIS-SA)
We will inform your product provider(s) to transfer your investment to your own name. Thereafter, you may liquidate them as you wish and have the sale proceeds paid to you directly.
Once transferred, your CPFIS investments will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.
Special Discounted Shares (SDS) Scheme
Your discounted Singtel shares will be automatically liquidated in the month following the automatic closure of your CPF account. The sales proceeds will be held together with your CPF savings, which you can transfer to your bank account at any point in time.
If you do not wish for your discounted Singtel shares to be automatically liquidated, please liquidate them before you renounce your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes
Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if I have unpaid taxes, MediShield Life premiums, CareShield Life premiums or outstanding education loan owed to a CPF member when my account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore citizenship/ permanent residency?
questions.text:
If you have unpaid taxes/MediShield Life premiums/CareShield Life premiums/outstanding education loan owed to a CPF member, we may recover the unpaid amount from your CPF savings when your CPF account is closed.
You are encouraged to settle any outstanding liabilities (e.g. insurance, tax and housing liabilities) before your CPF account is closed.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Can I use CPF savings to buy a property?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase residential properties in Singapore under the CPF Housing Scheme. Under this scheme, you can use your OA savings to:
Buy Housing & Development Board (HDB) flats
Buy or build private residential properties in Singapore
It's important to keep in mind that your Special Account (SA) and Retirement Account (RA) savings cannot be used for property purchases as these accounts are specifically meant to provide you with retirement income.
For comprehensive information about using your CPF savings for property purchase, please refer to the Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: Which property-related fees can I use my CPF savings for?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for the following:
1. Stamp duty (i.e. Buyer's Stamp Duty and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty)
Stamp duty must be paid to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore within 14 days of signing the sale and purchase agreement or accepting the option to purchase.
Generally, members will need to use cash for the stamp duty and apply for a reimbursement from their CPF savings when a CPF charge can be lodged on their property. A CPF charge is a legal claim the CPF Board places on your property to secure the refunds upon sale or disposal of the property, facilitated by lawyers appointed by the CPF Board when you apply to use CPF for property purchase.
The reimbursement process varies depending on the property type:
For completed properties: You can apply for CPF reimbursement (together with your lump sum drawdown) before legal completion, but payment will only be processed on the completion date. OA savings cannot be used for stamp duty before legal completion as the CPF charge can only be lodged after the seller's name is removed from the title.
For properties under construction: You can apply for reimbursement on or before the legal completion date. If the legal documentation for the CPF charge and the lodgment can be completed within the 14-day period, you may use your OA savings to pay the stamp duty directly.
For HDB loan applicants, please verify your reimbursement eligibility with HDB.
Note: If the developer has already paid the stamp duty, you cannot claim reimbursement from your CPF savings.
2. Transaction fee and lodgment fees
Your OA savings can cover:
Transaction fees charges by your lawyer's appointed bank
Singapore Land Authority’s lodgment fees for managing and disbursing your CPF savings
Note: We recommend consulting your lawyer about other potential costs and fees involved in the process.
3. Legal fees
These can be paid using your OA savings through:
HDB (if taking an HDB loan)
Your lawyer (if taking a bank loan)
Please note that monthly service and conservancy charges, along with other charges related to the use of the property, including taxes, cannot be paid with your CPF savings.
For comprehensive information about using your CPF savings for property purchases, please refer to the Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: I am planning to buy a property, but will be overseas and unable to handle the transactions. What should I do?
questions.text: If you are unable to handle property transactions in person due to overseas commitments, you can appoint a trusted person to act on your behalf through a Power of Attorney. This legal document gives your appointed representative the authority to manage your CPF savings and handle property-related matters in your absence. This ensures your property purchase can proceed smoothly even when you are not physically present in Singapore.

questions.title: Do I need a valuation report to use my CPF savings for property purchase if I am not taking a loan?
questions.text:
Yes, a valuation report is mandatory when using CPF savings for property purchase, regardless of whether you are taking a loan. This report determines the maximum amount of CPF savings you can use for your property purchase.
For HDB flats: Only HDB's valuation will be accepted, and it must be dated within three months from your application date.
For private properties: The valuation report must be:
Conducted by a licensed valuer, which can be your bank’s valuer
Dated within three months from your property purchase date

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy properties overseas?
questions.text:
CPF savings can only be used to buy properties in Singapore.
If you are looking to buy a property in another country, you will not be able to use your CPF savings to fund the purchase. It is important to keep this in mind when planning your property purchase and to ensure you have enough savings or financing options available for a property purchase outside of Singapore.

questions.title: What are the terms and conditions to use my CPF savings to buy an HDB flat or a private property?
questions.text: You can refer to the Terms and Conditions to use your CPF savings to buy a property.

questions.title: Can I use my Ordinary Account (OA) savings to service the housing loan taken by my parent(s) or sibling(s) or transfer my OA savings to their accounts to help with the loan payments?
questions.text:
You can only use your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to service the housing loan if you are the co-owner of the property. This ensures that when the property is eventually sold, the CPF savings you have used can be recovered and returned to your account for your retirement needs. If you are not the co-owner, you cannot use your OA savings or transfer your OA savings to your parents’ or siblings’ OA to help with their loan payments.
If they require financial assistance with their housing loan, they can:
If they have an HDB loan:
Apply for HDB's financial assistance measures
If they have a bank loan:
Approach their financier for alternative repayment arrangements

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to pay for HDB upgrading costs or the recess area of my HDB flat?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for both HDB upgrading costs and recess area purchases:
For HDB Upgrading Costs: You can make a lump sum payment through either of these methods:
1. Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Living in an HDB flat > Make Housing Payments
Processing time: three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
2. In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS10)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: three to five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
Note: If you wish to pay the upgrading cost via a monthly instalment plan, please approach HDB directly. You can refer to this FAQ for the instalment deduction date.
For Recess Area Purchase: The application process varies depending on your loan type:
If you have an HDB loan:
1. Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Living in an HDB flat > Apply to Purchase Recess Area
Processing time: three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
2. In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: three to five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
If you have a bank loan:
Make an appointment at any CPF Service Centre to submit your request. Please bring:
HDB’s letter of approval for the purchase of the recess area
A copy of the legal bill (if you are applying to use CPF savings for legal fees)
If you are a lawyer representing the member, you may write to us to submit the request.
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches and CPF Service Centres require prior appointments. For comprehensive information about using your CPF savings for property purchases, please refer to the Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: What is Edusave and can I use Edusave to pay for school fees?
questions.text: You may find out more details here - https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/edusave-account

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if my monthly income is above $4,000?
questions.text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme is designed to help senior Singapore Citizens with lower retirement savings save more and boost their retirement payouts. The average monthly income of $4,000 will cover most senior workers. If your average monthly income is above $4,000, you will not be eligible for the scheme as it is intended to provide additional support to those who need it the most.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Do the claim limits for High-Cost Drugs (HCD) and Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) apply if these treatments are administered during an inpatient stay or day surgery?
questions.text: Yes, if a patient receives High-Cost Drugs (HCD) or Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products (CTGTP) treatment during an inpatient or day surgery admission, the respective HCD/CTGTP claim limit will apply to these treatments, while the daily inpatient hospital limit will apply to the room and board charges. This ensures adequate healthcare financing support by MediShield Life and MediSave for patients who receive HCD or CTGTP treatment in inpatient or day surgery settings.

questions.title: If I am currently using GIRO to pay premiums, can I top up my MediSave to pay my MediShield Life/CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can top up your MediSave Account at any time, but your healthcare renewal premiums will continue to be deducted from your GIRO bank account unless you terminate the GIRO arrangement with your bank.
If you are currently on monthly GIRO instalments, topping up your MediSave Account will help pay off outstanding premiums. Your monthly GIRO deduction amount will remain unchanged, but the payment plan will end earlier once all outstanding premiums are fully paid.
You can top up your MediSave Account via the Top up MediSave Account online form. MediSave top-ups are generally credited within three working days and will be automatically deducted for premium payment(s). You can check your premium amounts on your Healthcare dashboard under the "Long-term care insurance" and "Health insurance" sections to determine how much to top up.
You may view the MediSave top-up(s) and premium deduction(s) in your Transaction history at cpf.gov.sg.
As MediSave top-ups could be deducted for healthcare premiums and medical expenses based on when deductions are due, please ensure that you have sufficient MediSave for all payments.

questions.title: How can I check for healthcare GIRO deductions on my bank statement?
questions.text: You can check your online banking, mobile banking app, or bank statement for transactions showing 'IBG CPF MSL MSL'. This code appears for all healthcare premium GIRO deductions (MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield).

questions.title: How long does ICA retain my personal data that were previously provided to ICA?
questions.text: ICA retains your data for as long as required under any relevant legislation, to fulfil the purpose for which the data was collected, and/or for official government purposes. You may wish to refer to ICA’s Privacy Statement for more information.

questions.title: Can I request for the deletion of my personal data that were previously provided to ICA?
questions.text: Data privacy regulations/rules in Singapore do not provide individuals the right to request for data erasure or deletion. ICA, however, will cease to retain your personal data where retention is no longer necessary under any relevant legislation, to fulfil the purpose(s) for which the personal data was collected for, or for official government purposes. You may wish to refer to ICA’s Privacy Statement for more information.

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on payments under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) if the claim is eventually rejected, unsuccessful or withdrawn?
questions.text:
When a WICA claim is rejected, unsuccessful, or withdrawn, employees may need to use their existing medical or hospitalisation leave entitlements for the absence period.
Any payments which the employee may receive under the Employment Act or employment contract (such as medical leave, hospitalisation leave, or continued wages during the period of incapacity) would be subject to CPF contributions. These are considered as regular employment remuneration, not WICA compensation.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Work injury compensation

questions.title: Can the deadline be extended to pay my outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premium?
questions.text:
You should make payment for your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums before the deadline. If you face difficulties in paying your outstanding premiums, you may apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). APS helps members who cannot pay their MediShield Life premiums after Government subsidies and have limited family support.
You can find out more about APS by calling 1800 222 3399 (or +65 6222 3399) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8).
Alternatively, you can:
1. Seek a family member's help to perform "Change Payer" to pay your outstanding premiums; or
2. Set up GIRO arrangement to pay your renewal premiums annually. Any outstanding premiums from previous policy years will be paid by monthly instalments.

questions.title: Will there be any fees for unsuccessful GIRO deduction of MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: CPF Board (Billing Organization) will not impose any charges for unsuccessful deductions of MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums. However, some banks will impose service charges as an unsuccessful deduction may be treated like a bounced cheque. Please contact your bank for further details on the fees and charges (if applicable).

questions.title: Will my new CPF working contribution partially pay off my outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums if I am on a monthly GIRO instalment plan?
questions.text:
Yes, your new CPF working contributions will be used to pay your outstanding MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums. This helps to reduce the outstanding amount and avoid enforcement actions.
If you are currently on a monthly GIRO payment arrangement, your monthly GIRO deduction amount will remain unchanged, but the payment plan will end earlier once outstanding premiums are fully paid.

questions.title: I am currently paying outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums through monthly GIRO instalments. Can I continue this arrangement to pay my future premiums?
questions.text:
If you have set up GIRO for healthcare renewal premiums, your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield renewal premiums shall be deducted from your GIRO bank account every year.
In the event of unsuccessful GIRO/ MediSave deduction for your renewal premiums, and you have an ongoing monthly GIRO arrangement, the renewal premiums will be included in your monthly GIRO payment plan.
Monthly GIRO instalment is only for payment of outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums). If your monthly payment arrangement has ended, you can request a new monthly instalment arrangement by writing to us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.
If you have terminated your previous GIRO arrangement with the bank, you may re-apply by clicking on "Setting up GIRO arrangement".

questions.title: Can I change the bank account to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: Yes. You will need to submit a new GIRO application with the new bank account details. The new application will generally be processed within 21 working days. We will continue to deduct your healthcare premiums from the current bank account until the new GIRO application is approved.

questions.title: Can I pay my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums by instalment through GIRO?
questions.text:
You can pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums by monthly GIRO instalments if you have outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums). The monthly deductions will be made from your bank account on the 15th of the month (or the next working day if 15th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
For MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life renewal premiums, there is no instalment option. The premiums will be deducted from your bank account every year, within a month after the cover is renewed.
Please maintain enough balance in your GIRO bank account. If you have set a payment limit on GIRO deductions, please ensure that the limit takes into account the total premium amount to be deducted. Note that some banks may charge administrative fees for unsuccessful deductions.
Please refer to the following FAQs for guidance on applying for GIRO to pay for your/your dependants' MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and ElderShield premiums:
How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?

questions.title: How do I apply for GIRO for my/my dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
You can use your own or a third party's bank account to apply for GIRO for your/your dependant's MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums by clicking on Set up GIRO for healthcare premiums.
Upon approval of your GIRO application, your healthcare renewal premiums will be deducted from your bank account every year, within a month after the cover is renewed. If you/your dependant has outstanding healthcare premiums, it will be paid in monthly instalments from the GIRO bank account.

questions.title: What happens if my Healthcare GIRO application is rejected or my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield GIRO deductions was unsuccessful for two or more consecutive months?
questions.text:
If your Healthcare GIRO application is rejected, you may re-apply by clicking on Setting up GIRO arrangement.
In the event of unsuccessful GIRO payment for your renewal premiums, the premiums will be deducted from MediSave. If your monthly GIRO deductions fail for two consecutive months, your payment plan will be suspended and you will need to write to us to request reactivation, which will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
We will impose new interest and penalties on your outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums if your GIRO application is rejected or GIRO deductions are suspended.

questions.title: How do I terminate my/my dependant's GIRO arrangement for MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: You can approach your bank to terminate your GIRO arrangement for healthcare premiums.

questions.title: How do I make an ElderShield claim?
questions.text:
If you are covered under ElderShield and would like to make a claim, you can arrange for a severe disability assessment with an MOH-accredited assessor and submit your application through the AIC’s eService portal (eFASS) using your Singpass.
If you are a caregiver submitting a claim for a mentally incapacitated ElderShield insured, you can log in eFASS using your Singpass to submit the application on his/her behalf.

questions.title: My employer has not paid me my salary and/or has dismissed me unfairly. What should I do?
questions.text: Educators who require help in managing employment disputes (e.g. salary, wrongful dismissal) may wish to tap on the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM)’s support services at https://www.tal.sg/tadm/about.

questions.title: I have successfully applied for a new Re-Entry Permit and retained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. How will this impact my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
As a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR), you are required to make CPF contributions on wages earned in Singapore. CPF contributions are not payable for employees who are neither Singapore Citizens nor SPRs.
Determining your Year of SPR status
Your CPF contribution rates as an SPR depend on how long you have held Permanent Resident status.
First-year rate: Applies from the day you obtain your SPR status, [i.e. the date indicated on your Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)] until the last day of the month of your first anniversary of SPR.
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following your first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of your second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following your second anniversary as an SPR onwards.

questions.title: Why are my full healthcare renewal premiums deducted from my GIRO bank account when I have set up monthly GIRO instalments?
questions.text:
If you have set up GIRO for healthcare renewal premiums, your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield renewal premiums will be deducted from your GIRO bank account every year. Monthly GIRO instalments are only for payment of past policy year’s outstanding premiums (excluding renewal premiums).
This arrangement was outlined in your GIRO application form.

questions.title: I am using a GIRO arrangement to pay my MediShield Life premiums. What happens to my GIRO when I upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
If you have applied for GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums and upgrade to an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) subsequently, the GIRO arrangement for your MediShield Life premiums will cease. Your existing GIRO arrangement for CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums (if any) will remain unchanged. You will need to have a separate premium payment arrangement with the IP insurer.
If you switch back to MediShield Life subsequently and would like to use GIRO for your MediShield Life premiums, you must re-apply.

questions.title: I am using GIRO for my MediShield Life and/or ElderShield premiums. Do I need to re-apply when joining CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Yes, you must re-apply for GIRO when joining CareShield Life. Your current MediShield Life and/or ElderShield GIRO arrangement will not automatically extend to cover CareShield Life premiums.
If you opt out of CareShield Life and return to ElderShield, you do not need to re-apply as your earlier GIRO application was extended to ElderShield.

questions.title: Why am I receiving notifications for CareShield Life and ElderShield through email/SMS or at a contact detail different from what I expected?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous efforts to improve our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These updates ensure better alignment with other notifications members receive from us.
Starting 24 November 2025, we are notifying members of their CareShield Life/ElderShield policy and payouts via email or SMS, using the contact details they have maintained with CPF Board.
You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered with CPF Board, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
This transition to digital notifications will ensure you are promptly informed of any premium deductions made from your MediSave, as part of our commitment to protecting members against fraudulent deductions and reducing our environmental footprint.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why am I receiving notifications for MediSave Care through email/SMS or at a contact detail different from what I expected?
questions.text:
As part of our continuous efforts to improve our members’ experience, we have made changes to the notifications we send. These updates ensure better alignment with other notifications members receive from us.
Starting 24 November 2025, we are notifying members of their MediSave Care withdrawals via email or SMS, using the contact details they have maintained with CPF Board.
You will receive notifications via one of the following modes:
a. If your email address is registered with CPF Board, you will receive an email notification;
b. If you do not have an email address registered with CPF Board, but have a mobile number registered, you will receive an SMS notification.
If you have installed the CPF Mobile App and enabled push notifications, you will receive push notification alerts on your mobile phone as an additional notification.
This transition to digital notifications will ensure you are promptly informed of any MediSave Care withdrawals, as part of our commitment to protecting members against fraudulent withdrawals and reducing our environmental footprint.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, after logging in with your Singpass.

questions.title: Why is my eGIRO application or setup unsuccessful and what can I do?
questions.text:
An eGIRO application or setup may be unsuccessful for several reasons. Here are the most common issues and how to resolve them:
Unable to use biometric login
You must enter your username and password manually in the designated fields as eGIRO does not support biometric login.
Browser closure during setup
If you accidentally close your browser while navigating to the bank’s website or whilst on the bank's website, the application will be unsuccessful. You will need to submit a new application.
Using the browser's back button
Avoid clicking your browser's back button whilst on the bank's website, as this will disrupt the setup process and you will need to submit a new application.
Rejecting transaction authentication
eGIRO transactions are protected by your bank's 2-Factor Authentication (2FA). When prompted, please verify your identity and authorise the transaction using a security token, one-time password, or mobile app authentication.
Important Setup Notes:
When completing your eGIRO application, you will see these optional fields:
a) Payment or transaction limit
This field is optional for selected banks. If you choose to set a limit, we recommend setting it higher than your current monthly contributions to allow for potential future increases.
b) Billing end date or expiry date
We recommend leaving this field blank. If you set an end date and subsequently need to extend the GIRO arrangement beyond that date, you will need to submit a new application. Please note that you will not receive any notification when your GIRO arrangement expires.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services

questions.text:

Determining your employee’s Year of SPR status

First-year rate: Applies from the day your employee obtains his SPR status until the last day of the month of his first anniversary. The SPR status date is shown on his Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.

When your employee was granted a new Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status, CPF contributions became payable from the day he obtained his new SPR status. This refers to the date indicated on his new valid Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA). Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.

questions.title: Why is my electronic Direct Debit Authorisation (eDDA) application or setup unsuccessful and what can I do?
questions.text:
An electronic Direct Debit Authorisation (eDDA) application or setup may be unsuccessful for several reasons. Here are the most common issues and how to resolve them:
Unable to use biometric login
You must enter your username and password manually in the designated fields as eDDA does not support biometric login.
Browser closure during setup
If you accidentally close your browser while navigating to the bank’s website or whilst on the bank's website, the application will be unsuccessful. You will need to submit a new application.
Using the browser's back button
Avoid clicking your browser's back button whilst on the bank's website, as this will disrupt the setup process and you will need to submit a new application.
Rejecting transaction authentication
eDDA transactions are protected by your bank's 2-Factor Authentication (2FA). When prompted, please verify your identity and authorise the transaction using a security token, one-time password, or mobile app authentication.
Corporate account approval timeout
If you're using a corporate bank account, the authorised approver must approve the application within 48 hours of submission. After this period, the application expires, and you will need to submit a new application.
Important Setup Notes:
When completing your eDDA application, you will see these optional fields:
a) Payment or transaction limit
This field is optional for selected banks. If you choose to set a limit, we recommend setting it higher than your current monthly submission amount to cater for future wage increases or bonus payments.
b) Billing end date or expiry date
We recommend leaving this field blank. If you set an end date and subsequently need to extend the DDA arrangement beyond that date, you will need to submit a new application. Please note that you will not receive any notification when your DDA arrangement expires.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: I have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment plan. My MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life cover has been renewed and has incurred new outstanding premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest will not be imposed on the new outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums while you have an ongoing monthly GIRO instalment arrangement. Your existing GIRO payment plan will be revised to include the new outstanding premiums. You will be notified of the revised instalment to be paid.

No, you can only use one bank account for the premium payment of MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield as they are under a single GIRO arrangement.

Can I change the bank account to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life/ElderShield premiums?
