questions.title: Where can I view the status of my GIRO application for my Healthcare premiums payment?

questions.title: My employee lost his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status and has now been granted a new SPR status. Do we need to re-submit the application for higher CPF contribution rates?
questions.text:
As your Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) employee has obtained new SPR status, you and your employee will have to pay CPF contribution at the graduated CPF contribution rates during the first two years of your employee’s new SPR status. This applies even though your previous application to contribute CPF at higher rates for your first/second Year SPR employee was approved.
If you and your SPR employee wish to contribute at higher rates, you will need to submit a new joint application with your SPR employee based on your entity type:
For UEN-registered entities
For individuals trading under own name

questions.title: What if my GIRO account does not have sufficient funds to pay for my MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
If you do not have sufficient funds in your GIRO account to pay your MediShield Life/ CareShield Life/ ElderShield premiums, the GIRO deduction will be unsuccessful and a second GIRO deduction attempt will be made.
The GIRO arrangement will be suspended if there are two consecutive unsuccessful deductions.
To avoid unsuccessful deductions, please maintain enough balance in your GIRO bank account. If you have set a payment limit on GIRO deductions, please ensure that the limit takes into account the total premium amount to be deducted. Note that some banks may charge administrative fees for unsuccessful deductions.

questions.title: I do not want to receive SMS and/or email notifications. How can I revert to paper notices for my property tax bill?
questions.text: We encourage you to try out the convenience of SMS and/ or email notifications. If you still prefer to receive paper notices, you can update your notification preferences at the digital service. You will no longer receive SMS and/ or email notifications informing you that your notice is ready for viewing on myTax Portal.

questions.title: Is there a grace period if I’m running late for my session?
questions.text: Patients are encouraged to be on time for their sessions. Should patients arrive late, no additional time will be given as we adhere strictly to prevailing patient appointments and clinic operational hours. Individuals must be aware that a full session may be charged if they arrive late.

questions.title: How is tax relief computed for my cash top-ups to Special Account/Retirement Account?
questions.text:
If your recipient is not eligible for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS):
You can enjoy tax relief of $8,000 per year on cash top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year on cash top-ups to your loved ones, up to the prevailing Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation:
Example 1: If you make a cash top-up of $10,000 to a recipient (self/loved one) whose limit to the prevailing FRS is less than $8,000.
For example, if the recipient’s limit to the prevailing FRS is $2,000
Estimated tax relief amount = $2,000
Example 2: If you make a cash top-up of $12,000 to a recipient (self/loved one) who has already reached the prevailing FRS.
Estimated tax relief amount = $0
If your recipient is eligible for MRSS:
Your cash top-up will first enable the recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $2,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief. You can continue to enjoy tax relief on cash top-ups that do not attract the MRSS matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation.
Example 1: If you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to an MRSS-eligible recipient (self/loved one), who has yet to receive any cash top-ups this year:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy = $2,000
Estimated tax relief amount = Total top-up amount - Matching grant amount = $3,000 - $2,000 = $1,000
Example 2: If you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to an MRSS-eligible recipient (self/loved one) who has already received $2,000 of cash top-ups this year:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy = $0
Estimated tax relief amount = Total top-up amount - Matching grant amount = $3,000 - $0 = $3,000
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I have received an Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore's (IRAS) notice and applied for GIRO payment arrangement for my healthcare premiums. Will interest be imposed on me?
questions.text: Interest and penalties will not be imposed on your outstanding MediShield Life and/ or CareShield Life premiums if CPF Board receives your GIRO application before the due date stated in IRAS' notice.

questions.title: Why do I see the option "Document upload" and am unable to make payment for my Re-Entry Permit (REP) after I login?
questions.text:

questions.title: How can I renew my Re-Entry Permit (REP) if my REP has expired and I am outside of Singapore?
questions.text:
If you are outside Singapore without a valid REP, you have to apply for an REP within 180 days from the date you are first physically outside Singapore without a valid REP to retain your PR status.
The REP application is subject to approval on a case-by-case basis. If you had applied for a new REP within the 180-day period, you will remain a PR until there is an outcome to your REP application. If your REP application is unsuccessful, you will lose your PR status the day after the REP application outcome is sent to you.
You will also lose your PR status automatically if you do not apply for a new REP within this 180-day period.

questions.title: What is Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:
The Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) enables you to supplement your retirement income if you're moving to a 3-room or smaller flat.
By committing your housing refunds towards your retirement payouts, you can enjoy lifelong income through CPF LIFE and receive a cash bonus of up to $40,000.
Find out more about SHB.
You may also use HDB’s Enquire Housing Monetisation Options e-Service to check your eligible Housing Monetisation options.

questions.title: How do I apply for Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus?
questions.text:

Silver Housing Bonus
Lease Buyback Scheme

questions.title: What are the features of CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE offers several key features to support your retirement:
Payouts that never run out:
It provides you with a monthly income no matter how long you live. With more Singaporeans living beyond 85 years old, this addresses concerns about outliving retirement savings.
Higher payouts with up to 6% interest:
Your premium continues to earn CPF interest of up to 6% per annum, risk free. The interest is factored into your monthly payouts, allowing you to receive higher monthly payouts from the start.
Capital guaranteed:
It guarantees that the total amount of payouts you receive over your lifetime plus the amount paid to your beneficiaries will be equal or more than your CPF LIFE premium.

questions.title: How can I increase my monthly payouts?
questions.text:
You can consider the following options to increase your monthly payouts:
Boost your retirement savings:
Make cash top-ups or CPF transfers to grow your retirement savings up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum. The more retirement savings you have, the higher your monthly payouts.
If you are born in 1957 or after, you can use the additional amount of retirement savings you can withdraw from age 65 to increase your monthly payouts via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Defer your monthly payouts up to age 70:
Start your monthly payouts later to allow your retirement savings to grow with risk-free interest rates of up to 6% per annum.
If your payouts have already started, you can defer them via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Monetise your property:
Consider options like the Lease Buyback Scheme or Silver Housing Bonus Scheme to supplement your monthly payouts.
If you wish to enquire on your revised payout, please write to us.

questions.title: Who can join CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
All CPF members can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65. The latest age to join CPF LIFE is one month before age 80.
There is no minimum CPF savings required to join, but the amount of payout you get is dependent on your Retirement Account balances when you join CPF LIFE.
You will be automatically included in CPF LIFE when you start your CPF monthly payouts if you were born on or after 1 January 1958 and have at least $60,000 in your CPF retirement savings when you start your monthly payouts.
If you are not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can still choose to join the scheme.
Tip: Use the Monthly payout estimator to see which LIFE plan suits you and see the estimated monthly payout based on your choice. Consider topping up your retirement savings in your Retirement Account(RA), to increase your monthly payouts.

questions.title: Can I retain my Ordinary Account savings instead of having them transferred to my Retirement Account to increase my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can retain your Ordinary Account (OA) savings for immediate withdrawal needs if you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account (RA).
If you have not set aside your FRS, your OA savings will be automatically transferred to your RA to provide you with higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts.
If you have housing obligations, you can use your CPF LIFE monthly payouts or any CPF savings in excess of your FRS to meet these needs.

questions.title: How much Ordinary Account savings will be transferred to my Retirement Account to increase my CPF LIFE payouts?
questions.text:
You can choose to transfer all your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to your Retirement Account (RA), up to the current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS).
If you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and have started your monthly payouts, your OA savings will be automatically transferred to your RA, up to your FRS. You will receive a notification before the transfer.
For example: Jane is born in 1960 and the principal amount in her RA is $148,000, which is below her FRS of $161,000. As she has started her monthly payouts, assuming she has $20,000 in her OA, $13,000 will be automatically transferred to her RA to set aside her FRS and increase her CPF LIFE monthly payouts. The remaining $7,000 will remain in her OA and she can choose to transfer it to her RA to increase her CPF LIFE payouts further or to withdraw anytime.

questions.title: How can I prolong my monthly payouts if I am not on CPF LIFE?
questions.text:
You can consider the following options to prolong your monthly payouts:
Join CPF LIFE: CPF LIFE provides lifelong monthly payouts, unlike payouts that stop when your retirement savings are depleted if you are not on CPF LIFE. You can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65 to one month before turning 80 via the Plan my monthly payouts service.
Reduce your monthly payouts: You can reduce your monthly payouts to extend the duration of your retirement income up to age 90. Submit your request via 'Write-to-us' with your Singpass.

questions.title: What is the amount I can withdraw from my retirement savings when I have an alternative lifelong income, such as pension or annuity?
questions.text:
The amount you can withdraw from your retirement savings when you have alternative lifelong income, such as a pension or annuity is subject to the Board’s approval and depends on the following factors:
Total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout:
The total guaranteed monthly payout amount may include multiple pension/annuities.
Instruments such as endowments, whole life policies and bonds are not considered as sources of lifelong income.
Comparison to CPF LIFE Standard Plan Payout computed based on your Full Retirement Sum:
If your total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout equals or exceeds the monthly payouts under CPF LIFE Standard Plan, you may withdraw all your CPF retirement savings*.
If your total guaranteed lifelong monthly payout is less than the monthly payouts under the CPF LIFE Standard Plan, you may withdraw your CPF retirement savings* partially.
*Withdrawable amount excludes any cash top-ups, CPF transfers to the Retirement Account (RA) and government grants.

questions.title: Do I have to top up my MediSave Account to the Basic Healthcare Sum if I start withdrawing my CPF savings from age 55?
questions.text: You do not need to top up your MediSave Account (MA) when you begin withdrawing your CPF savings from age 55. The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA.

questions.title: What is the minimum balance I need to set aside in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount required to set aside in your MediSave Account (MA). A portion of your working contributions will be allocated to your MA until your balance reaches the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). The BHS is the estimated savings you need in your MA to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. Any amount above the BHS will be channelled to your other CPF accounts, depending on your age. You can find out how MediSave contributions above the BHS are channelled to other CPF accounts via this link.

questions.title: I have saved the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in my MediSave Account (MA). What happens to the savings in my MA above the BHS?
questions.text:
Any savings in your MediSave Account (MA) above the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) will be channelled to your CPF Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA), depending on your age. The BHS cap and overflow arrangement are designed to prevent excessive saving in your MA while helping to supplement your retirement savings, which can be withdrawn according to the CPF withdrawal rules.
If your MA savings exceed the BHS, the excess will be channelled to your Ordinary Account (OA) if you are:
Below 55 years old and have met the current Full Retirement Sum (FRS) (consisting of your SA balance and any active CPFIS-SA investments) in your SA; or
55 years old or older and have set aside your FRS (which can be entirely in cash or a combination of property and cash) in your RA.
Savings in the OA can be used for other purposes, such as housing repayment or withdrawn if you meet the withdrawal requirements.

questions.title: If I am 66 years old in 2026 and my applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is $75,500, am I allowed to maintain a balance greater than my applicable BHS in my MediSave Account?
questions.text: You can only save up to your applicable Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) in your MediSave Account (MA), which is the maximum amount you can hold in your MA. The BHS is designed to cover your basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age and to prevent the excessive accumulation of funds in your MA.

questions.title: My child’s PSLE score does not meet your school’s cut-off point. As a Catholic family, do we get any advantage in terms of admission?
questions.text: The Secondary 1 Posting Exercise is based on students’ PSLE score. Appeals can only be considered if your child’s PSLE score meets the schools’ cut-off point of the posting year, subject to available vacancies and meeting MOE’s criteria.

questions.title: How do I find out the Annual Value (AV) of a property?
questions.text:
The owner of a property can check the current AV of his or her property at no cost by using our 'View Property Summary' digital service. All AVs shown are as at current date.
Please note that if there is any change to the AV stated in your 2026 Property Tax bill, it will only be reflected on the digital service from the effective date of change.
If you are not the owner of the property, you can use the 'Check Annual Value of Property' digital service to search the AV of a property at a fee of $2.50 per search. You can retrieve the AV of the current year and up to past five years. This digital service only provides information on AV, other information on the property is not made available.

questions.title: I just receive my property tax bill and I find the assessed Annual Value (AV) for my residential property is high. I am thinking of filing an objection against my AV. What is the likelihood of a successful downward AV revision through the objection process?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) is the estimated annual rent of the property if it were to be rented out. The AV of a residential property is assessed based on market rents of comparable properties and will be adjusted (either upwards or downwards) when there is market evidence to support the revision.
Based on our records, 98% of residential AV objections are unsuccessful with no amendments made to the original assessment. In other words, the AV for the vast majority of residential objections filed are found to be in line with market rents and are therefore unsuccessful.
IRAS adhere to robust valuation practices to ensure a fair and accurate assessment. While it is uncommon for objections to result in changes, IRAS remains committed to reviewing every submission thoroughly with all valid grounds carefully considered.
Before proceeding with an objection, please note that the following grounds for objection are not accepted and will be rejected:
1. High tax rates
2. Financial difficulties
3. You are not receiving any rental income as the property is either vacant or owner-occupied.
4. Issues relating to the property tax apportionment with developers for newly completed properties
We encourage you to review our FAQ section and case studies to understand how AVs are determined before deciding whether to proceed with an objection.
If you require financial assistance on your property tax obligations, please visit the webpage on payment plans.

questions.title: I recently moved from a HDB flat to a private condominium unit. Why is the property tax higher for my private condominium unit even though the size of the two properties is similar?
questions.text:
Our Property Tax (PT) regime is progressive and designed to distribute tax obligations equitably. Property Tax on residential properties follows a progressive tax rate schedule, where the higher value the property, the higher the property tax. This applies to both owner-occupier tax rates and non-owner-occupier tax rates for residential properties.
Private condominium units typically command higher rents in the market compared to HDB flats and would thus have higher AVs, even for units with similar floor areas due to the differences in their various property characteristics. For example, private condominiums have additional facilities and amenities (such as swimming pools, gyms, on-site security) that contribute to higher potential rents as compared to HDB flats.
Therefore, the annual PT for a condominium unit is higher than a HDB flat of a similar size because it has a higher AV and corresponding tax rates.

questions.title: To give me an idea of whether the AV of my property is fair, where can I find information on private residential properties or HDB flats that are let out?
questions.text:
To understand whether the AV of your property is fair and how it is calculated, we suggest the following helpful steps:
1. First, refer to our Case Studies:
(i) Private Condominium unit (PDF, 64KB)
(ii) Newly Built House (PDF, 60KB)
These case studies illustrate how we determine AV based on rents of similar properties in your neighbourhood.
2. Next, you may refer to rents of private residential properties made available on URA website (http://www.ura.gov.sg) and rents of HDB flats made available on HDB website (www.hdb.gov.sg).
Please note that the rental figures are intended only as a general guide and should not be used as a direct 1-to-1 comparison with your specific property. The AV of your property may differ as it considers various property specific factors such as its location, condition, size, etc.

questions.title: I am a retiree with sentimental attachment to my home. I no longer draw any monthly income, and I am the sole caregiver for my spouse who has many medical ailments. Can my circumstances allow for my AV be lowered so I can afford my property taxes, medical fees, and daily living expenses?
questions.text:
We understand your challenging financial situation and that your home is more than bricks and mortar. It holds deep personal value.
However, the AV of a property is assessed based on market rental evidence, and not on personal circumstances. While we are unable to reduce the AV of your property, we understand that property taxes can be a financial concern.
To assist you with your tax obligations, IRAS offers an interest-free instalment payment plan for up to 24 months to provide flexibility to lower your monthly instalment payments. To explore your options, you may apply for a longer payment plan via the ‘Apply/Manage GIRO Plan’ digital service at myTax Portal. Please note that instalment plans are only available if you choose to pay via GIRO.
If you are residing at your property, you will be enjoying the lower owner-occupier concession, as compared to higher tax rates for residential investment properties. The Government also granted property tax rebates for owner occupied properties in years 2023 to 2025, to help Singaporeans with cost-of-living concerns. These are measures to assist homeowners to manage their tax obligations.

questions.title: My property is old, needs repairs, and is not in perfect condition. I have not done any renovation works since I first moved in many years ago. Will IRAS peg my AV at a higher level based on the rents of the newer and bigger properties in my estate?
questions.text: While we consider the prevailing market rents of comparable properties in the locality, do rest assured that we will make appropriate adjustments and take into account the subject property’s unique characteristics and actual physical condition in determining its AV assessment.

questions.title: Can the AV be reduced to take into account the owner’s expenses such as interest cost, utilities, insurance and taxes?
questions.text: No, such expenses cannot be deducted for property tax purpose. AV is defined as the estimated gross annual rent at which the property can be let out on a yearly basis, with the landlord paying the expenses of repairs, insurance, maintenance and upkeep of the property.

questions.title: I Inherited my property and it has a very high Annual Value. I am staying in my property and do not generate rental income from it. I am just a regular salaried worker and do not intend to sell my property. Why do I need to pay higher property tax?
questions.text: As opposed to income tax, which taxes the income received by a person, property tax is a wealth tax. It is not a tax on rental income. It is thus levied based on the value of your property, which represents part of your overall wealth. However, to encourage home ownership, you can enjoy a lower tax rate for your owner-occupied residential property.

questions.title: I have stopped renting out my property. Why is it still taxed at the non-owner-occupier residential tax rates?
questions.text:
When the lease on your property ends and you have moved back into your home, you have to reapply for the owner-occupier tax rates for your property using ‘Apply/Withdraw Owner-Occupier Tax Rates’ digital service.
If the lease is pre-terminated, you can apply for the owner-occupier tax rates via our 'Apply/Withdraw Owner-Occupier Tax Rates' digital service with supporting documents to show that the lease has been pre-terminated. You may refer to the section above on “Applying for owner-occupier tax rates” for some examples of supporting documents that you can provide to show that the lease has been pre-terminated.

questions.title: I have bought a newly constructed property. When will I receive the property tax bill?
questions.text: Generally, your first Property Tax bill will be issued to you within 6 to 12 months from the date of transfer of the property, once your property tax assessment is finalised.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on other Government support available for persons with disabilities?
questions.text: For comprehensive information about disability support schemes and services, you may refer to the SG Enabling Guide at enablingguide.sg/schemes-grants-support or contact SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.

questions.title: Can caregivers top up to their loved ones under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
Anyone, including caregivers, loved ones, employers or members of the community, can assist eligible individuals in receiving the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme by making cash top-ups to their Retirement Account.
For more information on cash top-ups, Matched Retirement Savings Scheme eligibility, and what top-up monies and matching grants can be used for, please refer to the FAQs below:
How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
I am a caregiver. Can I check the eligibility of my loved ones for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?

questions.title: I am a parent of a child with disabilities. How can I check the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility for my child?
questions.text:
If you are a parent of a child below 21 years old, you can access the Child Dashboard using your own CPF account to check the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility status of your child.
If your child is a verified person with disabilities, you will see a section on MRSS on the child dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a caregiver. Can I check the eligibility of my loved ones for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
Eligible persons with disability will be notified via email or post, or login with their Singpass to view their eligibility status for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) via the Retirement Dashboard.
If you are a parent of a child with disability under 21 and he/she is eligible, you may check his/her eligibility status via your own CPF account. In your own CPF account, navigate to my cpf Home > Child Dashboard. If your child is eligible, you will see a section on MRSS.
If you are a deputy/donee for an eligible loved one, you may use your loved ones’ Singpass to login to his/her account to view his/her eligibility status for MRSS via the Retirement Dashboard.
If you are not a deputy/donee but would like to check your loved ones’ eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS), write to us.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a caregiver. What do I need to know about the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for persons with disabilities?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) is expanded to include Singaporeans of all ages with disabilities. Eligible persons with disabilities can receive a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $2,000/year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000 from the Government on cash top-ups received in their Retirement or Special Account (RA/SA). Anyone such as the member, their loved ones, employers^ or members of the community, can make the cash top-ups. As a caregiver, you can make cash top-ups to the RA or SA of eligible persons with disabilities to help build up their retirement savings earlier.
If your loved one is below 55 as of 31st December of the year, they are required to have their disability status verified with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).
If your loved one is 55 or above as of 31st December of the year, they will be assessed for eligibility regardless of their disability status. They are not required to have their disability status verified with MSF.
For more information on the eligibility criteria or the disability verification process, please refer to the FAQs below:
What are the eligibility criteria of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) from 1 January 2026 when the scheme is expanded to Singaporeans with disabilities?
I am a person with disability below 55. How can I check if I am verified as a person with disability and what should I do if I am not yet verified?
What is the submission deadline for the Disability Verification Form (DVF) to be included in the eligibility assessment for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) in the following year?
Will I need to verify my disability status every year to qualify for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What can my loved one use the top-up monies and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) matching grants for?
questions.text:
Top-ups and matching grant from the Matched Retirement Savings Schemes are meant to boost your loved one’s retirement savings and monthly retirement payouts.
In keeping with this purpose, such top-ups and matching grant monies will form the retirement savings in your loved one’s Retirement Account (which is created for him/her at age 55), and paid to him/her as higher monthly payouts in retirement from age 65.
These top-up monies and matching grant cannot be withdrawn for other purposes (e.g. withdrawn in a lump sum, withdrawn from the Retirement Account using property, transferred to loved ones or other CPF schemes such as education investment, insurance).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: How can I reschedule my conciliation session?
questions.text:
The conciliation session is directed by the Court, and all parties are required to comply with the Court directions. The MEO is unable to reschedule the session.
However, if you are unable to attend the conciliation session, please contact us and provide your reasons via an online enquiry at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw or call 1800-2255-529 during office hours. Please note that airtime charges may apply for calls made from mobile lines.

questions.title: How does the Matched MediSave Scheme compare with the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
The table below outlines the key differences between the Matched MediSave Scheme and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.
Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)
Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS)
What are the top-ups and matching grant used for?
Boost monthly payouts in retirement
Payment of approved healthcare insurance premiums (e.g. MediShield Life and CareShield Life) and approved medical treatments.
Where are my cash top-ups and the government matching grant credited to?
Retirement / Special Account (RA/SA)
MediSave Account (MA)
How much grant can I receive?
Up to $2,000 per year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000
Up to $1,000 per year
Who is eligible?
(The following conditions must all be met for the respective scheme)
Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above or verified persons with disabilities aged below 55
RA/SA savings*# less than current Basic Retirement Sum
Singapore Citizens aged 55-70 (inclusive)
MA balances less than 50% of current Basic Healthcare Sum
Self-employed persons must have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable
Average monthly income# is not more than $4,000
Annual Value of Residence# not more than $21,000
Owns not more than one property#
How can eligible members receive the matching grant?
Make cash top up to RA/SA
Make cash top up to MA
The two schemes complement each other to help support the lower-income seniors with their retirement and healthcare needs. For more information about MRSS and MMSS, please refer to cpf.gov.sg/mrss and cpf.gov.sg/mmss respectively.
*RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.
#Previous year’s data is utilised to assess your eligibility as these are the latest data available.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme but I have limited funds. Should I top up the Retirement / Special Account or MediSave Account?
questions.text:
If you and your loved ones have limited funds available for CPF top-ups and are eligible for both Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) and Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can consider which scheme better meets your needs. You may also wish to consider portioning your funds and top up to both your Retirement / Special Account (RA / SA) and MediSave Account (MA) to benefit from both schemes.
If you want to increase your retirement payout, you may consider topping up your RA / SA to benefit from MRSS. If you anticipate higher healthcare spending given your health circumstances, you may consider topping up your MA to benefit from MMSS.
You can refer to this comparison table to learn the key differences between the two schemes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for both the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and Matched MediSave Scheme. Can I participate in both schemes to receive the maximum Government grants?
questions.text: Yes, if you are eligible for both schemes, you can top up in cash to your Retirement / Special Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) of up to $2,000 per year, as well as to your MediSave Account to qualify for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) of up to $1,000 per year. You can top up to these accounts, anytime throughout the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What can I use the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant for?
questions.text: Matching grants granted under the Matched MediSave Scheme are credited to your MediSave Account (MA). You can use your MediSave savings to pay for approved healthcare insurance premiums (e.g. MediShield Life, CareShield Life) and approved medical treatments.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I still receive Matched MediSave Scheme grants if I am a recipient of Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS)?
questions.text: If you are a recipient of either the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB) or Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS), the cash top-ups used to qualify you for SHB or LBS will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant. Any voluntary cash top-ups to the MediSave Account that do not qualify for LBS or SHB may attract MMSS grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is implemented in January 2026. Eligibility is automatically assessed annually, and eligible members will be notified at the beginning of each year. Eligibility information will be available around the 2nd or 3rd week of January of each year, and the notifications are expected to be sent to eligible members around end January.
Checking your own eligibility:
Only members aged 55 to 70 (inclusive) may be eligible for MMSS. You can check your eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard by logging into your CPF account with Singpass.
Alternatively, when you are making cash top-up to your MediSave Account (MA), the online application form will display information on your eligibility.

questions.text: Please refer to the eligibility criteria under the Matched MediSave Scheme and assess if you qualify every criterion. You can submit an appeal via Write-To-Us.

questions.title: How do I check the amount of matching grant that I will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To find out the grant amount that you will receive under the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the following year based on this year’s cash top-ups, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard.
In addition, the dashboard will provide you with the remaining grant amount, if any, that you can receive if you make further top-ups.

questions.title: I am a self-employed person. How do I ensure that I have fully settled or are on a monthly instalment plan for my MediSave payable, so I can benefit from the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
You may check if you have fully settled or are on an active GIRO arrangement with CPF Board for your MediSave payable by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass.
If you have not made any arrangements to settle your MediSave payable, you may make full payment for your MediSave payable or request an instalment plan via the Manage your MediSave payable form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme at the beginning of the year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstances during the year?
questions.text:
Your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year is first determined at the beginning of the year. Changes to your financial circumstances (e.g. increase in monthly income) will not affect your eligibility for that year. Your eligibility for MMSS will be reassessed next year based on your new circumstances.
However, you will no longer be eligible for MMSS if:
You are no longer a Singapore Citizen within the year; or
You are a self-employed person (SEP) who has not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable
Find out more information on the conditions you need to meet to receive and keep the matching grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am self-employed and have outstanding MediSave payable. Why am I not eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme grant?
questions.text:
It is a statutory requirement for self-employed persons (SEPs) to make their mandatory MediSave contributions*. Hence, SEPs who have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable will not be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) grant.
*For platform workers, this also applies if you have outstanding MediSave payable from your platform work prior to 2025.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme this year, will I be automatically eligible in the following years?
questions.text: No, your eligibility for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is assessed annually. We will inform you at the beginning of the year if you are eligible. You can also check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will I be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme if I am turning 55 later this year?
questions.text:
Yes, you will be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) as long as you are 55 years old at the end of the assessment year and you meet the eligibility criteria.
You can check your eligibility for MMSS via Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Can I transfer my cash top-up to MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme to be used for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme instead?
questions.text:
Cash top-ups to MediSave Account made for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) cannot be transferred to Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) as the top-ups are irreversible. If you prefer to receive matching grants for retirement savings, you may consider making cash top-ups via this link for MRSS instead.
If you qualify for both MMSS and MRSS, but have limited funds to top up, you may refer to this FAQ for useful pointers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I make a cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
You can make a cash top-up to your own or your loved one’s MediSave Account (MA) via the Top up MediSave Account using PayNow QR1. Your cash top-up will be credited upon successful payment.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, please refer to this FAQ.
You may want to check whether you or your loved ones are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) before making a cash top-up.
1Subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded. To ensure that your cash top-ups are processed successfully, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once. You will need to submit a new application each time you wish to make another top-up.
For more information on how to check my and my loved ones’ eligibility for Matched MediSave, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How do I reverse the cash top up to my own MediSave Account?
questions.text: Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Is there a minimum amount I need to top up to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: There is no minimum amount of cash top-up needed to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme. However, the more you top up, the more matching grants you can receive, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What are the payment options to do the top-up to MediSave under Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Currently, members can use PayNow to make a cash top-up to yourself or your loved ones’ MediSave Account. Your cash top-up will be credited upon successful payment.
For more information on how to make cash top-up to receive the matching grant under Matched MediSave Scheme, you may refer to how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What do I need to do to receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), simply make a cash top-up to your MediSave Account (MA) by 31 Dec of the year of eligibility.
You can top up any amount using PayNow. Top-ups can be made by anyone, including yourself or your loved ones.
Your cash top-up

The matching grant will be credited to your MA at the beginning of the following year. Top-ups that attract MMSS matching grant will not qualify for tax relief.
For more information on how to make a cash top-up to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are mandatory MediSave contributions made by Self-Employed Persons that can be used to offset MediSave payable not counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
Contributions made through the Manage your MediSave payable (MMSP) form are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP), which is a statutory requirement that must be met first.
The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage additional voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave beyond these mandatory obligations. Hence, any contributions made through the MMSP form will not count towards MMSS.
Only voluntary cash top-ups made via the Top up MediSave Account (VCMA) form will be considered for MMSS, provided that SEPs have met the other eligibility criteria for MMSS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why is my voluntary cash top-up to my MediSave Account not updated in my healthcare dashboard under "Matching Grant Received This Year" for Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Voluntary cash top-ups to your MediSave Account for Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) require up to three working days to be processed and reflected in your healthcare dashboard. If you have recently made a top-up, the system may not have updated your matching grant status yet. We recommend checking your account after this processing period. Please note that top-ups eligible for MMSS cannot be claimed for tax relief purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: I am a taxi driver receiving contributions under the Drive and Save Scheme. Will these contributions be counted towards the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: Contributions made under the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme are specifically designated to fulfil your mandatory MediSave contributions as a Self-Employed Person (SEP). Hence, any contributions made under the DAS Scheme will not count towards the Matched MediSave Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Do I have to top up in a lump sum to be eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: No, you can make multiple cash top-ups throughout the year. The matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme is based on the total amount of top-ups you have received throughout the year, up to $1,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How are the matching grants and tax relief determined for my cash top-ups made to a recipient eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
If you are making a cash top-up to a recipient eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), your cash top-up of $1,000 will first enable your recipient to enjoy the matching grant of up to $1,000 per year from the Government and will thus not be eligible for tax relief. You can continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for your cash top-ups that do not attract the MMSS matching grant and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) matching grant ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
For example, if you make a cash top-up of $3,000 to your MMSS-eligible loved one (and made no other top ups), your loved one will first enjoy a matching grant of $1,000 from the Government, and you will be eligible for $2,000 of tax relief on your cash top-up that did not attract the matching grant.
For more information on the conditions for tax relief, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What conditions must I meet in order to receive and retain the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text:
To receive and retain the matching grant, you must:
Be eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year; and
Have received cash top-ups to MediSave Account (MA) during the year; and
Still be a Singapore Citizen when the matching grant is credited to your MA at the beginning of the following year.
If you are self-employed, have fully settled your MediSave payable or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What happens if I make multiple top-ups and exceed the annual matching cap of $1,000 for Matched MediSave Scheme? Will the excess top-ups be eligible for tax relief?
questions.text:
Givers of cash top-ups that attract the matching grant (up to $1,000 per year) under the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) will not receive tax relief.
However, you may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones). For more information on how to compute my tax relief for voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account, you may refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What if I pass away before receiving the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you pass away, your matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme will still be credited to your CPF account and paid out to your beneficiaries together with any remaining CPF savings.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: What incentives are there for me to top up to my loved ones under the Matched MediSave Scheme given that there is no tax relief for me?
questions.text:
Topping up to your loved ones’ MediSave accounts helps them to grow their healthcare savings and provide them with greater peace of mind.
Recipients of cash top-ups who are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) can also receive a matching grant of up to $1,000 per year from the Government, which further boosts their MediSave savings.
You may continue to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year for eligible cash top-ups that do not attract matching grants from MMSS and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme ($8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: When will I receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) and have received cash top-ups in that year, you can expect to receive the matching grant in your MediSave Account at the beginning of the following year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Why are CPF transfers not eligible for the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: The Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) is designed to encourage cash top-ups to senior Singapore Citizens with lower healthcare savings to help them save more. Thus, only cash top-ups to eligible members will be matched.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Will I still receive the matching grant under the Matched MediSave Scheme if my healthcare savings exceed 50% of the current Basic Healthcare Sum after topping up?
questions.text: Yes, you will receive the matching grant for the amount you received in cash top-up to your MediSave account as long as you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS) for the year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: Do I get tax relief for voluntary top-ups to the MediSave Account?
questions.text:
Yes, you can receive tax relief for voluntary top-ups to MediSave Account (MA), subject to specific conditions and limits:
ScenarioTax relief per yearConditions
You make a top-up to your MAUp to $8,000 for bothThe maximum top-up amount you can receive to your MA is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MediSave balance.
You are an employee/platform worker receiving a MA top-up from your employer/platform operator
You make a MA top-up to your loved onesUp to $8,000
The maximum top-up amount your loved one can receive to his/her MA is the difference between his/her Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and his/her current MediSave balance.
Spouse/sibling must have annual income ≤ $8,000 in previous year or is handicapped*
*Handicapped refers to people who are incapacitated because of physical or mental infirmity.
Important notes
Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS): From 1 January 2026, cash top-ups that qualify for the MMSS matching grant (up to $1,000/year) will not attract tax relief. Find out more on how this works.
Shared cap with Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA): $8,000 tax relief cap shared across top-ups to SA/ RA or MA.
Overall tax relief cap: Your total personal income tax relief (including CPF top-ups) is capped at $80,000/year.
Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How do I compute my tax relief for voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account?
questions.text:
The tax relief calculation depends on whether your recipient is eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS).
If your recipient is not eligible for MMSS:
You can enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000 per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000 per year for top-ups to your loved ones.
If your recipient is eligible for MMSS:
Your first $1,000 in annual cash top-ups receives government matching grant and no tax relief
For additional top-ups beyond the matched amount, you can enjoy tax relief of up to $8,000* per year for top-ups to yourself and another $8,000* per year for top-ups to your loved ones.
* The above tax relief cap applies to voluntary cash top-ups to MediSave Account and Special/Retirement Account.
Below are some examples of tax relief computation.
Example 1: In the year, you made cash top-ups totalling $3,000 to an MMSS-eligible recipient (yourself/loved one) who did not receive any other cash top-ups in the year. You did not make any other cash top-ups to yourself or others.
Calculation:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy: $1,000
Estimated tax relief you may enjoy: Total top-up amount ($3000) - Matching grant amount ($1000) = $2,000
Example 2: In the year, you made cash top-ups totalling $3,000 to an MMSS-eligible recipient (yourself/loved one) who has already received $1,000 cash top-ups and a matching grant from another giver in the same year. You did not make any other cash top-ups to yourself or others.
Calculation:
Estimated matching grant your recipient will enjoy from your cash top-up = $0
Estimated tax relief amount you may enjoy = Total top-up amount ($3000) - Matching grant amount ($0) = $3,000
To find out if your recipient is eligible for MMSS, your recipient can check his/her eligibility via the Healthcare dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account

questions.title: How do I make a top up to my MediSave Account?
questions.text:
You can make a top up to your MediSave Account using the Top up MediSave Account form and complete your payment using PayNow QR. Alternatively, you can also use the CPF mobile app and complete your payment via PayNow QR or OCBC Digital (if installed).

questions.title: Why is there no information about Singtel Special Discounted Shares (SDS) on my CPF Investment Dashboard?
questions.text: There is no information about SDS on your CPF Investment Dashboard because you do not have SDS shares. For members who successfully applied for and were allotted SDS shares during the original offering periods in 1993 and 1996, information about SDS shares will appear on their CPF Investment Dashboard. Please refer to this link for more details regarding the SDS scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do I have to top up in a single sum to be eligible for the matching grant?
questions.text: No, you can also make multiple smaller cash top-ups throughout the year. The matching grant is based on the total amount of top-ups you have received in the year, up to $2,000 per year.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: What happens to the monies granted through the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme if your loved one passes away?
questions.text:
Any unused top-up and grant monies under Matched Retirement Savings Scheme will be treated as part of the deceased member’s remaining CPF savings and will be distributed to the deceased’s beneficiaries.
If the deceased member had made a valid CPF nomination, his remaining CPF savings will be distributed in cash to his nominee(s) according to his CPF nomination. Find out more.
If the deceased member had not made a valid CPF nomination, his remaining CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution according to intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.
For more information on what happens to CPF monies, top-ups, and matching grants when a member passes away, please refer to the FAQs below:
What if my loved ones pass away before receiving the matching grant?
What are the CPF monies and assets of a deceased member covered under a CPF nomination?
Will my cash top-ups or CPF transfers be refunded to me if the recipient passes away?
What happens to a member's CPF savings when he passes away?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
