questions.title: Who is eligible to apply to be a deputy under the Mental Capacity Act?
questions.text:
To be able to apply to be a deputy under the Mental Capacity Act, you must be a 'relevant person' aged 21 or older—usually an immediate family member, close friend, or caregiver—who can convince the Court that it is in P's best interests for you to act as deputy.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/before-applying-to-be-deputy for more information.

questions.title: What initial considerations should I address before submitting a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Before applying, ensure you understand deputyship duties, assess whether P already has a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), obtain a medical report confirming P lacks capacity, and confirm consent from all other relevant persons.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/before-applying-to-be-deputy for more information.

questions.title: What documents must be prepared for a standard deputyship application?
questions.text:
The documents that you require include an originating application, support affidavit, medical report showing lack of capacity, financial statements, and proof of identity and relationship. For filings commenced before 15 October 2024, you need a Court-filed Originating Summons, doctor's medical affidavit, consent and notice forms, plus other supporting documents; they must be submitted via iFAMS or at the Court registry.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: When is it necessary to apply for deputyship using the standard process instead of the simplified one?
questions.text:
The standard process is required if the case is complex, involves disputes among family members, or if the applicant is not an immediate family member of P. It may also be necessary when financial decisions involve large sums or complex assets.
The simplified process is applicable only if all of the following applies to your case:
Only relevant persons as listed under P. 5, r.8(5) and (6) of the Family Justice (General) Rules 2024 may make an application under the simplified process.
All relevant persons to the person who lacks mental capacity (P), consent to the application. Relevant persons are people who have an involvement in P’s life and are likely to have an interest in your deputyship application.
You are applying for specific orders under the Mental Capacity Act, pursuant to Paragraph 61(2) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.
The aggregate of transactions sought should not be more than S$80,000 pursuant to Paragraph 61(2)(x) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on the differences between the standard and simplified process.

questions.title: Which law do I apply under to obtain deputyship for someone who lacks capacity?
questions.text:
You apply under the Mental Capacity Act 2008.
A deputy is an individual appointed by the court to make decisions on behalf of a person who lacks mental capacity. A deputy may be P's family member or friend.
A doctor has to certify that the person lacks mental capacity to make decisions due to an impairment of or disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain.
The Family Courts hear all deputyship applications under the Mental Capacity Act 2008.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on the differences between the standard and simplified process.

questions.title: What is the difference between the Mental Capacity Act 2008 and the Vulnerable Adults Act 2018?
questions.text:
The Vulnerable Adults Act 2018 (“VAA”) was enacted to safeguard vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect or self-neglect, and to provide for connected matters. You apply under the VAA when you want the State to intervene, in order to protect the vulnerable adults at risk of being abused, neglected or self-neglected. The VAA therefore acts as a shield for vulnerable adults from abuse or neglect.
The Mental Capacity Act 2008 (“MCA”) on the other hand was enacted to make provision relating to persons who lack capacity, and to provide for matters connected therewith. You apply under the MCA in order to appoint a deputy to make decisions relating to personal welfare, property, or affairs for an adult lacking capacity to do so. The MCA therefore allows others to act on behalf of someone lacking mental capacity. In summary, if the objective is to prevent a vulnerable adult from being abused or neglected, you should apply under the VAA.
If the aim is to appoint someone to make decisions for someone without the ability to do so, you should apply under the MCA.

questions.title: What happens after I file for a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Once filed, the Court reviews the application and the supported documents — if everything is in order, your order may be granted without you having to attend a hearing. You will be notified via iFAMS, post, and/or email, and you can then extract the formal Court Order. If clarification is needed or objections are raised, a hearing may be scheduled.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/before-applying-to-be-deputy for more information.

questions.title: What is deputyship under Singapore law and when is it needed?
questions.text:
Deputyship in Singapore refers to the legal process where the Court appoints a person (a deputy) to make decisions on behalf of someone who lacks mental capacity (referred to as 'P').
It is typically needed when P has not made a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and is unable to make decisions about their personal welfare or property and affairs.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: Who is considered a suitable candidate to be appointed as a deputy?
questions.text:
A suitable candidate for deputyship is usually a close family member or trusted individual who has a genuine concern for P's wellbeing. The Court considers the applicant's actual relationship to P, their ability to act responsibly, and any potential conflicts of interest before making the appointment. Accordingly, not all "relevant persons" may be suitable candidates.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What does it mean for someone to lack mental capacity?
questions.text:
Lacking mental capacity means that a person is unable to make decisions for themselves because of an impairment or disturbance in the functioning of their mind or brain. This can include conditions such as dementia, intellectual disabilities, or brain injuries.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What is the difference between a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and a deputyship order?
questions.text:
An LPA is a legal document made when a person still has mental capacity, appointing someone to act for them in the future.
On the other hand, a deputyship order is granted by the Court when the person already lacks capacity and no LPA is in place. Therefore, deputyship is a reactive measure.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What is the simplified deputyship application process and who qualifies for it?
questions.text:
The simplified deputyship application is a faster and more affordable route for those seeking to manage simple and uncontested matters for P. Applicants must meet certain criteria, including being an immediate family member of P and having no disputes with other family members or relevant persons.
You may apply for a simplified deputyship application via https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/services/ifams.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What is the estimated time required for a simplified deputyship application to be processed?
questions.text:
Once all documents are properly submitted and are in order, the simplified process typically takes about 4-6 weeks for the Court to review and issue a Court order.
However, this timeline may vary depending on the completeness and accuracy of the application.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What are the key responsibilities of a deputy once appointed by the Court under the Mental Capacity Act 2008?
questions.text:
A deputy is legally obligated to act in P's best interests, making decisions about personal welfare, healthcare, or property and finances based on what P would have wanted. Where the Order of Court provides that a certain act be done within a specified time frame, such action must be taken as ordered. Deputies must also keep records, avoid conflicts of interest, and may be required to report to the Office of the Public Guardian.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: Can a deputy make all types of decisions for P, or are there limitations?
questions.text:
Deputies are only allowed to make decisions specifically authorised by the Court order. They cannot make decisions outside the scope granted by the Court, such as consenting to marriage, divorce, or making a will on behalf of P.
Sections 25 and 26 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008 sets out some of these restrictions and excluded decisions.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: How much does it cost to apply for deputyship in Singapore?
questions.text:
For the simplified track, the application fee is S$40. For the standard route, filing fees vary and may range from S$300 - S$500, depending on the complexity of the case and the number of forms or documents filed.
Additional costs for both tracks may include medical reports and legal assistance or representation, if required.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What happens if someone wants to contest a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Any relevant person—such as a family member or someone with a genuine interest in P's welfare—can file an objection. The Court will then assess whether the objection is valid and may call for a hearing to resolve the matter.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: Can the Court appoint more than one deputy for the same person?
questions.text:
Yes, the Court can appoint multiple deputies for P. Typically, for the simplified track, there is a maximum of 2 deputies and 2 successor deputies; while for the standard track, the Court would normally not appoint more than 4 deputies.
Deputies may be appointed to act jointly (together) or jointly and severally (either one can act independently). The arrangement will be based on what is in P's best interests.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: What is a successor deputy and when should one be appointed?
questions.text:
A successor deputy is someone designated to take over deputyship if the current deputy is unable or unwilling to continue. This ensures continuity in decision-making for P, especially when the primary deputy becomes incapacitated or passes away.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: How long does a deputyship order last?
questions.text:
A deputyship order generally remains in effect for as long as P lacks mental capacity, unless the order of court specifies that it is valid for a specific period of time or until the Court revokes it. If circumstances change, such as P regaining capacity or the deputy resigning, the order can be reviewed. Each case depends on its own specific circumstances.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on deputyship applications in general.

questions.title: Can a deputy resign or be removed from their role?
questions.text:
Yes, a deputy may apply to resign with stated reasons as to how this would be in P’s best interests, and the Court can remove a deputy if they fail to act in P's best interests or breach their duties.
The Office of the Public Guardian can also recommend removal following investigations.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on deputyship applications in general.

questions.title: What oversight exists to ensure that deputies are acting responsibly?
questions.text:
The Office of the Public Guardian monitors deputies and may require them to submit periodic reports, including accounts of financial decisions made. The Court also retains the power to intervene in cases of misconduct or negligence.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on deputyship applications in general.

questions.title: Can a deputy apply to vary the deputyship order after it has been granted?
questions.text:
Yes, if there are significant changes in P's condition or needs, or if new powers are required, a deputy can apply to the Court to vary the existing order. The Court will consider whether the variation is in P's best interests.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information on deputyship applicatoins in general.

questions.title: How does the Court define a 'relevant person' in a deputyship application?
questions.text:
A relevant person is typically someone aged 21 or older who has a close relationship with P or an interest in P's welfare. They may be consulted during the application process and are entitled to raise objections if necessary.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: Where can I find the deputyship application forms and further guidance?
questions.text:
All deputyship forms and procedural guidelines are available on the Singapore Judiciary's official website under the Family Justice Courts section. It is advisable to read all instructions carefully before applying.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information, or https://epd2024-familyjusticecourts.judiciary.gov.sg/ for the list of forms available.

questions.title: Will I be reimbursed for expenses incurred in carrying out my duties as a Deputy?
questions.text: Under section 10 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008, if you have incurred reasonable expenses for P’s benefit, you may reimburse yourself out of money in P’s actual possession when performing your duties as a Deputy.

questions.title: If I have already been assigned as a deputy, where do I file my deputy reports?
questions.text:
A deputy is legally obligated to act in P's best interests, making decisions about personal welfare, healthcare, or property and finances based on what P would have wanted. Deputies must keep records, avoid conflicts of interest, and may be required to report to the Office of the Public Guardian.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship for more information.

questions.title: Who is allowed to object to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Any 'relevant person' may object to a deputyship application. This includes the person alleged to lack mental capacity, their spouse, children, parents, or other close relatives or caregivers who have a legitimate interest in the person's welfare.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What are the steps involved in objecting to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
To object, you must file an affidavit with the Family Justice Courts stating your reasons for objection. This affidavit must be filed within 21 days of receiving the Originating Summons and must be served on the applicant and other parties involved.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What should I include in my affidavit of objection when objecting to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Your affidavit should clearly state your relationship to the person, your concerns or objections to the deputyship application, and any supporting evidence such as documents or a medical report.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Is there a deadline to file my objection to someone else's deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes, you must file your affidavit of objection within 21 calendar days from the date you are served with the Originating Summons for the deputyship application.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What happens if I miss the 21-day deadline to file an objection?
questions.text:
If you miss the deadline, you may apply for leave (permission) from the Court to file your affidavit late. You must provide valid reasons for the delay.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Can the person alleged to lack capacity object to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes, the individual at the centre of the application can object if they believe they have mental capacity. A medical report supporting this claim must be included in their affidavit.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: If I was not named in a deputyship application, but I am concerned, can I still object?
questions.text:
Yes. You can apply to be added as a party in the proceedings. Once added as a 'relevant person', you may file your objection through an affidavit.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Do I need a medical report to support my objection to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
If you are asserting that the person still has mental capacity, your affidavit must be supported by a recent medical report prepared by a qualified professional.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Will there be a Court hearing if I object to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes. If an objection is filed, the Court will typically fix a hearing or a case conference to understand the basis of the objection and determine the appropriate next steps.
During the hearing, the Court will listen to both the objector and the applicant. The judge will evaluate the evidence presented to determine if the application should proceed or be modified.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Can I change my mind and withdraw my objection to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes, you may withdraw your affidavit of objection by filing a formal notice with the Court. If a hearing has been scheduled, inform the Court as early as possible.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Are there penalties if someone files a baseless or malicious objection to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes. The Court may order costs against any party who files a frivolous or vexatious objection that wastes time or misuses the Court process.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Can more than one person object to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes, multiple relevant persons may file separate affidavits if they each wish to raise different concerns or support a joint objection.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Can the Court appoint a different deputy if objections are raised?
questions.text:
Yes, the Court may decide not to appoint the proposed deputy and instead appoint another suitable individual if it is in the best interests of the person lacking capacity.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/object-to-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Where can I get legal help to file an objection to a deputyship application?
questions.text:
You may consult a lawyer, seek help from the Legal Aid Bureau, Community Justice Centre, or the Office of the Public Guardian. They will be able to guide you through the objection process.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/legal-help-support for more information.

questions.title: Who can file a simplified deputyship application online?
questions.text:
Any person (the applicant) who wishes to become a deputy under the simplified track can file online via iFAMS using their Singpass, provided the case meets the simplified process criteria. Generally, only relevant persons as listed under P. 5, r.8(5) and (6) of the Family Justice (General) Rules 2024 may make an application under the simplified process.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What conditions must be met for a case to qualify for the simplified deputyship process?
questions.text:
The simplified track applies only if all relevant persons consent and the orders sought are among the prescribed list—such as handling up to S$80,000 of funds or consenting to medical treatment.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.
Note:
The prescribed list is pursuant to Paragraph 61(2) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.
The aggregate of transactions sought should not be more than S$80,000 pursuant to Paragraph 61(2)(x) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.

questions.title: Which types of orders can be made under the simplified process?
questions.text:
Orders include withdrawing up to S$80,000 from P's bank accounts, consenting to medical/dental treatment, deciding on care services, opening/closing bank accounts, CPF matters, managing property renovations, and legal proceedings, among others.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.
Note:
The prescribed list is pursuant to Paragraph 61(2) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.
The aggregate of transactions sought should not be more than S$80,000 pursuant to Paragraph 61(2)(x) of the Family Justice Court Practice Directions.

questions.title: What is the maximum aggregate amount of money the deputy can use for P under simplified deputyship?
questions.text:
The total withdrawals from P's accounts under simplified deputyship must not exceed S$80,000. CPF funds may be handled separately up to S$60,000.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What happens after I file the simplified deputyship application?
questions.text:
After filing, relevant persons have up to 3 months to indicate consent in iFAMS. You pay the S$40 fee only after all consents are received. If all is in order, the Court will email you the deputyship order.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What if one of the relevant persons does not consent to my deputyship application?
questions.text:
If any relevant person objects or does not consent within 3 months, the case becomes ineligible for the simplified process and must follow the standard process.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Is attendance required in Court with the simplified track deputyship application?
questions.text:
Typically, no hearing is needed if your application is clear and no objections are raised. However, the Court may request your presence for clarification when necessary.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: Can urgent funding be requested before the full simplified order is granted?
questions.text:
Yes—an emergency withdrawal of up to S$5,000 from a POSB/DBS account may be applied for with consent from P's immediate family and typically processed within 3 working days.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What documentation is required to file the simplified deputyship application?
questions.text:
You need a medical report (submitted online via iFAMS by a doctor), completed application forms, and consent from all relevant persons. Specific forms are listed on the iFAMS portal.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What legislation and rules apply to simplified deputyship applications?
questions.text:
Applications for filings on or after 15 Oct 2024 follow the Family Justice (General) Rules 2024 (Parts 5–7) and relevant Practice Directions 4C, 5, and 6C.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What support resources are available for applicants who are considering making a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Guidance includes downloadable specimen medical certificates, deputyship brochures (ENG, CHN, MAL, TAM), and iFAMS user guides.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What happens if clarification or objections arise after filing for a simplified deputyship application?
questions.text:
The Court may schedule a hearing or request further documentation if clarification is needed or objections arise during the Court's review.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: How does simplified deputyship differ from the standard process?
questions.text:
Simplified deputyship is faster (4–6 weeks), cheaper (S$40), and limited in scope.
In contrast, the standard process costs between S$300–$500, takes 3–4 months, requires eLitigation filing, and accommodates broader or contested orders.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-simplified-deputyship-application for more information.

questions.title: What is a standard deputyship application?
questions.text:
It is the formal process by which one applies to the Family Justice Courts under the Mental Capacity Act for authority to make decisions on behalf of a person who lacks capacity.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: Is a medical report mandatory in a deputyship application?
questions.text:
Yes. A medical assessment, typically from a specialist, confirming the individual's lack of capacity, is required.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: What are the filing fees for a standard-track application?
questions.text:
You will incur Court filing fees which typically ranges from S$300 to S$500, depending on the documents you need to file.
These fees excludes other fees payable to doctors for the medical report and fees to affirm or swear affidavits, or if you decide to engage a legal professional to represent you in Court.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: How do I file the application for a standard deputyship?
questions.text:
File at the Family Justice Courts Registry, ensuring all forms, affidavits, reports, and fees are submitted together.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: How long does the typical standard deputyship application process take?
questions.text:
Typically, it would take about 3–4 months for the matter to conclude under normal circumstances. A longer time will be needed if hearings or objections occur.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: What are the powers a deputy can have?
questions.text:
Deputies may be granted power over property, finances, personal welfare, healthcare, or combinations thereof as ordered by the Court.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: What if the person regains capacity or passes away?
questions.text:
The deputyship order ceases either when the person regains capacity or dies. The deputy must inform the Court and Public Guardian. They will have to file an application for the deputy to be discharged so there will be no inconsistent Court Order in the records.
Please refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/file-deputyship-application-standard for more information.

questions.title: What is the change to the Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
The Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) was raised on 1 January 2026 to double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This provides CPF members aged 55 and above the option to voluntarily top up more to their Retirement Account (RA) for even higher monthly payouts in retirement.
You can top up your RA with cash or your Ordinary Account (OA) savings. Topping up your RA allows you to receive higher monthly payouts in retirement. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts through CPF top-ups.
For example, a member who is 55 in the current year could receive up to $3,400 monthly for life when they turn 65. Learn more about the payouts you can receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How much CPF monthly payout can I receive if I top up to the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
Your CPF monthly payout depends on several factors, including the age when you set aside the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) and when you start receiving payouts.
Illustrative Monthly Payouts for CPF LIFE Standard Plan:
Scenario
Monthly Payout
Age 55 in 2026 and top up to ERS in 2026
$3,200 – $3,400 from age 65
Age 65 in 2026, set aside your Full Retirement Sum at age 55 and top up to ERS in 2026

For a personalised estimate, please use the Monthly payout estimator.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check the amount that I can top up to my Retirement Account to reach the raised Enhanced Retirement Sum in 2026?
questions.text:
You may check your top-up limit on your Retirement Dashboard on 1 January 2026 once the Enhanced Retirement Sum is raised.
Find out how the top-up limit is computed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: From 2025, how are the matching grants and tax relief determined for my cash top-ups made to my loved ones eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
The first $2,000 of your cash top-ups to a Matched Retirement Saving Scheme (MRSS)-eligible loved one will be matched by the Government (up to $2,000 a year).
Cash top-ups that qualify for the MRSS matching grant will not qualify for tax relief.
Any cash top-ups above $2,000 will qualify for tax relief, subject to the conditions for tax relief. You can top up more to enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 a year.
Example
If you top up $3,000 to your MRSS-eligible parent in 2025:
First $2,000-> qualifies for Government matching grant (no tax relief).
Next $1,000 -> qualifies for tax relief.
For more detailed examples on how tax relief is computed, see How is tax relief computed for my cash top-ups to Special Account/Retirement Account?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: When will I receive the grant for current year’s cash top-ups made?
questions.text:
If you have received cash top-ups this year, the matching grant will generally be credited to your Retirement or Special Account by end February of the following year. You will be notified via email or post when the grant has been credited. You may also check your Transaction history. Please note the matching grant is capped at $2,000 a year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000.
For example, if you receive cash top-ups in 2026, the matching grant will generally be credited to your Retirement or Special Account by end February 2027.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am below age 55 and my disability status has not yet been verified with MSF. Once it is verified, will I become immediately eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
If you are below age 55 and complete your verification of disability status with MSF before 1 November of the current year, it will be used to assess your Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility annually from the following year.
For example, a member age below 55 who had verified his disability status with MSF before 1 November 2025 will have his MRSS eligibility automatically assessed annually from the following year (2026) onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: After my disability status is verified with MSF, how do I apply for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS)?
questions.text:
You do not need to apply for Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) after your disability status is verified. We will automatically assess your eligibility yearly at the beginning of each year. If you are below age 55, you will need to have your disability status verified with Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) before 1 November of the current year to be assessed for MRSS eligibility for the next year onwards.
For example, a member age below 55 who had verified his disability status with MSF before 1 November 2025 will have his MRSS eligibility automatically assessed annually from the following year (2026) onwards.
If you are eligible, we will notify you via email or post at the beginning of each year. You can also check your MRSS eligibility via the Retirement Dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why do CareShield Life premiums increase over time, and by how much annually?
questions.text:
Annual increases in CareShield Life payouts help protect the value of CareShield Life payouts over time. This needs to be supported by annual increases in CareShield Life premiums. To give Singaporeans greater certainty in the first five years, payouts and premiums* each increased by 2% per year from 2021 to 2025.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. To support this, premiums will increase annually, with premium support measures moderating increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.
The CareShield Life Council regularly reviews these trends and advises the Government on CareShield Life premium and payout adjustments in accordance with an actuarially sound adjustment framework. The Government will consider affordability of premiums when reviewing the council’s advice on premium adjustments.
*Premiums increase per year excludes GST.

questions.title: Why is my CareShield Life premiums payable until age 67?
questions.text:
Starting the CareShield Life premium payment duration at age 30, and ending at age 67 gives you a longer period to spread your premium payments, hence reducing the annual premiums payable.
The age at which premium payments end may be subsequently reviewed to take into consideration the changes in the re-employment age.

questions.title: Where can I find my CareShield Life premiums information?
questions.text: You may refer to the CareShield Life Premium Checker e-Service to view your premium details and premium support.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life Premiums increase and what happens after I reach 67?
questions.text:
CareShield Life premiums are designed to increase regularly to support the regular increase in payouts. The schedule of premium increases is not fixed, and will be regularly reviewed by the CareShield Life Council to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.
Following CareShield Life 2025 Review, payouts will increase by 4% per year from 2026 to 2030 to help policyholders keep up with rising long-term care costs. To support this, premiums will increase annually, with premium support measures moderating increases from 2026 to 2030 to about $38 on average and no more than $75.
If you are age 59 and above when you join CareShield Life, you will not have to pay premiums after 10 years.
If you are age 58 and below when you join CareShield Life, you will have to pay premiums until you reach age 67 (inclusive of the year you turn age 67). Thereafter, you will no longer need to pay for CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: What are the CPF allocation rates for 2026?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, the CPF contribution rates for employees aged above 55 to 65 are increased to strengthen their retirement adequacy.
Upon the closure of the Special Account (SA) for CPF members aged 55 and above, the CPF contributions allocated to SA will be fully allocated to the member’s Retirement Account (RA), up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the Ordinary Account.
You may refer to the CPF allocation rate table (PDF, 0.1 MB) for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can anyone, including entities, make voluntary top ups to my MediSave Account? How do I check if anyone has topped up for me?
questions.text:
Anyone, including entities (Community Partners, NGO, etc.) can make voluntary top-ups to your MediSave Account (MA). Entities will need to submit their intention to make voluntary top-ups to your MA. See more here.
If you are eligible for the Matched MediSave Scheme (MMSS), you can check if anyone has topped up to your MA on your Healthcare dashboard. The estimated cash top-ups you have received this year which will qualify you for the matching grant will be reflected.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: If I am a non-profit organisation and want to top up to a specific member, how can my organisation make such top-up and how do I know if the recipient of the top up will benefit from Matched MediSave Scheme?
questions.text: You can submit your request to make voluntary top-ups to specific members here and we will assess if the member is eligible and inform you accordingly.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my Government cash grants or benefits received for the year?
questions.text: We have moved records of CPF-administered cash grants from the Yearly Statement of Account to YourBenefits@LifeSG, as it provides a more comprehensive view of common Government-provided benefits you have received, covering schemes from multiple agencies including CPF Board. You would require Singpass to login. Please refer to the FAQ for more details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: As a platform operator, what are the conditions for me to enjoy tax deductions when I make Voluntary Contributions for my platform workers?
questions.text:
As a platform operator, you can enjoy tax deductions when you make Voluntary Contributions (VC) to your platform workers under the following conditions:
For cash top-ups to the Special or Retirement Account (SA/RA) of your platform worker under the Retirement Sum Topping-up Scheme, you will be eligible for an equivalent amount of tax deductions for the cash top-ups made. While such a cash top-up will be included in your platform worker’s taxable income, your platform worker will receive tax relief of up to $8,000 for cash top-ups made in each calendar year. The tax relief that your platform worker will receive also takes into consideration any cash top-ups that he has made to his own SA/RA and MediSave Account (MA).
For cash top-up to the MA (up to the Basic Healthcare Sum, which can qualify your platform workers for the Matched MediSave Scheme), you will be eligible for an equivalent amount of tax deductions for the cash top-ups made. While such a cash top-up will be included in your platform worker’s taxable income, your platform worker will receive tax relief* of up to $8,000 for cash top-ups made in each calendar year. The tax relief that your platform worker will receive also takes into consideration any cash top-ups that he has made to his own SA/RA and MA.
For VC to your platform worker’s MA (up to the platform worker’s CPF Annual Limit), you will enjoy tax deductions on the voluntary MediSave contributions of up to $2,730 per platform worker. These contributions are also tax exempt up to $2,730 for the platform worker, but will not qualify the worker for the Matched MediSave Scheme.
* If your platform workers are eligible to receive matching grant under the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme or the Matched MediSave Scheme, they will not receive tax relief for the top-ups that attract the matching grant.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Making voluntary CPF contributions

questions.title: When will I receive my monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts?
questions.text: You can expect to receive your monthly CareShield Life/ElderShield/MediSave Care payouts by the middle of each month.

questions.title: What are the conditions for me to enjoy tax relief to Special Account or Retirement Account?

Use Cash Top-ups and CPF Transfers for Retirement Form to view the tax relief you will receive on your top-up and make your cash top-up.
Only cash top-ups qualify for tax relief, and it depends on who you are topping up to and whether the amount is up to current year’s Full Retirement Sum (FRS).

Shared cap with MediSave Account (MA): $8,000 tax relief cap shared across top-ups to Special Account (SA)/ Retirement Account (RA) or MA.
Overall tax relief cap: Your total personal income tax relief (including CPF top-ups) is capped at $80,000/year.
Learn more about tax relief.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Where can I access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs)?
questions.text:
Eligible individuals can access subsidised referrals to public specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs) regardless of their Healthier SG enrolment status, as follows:
Singapore Citizens: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics. If you hold a CHAS, Merdeka Generation (MG), or Pioneer Generation (PG) card, you can also get subsidised referrals at CHAS clinics.
Permanent Residents: You can get subsidised referrals at polyclinics.
Enrolment in Healthier SG is not required for subsidised referrals.

questions.title: I am a senior and have received a letter on Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility. I do not understand the content in English. Is there a translated version?
questions.text:
If you have received a letter on your Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) eligibility and would like to view the translated contents, please refer to the following:

questions.title: I am eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme this year. Will I still be eligible if there are changes to my circumstances during the year?
questions.text:
Yes, you will still be eligible for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) for the year even if your circumstances change (e.g. increase in monthly income) during the year. Your eligibility for MRSS will be assessed next year based on your new circumstances.
However, do note that renouncing your Singapore citizenship during the year will make you ineligible for the scheme and matching grant.
Find out about the conditions which you need to meet to receive and keep the matching grant.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: I am a person with disability below 55. How can I check if I am verified as a person with disability and what should I do if I am not yet verified?
questions.text: The disability verification process is managed by SG Enable on behalf of MSF. To check whether you are verified or how to be verified, or to find out more information on the disability verification process, please refer to the Enabling Guide. For any further queries, please contact SG Enable at contactus@sgenable.sg or the hotline at 1800-8585-885.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Can I commence my monthly housing instalment if my application to be covered under Home Protection Scheme is pending or rejected?
questions.text:
Yes, you can still use your CPF savings to pay your monthly housing instalments even if your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application is still pending. You do not need to wait for HPS approval to begin your payments.
This applies even if your HPS application was rejected due to health conditions.
Find out more:
How do I apply to use my CPF savings for my housing loan monthly instalments?
What are the alternatives available if I am not eligible for a Home Protection Scheme cover?
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Within how many days must all co-owners submit our Home Protection Scheme applications to meet the 100% coverage requirement?
questions.text: All co-owners must submit their Home Protection Scheme applications within the next three calendar days of the first application being received. Please note that your application would be rejected if the household 100% coverage is not met as we did not receive all your applications within the next three calendar days.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How long does it take to process my MediShield Life Suspension application?
questions.text:
As relevant agencies may take some time to verify your permanent residency or other status, the processing of MediShield Life Suspension application may take up to three months or longer, depending on its complexity. We will inform you of the outcome once we have assessed your application.
Please visit our website at cpf.gov.sg/HealthcareFinancing if you need more information or write to us at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: I have already submitted my application for suspension of MediShield Life premium collection. It is pending approval. Why am I still receiving reminder letters to pay my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The premiums for your MediShield Life cover are still payable while your application is being processed. If your application is successful, premium collection will be suspended prospectively from the next policy year based on the date of receipt of your application.
Any outstanding premiums prior to the start of the Suspension Period remain payable. Please make payment promptly with the payment modes available to avoid any further enforcement action.

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why is the coverage status reflected as ‘Waiting for Cover’ on my Healthcare dashboard?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life coverage status will be reflected as 'Active' after your first premium is successfully deducted, which will take about two months after your application is approved.
However, please be assured that you will still be eligible for claims while your coverage status is 'Waiting for Cover'.

questions.title: My CareShield Life coverage status on my Healthcare dashboard is reflected as 'Waiting for Cover'. Will I be able to claim from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
As your CareShield Life application has been approved, you will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after your CareShield Life policy start date. This applies even if the premiums have not been deducted.
If you wish to claim from CareShield Life, you can submit your application via the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS) Application Portal using your Singpass.

questions.title: Will the nominee(s) and next-of-kin be notified to claim the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text:
If the deceased member had made a valid nomination, we will contact the nominee(s) within 10 working days after the Board is notified of the member's passing, providing them with details on the withdrawal process.
If the deceased member had not made a valid nomination, we will contact the next-of-kin at the deceased member's last known address, informing them that the CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution and details to claim the discounted Singtel shares (if any).
In some rare cases, there may be ongoing investigations related to a member’s nomination and the Board would require additional time before contacting the nominee(s). Interested parties can contact the Board at write to us to find out the status of the case.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Can the nominee instruct the Board when to sell the discounted Singtel shares at a certain price?
questions.text:
To sell the discounted Singtel shares at a certain price, the shares should be transferred to the nominee’s Central Depository (Pte) Ltd (CDP) account so that there is control over the sale of shares.
If the nominee wishes for the shares to be transferred to his CDP account, he will need to instruct us within six weeks from the notification of the member’s death. If we do not receive any instructions from the nominee within six weeks, we will sell the shares. The sale proceeds will be disbursed to the nominee, together with other nominated CPF monies, in cash. Find out what are the conditions under which we would sell the deceased member's discounted Singtel shares.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Will the Board sell the discounted Singtel shares upon the death of CPF member?
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Where can I find records of top-ups made to me?
questions.text:
You can view top-ups made in the:
Last five years
You can find records of top-ups made to you in the Retirement Savings Topping-Up History under “Received from” tab.
Beyond five years
You can access your CPF Transaction History through your Yearly Statement of Account. Please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Do I need to inform CPF Board the death of a CPF member?
questions.text:
If the deceased person was a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who passed away in Singapore, the relevant agencies will inform CPF Board of the death so you do not need to do so.
If the deceased person was a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who passed away overseas, you will need to report death to ICA.
If the deceased person was a foreigner with a CPF account, you will have to inform CPF Board of his death.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: I am a nominee. How will the deceased member's CPF savings be paid to me?
questions.text:
Your share of the deceased member’s CPF savings will be paid to you via:
PayNow to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account; or
Bank transfer via Interbank GIRO to your bank account
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How long will it take for the withdrawal amount to be refunded to the deceased's CPF account if the PayNow/IBG transaction was unsuccessful?
questions.text: The amount will be returned to the deceased's CPF account generally within four working days.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How do I know if I am eligible for Singpass?
questions.text: Please visit www.singpass.gov.sg to check your eligibility for Singpass.

questions.title: Why is it compulsory for me to use Singpass?
questions.text: Singpass is the common password used to transact online with different Government agencies. With Singpass, you no longer need to remember different passwords when transacting with Government agencies. Singpass provides greater authenticity on the person transacting online.

questions.title: When should a society hold its Annual General Meeting?
questions.text:
A society should hold its Annual General Meeting (AGM) in accordance with the requirements and timeline stipulated in its constitution. Its Annual Return must be submitted within 1 month after the AGM.
For more information, refer to Annual Returns .

questions.title: What is the fee for the registration of a society?
questions.text: Please refer to the fees as prescribed in the Societies Regulations.

questions.title: How long would I be able to save my draft application/submission in ROS eServices?
questions.text: Please note that the draft application/submission would be purged from the system if no action to verify and submit the application/submission is taken after 6 months.

questions.title: What is a society?
questions.text: A society is defined in the Societies Act as a club, company, partnership or association of 10 or more persons, whatever its nature or object, and not already registered under any other law.

questions.title: The following are common enquiries that can be addressed through other dedicated digital services and do not require an objection to be filed: (i) [Owner-occupier concession] I only own one property. I have moved back into my property which was previously let out. Please revise the tax rate/AV accordingly. (ii) [Newly completed landed residential property] My property is recently completed and have obtained TOP/CSC. Please revise my AV accordingly. (iii) [GIRO instalment plan] I would like to apply for GIRO instalment/ make changes to my existing GIRO instalment payment plan.
questions.text:
Before filing an objection, please note that the following enquiries can be addressed through other dedicated digital services:
(i) [Owner-occupier concession] If you would like to apply for the concessionary Owner-Occupier Tax rates, please do not file an objection, instead please:
1. Log in to mytax.iras.gov.sg with your Singpass
2. Select 'Property’
3. Select 'Apply/ Withdraw Owner-Occupier Tax Rates'
(ii) [Newly completed landed residential property] If you would like to inform us of the completion of your property (i.e. TOP/CSC obtained), please do not file an objection. Instead, please log in to myTax Portal and inform us via myTax Mail (secured correspond channel).
(iii) [GIRO Application] If you would like to apply for GIRO instalment/make changes to existing GIRO instalment plans, please do so via myTax Portal. Please refer to linked user guide (for individuals).

questions.title: What should you do if you want to nominate Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS), Mosques, or Madrasahs as your CPF nominee?
questions.text:
A nominee in a CPF nomination must be a legal entity. While all mosques and madrasahs in Singapore are non-legal entities, they are however vested entities under Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS).
If you intend to nominate any Singapore-based mosque or madrasah, you will need to nominate MUIS as a nominee. Please visit MUIS website to find out more on nominating MUIS.
If you nominate MUIS as a nominee in your CPF nomination, you should also inform MUIS via this form https://go.gov.sg/muis-cpfnomination.
If you wish to find out more information on nominating MUIS as a nominee, please contact MUIS at https://www.muis.gov.sg/contact-us.

questions.title: What unique identification number should I indicate for my foreign nominee in my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
We strongly recommend using the NRIC number equivalent to your foreign nominee’s home country as your nominee will need to produce the official document bearing this number when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.
If your nominee’s home country does not use an NRIC equivalent number for its citizens, please provide any other unique identification numbers by the home country’s government that is permanent. Your nominee must be able to produce the official document bearing this identification number when they apply to withdraw your CPF savings (upon your passing).
Nominees may face delays in receiving the deceased member’s CPF savings if they cannot produce the relevant documents bearing the unique identification number indicated in the deceased member’s CPF nomination.

questions.title: My nominee recently became a Singapore Citizen/Singapore Permanent Resident. Should I update their identification number?
questions.text: Yes, please update your nominee's identification number to their new NRIC number as soon as possible to ensure their records are current and accurate.

questions.title: My nominee has dual nationality. Which identification number should I provide in my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
You may check with your nominee(s) which national identification number they would prefer. Your nominee(s) will need to produce the official document bearing this number when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.
Nominees may face delays in receiving the deceased member’s CPF savings if they cannot produce the relevant documents bearing the unique identification number indicated in the deceased member’s CPF nomination.

questions.title: Can I indicate my nominee's work permit, employment pass or FIN number as their identification number in my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
No. These numbers are issued by Singapore authorities and are linked to immigration status. They can change or expire, and your nominees may not retain possession of their work permits, employment passes for which they will need to produce when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.
Nominees may face delays in receiving the deceased member’s CPF savings if they cannot produce the relevant documents bearing the unique identification number indicated in the deceased member’s CPF nomination.

questions.title: How do I view and update employer details in 'Account Settings'?
questions.text:
You can view and update your employer particulars such as principal place of business address and contact details in the 'Account Settings'.
(i) Principal place of business and contact details:
Login using your Singpass and go to 'Account Settings'. You can view or update your business address or contact details of the owner/employer representative and persons in charge of CPF contribution matters.
If you are an individual trading under your own name, you can only update the particulars for your own CPF Submission Number (CSN).
(ii) Employer name:
Write to us to update the details if you have recently made changes to the entity's name through your Unique Entity Number (UEN) issuance agency or the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority.
Update your employer details immediately when they change to ensure you receive important CPF information without delay.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: Why is there still an application fee if my application is made online?
questions.text: A fee is required for every passport application to cover the system and maintenance costs required for back-end processing.

questions.title: I am unable to submit my passport application online and would like to do it over the counter. Do I need to make an appointment?
questions.text: If you prefer to apply in person, visit the ICA Services Centre between 0800hrs and 1630hrs, Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays). While you do not need to schedule an appointment for this, please allow for some waiting time. The passport application fee payable is S$80.

questions.title: Why has ICA stopped accepting passport applications by post?
questions.text: We no longer accept passport applications by post. Online applications make it convenient to apply anytime, anywhere, with Singpass automatically populating your information for a more secure and seamless experience when applying for a passport.

questions.title: If I have withdrawn under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme, can I still apply to withdraw a lump sum from age 55 and payout eligibility age for my immediate retirement needs?
questions.text: No, you will no longer be able to make lump sum withdrawals from age 55 and payout eligibility age for your immediate retirement needs as the withdrawable savings are already paid out to you earlier under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme.

questions.title: How can I access my vaccination records, and what should I do if some records are missing?
questions.text:
Singaporeans who are born in 1996 or later are able to access their vaccination records via HealthHub with their Singpass.
Those who are born earlier (i.e. before 1996) are also able to access their vaccination records via HealthHub but only for records of vaccinations under the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS), which were given on or after 1 Nov 2017, and notified accordingly.
Recently Administered Vaccines: Contact the clinic where you received the vaccine to ensure they have submitted your records to the National Immunisation Registry (CDA-NIR).
Vaccination Records: For other inquiries regarding your vaccination records, you may reach out to CDA-NIR for assistance.

questions.title: If I paid the option fee for a resale condo on 15 May 2025 and exercise the Option to Purchase (OTP) on 9 July 2025, will I be subject to Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) if I sell the condo in 2028?
questions.text:
Yes. As the property is purchased on 9 Jul 2025, the holding period is 4 years. If you sell the property before 9 Jul 2029, you will be subjected to the SSD rates of 4%-16%. If you sell the property on or after 9 July 2029, no SSD is payable.
You may refer to Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for more information on SSD and its stipulated holding period.

questions.title: If I acquire partial share in a residential property from my co-owner, what would be the Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) applicable if the property is subsequently sold within the SSD holding period?
questions.text:
As you had acquired part share in the property at different times, the SSD holding period for each part share acquired will be computed from the respective acquisition date. If you sell the property within the relevant SSD holding period, you will be subjected to the SSD rates of 4%-16%.
You may refer to Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for more information on SSD and its stipulated holding period.

questions.title: Under the SNSS scheme, if my nominee is an underaged child (below age 16) and passes away, what happens to my CPF savings bequeathed to this child under SNSS, and what happens to my child's own CPF savings?
questions.text:
Under Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), if a nominee is an underaged child below 16 years old, the CPF savings bequeathed to the child under SNSS scheme will form part of the child's estate.
As for the child's own CPF savings; since the child is below 16 years of age and the minimum age requirement to make a CPF nomination is 16 years old and above, the child's own CPF savings is considered un-nominated, and would be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act or the Administration of Muslim Law (for Muslims).

questions.title: How do I avoid falling prey to phishing scams?
questions.text:
Your financial safety matters to us.
Here are some tips on how to protect yourself against phishing scams pretending to come from CPF Board:
Do not share your Singpass or bank log-in details with anyone. CPF officers will NEVER ask for your Singpass or bank log-in details.
Check the source of the message. CPF Board will only contact you through these official channels:
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
SMSes will only be sent from "gov.sg" sender ID.
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
WhatsApp sender is "CPF Board Text Us" with the blue badge. This is our official business account with the phone number 6031 5753.
Stay vigilant and examine the links embedded in the message. Messages from CPF Board may contain links to Government websites. Before clicking on such links, please check that the domain of the link ends with “.gov.sg” by hovering your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
Report any suspicious messages spoofing CPF Board via our CPF official hotline or Write to us. If unsure, check with the ScamShield app or call the 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: What are the anti-scam security measures available to CPF members?
questions.text:
CPF Board adopts a multi-pronged approach in safeguarding members' CPF savings from scams. This includes empowering members with self-help measures and working with other Government agencies and banks to enhance the overall ecosystem's scam detection capabilities. We prioritise security above convenience and continually review the evolving scam landscape and enhance our measures accordingly.
For example, in addition to our existing safeguards such as ensuring that CPF savings are credited to bank accounts that are verified to belong to the members, Singpass Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) and enhanced authentication measures, we have implemented a suite of measures to better partner our members in safeguarding their CPF savings from scams. These measures include:
Trusted Contact notification service
Members can appoint a trusted individual, such as a family member, to receive a copy of their notifications for the following important CPF transactions:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact detail update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
This gives members an additional safeguard by allowing a trusted individual to help identify unusual transactions and act quickly if needed. To find out more about the Trusted Contact notification service, please visit cpf.gov.sg/trustedcontact.
CPF Safety Switch
Members aged 55 and above who suspect their CPF account has been compromised or have fallen victim to a scam can immediately secure their CPF accounts by activating the CPF Safety Switch. Once activated:
All disbursements to members' registered bank account will cease, including any withdrawals currently being processed; and
Access to CPF online services through the CPF website and mobile app will be disabled, preventing unauthorised future withdrawals from members’ CPF accounts.
However, all incoming CPF contributions or recurring payments to organisations for housing and insurance will remain unaffected to minimise disruptions.
Daily Withdrawal Limit
A limit that all CPF members aged 55 and above can set to determine the maximum daily amount they want to withdraw online. The amount withdrawable by CPF members aged 55 and above remains subjected to the current withdrawal rules.
All CPF members aged 55 and above will have their online Daily Withdrawal Limit defaulted at $2,000 for a start. Members who prefer a different Daily Withdrawal Limit can adjust it up to a maximum of $50,000, at any time under Account settings. Increases to the Daily Withdrawal Limit may require enhanced authentication. There will also be a 12-hour cooling period to provide sufficient time for members to react in the event of unauthorised adjustments.
CPF Withdrawal Lock
CPF members who wish to disable online withdrawals or do not plan to withdraw soon can consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock, which instantly sets the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0. Please refer to the three simple steps to activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
To re-enable online withdrawals, members would need to increase the online Daily Withdrawal Limit under Account settings. This requires 12 hours to take effect and may require enhanced authentication. Online CPF withdrawals can be made after 12 hours from the time members re-adjust their Daily Withdrawal Limit upwards.
Alternatively, members can also make an appointment to withdraw in person at CPF Service Centres if they do not want to adjust their online limit. Generally, the next available appointment would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings in their bank account registered with us generally within five working days. To minimise any potential delay during the withdrawal process, we encourage members intending to make large withdrawals to plan in advance.
Please visit the FAQs below to find out more on the Daily Withdrawal Limit and the CPF Withdrawal Lock:
What type of CPF withdrawals does the Daily Withdrawal Limit apply to and how do I change the Daily Withdrawal Limit?
What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?
Can I choose to opt-out of the Daily Withdrawal Limit?
What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
Enhanced authentication and 12-hour cooling period when updating contact details via the Update Contact Details (UCD) form
Members who are updating their contact details via the UCD e-form under Account settings will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period. Members may also be prompted to verify their identity before submitting the update form.
Enhanced authentication when updating bank account details via the ‘Update Bank Account’ e-service
Members can update their bank account details with CPF Board to receive payments such as withdrawal of CPF savings and monthly payouts via my cpf digital services - Account settings with their Singpass.
Members may be prompted to verify their identity through enhanced authentication to update their bank account details. PayNow NRIC-linked bank accounts will be activated after a 12-hour cooling period, and all other bank accounts will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the account belongs to you.
Please visit the FAQs below to find out more about the new “Update Bank Account” e-service:
How do I update my bank account details with CPF Board?
Why do I need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account to make PayNow withdrawals if I have already withdrawn via PayNow previously?
Do I have to provide my bank account details to CPF Board if I do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board?
Which CPF payments will I receive in the bank account provided under my Account settings?

Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: What should I do if I fall prey to a malware/phishing scam?
questions.text:
In the unfortunate event that you fall prey to a scam, we recommend taking the following actions immediately:
Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account.
Reset your Singpass password if you think your Singpass has been compromised. For further assistance, please contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.
If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.
File a police report and provide all details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why is there a 12-hour cooling period?
questions.text:
The 12-hour cooling period is a safeguard that provides members sufficient time to take action to prevent any unauthorised adjustments to the CPF online Daily Withdrawal Limit, or changes to important personal information and bank account details from taking effect. The 12-hour duration is aligned with industry practice.
To minimise any delays when making withdrawals, we advise you to plan ahead and regularly ensure that your bank account and contact details are updated with the Board.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why is Singpass Face Verification failing for me?
questions.text:
There may be several possible reasons for this. For ways to improve the success of Singpass Face Verification, you should ensure that:
Your face is not covered
You keep still while scanning is in progress
Your environment is not too dark
There is no strong lighting in the background
You use a minimum resolution of two megapixels for the camera. If you are using a laptop, you may wish to try again using a mobile phone which has a better camera
If you require assistance with Singpass Face Verification, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly.

questions.title: How can I tell if the Workfare SMS I received is real?
questions.text:
Given the recent rise in scams and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received is genuinely from an official source.
As of 1 July 2024, all government SMS communications are sent under the sender ID “gov.sg”. The SMS will begin with the full name of the sending agency (e.g. “Central Provident Fund Board”) and end with “This is an automated message sent by the Singapore Government”, meaning you should not reply to the message.
This is only an example of a Workfare SMS. The actual SMS you receive may be different.
Here are some tips to help protect yourself against phishing SMSes that appear to be sent from CPF Board:
check that the SMS is sent from “gov.sg”to the mobile number registered with CPF Board. If you are unsure of whether you had registered your mobile number, log in to the CPF website with your Singpass and check your account settings.
verify that the last four characters of the masked NRIC number match your NRIC number.
We will never ask you to reply to a Workfare SMS or direct you to a non-Government website. If you receive suspicious SMS please report it at the CPF official hotline or write to us.
Be Cautious, Pay attention to scams and don't be the next victim of Fraud.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I know whether the emails I receive are genuinely sent by CPF Board?
questions.text: To ensure that an email is genuinely sent by the CPF Board, remember to always check that the sender’s email address ends with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I verify that the CPF Contribution Alert email I received is legitimate?
questions.text:
The CPF Contribution Alert is a notification service to inform CPF members who are Singapore Citizens and 3rd year onwards Singapore Permanent Residents when their monthly CPF contributions are credited.
Members will receive the email notification at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address which you have earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
If you have the CPF Mobile app installed, you will be directed to view your details via the app.
To verify if the CPF Contribution Alert email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on has a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a call claiming to be from MediShield Life. What should I do if this is a scam and my contact details are shared with external agencies?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Team does not contact members to request sensitive personal information or engage any external agencies to call members on MediShield Life matters. The MediShield Life Team will not disclose members’ contact details to external agencies without members’ consent.
If you receive an unexpected phone call from someone who claims to be from the MediShield Life Team, please be vigilant and do not provide your sensitive personal information (E.g. Singpass ID/password, bank account or credit card details). When in doubt, you may end the conversation with the individual and check with the organisation which the caller claims to represent directly. To verify the authenticity of such calls, you can call us directly at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a notification on topping up MediSave savings. How do I know that this notification is indeed sent by CPF Board?
questions.text:
Members will receive email notifications at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
To verify if the email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on have a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/letter claiming they are from the Household Means Eligibility System (HOMES). Are they legitimate?
questions.text:
HOMES is a Government system supporting the Silver Support (SS) Scheme in conducting household means-tests, which are used to assess a senior’s eligibility for the SS Scheme. If you or your family member had asked for a reassessment of SS eligibility, and there is a need for further clarification regarding your household information, the HOMES team may contact you via phone, email or letter to find out more on your household circumstances.
If you are unsure of the authenticity of the mobile number that you have received, please call their hotline 6818 1422 for confirmation.
If you have any query on HOMES, you may visit the HOMES website to provide your contact details and a brief description of your query.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/SMS from the CPF Board regarding my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS). How do I know if it is legitimate?
questions.text:
We understand your concern on phishing. Given the recent rise in scam and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is genuine.
Remain vigilant and cautious when receiving calls/emails/messages. Government officials, including CPF Board officers, will never:
Ask you to withdraw CPF or transfer money to them (or to other persons);
