Should you require any assistance in activating the CPF Safety Switch, you may make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours.
Please note that we will require members to verify their identity before activation.

questions.title: What transactions/services are affected when the CPF Safety Switch is activated?
questions.text:
While the CPF Safety Switch is active:
Access to your CPF online services will be disabled
All in-progress withdrawals will be stopped, and you will not be able to make any further withdrawals
Disbursements to your registered bank account will be stopped
You can only obtain information related to your CPF account at CPF Service Centre
Please note that CPF contributions and recurring payments to third-party organisations will not be affected by the CPF Safety Switch. In order to regain access to these services, find out more about deactivating the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: How do I know if my CPF Safety Switch activation request is successful?
questions.text:
You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you of the outcome of your activation request. Note that we will not be able to reach you if you have no registered contact details with us.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, before activating CPF Safety Switch.
SMS notifications from CPF Board will only be sent from the “gov.sg” sender ID, and the email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
After CPF Safety Switch has been activated, you will not be able to log in to your CPF account.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, activate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No, the CPF Safety Switch requires members to verify their identity before activation. CPF Board staff may also contact members via their registered contact details by the next working day to better understand their situation and provide further support as required.

questions.title: Is there a time limit for how long the CPF Safety Switch remains active?
questions.text:
No. The CPF Safety Switch will remain activated until we receive your instruction to deactivate it.
However, we recommend that you deactivate the CPF Safety Switch after you have performed the necessary actions to secure your CPF account. We will send periodic email and SMS reminders to members who may have forgotten to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: How do I deactivate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You may request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch through one of the following methods:
Call the CPF hotline at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) and select option ‘8’ after choosing your language during operating hours
Make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours
Note that your deactivation request will take around three to five working days to process, after we successfully verify your identity.

questions.title: How do I know if my deactivation request is successful?
questions.text: You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you once your deactivation request is successful. Generally, this may take three to five working days, and we may contact you for more information during this period.

questions.title: What should I do after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
For security reasons, the bank account you previously registered with CPF Board would be removed when the CPF Safety Switch was activated. Your bank account will not be automatically reinstated after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch, as your bank account may also have been compromised.
In order to receive CPF payments to your bank account again, you will need to register your bank account with CPF Board. You may also wish to review your registered contact details to ensure that they are up to date. If you are not intending to withdraw soon, you may consider lowering your Daily Withdrawal Limit or activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
Find out more about updating your registered bank account, Daily Withdrawal Limit, and activation of CPF Withdrawal Lock. Please note that increasing the Daily Withdrawal Limit, updating your contact details and registering a PayNow-NRIC linked bank account will require a 12-hour cooling period. All other bank account updates will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the account belongs to you.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No. Deactivation can only be performed by the member, who must complete our authentication process.

questions.title: What happens if I genuinely need to make an urgent withdrawal after activating CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
We understand that members may have legitimate urgent transactions even after activating the CPF Safety Switch. Members can call the CPF hotline or make an appointment to visit any CPF Service Centre during operating hours to request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch. During this process, CPF Board staff will work with the member to verify their identity, understand their situation and provide guidance on safe practices before reactivating access to CPF online services.
Deactivation of the CPF Safety Switch can only be performed by CPF Board staff after the member’s identity has been verified. This ensures that only the genuine account holder can regain access to their account and helps safeguard members' CPF savings from scammers who might otherwise pressure victims to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.
Do note that after deactivation, you will still need to update your bank account, which will take 12 hours for a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account or two working days for Interbank GIRO.

questions.title: I received a notification indicating that my CPF Safety Switch activation request is not successful. What should I do next?
questions.text: If you have been scammed, please call us at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) for assistance. You should also contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately, and reset your Singpass (for assistance, call Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533).

questions.title: What information do I need to prepare to activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
If you are calling the CPF hotline to activate the CPF Safety Switch, you will need to provide your personal details for us to verify your identity.
If you have made an appointment to CPF Service Centre, please be reminded to bring your identification documents (such as NRIC).

questions.title: What is the difference between CPF Safety Switch and CPF Withdrawal Lock?
questions.text:
While both measures effectively disable online CPF withdrawals, the CPF Safety Switch also prevents online access to your CPF account and stops all disbursements to your registered bank account from our records.
Hence, we encourage you to only activate the CPF Safety Switch if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam. Doing so will immediately cease any unintended monetary outflows and prevent informational loss in the event that your Singpass has been compromised.
If you wish to protect yourself against scams and do not need to withdraw immediately, consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock instead which will allow you to maintain your online access to your CPF account.
Table: Summary of differences between CPF Safety Switch and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: If a property owner passes away and their children inherit the property, is Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) payable if the children sell the property immediately?
questions.text:
For properties acquired pursuant to inheritance, the date of acquisition for SSD purposes will be based on the date the property was first acquired by the deceased. If the holding period had already elapsed on the date of sale of the property, no SSD is payable.
You may refer to Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for more information on SSD and its stipulated holding period.

questions.title: If Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple is granted for a couple’s joint purchase of their first matrimonial property (where one spouse is a Singapore Citizen and the other is a Singapore Permanent Resident), will the remission be clawed back if the Singapore Citizen subsequently buys over the SPR’s share of the property?
questions.text: No, there will be no clawback of ABSD as long as the remission conditions under the Stamp Duties (Spouses) (Remission of ABSD) Rules are met as at the date of purchase of the property by the married couple.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am an owner of a residential property and co-own an inherited residential property with a sibling. If I intend to buy over my sibling's share, will I be liable to pay Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) on the purchase?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore citizen who owns two properties (albeit partial interest in one property), the acquisition of your sibling's share would be counted as your third property and subject to the prevailing ABSD rate.
However, as you are a Singapore citizen who owns two properties and acquiring additional interest in one of the two properties which you already have a partial interest in, partial ABSD remission may be applicable under Stamp Duties (Transfer of Interest in Property which Buyer has Interest) (Remission of ABSD) Rules.
Please note that BSD is still payable on the acquisition of your sibling's share in the property.
You may refer to Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) for more information on ABSD.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I own a private property jointly with my spouse and purchase a second private property in my sole name, can I apply for ABSD remission by selling the first property within six months of signing the option to purchase the second property?
questions.text:
No. To qualify for ABSD remission, the purchase of second residential property must be a joint purchase by a married couple where at least one spouse is a Singapore citizen and all other remission conditions are met.
You may refer to Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple for more information on the remission conditions.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Are Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs) liable for ABSD of 30% when buying a resale HDB flat before selling their current property?
questions.text: For the acquisition of an HDB flat by SPRs, partial ABSD remission may be granted such that a lower ABSD rate of 5% is payable under the Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission. Remission is granted automatically upon approval of the acquisition by HDB.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If the deceased's HDB flat has been transferred to his surviving spouse named in the Will, and the spouse subsequently wishes to add their son as co-owner, is stamp duty payable on the transfer?
questions.text:
Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) remission may be applicable on the transfer of the partial share to the son under the Transfer of HDB Flat within Family Remission if the remission conditions are met.
Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission may be applicable on the transfer under the Acquisition of HDB Flats and new Executive Condominium (EC) Units Remission if the remission conditions are met.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is stamp duty payable on transfer of shares from a foreign registered company to a Singapore registered entity with the same beneficial owners?
questions.text: Stamp duty is payable on the share transfer instrument between the transferor and transferee, even if they have the same beneficial owners.

questions.title: Is stamp duty payable on the inheritance of a property (residential or non-residential)?
questions.text: Stamp duty is not payable for properties acquired by beneficiaries (whether an individual, entity or trust) by way of assent in accordance to the Deceased's Will, Intestate Succession Act or Muslim Law of Inheritance.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: What is the net trade income used to compute my MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your age and net trade income assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). This refers to your gross trade income minus all allowable business expenses, capital allowances and trade losses as determined by IRAS.
From work year 2025, if you are also a platform worker, your MediSave contributions will be computed on your net trade income after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). This is because CPF contributions on your net earnings from platform work are payable by your platform operator(s).
You can use the Self-Employed MediSave Contribution Calculator to calculate the amount of MediSave you need to contribute or use the MediSave contribution rates to derive your MediSave contribution amount for the respective work years.

questions.title: I have more than one source of trade income. Do I have to make MediSave contributions on all these sources of income?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on the annual net trade income1 (NTI) from all your trades. If your total NTI from all your trades exceeds $6,000, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions.
You can refer to these examples of how MediSave contributions are computed on multiple sources of NTI.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.

questions.title: Do I still have to contribute to my MediSave if I am a self-employed person and an employee and/or a platform worker?
questions.text:
If your annual net trade income1 (NTI) exceeds $6,000, you are required to contribute to your MediSave Account as a self-employed person (SEP), in addition to the CPF contributions you have made on your employment/platform work.
This is the same as how employees with multiple jobs are required to make CPF contributions for all the wages from each job.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards
You can apply to limit your MediSave payable as an SEP, if your total income from all employment (excluding Additional Wages2) and platform work for the year3 exceeds the maximum total annual income.
Learn more about the conditions for limiting your MediSave payable as an SEP at this FAQ.
2Additional Wages are wage supplements which are not granted wholly and exclusively for the month. Examples are the annual bonus, leave pay, incentive and other payments made at intervals of more than a month.
3Applicable from work year 2025 onwards
If you are a platform worker concurrently working as an employee, you can refer to this FAQ on refunding your share of excess CPF contributions (if any) on your platform earnings.

questions.title: I am holding two types of licences (e.g. LTA and ACRA). Do I have to make MediSave contributions for both licences?
questions.text:
Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your age and net trade income1 (NTI) for the year. Regardless of the number of licence(s) you hold, if you earn an annual NTI of more than $6,000, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards

questions.title: How will participating in Contribute As You Earn affect my MediSave contributions payable?
questions.text:
Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) does not change the amount of MediSave contributions you have to make based on your net trade income (NTI). Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required to contribute to their MediSave Account (MA) if their annual NTI1 exceeds $6,000.
The only change is in how the contributions are made. Under CAYE, the agency/company you provided a service to will help to deduct a portion of your service payment and contribute the amount to your MediSave Account, as and when it makes a service payment to you.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
Your CAYE contributions are based on your estimated annual revenue and expenses. Thus, CAYE contributions are an estimate of your MediSave payable. After you declare your NTI for the year, your MediSave payable will be computed.
If your total CAYE contributions are higher than your MediSave payable for the latest year, your excess CAYE contributions will be used to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years2. Any remaining CAYE contributions will then be refunded to you.
If your total CAYE contributions are lower than your MediSave payable, you’ll be required to top up the remaining amount. You’ll be notified accordingly, and you can choose to make payment via lump-sum payment(s) or sign up for GIRO instalments.
2This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. Please write to us if you do not wish to use your CAYE contributions to offset your outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn, how much MediSave contribution would I have to make from my service fee?
questions.text:
Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), the amount of MediSave contribution deducted from your service fee is based on your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year.
Your CAYE contribution rate is computed by the following formula:
CAYE contribution rate = (A x B) / C
where
A is the MediSave contribution rate for your estimated annual Net Trade Income (NTI)1 and age for the year;
B is your estimated annual NTI1 for the year2; and
C is your estimated annual revenue for the year2
1 Your estimated annual NTI is derived using your estimated annual revenue less estimated annual expenses for the year.
2 If you did not provide your estimated annual revenue and expenses for the year, it will be based on your actual revenue and expenses assessed by IRAS in the preceding year.
A floor CAYE contribution rate of 2% will apply if you have earned more than $6,000 two years ago.
To ensure that your CAYE contribution rate reflects your business outlook for the year accurately, please estimate your revenue and expenses by logging in to the Self-employment dashboard using your Singpass, under Contribute As You Earn > Update contribution rate. You can adjust your CAYE contribution rate as and when there are changes to your estimated revenue and expenses. Generally, your updated rate will apply to payments made from the next day.
Otherwise, a personalised default CAYE contribution rate computed based on your NTI assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the preceding year will apply.
From work year 2025, the NTI used to compute your default CAYE rate will exclude net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s).
Example on how the CAYE contribution rate will be computed
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Will the estimated income that I provided for the computation of my Contribute As You Earn contribution rate be used as the income to compute my MediSave payable?
questions.text:
The estimated income information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only used to compute the CAYE contribution rate. It will not be used as your actual income to compute your MediSave payable for the year.
You will still need to declare your actual net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the following year. Your MediSave payable for the year will then be computed based on your NTI1.
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What are the requirements for translating non-English documents in IDERA and CDCL applications?
questions.text:
a. All documents must be translated into English.
b. Each translated document must be accompanied by
i. a declaration by the translator that the English translation is a complete, accurate and true representation of the original document; and
ii. the resume of the translator showing the translator's qualifications, experience and relevant credentials.
topics: Aviation Safety / Aircraft Airworthiness and Registration

questions.title: How do I apply to reserve my Ordinary Account (OA) savings, so that they will not be transferred to my Retirement Account and remain in OA for my housing payments after I turn 55 years old?
questions.text:
You can apply to reserve all or part of your Ordinary Account (OA) for housing payments. This prevents these funds from being automatically transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) when you turn 55.
When to apply
You can apply within six months before your 55th birthday. Please allow at least five working days for processing.
Eligibility
You do not need to reserve your OA savings if:
You have fully redeemed your housing loan, unless you need to use them for your future housing payments; or
Your Special Account (SA) savings can meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) so your OA savings will not be transferred to your RA.
However, you cannot reserve your OA savings if you are above 55 years old or have withdrawn your CPF under the Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) scheme.
Important considerations
The reserved amount will remain in your OA and earn 2.5% instead of being transferred to your RA to earn 4% interest. This could reduce your monthly payouts when you are eligible to start your monthly payouts, so it is important to plan your finances carefully and consider how housing reservations may impact your retirement plans.
Usage restrictions
The reserved OA savings can only be used for housing payments, subject to applicable housing withdrawal limits. You cannot use these reserved funds for other CPF schemes, including Home Protection Scheme premiums.
After age 65
When you begin receiving monthly payouts, any unused reserved OA savings will be transferred to your RA if you have not set aside the FRS. This transfer helps to increase your monthly payouts. Please remember to make alternative financing arrangements for your housing loan repayments when you apply to start monthly payouts.
Making Changes to Your Reservation
If you would like to amend your reservation, please visit this FAQ. To cancel your reservation entirely, please visit this FAQ.

questions.title: How can I cancel my reservation of Ordinary Account savings to be used for my housing payments?
questions.text:
To cancel your reservation to use Ordinary Account (OA) savings for housing payments, please write to us with your request.
Important note for members aged 55 and above:
Once your OA savings are unreserved, they will automatically be transferred to your Retirement Account if you have not set aside your Full Retirement Sum.
If you need to make changes to your existing reservation rather than cancel it completely, please visit this FAQ.

questions.title: How can I amend the amount reserved in my Ordinary Account savings for my housing payments?
questions.text:
If you are below 55:
Submit a new application
If you are 55 and above, please write to us if you wish to:
Reduce the amount reserved in your OA. Please note that OA savings you have unreserved will be transferred to your Retirement Account if you have not met your Full Retirement Sum.
Update the amount reserved in your OA for a different property.
Cancelling your reservation entirely
If you would like to cancel your existing reservation, please visit this FAQ for guidance.

questions.title: Why did CPF Board send me a notification to view my transactions? Is it legitimate?
questions.text:
Monthly notifications are sent to members with registered email addresses, reminding them to review their transactions every month. This ensures members can promptly identify and report any discrepancies.
To verify the legitimacy of the notification, members should:
1. Ensure that the sender’s email address is correctly spelt and ends with @e.cpf.gov.sg.
2. Ensure that the hyperlinks or links they click on has a domain ending with “gov.sg”.
To ensure your email address is up-to-date, you can check or update it using your Singpass.
Protect yourself from phishing: Learn how to identify phishing links and safeguard your account.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: How do I submit my LPA application if I do not have a smartphone or do not know how to make online applications?
questions.text:
Refer to the Quick Reference Guide on how to submit an online LPA application.
If challenges persist, or if you do not have a smartphone, you may submit your LPA application in hardcopy to 3 Bishan Place #03-00 CPF Building Singapore 579838.
Also note that the processing of hardcopy applications will take longer than online applications in OPGO.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / Information on LPA

questions.title: What if I do not wish to participate in Contribute As You Earn?
questions.text:
Self-employed persons (SEPs) who have completed a job with Government agencies will be automatically enrolled into Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). CAYE will not apply to SEPs who completed jobs with the private sector.
The CAYE scheme helps SEPs save for their healthcare needs through smaller and more regular MediSave contributions each time they receive a service payment. This helps to reduce the MediSave payable in the following year (after SEPs declare their Net Trade Income and have their MediSave payable computed). CAYE will help with the upkeep of current MediSave obligations and prevent snowballing of the payable.
You can choose to set your CAYE contribution rate to 0% if you’ve made your MediSave contributions in full or are on GIRO instalment plan.
If you’re in financial hardship and unable to set aside monies for your CAYE contributions, you may write to us. We will assess your request and inform you of the outcome in writing.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: When I sell my existing property, what can I do with the sale proceeds that are refunded to my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
When you sell your property, the refunded sale proceeds are credited to different CPF accounts depending on whether you have reached age 55:
If you are below 55
Sale proceeds are credited to your Ordinary Account (OA).
If you are 55 and above
Your sale proceeds are first used to top up your Retirement Account (RA) to meet your required retirement sum. Any remaining balance stays in your OA.
What you can do with the refunds in your Ordinary Account:
Maximise retirement savings: Transfer your OA balance to your Special Account (if below age 55) or RA (if age 55 and above) for higher retirement payouts. Find out more about CPF top-ups.
Purchase property: Use the savings for property payments. If any housing grants are refunded to your OA, they may be used for future property purchase (such as HDB flat and private properties), subject to CPF housing usage rules and limits. Find out more about the use of CPF for housing.
Earn guaranteed returns: Keep the monies in your CPF accounts to earn risk-free interest. Find out more about CPF interest rates.
Withdraw for immediate needs if you are above age 55: Find out more about withdrawals.
If you are age 55 and above and planning to buy a smaller HDB flat
If you are planning to buy a 3-room or smaller HDB flat, you can use your RA refunds in excess of your Basic Retirement Sum for your property purchase, provided you meet these conditions.
Purchase the flat within three years of selling this property
The new flat costs less than your previous property’s selling price
You have not been issued with a CPF LIFE plan, so there are available savings in your RA
Check your Home ownership dashboard for available amounts and ensure the funds are accessible when needed for your purchase.

questions.title: I have redeemed Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discount but the full MediShield Life premium was still deducted from my payer’s MediSave Account. Why was the discount not applied before premium deduction?
questions.text:
Your premium payer will receive the redeemed premium discount as a reimbursement to their MediSave Account on the same day after the full premium is deducted. The net premium amount paid is the same regardless whether the discount is applied before or after premium deduction.
Your premium payer may check the reimbursement after premium deduction in his/her CPF Transaction History or contact your Integrated Shield Plan insurer directly if needed. You may also view your premium discount information in your Healthcare Dashboard.
For more information on MediShield Life premium discount, please refer to the detailed step-by-step guide under Section 5.

questions.title: I have redeemed my Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts on the Healthy 365 app, but my Healthcare Dashboard shows no redemption. How long will it take for my Healthcare Dashboard to be updated?
questions.text:
After you have redeemed your Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts, your Healthcare Dashboard will be updated with your premium discount information instantly.
If the information does not appear, please log out of the CPF digital services and log back in to refresh your session.

questions.title: How can I claim the deceased member's discounted Singtel shares if no nomination was made?
questions.text:
The claims process depends on whether the deceased member held a personal securities account and whether an executor or administrator has been appointed under Grant of Probate (GP) or Letter of Administration (LA). For more information on how to apply for a GP or LA, visit Singapore Courts’ website.
ScenarioProcess
Deceased member held a personal securities account
We will automatically transfer the discounted Singtel shares to the account.
Deceased member did not have a personal securities account, but an executor or administrator has been appointed
We will transfer the discounted Singtel shares to the estate securities account opened by his appointed executor(s) or administrator(s).
If there is no securities account or estate securities account, the appointed executor(s) or administrator(s) may instruct the Board to sell the Singtel shares.
Deceased member did not have a personal securities account, and no executor or administrator has been appointed
We will sell the discounted Singtel shares.
If the estate is below $50,000, the deceased member’s family has two options to claim the sale proceeds:
Approach the Public Trustee to administer the shares together with the estate of the deceased member.
Appoint a proper claimant to claim the sales proceeds or any dividends in cash directly from the Board. Write to us for more details about the application via the proper claimant route.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: When will the deceased member's CPF savings be paid to me after I have submitted the withdrawal application form?
questions.text:
We will contact the nominee(s) within 10 working days after the Board is notified of the member's death. If you are not eligible for automatic disbursement, you will receive instructions on how to submit the withdrawal application in our notification.
The processing time of the withdrawal application depends on whether the deceased member held Singtel Discounted Shares as additional time is required to process the shares.
ScenarioProcessing Time*
CPF savings without Singtel Discounted Shares17 working days
CPF savings with Singtel Discounted Shares17 working days + 7 working days to transfer / sell shares
* Upon receiving all required documents
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: When will the deceased member's CPF savings be paid to me if no nomination was made?
questions.text:
If no nomination is made, the deceased member’s CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution according to intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws. The transfer will typically take place within 17 working days after the Board is notified of the member's death.
The PTO will contact the beneficiaries with instructions on how to claim the funds. Beneficiaries will need to provide documentation to prove their relationship with the deceased member to the PTO. The entire processing time can take up to six months and it involves an administrative fee, which will be deducted from the deceased member's CPF savings.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What is the new investment scheme about and who is it for?
questions.text:
The new investment scheme will offer simplified, low-cost and diversified life-cycle investment products, which automatically rebalance investors’ portfolios towards less risky assets as they approach target date. This caters to members who want to stay invested for the long term, but may have less financial expertise or prefer not to actively manage their investments.
It also serves as a complementary option to the risk-free interest rates enjoyed by members today and the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), by providing an additional choice for members who are willing to take some risk for higher potential returns on their CPF savings. The new scheme will provide a lower-cost option since all-in fees will be capped. With a limited number of products, it will also simplify investment decisions for members who may otherwise find it complex to navigate the range of CPFIS offerings.
The new scheme is expected to be launched in the first half of 2028.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: What are the benefits of the new investment scheme?
questions.text:
The new investment scheme offers members a simplified investment option if they want to potentially earn higher returns but lack expertise in navigating CPF Investment Scheme offerings or prefer not to actively manage investments.
The new scheme helps members stay invested for the long term and ride out market volatility while calibrating their investment risk exposure at different life stages and mitigating the risk of market downturns during exit.
The key features include:
Automatic portfolio management where members' investments will rebalance along a glidepath towards less risky assets as they approach target date, shifting gradually from higher-risk to lower-risk assets, before being liquidated in phases. This means members do not need to actively manage their investments or make complex decisions about when to adjust their portfolio.
Members will have simplified choices with only two to three reputable product providers offering a small number of options, making decision-making much easier.
All-in fees will also be capped to keep costs low, allowing members to retain and benefit from more of their investment returns.
When members' investments are fully liquidated, the sale proceeds will be transferred to their Retirement Account (RA) up to the Full Retirement Sum, with any remaining proceeds going to their Ordinary Account. These funds in the RA can then help boost members' monthly CPF LIFE payouts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: Is the new investment scheme safe for my retirement savings?
questions.text:
As with all investment products, the new investment scheme will carry investment risk, with returns subject to market conditions. However, the scheme will have certain features that help to mitigate against downside risks, such as automatic age-based rebalancing of investors' portfolio mix, with phased liquidation towards the target date.
For members who prefer a risk-free approach, they can continue to keep their savings in their CPF accounts to earn the risk-free CPF interest rates. Members can consider cash top-ups to their CPF accounts, or transfer Ordinary Account savings to their Special Account, which will go towards boosting their CPF LIFE monthly payouts in retirement.
CPF Board will also enhance investor education to help members determine whether the new scheme is suitable for them. Members are encouraged to carefully consider their investment objectives, risk tolerance, and investment horizon before making any investment decisions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: What is the difference between the new investment scheme and existing unit trusts under the CPF Investment Scheme?
questions.text:
The new investment scheme removes the need for members to select funds as the product provider will offer a pre-mixed portfolio of global and diversified funds that follows a glidepath, with phased liquidation before target date to mitigate risk of exiting during a downturn.
Members do not need to actively rebalance their portfolio as products under the new scheme automatically adjust members’ investment portfolio mix as they approach target date.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: What are the expected returns for the new investment scheme?
questions.text:
Based on existing market studies, life-cycle products show potential to achieve good returns over a long-term horizon.
The selected product providers under the new scheme will be required to provide more details on their specific products in a clear and transparent manner when launched, including illustrative returns commensurate with the risk profile of the product. You may refer to the product provider factsheet/projection once available.
It is important to understand that products under the new investment scheme, as with all investment products, carry investment risk, and returns are subject to market conditions. Therefore, members are encouraged to carefully consider their investment objectives, risk tolerance, and investment horizon before making any investment decisions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: When will the new investment scheme be launched?
questions.text:
We will engage the industry from March 2026 on the product specifications for the new investment scheme and invite expressions of interest to offer such products. Selected providers are expected to be announced in the first half of 2027, followed by the launch of the new scheme in the first half of 2028.
Further details will be announced at a later date.
topics: Growing Your Savings / New simple, low-cost investment scheme for retirement

questions.title: What are the changes to the CPF contribution rates for senior workers that will take effect from 1 January 2027?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2027, CPF contribution rates for employees aged above 55 to 65 will be increased to strengthen their retirement adequacy. The changes will apply to wages earned from 1 January 2027 onwards. With this increase in 2027, we will have reached the target contribution rates for senior workers aged above 60 to 65.
