questions.title: I wish to apply, retain, or renew a business registration or licence with my business partners. Do all of us need to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for our MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Yes, all owners or partners who wish to apply, retain, or renew their business registration or licence are required to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable.
Existing business registrations and licences may be subject to cancellation if any of the owners or partners have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable. The relevant licensing agency (e.g., ACRA) will send a notice to all owners or partners to inform them of any early business registration or licence cancellations.

questions.title: How long will the PR application outcome letter/ result be available online?
questions.text:
Please note that the outcome letter/ result will only be available for online viewing for up to two months from their issuance date. To download the outcome letter, you may log in to MyICA (Singpass holder)/ ICA e-Service (non-Singpass holder) within the stipulated deadline.
Once the deadline has passed, there is no longer any option to view, access, or download the outcome letter online.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Permanent Residence (PR)

questions.title: What is Quarantine Order Allowance (QOA)? Who is eligible and how can I apply?
questions.text:
The QOA is set up to mitigate financial impact for those who have been served QO, and completed their QO without any breaches.
Claims of $100 per day can be made by self-employed Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, or Singapore-registered companies whose employees under QO are Singaporean Citizens, Permanent Residents or Work Pass Holders.
As of 1st July 2021, approved caregivers of a Person-Under-Quarantine (PUQ) can apply for the QOA, subject to the same eligibility requirements. Applications can be submitted by self-employed Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, or by Singapore-registered companies whose employees are Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents or Work Pass Holders.
For employer whose employee is issued with a QO, you can only apply for the QOA after your employee has completed the quarantine and application must be sent to MOH within 90 days.
To apply for Quarantine Order Allowance, click here https://go.gov.sg/moh-qoa-app-form
For enquiries, please write in to MOH_QOA@moh.gov.sg.

questions.title: How do I make a partial repayment or full repayment of my housing loan?
questions.text:
Before making any repayment, check that you have sufficient CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings and verify that you have not exceeded the maximum amount of CPF savings allowed for your property. You can view your Home ownership dashboard to find your latest housing usage and usage limit (if any).
You can use your CPF savings to make a partial repayment or full repayment of your housing loan through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan:
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Make Partial Repayment of Housing Loan/Make Full Repayment of Housing Loan
Processing time: generally within three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches require prior appointments.
If you are making a full repayment of your housing loan, your HPS cover (if any) will be automatically terminated when we are notified by HDB that you have fully repaid your loan. You do not need to inform the Board to terminate your HPS cover. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF OA.
If you have a bank loan:
Seek approval from your housing loan financier
Submit an online application with your Singpass
For full repayment of housing loan, upload a copy of these documents in the application:
The bank’s redemption statement and
A copy of your lawyer’s legal bill (if any)
Processing time: generally within five working days
If you are making a full repayment of your housing loan, your HPS cover (if any) will be automatically terminated when we are notified by the bank that you have fully repaid your loan. You do not need to inform the Board to terminate your HPS cover. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF OA.

questions.title: If I did not apply to use my CPF savings when I bought my property that is financed with a bank loan, can I now use my CPF savings for monthly instalments?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF savings for the monthly instalments of your property.
If you own an HDB flat with bank loan:
Submit an online application with your Singpass
Include your financier’s details and your outstanding housing loan amount in the application
If you own a private property with bank loan:
Submit your request through your lawyer
A conveyancing lawyer is required when using your CPF savings for the first time. For more information, please visit this FAQ.
Tips for sustainable housing payments:
While your CPF savings can help with housing payments, remember that these savings are primarily for your future retirement needs. For a sustainable approach, consider the following:
ensure your monthly instalment does not exceed your monthly Ordinary Account (OA) contributions
use a mix of cash and OA savings for housing payments
retain an amount in your OA equivalent to six months' worth of monthly instalments for emergencies
This approach allows you to service your housing loan during unexpected situations while ensuring your OA savings continue earning attractive interest rates.

questions.title: I do not have enough funds in my CPF Ordinary Account for my housing instalment payment because my CPF contributions are credited after the instalment deduction date. What should I do?
questions.text: If your CPF contributions are consistently credited after the deduction date, you may consider making a one-time cash payment to cover one month's instalment. This builds up your account balance, ensuring you have sufficient funds for future deductions before new contributions are credited each month. Once you have made this cash payment, your subsequently monthly instalments should be deducted successfully using your existing Ordinary Account savings.

questions.title: I have withdrawn my CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme. Do I need to refund the CPF principal amount and accrued interest when I sell my property?
questions.text:
Yes, you must refund the principal CPF amount withdrawn for your property and the accrued interest to your CPF account when you sell your property. The refunds will be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Reduced Retirement Sum (RRS), and any remaining refunds in excess of the RRS will be credited to your Ordinary Account (OA). Check the amount that you have to refund in the “What happens if” section on your Home ownership dashboard.
Withdrawing additional CPF savings after refunds are credited
Once the refunds from your property sale have been credited to your CPF account, you can submit an online request using your Singpass for CPF to assess your eligibility for further withdrawal under the RLE scheme.
We will review your request and inform you of your eligibility status.

questions.title: Why do I need to refund the accrued interest on the amount of CPF savings used for my property?
questions.text:
CPF savings are primarily designed for your retirement needs. When you use these savings to purchase property, the money stops earning interest in your CPF account.
Accrued interest is the interest your CPF savings would have earned if they had remained in your account rather than being used for property purchase.
Refunding both the principal amount and accrued interest ensures your retirement savings are fully restored to what they would have been if they had remained in your CPF account. Without this refund, your retirement funds would be permanently reduced.
The calculation of accrued interest runs from the date you first used your CPF savings until you make the refund. It uses CPF's prevailing interest rates, compounded annually throughout this period.

questions.title: The Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) policy is auto-issued to me. Why do I need to declare my health to be covered under DPS?
questions.text:
Eligibility for Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage is subject to you being in good health at policy commencement.
As with any life insurance, Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage may be declined or deferred if a member has serious pre-existing medical conditions prior to policy commencement. This underwriting practice is essential to ensure the scheme’s viability and maintain affordable premiums for all insured members.
The DPS insurer will not consider claims from members who have serious pre-existing medical conditions, or have provided false or misleading statements or withheld relevant information in their health declaration.
Please refer to Great Eastern Life for further information regarding examples of serious pre-existing medical conditions that may affect your eligibility for coverage.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I retired in March 2026 this year and have no income since then. However, I received a notification to file for the Year of Assessment 2026. What should I do?
questions.text: Income tax is assessed on a preceding calendar year basis. The notification to file for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2026 is for you to file for the income earned by you in 2025. You will be required to file an income tax return for YA 2026 if you have received a letter, form or SMS from IRAS informing you to do so.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: I am a self-employed person and have not been filing my income tax return as my income is below the income filing threshold requirements. However, I need my tax bill (i.e. Notice of Assessment) for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2026 to apply for government assistance scheme. How can I get my tax bill?
questions.text:
You can e-File your Income Tax Return for the YA 2026 at myTax Portal between 1 Mar 2026 and 31 Oct 2026. This only applies to self-employed persons who did not receive any notification to file but require the tax bill.
If you encounter any issue when trying to e-File your Income Tax Return, please chat with us or call us from Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (except Public Holidays). Alternatively, you can email us via myTax Portal using your Singpass or Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA).
topics: Individual Income Tax / Individuals required to file tax

questions.title: Will employers receive support for the increase in CPF contribution rates from 1 January 2027??
questions.text:
The CPF Transition Offset (CTO) will provide transitory wage offsets to help mitigate the rise in business costs due to the increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2027. This offset is equivalent to half of the increase in employer CPF contribution rates for every Singaporean and Permanent Resident worker they employ who is aged above 55 to 65.
Find out more about CPF Transition Offset.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: How do I apply for an LPA without fees? Is the application process different now?
questions.text: There is no change to the application process. You are encouraged to submit your LPA online at Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) - MSF by logging in with your Singpass. You may refer to the Quick Reference Guide on the OPG website for step-by-step instructions to submit an LPA.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / LPA Fee Waiver

questions.title: Will I receive CPF Contributions during my traineeship?
questions.text: Trainees are not considered employees during their training period with the agencies and there is no employment relationship, thus Trainees will not receive CPF contributions.

questions.title: As a platform worker, do I still need to declare my income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore?
questions.text:
For tax purposes, you will need to declare your income derived from platform work and any non-platform work in the year to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). You should declare each source of income separately when filing your tax return to IRAS. Each trade should be reported under its own distinct nature of business category.
For example, if you earned income as a freelance tutor and a private hire car driver, you should declare these sources of income separately, under “Tutor/Lecturer” and “Taxi/Private Hire Car Driver” respectively. This will allow the consolidated statement/Form B from IRAS to display your income from self-employment and platform work as separate items, to facilitate the computation of the mandatory MediSave contributions for your income as a freelance tutor. You may refer to IRAS’ website for more information on reporting your income.
Refer to IRAS’ step-by-step guide to declare your income(s).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from self-employment and platform work. Why is my net trade income in the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons not the same as the Notice of Assessment from the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore?
questions.text:
You will need to declare your net trade income (NTI) from both self-employment (non-platform work) and platform work to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). The Notice of Assessment (NOA) issued by IRAS will inform you of the assessable NTI from both self-employment and platform work, as you need to pay income tax on both sources of income.
For work year 2025 onwards, your self-employed MediSave contributions are computed on the NTI after excluding net earnings from platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). This is because CPF contributions on your net earnings from platform work are payable by your platform operator(s). The notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions for your other income earned as a self-employed person.
Learn more about how MediSave contributions are computed. You may use this calculator to compute the mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have already made CPF contributions as a platform worker. Do I still need to contribute MediSave in the following year for my other self-employed work?
questions.text:
For work year 2025 onwards, if you are only receiving platform earnings in the year, platform operators would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions on your platform earnings for you every month. Therefore, you do not need to make your own MediSave contributions on such platform earnings in the following year.
If you derive self-employed income from non-platform work (e.g. giving tuition, or taxi street-hail jobs), you will still need to make MediSave contributions on these incomes in the following year on your own, as per status quo, after you have declared your net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). Your MediSave contributions are computed on your NTI after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). CPF Board will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions once IRAS has assessed your income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from self-employment and platform work. How can I check that the MediSave contributions in my notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons are only for my self-employment income and have excluded my platform work earnings?
questions.text:
In computing your self-employed MediSave contributions, we will first take your annual net trade income (NTI) assessed by IRAS [A], and deduct your net earnings from platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) [B]. The remaining income [C]* is stated in your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons, and will be used to compute your mandatory MediSave contributions.
* [C] = [A] – [B]
To verify the income stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C], you should first ensure that you have declared each source of income from self-employment and platform work separately to IRAS. Refer to IRAS’ guide for details. You can then download your consolidated statement from IRAS to verify the income shown in your notice of CPF contributions:
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
Your consolidated statement will show the breakdown of your income (in the “Adjusted profit/loss” row), by nature of business.
E.g. assume you are a freelance tutor and private hire car driver. You can verify the NTI stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C] against the “Adjusted profit/loss” reflected under “Tutor/Lecturer” in your consolidated statement.
If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, you can follow the same steps above and verify against your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
If you have difficulties accessing the tax portal, locating notices issued by IRAS, or need to redeclare your income for self-employment and platform work separately, please contact IRAS.
If the income reflected in your notice of CPF contributions [C] differs from the “adjusted profit/loss” stated in the consolidated statement (for the nature of businesses not relating to platform work), please Write to Us and provide us with:
Your consolidated statement (or Form B if you are on paper returns for tax filing); and
All your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s) for the year
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from platform work only and my platform operator(s) is/are making CPF contributions on my behalf. Why did I receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed person informing me to make mandatory MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
You will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons if your annual net trade income (NTI) exceeds $6,000, after excluding net earnings from platform work declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
For work year 2025 onwards, if you only earned income from platform work and received a notice of CPF contributions, please Write To Us so that we can assist with your case. Please provide us with your tax filing consolidated statement issued by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s). If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, please provide us with a copy of your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
You may refer to the following steps or the steps to download notices issued by IRAS (including consolidated statement):
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
If you encounter any difficulties accessing the tax portal or locating notices issued by IRAS, please contact IRAS for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief as a self-employed person when I make mandatory MediSave contributions or make voluntary top-ups to my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person (SEP), you can enjoy full tax relief on your mandatory MediSave contributions.
You can also enjoy tax relief as an SEP for the following voluntary contributions:
MediSave contributions made to offset future MediSave payable, made via the Manage your MediSave Payable form; and
Voluntary top-ups to 3 CPF accounts
The tax relief for these voluntary contributions will be capped at the lowest of:
37% of your net trade income1 2 or
CPF annual limit of $37,7402 or
Actual voluntary amount contributed by you
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards if you are a mandatory or opt in platform worker
2Amount less tax relief allowed on mandatory MediSave contributions
Please visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website for more information.

questions.title: Do Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions qualify for tax relief?
questions.text:
Similar to other forms of self-employed CPF contributions, Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions made in a calendar year will qualify for tax relief in the following year. For example, relief on CAYE contributions made between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025 will qualify for tax relief in the Year of Assessment (YA) 2026.
Please refer to this FAQ for more information on the tax eligibility of your contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why does it not show up on the Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life policy details will only be displayed on your Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section after successful deduction of your first premium.
Please be assured that your coverage has already commenced from the date your application was approved. You will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after this date.

questions.title: How do I calculate the CPF contributions based on net earnings of a platform worker?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution is calculated based on platform workers’ net earnings (after fixed expense deduction amount) and the contribution rate applicable to their age, earnings and opt-in status.
Illustration
Step 1: Determine a platform worker’s gross earnings: $3,000
Step 2: Apply the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount (FEDA): 60% expense for cars
Step 3: Compute the net earnings: $3,000 x (1-60%) = $1,200
Step 4: Key in the net earnings into platform worker CPF Contribution Calculator to find out the contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Do I need to update my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account as my registered bank account with CPF each time I make a withdrawal or switch to another PayNow-linked bank account?
questions.text:
No, you only need to perform the update of your registered bank account to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account once and wait 12 hours for it to be activated. You can do so via Account settings. Thereafter, you may apply for retirement withdrawals for immediate needs via PayNow anytime to receive your CPF withdrawals almost instantly.
There is no need to update the Board if you have linked your PayNow-NRIC to a different bank account. Your CPF payments will automatically be made to whichever bank account you have linked to your PayNow-NRIC.

questions.title: What happens to my Retirement Account (RA) savings if I used it to purchase annuity(ies) under the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS), after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you are no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, and have previously purchased annuity(ies) using your Retirement Account savings under the Retirement Sum Scheme, any surrender value arising from the termination of such annuities will be paid directly to you by the respective insurer.
In the event of your death, any benefits payable will be paid to your beneficiary in accordance with the terms and conditions of the annuity policy by the insurer.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: If I have housing arrears, how do I apply to use my CPF savings to pay for it?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to pay for housing arrears through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan:
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Pay Overdue Housing Loan or Upgrading Cost with CPF
Processing time: generally within three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches require prior appointments.
If you have a bank loan:
Submit an online application with your Singpass at least five working days before the monthly instalment deduction date
Processing time: generally within three working days

questions.title: How do I check my Permanent Residence (PR) application status?
questions.text:
Please log in to MyICA (Singpass holder)/ ICA e-Service (non-Singpass holder below 15 years old) within two months from the outcome release date.
For applicants whose Singpass accounts have been invalidated and who no longer hold a valid pass, please note that your PR application has been rejected. Access to application status via the online portal is only available to user with a valid Singpass. You may consider submitting a fresh application online if there are changes to your circumstances.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass
Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass / Permanent Residence (PR)

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my voluntary housing refund application?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your voluntary housing refund application online via Activities.
Once your application has been successfully processed, the refunded amount will be credited to your CPF account. You can then view the details in your 15-months Transaction History by logging in to my cpf digital services or CPF Mobile app using your Singpass. You will also receive an email notification once your application has been processed.
Please note that the amount refunded will be used to reduce the principal amount withdrawn for your property, followed by its accrued interest.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: Am I eligible for CPF Housing Grants?
questions.text: CPF Housing Grants (CHG) are administered by HDB. Please visit HDB’s website for the detailed eligibility criteria and application information.

questions.title: What is the difference between joint-tenancy and tenancy-in-common?
questions.text:
The key differences lie in how ownership shares are held and what happens to a co-owner's share when they pass away.
Joint-tenancy
All co-owners have equal interest in the property, regardless of how much each person paid towards the purchase. When a joint tenant dies, their share automatically goes to the remaining co-owner(s), even if they have made a will stating otherwise.
Tenancy-in-common
Each co-owner holds a separate and definite share in the property while having rights to use the entire property. Unlike joint tenancy, owners can hold different ownership percentages. For example, one owner may hold 50% while two others hold 25% each.
When a tenant-in-common passes away, their share does not automatically transfer to the other owners. Instead, it will be distributed on according to their will. If no will exists, the share will be distributed according to the Intestate Succession Act.

questions.title: How can I get my title deed for my property?
questions.text:
You can obtain your title deed after fully paying off your housing loan. The process varies depending on your property type and earlier loan arrangement.
If you own an HDB flat with HDB loan
Contact HDB directly to retrieve your title deed.
If you own an HDB flat with a bank loan
Contact your bank to retrieve your title deed.
If you own a private property
When you use CPF savings to purchase a private property, a CPF charge is created on your property to secure repayment of the amount used plus accrued interest when the property is sold. This CPF charge may remain on the property even after your housing loan is fully paid off.
Once your mortgage and all other charges (including the CPF charge and other registered charges) are fully discharged, please contact SLA to issue your title deed.

questions.title: I obtained an overdraft facility to buy a private property. Can I use my CPF savings to redeem the overdraft?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF savings to repay the overdraft, provided it was used solely to purchase the private property.
Application Process
You must authorise your lawyer to submit an online application on your behalf by signing the Letter of Authorisation, Declaration, Consent & Agreement.
Required Documents
Your lawyer will need to attach the following documents in the application:
Financier's letter of offer.
Financier's letter to confirm that the overdraft was used strictly to buy the property or was partially used to buy the property. If the overdraft was used partially to buy the property, please attach the monthly statement of account of the overdraft account from the time it was disbursed for payment of the property to the date of application to use CPF savings.
Financier's statement showing the current outstanding amount of the overdraft.
Final Step
Once the application is approved, you will need to arrange for your financier to convert the overdraft facility to a housing loan.

questions.title: I plan to purchase my next property before receiving the CPF refunds from the sale of my current property. How can I proceed if I do not have enough cash or CPF savings to cover the purchase?
questions.text:
You can consider taking a bridging loan from any bank, provided that HDB and/or the bank approve the arrangement.
Important condition to note
The total amount of CPF savings withdrawn plus all loans (including the bridging loan) cannot exceed the lower of the purchase price or the valuation price of the property at the time of purchase.
After selling your existing property
Your CPF savings will be refunded to your CPF accounts. You can then use these funds to pay off the bridging loan once you have completed the legal documentation and settled any outstanding cash amount.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a Small Office Home Office unit?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to purchase a Small Office Home Office (SOHO) unit only if the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) has approved it for residential use. If the unit is approved for office use, you cannot use your CPF savings for the purchase.
SOHO developments are approved by the URA for either office or residential use, but not for both. It is important to verify the approved use of the property before committing to any purchase.

questions.title: What should I do if I would like to use the CPF Housing Top-Up Grant for my HDB flat?
questions.text:
The process depends on your loan type:
If you have an HDB loan
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within three to five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
If you have a bank loan
Submit an online application with your Singpass
Processing time: generally within five working days

questions.title: If someone who had used CPF savings for a property passes away, must we repay the CPF housing refund to the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold?
questions.text: No, you do not have to refund the CPF savings used by the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold.

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property or to pay for the housing loan of my existing property?
questions.text:
If you are buying an HDB flat
You can use your CPF savings to buy an HDB flat or pay the housing loan of your existing HDB flat, provided you are the owner of the HDB flat. You will need to contact HDB directly regarding this matter.
If you are buying a private property
You will need to obtain consent from the Official Assignee before you can use your CPF savings to buy a private property or pay the housing loan of your existing property.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I request to make a partial repayment and leave some monies in my CPF Account for my housing loan?
questions.text: Yes, you can request to make a partial repayment of your housing loan from your CPF account even if you are a bankrupt. This arrangement allows you to retain some funds in your account to continue servicing for your housing loan.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am not the next‑of‑kin and cannot prove my relationship with the deceased. How can I urgently apply for a burial or cremation permit?
questions.text:
If you are not the next‑of‑kin (NOK), you may still apply for a burial or cremation permit if the deceased’s NOK authorizes you to do so.
In such cases, you will need a Letter of Authorisation (LOA) from the deceased’s next‑of‑kin. The LOA template is available here.
Please submit the completed LOA together with your application via NEA’s e‑portal.
If you encounter issues with the submission and the issue is not resolved within 24 hours, please contact MyLegacy at go.gov.sg/edc for assistance.

questions.title: Where can I check the number of discounted Singtel shares I have?
questions.text: You can login to my cpf Online Services with your Singpass and check the "Discounted Singtel shares" section in the Investment dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How can I retrieve my Healthcare payments and claims statement online?
questions.text:
You can view your healthcare payments and claims details (containing information such as the name of patient, hospital registration number (HRN), hospitalisation period, etc), with transaction dates within the last 15 months at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
Log in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' and select 'View past 15 months'
Select the period you require and click 'Search'.
Select the PDF icon at the top-right-hand corner of the page to save/print the statement.
Here is a step-by-step guide on how you can retrieve the Healthcare payments and claims statement. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
Please note that your claim details are available on your Healthcare dashboard for up to 15 months, after which they will no longer be retrievable. Download your statement in a timely manner to ensure you always have a copy for your own records or future use.
When submitting reimbursement claims to your employer or insurer, a digital copy should be sufficient.

questions.title: I changed job in 2025. Must I key in my employment income from the first employer?
questions.text: You do not have to report employment income from the first employer if clearance has been sought on the said income. Refer to Re-employment in Singapore for more details.
topics: Individual Income Tax / General tax matters

questions.title: I did not receive my Singpass password as I have changed my address. What should I do?
questions.text:
The Singpass PIN will be sent to your registered address maintained by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM). You or your employer need to login to EP Online to update the address. Your employer can make the change on your behalf. After that, you can request for a new Singpass mailer to be sent to you. Visit Singpass Portal > Select "Services" on the top scroll bar > Select "Reset password". Enter your "FIN number" and "Date of issue".
For enquiries on filing of income tax, please visit Tax Season 2026 – All you need to know
For enquiries on assessment, please visit Tax Season 2026 – About Your Tax Bill
If your enquiry is regarding your personal tax matters, email us at myTax Portal with your Singpass or Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA).
topics: Individual Income Tax / General tax matters

questions.title: My salary is paid by my foreign employer in my home country/region. Am I liable to Singapore income tax?
questions.text: Yes, income earned for the period you render your services is taxable in Singapore. Taxable income includes your salary, bonus, allowances and housing provided by the foreign employer and the local sponsor company.
topics: Individual Income Tax / General tax matters (for employees working for foreign employers)

questions.title: I am based outside Singapore and travel into Singapore for business purpose. Am I liable to Singapore income tax if I am paying taxes in my home country/region?
questions.text: If you are a tax resident of a jurisdiction that has a DTA with Singapore, it may protect you from being taxed twice on the same income. This depends on the provisions of the DTA. Find out more about DTA Calculator - Dependent Services (XLS, 288KB).
topics: Individual Income Tax / General tax matters (for employees working for foreign employers)

questions.title: I have tendered my resignation/am leaving Singapore for more than 3 months. What are my tax obligations in Singapore?
questions.text: As part of the tax clearance process, your employer is required to withhold the payment of all monies due to you from the date they are aware of your impending cessation of employment or departure from Singapore. Your employer is also required to file Form IR21 for you at least one month before you cease employment with them, go on overseas posting, or leave Singapore for more than three months. You may refer to this link for more details on the tax clearance process.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employees

questions.title: My employer has filed for my tax clearance. How do I pay my income tax balance? Can I continue to use GIRO?
questions.text:
Upon tax clearance, any existing GIRO instalment plan you have with IRAS will be terminated. If the monies withheld by your employer are insufficient to cover your income tax balance, you are required to pay the shortfall as stated in your Income Tax Bill Overview letter within 7 days of the date of the letter, via other electronic payment modes.
However, if you will be re-employed by another Singapore employer immediately after your cessation of employment and wish to continue paying your income tax via GIRO instalments, please email us your request along with the required documents at myTax Portal using your Singpass or Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA).
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employees

questions.title: I have only worked for less than half a year in Singapore. Why is my income tax so high?
questions.text: You may have been assessed as a non-tax resident, where the overall tax rate tends to be higher. You can check if you qualify to be a Singapore tax resident, and if you do, you may file an amendment using the 'Amend Tax Bill' digital service at myTax Portal. Alternatively, you can email/post the completed Request for Tax Reassessment (DOC, 203KB) form to us. Your income tax balance must be settled by the due date regardless of any amendment request. Any credit balance that arises from the review of your assessment will be automatically refunded within 30 days.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employees

questions.title: Payment reminder or late payment penalty on Tax Clearance Directive
questions.text: If you would like to seek IRAS’ guidance and advice on the tax treatment for your case (excluding hypothetical or tax planning enquiries), please give us the full facts of the case and your company’s UEN.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employers

questions.title: Is tax clearance required for a foreign intern?
questions.text: Tax clearance is not required for a foreign intern who is doing his business or industrial attachment as a compulsory part of his educational programme and is only paid subsistence allowances to meet his daily expenses and board and lodging in Singapore. However, if the foreign intern enters into an employment contract and is remunerated for services rendered to the organisation in Singapore, tax clearance will be required.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employers

questions.title: Are severance payments taxable? How do I report them in the Form IR21?
questions.text: Please refer to this webpage for more information on the taxability of the different types of severance payments. Please report the details of the payments accordingly in Section F of the Form IR21 for our review. If your organisation is carrying out a mass retrenchment exercise, you can check with us on the taxability of the payments once the retrenchment package has been finalised by providing details of the retrenchment package and the basis of arriving at each component.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employers

questions.title: My employee is transferred to a related company in Singapore. Is tax clearance required?
questions.text: Tax clearance is not required if the employee is transferred due to a company merger or takeover, or a restructuring or posting within the same group of companies. However, you are required to notify us of the transfer using this template (XLS, 44KB).
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employers

questions.title: My employee has some unexercised share options/unvested shares. How should I report them?
questions.text: Please refer to this webpage for more information.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax clearance for Employers

questions.title: How can I recover pre-filled information that has been deleted?
questions.text:
Pre-filled information cannot be recovered once deleted. To add employees’ records, refer to the user guide on 'Submit Employment Income Records' (PDF,
1.1 MB).
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: IRAS requires the annual income information but the CPF submissions are done monthly. How will the data from CPF Board be reflected at the 'Submit Employment Income records' digital service?
questions.text:
The monthly income and deduction information e-Submitted to CPF Board for each employee will be summed up and pre-filled as the annual income.
Note:
If you use a different CSNs with the same UEN (e.g. 12345678A-PTE-01 and 12345678A-PTE-02), all the employees' information under the respective CSNs will be summed up.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: Will my claims, refunds or adjustments to CPF Board be reflected at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: All changes to CPF Board will be reflected in the prefilled data. However, if changes are made close to the prefilling date, they may not be included as the data would have already been processed and prefilled into the system. If the amount is not accurate, please adjust the pre-filled data before submitting to IRAS.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: How will the Ordinary Wages (OW) and Additional Wages (AW) that I have submitted to CPF Board be shown at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: OW and AW will be shown as 'Salary' and 'Bonus' respectively.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: Will donation information submitted to CPF Board be shown at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text:
Donations deducted through employees' salary for CDAC, SINDA and Eurasian Community Fund will be pre-filled under the 'Donations' field.
However, contributions/donations to Mosque Building Fund, Mendaki Fund and Community Chest will not be pre-filled. Employers must manually input these amounts under the respective fields.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: Can authorised third party (e.g. tax agent) view and edit the pre-filled data at myTax Portal?
questions.text:
Authorised third party will not be able to view and edit the pre-filled data. Only authorised staff with the 'Approver' role for the 'Submission of Employment Income Records' digital service
via Corppass can view, edit and delete the pre-filled data.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: I am using a payroll software that can generate complete employee records. Can I deregister from the AIS Data link-up service?
questions.text:
Since your payroll software already has all the necessary employees’ information for submission, you can deregister from the AIS Data Link-up Service.
To deregister, follow these steps:
Staff with 'Approver' or 'Preparer' (PDF, 690KB) role (exclude tax agents) for the 'Submission of Employment Income Records' digital service to log in to myTax Portal.
Select 'Employers' > 'Register Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS) for Employment Income'
Click 'De-Register' under the 'AIS Data Link-up Service' section.
Select the reason for withdrawal, complete the 'Applicant Details', 'Declaration' and click 'Submit'.
An acknowledgement page will appear once the deregistration is successful.
Note: Your organisation will remain registered for AIS and is still required to submit employees’ employment income information to IRAS by 1 Mar each year.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: If the contribution details were not e-Submitted to CPF Board by 14 Jan, will the information be pre-filled at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text:
Submissions made after 14 Jan will not be pre-filled and employers will have to manually add the income information which have been submitted to CPF Board after 14 Jan at IRAS' digital service.
For example
If the CPF contribution for the month of Dec 2025 is submitted after 14 Jan 2026, the data for Dec 2025 will not be pre-filled for the YA 2026 submission. You will have to manually add the income information for Dec 2025 at IRAS' digital service.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: There were changes to my employees' personal particulars during the year. How will the particulars be reflected at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: Your employees' personal particulars will be pre-filled based on the latest CPF submission or MOM data. Please verify and update the information in the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service in myTax Portal to ensure the accuracy and completeness of your employees' personal particulars (e.g. date of birth and name as per NRIC).
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: What should I do if my organisation hires both local and foreign employees, but the foreign employees' data is not pre-filled at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: You must add your foreign employees' record manually and submit both your foreign employees' records and the local employees' records. Find out on how to add employee records on Page 12 of the user guide (PDF, 1.1 MB).
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: What should I do if some components of my employees' salary package do not require CPF Contributions and are not included in my submissions to CPF Board (e.g., provision of accommodation)?
questions.text: You must manually add the income items that are taxable but not prefilled, in 'Submit Employment Income Records', before you submit the same to IRAS. Examples of such items include Director's fees, Tax paid by employer, Benefits-in-Kind, Stock Option Gains etc.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: What should I do if some components of my employees' salary package are not taxable but they have been included in my submissions to CPF Board (e.g., income of employees who are posted overseas)?
questions.text: For income items that are not taxable, you must make the necessary adjustments at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service. Examples of such items are income of seamen, income earned from overseas postings that is not incidental to Singapore employment, etc.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: Do I need to prepare the appendices if Benefits-in-Kind or Stock Option Gains are provided to my employees?
questions.text: If there are Benefits-in-Kind or Stock Option Gains given to your employees, you must complete and submit the relevant appendices (Appendix 8A and Appendix 8B) at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: 1. My pre-filled employment income is wrong, what should I do?
questions.text: Your employer has submitted your income information for the year 2025 (Year of Assessment 2026) to us directly. For any discrepancy, please check with your employer directly. They will resubmit the information to us if there are errors in the original submission, and this will be included in your tax bill.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax Season 2026 - All you need to know

questions.title: 2. My employer is not under Auto-Inclusion Scheme (AIS), what information do I need to file my Income Tax Return?
questions.text:
If your employer is not participating under AIS, your employer should have provided you with the Form IR8A by 1 Mar. You should enter the details during your tax filing as per the information in your Form IR8A. If you do not have the Form IR8A, please request it from your employer.
You are not required to submit your Form IR8A or other supporting documents unless specifically stated at the acknowledgement page after you have filed.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax Season 2026 - All you need to know

questions.title: 3. Can I claim personal reliefs and rebates?
questions.text:
You may claim personal reliefs and rebates if you are Singapore tax resident and have met the qualifying conditions for the respective reliefs/rebates in the preceding year (i.e. 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025).
Find out which reliefs you may be eligible for:
PERSONAL RELIEF CHECKER
To check your eligibility for Parenthood Tax Rebate, use the Parenthood Tax Rebate Eligibility Tool (XLSM, 67KB).

questions.title: 4. Can I claim expenses?
questions.text:
Generally, you may claim tax deductions on expenses "wholly and exclusively" incurred in earning your income. Find out more about deductions for the different types of expenses (e.g. employment expenses, business expenses).
To simplify the tax filing for rental expenses, you may opt to claim the rental expenses based on 15% of the gross rental income derived from the tenanted residential property, instead of the actual amount of deductible expenses incurred. In addition to the 15%, you may claim a deduction on interest paid on the loan taken to purchase the property. You may use the Rental Calculator (XSLM, 146KB) to decide if it is beneficial to claim 15% deemed rental expenses or to claim based on actual rental expenses incurred. Find out more about the Simplification of Claim of Rental Expenses for Individuals.
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax Season 2026 - All you need to know

questions.title: 5. What if I require more time to file my Income Tax Return?
questions.text: If you need additional time to file your Income Tax Return, an extension of up to 14 days may be granted. You may use 'Apply for Extension of Time to File' digital service at myTax Portal.

questions.title: How do I make payment for my property taxes?
questions.text:
The easiest way is to pay using AXS with your property tax reference number shown on your bill or by scanning PayNow QR code in myTax Portal. Your payment will be posted into the tax account immediately.
Alternatively, you can make payment via internet banking. Please quote the 8-character tax reference number when making payment. The payment will be updated in 3 working days.

questions.title: I have made payment for my property tax. How come it still shows the outstanding tax in the tax portal? Has IRAS received my payment?
questions.text: We wish to share that for payment made via internet banking or bank transfer, it will be usually posted into your tax account within 3 working days.

questions.title: My sales completion is on Jan 2026. Am I required to pay the 2026 property tax?
questions.text:
Property tax is payable in advance in the month of January. If the sale completion of your property is in the year 2026, you are required to pay the whole year tax. During the sale completion, the HDB officer or your lawyer will apportion the tax liability between you and the buyer, so that you will be reimbursed accordingly.
The apportionment of property tax liabilities is a private arrangement between the seller and buyer. The HDB officers (for HDB flats) or your lawyer would usually assist you in apportioning the tax amount and in seeking the reimbursement from the buyer. IRAS does not apportion nor arbitrate property tax liabilities between the parties.
Please check with the HDB officers (for HDB flats) or your lawyer regarding your property tax obligations for the year.

questions.title: I have sold my property effective from Dec 2025. Am I still required to pay the property tax for 2026?
questions.text: If the sale completion is before 1 Jan 2026, you may ignore the property tax bill for year 2026. HDB or your lawyer would notify IRAS within one month of the transfer so that the new owner will be billed for the year 2026. If you continue to be billed after the transfer of your property, please check with your lawyer if IRAS has been notified of the transfer.

questions.title: How to apply for a travel application as a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Applying for permission to travel outside Singapore as a Bankrupt
Bankrupts are required to submit and obtain permission from their trustee in bankruptcy before they are allowed to leave, remain or reside outside Singapore. This includes all trips, whether for work, personal reasons, or emergencies.
Submitting your travel application
Step 1: Login to the Insolvent Person's Portal at https://go.gov.sg/bankruptcy via Singpass Login.
Step 2: Fill in your travel details
Travel dates
Destination
Reason for Travel
Sponsor for the trip
Step 3: Upload supporting documents
E.g., employment letter, doctor's memo or death certificate
Step 4: Review and submit
The step-by-step guide to submitting a travel application can be found at https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/bankruptcy/information-for-bankrupts/userguides/.
What happens after you submit
You will receive the outcome via SMS and/or email from your appointed trustee. If you have any enquiries, please contact your appointed trustee in bankruptcy for assistance.

questions.title: How to check my bankruptcy or discharge status?
questions.text:
Discharge from bankruptcy
A discharge means being released from bankruptcy. The bankrupt will no longer be liable for debts owed in bankruptcy, except for certain types of debts such as debts owed to government.
Certificate of Discharge
Bankrupts who were discharged from bankruptcy by the Official Assignee will receive their Certificate of Discharge at their registered address via post.
Letter of Discharge
Bankrupts may request for a letter of discharge from the Insolvency Office if their bankruptcy was discharged by a court order of the High Court. Please submit your request through the online enquiry form at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw. A copy of the letter will be sent to you via email.
Insolvency Search
Bankrupts may also conduct a paid search using the Insolvency Search Service at https://go.gov.sg/bankruptcy on our website. A fee of $6.00 is payable for each search.
If you encounter any problems with this service, pleae contact us at 1800-2255-529* (during office hours) or submit an online enquiry through Contact Us @ OneMinLaw.
*Airtime charges may apply to calls made from mobile phones to '1800' local toll-free numbers.

questions.title: How to check the status of my travel application?
questions.text:
Travel Application
Bankrupts are required to obtain their appointed trustee in bankruptcy's (this is the person assigned by the court to manage your bankruptcy case) prior consent before they are allowed to leave, remain or reside outside Singapore.
Status of application
Bankrupts can check on the status of their travel application by logging in to theInsolvent Person's Portal via Singpass Login.
The status of the application will be reflected on the dashboard located at the landing page of the Insolvent Person's Portal.
Notification of approval
Bankrupts should receive the outcome of their application via SMS and/or email. If there are any enquiries, bankrupts should contact their appointed trustee in bankruptcy via the contact details provided in the court documents for assistance.

questions.title: How to file Statement of Account of Moneys and Property Received (SMP) form?
questions.text:
Filing a Statement of Account of Moneys and Property Received ("SMP")
The SMP is a mandatory report filed and submitted every 6 months by the bankrupt to the appointed trustee in bankruptcy (this is the person assigned by the court to manage your bankruptcy case) detailing an account of all moneys and property which have come to his hand for his own use.
Submitting your SMP
Step 1: Login to the Insolvent Person's Portal at https://go.gov.sg/bankruptcy via Singpass Login.
Step 2: Fill in your details
Personal particulars
Employment details
Any other sources of income
Particulars of financial supporters, if any.
Step 3: Upload supporting documents
E.g., Employment letter, CPF statement, Utility Bills and IR8A from IRAS.
Step 4: Review and submit
The step-by-step guide to submitting a SMP can be found at https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/bankruptcy/information-for-bankrupts/userguides/.
What happens after you submit
The bankrupt will receive an e-filing number after submitting the SMP. The appointed trustee will review the submission and contact the bankrupt if there are any clarifications required.

questions.title: Can I appeal a travel application?
questions.text:
Travel Application
Bankrupts are required to obtain their appointed trustee in bankruptcy's (this is the person assigned by the court to manage your bankruptcy case) prior consent before they are allowed to leave, remain or reside outside Singapore.
Rejection of Travel Application
Travel applications submitted by bankrupts may be declined due to insufficient documentation, including inadequate details about your employer and/or the party funding your trip.
Appealing the rejection
Bankrupts whose travel application have been rejected may submit an appeal to their appointed trustee in bankruptcy (this is the person assigned by the court to manage your bankruptcy case) via the contact details provided in the court documents.
Appeals must specifically address the grounds for initial rejection and include all additional supporting documentation required for reconsideration.

questions.title: What are the benefits of using the Will Learning tool?
questions.text: This tool helps you learn about the importance of having a will, key decisions you need to make, and important considerations when distributing your assets. By working through these decisions beforehand, you'll be better prepared for conversations with lawyers or other professionals when you're ready to draft your official will. The tool makes will-writing concepts easy to understand through hands-on learning rather than simply reading about them.

questions.title: Is my personal information secure when using this Will Learning tool?
questions.text:
Your privacy is protected when using this tool. Any personal information you choose to enter is automatically deleted once you complete the learning exercise. If you save your progress to return later, your information is stored securely and temporarily until you finish or delete it yourself.
Please note that entering personal information is entirely optional throughout the tool - you can complete the learning exercise without providing any personal details. However, if you do include your information, it will help create a Will Preparation Template with your decisions and details recorded for your future reference.

questions.title: Does my will need to be written in English?
questions.text:
No, there is no legal requirement for your will to be written in English. However, there are practical considerations to keep in mind if a will is written in another language.
Your will needs to be clearly understood by your executors, beneficiaries, and the courts. Using English may make this process smoother, as all documents filed or used in the Court must be in the English language. If your will is written in another language, translation will be required.
Please note that this learning tool is currently available only in English.

questions.title: What should I do after completing the Will Learning tool?
questions.text:
At the end of the tool, you'll receive a Will Preparation Template that summarises your decisions. This template is not a legal will, but it's a useful reference document to bring to a lawyer when creating your actual will.
While you're not legally required to use a lawyer, doing so can help ensure that your will is legally sound and consider scenarios you might have missed, particularly if you have more complex estate planning needs. The template will help guide these conversations and make the process more efficient.

questions.title: Can I use the Will Learning tool to write a legally binding Will?
questions.text: No, nothing you enter in the learning tool is final or legally binding. This is purely a learning tool to help you understand will-writing concepts. The Will Preparation Template you receive at the end can be revisited and amended at any time, even after completing the exercise.

questions.title: Can the Will Preparation Template serve as my official will if I get it witnessed and signed?
questions.text: No. The tool is meant for learning only. The intent of the Will Preparation Template is to equip you with a prepared set of documented decisions and details, to make it easier when you visit your lawyer. It is not intended to act as your will. There may be specific clauses and circumstances that your will should cover, that would not be sufficiently covered by the preparation template.

questions.title: What legal expertise was involved in creating this Will Learning tool?
questions.text: This tool has been reviewed by lawyers specialising in estate planning, to ensure factual accuracy of its content. This was last reviewed in December 2025.

questions.title: How long does it take to complete the Will Learning tool and how long is my progress saved?
questions.text: The learning tool need not be completed in one sitting and you may take as much time as you need during each session to facilitate your learning. You can save the progress of your learning, and revisit it later. Your progress will be saved up to 6 months from the start of your learning, after which your data and progress will be purged and reset.

questions.title: Can I modify the Will Preparation Template after completing the tool?
questions.text: You cannot modify your responses within the learning tool once completed, as this data is not stored after completion. However, you can edit the Will Preparation Template document that you download and receive at the end, outside of this tool. If you want to go through the learning exercise again with different inputs, you can restart the tool from the beginning, although that is not necessary once you've completed the learning.

questions.title: I am a Muslim. Can I use the Will Learning tool to draft my Wasiat?
questions.text:
If you’re a Muslim who’s interested in using this tool, it’s important to understand the key differences between a civil will and Wasiat.
Wasiat follows specific Islamic inheritance rules:
You can only distribute up to one-third of your estate through a Wasiat.
This portion can only go to non-Faraid beneficiaries, who are not already entitled to inherit under Islamic law (for example, adopted children, non-Muslim family members, or charities).
The remaining two-thirds of your estate must be distributed according to Faraid rules, as per the Inheritance Certificate issued by Syariah Court.
In contrast, non-Muslims can use civil wills to distribute their entire estate to anyone they choose, whether individuals or organisations.
This learning tool is designed for civil wills and may be helpful for general understanding of will-writing. Wasiat works differently and estate distribution methods explained in the tool differ from Islamic inheritance law.
Seek specific guidance on Wasiat and Faraid rules from a trained professional if you're considering Islamic estate planning. For more information, refer to Muis’ Wasiat Planning Guide.

questions.title: After completing the learning, can I write my own will without going to a lawyer?
questions.text:
Yes, you can legally write your own will without a lawyer. The learning tool covers basic will-writing concepts and simple scenarios to help you understand the process.
However, writing a legally sound will involves many technical requirements and potential complications that this tool cannot fully address. A lawyer can help ensure your will meets all legal requirements, consider scenarios you might not have anticipated, and draft clear language that reduces the risk of disputes later.
If you choose to write your own will, we strongly recommend having it reviewed by a lawyer before finalising it, especially if your situation involves complex assets, family circumstances, or cross-border considerations.

questions.title: What if I need in-person support or cannot use this digital Will Learning tool?
questions.text:
If you're unable to use this digital learning tool or prefer in-person guidance, you can:
Consult directly with a lawyer who specialises in estate planning for personalised assistance with will-writing
Contact community legal clinics or legal aid services if you need affordable legal guidance (subject to meeting the qualifiying criteria)
Seek help from family members or trusted friends to navigate the digital tool together
While this online tool provides a convenient way to learn about will-writing basics, it's not the only path to understanding or creating a will. Professional legal advice remains available through traditional channels.

questions.title: How can the Public Trustee's Office help to administer a Deceased's estate (bank account, shares, motor vehicles, etc.)
questions.text:
What is estate administration
Estate administration is the legal process of realising and distributing a Deceased’s assets according to his / her will or the intestacy law.
What assets can be administered by the Public Trustee's Office
Deceased’s moneys in banks or other financial institutions in Singapore;
Deceased’s shares which are listed on the Singapore Exchange;
Deceased’s fully paid-up vehicles except commercial vehicles like taxis;
Deceased’s salary that was owed;
Deceased’s items in a safe-deposit box;
Deceased’s moneys paid as government compensation; and
Deceased’s moneys from the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme.
How does the Deceased’s next of kin make an estate application
An online application can be made via https://go.gov.sg/pto and select "Deceased’s Assets other than Un-nominated CPF Moneys / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA" for the Public Trustee to administer the Deceased’s estate. The next of kin will be required to disclose information on the Deceased’s shares, bank savings account, death gratuity, insurance policies and vehicles owned (if any) in the online application.
You will need to have your Singpass ready in order to access our online application form. You may apply for your Singpass at https://www.singpass.gov.sg if you do not have one.
If you are ineligible to apply for a Singpass, you may apply for a login ID and password through our website: https://go.gov.sg/pto.
Where the total value of the asset more than $50,000, you will have to engage your own solicitors to administer the Deceased’s estate. The Public Trustee’s Office does not provide a list of solicitors.
Outcome
As a general rule, we will distribute the moneys within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation from the beneficiary or the date of receipt of the Deceased’s moneys, whichever is later.

questions.title: How to claim the Deceased's shares?
questions.text:

If the value of the shareholding is $5,000 or below, you can approach CDP directly to claim the Deceased’s shareholding.
Please take note that the Public Trustee can only assist in the transfer of the Deceased’s CDP shares, if the total value of the estate is $50,000 or less, to the intended transferee.
Common types of documents required are:
Death Certificate of Deceased
Birth Certificate of Deceased
Marriage Certificate of Deceased
Decree Nisi Absolute (if the Deceased was divorced)
Birth Certificate of Beneficiary
Identity Card of Beneficiary
Death Certificate of Beneficiary (if Deceased)
Marriage Certificate of Deceased’s Parents
Death Certificate of Parent (if Deceased)
Certificate of Inheritance (For Muslims only)
If there are multiple beneficiaries, (e.g., Deceased left behind a spouse and children) the other family members may choose to give up his / her share so claimant can claim the shares. Alternatively, the claimant may buy over the other beneficiary’ shares.
Important: Only beneficiary who is 21 years old and above can give up his / her share.
What happens next
· You will get an email confirming your application was received
· A case officer will review your application
· If more documents are needed, you will be notified
· You will be asked to make payment of the administration fee for transfer of shares / vehicle
If you need help
