questions.title: How to check if Deceased's CPF monies have been transferred to the Public Trustee's Office
questions.text:
If someone passed away, his / her CPF moneys may be forwarded to the Public Trustee for distribution to the beneficiary if it was not nominated. Here's how to check if this has happened.
What happens to un-nominated CPF moneys
Un-nominated CPF moneys means CPF savings which the Deceased did not choose who should receive the moneys. When someone passed away, the CPF Board will forward these moneys to the Public Trustee for distribution to the beneficiary according to intestacy law.
Timeline for transfer
Upon receiving notification of the death of the CPF member, they typically require 17 working days to transfer the un-nominated CPF moneys to the Public Trustee’s Office.
How you will be notified
The next of kin will be notified by post.
How to check if the transfer has happened
Option 1: Wait for the notification letter
The Public Trustee's Office will out a letter to the next of kin once they receive the CPF moneys from CPF Board.
Option 2: Contact the Public Trustee's Office directly
If the next of kin did not receive the notification after 6 weeks of Deceased’s death, you may contact the Public Trustee's Office via:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM
Before you call, please get ready the Deceased's identity number

questions.title: How are un-nominated CPF moneys distributed among beneficiaries?
questions.text:
Un-nominated CPF moneys means the Deceased’s CPF savings where the Deceased did not choose who should receive the moneys. When someone passed away, the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) distributes these savings to the beneficiary.
The distribution rules are different for Muslim and non-Muslim families because they follow different legal systems.
For non-Muslim families
The un-nominated moneys are distributed in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act 1967.
Distribution rules
Situation
Person passed away leaving
How the moneys / estate is shared
1
Spouse, no children, no parents
100% to surviving spouse
2
Spouse and children
50% to surviving spouse, 50% shared equally among children (and/or grandchildren if children are deceased)
3
Children, no spouse
100% shared equally among children (or their children if deceased)
4
Spouse and parents, no children
50% to surviving spouse, 50% shared equally among surviving parents
5
Parents, no spouse, no children
100% shared equally among surviving parents
6
Brothers or sisters, no spouse, no children, no parents
100% shared equally among brothers and sisters (or their children if deceased)
7
Grandparents, no other above beneficiary
100% shared equally among surviving grandparents
8
Uncles and aunts, no other above beneficiary
100% shared equally among surviving uncles and aunts
Example
If someone passed away leaving a wife and 2 children:
Wife receives: 50% of the CPF moneys / estate
Each child receives: 25% of the CPF moneys / estate
You may also visit our Intestacy Calculator to reference who are the potential beneficiary.
For Muslim families
If the Deceased was a Muslim, the distribution follows Islamic inheritance law under the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966.
The Syariah Court will issue an Inheritance Certificate that lists down who are the beneficiary and how much each person receives.
How to find out your share
Option 1: Use the Online Trial Inheritance Calculator
Thereafter apply for an Inheritance Certificate from the Syariah Court
What to do next
Every family situation is different. Before you make an application with the Public Trustee’s Office, make sure you have all the required documents ready
(what are the documents to be submitted to the Public Trustee).
How to apply for the distribution of un-nominated CPF moneys:
· Visit our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto
· Click on Administration of Deceased’s CPF / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA
· Log in with your Singpass
Need help with the steps? Download the step-by-step guide.
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: Who cannot act as a Beneficiary Representative?
questions.text:
The following beneficiary cannot act as a Beneficiary Representative:
Undischarged bankrupts
Children under the age of 21
Mentally incapacitated persons
Prison inmates

questions.title: What happens if one of the beneficiaries is a child under the age of 21 and is unable to provide consent for the Beneficiary Representative application?
questions.text: The Public Trustee’s Office will require the Beneficiary Representative to submit documents to prove the familial relationship of the child and the Deceased CPF member. Thereafter, the child’s share will be held in trust by the Public Trustee until the child attains the age of 21 years old. The Beneficiary Representative will be able to represent the other beneficiary after obtaining his / her consent to receive the moneys on his / her behalf.

questions.title: If a beneficiary objects to the Beneficiary Representative representing him / her, can the Beneficiary Representative still submit a claim?
questions.text:
No, the Public Trustee’s Office will reject the Beneficiary Representative’s claim where disputes have been observed or made known to our office.
All beneficiary must give consent. If the Beneficiary Representative is unable to obtain all beneficiary’s consent, he / she has to disclose it at point of application and will be redirected to submit a standard claim instead.

questions.title: Can the Beneficiary Representative still apply to make a claim if he / she knows the existence of other beneficiary but is unaware of all the beneficiary’s name, identity number, and contact details?
questions.text:
The Beneficiary Representative approach is a simplified process for disbursing the un-nominated CPF moneys of a Deceased CPF member that do not exceed $10,000.
Under the Beneficiary Representative approach, an eligible beneficiary who is entitled to a share of the un-nominated CPF moneys is allowed to represent all the other beneficiary to receive the full claim of the CPF moneys on his / her behalf, upon obtaining his / her consent. He / she is known as the Beneficiary Representative.
The onus is on the Beneficiary Representative to distribute the moneys to all the other beneficiary in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act 1967 (for non-Muslims) or the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966 (for Muslims), subject to any instruction which the beneficiary may give concerning his / her entitlements.
The Beneficiary Representative will be unable to proceed with the Beneficiary Representative application as he / she is unable to obtain the consent of all beneficiary.
The Beneficiary Representative will then have to submit a standard claim application instead. For more information on standard claim application, please refer to https://go.gov.sg/cpf-estate.

questions.title: Can I get the Public Trustee’s assistance in resealing in Singapore, Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that was obtained overseas
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not assist in resealing in the Singapore Courts for Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that were obtained overseas. You will have to engage a Singapore lawyer to assist you.
You can search for a Singapore law practice or lawyer using the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's online search function athttps://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/. Please note that the search results are based on information provided by law practices and lawyers. The Ministry of Law does not make any warranty or representation as to their accuracy, completeness or reliability.

questions.title: Does the Public Trustee assist in the administration of a Deceased’s share in a HDB flat if it is of small value?
questions.text: On a case-by-case basis, the Public Trustee does administer a Deceased’s small value share in a HDB flat. You will have to submit an online application for the Public Trustee to administer the Deceased’s estate so that we may consider your request. We cannot act if the person who died was the sole owner of a HDB flat and there is a beneficiary to inherit whole or part of the flat.

questions.title: Can I get moneys from my child's held-in-trust fund to support them?
questions.text:
If you are the parent or guardian of a child and you are having financial difficulties, you may be able to get a maintenance allowance from your child's trust fund to help support them.
What is a maintenance allowance
A maintenance allowance is moneys that the Public Trustee's Office can release from your child's trust fund to help pay for his / her daily needs like food, housing, and school fees, etc.
Under the Women's Charter 1961 (sections 68 and 70), parent and guardian has a legal duty to support his / her child. When you cannot afford this support, we may release some of the child's own moneys to help.
You can apply if:
You are the parent or legal guardian of the child
The child has moneys held in trust with the Public Trustee's Office
You are facing financial difficulties in supporting the child
What we consider when reviewing your application
We will look at these four factors to decide if you qualify and how much moneys to release:
Your income, property and other financial resources.
Your financial needs and responsibilities.
The financial needs and the age of the child.
The way in which the child is being or is expected to be educated or trained.
We may also consider other factors relevant to the application.
How the moneys are paid
The maintenance allowance will be paid into a joint savings account (shared between you and your child) every 3 months in January, April, July and October.
The moneys are transferred automatically using GIRO (which means automatic bank transfer from the trust fund to your joint account).
[Important] You must have the following documents ready:
Joint savings account with your child before applying.
Birth certificate of the child and your Identity Card (if you are the parent)
Guardianship documents (if you are the guardian, not the parent)
What to do next
To apply for a maintenance allowance:
· Visit our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto
· Click on “Maintenance and Allowance for Minor”
· Log in with your Singpass
Need help with the steps? Download the step-by-step guide.
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: What happens if I cannot afford to pay the extra expenses ie school fees?
questions.text:
If you cannot afford to pay for your child's expenses like school fees, medical bills, or other necessary costs, the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) may pay or reimburse these expenses from your child's trust fund after assessment.
What expenses can be covered
PTO can pay for expenses that are necessary for your child's wellbeing and development, such as:
School fees and educational costs
Welfare of the child
Example: If your child needs $2,000 for school fees and you cannot afford it, we can pay the school directly from your child's trust fund.
How we decide
PTO will consider your application based on:
Your financial situation and ability to pay
Whether the expense is necessary for your child
The amount of moneys available in your child's trust fund
How payments work
If PTO approve your request:
Option 1: Direct payment
You provide the institution's bank details
We pay directly to the service provider (school, hospital, etc.)
Option 2: Reimbursement
You pay first and keep the receipt
We reimburse you after approval
Moneys is transferred to your account
What to do next
To apply for expense coverage:
Visit our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto
Click on “Maintenance and Allowance for Minor”
Log in with your Singpass
Need help with the steps? Download the step-by-step guide.
Required documents
Proof of the expense (invoice, bill, receipt)
Institution's bank information (if we pay directly to the service provider)
Birth certificate of the child and your identity card (if you are the parent)
Guardianship documents (if you are the guardian, not the parent)
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: Can I print or download my Statement of Account?
questions.text:
Yes, you can print or download your Statement of Account in PDF format from the Public Trustee's Office e-Services for your records. The Statement of Account is available immediately once you access it online.
What is a Statement of Account
A Statement of Account is a document that shows:
The balance in your child's trust fund
Moneys paid into the beneficiary(s)’ account
Transaction dates and details
How to print or download your statement
Visit our e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto
Click on “Statement of Account”
Log in with your Singpass
Need help with the steps? Download the step-by-step guide.
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw /
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: What will happen to my trust moneys if I do not claim it immediately after I reach my age of majority?
questions.text:
You will receive a letter before you reach your age of majority (18 or 21 years old). If you do not claim your trust moneys after you reach age of majority, the Public Trustee's Office will treat your moneys as unclaimed moneys until you come forward to claim it.
To learn more about age of majority, download the brochure.
Status of your moneys
Your unclaimed moneys are protected:
Your moneys remain safe and secure with the Public Trustee's Office
No fees are deducted for keeping your moneys unclaimed
Your moneys do not expire - you can claim it at any time
What you need to claim your moneys
You can submit the required documents to us via e-Services at https://go.gov.sg/pto :
If you are a Singaporean with a local bank account:
Bank account passbook / bank account statement or PayNow
If you are a foreigner with a local bank account:
Your Identification Card that you used to open the bank account
Front page of your personal bank account passbook or bank account statement
If you are living overseas and for us to pay the moneys to you via telegraphic transfer:
Your Identification Card that you used to open the bank account
Front page of your personal bank account passbook or bank account statement showing:
-Bank account number
-Sort code of the bank
-Swift code of the bank
-Name of the bank and bank branch (if any)
-Address of the bank
-Your preferred currency for payment
-Your overseas residential address
Important things to know
There are no fees or penalties for claiming your moneys late
Family members cannot claim for you
Keep your contact details updated (address and email)
If you need help
Contact the Public Trustee's Office:
Phone: 1800 225 5529 (airtime charges may apply for mobile calls)
Online enquiry: Contact Us @ OneMinLaw at https://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw
[Note] Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM

questions.title: Do I need to pay CPF contributions for my foreign employee who has recently obtained Singapore Permanent Residence status?
questions.text:
Yes, CPF contributions are payable once your foreign employee obtains his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status. Please ensure that your employee informs you of his SPR status.
For the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, to help your employee adjust to the lower take-home pay, both you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at graduated rates (refer to Tables 2 and 3). From the third year onwards, you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at the full rates (refer to Table 1).
Determining your employee’s year of SPR status
The year of SPR status determines your employee’s CPF contribution rates.
First-year rate: Applies from the day your employee obtains his SPR status until the last day of the month of his first anniversary. The SPR status date is shown on his Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.
Example
If your employee obtained his SPR status on 15 January 2026, the start and end dates for first, second and third year of obtaining SPR status are shown in the table below:
Years of obtaining SPR statusStarts fromEnds on
First year15 January 202631 January 2027
Second year1 February 202731 January 2028
Third year1 February 2028Not applicable
Computing CPF contributions
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Example
Assuming your employee obtains his SPR status on 15 March 2026 and he receives OW and AW for March 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is required on the pro-rated wages from 15 to 31 March 2026.
For AW
• CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable while the employee was a foreigner i.e. before 15 March 2026.
• CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable on or after 15 March 2026.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Can I nominate a foreign person?
questions.text:
If you are nominating someone who is not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please provide the nominee’s full name, foreign identification number and mailing address in your nomination form so that the Board can contact him swiftly when distributing your CPF savings.
Please note that if you are nominating a foreigner or a Singapore Citizen / Permanent Resident residing overseas, there may be inheritance tax implications in the country of residence. You are advised to seek your own legal or tax advice in the country of residence before making your nomination.

questions.title: How often should I review or update my nomination?
questions.text: Members are encouraged to review their nomination annually or more regularly if experiencing key life milestones, such as marriage, childbirth, divorce, death of a nominee, or entering their golden years. Reviewing and updating CPF nominations allows their CPF savings to be distributed according to their latest bequeath intentions.

questions.title: I made my CPF nomination many years ago. Why can't I view it online?
questions.text:
CPF nominations made many years ago were typically handwritten on hardcopy forms. Such old nominations may contain illegible handwriting, and this makes accurate transcription of the details for online viewing challenging. As such, these old nomination details cannot be made available online.
You are encouraged to make a new CPF nomination. Once you make a new nomination, you will be able to view your latest nomination details online.

questions.title: How can I get a referral for subsidised care at public SOCs?
questions.text: A referral for subsidised care at public SOCs can be obtained from either CHAS clinics or polyclinics. Do note that you will need to be a PG/MG/CHAS cardholder to obtain subsidised SOC referrals from CHAS clinics.

questions.title: What course do I need to attend to be recognized by MOM as an industrial audiometric technician?
questions.text: You should attend the Perform Industrial Audiometric Screening course and obtain the certificate of completion (Statement of Attainment) or equivalent. Certification from former training providers such as Siemens, National Productivity Board and Singapore Polytechnic are also accepted.
topics: Workplace safety and health / Medical monitoring

questions.title: I cannot renew a Work Permit through WP Online due to Safety Orientation Courses (SOC) issues. What should I do?
questions.text:
Check the worker’s training record on the WSH training records eService.
If the record shows ‘Competent’, resubmit the eIssuance request through WP Online.
If the record shows ‘Not Yet Competent’, the worker must retake the course and assessment. For renewal, the SOC must be valid for at least one month from Date of Expiry.
If no record exists, contact your training provider to ensure they have uploaded the training record and verify that the worker’s details on the certificate match their Work Permit Card exactly.
For SOC courses, results will be auto transmitted to MOM upon completion of the assessments. The results will be reflected in the WSH training records eService within 8 hours after the upload.
For non-SOC courses (Supervisor and above), Training Provider is required to upload the course results to MOM within 5 working days of course completion. The results will be reflected in the WSH training records eService within 8 hours after the upload.
topics: Workplace safety and health / WSH Training (including Safety Orientation Courses linked to Work Permit applications)

questions.title: Can I take a vaccination if I am currently unwell, such as having the flu?
questions.text:
It is generally recommended to postpone vaccinations if you are experiencing moderate to severe illness, such as a high fever or significant flu symptoms. However, if your symptoms are mild, you may still be able to take the vaccination.
To ensure your safety, consult your doctor or healthcare provider for advice tailored to your specific health condition before proceeding with the vaccination.

questions.title: I’m allergic to the flu vaccine but received a push notification from the HealthHub app. Does this mean I can now take the vaccine?
questions.text: Receiving a push notification from the HealthHub app does not necessarily mean that you are now suitable to take the flu vaccine if you are allergic to it. The notification is a general reminder for flu vaccination. If you have a known allergy to the flu vaccine, consult your healthcare provider before proceeding. They can assess your medical history and advise if the vaccination is suitable for you or whether alternative flu vaccine options are available.

questions.title: When will I know if my proposal will be supported?
questions.text: Evaluation outcome letters will be sent out to operators who have submitted proposals by Oct 2026. Operators are expected to implement proposals from Nov 2026 onwards and complete them within a year. Final reports will need to be submitted by Jan 2028.

questions.title: How many proposals can I submit? Can I submit a proposal together with another operator as a consortium?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of proposals you may submit, though applicants are encouraged to put forward strong proposals. Each application should cover a single idea or project, and must be submitted by a single operator, consortium proposals are not accepted.

questions.title: If one or all of my nominees pass away before me, what will happen to their share of monies?
questions.text:
If your nominee passes on before you, his/her share will be given to the surviving nominee(s) in the same proportion you have specified.
For example, a CPF member made the following nomination:
Nominee A: 60%
Nominee B: 30%
Nominee C: 10%
Nominee A passed on and the CPF member did not make a new nomination. Nominee A's 60% share will be redistributed between the surviving nominees (i.e. Nominee B and Nominee C) in proportion to their original allocations. The distribution outcome will be as follows:
Nominee B will receive 75% (30% of 40%* = 75%)
Nominee C will receive 25% (10% of 40%* = 25%)
*40% is the total shares originally allocated to Nominee B and C.
If there are no surviving nominee(s), your nomination is considered revoked and your savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution under the intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property with a lease of less than 20 years?
questions.text: No. To use your CPF savings for property purchase, the property must have a remaining lease of more than 20 years. This requirement ensures the prudent use of your CPF savings and aligns with HDB loan eligibility criteria.

questions.title: Who is responsible for reimbursing my MediSave Account for hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text: Third parties with a contractual obligation (e.g. your employer or insurer) are required to reimburse your MediSave Account for your hospitalisation expenses.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my reimbursement if I have already submitted a claim to my insurer after using my MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses?
questions.text:
You can check your reimbursement status on cpf.gov.sg/healthcare.
Simply login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass, and go to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' to view the recent transactions. You can also click on 'View past 15 months' to see additional transactions.
For reimbursed claims, you will see the message "You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details". Click 'View details' to see the reimbursement details.

questions.title: Can an overseas insurance company disburse the approved reimbursement to my MediSave Account via telegraphic transfer, or is it only by cheque?
questions.text: Your insurer may submit reimbursements to MediSave and/or MediShield Life electronically via the MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service.

questions.title: How can I apply for reimbursements for my MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text:
If you have utilised your MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, and your employer or insurer has contractual obligations to reimburse you for your medical expenses, please approach them to find out how they can reimburse to your MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
Your employer or insurer may require you to provide the following supporting documents:
i. Finalised medical bill - showing the itemised charges and the source of payment (e.g. cash, MediSave, Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life).
ii. Healthcare payments and claims statement - showing the payment information including the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) used to identify the claim details for reimbursement purposes. The HRN is a 13-character alphanumeric registration number (e.g. 522016A02QL6E). You can retrieve this statement online from your Healthcare dashboard.
For claims that have been reimbursed, you will see the message 'You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details'. Click 'View details' to view the reimbursement details on the Healthcare payments and claims statement.
If you do not have Singpass, you can register for an account online.

questions.title: If I used cash, MediSave and MediShield Life for my medical bill, is there a specific order in which my employer or insurer should perform the reimbursement?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, your employer or insurer should reimburse you in the following order:
i. Cash reimbursement - For the amount you paid in cash.
ii. MediSave reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your payer's or your MediSave Account.
iii. MediShield Life reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life.
This order minimises your cash outlay and restores the balances in your MediSave Account.

questions.title: I am making a reimbursement claim from my employer or insurer for my medical bills. Is it compulsory to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement?
questions.text: CPF Board does not require any documents from your employer or insurer to process the reimbursement. You are not required to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement when making a reimbursement claim. If your employer or insurer requests a statement, they should accept a digital copy.

questions.title: When do I need to apply for reimbursement to my MediSave and/or MediShield Life from my third-party-payers for my healthcare expense?
questions.text:
Please submit your reimbursement request to your employer or insurer once your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claims have been processed and reflected in your Healthcare payments and claims statement. Your employer or insurer may need your Healthcare payments and claim statement to assess your request. Find out more on how to retrieve your Healthcare payments and claims statements and apply for reimbursement.
Please note that your Healthcare payments and claims statement will no longer be available for retrieval once it is older than 15 months.

questions.title: How do I apply to use Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay my outstanding CPF education loan?
questions.text:
You may log in to the Student Finance System (SFS) via the Ministry of Education (MOE) website using your Singpass and apply for the use of your Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay your outstanding CPF education loan.
Please note that your request will be submitted directly to MOE for processing.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: My employee has renounced his Singapore Citizenship/Singapore Permanent Resident status. Do I need to pay his CPF for the entire month?
questions.text:
If your employee has renounced his Singapore Citizen/Singapore Permanent Resident (SC/SPR) status, you would need to pay CPF contributions for him for the period when he is still a SC/SPR. CPF contributions are not required from the day your employee becomes a foreigner.
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Please ensure your employee informs you when he renounces his SC/SPR status.
Example
Assuming your employee renounces his SC/SPR status and becomes a foreigner on 10 January 2026 and he receives OW and AW for January 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is only required on the pro-rated wages for the period 1 to 9 January 2026.
For AW
CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable to the employee between 1 to 9 January 2026.
CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable on or after 10 January 2026.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: For any further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement, please write to us and we will assist you with your enquiries.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Are there any charges for the MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service?
questions.text: The MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service is provided free of charge.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: In what order should I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds if they have paid for medical expenses using cash, MediSave and MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, the reimbursement order should be as follows:
Amount paid in cash
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life
This order minimises your employees, platform workers or insureds' cash outlay, and preserves their MediSave for future use.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I was notified by the Medical Institution that my employee, platform worker or insured's medical bill was cancelled or amended. How can I make changes to the reimbursement I submitted earlier?
questions.text: If you need to amend the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement you previously submitted, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I need to submit a reimbursement to my employee, platform worker or insured's MediSave and/or MediShield Life. How do I go about doing it?
questions.text:
You can submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements to your employee, platform worker or insured quickly and easily via CPF's online reimbursement system, also known as the Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
Learn more about how to submit a reimbursement via the IR service.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life within a specific time period?
questions.text: We strongly encourage you to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds promptly. Timely reimbursement is particularly helpful if they need their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for further treatments.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Can I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds in cash for a medical bill paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text: You cannot reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds in cash if the medical bill was paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the utilised amount must be made directly to the employees, platform workers or insureds’ MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Apart from the Internet Reimbursement service, are there other ways to submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements?
questions.text:
To support our go green program and the Smart Nation initiative, we only accept reimbursements via our Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
If you encounter any difficulties while submitting reimbursements via this IR service, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: If my employees, platform workers or insureds have used their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, do I need to reimburse them?
questions.text: As an employer, platform operator or insurer, you are required to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life if you have a contractual obligation to cover their medical expenses.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: What happens if the amount of MediSave contributions the self-employed person has made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is lower than his MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
The self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave payable for income earned in the year will be computed after the SEP has declared his actual income in the following year.
If the SEP’s total Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution is lower than his MediSave payable for the latest year, he will be required to top up the shortfall.
Example:
Sam has made a total contribution of $2,100 via CAYE in 2023. The following year, Sam is informed that his MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $3,000. Sam will have to top-up the shortfall of $900.
This example is illustrated within the table below:
Estimated 2023 NTI
$21,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,100
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$30,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$3,000
Shortfall Sam has to top up
$900
(i.e. $3,000 - $2,100)
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What is CPF at Your Service?
questions.text:
CPF at Your Service is an initiative that brings CPF services directly to seniors in the community, instead of requiring them to visit CPF Service Centres.
Through partnerships with selected Active Ageing Centres across Singapore, CPF officers and volunteers will provide this personalised assistance at locations where seniors already gather and are familiar with. The initiative is part of CPF Board’s commitment to reaching seniors who may benefit from guidance on their CPF matters.
CPF at Your Service can help you with:
Checking your CPF retirement, housing and healthcare scheme status
Updating your contact details or registered bank account
Understanding your CPF top-up eligibility and how to make top-ups
Understanding your retirement withdrawal eligibility and the withdrawal process
To find out when CPF at Your Service will be at an Active Ageing Centre near you, please check for event announcements at your Active Ageing Centre.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: How do I know if my refund for PayNow QR, Apple Pay or Google Pay has been completed?
questions.text:
Refunds will be credited back to the original payment method used:
PayNow QR: refunded to the bank account linked to the PayNow transaction
Apple Pay / Google Pay: refunded to the underlying card linked to the digital wallet
A separate notification may not be sent when the refund is processed. We recommend checking your bank or card statement to confirm.
To check whether your refund has been completed, please refer to:
Your bank account statement or banking app transaction history (for PayNow QR refunds), or
Your credit or debit card statement linked to Apple Pay or Google Pay
Refund processing time may vary depending on your bank or card issuer.

questions.title: How to view your Debt Repayment Plan and DRS case details via the debtor's portal
questions.text:
The Insolvency Office E-Services lets you check your Debt Repayment Plan and Debt Repayment Scheme (DRS) case details online anytime.
Before you start
You will need:
● Your Singpass account
● Your DRS case reference number/NRIC number
● A computer or mobile device with internet access
Step-by-step instructions
Step 1: Go to the debtor's portal
Visit the portal at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/ipto/forms/io/io-home.form#drs
Step 2: Log in to your account
Click “Debtor’s Portal” and use your Singpass to access your account.
Step 3: At the dashboard, click on "Reports" on the left-hand panel of the dashboard
Step 4: View your details
You can now see:
● Payment schedule and amounts
● Case status and updates
What happens next
After viewing your details:
● Contact us at https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/ if you have questions about your case
● Check back regularly for updates on your case status
Need help?
If you cannot access the portal or view your details:
● Try clearing your browser cache or using a different browser
● Contact us via https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Visit: Ministry of Law Services Centre: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118 during office hours

questions.title: I missed My DRS Monthly Instalment Payment. What Should I Do?
questions.text:
If you missed your monthly instalment payment for your Debt Repayment Scheme (DRS), you need to act quickly to avoid being failed from the scheme.
Important: Missing payments may result in the issuance of a Certificate of Failure. .
What to do: Contact the Official Assignee immediately and make your payment as soon as possible.
Act immediately - within 24 hours
Time is critical. The sooner you contact the Official Assignee (OA) and make your payment, the better your chances of staying on DRS.
Don't wait - hoping the problem will go away will only make things worse.
Step 1: Contact the Official Assignee immediately
Call the OA as soon as possible:
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Best times to call: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday
What to say when you call:
1. Give your details: "My name is [Your Name], DRS Case Reference [Your Number]"
2. Explain the situation: "I missed my monthly payment due on [Date] because [Reason]"
3. Show you're taking action: "I want to make the payment and stay on DRS"
4. Ask for guidance: "What do I need to do to resolve this?"
Step 2: Explain why you missed the payment
Be honest about the reason:
Valid reasons include:
● Bank account issues, Temporary financial hardship
● Medical emergency, Loss in employment, Family crisis
● Technical problems with payment portal, did not receive payment reminder
Prepare supporting evidence if needed:
● Medical certificates, Termination letters, Bank statements showing account issues or any documents proving your inability to pay
Step 3: Make your missed payment immediately
Payment options:
Online payment (fastest)
5. Go to the MinLaw eServices portal: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/ecoll/
6. Select "Debt Repayment Scheme" → "DRS Payment by Debtor"
7. Enter your Case Reference or NRIC
8. Select "Monthly Instalment" (NOT Annual Fees)
9. Pay your missed payment amount: refer to your Debt Repayment Plan
10. Save your payment receipt - you'll need this as proof
Step 4: Confirm payment with the OA
After making payment:
11. Call the OA again at 1800 2255 529
12. Provide your payment details:
○ Transaction reference number
○ Payment date and time
○ Amount paid
13. Ask for confirmation that your payment has been received
14. Request written confirmation via email if possible
What happens next?
If you act quickly (within 1-2 days):
● OA may allow you to continue in DRS with a warning
● You may need to provide additional assurance of future payments
If you delay or miss multiple payments:
● You may be found unsuitable for DRS
● Your case may be failed from the scheme, if you have commenced on the plan
Preventing future missed payments
Set up reminders:
● Calendar alerts on your phone on the 30th day of each month
● Email reminders to yourself a few days before the due date
Plan ahead:
● Check your account balance a week before the due date
● Set aside money for DRS payments at the beginning of each month
● Contact OA early if you anticipate payment difficulties
What if you can't afford future payments?
If your financial situation has changed:
15. Contact the OA immediately - don't wait until you miss another payment
16. Explain your circumstances:
○ Loss of employment, Reduced income, medical expenses, family emergency
17. Provide supporting documents:
○ Latest pay slips, medical bills, termination letter, bank statements
Important: The OA may be able to help if you communicate early and honestly.
Important reminders
● Act within 24 hours - the sooner you contact the OA, the better
● Be honest about why you missed the payment
● Make the payment immediately
● Get confirmation that your payment has been received
● Set up systems to prevent future missed payments
● Communicate early if you anticipate future payment problems
Contact information
Official Assignee (IPTO):
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
● Office Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM
For more DRS information: Visit https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/debt-repayment-scheme/about-debt-repayment-scheme/

questions.title: What is a Creditors' Meeting in DRS?
questions.text:
A Creditors' Meeting is a meeting where you, your creditors (people whom you owe money to), and the Official Assignee (“OA”) discuss and finalize your Debt Repayment Plan. During the meeting, the OA conducts further assessment on your suitability for the DRS.
When it happens: After you are assessed as suitable for the DRS but before your Debt Repayment Plan starts (if applicable).
Purpose: To clarify any questions about your financial situation and agree on the specific terms of how you will pay back your debts.
Who attends the Creditors' Meeting?
Required attendees:
● You (the debtor) - attendance is compulsory
● Official Assignee (OA) - the case officer managing your case
● Your creditors - people or companies whom you owe money to
Optional attendees:
● Your lawyer
What happens during the meeting?
The Official Assignee will:
● Review your financial information and debt repayment proposal
● Ask questions about your income, expenses, and assets
● Explain the DRS process and rules
Your creditors may:
● Ask questions about your ability to pay
● Discuss the proposed repayment amount and timeline
● Raise concerns about your financial disclosure
You will need to:
● Answer questions about your financial situation honestly
● Explain any changes in your circumstances since your application
● Agree to the final repayment terms
Do you have to attend?
Yes, attendance is compulsory. You must attend the Creditors' Meeting unless you have prior written permission from the Official Assignee to be absent.
Valid reasons for absence:
● Medical emergency requiring hospitalization
● Overseas work commitment that cannot be rescheduled
● Family emergency (death, serious illness)
What happens if you don't attend:
● Without valid reason: You may be found unsuitable for the DRS
● Without paying the required fee: You may be found unsuitable for the DRS
● If found unsuitable: Your case will be referred back to the High Court for bankruptcy proceedings
How to prepare for the meeting
Before the meeting:
1. Pay the required fee: $250.00 review fee must be paid via eCollection before the meeting
2. Gather your documents:
○ Receipt of the $250.00 review fee paid
○ Updated debt statements, any new financial information
3. Review your repayment proposal: Make sure you understand and can afford the proposed monthly payments
4. Prepare to answer questions about:
○ Your current income and job situation
○ Your monthly expenses and living costs
○ Any assets you own
○ Changes since your DRS application
What to bring:
● Photo identification (NRIC), All requested documents
How to request permission to be absent
If you cannot attend due to a valid reason:
5. Contact the Official Assignee immediately at 1800 2255 529
6. Submit a written request explaining:
○ The reason you cannot attend
○ Supporting evidence (medical certificate, travel documents, etc.)
7. Submit your request at least 7 working days before the meeting
Contact details for requests:
● Phone: 1800 2255 529
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
What happens after the meeting
If the meeting goes well:
● Your Debt Repayment Plan is finalized
● You will be informed of the date required to pay your first instalment, first annual fee and to acknowledge the terms and condition and debt repayment plan by a specified date.
● Your DRS payments will start on the date specified in your plan
● The above is subject to the aggregate of your debts not exceeding the DRS threshold of $150,000 and no new claims from creditors.
If there are issues:
● meeting may be postponed, additional information may be requested, your case may be reviewed further
Important reminders
● Arrive on time: Arrive 15 minutes before your scheduled meeting time
● Be honest: Answer all questions truthfully - providing false information can disqualify you from DRS
● Ask questions: If you don't understand something, ask for clarification
Need help or have questions?
Contact the Official Assignee:
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
For more DRS information: Visit https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/debt-repayment-scheme/about-debt-repayment-scheme/

questions.title: How to Submit Documents to the Official Assignee (OA)
questions.text:
You may need to submit supporting documents to the Official Assignee (OA) as part of your Debt Repayment Scheme (DRS) case.
Important: The OA does NOT accept documents through the Online Enquiry form. You must use the debtor's portal instead.
Correct submission method: MinLaw eServices debtor's portal only
When do you need to submit documents?
You need to submit documents when the OA requests them for:
● DRS assessment, change in circumstances
● Income verification, expense documentation
● Case updates
Timeline: Submit documents within 7 days of the OA's request
Document requirements:
● Clear and readable - scan or photo must be sharp
● Complete pages - do not cut off any information
● Current - documents must be recent as specified by OA
● Original language - if not in English, please provide certified translation
Before you start
You will need:
● Digital copies of your documents (PDF, JPG, or PNG format)
● Internet access to use the online portal
File size limits: Maximum 5 MB per file
Supported file types: PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, DOC, DOCX
Step 1: Access the debtor's portal
1. Visit the MinLaw eServices debtor's portal: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/ipto/forms/io/io-home.form
2. Select “Debt Repayment Scheme”
3. Select "Debtor’s Portal”
Step 2: Log in to your account
1. Select "Log in with SingPass”
2. Scan the SingPass QR code
3. Complete 2FA authentication if required
4. Wait for the portal to load your case information
5. Check that your name and case details are correct
Step 3: Navigate to document submission
6. Look for "Supporting Documents" on the left-hand panel of your portal.
7. Click on the “Supporting Documents” option.
8. Review any specific instructions for your submission.
Step 4: Select document type
9. Choose the type of document you are submitting:
10. Select the specific document category from dropdown menu
11. Add a description of what you are submitting
Step 5: Upload your documents
12. Click "Choose File" or "Browse"
13. Select your document from your computer or phone
14. Check the file name - make sure it clearly describes the document
15. Repeat for additional documents if submitting multiple files
16. Review your uploads:
○ Check all files are attached
○ Check file names are clear
○ Check document types are correct
Step 6: Submit your documents
17. Review everything carefully:
○ All required documents are attached
○ Document types are correctly selected
○ Subject line and message are clear
○ Your contact details are current
18. Click "Submit" or "Send Documents"
19. Wait for confirmation - do not close the browser window
20. Save your submission reference number
Step 7: Confirm successful submission
21. Check for confirmation message on screen
22. Save or print the confirmation page
23. Note your submission reference number
24. Check your email for confirmation within 24 hours
What happens after you submit?
Confirmation: You will receive an email confirmation that your documents have been received
Review outcome: The OA will contact you if:
● Documents are unclear or incomplete
● Your case status has changed
Next steps: Wait for OA assessment, Attend scheduled meetings
If you have problems submitting documents
Common issues and solutions:
Problem
Solution
Cannot access portal
Check internet connection, try different browser, clear browser cache, contact eServices helpdesk
Login not working
Check NRIC/case number, ensure Singpass is working, reset password if needed
File won't upload
Check file size (max 5 MB), check file type is supported, try different file format
Portal shows error message
Take screenshot of error, try again later, contact IPTO with error details
No confirmation received
Check spam folder, wait 24 hours, contact IPTO with submission reference number
For document submission questions: Contact the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office (IPTO):
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/ (for questions only, NOT for document submission)
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
Important reminders
● Use the correct portal: Only submit documents through the debtor's portal, NOT the Online Enquiry form
● Submit on time: Late submissions may affect your DRS status
● Keep copies: Save copies of all documents that you have submitted
● Check file quality: Ensure documents are clear and readable
● Follow up: Contact IPTO if you don't receive an email confirmation within 24 hours
● Update contact details: Inform IPTO if your email or phone number changes
Alternative submission methods
If you cannot use the online portal:
● Submit in person during office hours at the following address 45 Maxwell Road, #06-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
Note: Debtors are encouraged to submit their documents online
Need help or have questions?
Contact the Official Assignee:
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/ (for questions only)
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
For more DRS information: Visit https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/debt-repayment-scheme/about-debt-repayment-scheme/

questions.title: How to Make Monthly Instalment Payments for DRS
questions.text:
You must make monthly instalment payments as part of your Debt Repayment Scheme (DRS). These payments help you pay back your debts over time.
Payment method: Online only through the MinLaw eServices portal
Important: You must pay on time every month. Late payments may result in failure from DRS.
Before you start
You will need:
● Your DRS Case Reference number OR your NRIC number
● A credit or debit card for payment
● Internet access to use the online payment portal
Your monthly payment amount: Please refer to the email that the OA has emailed you.
Payment due date: 30th day of each month
Step 1: Go to the payment website
1. Visit the MinLaw eServices portal: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/ecoll/
2. Read the terms and conditions carefully
3. Click the "Agree" button to continue
Step 2: Select your payment type
4. Look for "Debt Repayment Scheme" in the list of services
5. Click on "Debt Repayment Scheme"
6. Select "DRS Payment by Debtor" from the options
Step 3: Enter your details
7. Enter your identification:
○ Type in your DRS Case Reference number OR
○ Type in your NRIC number
8. Click "Proceed”
9. Check that your case details appear correctly
Step 4: Choose what to pay
10. Select "Monthly Instalment" from the payment options
11. Do NOT select "Annual Fees"
12. Check that the payment amount shows your correct monthly instalment: Amount: $X
13. Key in your name in the “Payer’s Name”
14. Click "Add to Cart"
15. Click “Checkout”
16. At the payment summary click “Proceed to pay”
17. Enter your email address at the “Payment Status Notification” field.
18. Select the preferred payment mode and click “pay”
Step 5: Make your payment
19. Choose your payment method:
○ Credit card (Visa, Mastercard)
○ Debit card
20. Enter your card details:
○ Cardholder name (exactly as shown on card)
○ Card number (16 digits)
○ Security code (CVV - 3 digits on back of card)
○ Expiry date (MM/YY)
○ Email address
21. Click "submit"
Step 6: Confirm your payment
22. Wait for the payment confirmation page to load
23. Save or print your receipt - you will need this as proof of payment
24. Write down your transaction reference number
25. Keep your receipt until your next payment is due
What happens after you pay
Processing time: Within 1-2 working days
Confirmation: You will receive an email confirmation within 24 hours
Receipt: Keep your payment receipt and transaction number for your records
If you have problems with payment
Common issues and solutions:
Problem
Solution
Card payment declined
Check card details are correct, ensure sufficient funds, contact your bank, try a different card
Cannot find your case
Check NRIC/case number, ensure you are placed on the DRS (not just applied), contact IPTO
Wrong payment amount showing
Do not proceed - contact IPTO immediately to verify correct amount
Website not working
Try different browser, clear browser cache, try again later, contact eServices helpdesk
Payment went through but no confirmation
Wait 24 hours for email, check spam folder, contact IPTO with transaction number
For DRS payment questions: Contact the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office (IPTO):
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
Important reminders
● Pay on time: Late payments can result in failure from DRS
● Pay the correct amount: Only pay your monthly instalment amount, not annual fees
● Keep receipts: Save all payment confirmations
● Check your email: Make sure you receive confirmation after each payment
● Plan ahead: Set up calendar reminders for your monthly due date
● Contact IPTO immediately if you cannot make a payment due to financial hardship
What if you miss a payment?
If you cannot make your monthly payment:
1. Contact IPTO immediately at 1800 2255 529
2. Explain your situation - temporary financial difficulty, loss of employment, medical emergency
3. Provide supporting documents if requested
4. Do not ignore the missed payment - this may result in failure from DRS
Possible options:
● Extension of payment deadline
Need help or have questions?
Contact the Official Assignee:
● Phone: 1800 2255 529 (Local) / +65 6225 5529 (Overseas)
● Online Enquiry: https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/enquiry/
● Office: 45 Maxwell Road, #07-11 The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118
For more DRS information: Visit https://io.mlaw.gov.sg/debt-repayment-scheme/about-debt-repayment-scheme/

questions.title: How to Pay the DRS Annual Fee

4. Look for "Debt Repayment Scheme" in the list of services

Step 3: Enter your details
7. Enter your identification:
○ Type in your DRS Case Reference number OR
○ Type in your NRIC number
8. Click "Proceed”
9. Check that your case details appear correctly
Step 4: Choose what to pay
10. Select "Annual Fees" from the payment options
11. Check that the fee amount shows as current fee: $300.00/$350.00
12. Enter “Payer’s Name”
13. Click "Add to Cart"
14. Click “Checkout”

16. Enter your email address in the Payment Status Notification section
Step 5: Make your payment
17. Choose your payment method:
○ Credit card (Visa, Mastercard)

18. Enter your card details:

21. Save or print your receipt - you will need this as proof of payment

23. Keep your receipt until your next payment is due
What happens after you pay
Processing time: Payment is processed within 1-2 working days

Receipt: Keep your payment receipt and transaction number for your records
If you have problems with payment
Common issues and solutions:
Payment Troubleshooting
Problem
Solution

Check card details, contact your bank, try different card
Cannot find your case
Check NRIC/case number, contact IPTO
Website not working
Try different browser, clear cache, try later
For DRS payment questions: Contact the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office (IPTO):
● Phone: 1800 2255 529

Important reminders
● Pay before the deadline: Late payment may result in failure from DRS
● Keep your receipt: You may need it as proof of payment
