Under the CDRA, a landlord may be required to put up a compliance bond if their tenant is a nuisance-maker. This is to ensure that the tenant complies with court orders.
For more information, you may wish to refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/apply-person-to-enter-compliance-bond
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / General Overview

questions.title: What is a "Compliance Bond"?
questions.text:
In the CDRT, a compliance bond is a financial guarantee given by a third party (usually a landlord) to guarantee that a person (the contravening party) will comply with a court order.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/apply-person-to-enter-compliance-bond
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / Court Outcomes

questions.title: Is doxing by a neighbour covered by the CDRT?
questions.text:
While surveillance and harassment can potentially form the basis for a CDRT claim, it may be more appropriate for you to proceed under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) as there are specific remedies thereunder which may be more suitable for cases involving doxing.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-neighbour-dispute-claim
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / General Overview

questions.title: Can I vary a court order issued by the CDRT?
questions.text:
As at 1 June 2026, there is no express provision that permits the CDRT to vary a court order that it has issued. However, Parliament has passed legislation to introduce powers permitting such variations and the relevant provisions will take effect in due course.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/community-neighbour-dispute-claims
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / Court Outcomes

questions.title: Are CDRT hearings open to the public?
questions.text:
No, hearings before the CDRT are typically held in private (in chambers) to protect the privacy of neighbours and reflect the sensitive nature of community disputes.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-neighbour-dispute-claim-hearing
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / General Overview

questions.title: Can the CDRT issue a Mandatory Treatment Order (MTO)?
questions.text:
As at 1 June 2026, the CDRT does not have powers to issue an MTO. However, Parliament has passed legislation to introduce such powers and the relevant provisions will take effect in due course.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-neighbour-dispute-claim
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What happens if I lose my case in the CDRT?
questions.text:
If you lose your case or if your case is dismissed, you will not be able to obtain the orders that you wished to seek from the CDRT in your claim. You may also be ordered to pay the other party's costs or disbursements. As such, you should ensure that your claim is well-supported by evidence before filing it.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-neighbour-dispute-claim
topics: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What is the Protection from Harassment Court (PHC)?
questions.text:
The PHC is a specialist court dedicated to dealing with harassment matters, whether online or offline. The PHC has oversight of all criminal and civil cases under the Protection from Harassment Act (“the POHA”).
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What types of behaviour are eligible for a claim in the PHC?
questions.text:
The PHC hears cases where a contravention under sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 15 of the POHA has occurred. These provisions encompass, but are not limited to, threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour, the use of physical violence, stalking, and the publication of false statements.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: Who is considered a “victim” under POHA?
questions.text:
A victim is any individual who has been the target of harassment. Additionally, for false statements, a "target person" (who can be an individual or an entity like a company) can apply for relief.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What are “Simplified Proceedings” under POHA?
questions.text:
Simplified proceedings were introduced to provide for a less expensive and simpler court user experience. Victims may seek relief by simply making an application online, using a simplified platform (the Community Justice and Tribunals System or “CJTS”), at a lower cost. It does not apply in certain prescribed scenarios, such as where there is a claim for damages exceeding $20,000.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/before-making-an-application-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What are “Standard Proceedings" under POHA?
questions.text:
If your matter is unsuitable for the simplified track, standard proceedings will apply. Standard proceedings usually require more specific legal documentation and are filed through the eLitigation system instead of through CJTS.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/before-making-an-application-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What is the monetary limit for simplified claims under POHA?
questions.text:
If you are seeking financial compensation (damages) through the simplified track, the maximum amount you can claim is $20,000. If your claim is higher, you must use the standard track.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/before-making-an-application-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: Is there a time limit to file a POHA claim?
questions.text:
Yes, for simplified proceedings, you must generally file your claim within 2 years from the date the harassment occurred. For standard proceedings, the limitation period may be longer, depending on the nature of the claim.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What is a Protection Order (PO) under POHA?
questions.text:
A Protection Order (PO) is a court order that prohibits the harasser from continuing their behaviour. It can include specific directions, such as prohibiting communications with the victim, or removing any publication causing harassment.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What is an Expedited Protection Order (EPO) under POHA?
questions.text:
An EPO is a temporary order that is granted when urgent intervention is needed due to continuing or imminent harm which would have a substantial adverse effect on the victim. For example, a victim can apply for an EPO if there is use of violence or risk of violence.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: How quickly can an Expedited Protection Order application be heard?
questions.text:
The PHC aims to hear EPO applications within 48 to 72 hours of filing, and in 24 hours if there is actual violence or risk of violence.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What is a False Statement Order (FSO)?
questions.text:
An FSO may be sought when the contravening party publishes a false statement of fact. The court can order the contravening party to stop publishing the statement or issue a correction.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What is a Stop Publication Order and can it apply to third parties?
questions.text:
A stop publication order may require a Respondent or any other individual or entity to stop publishing the relevant statement, and not to publish any substantially similar statement.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What is a Correction Order?
questions.text:
This order requires the harasser to publish a correction notice to the effect that the court has determined the relevant statement to be false and thus correct the false statement. The court usually specifies exactly where and how this notice must be displayed (e.g., on the same Facebook page).
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What are Mandatory Treatment Orders (MTO) issued by the PHC?
questions.text:
If a protection order is granted, the victim may also request that the court order the harasser to undergo psychiatric treatment if a mental condition contributed to the offending conduct. Before an MTO can be issued, the harasser must satisfy the requirements under the POHA and key parts of the assessment are conducted by a psychiatrist.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: How much does it cost to file a simplified claim in the PHC?
questions.text:
Filing a claim for a Protection Order usually costs $30. If you are also claiming damages, the fee increases based on the amount claimed (up to $60).
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: How do I file a POHA or PHC claim online?
questions.text:
Simplified proceedings are filed through the Community Justice and Tribunals System (CJTS). You log in with your Singpass, fill out the forms, and upload your evidence digitally.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: How do I file a POHA claim on the Standard Track?
questions.text:
Standard proceedings are filed through eLitigation. You can do so by visiting the eLitigation Service Bureau for assistance.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: Can I handle my own POHA case?
questions.text:
Yes, parties can be self-represented for POHA matters and conduct proceedings on their own.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/file-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What does it mean to "serve" the documents in a POHA matter?
questions.text:
After filing a Claim on CJTS, a claimant must give a copy of the court papers and all the documents filed in court to the other party (the Respondent) so they are aware of the legal action and of the allegations that the claimant intends to rely on in court proceedings. This is called "service of process." There are specified ways in which service is to be carried out under the relevant laws and rules.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What if I cannot find the harasser or am unable to find out the harasser’s registered address to carry out service?
questions.text:
If you do not have the proper address of the harasser to effect service, you may make an application to the Court stating that you are unable to obtain the proper address of the Respondent despite your best efforts, and seek the Court’s permission to instead effect service through the Respondent’s email address or other electronic means.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What should I do if I am served with a POHA Claim?
questions.text:
If you intend to file a response, you must do so within 14 days of being served with the claim. If you fail to attend proceedings, the court may grant an order against you in your absence.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-respond-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What is a Case Management Conference (CMC)?
questions.text:
A Case Management Conference (or “CMC”) is a pre-trial proceeding convened before a Deputy Registrar (who is also a judge). Parties will be guided and given the opportunity to discuss whether the case can be settled through mediation. If a case is not settled, parties will be given directions for documents to be filed and to prepare for trial.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-protection-from-harassment-hearing
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What would count as good or persuasive evidence in a POHA claim?
questions.text:
Screenshots of text messages, social media posts, audio recordings, CCTV footage, and police reports may be relevant and material.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: Is breaching an Expedited Protection Order or Protection Order a crime?
questions.text:
Yes. Breaching an EPO or PO are criminal offences. The offending party is liable for a fine or imprisonment, or both.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: How is "stalking" legally defined under the POHA?
questions.text:
Stalking under the POHA involves but is not limited to acts such as following the victim, loitering around the victim’s workplace or residence, sending unwanted items, or monitoring the victim’s communications.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What exactly is "doxing"?
questions.text:
Doxing is the publication of identity or identifying information (such as the name, address, and/or workplace) with the intent to cause harassment, alarm, or distress to the victim.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: Can I appeal if I lose the case?
questions.text:
An avenue of appeal exists. However, for simplified proceedings, you must first apply for leave (or permission) to appeal from the court within 7 days of the decision. If leave is granted, the appeal is heard by the General Division of the High Court.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/appeal-protection-from-harassment-decision-judge
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Appeals

questions.title: What is a "Default Order" issued by under POHA?
questions.text:
If the Respondent (the person you are suing) does not respond to your claim or attend the CMCs or trial, the court may make an order in your favour.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: How do I challenge a Default Order?
questions.text:
If a default order was made against you because you failed to attend the CMC or trial and if you wish to challenge this order, you must file an application to set aside the default order and explain why you were absent (including providing the necessary documentation to substantiate your reason(s)).
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: Can I change the terms of a Protection Order later?
questions.text:
Yes, if circumstances change (e.g., the harasser moves away or the behaviour resumes in a different way), you can make an application to vary, suspend or cancel the order and provide your supporting evidence.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/vary-suspend-cancel-protection-from-harassment-order
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What is a General Correction Order issued under the POHA?
questions.text:
This is an order directed at the publisher of a false statement requiring them to publish in Singapore a general correction notice that is visible to the public.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: Does the PHC handle disputes between neighbours?
questions.text:
Yes, if the neighbour's conduct amounts to a contravention of the POHA. If not, you may wish to instead consider whether the dispute with your neighbour would be more appropriately heard in the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal (CDRT).
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/before-making-an-application-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / General Overview

questions.title: What is a Disabling Order under the POHA?
questions.text:
A Disabling Order can be made to order an internet intermediary to disable user access to a false statement, if its platform or service has been used to publish a false statement of fact.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: Are PHC hearings private?
questions.text:
PHC CMCs and trials are generally held in chambers, which means the public and media are not allowed to attend them.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-protection-from-harassment-hearing
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What is a Targeted Correction Order issued under the POHA?
questions.text:
A Targeted Correction Order typically requires an internet intermediary (like an internet service provider or website host) to send a correction notice to every user who accessed the false statement.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: How do I prove that a statement is "False" if I am filing a claim for a false statement order or an interim false statement order?
questions.text:
You must show that the statement is one of "fact" (not just an opinion) and that it is objectively untrue or misleading (whether in whole or in part). You bear the burden of proving its falsity on a balance of probabilities.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: What is mediation, and are there fees or charges for mediation?
questions.text:
Often, the PHC will refer parties to mediation to settle their dispute. If done within the State Courts' framework for POHA matters, mediation is generally included as part of the process and there are no additional charges.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-protection-from-harassment-hearing
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: Can the Judge or Tribunal Magistrate refer a case to the Police?
questions.text:
A judge presiding over the matter in the PHC does not “send” cases to the police. However, if the judge is satisfied during a hearing for an application for an EPO that criminal investigation is warranted, the judge may refer the matter to the police for investigation but does not determine whether prosecution ensues. Subsequent action under the criminal process, if any, is separate and distinct from the civil proceedings initiated by the claimant in the PHC.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Court Outcomes

questions.title: What if the harasser is not in Singapore?
questions.text:
The POHA has "extraterritorial" reach in certain circumstances. Generally, the court has extra-territorial jurisdiction if the victim was in Singapore at the time of the harassment and the harasser knew or had reason to believe that the victim was in Singapore, or if the harasser was in Singapore at the time of the harassment even if the victim was overseas.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/cases-eligible-protection-from-harassment
topics: The Protection from Harassment Court / Filing Process

questions.title: How do I check my Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) balance if I wish to repay my education loan using my PSEA funds?
questions.text:
You may log in to the Ministry of Education’s Student Finance System (SFS) using your Singpass to check your account balance.
For more information on how to check the outstanding loan amount repayable under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, please refer to this FAQ.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What are the CPF contribution rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents?
questions.text:
For more details on the CPF contribution rates, see rates for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents.
You can use our CPF Contribution Calculator to calculate the CPF contributions applicable to your employees.
For past rates, see past CPF contribution and allocation rates.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: What are the criteria I must meet before I can file a claim at the Small Claims Tribunal ("SCT")?
Are there any prerequisite steps I need to complete before I file an SCT Claim?
questions.text:
Yes, it is compulsory that you first take a pre-filing assessment to determine your eligibility to file an SCT Claim. The pre-filing assessment is available on https://cjts.judiciary.gov.sg/
It is also strongly recommended that you understand the possible orders which the Tribunal may make, of which the full details can be found at this link: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/understand-outcomes-small-claim

questions.title: Where do I find the Memorandum of Consent form to fill in?
questions.text: You can find the sample form for a Memorandum of Consent under the "Claim Limit" portion of the "Key Facts" section in this link: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-small-claim

questions.title: What are the fees involved with filing or responding to an SCT Claim?
questions.text: The full list of fees can be found at this link: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-small-claim#fees

questions.title: What are the documents which I will need before I am able to file an SCT Claim?
questions.text:
You will need to prepare for upload the following:
Supporting documents for your claim. Examples include invoices, receipts, contracts, tenancy agreements, stamp duty certificates, photographs, emails or messages.
If your claim amount exceeds $20,000 but does not exceed $30,000, you will need to upload a Memorandum of Consent. This must be signed by both you and the respondent.
In addition, if you are claiming as a business entity, you will need to prepare for upload the following:
A Letter of Authorisation on your entity's letterhead for your authorised representative in relation to every court attendance.
Your company's ACRA business profile obtained within 1 month of filing (Purchase the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) business profile online on ACRA’s website.)
Additional items you need to upload if the respondent is a business entity:
Respondent's ACRA business profile obtained within 1 month of filing. You may purchase the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) business profile online on ACRA’s website.
Alternatively, you may enquire with any ACRA-accredited service providers)

questions.title: How do I file my SCT Claim?
questions.text:
Log in to Community Justice Tribunals System ("CJTS"). Under the Online Applications tab, select Claim Form.
Follow the instructions to fill in the required information and pay the filing fees. Your application will only be processed after you have paid.
After you have paid, you will need to:
Choose a consultation date and time.
Save and print a copy of the claim and Notice of Consultation to serve on the respondent.
Please refer to the SCT User Guide on CJTS if you require further information.

questions.title: What must I do after I file my SCT Claim?
questions.text:
You must serve the Notice of Consultation and Claim form on the Respondent within 7 days, and file a Declaration of Service with proof of service on CJTS.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-small-claim

questions.title: What does "Service" of a claim or document mean?
questions.text:
Service means either handing delivery the document that is to be served personally to the person to be served, or sending that document to that person by registered post to their last known residential address, registered address or, for businesses, their ACRA registered address.
If the person to be served is a party to the proceedings, and has been notified of their right to access CJTS, the submission of documents through CJTS also constitutes service. The SCT may, in any particular case, order that a document be served on a person by any other means.

questions.title: When must I serve the Notice of Consultation on the Respondent by?
questions.text: You must serve the Notice of Consultation on the Respondent within 7 days after you have filed the SCT Claim.

questions.title: What must I do after serving the Notice of Consultation on the Respondent?
questions.text:
You must file a Declaration of Service on CJTS before the first consultation. To do so, login to CJTS.
Under the Online Applications tab, select Declaration Of Service and follow the instructions.

questions.title: What do I need to do to prepare for my hearing?
questions.text:
You should do the following:
Prepare the explanation for your case
You should be prepared to explain your case to the SCT. If your claim or defence consists of smaller parts, you have to explain every individual part in detail.
Example: You should be able to explain every invoice that makes up your claim or the different defects raised in a renovation case.
Submit all your supporting evidence
You should submit all the evidence you want the SCT to consider.
If the evidence is in the form of a document, you should upload it on CJTS. Where the words in any document are not in English, a certified translation of the words into English must be provided.
If the evidence is an audio or video recording, you should copy it onto 2 CDs. Submit 1 CD to the State Courts Service Hub (State Courts, Level 2) and serve 1 CD on the other party. You can do so in advance or during the first consultation.
You should also prepare a transcript of the important part(s) of the audio or video recordings to state the relevant fact (ie, the action that is seen, the exact words that are used, the type(s) of sound(s) that are heard).
Where the words that are used in the audio or video recording are not in English, a certified translation of the words into English must be provided. The transcript must be uploaded into CJTS.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-small-claims-hearing

questions.title: Am I allowed to call witnesses at my hearing?
questions.text:
Yes, parties are allowed to call witnesses at an SCT hearing. However, parties will first need to notify the registrar of the witnesses they intend to call at the Consultation, and again to the Tribunal Magistrate at the SCT Hearing. The Tribunal Magistrate has discretion over which witnesses can appear to testify.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-small-claims-hearing

questions.title: What if my witness does not want to appear in Court?
questions.text:
If your witnesses are reluctant to attend court, you may file a Summons to Witness via CJTS to compel them to attend.
The application can be submitted only if the case has been fixed for Hearing before the Tribunal Magistrate and the hearing date has been fixed. Further, the application must be submitted at least 3 days before the hearing date. This application is subject to the SCT’s approval.
Please refer to the SCT User Guide on CJTS if you require further information.

questions.title: My witness is not fluent in English. Do the Courts provide interpreters?
questions.text:
Yes, the Courts provide interpretation services for Mandarin, Hokkien, other local Chinese dialects, Malay and Tamil. Indicate your preferred language via CJTS or during the Consultation.
For any other languages, parties are required to arrange for their own interpreter at their own cost.

questions.title: What do I need to bring for my SCT hearing?
questions.text:
You will need to bring the following documents to Court:
Identification documents. This includes your:
NRIC or passport, and employment pass (if applicable).
Supporting documents.
Bring the originals for all documents uploaded on CJTS. Examples include contracts, invoices and stamp duty certificates. If there are documents you have not uploaded on CJTS, prepare at least 3 copies of the documents so they can be given to the other party and the SCT.
Translation of documents
All documents that are not in English should be accompanied by English translations.
(If you are the claimant) Declaration of Service
If you have filed a Claim, ensure you have uploaded the Declaration of Service on CJTS and bring a copy to court. This shows that you have brought the Claim to the attention of the other party.
(If you are representing a corporate entity) Authority
Ensure that you are allowed to represent the party you are representing, and have full authority to make decisions on their behalf. Check that you have uploaded the Letter of Authorisation on CJTS and bring the original copy to court.

questions.title: Can another person/ party accompany me to SCT proceedings?
questions.text:
Yes, parties may be accompanied by a family member, friend or volunteer under the Community Courts and Tribunals (CCT) Friend Scheme to provide administrative or emotional support during court proceedings. This request is subject to the SCT's approval.
You should note that a CCT Friend cannot act as your lawyer or legal representative, provide you with any legal advice on the legal merits of the case, advise you on how to present your case or communicate with you during the proceedings in a disruptive way.
In addition, a CCT Friend cannot be someone who is an advocate, solicitor or a legally qualified person from any jurisdiction, is or may be a witness in the proceedings, or has a direct or indirect interest in the outcome of a claim in the dispute.
Information on applying for a CCT Friend can be found here: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/legal-help-support/cct-friend-scheme

questions.title: Where do I go on the day of my SCT consultation/hearing?
questions.text:
Please proceed to Level 3 of the State Courts. Take a queue number for Consultation from the queue machine and wait in the waiting area. When your queue number is called, proceed to the registrar’s chambers.
Some consultations/hearings may be via remote/virtual means. Please refer to the relevant notices that would have been provided to you ahead of the consultation/hearing date.

questions.title: What are the possible outcomes of the Consultation?
questions.text:
The Consultation is a court proceeding in which a registrar will facilitate a discussion between both parties. The aim is to resolve the dispute without moving on to a Hearing.
If parties reach a settlement during the Consultation, the registrar may record a consent order to reflect their agreement.
Parties will receive a copy of the consent order from the registrar or online through CJTS, or both.
If a settlement is not reached, the registrar will give further directions for the case. The registrar may:
Arrange for a hearing before a tribunal magistrate. This can occur within 24 hours of the date of the consultation.
Arrange for further consultations.
Direct the parties to seek mediation.
Discontinue the claim, if it does not fall within what the SCT can hear.
(If a party is absent) Issue a default order against the party.
(If the claimant is absent) Dismiss the claim.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/at-small-claims-consultation

questions.title: I have received a Notice of Consultation. What do I need to do now?
questions.text:
If someone has commenced a Claim against you in the SCT, you are the Respondent. The person who filed the claim is the Claimant.
After you receive a Notice of Consultation, take note of the date, time and venue of the Consultation on the notice. You must attend this Consultation, where a registrar will attempt to resolve the dispute.
If the matter cannot be settled, the claim may proceed to a Hearing before a Tribunal Magistrate.
If you do not turn up, the SCT can still make an order against you, such as a default Order.
Information on what you should prepare before attending a Consultation can be found here: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/before-going-to-court-small-claim
In addition, the Notice of Consultation will contain the Claim number and a one-time reference number. You should use the Claim number and one-time reference number to access the case filed against you on CJTS. Please refer to the SCT User Guide on CJTS if you require further information.

questions.title: What are my possible options in response to the Claim?
questions.text:
You can respond to the Claim in one of the following ways:
Admit the Claim: Admitting to a Claim against you means that you agree with it and do not dispute it. In such cases, you should log in to CJTS, choose the appropriate SCT Claim number and select a checkbox to admit the Claim. You will not need to attend the Consultation or the Hearing.
However, you must attend the Consultation and make your request with supporting documents if you wish to do any of the following:
(a) Admit only part of the claim and dispute the rest.
(b) Admit the full claim but pay in instalments.
Dispute the Claim: Disputing the Claim means you do not agree with it. Even if you dispute a Claim, you must attend the Consultation, otherwise, the court may make a default Order in your absence.
File a Counterclaim: If you also have an eligible claim against the claimant, you may file a counterclaim. The requirements of filing a counterclaim are the same as filing a claim.
Further information on responding to a Claim can be found here: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-respond-small-claim

questions.title: What if I am absent for my Consultation or Hearing?
questions.text:
If you are absent from a Consultation or Hearing, a default Order may be made against you.
If you are the Claimant, your claim may be dismissed.
If you are the Respondent, an Order may be made in the Claimant's favour. You may apply to set aside the default Order within 1 month from the date the Order was made.

questions.title: What is a default Order?
questions.text:
There are two types of default Orders which may be made against you if you were absent for a Consultation or Hearing at the SCT:
If you are the Claimant, your claim may be dismissed.
If you are the Respondent, an Order may be made in the Claimant's favour.
You may apply to set aside the default Order within 1 month from the date the Order was made.
For more information, you may refer to https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/set-aside-small-claims-order

questions.title: What if I am not satisfied with the Order made by the registrar at the Consultation or the Magistrate at the Hearing?
questions.text:
Orders by the SCT are final and binding. Parties may appeal against a decision by the SCT under specific circumstances.
Information on when you can appeal can be found at this link: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/appeal-small-claims-order

questions.title: What if a party does not comply with the Order made against him?
questions.text:
You may apply to execute or enforce an Order by the SCT if you are the Claimant or Counterclaimant, and the other party does not comply with the Order that was made in your favour.
Orders issued by the SCT can be executed or enforced in the same way as a District Court Order, and you may start execution or enforcement proceedings against them in the civil courts.
Information can be found here: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/small-claims/execute-enforce-a-small-claims-order

questions.title: Are there any other forms of resolving the dispute other than attending Consultations and Hearings?
questions.text:
Yes, parties can try to settle your dispute.
Parties may try to settle a dispute through participating in have the option of e-Mediation and e-Negotiation on CJTS.
If you reach an agreement with the other party as a result of e-Mediation or e-Negotiation, either party may apply for a consent Order to record the agreed terms, or the Claimant may withdraw the Claim.
If you do not reach an agreement with the other party, both parties will have to attend the next scheduled Consultation or Hearing.
More information can be found here: https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/alternatives-to-trial/enegotiation-emediation

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I am on an overseas-based contract and working in Singapore temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable if you are on an overseas-based contract and working in Singapore on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely in Singapore temporarily for personal reasons.
Please note that while your employer is still obligated to make CPF contributions for non-temporary stints in Singapore, enforcement may be limited where your employer is based overseas with no presence in Singapore and is not registered with ACRA. In such cases, CPFB may have limited ability to assist with your claims.
If you and your employer are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable if I am on a Singapore-based contract and working overseas temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions remain payable if you are on a Singapore-based contract and working overseas on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely overseas temporarily for personal reasons.
If you and your employer are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: What happens when I make a voluntary housing refund if I am 55 years old or older?
questions.text:
The refunded amount will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This transfer will help boost your retirement savings and provide you with a higher monthly payout when you reach age 65.
Any refunds that exceed your FRS in your RA will remain in your Ordinary Account (OA), which you can withdraw anytime. You can check the amount you can withdraw on your Retirement dashboard.
Example
Note: The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) depends on the year you turn 55 and may differ from the amount shown in this example. The figures below are for illustration only.
Assumptions:
1. You turned 55 years old in 2023
2. Your Full Retirement Sum is $198,800
3. You have received less than $30,000 in housing grants
Current RA balance$98,800
Current OA balance$100,000
Principal amount withdrawn for the property and the accrued interest (P+I)$500,000
If you make a voluntary housing refund of $200,000:
New RA balance: $198,800
Part of the refund $100,000 is used to top up your RA to meet your FRS.
New OA balance: $200,000
The remaining refund of $100,000 remains in the OA after topping up your RA to meet the FRS. The balance in the OA can continue to be used for housing payments.
Revised P+I: $300,000
The voluntary housing refund of $200,000 is used to reduce the P+I.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: How much should I refund to my CPF account if I have a Court order granted before 1 January 2013 directing a sale, transfer or disposal of my property?
questions.text:
If you have a Court Order granted before 1 January 2013, the amount to be refunded depends on your age at the time of sale, transfer or disposal of your property.
If you are below 55:
You must refund the CPF principal amount withdrawn and the accrued interest when you sell, transfer, or dispose of your property.
If your selling price (including option monies) cannot fully cover both the outstanding housing loan and the required CPF refund, you do not need to top up the shortfall in cash, provided the property is sold at market value. However, any option monies received in cash from your buyer must be refunded to both you and your co-owner's CPF accounts before the transaction can be completed.
If you are 55 and above:
Please write to us directly to determine the specific amount you need to refund upon sale, transfer, or disposal of your property.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: I did not use CPF savings for the matrimonial property but pledged the property to set aside my retirement sum. Can the Court order a transfer of this property to my ex-spouse
questions.text: Yes, the Court can still order the transfer of the property to your ex-spouse upon the refund of your pledged amount to your CPF account. The Court may also order for the transfer with a partial refund or without a refund. For such orders, upon the subsequent disposal of the property by your ex-spouse, the unrefunded pledged amount will have to be refunded to your ex-spouse’s CPF account (since it was not earlier refunded to your CPF account).
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: The courts ordered my ex-spouse and me to make our CPF refunds from our respective shares of sale proceeds. My share is insufficient to make the full refund. Can I waive the shortfall in refund?
questions.text:
No, full requisite CPF refunds must be made in accordance with CPF legislation upon the sale of the property in a divorce. If your (or your ex-spouse’s) respective share of sale proceeds are not enough to cover the required refunds to your CPF account, you will need to make up the shortfall in cash.
If you and your ex-spouse are unable to proceed with the sale of the property, please seek legal advice on how your proprietary share in the matrimonial asset can be satisfied.
topics: Other Schemes / Division of CPF-related assets in a divorce

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee on an overseas-based contract who is working in Singapore temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable for an employee on an overseas-based contract who is working in Singapore on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely in Singapore temporarily for personal reasons.
If you are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable for my employee on a Singapore-based contract who is working overseas temporarily?
questions.text:
CPF contributions remain payable for an employee on a Singapore-based contract who is working overseas on a temporary basis. Examples of temporary work arrangements include attending meetings, conferences, or training, or working remotely overseas temporarily for personal reasons.
If you are unsure of your CPF obligations, you may write to us with the relevant facts of your case for assessment.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Who should receive CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I use the same CPF Submission Number (CSN) to make both mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
No. A separate CPF Submission Number (CSN) is required for voluntary contributions (VC) - the CSN for mandatory contributions should not be used for this purpose.
To make VC to your employee's three CPF accounts, use your existing CSN with the payment code "VCT" (eg. 123456789-VCT-01). To make Additional MediSave Contributions Scheme (AMCS) contributions to your employee's MediSave Account, use your existing CSN with the payment code "AMS" (eg. 123456789-AMS-01).
Submission and payment of VC for your employees can be done the same way as mandatory CPF contributions via CPF EZPay. If you do not have a CSN with the "VCT" or "AMS" payment code, you may apply for one.
topics: Employer - Making Voluntary CPF Contributions / Voluntary contributions

questions.title: Why do I need to fill in the policy number and claim number of my employee, platform worker or insured in the E-File Excel for MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: The policy number and claim number fields were added based on requests from companies to help track their MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement submissions and match them with their records. These fields are optional and not compulsory.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Will I be notified about the status of my Direct Debit Authorisation application?
questions.text: You will be notified once the bank has approved your Direct Debit Authorisation (DDA) application, which generally takes four to six weeks. Once your DDA is approved, you can begin submitting reimbursements online.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I realised that I submitted the same reimbursement multiple times via E-File. What should I do?
questions.text:
If you submit duplicate reimbursements on the same day before 5:30pm, the most recent submission will override the previous one, and only the latest file will be processed.
If you have submitted duplicate reimbursements on different days, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: My reimbursement submission via E-File is unsuccessful, and I received a rejection reason. How should I correct my submission?
questions.text: Please refer to the common rejected reasons and their corresponding corrective actions before resubmitting.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I submitted reimbursements via E-File today, but realised there was a mistake in my submission after submitting the Excel file. What should I do?
questions.text:
You can override your previous submission by resubmitting the corrected file before 5:30pm on the same day.
For further clarification, please write to us.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I noticed that I need to fill in the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) for submitting reimbursement via E-File. How do I obtain the HRN?
questions.text:
The Hospital Registration Number (HRN) can be found in the following documents:
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s final medical bill
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement
Your employee, platform worker or insured’s MediSave Transaction Statement
Please refer to this guide for more information on where to find the HRN.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to attach the employee, platform worker or insured's hardcopy healthcare payments and claims statement for submitting MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement?
questions.text:
CPF Board does not require any documents from employers, platform operators or insurers to process the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement.
You should not request a hardcopy Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured. Employers, platform operators or insurers should accept a digital copy of the Healthcare Payments and Claims Statement from your employee, platform worker or insured if required.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Who are considered as immediate family members under the Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA)?
questions.text:
Ø Immediate family members are the child’s grandparents, or any other siblings below 21 years old who meet the following criteria:
(1) Live at the same address as the applicant,
(2) Not working, or do not have any source of income
(3) Singaporean, PR or Foreigners with valid passes (e.g. LTVP, LTVP+, Student Pass, Employment Pass, Dependent Pass, Work Permit, other passes of duration more than or equal to 2 years, etc.).

questions.title: How do I apply for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) coverage?
questions.text:
The process to apply for coverage under Home Protection Scheme (HPS) is as follows. Your application will be subject to the Board's approval and you being in good health.
New Flat Owners
Type of Housing LoanHow to Apply
HDB LoanYou will be prompted to apply for an HPS cover when applying to use your CPF savings for the new flat purchase via HDB. You do not need to submit your HPS application form via CPFB.
Bank LoanYou may apply for an HPS cover before applying to use your CPF savings for monthly housing instalments via CPFB.
Existing Flat Owners
Type of Housing LoanHow to Apply
HDB LoanYou will be prompted to apply for an HPS cover when applying to use your CPF savings for monthly housing instalments via HDB. You do not need to submit your HPS application form via CPFB.
If you are not applying to use your CPF savings for monthly housing instalment, you may apply for an HPS cover.
Bank LoanIf you are applying to use your CPF savings for your monthly housing instalments, or wish to be covered under HPS, you may apply for an HPS cover.
If you have a previous HPS cover that had lapsed recently, you may apply to reinstate your cover.
When did your HPS cover lapse or end*?Next steps
Ended 6 months or lessApply to reinstate your HPS cover online
Ended more than 6 months but less than or equal to 1 year ago
Apply to reinstate your HPS cover online with supporting reason and health declaration.
Your eligibility to reinstate your previous HPS cover is subject to approval.
Ended more than 1 year ago
Apply for a new HPS cover with health declaration.
Your eligibility for the new HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health.
*You may check your HPS cover end date from the hardcopy lapse letter (Ref: HPS/Lapse) sent to you.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Will the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) payouts be made directly to persons with disabilities?
questions.text:
If the person with disabilities is 18 years old or above, and is of sound mind at point of disbursement, the disbursement will be made to the person with disabilities via his/her bank account.
If the person with disabilities is below 18 years old, the disbursement will be made to the legal guardian or the court-appointed deputy (if he has one), when the deputy or legal guardian applies to the Board on behalf of the person with disabilities.
If the person with disabilities is 18 years old or above and lacks mental capacity:
If he made a valid Lasting Power of Attorney to appoint a donee, CPF Board would make payment to the donee when he steps forward to apply on behalf of the person with disabilities.
If he had not made a valid Lasting Power of Attorney, a third party may apply to the court to be appointed as the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nominee's deputy, and the Board will make payment to the court-appointed deputy when he applies to the Board on behalf of the person with disabilities.

questions.title: How to report a scam?
questions.text:
If you have been scammed, or wish to provide information about a scam, you may lodge an online report via the following link: http://www.police.gov.sg/E-Services if you have a SingPass account.
Alternatively, you may do so at any Neighbourhood Police Centre (NPC) (open 24 hours), or at any Neighbourhood Police Post (NPP) (open from 12.00pm to 10.00pm). The locations of our NPCs and NPPs can be found at https://www.police.gov.sg/contact-us

questions.title: How to report a sham marriage?
questions.text: You may report it to the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority via the following link: https://www.ica.gov.sg/feedbackform

questions.title: How can I join the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority?
questions.text: Thank you for your interest in joining the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA). You may wish visit the Careers@Gov Portal to find out more about positions available in ICA and apply online via https://www.careers.gov.sg.

questions.title: Where is the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority located?
questions.text:
The Immigration & Checkpoints Authority is located at:
ICA Services Centre
2 Crawford Street
Singapore 207218

questions.title: Where can I find the press releases by MHA?
questions.text: You can visit the following url - Newsroom | Ministry of Home Affairs for press releases issued by MHA

questions.title: What criminal offences will be deemed serious enough for the Government to revoke the immigration status of an offender?
questions.text:
Foreigners, including Permanent Residents (PRs), who break our laws or engage in undesirable conduct may have their passes or permits cancelled, and be prohibited from re-entry into Singapore. PRs who have been convicted of an offence will have their PR status reviewed by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority.
Please refer to the following link for more information:
https://www.mha.gov.sg/media-room/newsroom/situations-where-permanent-residency-or-work-passes-are-revoked-when-a-criminal-offence-is-committed-in-singapore/

questions.title: How can foreign spouses of Singaporeans obtain Permanent Residency (PR) or Singapore Citizenship (SC)?
questions.text:
Foreign spouses of Singapore Citizens (SCs) are considered more favourably for Permanent Residency (PR) or citizenship compared to those without family ties to Singaporeans.
All PR and citizenship applications from foreign spouses are evaluated holistically on a range of criteria to ensure that the SC sponsor can support the family and that the marriage is stable. For example, we take into consideration the length of marriage and whether the couple has any SC children.
Eligible foreign spouses who do not qualify for PR may be granted a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) or LTVP-Plus (LTVP+) which allows them to remain in Singapore with their families. The LTVP+ was introduced in 2012 to provide foreign spouses of SCs greater certainty of stay. Compared to ordinary LTVPs, they provide a longer period of residency and additional benefits such as subsidies for inpatient services in public hospitals.
Foreign spouses on LTVP or LTVP+ can also obtain a Letter of Consent or Pre-Approved Letter of Consent to work.

questions.title: I applied for financial assistance at the Social Service Office (SSO), but my application was rejected. How do I appeal?
questions.text: You may approach your officer directly, preparing any relevant supporting documents (e.g. updated payslips, medical certificates).

questions.title: Is Long-Term Assistance (LTA) a permanent scheme, or is it only provided for a limited period?
questions.text: ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA) provides long-term support to those permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, and have inadequate family support or savings to rely on for daily needs. Eligibility and duration of support are subject to periodic review based on the individual's circumstances.

questions.title: Where can I find My Legacy vault?
questions.text: My Legacy vault has been renamed to a dashboard. To access your dashboard, you’ll have to log in to MyLegacy@LifeSG with Singpass.

questions.title: Why is My Legacy discontinuing personal information, funeral plan and will record storage?
questions.text: Information entered and maintained by users can change over time, and users may also keep the same or related information elsewhere. This means My Legacy can become another place that users need to remember to keep updated. We are therefore moving away from storing certain user-entered information, and towards helping users access relevant information from appropriate sources where possible.

questions.title: What data from My Legacy will be deleted?
questions.text: On 4 January 2027, all personal information, funeral plans, and will records stored in My Legacy will be permanently deleted. These records will no longer be accessible to you or any Trusted Persons you have shared them with. Data from other services, such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney, will be unaffected.

questions.title: Will my Trusted Persons still have access to my information?
questions.text: After 4 January 2027, your Trusted Persons will no longer be able to access any personal information, funeral plans, or will records you have shared with them. They will still have access to other information shared with them, such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney. We recommend letting your Trusted Persons know about these changes so they can make alternative arrangements.

questions.title: How can I save my information before it gets deleted?
questions.text: A summary document consolidating your inputs is generated for each section – personal information, will, and funeral plan. Log in to MyLegacy@LifeSG and go to each section within your dashboard to download the respective documents. Please do this before 4 January 2027.

questions.title: Why am I unable to download a summary of my information?
questions.text: If you do not see the option to download a summary in a particular section, it means you do not have any existing information stored in My Legacy for that section. However, if you recall having information there and suspect that this is a technical error, please contact us for assistance.

questions.title: Can I edit my information before I download a summary?
questions.text: No, editing is no longer available. Please download your summary document and update it separately as needed.

questions.title: I previously uploaded supporting documents with my details but they are not in the summary document. Where can I find them?
questions.text: The summary document indicates whether you have supporting documents, but does not include the documents themselves. You can download your supporting documents separately from the individual sections within your dashboard.

questions.title: What should I do with my will record after downloading it?
questions.text: You may wish to deposit your will with the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) Wills Registry for secure storage (fees apply). My Legacy is also working towards retrieving will information directly from the SAL Wills Registry in future, so that your details are always up to date.

questions.title: I am a Trusted Person for someone else. What do I need to do?
questions.text: After 4 January 2027, you will no longer have access to any personal information, funeral plans, or will records that were shared with you through My Legacy. We recommend speaking with the person who shared their information with you to ensure you stay updated through other means.

questions.title: Will My Legacy’s dashboard still be useful after these changes?
questions.text: Yes. Your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney will continue to be accessible through your dashboard, giving you a single, convenient place to view your key legacy plans. My Legacy will also continue to explore new services and improvements.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Trusted Contact appointment request via your Activities page using your Singpass.
You may also view your appointed Trusted Contacts at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Only Trusted Contacts who have accepted your appointment request will be listed under “Your Trusted Contacts”.

questions.title: How does diversification help to limit my risk in investing?
questions.text:
Diversification, or spreading your assets among several investments, helps you smooth out potential ups and downs of your investment returns. Even if one investment does poorly, the others may do better, thereby potentially improving your overall return.
You can diversify your investments at two distinct levels by spreading your investments among:
different asset classes - cash equivalents (e.g., fixed deposits),bonds and stocks and/or
different markets - geographic regions, foreign countries, foreign currencies, industries and companies.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is the Skills Development Levy (SDL) and who is it for?
questions.text:
The Skills Development Levy (SDL) is a compulsory levy for employees working in Singapore to fund workforce upgrading programme.
You must pay SDL for:
All employees working in Singapore, including permanent, part-time, casual and temporary staff
Foreign employees on work permits and employment pass holders
You do not pay SDL for employees working overseas.
For more information on SDL, please visit this webpage.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / Skills Development Levy (SDL)

questions.title: How do I calculate and pay the Skills Development Levy (SDL)?
questions.text:
You must contribute Skills Development Levy (SDL) for all your employees*. The levy is calculated as follows:
0.25% of each employee's monthly total wages
Minimum: $2 for employees earning less than $800 a month
Maximum: $11.25 for employees earning more than $4,500 a month
*All employees working in Singapore, including permanent, part-time, casual, and temporary staff
After computing SDL for each employee, add up the amounts and and round the total down to the nearest dollar.
Here’s an example of an SDL computation:

questions.title: Can I change the parent's name on child's birth certificate?
questions.text:
The parents’ identification details shown on a child’s birth certificate are based on the official documents provided at the time of birth registration. After the birth is registered, ICA does not update the parents’ details on the child’s birth certificate.
If a parent has changed their name, use the parent’s deed poll together with the child’s birth certificate for transactions that require verification of the updated name. The updated name will not appear on the child’s birth certificate.
topics: Birth and Death Registration / Change of Particulars

questions.title: Can I reinstate my Singapore PR application after withdrawing it?
questions.text: If you withdraw your application, you cannot reinstate it. The processing fee is non-refundable and non-transferable. If you want to apply again, you must submit a new application.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass

questions.title: What should I do if my Singapore Citizenship sponsor passed away while my application is still in progress?
questions.text: We are so sorry for your loss. If your sponsor has passed on while your Singapore citizenship application is being processed, you should withdraw the current application and submit a new application through the Singapore Citizenship application e-Service, with details of the new sponsor, if applicable.
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass

questions.title: Can I apply for Singapore Citizenship without my parents’ consent if I am below 21?
questions.text: If you are under 21, you must get your parent(s)’ consent before you can submit a Singapore citizenship application
topics: Apply for Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long Term Visit Pass

questions.title: Does the Certificate of Identity (COI) have a Machine Readable Zone (MRZ)?
questions.text:
The Certificate of Identity (COI) issued to stateless Singapore permanent residents does not include a Machine Readable Zone (MRZ).
ICA does not issue alternative travel documents with an MRZ for stateless permanent residents. If your destination country requires a travel document with an MRZ, please check with their embassy or high commission for alternative entry requirements.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters
PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters / Certificate of Identity

questions.title: How can I apply for a Single or Multiple Journey Temporary Travel Document (TTD)?
questions.text: Temporary Travel Document (TTD) applications are assessed on a case-by-case basis. If you would like to apply for a Single Journey Temporary Travel Document (SJTTD) or a Multiple Journey Temporary Travel Document (MJTTD), submit your request via the ICA Feedback Formand attach any supporting travel documents. ICA will review your request and advise you on your eligibility to apply for a Temporary Travel Document.

questions.title: What is the processing time for an application once I have submitted all the required documents?
questions.text: Applications are processed within 15 working days from the date of receipt of all required documents, subject to the complexity of individual cases.

questions.title: I got married overseas, but I need a Singapore marriage certificate for use overseas. What should I do?
questions.text: If you require a Singapore marriage certificate, you can register your overseas civil marriage with ROM here.

questions.title: I registered my divorce in Singapore. How long does it take to be reflected in Singpass? Is it possible to expedite this process?
questions.text: If your divorce was granted in Singapore, your Singpass information is typically updated automatically within 2 weeks. Should your status remain unchanged after 1 month, please submit an application with your divorce documents through 'Our Marriage Journey' portal at https://www.marriage.gov.sg/marital-status-update under "For Divorce/Annulment Update".

questions.title: Why are statutory declarations required for my application?
questions.text: A statutory declaration is a formal written statement that you affirm to be true before a Commissioner for Oaths under the Oaths and Declarations Act. It serves to verify the accuracy of the marriage details you have provided and to confirm that there are no legal impediments affecting the marriage.

questions.title: Can I continue to work while my application to renounce my permanent residency is being processed?
questions.text:
You must declare in your application that you are not employed in Singapore.
This allows us to change your residential status from a permanent resident to a visitor.
topics: PR and Re-Entry Permit Related Matters

questions.title: What are the signs of infection?
questions.text:
Fever or chills
Feeling unwell or lethargic
Cough, breathlessness, or chest pain
Burning sensation or pain when passing urine
Redness, swelling, or discharge from wounds
New pain anywhere in the body
👉 Key message: If you notice any of these, seek medical advice early—infections can worsen quickly after transplant. Do note that because immunosuppressive drugs weaken the immune system, fever and redness may be absent or mild, even when an infection is present.

questions.title: Are the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) wage requirements inclusive of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The Progressive Wage Model (PWM) wage requirements include employee’s CPF contributions, but not employers’ CPF contributions. Employers must contribute their share of CPF contributions on top of the wage amount, based on the applicable contribution rates.
Example:
If the PWM monthly wage requirement is $2,500, employers should pay at least $2,500 in wages (inclusive of employee’s CPF contributions). Additionally, the employer must contribute their share of CPF contributions calculated on this $2,500 wage, based on the applicable CPF contribution rates.
You can also check if your employers are paying you the correct wages using the Progressive Wage (PW) Portal.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: For NRIC holders, how can I update my marital status?
questions.text:
Please be informed that Marital Status is not a registrable item under the National Registration Act, and ICA does not update marital status on NRICs.
If you wish to update your marital status, please contact the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) for assistance.

questions.title: When applying for Singapore citizenship and my surname has not shown during the application. How do I update my surname on my IC without replacing a new one?
questions.text: You do not need to apply for a replacement IC if you are a Permanent Resident holding on to a blue IC. Please submit your request via the ICA Feedback Form and attach the latest biodata page of your foreign passport for us to process the update.

questions.title: What if I do not wish to receive the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN)?
questions.text:
The MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) and any interest earned on it will be recovered from the child’s CPF account if, within two years of receiving the MGN, the following person(s) notify the CPF Board or the Ministry of Health in writing that they want the MGN to be returned:
Where the child is aged below 21 years old: The parent or legal guardian, acting on behalf of the child.
Where the child is aged 21 years and above: The child.
Once the CPF Board or the Ministry of Health is notified in this manner, the condition to retain the MGN will no longer be met and the MGN and the interest earned on it will be recovered. For more information on the conditions to receive and retain MGN, please see this page.
For more information about the MGN, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.

questions.title: What conditions must my child meet to receive and retain the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN)?
questions.text:
To receive and retain the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN), the following conditions need to be met:
Your child must be a Singapore Citizen at birth, or become one by the age of 2 (the grant amount will depend on the date the citizenship is obtained).
If your child was born overseas, the child's birth must be registered with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or through a Singapore Overseas Mission before the age of 12.
No request to return the MGN was made within two years of receiving the MGN. For more information on the request, please see this page.
For more information about the MGN, please visit madeforfamilies.gov.sg.

questions.title: I want to use my CPF savings to fully redeem my housing loan. Where can I find the Principal Outstanding and Accrued Interest in my redemption statement?
questions.text: You may refer to this guide to fill in the Principal Outstanding and Accrued Interest fields when making a full housing loan payment.

questions.title: Who can submit the appeal for my rejected Singapore Citizenship, Permanent Residence or Long-Term Visit Pass?
questions.text:
The sponsor of the rejected application must submit the appeal using Singpass. If there was no sponsor, the main applicant must submit the appeal.
If the original application was submitted without Singpass, you must submit the appeal using the same email address.

questions.title: Why did I encounter an error when trying to submit my Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residence/ Long-Term Visit Pass appeal?

You can only submit an appeal if your previous application was rejected within the last 12 months.
The sponsor of the rejected application must submit the appeal using Singpass. If there was no sponsor, the main applicant must submit the appeal.

questions.title: Can I submit a new appeal for Singapore Citizenship, Permanent Residence, or Long-Term Visit Pass if I currently have a pending application?

If you have a pending application for Singapore Citizenship, Permanent Residence, or Long-Term Visit Pass, you cannot submit a new appeal for the same pass or status.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay for Accident and Emergency (A&E) expenses if you are subsequently admitted to the hospital after seeking care at the A&E department, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable to your inpatient or day surgery bill.
If you are not admitted, you cannot use MediSave to pay for standalone A&E expenses. However, if you have incurred A&E expenses for a CT scan performed for traumatic brain injury at the A&E department of an approved medical institution in Singapore, you can withdraw from your MediSave through the medical institution under the MediSave withdrawal limit for outpatient scans.

questions.title: When will my CPF contribution rates change when I turn 55, 60, 65 or 70?
questions.text:
Your CPF contribution rates will change from the first day of the month after the month of your 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday. This is because on your birthday, you are considered to have just turned the relevant age and remain in your current age group for that month. From the following month onwards, you will move into the next age group and the new contribution rates will apply.
Example
Your 55th birthday falls on 13 January 2026.
For wages earned in January 2026
For wages earned in February 2026
Age group
55 years and below
Above 55 to 60 years
Total contribution rate
37% of total wages (>$750)
34% of total wages (>$750)
Employer and Employee share
Employer share: 17%
Employee share: 20%
Employer share: 16%
Employee share: 18%
Since your birthday falls in January 2026, your new contribution rates will apply from 1 February 2026 onwards.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

This is because on their birthday, your employee is considered to have just turned the relevant age and remains in their current age group for that month. From the following month onwards, they will move into the next age group and the new contribution rates will apply.
Example
Your employee's 55th birthday falls on 13 January 2026.
For wages earned in January 2026
For wages earned in February 2026
Age group
55 years and below
Above 55 to 60 years
Total contribution rate
37% of total wages (>$750)
34% of total wages (>$750)
Employer and Employee share
Employer share: 17%
Employee share: 20%
Employer share: 16%
Employee share: 18%
Since your employee's birthday falls in January 2026, the new contribution rates will apply from 1 February 2026 onwards.
