questions.title: I am an Indian Muslim/Chinese Muslim. Must I contribute to MBMF as well as SINDA/CDAC? Can I opt out from MBMF?
questions.text: Yes, Chinese Muslims and Indian Muslims are required to contribute to both MBMF and CDAC/SINDA respectively, as each organisation’s fund supports the development of their respective communities. To opt out of any fund, you may submit a request directly to the relevant organisation or through your employer.

questions.title: What about Non-Malay Muslims contributing to both MBMF and CDAC/SINDA/EA who are not receiving assistance from any SHGs?
questions.text: Non-Malay Muslims are eligible to benefit from programmes offered by both MENDAKI/MUIS and their respective SHG (CDAC/SINDA/EA), subject to each programme's eligibility criteria. If you are unsure of what assistance is available to you, we encourage you to reach out directly to MENDAKI, MUIS, or your respective SHG for guidance.

questions.title: What is the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL)?
questions.text:
Students taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in the following Post-Secondary Education Institutions (PSEIs) can apply for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL):
Institute of Technical Education (ITE)
Polytechnics
Arts institutions - LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA), University of the Arts Singapore (UAS)
Autonomous Universities
The MOE HESL is interest-free during the student’s course of study.
Click on the image below for a quick guide on the MOE HESL.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What happens if there are not enough savings in my CPF Ordinary Account for payment of tuition fees?
questions.text:
You will be informed in writing if there are not enough savings in your Ordinary Account for the payment of the tuition fees. In such cases, you will need to make alternative arrangements to pay the tuition fees in cash, or consider other financing options such as the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) or use of the student (borrower)'s Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds.
The MOE HESL is available to all full-time students of the polytechnics and universities and covers up to 90% of the tuition fees payable. For eligible students, it may also cover the balance of the subsidised tuition fees not covered by the base provision and loan for living allowance. It is also interest-free during the course of study, unlike the CPF Education loan where interest starts to accrue from the time of withdrawal.
If the student is unable to repay the MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, he/she may appeal to defer repayment and interest and the appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis. While CPF may also allow for deferment during challenging times, the interest continues to accrue as it is essential to fully restore the savings intended primarily for retirement. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: I intend to take a loan to finance my tertiary education and I will repay it promptly upon graduation. Which would be a better option for me - the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) or the CPF Education Loan?
questions.text:
The MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) is a better option as it is interest-free during the course of study, unlike the CPF Education loan where interest starts to accrue from the time of withdrawal. This means that if you repay the MOE HESL fully right after graduation, you will not incur any interest at all.
If you are unable to repay your MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, you may appeal to defer repayment and interest. Your appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
While CPF may also allow for deferment during challenging times, interest continues to accrue as it is essential to fully restore the savings intended primarily for retirement. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Can I reserve my CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for a student’s tertiary education, so that the savings are not transferred to the Retirement Account (RA) when I turn 55?
questions.text:
As your Ordinary Account (OA) savings are meant to boost your retirement savings when you turn 55, you will not be able to reserve your OA savings for a student’s tertiary education. At age 55, your Special Account (SA) and OA savings will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to meet the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) applicable to you. Your RA savings will continue to grow steadily and provide you with lifelong monthly payouts in retirement. You may find out more about the prevailing interest rate.
If you have set aside your FRS, whether fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash, any remaining SA savings will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA). You are eligible to withdraw in cash the remaining OA savings after setting aside the FRS, or up to $5,000 if you are unable to set aside the FRS. You can then use the cash as you wish, including towards the student’s education.
You may wish to consider the MOE's Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) to finance the student’s education. The MOE HESL is available to all full-time students of Post-Secondary Education Institutions (PSEIs) and covers up to 90% of the tuition fees payable. For eligible students, it may also cover the balance of your subsidised tuition fees not covered by the base provision, as well as a loan for living allowance. Additionally, it is interest-free during the course of study, unlike the CPF Education loan where interest starts to accrue from the time of withdrawal.
If the student is unable to repay the MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, he/she may appeal to defer repayment and interest and the appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis. While CPF may also allow for deferment during challenging times, the interest continues to accrue as it is essential to fully restore the savings intended primarily for retirement. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
The student can also approach their educational institution to find out about the other financial assistance schemes available.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Compared to the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL), isn't the CPF Education Loan a better option as I will pay the interest to the member’s CPF Ordinary Account so that they can benefit from it?
questions.text:
The MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) is interest-free during the course of study. This means that if you repay the loan fully right after graduation, you will not incur any interest at all for the MOE HESL. If you are unable to repay your MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, you may appeal to defer repayment and interest. Your appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
On the other hand, if you borrow from a member (lender)’s CPF Ordinary Account (OA), the interest starts to accrue from the time the savings are withdrawn to pay the educational institutions. When you repay the accrued interest to the member’s OA, you are simply restoring their OA balance to what the government would have paid them regardless. There is no additional benefit to them. By not using the member’s OA savings, the government will be paying them an OA interest of up to 3.5% during your period of study, allowing them to accumulate more CPF savings for their retirement.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Why can't I use more CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings for the student's tertiary education?
questions.text:
CPF is primarily intended to meet members’ retirement needs. As such, while students (borrowers) may take a loan from a member (lender)’s CPF Ordinary Account (OA) for their education, there is a limit on the total amount that can be withdrawn for this purpose.
You may wish to consider MOE’s Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) to finance the student’s education. The MOE HESL is available to all full-time students of the polytechnics and universities and covers up to 90% of the tuition fees payable respectively. It is also interest-free during the course of study, unlike the CPF Education loan where interest starts to accrue from the time of withdrawal.
If the student is unable to repay the MOE HESL due to further studies or financial difficulties due to unemployment or medical condition, he/she may appeal to defer repayment and interest and the appeal will be considered on a case-by-case basis. While CPF may also allow for deferment during challenging times, the interest continues to accrue as it is essential to fully restore the savings intended primarily for retirement. For more information on the MOE HESL, please refer to this link.
The student can also approach their educational institution to find out about the other financial assistance schemes available.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How do I apply for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL)?
questions.text:
To apply for MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL), please apply through the StudentLoan (SLSG) portal using your Singpass account.
For more information on MOE HESL, please visit MOE HESL website or approach your institution.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: What happens to my online CPF Education Loan application that have been endorsed by the CPF member (lender)?
questions.text:
If your CPF Education Loan application is successful, you will be notified on the application status generally within the next two months after the conditions have been met. You can check the application status under "Activities" by logging in to CPF website with your Singpass.
For all unsuccessful/ invalid applications, it could be due to one of the following reasons:
Did not meet the eligibility criteria i.e CPF member does not have sufficient Ordinary Account savings up to the Available Withdrawal Limit for education purposes.
Application was not endorsed by member within the deadline of 14 days.
Duplicate application detected i.e it is a one-time application for the whole course of study.
You may wish to consider the MOE Higher Education Student Loan that is interest-free during your course of study, if your application for the CPF Education Loan is unsuccessful.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: How much of tuition fees can be paid using CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings?
questions.text:
The savings in the CPF Ordinary Account (OA) can be used to pay up to 100% of your own, your spouse’s, your children’s, or your siblings’ tuition fees. However, if you are paying for your relatives’ tuition fees, the percentage of tuition fees that can be paid using your OA savings is:
10% if your relative(s) is studying at a university;
25% if your relative(s) is studying at a polytechnic or pursuing an approved Technical Engineer Diploma (TED) or a Technical Diploma at Institute of Technical Education (ITE); or
50% if your relative(s) is studying at an art institution.
To pay the remaining tuition fees, the student may consider using the Post- Secondary Education Account funds or applying for the MOE Higher Education Student Loan, subject to eligibility.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: Does MediShield Life or MediSave cover the GST charged on my medical bill?
questions.text: Yes, MediShield Life claim payouts and MediSave withdrawals are based on the bill amounts submitted by the medical institution, subject to the applicable limits under the respective schemes. If the bill includes GST, the GST amount will be included in the payout.

questions.title: When will the Government revise the Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) and Annual Value (AV) thresholds for MediShield Life or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, and how will I receive the updated premium subsidies?
questions.text:
The Government periodically reviews and updates the Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) and Annual Value (AV) thresholds used to determine subsidy levels and grant support, to ensure households with greater needs receive continued support. The revisions aim to improve affordability and help more households receive the healthcare subsidies and grant support they need, taking into account changes in household incomes and property AVs.
You do not need to take any action for your Premium Subsidies to be updated. Your Premium Subsidies will automatically be applied based on your eligibility under the revised criteria when your policy commences or renews. You can log in to MediShield Life e-Service with your Singpass to check your MediShield Life or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies eligibility.

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief for topping up my MediSave Account to pay my MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text:
Top-ups to MediSave Account to pay MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums are considered voluntary contributions.
Eligible members will enjoy tax relief for these top-ups. You can refer to the IRAS website for details on the eligibility criteria and amount of tax relief for voluntary MediSave contributions.

questions.title: How do I top up my MediSave for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums, and how can I check if it has been successfully processed?
questions.text:
You can make a top-up to your MediSave for MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premium payments via the Top up MediSave Account online form. MediSave top-ups are generally reflected immediately and will be deducted for premium payment.
You can view your MediSave top-ups by logging in to cpf.gov.sg with your Singpass. The top-up will be shown as "VOLUNTARY CON TO MEDISAVE A/C" or "HEALTHCARE TOP-UP" in your transaction records. If the top-up amount is not immediately reflected in your MediSave Account, check your MediSave Account balance after five working days, as some transactions may take longer to process.

questions.title: Why am I responsible for my child's outstanding MediShield Life premiums, and whose MediSave account will be used for the deduction?
questions.text:
Generally, parents of children under age 21 would be informed of their children's MediShield Life coverage and premium matters.
Under the MediShield Life Act or Regulations, parents are legally liable to pay for their child's MediShield Life premiums until the child reaches age 21. Should the children's premiums remain outstanding and unpaid, premiums may automatically be deducted from parents' MediSave Accounts.
Alternatively, you can top up your child's MediSave Account by referring to:
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?
For divorced parents who do not have custody and are not liable to maintain their child, you can write to us with a copy of court documents for assessment.

questions.title: What is the stamp duty applicable if I solely own a private property and wish to transfer this property to my husband who is a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)?
questions.text:
Both Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) will be payable on the transfer of the property to your husband. Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) may also be payable if you transfer the property within the holding period.
Stamp duty will be computed based on the purchase price or market value of the property, whichever is higher.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is stamp duty payable if a child's share in the HDB flat is transferred to his/ her parents, who are the remaining co-owner(s) of the HDB flat?
questions.text: Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) is not payable on the transfer of the child's partial share to his/her parents under the Transfer of HDB Flats within Family Remission if all the remission conditions are met. Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) may be applicable based on the profile of the parents.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) who is married to a Singapore Citizen. If I acquire a share in a residential property that is already owned by my spouse, will this be considered as our first property owned together and will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable?
questions.text:
If you are a SPR acquiring a partial share of a residential property that is already owned by your spouse, ABSD will be payable on the partial share acquired.
The ABSD Remission for a Married Couple is not applicable in this scenario, as the residential property must be purchased jointly by both spouses at the time of acquisition in order to qualify for the remission.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I am a Singapore Citizen purchasing another residential property before disposing of my existing residential property, can I apply for a refund of ABSD after the existing property is sold?
questions.text: There is no refund of ABSD if you purchase another residential property before disposing your existing property, unless you qualify for the ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen (SC) Seniors Remission.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: How can I determine whether an agreement for the use or occupation of premises is a licence agreement or a tenancy agreement, and whether lease duty is payable?
questions.text:
Licence agreements may not be liable to stamp duty if the agreement is intended only as a licence and does not act as a lease. Please note that if a licence agreement is executed in connection with a lease, the licence agreement would be liable to stamp duty.
If you are unsure if your agreement is a licence or a lease/tenancy, you may wish to seek independent legal advice or submit the document for adjudication. Please note that adjudication fees will be payable for the latter.

questions.title: If my spouse and I dispose of our jointly owned residential property and subsequently purchase one residential property each under our respective names, will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable?
questions.text: ABSD will not be payable on either property purchase, provided that both you and your spouse are Singapore Citizens and neither of you owns any other residential property at the time of purchase
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Is stamping required on a tenancy agreement with a short lease term?
questions.text: Stamp duty is a tax on dutiable documents relating to any immovable property in Singapore and any stock or shares. Accordingly, if there is a tenancy agreement executed and the Average Annual Rent (AAR) exceeds $1,000, stamping is required and lease duty is payable.

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen who owns one residential property in my personal name and another through a company. If I purchase another residential property under my personal name, will it be treated as my second or third residential property for Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) purposes?
questions.text: As you own one residential property in your personal name, the purchase of another residential property will be regarded as the acquisition of your second residential property for ABSD purposes.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: If I, a Singapore Citizen, sell my HDB flat that is jointly owned with my husband, who is a Singapore Permanent Resident, and subsequently purchase a private residential property jointly with him, will Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be payable?
questions.text: ABSD will not be payable on the purchase under the ABSD Remission for a Married Couple, provided that neither you nor your spouse owns any other residential property at the time of the joint purchase of the private residential property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am a Singapore Citizen who owns properties in overseas. If I purchase my first residential property in Singapore, is Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) payable?
questions.text: Properties owned outside Singapore are not included in the property count for ABSD purposes. Accordingly, if you purchase your first residential property in Singapore, ABSD is not payable for Singapore Citizens.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: My spouse transferred partial share in her private property to me. Will Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) be calculated based on the value of the partial share transferred or on the full value of the property?
questions.text: BSD and ABSD (if applicable) will be computed based on the purchase price or market value of the partial share in the property transferred (whichever is higher), rather than on the full value of the property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: I am the sole owner of an HDB flat and wish to transfer full ownership of the flat to my mother, who is currently listed as an occupier of the flat. She is a Singapore Citizen and does not own any other residential property. Will Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) be payable on the transfer?
questions.text: BSD is payable on the transfer of the HDB flat to your mother, computed based on the purchase price or market value of the property, whichever is higher.

questions.title: If my spouse solely owns our matrimonial home, will the property be included in my property count for Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) purposes when I purchase a residential property in my sole name?
questions.text: As the property is in your spouse's sole name, it is not included in your property count for ABSD purposes. Accordingly, ABSD will not be payable on your purchase of a residential property in your sole name if you are a Singapore Citizen who does not own any other residential property.
topics: Stamp Duty / Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)

questions.title: Can I upgrade or downgrade between ElderShield 300 and ElderShield 400?
questions.text: Switching between ElderShield plans is not possible. ElderShield 300 insureds were given a one-time option to upgrade to ElderShield 400 in 2007, and this option is no longer available. Downgrading from ElderShield 400 to ElderShield 300 is also not allowed.

questions.title: Is CareShield Life mandatory and do I have to join it?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is universal and mandatory for the following groups:
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, are automatically enrolled on 1 October 2020, or when they turn 30, regardless of any pre-existing conditions or disabilities.
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents born between 1970 and 1979 were automatically enrolled from 1 December 2021 if they were covered under ElderShield 400 and had not developed severe disability at the point of auto-enrollment.
Foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards and are born in 1979 or earlier are automatically enrolled provided they have no severe disability (if granted residency from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025). From 1 January 2026, automatic enrolment applies only to those with no disability at all.
The scheme is made mandatory to ensure that all Singaporeans, including those who are more vulnerable such as the lower-income group and those with pre-existing severe disabilities, have basic protection for long-term care needs. The Government will support Singaporeans who are unable to afford their premiums, so that no one loses their coverage due to financial difficulties.
If you were not automatically enrolled, you can apply to join CareShield Life. A 60-day free-look period applies from the start of coverage, after which you will not be able to terminate your coverage.

questions.title: Am I still eligible to be covered under CareShield Life if I have pre-existing disabilities?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later, including those with pre-existing severe disabilities, are covered under CareShield Life from 1 October 2020 or when they turn 30, whichever is later.
As part of collective responsibility, those with pre-existing severe disabilities are required to pay one year premium to join the scheme. This payment amount is less than the first monthly CareShield Life payout they will receive. Upon joining the scheme, they will continue to receive monthly payouts for as long as they are unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living. The Government will provide means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support to help those who are still unable to afford premiums even after subsidies.

questions.title: How do I view and make payment for composition amount and late payment interest?
questions.text:
You can view and pay composition amount and late payment interest via the following methods:
Composition Amount
Pay composition amount
Late Payment Interest*

For more information, please refer to:

Employer - Platform Operator / Enforcement and penalties for non-compliance

questions.title: Will interest and penalties be imposed if I make partial payment for my outstanding MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums before the IRAS deadline?
questions.text:
Yes, paying only part of your outstanding MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums would not stop interest and penalties from being charged. To avoid these charges, you will need to pay the full amount by the deadline stated in your IRAS notice.
If any MediShield Life or CareShield Life premiums remain unpaid, you may continue to be charged annual interest of 4% (compounded) and penalties of up to 17% of the outstanding amount.
We encourage you to pay your premiums in full by the deadline to avoid any further charges or enforcement action. For payment options, refer to "How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)s' CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?"

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier. Can I join or upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1979 or earlier and do not have any pre-existing disability, you can join CareShield Life. This applies whether you:
Previously opted out from ElderShield or did not qualify to join ElderShield
Are currently covered under ElderShield and wish to upgrade to CareShield Life
To join or upgrade to CareShield Life, you can apply via Application to join CareShield Life form using your Singpass. You may need to undergo a disability assessment, and will be informed by the Agency of Integrated Care if this is required.
For information on your personalised premiums and premium support, you can access the CareShield Life Premium Checker using your Singpass.

questions.title: Will ElderShield 300 or 400 insureds receive premium subsidies if they upgrade to CareShield Life?
questions.text: CareShield Life premium subsidies will be extended to eligible Singaporeans, including those currently on ElderShield 300 or 400 (born in 1979 or earlier), if they upgrade to CareShield Life. These subsidies are intended to support the increased benefits under CareShield Life and ensure that CareShield Life premiums remain affordable. You can refer to the types of premium support available for more information.

questions.title: I have recovered from a severe disability. Can I join CareShield Life, even if I was previously receiving payouts from ElderShield?
questions.text:
You can join CareShield Life if you have recovered from your severe disability and are able to perform all Activities of Daily Living1 independently, regardless of whether you previously received payouts from ElderShield. You may need to undergo a disability assessment, and will be informed by the Agency of Integrated Care if this is required.
1 Activities of Daily Living refers to feeding, dressing, toileting, washing, walking or moving around, and transferring from bed to chair and vice versa.

questions.title: I was born in 1979 or earlier. Will the ElderShield premiums I have already paid be taken into account when I join CareShield Life?
questions.text: If you were continuously insured under ElderShield before joining CareShield Life, your past ElderShield premiums will be taken into account when computing your CareShield Life premiums, resulting in lower premiums. Your premiums will be lower compared to those in the same cohort who were not insured under ElderShield.

questions.title: What changes are being made to My Legacy on 4 January 2027, and what do I need to do?
questions.text:
We’re changing how My Legacy helps you organise and access important information for you and your loved ones.
From 4 January 2027, My Legacy will no longer store certain information that is entered and maintained by users. Key legacy-planning information that is available from Government records will continue to be accessible through your dashboard.
What is changing?
My Legacy will discontinue the storage of personal information and funeral plans. This includes information such as important documents, financial accounts, bills and payments, properties, vehicles and digital accounts.
We are also working towards retrieving will-storage details directly from the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) Wills Registry, instead of requiring you to maintain a separate record in My Legacy. The Wills Registry was established by the Ministry of Law specifically to maintain information about wills and is now managed by SAL.
During this transition, you will not be able to store or update will details in My Legacy.
What will happen to information I have already stored?
On 4 January 2027, all personal information, will records and funeral plans stored in My Legacy will be permanently deleted.
After this date, these records will no longer be accessible to you or any Trusted Persons you have shared them with.
Your Advance Care Plan, CPF nomination and Lasting Power of Attorney are not affected. These will continue to be synced to your account, and Trusted Persons you have shared them with will continue to have access.
What do I need to do before 4 January 2027?
If you have personal information or a funeral plan stored in My Legacy:
Download the information you wish to keep and decide how you would like to store or share it with your loved ones or Trusted Persons.
If you have a will record stored in My Legacy:
You may consider depositing your will record with the SAL Wills Registry. Fees apply.
We are working towards retrieving will-storage information from the SAL Wills Registry through My Legacy, so that this information can be obtained from the dedicated Wills Registry instead of being separately entered and maintained by users in My Legacy.
If someone has shared information with you as a Trusted Person:
You will no longer have access to the affected information after 4 January 2027. Please speak to the person who shared the information with you about how they would like to keep you informed.
Why is My Legacy making these changes?
We recognise that some users have found these features useful for keeping important information together for themselves and their loved ones.
The underlying need remains important. What we are changing is how My Legacy supports it.
Today, information in these sections is entered and maintained by users. It can change over time, and users may also maintain the same or related information elsewhere. This means My Legacy can become another place that users need to remember to keep updated.
Where relevant information can be obtained from an existing authoritative source, we want to move towards helping you access it from that source rather than requiring you to maintain another copy in My Legacy. Our work towards retrieving will-record information from the SAL Wills Registry is one example of this approach.
For information that individuals need to maintain themselves, for example personal or digital account information, you can download what you have stored in My Legacy and choose how best to keep and share it with the people who may need it.
My Legacy will continue to focus on helping you and your loved ones access important legacy-planning information and services, including information from Government records such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF nomination and Lasting Power of Attorney.

questions.title: How long will it take to receive the outcome of my Home Protection Scheme application after my medical examination?
questions.text:
Processing time for your Home Protection Scheme (HPS) application depends on your individual circumstances.
After your medical examination, CPF Board will review the results and assess your eligibility. In some cases, additional information may be required before an outcome can be determined, and this may result in a longer processing time.
If you have not received an update on your application three weeks after your medical examination, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Would I have duplicate coverage or pay double premiums if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) when I am already covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text: There is no duplication in coverage and you are not paying double premiums. Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life for life. When you buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) through a private insurer, the IP consists of two components: your existing MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance coverage component. You will continue to be able to enjoy MediShield Life benefits when you buy an IP.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for my family members, and is there a limit?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave to pay Integrated Shield Plan (IP) premiums for your family members, including your spouse, parents, children, grandparents and siblings. There is no limit to the number of family members you can help pay for.
However, you should consider the long-term affordability of IP premiums for your family members and whether you will have enough MediSave savings for your own healthcare needs, including during your retirement years.

questions.title: How do Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Supplement plans and other private insurance plans for disability differ from CareShield Life in several ways.
Most private insurance plans for disability cover total and permanent disability, or are meant to insure against loss of income when one develops a disability and is unable to work. This is why they typically cease coverage between ages 60 and 70, when most insureds retire. CareShield Life, however, provides lifetime coverage and continues to cover you even if you develop severe disability in your later years.
Unlike private insurance plans, which cease coverage if insureds are unable to pay premiums, CareShield Life coverage will not lapse if you are unable to pay premiums due to financial difficulties. The Government will provide premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support.

questions.title: How do I defer or restart my CPF LIFE monthly payouts?
questions.text:
You can defer your monthly payouts using our Plan My Monthly Payouts service.
You can use the same service to restart your monthly payouts any time before age 70. Please note that your payouts will automatically start at age 70, even if you have not submitted any instruction to do so.

questions.title: Why do I need to login to “Your Benefits” via Singpass?
questions.text: Singpass keeps your personal data better protected through two-factor authentication. As the information displayed in “Your Benefits” is personalised to an individual, this will require the individual to log in via Singpass to retrieve personal information such as home address.

questions.title: Why can't I see the amount of MediShield Life Premium Subsidies my child received in the LifeSG application/website? Where can I find this information?
questions.text:
If you are the payer for your child's MediShield Life premiums, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to find out how much MediShield Life Premium Subsidies your child has received.
Alternatively, contact CPFB at medishieldlife.sg/writetous or 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: What is a Top-Up Grant?
questions.text:
It provides assistance for Singles Grant recipients who bought an HDB resale flat or those who bought a 2-room or 2-room Flexi flat from HDB as:
- Singles (on their own, with other first-timer single citizens, or with parents); or
- Families with a non-resident spouse
and have met one of the following conditions:
- Married a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) after the flat purchase
- Spouse/child has obtained Singapore citizenship or SPR status
Eligible households must submit their application for the Top-Up Grant within 6 months of their marriage registration or spouse/child becoming an SC/SPR.
Read more about the Top-Up Grant.

questions.title: Can I share my scheme payout details with my family members and friends?
questions.text:
While you may choose to share the details of your benefits with others, we wish to highlight that such information in “Your Benefits” is private and confidential to you.
We strongly advise against sharing your Singpass credentials or allowing others to access your account directly as this may compromise the security of your Singpass account, which contains many personal details. If you need to share “Your Benefit” details, you should explore other ways such as using a statement screenshot.

questions.title: I can only see the amount of Merdeka Generation Package MediSave top-up I received in "Your Benefits" @LifeSG. Where can I see the rest of my Merdeka Generation Package benefits?
questions.text: To find out more about your Merdeka Generation Package benefits, visit http://go.gov.sg/mgpackage.

questions.title: Where can I find more information about the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text: For more information about the Silver Support Scheme, please visit cpf.gov.sg/sss.

questions.title: Do I have to submit supporting documents when I submit a claim? How do I know whether the supporting documents are sufficient?
questions.text:
Please submit supporting documents with the following details when submitting a claim:
1. Course fee
2. Government subsidy
3. Receipt/net course fee payable (inclusive of GST)
4. Your name as per NRIC

questions.title: How can I collect my child’s birth certificate?
questions.text:
From 29 May 2022, all birth certificates will be issued digitally in the PDF format. After you’ve registered your child’s birth, you’ll be notified via SMS or email when the digital birth certificate is ready for download.
Do note that if you did not provide a local mobile number, you will not be notified via SMS.
Follow the instructions to download the certificate from the ICA website within 90 days. Do remember to save it to your personal device.
To get a printed copy of the birth certificate, you can print the downloaded PDF.
topics: Registering your child’s birth / Birth Certificate

questions.title: Who should I contact if I did not receive any notification to download my child’s digital birth certificate?
questions.text: If it has been more than 3 working days since you’ve submitted your application, please email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg for help
topics: Registering your child’s birth / Birth Certificate

questions.title: How can I get help to register my child’s birth online, or to download the digital birth certificate?
questions.text: You can email ICA at ICA_Birth_RBD@ica.gov.sg, or visit a ServiceSG centre for help.
topics: Registering your child’s birth / Online application

questions.title: Can I change the name of my child after submitting the application?
questions.text:
Once you’ve submitted your application, you’ll not be able to make any changes online.
After the birth has been registered, you may be able to alter your child’s name before they turn 1 year old. Fees will be charged for the application.
topics: Registering your child’s birth / Online application

questions.title: Can I use LifeSG to register my child’s birth online?
questions.text:
Yes, as long as your child is born in Singapore and you’re the biological parent. In fact, from 29 May 2022, registrations for all eligible births in Singapore should be done online.
If you’re eligible for a Singpass account, you can register your child’s birth on the LifeSG website or mobile app. If you’re not eligible for Singpass (not a Singapore citizen, permanent resident, or FIN holder), you should register your child’s birth on the LifeSG website. Registration costs $18 and you can pay with PayNow, credit or debit card.
topics: Registering your child’s birth / Online application

questions.title: How do I receive notifications from the LifeSG app?
questions.text:
You can turn on notifications by following these steps:
1) Go to Profile via the bottom navigation.
2) Tap the gear icon on the top right of the screen.
3) Select Notifications under the Preferences section.

questions.title: What happens after I have contacted a centre?
questions.text: The centres should acknowledge your enquiry within 3 to 5 working days and advise you on enrolment matters, should a vacancy be available. Please follow-up with the centre directly if you do not hear from them within 2 weeks.

questions.title: Why can't I see the amount of Additional Premium Support my child received in the LifeSG application/website? Where can I find this information?
questions.text:
If you are the payer for your child's MediShield Life premiums, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard to find out how much Additional Premium Support your child has received.
Alternatively, please write to medishieldlife.sg/writetous or call 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays). Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: How can parents check their child's MediSave balance?
questions.text:
You can view your child's Transaction History statement for the last 15 months by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard if:
1. You and your child are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents, and
2. Your child is below the age of 21 and has received CPF contributions (including Government grants such as the MediSave Grant for Newborns).
If you do not see your child's name listed in the Child dashboard, please submit a request to include your child via cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: Do I need to apply for the MediSave Grant for Newborns for my child?
questions.text:
All eligible newborns will receive the grant automatically after birth registration. You can check your child's CPF statement online by logging in with your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard.
If your child is born overseas, you can register his or her birth with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority directly, or through the relevant Overseas Missions.
If your child is eligible but did not receive the grant a week after registering his or her birth, please write to the Central Provident Fund Board at cpf.gov.sg/writetous.

questions.title: Why are the MediShield Life Premium Subsidies I am eligible for, as seen in CFPB's Healthcare Dashboard, different from those shown in "Your Benefit"@LifeSG?
questions.text:
"Your Benefits"@ LifeSG shows the total amount of subsidies that you have received for your MediShield Life policies starting in 2023 and 2024. The total amount of subsidies might include the following types of MediShield Life subsidies (depending on your eligibility):
1. Means-tested Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents.
2. Pioneer Generation Subsidies for the Pioneer Generation seniors.
3. Merdeka Generation Subsidies for the Merdeka Generation seniors.
You may wish to log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to find out more about the specific type and amount of MediShield Life subsidies you are currently eligible for.

questions.title: I want to appeal for higher MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. Where/How can I do so?
questions.text:
If you wish to have your eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies reassessed, you may submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service. You may also write to us at medishieldlife.sg/writetous or call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: What are the different MediShield Life premium subsidies and am I eligible for them?
questions.text:
The Government offers the following subsidies to keep MediShield Life premiums affordable:
1. Means-tested Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents (from 15% - 50% of premiums).
2. Special Pioneer Generation Subsidies for the Pioneer Generation seniors (from 40% - 60% of premiums).
3. Additional Merdeka Generation Subsidies for the Merdeka Generation seniors (from 5% - 10% of premiums).
In addition to these subsidies, there is Additional Premium Support (APS) to help members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.
You may log in to Healthcare dashboard 'Coverage and premium details' to check how much MediShield Life subsidies you can receive.

questions.title: Do I have to return the CPF housing grant(s) to HDB when I sell my flat?
questions.text: There is no need to return the CPF housing grants to HDB when you sell your HDB flat. However, any CPF savings used for the purchase of the flat, either as downpayment or monthly instalments, are to be returned with accrued interest to your CPF account when you sell your flat.

questions.title: What is a Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) bonus?
questions.text: It is a cash bonus disbursed to Singapore Citizen owners who have done a top-up to their CPF Retirement Account(RA) under the Lease Buyback Scheme.

questions.title: How do I check if I'm eligible?
questions.text:
You may apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter via the HDB Flat Portal. It will inform you upfront of your eligibility to purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amounts of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.
Read more about the application for an HFE letter.

questions.title: Where can i find out more about the Edusave scheme?
questions.text: For more information, please visit: MOE Edusave Account FAQs

questions.title: What are CPF housing grants?
questions.text:
They are Government subsidies given to eligible citizen households buying new or resale HDB flats. For new flats, they are given on top of the significant market discounts in the flat prices.
The housing grants are credited into flat buyers' and their core members' CPF Ordinary Accounts. They can be used to offset the purchase price of the flat and reduce the housing loan required for the flat purchase.
Read more about the CPF housing grants.

questions.title: Do I need to re-apply for Additional Premium Support after the two-year validity period?
questions.text: You will be invited to re-apply for Additional Premium Support (APS) if you have insufficient MediSave savings and limited family support to pay your premiums after the two-year validity period. There is no need for you to re-apply for APS ahead of time.

questions.title: Where can I find more information on the Assurance Package, GST Voucher, Majulah Package and MediSave Bonus?
questions.text: For more information about these governments schemes, please visit govbenefits.gov.sg.
topics: Majulah Package / Earn and Save Bonus

questions.title: I have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Why is it not reflected in the CareShield Life Premium Checker?
questions.text:
If you have recently submitted an appeal for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies, your appeal may still be processing and the outcome may not be reflected here.
If you require assistance with your latest appeal or form submission, please contact careshieldlife.gov.sg/writetous or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays). Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: I want to appeal for higher CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. Where can I do so?
questions.text:
If you wish to have your eligibility for CareShield Life Premium Subsidies reassessed, you may submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service. You may also contact us at careshieldlife.gov.sg/writetous or call the Healthcare Hotline at 1800-222-3399 from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT8 / excluding public holidays).
Please note that airtime charges will apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines.

questions.title: What is the rationale for imposing Goods and Services Tax (GST) on MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums?
questions.text: We have a broad-based Goods and Services Tax (GST) system, with minimal exemptions as this approach helps to keep the GST rate relatively low. GST is a tax on domestic consumption of goods and services, and is payable on insurance contracts such as health, motor, and fire insurance. Therefore, it applies to MediShield Life, CareShield Life and ElderShield premiums.

questions.title: What are some common causes of dysphagia?
questions.text:
Dysphagia can result from various conditions including:
Stroke
Neurological conditions (like Parkinson's disease)
Head and neck cancer or its treatment
Age-related changes
Brain injury
Muscle weakness

questions.title: How do I apply for Home Palliative Care and what is the cost?
questions.text:
How to apply
Do talk to a doctor (GP or a doctor from your hospital or polyclinic) who is familiar with your loved ones’ condition and needs. They can help to make the necessary referral.
You may also visit an AIC Link to get help with the application.
Cost
Charges may apply. Please check with your service providers.
You may also talk to your medical social worker at the hospital or polyclinic if you need help with the fees.
Please click here for more information about Home Palliative Care.
topics: Home Care Services / Home Palliative Care

questions.title: What is CareShield Life?
questions.text:
CareShield Life is a long-term care insurance scheme launched on 1 October 2020 by Ministry of Health (MOH). It provides basic financial protection should you become severely disabled, especially during old age, and need care for a prolonged period of time.
The monthly payout can be used for care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses.
Click here for more information on CareShield Life.

questions.title: Overview of CareShield Life
questions.text:
Why you need CareShield Life
One in two Singapore Residents are expected to develop severe disability at some point in their lifetime, and may need long-term care due to:
A sudden disabling event (e.g. stroke)
Worsening of chronic conditions and diseases (e.g. diabetes), or progression of age-related illnesses (e.g. dementia)
How CareShield Life works
It’s important to plan early for our future long-term care needs, but it’s difficult as the costs of long-term care is uncertain.
CareShield Life pools our risks together and ensures protection against potentially catastrophic long-term care costs, providing peace of mind.
Click here for more information on CareShield Life.

questions.title: Who’s covered under CareShield Life?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible to join, but when you can join depends on the year you were born.
Born in 1980 or after
Automatically covered once you turn 30
You’re automatically covered once you turn 30, or from 1 October 2020, whichever is later, regardless of any pre-existing medical conditions and/or disability.
If you were born in 1990 or later, we’ll write to you with more information about two months before your 30th birthday.
Born in 1979 or earlier
Optional participation
Your participation in CareShield Life is optional^.
If you were born between 1970 and 1979, insured under ElderShield 400, and have not developed severe disability, you had been automatically enrolled into CareShield Life from 1 December 2021. No action is required if you wish to join CareShield Life.
If you were not automatically enrolled and wish to join CareShield Life, you may access the Application to join CareShield Life e-Service with your Singpass and enjoy a 60-day free-look period.
Apply for CareShield Life
^ Except foreigners who become Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents from 1 October 2020 onwards, for whom participation is mandatory, provided they do not have severe disability (if granted residency status from 1 October 2020 to 31 December 2025) or any disability (if granted residency status from 1 January 2026 onwards).
Click here for more information on CareShield Life.

questions.title: How to check my premium and subsidies?
questions.text:
Calculate your premium and subsidies
Find out about your CareShield Life premiums and applicable subsidies.
Check your premium

questions.title: How do I know if my loved one meets the severe disability criteria?
questions.text:
He/ she will need to see an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor who will determine their disability level.
If he/ she is found to have mild or moderate disability instead, there are other financial assistance schemes that you can turn to for help, like the Home Caregiving Grant or MDW Levy Concession. Please find out more about the other financial assistance schemes here.

questions.title: What is the cost for the disability assessment?
questions.text:
For CareShield Life claims, the assessment fee for the first disability assessment will be waived. It does not matter whether your loved one is assessed to be severely disabled, or whether the claim is successful.
If this is not your loved one’s first time being assessed for CareShield Life claims, the assessor will collect an assessment fee from you. The cost of the assessment ranges from $100 (if you visit the assessor’s clinic) to $250 (if the assessor does a home visit).
You will need to pay the assessment fee first to the assessor. The amount will be reimbursed if your loved one is assessed to be severely disabled.
The assessment must be done by a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

questions.title: Would someone with dementia or other cognitive challenges automatically qualify for CareShield Life claims?
questions.text:
No, as such conditions affect people’s ability to carry out the six activities of daily living at different levels.
In order to qualify for a CareShield Life claim, your loved one still needs to undergo a disability assessment by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. The assessor will consider the impact of your loved one’s cognitive challenges as part of the assessment.

questions.title: How can we change details of the care recipient, , bank account/payee for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
To change scheme details
Log in with Singpass on eFASS. Go to “Manage My Schemes” > “Change in Scheme Details.”
If you are updating the details for someone who lacks mental capacity for the first time, please read here.
To change the payee to a nursing home that the care recipient is living at
If you are using CareShield Life to offset the cost of the nursing home fees, you can ask for the payout to be made directly to the nursing home.
For this change in payee, please approach the nursing home your loved one is residing at to help you submit the “Change in Application Details” Form to AIC.
Do keep a copy of the application documents for your own reference.

questions.title: What changes are being made to My Legacy on 4 January 2027, and what do I need to do?
questions.text:
We’re changing how My Legacy helps you organise and access important information for you and your loved ones.
From 4 January 2027, My Legacy will no longer store certain information that is entered and maintained by users. Key legacy-planning information that is available from Government records will continue to be accessible through your dashboard.
What is changing?
My Legacy will discontinue the storage of personal information and funeral plans. This includes information such as important documents, financial accounts, bills and payments, properties, vehicles and digital accounts.
We are also working towards retrieving will-storage details directly from the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) Wills Registry, instead of requiring you to maintain a separate record in My Legacy. The Wills Registry was established by the Ministry of Law specifically to maintain information about wills and is now managed by SAL.
During this transition, you will not be able to store or update will details in My Legacy.
What will happen to information I have already stored?
On 4 January 2027, all personal information, will records and funeral plans stored in My Legacy will be permanently deleted.
After this date, these records will no longer be accessible to you or any Trusted Persons you have shared them with.
Your Advance Care Plan, CPF nomination and Lasting Power of Attorney are not affected. These will continue to be synced to your account, and Trusted Persons you have shared them with will continue to have access.
What do I need to do before 4 January 2027?
If you have personal information or a funeral plan stored in My Legacy:
Download the information you wish to keep and decide how you would like to store or share it with your loved ones or Trusted Persons.
If you have a will record stored in My Legacy:
You may consider depositing your will record with the SAL Wills Registry. Fees apply.
We are working towards retrieving will-storage information from the SAL Wills Registry through My Legacy, so that this information can be obtained from the dedicated Wills Registry instead of being separately entered and maintained by users in My Legacy.
If someone has shared information with you as a Trusted Person:
You will no longer have access to the affected information after 4 January 2027. Please speak to the person who shared the information with you about how they would like to keep you informed.
Why is My Legacy making these changes?
We recognise that some users have found these features useful for keeping important information together for themselves and their loved ones.
The underlying need remains important. What we are changing is how My Legacy supports it.
Today, information in these sections is entered and maintained by users. It can change over time, and users may also maintain the same or related information elsewhere. This means My Legacy can become another place that users need to remember to keep updated.
Where relevant information can be obtained from an existing authoritative source, we want to move towards helping you access it from that source rather than requiring you to maintain another copy in My Legacy. Our work towards retrieving will-record information from the SAL Wills Registry is one example of this approach.
For information that individuals need to maintain themselves, for example personal or digital account information, you can download what you have stored in My Legacy and choose how best to keep and share it with the people who may need it.
My Legacy will continue to focus on helping you and your loved ones access important legacy-planning information and services, including information from Government records such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF nomination and Lasting Power of Attorney.

questions.title: What are the difference(s) between ACP, Advance Medical Directive (AMD) and Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
AMD and LPA are legal documents, while ACP is not.
AMD is to inform the doctor treating you (in the event you become terminally ill and unconscious) that you do not want any extraordinary life-sustaining treatment to be used to prolong your life.
LPA allows you to appoint one or more trusted persons (Donees) to act on your behalf for personal welfare and/or property and affairs matters should you lose mental capacity to make your own decisions.
ACP is useful because it would serve as a guide for your loved ones and healthcare team to act according to your best interests in the event that you are unable to make decisions or speak for yourself. The ACP will include healthcare preferences such as extent of treatment, pain control options etc. It also allows you to appoint up to 2 Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons (NHS) to speak on your behalf when you cannot speak for yourself.

questions.title: What's the difference between LPA Form 1 and Form 2?
questions.text:
LPA Form 1 is a standard form used by most people to make an LPA. It allows you to:
appoint up to 2 Donees
appoint 1 Replacement Donee (optional)
grant your Donees powers to decide on your personal welfare, property and affairs, or both
The online LPA Form on My Legacy is Form 1, which you can prepare by yourself.
LPA Form 2 is the non-standard form to make an LPA, for those who want to:
appoint more than 2 Donees
appoint more than 1 Replacement Donee
grant your Donees specific or customised powers
A lawyer must be consulted to prepare an LPA Form 2. The lawyer will do this online, and you'll be asked to review and accept your LPA draft online.

questions.title: What is the difference between LPA and ACP? If I have made a decision related to my health in the ACP, can the person nominated in my LPA overturn the decision?
questions.text:
An LPA grants your Donee the legal rights to make decisions for you if you’re unable to do so, but it does not tell your Donee what to do for your Personal Welfare.
An ACP helps you to communicate to your Donee, your healthcare team and your loved ones, what decisions they should make for your Personal Welfare. This includes decisions such as where you should live, who you should live with, your daily lifestyle and healthcare decisions.
Appointing the same person as your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers and ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson is strongly encouraged as it will help to avoid conflicts amongst your loved ones. However, you do not have to do so, and in that situation, the LPA Donee with Personal Welfare remains the legal decision maker while the NHS is who the healthcare team will consult on healthcare decisions and discussions as the NHS is meant to be your spokesperson.

questions.title: Once I have started to draft my LPA, is there a deadline for the LPA to be submitted to OPG?
questions.text: You must submit your LPA to OPG for registration within 6 months from the date of your LPA application. This means that you must obtain your Donee's consent to be appointed and have your LPA certified by a Certificate Issuer within this period. After 6 months of creation of your LPA, your draft LPA will be removed from OPGO and you will need to redraft your LPA.

questions.title: Can I appoint a non-Singaporean as my LPA Donee?
questions.text:
A non-Singaporean can be a Donee. You may appoint a foreign Donee in your LPA, so long as they meet the requirements of being a Donee e.g. 21 years old and above. If the foreign Donee has a Singpass account, the donor may make an LPA online. The Donee may log in to OPGO via Singpass to accept the appointment.
If the Donee does not have a Singpass account, the donor may submit a hardcopy LPA form together with the cover letter on why a hardcopy LPA is submitted. Mail in or drop off the completed hardcopy LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) at 3 Bishan Place #03-00, CPF Bishan Building, Singapore 579838.

questions.title: How do I view the full copy of my registered Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
After your LPA has been registered, you and your Donees can retrieve it at any time by logging in to the Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) with your Singpass.
If you would like to keep a printed copy of the LPA for personal reference, you can print the PDF after downloading it from OPGO. However, the printed copy will be watermarked and cannot be used for transactions.
Please follow the steps below to view the full LPA:
Open the LPA with Adobe Acrobat Reader DC.
Click on the paper clip icon located on the left panel. This opens up a tab called ‘Attachments’.
Double click the attachment named LPA Form_Certified_XXXXX.pdf to view your full LPA.
Please ensure that your device’s default setting is opening the PDF via Adobe instead of web browser.

questions.title: Must my Advance Care Planning (ACP) Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS) be my LPA Donee?
questions.text:
No, you do not have to appoint your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers to be your ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson.
However, you’re encouraged to do so, to reduce conflicting decisions made by your Donee and NHS.
An LPA grants your Donee the legal rights to make decisions for you if you’re unable to do so, but it does not tell your Donee what to do for your Personal Welfare. An ACP helps you to communicate to your Donee what decisions they should make for your personal welfare. This includes decisions such as where you should live, who you should live with, your daily lifestyle and healthcare decisions.
Because of this, appointing your LPA Donee with Personal Welfare powers as your ACP Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson will help to avoid conflicts amongst your loved ones.

questions.title: Can non next-of-kins (e.g. social service practitioners, godchildren, funeral directors) download the digital death certificate for a deceased person with no next-of-kin (e.g. single elderly)?
questions.text:
Only Next-of-Kin of the deceased or persons authorised by the Next-of-Kin are allowed to download a copy of the digital death certificate from My Legacy.
The Next-of-Kin for this purpose are:
spouse,
parent,
child,
sibling,
grandparent,
grandchild,
aunt/uncle; and
niece/nephew.
For deceased with no immediate Next-of-Kin, individuals who are assisting in the post-death matters can approach the hospital or certifying doctor for a hardcopy printout of the death certificate.

questions.title: What happens if an appointed Donee dies and you need to appoint a replacement Donee? Do you still need to revoke your existing LPA or is there another process to make it simpler?
questions.text:
If your LPA has 2 Donees appointed to act jointly and severally, with the same powers conferred to both, and 1 Donee dies, the remaining Donee is still able to act on the LPA and the LPA remains effective. If each Donee was only given specific powers, the remaining Donee can only act on the power that was granted to them, and the replacement Donee (if named within the LPA) will replace the Donee who has passed on. If no replacement Donee was named, the existing Donee can only act within the powers that was granted. To include a new Donee to cover the other powers not granted to the remaining Donee, you must revoke your LPA and make a new LPA.
If your LPA only had 1 Donee and a replacement Donee was also indicated, the replacement Donee will replace the Donee who passed on and the LPA remains effective. If no replacement Donee was named within the LPA, then the LPA will become invalid and a new LPA must be made to appoint a new Donee.
If your LPA had 2 Donees appointed to act jointly on your LPA, the Donees must act together and not individually. When any one Donee is no longer able to act, all the Donees in the joint appointment will be terminated. If there was a replacement Donee stated in the LPA, the replacement Donee will replace the 2 Donees who were appointed to act jointly. Otherwise, the LPA will no longer be in effect. Should the LPA no longer be effective, rather than revoke the LPA, you would have to make a fresh LPA to appoint new Donees to act on your behalf.

questions.title: What are the fees involved when making an ACP?
questions.text:
There are no fees involved to complete and register your ACP using the myACP online service.
If you make an appointment with an ACP facilitator, some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Cost may vary, so please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: Do we still need to return the deceased's NRIC to the police?
questions.text: There is no longer a need to surrender the deceased’s NRIC in police station for physical invalidation. To prevent it from being misused, you can either destroy the NRIC or punch a hole in it.

questions.title: Can I nominate my family members who are not a Singaporean/ Permanent Resident as my CPF Nominees?
questions.text: CPF members can nominate any person in their nominations, including those who are non-Singaporeans / Permanent Residents.

questions.title: Is there any cost involved in making an Advance Medical Directive (AMD)?
questions.text: To make an AMD, you will have to consult a doctor who, as a witness, is required to explain the AMD. You may have to pay the doctor for the services rendered. However, the AMD form itself is free.

questions.title: Does a Donor still need to visit a Certificate Issuer in person?
questions.text:
Yes, the Donor needs to visit a Certificate Issuer in-person to certify the LPA. An LPA is an important legal document.
Visiting a certificate issuer in person helps us to make sure that you:
understand the purpose of the LPA
understand the powers you are granting your Donees
are not under pressure to make the LPA
After your LPA has been certified, the certificate issuer will submit the LPA application to the Office of the Public Guardian on your behalf via OPGO.
Do note that your LPA must be submitted to OPG for registration within 6 months from the date of your LPA application. This includes obtaining your Donee's consent to be appointed and your LPA certification.

questions.title: What if I do not have anyone suitable around me to be my Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS)?
questions.text:
If you’ve appointed or are intending to appoint a Professional Deputy as a Donee in your Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), you can appoint the same person as your NHS. Make sure they are agreeable before you appoint them. You can find more details and the list of Professional Deputies on the Ministry of Social and Family Development website.
Alternatively, speak to an ACP facilitator to document and register your ACP. They’ll be able to guide you in making decisions on your healthcare preferences.
Some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: After completing the learning, can I write my own will without going to a lawyer?
questions.text:
Yes, you can legally write your own will without a lawyer. The learning tool covers basic will-writing concepts and simple scenarios to help you understand the process.
However, writing a legally sound will involves many technical requirements and potential complications that this tool cannot fully address. A lawyer can help ensure your will meets all legal requirements, consider scenarios you might not have anticipated, and draft clear language that reduces the risk of disputes later.
If you choose to write your own will, we strongly recommend having it reviewed by a lawyer before finalising it, especially if your situation involves complex assets, family circumstances, or cross-border considerations.

questions.title: Can I use the Will Learning tool to write a legally binding Will?
questions.text: No, nothing you enter in the learning tool is final or legally binding. This is purely a learning tool to help you understand will-writing concepts. The Will Preparation Template you receive at the end can be revisited and amended at any time, even after completing the exercise.

questions.title: How do I add, remove or share documents with a Trusted Person on My Legacy vault?
questions.text:
1) Adding a Trusted Person
To add a Trusted Person, login via Singpass to My Legacy vault. Under “Secure Sharing”, click on “View Trusted Persons”.
Then, click on “Invite new person” and key in the details as prompted before clicking on “Invite” to confirm the invitation. If your trusted person does not receive the notification via SMS / Email, please ask them to login directly to Vault to accept the invitation. Note that invites expire in 3 weeks and you only can add the same person up to 5 times before you are unable to add them anymore.
Once successful, you should see a pending invite which will shift into the “Accepted” tab, once your Trusted Person has accepted the invite.
2) Removing a Trusted Person
To remove a Trusted Person, click on the Trusted Person (under “Accepted” or “Pending”), then click “More”, and finally click “Remove Trusted Person”. Do note that edit only allows you to edit sharing access. If you need to amend the details of a Trusted Person, this will be done by removing them and adding them back with the amended details.
3) Sharing Documents with Trusted Persons
Once a Trusted Person has accepted the invite, click on the added Trusted Person, then click “Share Documents”. Under the Share Documents page, select between “Now, After Death or Never” to choose which access the Trusted Person has.

questions.title: Does my Trusted Person know who else I have added to My Legacy vault?
questions.text: No. Trusted Persons can only see your Legacy vault contents. They cannot see who you have added. It is good practice to keep your Trusted Persons, next-of-kin and important others aware of who you have added as a Trusted Person.

questions.title: How will the body be recovered under a whole body donation?
questions.text: If death occurs at the hospital, the body will be transferred to the mortuary, and collected by the assigned hospitals or university on the same day. If death occurs at home or other locations other than the hospital, the next-of-kin should contact the National Organ Transplant Unit (NOTU). NOTU will inform the assigned hospitals or university to make arrangements to collect the body from the location on the same day.

questions.title: What will happen to the joint property if one of the owner(s) passed away?
questions.text:
If the property is under joint tenancy, the person's share in the flat will be transferred to the remaining owner(s) and the remaining owners should lodge a Notice of Death (NOD) with Singapore Land Authority (SLA).
For HDB, the owner(s) can retain the existing flat provided that they:
are a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)
are at least 21 years old; and
satisfy HDB's eligibility rules and conditions to own a flat.
You can refer to the following page on HDB under the title "Demise of joint owner" for more information.

questions.title: If I appoint my Donees to act jointly on my LPA and one of my Donee passes on, is the remaining Donee the sole decision maker to act on the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)? (I do not have a replacement donee)
questions.text:
If your Donees are appointed to act jointly on your LPA, the Donees must act together and not individually. When any one Donee is no longer able to act, all the Donees in the joint appointment will be terminated.
If there was a replacement Donee appointed in the LPA, the replacement will replace the 2 Donees who were appointed to act jointly. Otherwise, the LPA will no longer be in effect.
You are thus advised to carefully think through the appointment of your Donees as well as indicate a replacement Donee to cover unexpected situations.

questions.title: How many people can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text: There is no limit to the number of persons who can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate. However, to download a death certificate, they must be a next-of-kin, or are authorised by a next-of-kin. To download a stillbirth certificate, they must be the parent of the stillborn baby, or are authorised by the parent.

questions.title: Can I complete an Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before I see a doctor?
questions.text: You can fill in your details on the Advance Medical Directive (AMD) Form 1 before seeing a doctor. However, your two witnesses and you must sign the form at the same sitting.

questions.title: I missed downloading the digital death certificate from My Legacy within 30 days from the date of death. How can I get a copy of the death certificate?
questions.text: Please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA using this form.

questions.title: How do I report a death that has occurred overseas?
questions.text:
If a Singapore citizen or permanent resident had passed on overseas, you should register the death and get a death certificate from the foreign authorities in the country where the person had passed on. You can then report the death to ICA with the foreign death certificate to update ICA's records.
If you are also bringing ashes home, please refer to this webpage.
Please refer to ICA website for more information on Reporting a Death that Occurred Overseas.

questions.title: I wish to choose and pre-buy a family niche. Can you provide guidance how to do so?
questions.text: The government-managed columbaria at Choa Chu Kang and Mandai are not for advance sale. Applicants will need to provide a death certificate of the deceased at the point of payment.

questions.title: How can the next-of-kin submit the digital death certificate to banks if they are requesting an "original" hardcopy?
questions.text:
For deaths that occur after 29 May 2022, only digital death certificates will be issued.
If the bank requests for an original hardcopy, you can provide the digital death certificate to the banks. The bank is able to verify these death certificates by scanning the QR code printed at the bottom right of the digital death certificates or via this link.

questions.title: Is it possible for me to leave my HDB flat to a non next-of-kin?
questions.text:
You may wish to consider writing a will to ensure that the ownership of the HDB flat is distributed according to your wishes. In the absence of a will, your flat and other assets will be distributed in accordance with the Intestate Succession Act (ISA).
However, you should pay special attention to the ownership type of the HDB.
