If the flat is under joint ownership, the deceased shares will transfer to the remaining joint owners and cannot be willed away. Only HDB's that are solely owned, or owned via tenancy-in-common, can will away their share of the property according to their wishes. It is strongly advised that a lawyer is consulted for matters relating to writing your will.
You may read more information about retaining a flat following life events at HDB's website.

questions.title: How do I search for a certificate issuer?
questions.text: You may make appointments with a Certificate Issuer (CI) or check a list of CIs through this webpage. Only individuals accredited by the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) can certify your LPA.

questions.title: How to find the approved funeral services providers/undertakers that handles HIV deceased. Is it a must for the deceased to be buried or cremated within 24 hours?
questions.text: The list of approved funeral services providers that could handle HIV deceased can be found in the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) website. There is no requirement for HIV deceased to be buried or cremated within 24 hours.

questions.title: Can the Will Preparation Template serve as my official will if I get it witnessed and signed?
questions.text: No. The tool is meant for learning only. The intent of the Will Preparation Template is to equip you with a prepared set of documented decisions and details, to make it easier when you visit your lawyer. It is not intended to act as your will. There may be specific clauses and circumstances that your will should cover, that would not be sufficiently covered by the preparation template.

questions.title: Does my Trusted Person(s) have any legal power?
questions.text: No, your Trusted Persons do not have any legal powers. If you would like to legally appoint them to carry out your wishes, consider a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and naming an executor in a will.

questions.title: Can my Trusted Person(s) invite other people to access My Legacy dashboard?
questions.text: No. Only people you have personally added as a Trusted Person can see the contents of your dashboard.

questions.title: Upon the death of a sole owner or co-owner of a HDB flat under tenancy-in-common, what should the family do?
questions.text: The deceased's family needs to apply to the Courts for the Grant of Letters of Administration (if the deceased did not leave a Will) or Grant of Probate (if there is a Will). With the document, the appointed person can then follow up to effect the change in the name of the flat from the deceased owner to the appointed person. Visit HDB's website to learn more.

questions.title: Upon the death of a co-owner of a HDB flat under joint tenancy, what should the family do?
questions.text: Under the Land Titles Act, the surviving owner(s) is/are required to lodge a Notice of Death (NOD) with Singapore Land Authority (SLA) so that the ownership of the whole flat is vested in the surviving owner(s). Visit HDB's website for more information on retaining a flat following life events.

questions.title: Will the death or stillbirth certificate be available for download indefinitely?
questions.text: No, you can only download it within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth. If there is a replacement certificate, it will be available for download 30 days from the date of issuance. You should save a copy of the certificate in your personal device.

questions.title: How many times can I download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
There is no limit to the number of times you can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate, if you are authorised to do so.
However, you can only download it within 30 days from the date of death or stillbirth. You should save a copy of the certificate in your personal device.

questions.title: Who can download the digital death or stillbirth certificate?
questions.text:
Death certificate
You can download the digital death certificate if:
you are a next-of-kin of the deceased; or
you are authorised by a next-of-kin
Stillbirth certificate
You can download the digital stillbirth certificate if you are the parent of the stillborn baby,
you are the parent of the stillborn baby; or
you are authorised by the parent

questions.title: What are the documents required for reporting overseas death?
questions.text:
To report a death that occurred outside Singapore, you will need to provide the following documents:
Your identification document (NRIC or passport)
Death certificate issued by the foreign authority (or certified true copy of the death certificate)
Deceased's Singapore identification documents (NRIC, Singapore passport or Long Term Pass card)
Coffin import/export permit (if available)
Burial/cremation permit (if available)
If you are a proxy, a letter of authorisation and identification document of the deceased's next-of-kin.
You may report the death of your family member (Singapore resident or Long-Term Pass holder) who died overseas to ICA via FormSG.

questions.title: Can family members overrule or object my Advance Medical Directive (AMD) from being carried out?
questions.text: If you have made an AMD, regardless of objections from members of your family, the doctors will have to respect your AMD. Hence, while making an AMD is a very personal decision, we encourage you to discuss it with your family members and loved ones. This will help them to understand and respect your wishes should you become terminally ill.

questions.title: Can a foreigner apply for a niche at NEA Columbarium?
questions.text: Due to space constraints, only the cremated ashes of individuals who are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents and foreigners whose immediate next-of-kin are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents may be stored in a government managed columbarium.

questions.title: If I have already made a Will, do I still need to make a CPF Nomination?
questions.text:
Your CPF savings are not covered under your will and hence cannot be distributed by way of will.
CPF savings do not form your estate (a will covers distribution of a deceased's estate) and are protected from creditor claims on any outstanding debts. This arrangement protects your CPF savings and ensures that your nominees receive your CPF savings expeditiously.
You are encouraged to make a CPF nomination if you want to distribute your CPF savings according to your wishes. Otherwise, your CPF savings will be distributed by the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) in accordance to the intestacy laws (for non-Muslims) of Singapore or the inheritance certificate (for Muslims) to your family members. Administrative fees apply and your next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration.

questions.title: Do I have to update my CPF Nomination record when there are changes to my circumstances (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee)?
questions.text: If your circumstances have changed (e.g. recent marriage, child birth, death of nominee), your current CPF nomination may no longer meet your wishes. You are encouraged to update your CPF nomination to keep it relevant with your current circumstances.

questions.title: If I want to speak to an ACP facilitator, must I visit in person?
questions.text:
You can speak to a certified ACP facilitator in person or virtually via video conferencing.
You can choose to find an ACP service provider that offers online services. You can meet then meet with the facilitator virtually via video conferencing.

questions.title: What if I want to speak to someone when using the myACP online service?
questions.text:
While filling out the form, you might want to seek guidance from loved ones, an ACP facilitator, your healthcare team, or a religious community. You can save a draft and return within 6 months of creating it to register your ACP.
If you plan to complete your ACP with an ACP facilitator, bring a copy of your inputs for discussion and confirmation. Once confirmed, they'll register your ACP. Some service providers may charge a nominal fee for doing an ACP. Please check with the respective organisations for details.

questions.title: What if I am unable to finish my ACP in one sitting when using the myACP online service?
questions.text:
The myACP online service supports a "save draft" feature. You may save drafts at any time and come back to it later.
However, you'll need to complete your ACP and obtain consent from your Nominated Healthcare Spokespersons (NHS) within 6 months of creating your online ACP to register your ACP.
If this is not done within the 6 month window, your application will expire, and you'll need to start over.

questions.title: Can I use myACP online service if I have a chronic condition?
questions.text:
Yes, you can.
Following the submission of your ACP, especially if you've chronic conditions (for example, diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease) or any other medical concerns, you may also consult your regular doctor.
They'll be able to advise on appropriate treatment goals and preferences based on your medical condition. If you wish to make changes to your ACP later, you can do so using the myACP service.

questions.title: How long does it take for trusted persons to be notified when the deceased has passed away?
questions.text:
A Trusted Person will not be notified of the deceased's status.
Once the death has been reported to ICA, the Trusted Person(s) would be able to view the document(s) in their My Legacy dashboard, by logging in using their Singpass (if the user has selected the option for the Trusted Person(s) to view the document(s) after his/her death).

questions.title: Will I be able to access the bank statements of my deceased next-of-kin?
questions.text:
As the banks are required to comply with customer information confidentiality requirements under the Banking Act, the banks are unable to disclose details pertaining to the bank account(s) held by the deceased without the appropriate court documents such as the Grant of Probate (if the deceased made a will) or Grant of Letters of Administration (if the deceased did not make a will).
You can check the Family Justice Courts website - https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/apply-for-letters-of-administration) or enquire with the Family Justice Courts for more information on the court procedure.

questions.title: What is the process for repatriating a body from Singapore, and is the export status indicated on the death certificate?
questions.text: The death certificate will only reflect details of the deceased and cause of death. To export a body out of Singapore, you will need to apply for an export permit with NEA Port Health. For more details, please visit NEA's website.

questions.title: If the deceased passed on without a will and did not make a CPF nomination. Will CPF contact the next-of-kin directly or do we need to appoint an administrator ourselves?
questions.text:
If a member did not make a CPF nomination, upon his/her passing, his/her CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws (for Muslims).
The next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration and approach PTO to proceed with the distribution. PTO will charge an administrative fee for this service. You may read more here.

questions.title: How to check the deceased's CPF nomination?
questions.text: You may refer to this FAQ from CPFB for more details.

questions.title: Will My Legacy's dashboard still be useful after these changes?
questions.text: Yes. Your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney will continue to be accessible through your dashboard, giving you a single, convenient place to view your key legacy plans. My Legacy will also continue to explore new services and improvements.

questions.title: I am a Trusted Person for someone else. What do I need to do?
questions.text: After 4 January 2027, you will no longer have access to any personal information, funeral plans, or will records that were shared with you through My Legacy. We recommend speaking with the person who shared their information with you to ensure you stay updated through other means.

questions.title: What should I do with my will record after downloading it?
questions.text: You may wish to deposit your will with the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL) Wills Registry for secure storage (fees apply). My Legacy is also working towards retrieving will information directly from the SAL Wills Registry in future, so that your details are always up to date.

questions.title: I previously uploaded supporting documents with my details but they are not in the summary document. Where can I find them?
questions.text: The summary document indicates whether you have supporting documents, but does not include the documents themselves. You can download your supporting documents separately from the individual sections within your dashboard.

questions.title: Why am I unable to download a summary of my information?
questions.text: If you do not see the option to download a summary in a particular section, it means you do not have any existing information stored in My Legacy for that section. However, if you recall having information there and suspect that this is a technical error, please contact us for assistance.

questions.title: How can I save my information before it gets deleted?
questions.text: A summary document consolidating your inputs is generated for each section – personal information, will, and funeral plan. Log in to MyLegacy@LifeSG and go to each section within your dashboard to download the respective documents. Please do this before 4 January 2027.

questions.title: Will my Trusted Persons still have access to my information?
questions.text: After 4 January 2027, your Trusted Persons will no longer be able to access any personal information, funeral plans, or will records you have shared with them. They will still have access to other information shared with them, such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney. We recommend letting your Trusted Persons know about these changes so they can make alternative arrangements.

questions.title: What data from My Legacy will be deleted?
questions.text: On 4 January 2027, all personal information, funeral plans, and will records stored in My Legacy will be permanently deleted. These records will no longer be accessible to you or any Trusted Persons you have shared them with. Data from other services, such as your Advance Care Plan, CPF Nomination, and Lasting Power of Attorney, will be unaffected.

questions.title: Why is My Legacy discontinuing personal information, funeral plan and will record storage?
questions.text: Information entered and maintained by users can change over time, and users may also keep the same or related information elsewhere. This means My Legacy can become another place that users need to remember to keep updated. We are therefore moving away from storing certain user-entered information, and towards helping users access relevant information from appropriate sources where possible.

questions.title: Where can I find My Legacy vault?
questions.text: My Legacy vault has been renamed to a dashboard. To access your dashboard, you’ll have to log in to MyLegacy@LifeSG with Singpass.

questions.title: Can I modify the Will Preparation Template after completing the tool?
questions.text: You cannot modify your responses within the learning tool once completed, as this data is not stored after completion. However, you can edit the Will Preparation Template document that you download and receive at the end, outside of this tool. If you want to go through the learning exercise again with different inputs, you can restart the tool from the beginning, although that is not necessary once you've completed the learning.

questions.title: How long does it take to complete the Will Learning tool and how long is my progress saved?
questions.text: The learning tool need not be completed in one sitting and you may take as much time as you need during each session to facilitate your learning. You can save the progress of your learning, and revisit it later. Your progress will be saved up to 6 months from the start of your learning, after which your data and progress will be purged and reset.

questions.title: What legal expertise was involved in creating this Will Learning tool?
questions.text: This tool has been reviewed by lawyers specialising in estate planning, to ensure factual accuracy of its content. This was last reviewed in December 2025.

questions.title: What should I do after completing the Will Learning tool?
questions.text:
At the end of the tool, you'll receive a Will Preparation Template that summarises your decisions. This template is not a legal will, but it's a useful reference document to bring to a lawyer when creating your actual will.
While you're not legally required to use a lawyer, doing so can help ensure that your will is legally sound and consider scenarios you might have missed, particularly if you have more complex estate planning needs. The template will help guide these conversations and make the process more efficient.

questions.title: Does my will need to be written in English?
questions.text:
No, there is no legal requirement for your will to be written in English. However, there are practical considerations to keep in mind if a will is written in another language.
Your will needs to be clearly understood by your executors, beneficiaries, and the courts. Using English may make this process smoother, as all documents filed or used in the Court must be in the English language. If your will is written in another language, translation will be required.
Please note that this learning tool is currently available only in English.

questions.title: What are the benefits of using the Will Learning tool?
questions.text: This tool helps you learn about the importance of having a will, key decisions you need to make, and important considerations when distributing your assets. By working through these decisions beforehand, you'll be better prepared for conversations with lawyers or other professionals when you're ready to draft your official will. The tool makes will-writing concepts easy to understand through hands-on learning rather than simply reading about them.

questions.title: I am not the next‑of‑kin and cannot prove my relationship with the deceased. How can I urgently apply for a burial or cremation permit?
questions.text:
If you are not the next‑of‑kin (NOK), you may still apply for a burial or cremation permit if the deceased’s NOK authorizes you to do so.
In such cases, you will need a Letter of Authorisation (LOA) from the deceased’s next‑of‑kin. The LOA template is available here.
Please submit the completed LOA together with your application via NEA’s e‑portal.
If you encounter issues with the submission and the issue is not resolved within 24 hours, please contact MyLegacy at go.gov.sg/edc for assistance.

questions.title: Can I share my legacy plans with a service provider?
questions.text:
There is no restriction in sharing your legacy plans with people you trust, so long as there is a personal Singpass login that can be associated with the Trusted Person logging in to view your shared documents.
However, it is recommended to keep your Singpass ID, password and 2FA details confidential.

questions.title: I noticed incorrect information on the death or stillbirth certificate. What should I do?
questions.text:
If it is within 6 months from the date of death or stillbirth, please notify the doctor or hospital to correct the information and issue a replacement certificate. Once a replacement certificate is issued download the replacement death or stillbirth certificate online, within 30 days from the date of issuance.
Please delete the version with incorrect information from your personal devices thereafter, as it will not be valid.
If it has been more than 6 months, please contact the Registry of Births and Deaths, ICA.

questions.title: Who is considered next-of-kin for the purposes of downloading a death certificate?
questions.text:
You'll be considered a next-of-kin who's allowed to download the digital death certificate if your relationship to the person who has died is listed here:
Parent
Spouse
Child or step-child
Sibling
Step or half-sibling
Grandparent
Grandchild
Uncle
Aunt
Niece or nephew
You'll be asked to declare your relationship when you make a request to download the digital death certificate.

questions.title: If I had not opted out of the Human Organ Transplant Act (HOTA) and I die at home, will my body be transported to a hospital for transplantation purposes?
questions.text: HOTA applies only to deaths in the hospitals which fulfill specific conditions.

questions.title: Will the Human Organ Transplant Act (HOTA) apply to citizens who pass away overseas?
questions.text: HOTA does not apply to deaths that occur overseas.

questions.title: Can I collect cremated ashes on the same day?
questions.text: If the cremation is in the morning, the ashes will be ready for collection by the afternoon. If the cremation is in the afternoon, the ashes will be ready the next day.

questions.title: What happens if one, or all, of my CPF nominees pass away?
questions.text:
The deceased nominee's share will be given to the surviving nominees in the same proportion as you have specified. If you have no surviving nominees, then your CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to your family members under the Intestate Succession Act or the Inheritance Certificate (for Muslims). The PTO charges your beneficiaries an administration fee for the distribution of your CPF savings.
You can also make a new CPF nomination and specify new nominee(s) or reallocate your shares to your surviving nominee(s) in accordance with your preference at any time. You are encouraged to regularly review your CPF Nomination and update it so that it continues to fit your intentions.

questions.title: What should I do to prove that my Donor has lost mental capacity?
questions.text: If a Donor loses mental capacity, the Donee should download the medical report template on MSF's website and arrange for the Donor to be evaluated by a registered medical practitioner to certify that the Donor has lost mental capacity.

questions.title: Is it possible to issue the death certificate in another language?
questions.text:
All death certificates issued by ICA are in English. ICA does not issue death certificates in any other languages.
You may wish to have the document translated by a translator/agency recognised by the relevant foreign authorities for which this translation is required.
You are advised to check directly with the party requesting this translated death certificate on their requirements.

questions.title: How do I check whether my deceased next-of-kin made a CPF nomination?
questions.text: Please refer to this FAQ by the Central Provident Fund Board for more information on CPFB processes with regards to CPF Nomination.

questions.title: How do I pulverize the cremated remains of my deceased next-of-kin?
questions.text:
The National Environment Agency can only pulverised the cremated remains under the following circumstances:
a) At the time of collecting the cremated remains after cremation at Mandai Crematorium;
b) At the time of collecting the cremated exhumed remains after exhumation at Choa Chu Kang cemetery; and
c) For the usage of Inland Ash Scattering (IAS) Facility at Garden of Peace.

questions.title: How can I find help on using Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO)?
questions.text:
You may view instructional videos and Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) on how to use the various services on OPGO, such as applying for an LPA, accepting an LPA Donee appointment, certifying an LPA, and submitting a Deputy Report. The videos are subtitled and voiced in English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil.
If you need guided assistance, you can seek help from your family first. Alternatively, you may also approach community touchpoints at ServiceSG centres.

questions.title: How to check the deceased's insurance policy?
questions.text:
Each insurance provider may have their own processes with regards to the release of information related to a deceased policyholder.
You can check with the insurance company on the necessary documentation needed such as a death certificate and proof of your relationship to the deceased, to establish your legitimacy in seeking this information.

questions.title: If a person nominates the religion organization under their CPF nomination, will CPF inform the organization?
questions.text:
Nominations are confidential. CPFB will not disclose your nomination details to anyone, including your nominee(s).
This will only be done when you pass away. You are encouraged to keep your nominees informed yourself, should you wish for them to know of the CPF Nomination.

questions.title: Is burial cost a recurring fee or one time only cost?
questions.text:
The Choa Chu Kang Cemetery Complex is the only cemetery in Singapore open for burials that is managed by the National Environment Agency (NEA). The burial fee as indicated in NEA's website is a once-off payment.
The payment of the burial fee for the grave plot is to be made at the service counters before burial. Foreigners are allowed to be buried in Singapore only if the deceased persons have immediate family members who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents. More information related to burial can be found at NEA's website.

questions.title: Why were some of my Retirement Account (RA) savings transferred to my Ordinary Account (OA) when I started my monthly payouts? How is the amount transferred computed?
questions.text:
Members born from 1957 onwards can withdraw an additional amount from their Retirement Account (RA) when they turn 65. Once you start your payouts, your RA savings will need to be used to provide for your payouts. You can choose to use part or all of your withdrawable RA savings to increase your monthly payouts via the Plan my monthly payouts service. In that case, the amount used to increase payouts will no longer be withdrawable. If you do not choose to use it to increase your monthly payout, the amount will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA) so that it remains available for your future withdrawal at any time.
Refer to the infographic below for examples of the transfer of monies from your RA to your OA.

questions.title: My child obtained Singapore Citizenship after birth. Is my child eligible to receive SG Child Support Package benefits?
questions.text: Children who become Singapore Citizens after birth will receive benefits based on the date they obtained their Singapore Citizenship. More details will be announced at a later date.

questions.title: What should be the reporting year for my society for the submission of Annual Return?
questions.text:
The Annual Return submission form will pre-populate the financial reporting period under "Reporting Period for Statement of Accounts From and To" based on the society's last submitted Annual Return. The society must review and amend the pre-populated dates if they do not reflect the actual financial period to be reported.
The "Reporting Year of Annual Returns" will be populated automatically based on the "To" date of the financial reporting period entered and cannot be edited manually. For example, if a society's last Annual Return was submitted for the reporting year 2000, the system will pre-populate the next financial reporting period with dates in 2001. If the society wishes to submit an Annual Return for a later period, such as 1 Apr 2024 to 31 Mar 2025, it should amend the "From" date to “1 Apr 2024” and the "To" to “31 Mar 2025” accordingly. The reporting year will then be automatically populated as 2025, based on the year of the "To" date.

questions.title: How do I submit the MediShield Life and CareShield Life Health Declaration form for Permanent Residence applicants?
questions.text:
All new Singapore Permanent Residence applicants who have received Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s In-Principle Approval are required to declare their health condition for MediShield Life and CareShield Life before completing formalities with ICA. The health status declared will not affect their Singapore Permanent Residence application.
The health declaration can be submitted via the "MediShield Life and CareShield Life health declaration for permanent residence applicants" form on the CPF website. Upon receiving In-Principle Approval from ICA, please wait one day before submitting the form. Each applicant must submit a separate individual form. Singpass login is required.
Applicants age 21 or older
If you are the applicant, please log in using your Singpass and select “Myself” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section. If you do not have a Singpass account, please apply for one. If you are unable to apply for a Singpass account, please have a family member who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident log in using their Singpass and select “A Family Member” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section.
Applicants under age 21
Applicants under age 21 must have a parent or legal guardian submit the Health Declaration on their behalf. If the parent or legal guardian is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, they must log in using their Singpass and select “A Family Member” under the “Select Person to be Insured” section. For applicants with a foreign parent or legal guardian, see the “Applicants without Singpass” section below.
Applicants without Singpass
If you are unable to apply for Singpass or do not have a family member who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with Singpass who can submit the Health Declaration form on your behalf, please use the Health Declaration form for applicants without Singpass instead. Foreign parents or legal guardians of applicants under age 21 with Singpass should also use this form.
Please note that submissions from applicants age 21 or older who have Singpass will not be processed through this form.
After Submission
You can check the status of your health declaration via "Activities". If you are required to attend a disability assessment for CareShield Life, the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will notify you of the details, or you can contact AIC at apply@aic.sg. Please attend the assessment promptly within the specified timeframe. You will be informed of the outcome via email, SMS or hardcopy once your application is processed.

questions.title: Why did I receive an error message when trying to redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life premium discounts?
questions.text:
To redeem Healthpoints for MediShield Life (MSHL) premium discounts, you must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident covered under MediShield Life or an Integrated Shield Plan, and aged 40 and above. You could be ineligible due to the following reasons (non-exhaustive):
1. You have been granted suspension of MSHL premium collection; or
2. You are a new Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident whose MSHL cover is still being issued.
For members who are assessed as eligible for Additional Premium Support (APS) or on the Fixed Amount on Ward (FAW) and Co-payment on Ward (CPW) Pensioner schemes, redemption of Healthpoints for MSHL premium discounts is not applicable as you are not required to pay MSHL premiums.
If your premiums are fully covered by APS or FAW or CPW Pensioner schemes, you can redeem your Healthpoints for other rewards such as grocery vouchers, transport credits, or lifestyle benefits instead.

questions.title: I have applied for a PSC Scholarship before and was unsuccessful. Can I apply again?
questions.text: You may re-apply in a subsequent year stating your new qualifications and/or achievements.

questions.title: How can I be sure that my application form has been successfully submitted through the application portal?
questions.text: You will receive an email acknowledgement upon successful submission of your application form, essay and supporting documents.

questions.title: I encountered technical difficulties while trying to submit my application on the portal. How should I proceed?
questions.text: Check and ensure that you are using a supported browser (e.g. Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Microsoft Edge) to access the application portal. If you are still unable to access the portal, please write to psc@psd.gov.sg with a screenshot of your browser and the error message for assistance.

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life coverage upon death?
questions.text: When an insured passes away, their CareShield Life policy will be terminated immediately. There is no death benefit for CareShield Life, so no payouts will be made upon the insured's passing. Any premiums paid will be refunded to the premium payer's MediSave if the insured passes away within the first 60 days of the first policy year. No premium refund will be made thereafter. If you wish to obtain insurance that provides death benefits, you can purchase Supplement plans that provide this option.

questions.title: What happens if my Direct Debit deduction is unsuccessful for my company’s CPF contributions?
questions.text:
You will receive an email notification from CPF Board if your Direct Debit fails (e.g. due to insufficient funds or exceeding your bank's payment limits) for your company’s CPF contributions.
CPF Contributions
Scenario(s)What HappensAction Required
a. First deduction fails, second deduction scheduledA second attempt will be made seven calendar days later.
Ensure you have sufficient funds in your bank account before the second attempt.
To pay immediately via PayNow QR instead, make a new submission via CPF EZPay for a PayNow QR code and write to us to cancel the second deduction at least two working days before the scheduled date to avoid double payment.
b. First deduction fails with no second deduction scheduled1; or
c. Second deduction also fails
No further deduction attempt will be made. You will need to make a new submission via CPF EZPay and pay using PayNow QR
Note: Late payment interest may be incurred.
1For voluntary contributions to three CPF accounts or Additional Medisave Contribution Scheme, no further attempt will be made if the deduction fails. You will need to make a new submission via CPF EZPay and pay using PayNow QR.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes
Employer - Platform Operator / Setting up of Direct Debit Authorisation

questions.title: I am making payment via PayNow QR. What do the different payment statuses on the 'View/Amend/Delete Submission' screen in CPF EZPay mean, and what do I need to take note of when making payment?
questions.text:
There are three payment statuses you may see when making payment via PayNow QR:
StatusWhat it meansWhat you need to do
PaidYour payment was successful.No action required.
Pending PaymentYour payment has not been received yet. This status cannot be manually deleted.Ensure payment is made within seven working days of submission, or the status will automatically update to 'Not Paid'.
Not PaidYour payment was not received within seven working days of submission.Resubmit your CPF contributions and make a new PayNow QR payment.
When making payment, please note the following:
Personal bank accounts
Scan the PayNow QR code before 23:59 hrs on the day of submission. If the QR code expires before you scan it, you will need to resubmit your CPF contributions to generate a new one.
Corporate bank accounts
The Maker must scan the PayNow QR code before 23:59 hrs on the day of submission. Once scanned, the Authoriser must approve the payment promptly. Payments received after seven working days from the date of submission will be refunded, and a new submission with a new PayNow QR payment will be required.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Payment modes

questions.title: How do I know if my loved one meets the severe disability criteria for MediSave Care?
questions.text:
He/ she will need to see an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor who will determine their disability level.
There is an assessment fee you will need to pay first, which will be reimbursed if your loved one is assessed to be severely disabled.
If he/ she is found to have mild or moderate disability instead, there are other financial assistance schemes that you can turn to for help, like the Home Caregiving Grant or MDW Levy Concession. Please find out more about the other financial assistance schemes here.
Click here to read more information about MediSave Care.

questions.title: How can I apply to SMF for hearing aids?
questions.text:
Hearings aids are applied through the audiologist in the restructured hospitals. If your loved one is not receiving care at any of these locations, you can visit the doctor at the polyclinic or a CHAS clinic for a referral to the Ear, Nose, Throat (ENT) department of a restructured hospital.
Click here to read more information about SMF assistive devices.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)

questions.title: Tell me more about the means-testing criteria.
questions.text:
Household monthly income per person is the criteria used when there is a household income. (“Household” refers to the NRIC address)
It is calculated as the total gross household monthly income divided by the total number of family members living together in the household. Gross monthly household income includes basic employment income, trade/self-employed income, overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions, and bonuses.
When there is no household income, Annual Value (AV) is used instead. AV is the estimated gross annual rent of a property if it were to be rented out, excluding furnishings and maintenance fees. It is determined by IRAS, and may be checked via IRAS website. Subsidy levels in 2026 will be determined using 2025 Annual Values.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)

questions.title: How will seniors or persons with disabilities know if they are eligible for SMF or Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)?
questions.text:
Some seniors and persons with disabilities may have received subsidies from both SMF and ATF* for support. With policy changes to SMF and ATF schemes from 14 Feb 2022, seniors and persons with disabilities are now served under just one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime. If the applicant has tapped on ATF before the age of 60, the applicant shall continue to be served by ATF and not SMF. If the applicant first tapped on ATF at the age of 60 or older, the applicant shall be served by SMF.
*ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities to purchase assistive technology devices to enable independent living.
Click here to read more information about SMF assistive devices.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)

questions.title: What healthcare items are covered in the SMF subsidy?
questions.text:
SMF subsidises the cost for home healthcare items such as:
Catheters and catheter set
Urine bags and bag hangers
Ostomy care items (eg stoma paste/ strip/ ring, stoma baseplate/ wafer/ barrier, closure clamps, elastic tape, Brava/ Stomaehesive powder and lubricating deodorant)
Milk feeds
Nasogastric tubes, pH indication test strips and needleless syringes
Thickeners
Wound dressings
Adult diapers and underpads
Nasal oxygen cannula
Click here to read more information about SMF healthcare items.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)

questions.title: How to apply for Healthcare Items under SMF?
questions.text:
Please approach your care provider for home medical, home nursing, home or day hospice services to assist you in applying for this SMF subsidy.
This SMF subsidy can only be applied through your service provider.
Click here to read more information about SMF healthcare items.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF)

questions.title: I am currently receiving the MDW Levy Concession for Persons with Disabilities. Do I need to reapply if there are changes?
questions.text:
If there are changes in the MDW, MDW employer or address:
You do not need to reapply for the levy concession.
If you are hiring a helper to take care of a new care recipient:
You will need to submit a fresh application.
Do note that each household can get up to two levy concessions if caring for two eligible persons with disabilities at the same time.
Click here to read more information about MDWLC PWD.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Migrant Domestic Worker (FDW) Levy Concession

questions.title: Why do I still see outstanding MediShield Life premiums in my Healthcare dashboard after making payment, or continue to receive payment notifications?
questions.text: If you have already made payment for your MediShield Life premiums, no further action is needed. We will notify you again if there is insufficient MediSave for premium payment. Allow five working days for the payment to be processed and reflected in the system before logging in to your Healthcare dashboard to check again.

questions.title: What is Mediation Direction?
questions.text:
A Mediation Direction is an order issued by authorised officers from Housing & Development Board (HDB), People’s Association (PA), Community Mediation Centre (CMC) or Community Relations Unit (CRU) to residents who are neighbours. The Mediation Direction is backed by law and must be complied with.
It requires the named individuals to attend a mediation session at the CMC or at a designated venue to discuss their issues amicably.

questions.title: Can I appeal against the Mediation Direction?
questions.text:
Appeals against the issuance of a Mediation Direction will not be acceded to. The Mediation Direction was issued as community mediation can help neighbours find common ground and resolve the matter amicably. Parties are strongly encouraged to participate in the mediation session and use the opportunity to work towards a mutually acceptable outcome.
Please note that failure to comply with the Mediation Direction without reasonable excuse is an offence under Section 13R of the Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015.

questions.title: What is the difference between voluntary mediation and directed mediation?
questions.text:
Voluntary mediation is initiated by the applicant who wishes to use the mediation service to discuss their matters with the other party facilitated by a trained mediator. Both parties have to agree to take part in the mediation process.
Directed mediation is initiated when an authorised officer issues a Mediation Direction (MD) requiring the named individuals to attend a mediation session. Attendance is compulsory. Failure to comply without a reasonable excuse is an offence under Section 13R of the Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015, and may result in a fine of up to $1,500.

questions.title: Where can I obtain information on my housing loan amount and monthly housing loan repayments?
questions.text:
To obtain a personalised estimate of your housing loan amount, monthly instalments and loan repayment period, you may approach HDB to apply for the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter, or your financier if you intend to take up a bank loan.
If you are still exploring your housing options, you may use the Home Purchase Planner to estimate your loan amount, together with the corresponding monthly instalment amount and loan repayment period. The Home Purchase Planner also helps you estimate your home purchase budget and illustrate its impact on your retirement.

questions.title: How do I receive CTG?
questions.text:
Eligible care recipients and caregivers can sign up with the training providers for the caregivers to attend the course. If eligible, the CTG subsidy will be reimbursed to the training provider after the training has been completed. You only need to pay for the co-payment amount.
Please click here for more information on the Caregivers Training Grant (CTG).

questions.title: If there is more than one caregiver taking care of the same person, are they all eligible for CTG?

Please click here for more information on the Caregivers Training Grant (CTG).

questions.title: Can I use the CTG to go for any training programmes I think is useful?

Please click here for more information on the Caregivers Training Grant (CTG).

questions.title: What is ElderShield?
questions.text:
ElderShield is a long-term care insurance scheme for Singaporeans and PRs who become severely disabled.
The monthly payout can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses.
As of 1 January 2020, this insurance scheme has stopped accepting new sign-ups.
Please click here for more information on ElderShield.

questions.title: If the ElderShield payout stopped because my loved one got better, can we claim for ElderShield again if he/ she becomes severely disabled later?
questions.text:
Yes, you can reapply and receive ElderShield payouts again if your loved one is assessed to meet all the eligibility criteria.
Please click here for more information on ElderShield.

questions.title: I have received my Letter of Intent but am currently overseas and unable to return to Singapore by 13 October 2026. How do I go about completing my medical assessment?
questions.text: If you are currently overseas, you may submit a request to have your medical assessment conducted by a preferred provider of your choice. Please submit your request online at go.gov.sg/hmarequest from 14 September onwards, upon receiving your Letter of Intent for us to email the medical checklist to your medical service provider. Please note that the link will only be accessible from 14 September.

questions.title: What is ElderFund?
questions.text:
ElderFund is a discretionary government assistance scheme to support lower-income, severely disabled Singapore Citizens aged 30 and above with their long-term care needs.
The payout can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services or daily expenses.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: If the ElderFund payout stopped because my loved one got better, can we apply again if he/ she becomes severely disabled later?
questions.text:
Yes, you can reapply and receive ElderFund payouts again if your loved one is assessed to meet all the eligibility criteria.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: If my loved one has IDAPE, ElderShield 300/400, CareShield Life, supplements, or MediSave Care, can he/ she still qualify for ElderFund?
questions.text:
ElderFund supports Singapore Citizens who are not:
A CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder / supplement plan policyholder
An active recipient of CareShield Life or ElderShield (including supplement claims)
Eligible for or currently receiving payouts from Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)
It also seeks to support Singapore Citizens who have low MediSave balances (ie less than $10,000). This means that the amount that they are able to draw from MediSave will not be the full $200 monthly sum allowable under MediSave Care.
Singapore Citizens who are unable to meet their long-term care costs, even after receiving payouts under ElderShield/ CareShield Life, MediSave Care (from himself or his spouse) or IDAPE, may be considered for ElderFund on a case-by-case basis.
Please speak to a medical social worker or AIC for advice.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: How is ElderFund different from MediFund or ComCare? If I am severely disabled and need help, who should I go to?
questions.text:
MediFund supports patients (regardless of disability) who are unable to cope with medical bills. ComCare provides social & medical assistance to low-income individuals or families. ElderFund specifically supports severely disabled, low-income Singaporeans aged 30 and above who meet the scheme’s eligibility criteria with their long-term care needs (eg to pay nursing home fees, home care expenses, etc).
Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund and ComCare support Singaporeans who are unable to pay for their care even after government subsidies and other means of support.
If you have challenges meeting your long-term care needs, please approach a social worker (eg with your long-term care provider or the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) for help. You can also speak to AIC for advice.
MOH and MSF work closely together to ensure that needy Singaporeans do not undergo unnecessary hurdles in seeking assistance for their healthcare, long-term care and daily living expenses.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: Will my loved one be automatically included for ElderFund if he/ she is receiving payouts from other moderate disability schemes like PioneerDAS or Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)?
questions.text:
No. ElderFund’s eligibility criteria are stricter as it is a severe disability scheme.
If your loved one is eligible for ElderFund, you may apply for PioneerDAS or HCG without going for a separate assessment (if you meet those schemes’ criteria).
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: How can we appeal for ElderFund?
questions.text:
If you do not meet ElderFund’s criteria but need help with long-term care costs, please contact AIC.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: How was the payout amount of $250 a month decided? Will the amount increase over time?
questions.text:
The payout is set to help lower-income Singaporeans with basic long-term care needs, and is similar to IDAPE’s payout. The government will review the scheme to ensure it stays relevant.
If you still need help with your care costs after tapping on various Government subsidies, you can apply for financial assistance through Government-funded safety nets such as MediFund or ComCare.
Please click here for more information on ElderFund.

questions.title: Where can I get more information about disability support and resources?
questions.text: Visit SG Enable’s Enabling Guide, an online resource for persons with disabilities and their caregivers, as well as professionals looking for disability support.

questions.title: What is the cost for Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)?
questions.text:
You will need to pay the assessment fee first, with some exceptions for CareShield Life policyholders (read more here). It will be reimbursed if the care recipient is assessed to be severely disabled.
The assessment costs $100 if you visit the assessor’s clinic for the session, and $250 if it is a house call. The cost is inclusive of GST.
topics: Financial Assistance Schemes / Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)

questions.title: What happens to my MediShield Life, CareShield Life or ElderShield or Integrated Shield Plan coverage if I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
When you renounce your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency, your MediShield Life, CareShield Life or ElderShield coverage will be terminated upon renouncement.
If you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), the MediShield Life component of your IP will terminate at the end of the current policy year. To continue with your policy, you need to check with your insurer whether they will insure you fully without the MediShield Life component.
Foreigners who were given a concession to remain under the MediShield Life scheme prior to 1 November 2015 or ElderShield scheme prior to 1 April 2024 should note that CPF accounts for all foreigners have closed on 1 April 2024. Coverage will continue as long as premiums are paid. If no alternative payment arrangements are made and premiums remain unpaid, your MediShield Life or ElderShield cover will lapse.

questions.title: What happens to the outstanding MediShield Life premiums after renouncing my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status?
questions.text:
As insurance coverage had been provided to you before you renounced your Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status, MediShield Life outstanding premiums remain payable even after renouncement.
If you have outstanding MediShield Life premiums, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will carry out enforcement actions, including the imposition of compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% on your outstanding premiums. IRAS may also appoint agents such as CPF Board and banks to recover your outstanding premiums from your CPF savings or bank accounts.
To avoid enforcement actions, please pay your outstanding premiums in full. You can refer to "How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)'s CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?" for payment options.

questions.title: Why does HDB charge the Family Season Parking (FSP) at 50% of the normal season parking (SP) charge?
questions.text: As the motorist has an existing HDB residential SP, we charge a lower rate for the FSP in support of the government's pro-family policy.

questions.title: I am staying in a private property, can I apply for Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: The FSP is only applicable to HDB residents who have already bought a regular season parking (SP) to park at their own residential car park. You can pay short-term parking charges when visiting your family members, or purchase SP, subject to availability of parking lots.

questions.title: Why do we need to have Family Season Parking (FSP) e-Service?
questions.text: You can apply for FSP through the e-Service at your own convenience, without visiting the HDB Branch to submit documentary proof of your relationship.

questions.title: When will the season parking payment be charged to my credit card?
questions.text: The season parking payment would be charged to your credit card on the 18th of every month.

questions.title: Where can I buy the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: If you are purchasing FSP for the first time, you can apply for family season parking. Subsequently, you can renew the family season parking like a normal season parking. You may also subscribe to auto renewal methods like GIRO or credit card, if eligible.

questions.title: I am granted 4-months free parking at my residential car park, why am I not allowed to purchase Family Season Parking (FSP) via the e-Service?
questions.text: We are currently enhancing our system to allow new residents with 4-months free parking to apply for FSP.

questions.title: What is Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: To facilitate family visits and foster closer family ties, HDB has introduced FSP scheme. With a season parking at the residential car park, motorist can purchase FSP at 50% of the Tier 1 rate at his/ her family member’s (grandparents, parents, in-laws, siblings, children) designated car park, subject to availability of parking lots.

questions.title: Why are car parks being offered to me with different timings (e.g. 7:00am to 7:00pm)?
questions.text: HDB car parks are built primarily to serve our residents’ parking needs. As some of the HDB car parks have high parking demand, we are unable to provide whole day Family Season Parking (FSP). To exercise flexibility, we allow daytime FSP to those who do not need to park in the night, at the same rates as a whole day FSP. You may also choose to enjoy a whole day FSP at an alternative car park.

questions.title: I have purchased a Family Season Parking (FSP). Where can I park my vehicle?
questions.text: You can park your vehicle at the allocated car parks within the same car park group.

questions.title: If I am driving a commercial vehicle under Vehicle Parking Certificate (VPC) scheme, can I buy the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: No. Commercial vehicles under the VPC scheme are not allowed to park at HDB's residential car parks due to safety and environmental concerns. Commercial vehicles are required to park at the centralised lorry/ bus parks which are located at the fringe of the housing estates.

questions.title: Is there any restriction on the parking hours of the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: There is no restriction on the parking hours for low occupancy car parks. For high occupancy car parks, there is a time restriction. We will inform you of the time restriction when you purchase the FSP.

questions.title: If I have a non-HDB season parking (SP) e.g. URA, JTC, would I be able to purchase the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: The FSP is only open to HDB residents who have a residential SP. Hence, you are not eligible to purchase the FSP.

questions.title: Can a residential season parking (SP) holder purchase more than one Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: A residential SP holder can purchase more than one FSP subject to eligibility and availability. There is no limit on the number of FSP a resident can purchase. This is in recognition that there may be more than one family member being visited on a regular basis.

questions.title: If I have a residential season parking (SP) and my parents are residing in the living quarter of an HDB shop, can I buy a Family Season Parking (FSP) at the car park serving the shop? Can the reverse situation be considered?
questions.text: If you are living at the HDB shop (with living quarter), you are eligible to purchase the FSP to visit your family residing in the HDB residential flat, subject to availability of parking lots.

questions.title: Can I buy the Family Season Parking (FSP) to park in the car park within the restricted zone area if my family members are residing there?
questions.text: You can purchase a FSP at 50% of non-concessionary monthly season parking charges, subject to availability of parking lots.

questions.title: If I have a season parking (SP) for my office/ stall/ shop in an HDB estate but do not have a residential SP, can I purchase the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: No. The FSP is only applicable to HDB residents who already purchased a residential SP.

questions.title: I have season parking (SP) for my residential car park for October 2019 and today is 18 October 2019, why does the system charge my Family Season Parking (FSP) full rate when I apply for FSP at my parents’ residential car park?
questions.text: You will need to have a valid SP at your residential car park before you can purchase FSP. For example, if your residential SP expires on 31 October 2019, you can only purchase FSP till 31 October 2019. As SP is meant for long-term use, you are unable to buy SP or FSP with less than a month. You may consider renewing your residential SP for November 2019 before buying FSP from 18 October to 30 November 2019, allowing you to pay a pro-rated rate for the month of October 2019 and full rate for November 2019.

questions.title: Is there any restriction to the type of vehicles eligible for the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: You can purchase FSP for cars, motorcycles, or commercial vehicles (which can fit into a car lot and depending on its unladen weight).

questions.title: Will residents be deprived of the parking lots? How does HDB protects resident season parking (SP) holders' interest?
questions.text: We will only sell the Family Season Parking (FSP) to SP holders after the parking needs of the residents are met. If the car park's occupancy is in high demand, we will only allow daytime FSP for that car park or offer an alternative car park to the applicants.

questions.title: Can I park at the lots reserved for season parking (SP) holders with my Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: Yes, you can park at the lots reserved for SP holders.

questions.title: Can I purchase a pro-rated Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: Yes, you can purchase a pro-rated FSP under the same conditions as residential [BC1] SP.

questions.title: Can I terminate my residential season parking (SP) and keep my Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: The FSP is only applicable to HDB's residents who have already bought the residential SP. You are unable to keep the FSP once your residential SP has expired or is terminated.

questions.title: Do I need to submit any documents to buy the Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: We will check our existing records on the relationship between you and your family member. If we do not have the records, you would need to provide documentary proof of the relationship between you and the family member when you apply.

questions.title: On the definition of family members for Family Season Parking (FSP), will HDB exercise any flexibility?
questions.text: In general, family members for this FSP scheme are defined as parents, children, grandparents, siblings, and parents-in-laws.

questions.title: My relationship with my kin could not be verified, what should I do?
questions.text: If we are unable to verify the relationship with your family member, you will need to submit documentary proof of the relationship at your managing HDB Branch. We will process the application once we have received the documents.

questions.title: Can I submit documentary proof of relationship without visiting the Branch?
questions.text: Yes, you can send the scanned copy of the documents to your managing HDB Branch via email.

questions.title: Why is there a need to have the 10-digit In-Vehicle Unit (IU) number before applying for Family Season Parking (FSP)?
questions.text: The IU number is required for car parks implemented with the Electronic Parking System. The 10-digit IU number is located on the left hand side of your IU.

questions.title: Will I be given a 2% rebate if I buy the Family Season Parking (FSP) via GIRO?
questions.text: Yes, you will be able to enjoy the 2% rebate upon successful GIRO deduction.

questions.title: I just did a change of scheme recently. Why can't I change my scheme again?
Can I purchase season parking for less than a month?
questions.text: Season parking is sold on a calendar month basis and for long-term use. For first-time purchaser, you can buy a pro-rated season parking for the current month and full rate for subsequent month. If you need a season parking for less than a month, HDB can exercise flexibility to sell you a season parking for the remaining days of the current month at the full rate.

questions.title: If I apply for season parking, what are the scenarios which do not allow termination and refunds?
questions.text: First-time purchasers can apply season parking for the current month with full rate or buy a longer-term season parking with pro-rated charge for the current month plus full rate for following month. As season parking is for long-term use, termination and refund of the pro-rated season parking (i.e. current month and subsequent month) is not allowed. For example, if you purchase season parking from 13 March to 31 May, you will not be allowed to terminate your season parking from 13 March to 30 April. You can, however, terminate your unused season parking from 1 May to 31 May on 30 April. Unused season parking charges from 1 May to 31 May will be refunded.

questions.title: Why did I not receive an immediate outcome of my request to cancel the GIRO arrangement?
questions.text: As the system is already processing the GIRO deduction for your current season parking I prior to your request to cancel the GIRO arrangement we will update you of the outcome via email after the GIRO deduction cycle. You do not need to resubmit your request. We seek your patience and understanding on this matter.
